1. Puggalakathā

1. The Direct and Inverse Order

1. iminā lakkhaṇena sakavādīpucchā dassitā Puggalo [M 0.0001][P 0.0001][V 0.0001][T 0.0001] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenāti (syā. pī. ka. sī.)? Āmantā. Yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

1. Is a person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, is that person apprehended by that in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? This should not be said.

Ājānāhi [V 0.0002] niggahaṃ. Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning, then indeed, friend, it should be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re no vata re (syā. pī.) vattabbe – “puggalo [M 0.0002] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

But if it is not to be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning,' then indeed, friend, it should not be said: 'A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

Anulomapañcakaṃ.

The Fivefold Direct Argument.

2. iminā lakkhaṇena paravādīpucchā dassitā Puggalo [T 0.0002] nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo [P 0.0002] saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

2. Is a person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? This should not be said.

Ājānāhi paṭikammaṃ. Hañci puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the rejoinder. If a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning, then indeed, friend, it should be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

But if it is not to be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning,' then indeed, friend, it should not be said: 'A person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

Paṭikammacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad on Rejoinder.

3. Tvaṃ ce pana maññasi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ [V 0.0003] no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’ti, tena tava tvaṃ (syā.) ṭīkā oloketabbā tattha hetāya paṭiññāya hevaṃ paṭijānantaṃ ṭīkā oloketabbā hevaṃ niggahetabbe. Atha taṃ niggaṇhāma. Suniggahito ca suniggahitova (syā.) hosi.

3. But if you think: 'It should indeed be said, "a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning,"' then, because of that reason and that proposition of yours, one who makes such a proposition should be refuted thus. Now we refute you. And you are well refuted.

Hañci [M 0.0003] puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena[T 0.0003], tena vata re vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

No [P 0.0003] ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti idaṃ te micchā.

But if it is not to be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning,' then indeed, friend, it should not be said: 'A person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person not apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—this of yours is wrong.

Niggahacatukkaṃ.

The Tetrad of Refutation.

4. Ese ce dunniggahite hevamevaṃ hevameva (syā.) tattha dakkha. Vattabbe kho – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,” no ca vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. No ca mayaṃ tayā tattha hetāya paṭiññāya hevaṃ paṭijānantā hevaṃ niggahetabbā. Atha maṃ niggaṇhāsi. Dunniggahitā ca dunniggahitāva (syā.) homa.

4. If this refutation is a poor one, then see it thus in that case. It should indeed be said: 'a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning,' but it should not be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' And we, making such a proposition with that reason and proposition, are not to be refuted thus by you. Yet you refute me. And we are poorly refuted.

Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

If a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning, then indeed, friend, it should be said: 'Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning.' What you say in that case—'It should indeed be said, "a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning," but it should not be said, "Whatever is a real and ultimate meaning, by that is that person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning"'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho[T 0.0004], tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti[V 0.0004]. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho [M 0.0004] paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti idaṃ te micchā.

If it should not be said: 'Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate,' then, friend, it should not be said: 'A person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate.' The statement you make in that regard—'It should indeed be said: "A person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate," but it should not be said: "Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate"'—that statement of yours is wrong.

Upanayanacatukkaṃ.

The Application Tetrad.

5. Na [P 0.0004] hevaṃ niggahetabbe. Tena hi yaṃ niggaṇhāsi – “hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, no ca vattabbe – yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

5. One should not be refuted in this way. Therefore, however you refute me—'If a person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, then, friend, it should indeed be said: "Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate."' The statement you make in that regard—'It should indeed be said: "A person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate," but it should not be said: "Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate"'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti idaṃ te micchā. Tena hi ye kate niggahe se niggahe [T 0.0005] dukkaṭe. Sukate paṭikamme. Sukatā paṭipādanāti.

If it should not be said: 'Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate,' then, friend, it should certainly not be said: 'A person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate.' The statement you make in that regard—'It should indeed be said: "A person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate," but it should not be said: "Whatever is real and ultimate, from that, that person is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate"'—that statement of yours is wrong. Therefore, the refutation you have made is ill-made. My rejoinder is well-made. My presentation is well-made.

Niggamanacatukkaṃ.

The Conclusion Tetrad.

The Application Tetrad.

10. Na hevaṃ niggahetabbe. Tena hi yaṃ niggaṇhāsi – “hañci puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – ‘vattabbe kho – puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, no ca vattabbe – yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti micchā.

10. One should not be refuted in this way. Therefore, that which you refute—‘If a person is not found in a real and ultimate sense, then for that reason, O good sir, it should indeed be said: “That person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is real and ultimate.” That which you state therein—“It should indeed be said: ‘A person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said: ‘That person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is real and ultimate’”’—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘yo saccikaṭṭho paramattho, tato so puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā’”ti idaṃ te micchā. Tena hi ye kate niggahe se niggahe dukkaṭe. Sukate paṭikamme. Sukatā paṭipādanāti.

If, however, it should not be said: ‘That person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is real and ultimate,’ then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said: ‘A person is not found in a real and ultimate sense.’ That which you state therein—‘It should indeed be said: “A person is not found in a real and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said: “That person is not found in a real and ultimate sense in the same way as that which is real and ultimate”’—this of yours is wrong. Therefore, the refutation that was made was badly made. The counter-refutation was well made. The establishment of the argument was well done.

Niggamanacatukkaṃ.

The Concluding Tetrad.

Dutiyo niggaho.

5. Suddhikasaṃsandanaṃ

17. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

17. Is a person apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and is form also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is form one thing and the person another? It should not be said so.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti [T 0.0013] micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and form is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, then you must surely say, ‘Form is one thing and the person another.’ Your statement that it should be said, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and form is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘Form is one thing and the person another,’ is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena’[P 0.0012], no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, ‘Form is one thing and the person another,’ then you must not say, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and form is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense.’ Your statement that it should be said, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and form is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘Form is one thing and the person another,’ is wrong… and so on….

18. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… saññā ca upalabbhati…pe… saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti…pe… viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

18. Is a person apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and is feeling apprehended in the real and ultimate sense… and so on… and perception… and so on… and volitional formations… and so on… and is consciousness apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is consciousness one thing and the person another? It should not be said so.

If a person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, then you must surely say, ‘Consciousness is one thing and the person another.’ Your statement that it should be said, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘Consciousness is one thing and the person another,’ is wrong.

No [M 0.0012] ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. But if it should not be said, ‘Consciousness is one thing and the person another,’ then you must not say, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense.’ Your statement that it should be said, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘Consciousness is one thing and the person another,’ is wrong… and so on….

19. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, cakkhāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotāyatanañca upalabbhati… ghānāyatanañca upalabbhati… jivhāyatanañca upalabbhati… kāyāyatanañca upalabbhati… rūpāyatanañca upalabbhati… saddāyatanañca upalabbhati… gandhāyatanañca upalabbhati… rasāyatanañca upalabbhati… phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca upalabbhati… manāyatanañca upalabbhati… dhammāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

19. Is a person apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and is the eye-base apprehended in the real and ultimate sense… and so on… and the ear-base… the nose-base… the tongue-base… the body-base… the form-base… the sound-base… the odor-base… the taste-base… the tangible-base… the mind-base… and is the mind-object-base apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? …and so on….

20. Cakkhudhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotadhātu ca upalabbhati… ghānadhātu ca upalabbhati… jivhādhātu ca upalabbhati… kāyadhātu ca upalabbhati… rūpadhātu ca upalabbhati… saddadhātu ca upalabbhati… gandhadhātu ca upalabbhati… rasadhātu ca upalabbhati… phoṭṭhabbadhātu ca upalabbhati… cakkhuviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… sotaviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… ghānaviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… jivhāviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… kāyaviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… manodhātu ca upalabbhati… manoviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati… dhammadhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

20. And is the eye-element apprehended in the real and ultimate sense… and so on… and the ear-element… the nose-element… the tongue-element… the body-element… the form-element… the sound-element… the odor-element… the taste-element… the tangible-element… the eye-consciousness-element… the ear-consciousness-element… the nose-consciousness-element… the tongue-consciousness-element… the body-consciousness-element… the mind-element… the mind-consciousness-element… and is the mind-object-element apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? …and so on….

21. Cakkhundriyañca [P 0.0013][T 0.0015] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotindriyañca upalabbhati… ghānindriyañca upalabbhati… jivhindriyañca upalabbhati… kāyindriyañca upalabbhati [V 0.0014] … manindriyañca upalabbhati… jīvitindriyañca upalabbhati… itthindriyañca upalabbhati… purisindriyañca upalabbhati… sukhindriyañca upalabbhati… dukkhindriyañca upalabbhati… somanassindriyañca upalabbhati… domanassindriyañca upalabbhati… upekkhindriyañca upalabbhati… saddhindriyañca upalabbhati… vīriyindriyañca upalabbhati… satindriyañca upalabbhati… samādhindriyañca upalabbhati… paññindriyañca upalabbhati… anaññātaññassāmītindriyañca upalabbhati… aññindriyañca upalabbhati… aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

21. And is the eye faculty apprehended in the real and ultimate sense… and so on… and the ear faculty… the nose faculty… the tongue faculty… the body faculty… the mind faculty… the life faculty… the femininity faculty… the masculinity faculty… the pleasure faculty… the pain faculty… the joy faculty… the displeasure faculty… the equanimity faculty… the faith faculty… the energy faculty… the mindfulness faculty… the concentration faculty… the wisdom faculty… the faculty of I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown… the faculty of final knowledge… and is the faculty of one who has final knowledge apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is the faculty of one who has final knowledge one thing, and the person another? It should not be said so.

Ājānāhi [M 0.0013] niggahaṃ. Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, then you must surely say, ‘The faculty of one who has final knowledge is one thing, and the person another.’ Your statement that it should be said, ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge is also apprehended in the real and ultimate sense,’ but it should not be said, ‘The faculty of one who has final knowledge is one thing, and the person another,’ is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ [T 0.0016] añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, ‘The faculty of one who has final knowledge is one thing and the person another,’ then, good sir, you must not say, ‘A person is found in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge is also found in the true and ultimate sense.’ What you say there—that ‘it should be said, “A person is found in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge is also found in the true and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said, “The faculty of one who has final knowledge is one thing, and the person another”’—is wrong…pe….

28. Rūpaṃ [V 0.0017] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanāti? Āmantā. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

28. Is form cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and is feeling also cognized in a real and ultimate sense? Is form one thing and feeling another? Yes. Is a person cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and is form also cognized in a real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is form one thing and a person another? It should not be said thus.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca [M 0.0016] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If form is cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and feeling is also cognized in a real and ultimate sense—form being one thing and feeling another—and a person is cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and form is also cognized in a real and ultimate sense; then indeed, good sir, it should be said, 'Form is one thing, and a person is another.' Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, 'Form is one thing, and a person is another,' then indeed, good sir, it should not be said, 'Form is cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and feeling is also cognized in a real and ultimate sense; form is one thing and feeling another; a person is cognized in a real and ultimate sense, and form is also cognized in a real and ultimate sense.' Ājānāhi [P 0.0016] niggahaṃ. Hañci viññāṇaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ aññe saṅkhārā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘viññāṇaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ aññe saṅkhārā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If consciousness is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and mental formations are also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is one thing and mental formations are another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense; then, sir, it should indeed be said: ‘Consciousness is one thing and a person another.’ That which you state therein—‘It should indeed be said: “Consciousness is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and mental formations are also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is one thing and mental formations are another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said: “Consciousness is one thing and a person another”’—is incorrect.

No ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “viññāṇaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ aññe saṅkhārā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca [T 0.0023] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi [M 0.0018] – “vattabbe kho – ‘viññāṇaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ aññe saṅkhārā, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

If, however, it should not be said: ‘Consciousness is one thing and a person another,’ then, sir, it should not be said: ‘Consciousness is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and mental formations are also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is one thing and mental formations are another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.’ That which you state therein—‘It should indeed be said: “Consciousness is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and mental formations are also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is one thing and mental formations are another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said: “Consciousness is one thing and a person another”’—is incorrect...

34. Cakkhāyatanaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotāyatanañca upalabbhati…pe… dhammāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotāyatanaṃ upalabbhati…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, cakkhāyatanañca upalabbhati…pe… manāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

34. The eye-base is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the ear-base is also apprehended... and the mind-object-base is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense... the ear-base is apprehended... the mind-object-base is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the eye-base is also apprehended... and the mind-base is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense...

35. Cakkhudhātu [V 0.0020] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotadhātu ca upalabbhati…pe… dhammadhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotadhātu upalabbhati…pe… dhammadhātu upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, cakkhudhātu ca upalabbhati…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

35. The eye-element is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the ear-element is also apprehended... and the mind-object-element is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense... the ear-element is apprehended... the mind-object-element is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the eye-element is also apprehended... and the mind-consciousness-element is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense...

36. Cakkhundriyaṃ [P 0.0017] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotindriyañca upalabbhati…pe… aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotindriyaṃ [T 0.0024] upalabbhati…pe… aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… cakkhundriyañca upalabbhati…pe… aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyanti? Āmantā. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

36. The eye-faculty is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the ear-faculty is also apprehended... and the faculty of one who has fully known is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense... the ear-faculty is apprehended... the faculty of one who has fully known is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense... and the eye-faculty is also apprehended... and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense. Is the faculty of one who has fully known one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another? Yes. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and is the faculty of one who has fully known also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is the faculty of one who has fully known one thing and a person another? It should not be said thus.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If the faculty of one who has fully known is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has fully known is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge is another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has fully known is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense; then, sir, it should indeed be said: ‘The faculty of one who has fully known is one thing and a person another.’ That which you state therein—‘It should indeed be said: “The faculty of one who has fully known is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has fully known is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge is another, and a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has fully known is also apprehended in the true and ultimate sense,” but it should not be said: “The faculty of one who has fully known is one thing and a person another”’—is incorrect.

No [M 0.0019] ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca [T 0.0025] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, puggalo upalabbhati [V 0.0021] saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, 'The faculty of one who has known is one thing, the person another,' then it should indeed not be said, 'The faculty of one who has known is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of final knowledge is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense, the faculty of one who has known is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another, a person is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has known is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense.' What you say there—'It should indeed be said: "The faculty of one who has known is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of final knowledge is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense, the faculty of one who has known is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another, a person is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the faculty of one who has known is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense," but it should not be said: "The faculty of one who has known is one thing, the person another"'—is wrong… and so on.

37. Rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanāti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ [P 0.0018] bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,” rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

37. Is form cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and is feeling also cognized in the true and ultimate sense? Is form one thing, feeling another? Yes. It was said by the Blessed One: 'There is a person practicing for their own welfare,' and is form also cognized in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is form one thing, the person another? This should not be said.

Ājānāhi paṭikammaṃ. Hañci rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,” rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; tena vata re vattabbe – aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggaloti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the rejoinder. If form is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and feeling too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and form is one thing, feeling another, and it was said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person practicing for their own welfare,' and form is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense; then it should indeed be said: 'Form is one thing, the person another.' What you say there—'It should indeed be said: "Form is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and feeling too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense; form is one thing, feeling another; it was said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person practicing for their own welfare,’ and form is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense," but it should not be said: "Form is one thing, the person another"'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe [T 0.0026] – “rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – ‘atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,’ rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘rūpaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ rūpaṃ aññā vedanā, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno, rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ rūpaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, 'Form is one thing, the person another,' then it should indeed not be said, 'Form is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and feeling too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense; form is one thing, feeling another; it was said by the Blessed One, "There is a person practicing for their own welfare," and form is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense.' What you say there—'It should indeed be said: "Form is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and feeling too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense; form is one thing, feeling another; it was said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person practicing for their own welfare,’ and form is also cognized in the true and ultimate sense," but it should not be said: "Form is one thing, the person another"'—is wrong… and so on.

38. Rūpaṃ [M 0.0020] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saññā ca upalabbhati… saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti… viññāṇañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

38. Form is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, perception too is cognized… volitional formations too are cognized… and consciousness is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

39. Vedanā [V 0.0022] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saññā ca upalabbhati… saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti… viññāṇañca upalabbhati… rūpañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

39. Feeling is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, perception too is cognized… volitional formations too are cognized… consciousness is cognized… and form too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

40. Saññā upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, saṅkhārā ca [P 0.0019] upalabbhanti… viññāṇañca upalabbhati… rūpañca upalabbhati… vedanā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

40. Perception is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, volitional formations too are cognized… consciousness too is cognized… form too is cognized… and feeling too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

41. Saṅkhārā upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, viññāṇañca upalabbhati… rūpañca upalabbhati… vedanā ca upalabbhati… saññā ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

41. Volitional formations are cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and consciousness is cognized… and form is cognized… and feeling is cognized… and perception too is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

42. Viññāṇaṃ [T 0.0027] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, rūpañca upalabbhati… vedanā ca upalabbhati… saññā ca upalabbhati… saṅkhārā ca upalabbhanti saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

42. Consciousness is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and form is cognized… and feeling is cognized… and perception is cognized… and volitional formations too are cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

43. Cakkhāyatanaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotāyatanañca upalabbhati…pe… dhammāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotāyatanaṃ upalabbhati…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena cakkhāyatanañca upalabbhati…pe… manāyatanañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

43. The eye-base is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the ear-base is cognized… and so on… and the mind-object base is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on… the ear-base is cognized… and so on… the mind-object base is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the eye-base is cognized… and so on… and the mind-base is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

44. Cakkhudhātu upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotadhātu ca upalabbhati…pe… dhammadhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotadhātu upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… dhammadhātu upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, cakkhudhātu ca upalabbhati…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu ca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe….

44. The eye element is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the ear element is cognized… and so on… and the mind-object element is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on… the ear element is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on… the mind-object element is cognized in the true and ultimate sense, and the eye element is cognized… and so on… and the mind-consciousness element is cognized in the true and ultimate sense… and so on.

45. Cakkhundriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, sotindriyañca upalabbhati…pe… aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena…pe… sotindriyaṃ upalabbhati…pe… aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, cakkhundriyañca upalabbhati…pe… aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; aññaṃ [T 0.0028] aññātāvindriyaṃ [M 0.0021] aññaṃ aññindriyanti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,” aññātāvindriyañca [V 0.0023] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

45. The eye faculty is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, the ear faculty is also apprehended… and so on… and the faculty of one who has come to know is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate… and so on… and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate. Is the faculty of one who has come to know one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person practicing for their own welfare,' and is the faculty of one who has come to know also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate? Yes. Is the faculty of one who has come to know one thing and the person another? It should not be said thus.

Ājānāhi [P 0.0020] paṭikammaṃ. Hañci aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,” aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena; tena vata re vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the rejoinder. If the faculty of one who has come to know is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, and the faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another, and it has been said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person practicing for their own welfare,' and the faculty of one who has come to know is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate; then, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the person is another.' That which you say in this regard—'It should indeed be said: “The faculty of one who has come to know is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, the faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge is another, and it has been said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person practicing for their own welfare,’ and the faculty of one who has come to know is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate,” but it should not be said: “The faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the person is another”'—is wrong.

No ce pana vattabbe – “aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – ‘atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,’ aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘aññātāvindriyaṃ upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññindriyañca upalabbhati [T 0.0029] saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aññaṃ aññindriyaṃ, vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno, aññātāvindriyañca upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘aññaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ añño puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

But if it should not be said, 'The faculty of one who has come to know is one thing, the person another,' then, good sir, it should indeed not be said, 'The faculty of one who has come to know is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, the faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge another; it has been said by the Blessed One, “There is a person practicing for their own welfare,” and the faculty of one who has come to know is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate.' That which you say in this regard—'It should indeed be said: “The faculty of one who has come to know is apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, and the faculty of final knowledge is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate, the faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the faculty of final knowledge is another; it has been said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person practicing for their own welfare,’ and the faculty of one who has come to know is also apprehended in the sense of what is real and ultimate,” but it should not be said: “The faculty of one who has come to know is one thing and the person is another”'—is wrong... and so on.

Opammasaṃsandanaṃ.

Juxtaposition by Comparison.

7. Catukkanayasaṃsandanaṃ

7. Comparison by the Fourfold Method

46. Puggalo [V 0.0024] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

46. Is a person apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality? Yes. Is form the person? It should not be said so.

Ājānāhi [M 0.0022] niggahaṃ. Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘rūpaṃ puggalo’”ti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality, then indeed, good sir, it should be said, 'Form is the person.' That which you state there—'It should indeed be said, “A person is apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality,” but it should not be said, “Form is the person”'—is incorrect.

No ce pana vattabbe – “rūpaṃ puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘rūpaṃ puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

49. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ puggalo…pe… cakkhāyatanasmiṃ puggalo…pe… aññatra cakkhāyatanā puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ puggalo…pe… dhammāyatanasmiṃ puggalo…pe… aññatra dhammāyatanā puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ dhammāyatanaṃ…pe….

49. Is a person apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality? Yes. Is the eye-base the person…pe… is a person in the eye-base…pe… is a person apart from the eye-base…pe… is the eye-base in a person…pe… Is the mind-object-base the person…pe… is a person in the mind-object-base…pe… is a person apart from the mind-object-base…pe… is the mind-object-base in a person…pe…

Cakkhudhātu puggalo…pe… cakkhudhātuyā puggalo…pe… aññatra cakkhudhātuyā puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ cakkhudhātu…pe… dhammadhātu puggalo…pe… dhammadhātuyā puggalo…pe… aññatra dhammadhātuyā puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ dhammadhātu…pe….

Is the eye-element the person…pe… is a person in the eye-element…pe… is a person apart from the eye-element…pe… is the eye-element in a person…pe… Is the dhamma-element the person…pe… is a person in the dhamma-element…pe… is a person apart from the dhamma-element…pe… is the dhamma-element in a person…pe…

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalasmiṃ aññātāvindriya”nti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘puggalasmiṃ aññātāvindriya’”nti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If, friend, a person is apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality, then indeed it should be said, 'The faculty of final knowledge is in the person.' That which you state there—'It should indeed be said, “A person is apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality,” but it should not be said, “The faculty of final knowledge is in the person”'—is incorrect.

No ce pana vattabbe – “puggalasmiṃ aññātāvindriya”nti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti[T 0.0032]. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthena,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘puggalasmiṃ aññātāvindriya’”nti micchā…pe….

50. Puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno”ti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

50. Is a person not apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person who is practicing for his own welfare'? Yes. Is form the person? It should not be said so.

Ājānāhi [M 0.0024] paṭikammaṃ. Hañci vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,” tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ puggalo”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘rūpaṃ puggaloti’” micchā.

Acknowledge the rejoinder. If, friend, it was said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person who is practicing for his own welfare,' then indeed it should be said, 'Form is the person.' That which you state there—'It should indeed be said, “It was said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person who is practicing for his own welfare,’” but it should not be said, “Form is the person”'—is incorrect.

No ce pana vattabbe – “rūpaṃ puggalo”ti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “vuttaṃ bhagavatā – ‘atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno’”ti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘vuttaṃ bhagavatā – atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno,’ no ca vattabbe – ‘rūpaṃ puggalo’”ti micchā…pe….

If, however, it should not be said, 'Form is the person,' then indeed, friend, it should not be said, 'It was said by the Blessed One, “There is a person practicing for his own welfare.”' That which you state there—'It should indeed be said, “It was said by the Blessed One, ‘There is a person practicing for his own welfare,’” but it should not be said, “Form is the person”'—is incorrect… and so on.

51. Puggalo nupalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno”ti? Āmantā. Rūpasmiṃ puggalo…pe… aññatra rūpā puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ rūpaṃ…pe….

51. Is a person not apprehended in the sense of a true and ultimate reality? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One, 'There is a person practicing for his own welfare'? Yes. Is a person in form…pe… is a person apart from form…pe… is form in a person…pe…

Vedanā [V 0.0027] puggalo…pe… vedanāya puggalo…pe… aññatra vedanāya puggalo…pe… puggalasmiṃ vedanā…pe….

Is feeling the person…pe… is a person in feeling…pe… is a person apart from feeling…pe… is feeling in a person…pe…
