175. So ca añño ca karonti, so ca añño ca paṭisaṃvedentīti? Āmantā. Sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkhanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

175. Do both that same one and another act, and do both that same one and another experience the result? Yes. Is happiness and suffering both self-made and made by another? It should not be said thus.…

176. Kalyāṇapāpakāni kammāni upalabbhantīti, kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ kattā kāretā vipākapaṭisaṃvedī upalabbhatīti? Āmantā. Neva so [M 0.0048] karoti na so paṭisaṃvedeti, na añño karoti na añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

176. Given that good and bad kamma are apprehended, is a doer, an instigator, and an experiencer of the result of good and bad kamma apprehended? Yes. Does that same one neither act nor experience the result, and does another neither act nor experience the result? It should not be said thus.…

177. Neva [V 0.0054] so karoti na so paṭisaṃvedeti, na añño karoti na añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Āmantā. Asayaṅkāraṃ aparaṅkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkhanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

177. Does that same one neither act nor experience the result, and does another neither act nor experience the result? Yes. Is happiness and suffering not self-made, not made by another, and arisen fortuitously? It should not be said thus.…

178. Kalyāṇapāpakāni [T 0.0067] kammāni upalabbhantīti, kalyāṇapāpakānaṃ kammānaṃ kattā kāretā vipākapaṭisaṃvedī upalabbhatīti? Āmantā. So karoti so paṭisaṃvedeti, añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedeti, so ca añño ca karonti so ca añño ca paṭisaṃvedenti, neva so karoti na so paṭisaṃvedeti, na añño karoti na añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

178. Given that good and bad kamma are apprehended, is a doer, an instigator, and an experiencer of the result of good and bad kamma apprehended? Yes. Does that same one act and that same one experience the result; does another act and another experience the result; do both that same one and another act and both experience the result; or does that same one neither act nor experience the result, and does another neither act nor experience the result? It should not be said thus.…

179. So karoti so paṭisaṃvedeti, añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedeti, so ca añño ca karonti so ca añño ca paṭisaṃvedenti, neva so karoti na so paṭisaṃvedeti, na añño karoti na añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Āmantā. Sayaṅkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ, paraṅkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ, sayaṅkatañca paraṅkatañca sukhadukkhaṃ, asayaṅkāraṃ aparaṅkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkhanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

179. Does that same one act and that same one experience the result; does another act and another experience the result; do both that same one and another act and both experience the result; or does that same one neither act nor experience the result, and does another neither act nor experience the result? Yes. Is happiness and suffering self-made; made by another; both self-made and made by another; or not self-made, not made by another, and arisen fortuitously? It should not be said thus.…

180. Kammaṃ atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0054]. Kammakārako atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

180. Does kamma exist? Yes. Does a doer of kamma exist? It should not be said thus.…

181. Kammaṃ atthīti, kammakārako atthīti? Āmantā. Tassa kārako atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

181. Given that kamma exists, does a doer of kamma exist? Yes. Does a doer of that one exist? It should not be said thus.…

182. Tassa kārako atthīti? Āmantā. Tassa tasseva natthi dukkhassa antakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

182. Does a doer of that one exist? Yes. For that very one, is there no making an end to suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus.…

183. Kammaṃ atthīti, kammakārako atthīti? Āmantā. Puggalo atthīti, puggalassa kārako atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

183. Given that kamma exists, does a doer of kamma exist? Yes. Given that a person exists, does a doer of the person exist? It should not be said thus.…

184. Kammaṃ [M 0.0049][V 0.0055] atthīti, kammakārako atthīti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ [T 0.0068] atthīti, nibbānassa kārako atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

184. Given that kamma exists, does a doer of kamma exist? Yes. Given that Nibbāna exists, does a doer of Nibbāna exist? It should not be said thus.…

185. Kammaṃ atthīti, kammakārako atthīti? Āmantā. Mahāpathavī atthīti…pe… mahāsamuddo atthīti… sinerupabbatarājā atthīti… āpo atthīti… tejo atthīti… vāyo atthīti… tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatayo atthīti, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ kārako atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

185. Given that kamma exists, does a doer of kamma exist? Yes. Given that the great earth exists… the great ocean… Sineru, king of mountains… water… fire… wind… grass, wood, and trees exist, does a maker of grass, wood, and trees exist? It should not be said thus.…

186. Kammaṃ atthīti, kammakārako atthīti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ kammaṃ, añño kammakārakoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

186. Given that kamma exists, does a doer of kamma exist? Yes. Is kamma one thing and the doer of kamma another? It should not be said thus.…

187. Vipāko atthīti? Āmantā. Vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

187. Does the result exist? Yes. Does one who experiences the result exist? It should not be said thus.…

188. Vipāko atthīti, vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Tassa paṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Na [P 0.0055] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

188. Given that the result exists, does one who experiences the result exist? Yes. Does one who experiences that one exist? It should not be said thus.…

189. Tassa paṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Tassa tasseva natthi dukkhassa antakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vipāko atthīti, vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Puggalo atthīti, puggalassa paṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

189. Does one who experiences that one exist? Yes. For that very one, is there no making an end to suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus.… Given that the result exists, does one who experiences the result exist? Yes. Given that a person exists, does one who experiences the person exist? It should not be said thus.…

190. Vipāko atthīti, vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ atthīti, nibbānassa paṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

190. Having considered that 'result exists,' does one who experiences the result exist? Yes. Having considered that 'Nibbāna exists,' does one who experiences Nibbāna exist? It should not be said thus… and so on.

191. Vipāko atthīti, vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Mahāpathavī atthīti…pe… mahāsamuddo atthīti… sinerupabbatarājā atthīti… āpo atthīti… tejo [V 0.0056] atthīti… vāyo atthīti… tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatayo [T 0.0069] atthīti, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ paṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

191. Having considered that 'result exists,' does one who experiences the result exist? Yes. Having considered that 'the great earth exists'… and so on… 'the great ocean exists'… 'Sineru, king of mountains, exists'… 'water exists'… 'fire exists'… 'wind exists'… 'grass, wood, and trees exist,' does one who experiences grass, wood, and trees exist? It should not be said thus… and so on.

192. Vipāko atthīti, vipākapaṭisaṃvedī atthīti? Āmantā. Añño vipāko, añño vipākapaṭisaṃvedīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. (Saṃkhittaṃ)

192. Having considered that 'result exists,' does one who experiences the result exist? Yes. Is the result one thing, and the one who experiences the result another? It should not be said thus. (Abbreviated.)

Purisakārānuyogo.

The Inquiry into the Agent.

Kalyāṇavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter: Kalyāṇa.

14. Abhiññānuyogo

14. The Application of Direct Knowledge.

193. Na [M 0.0050] vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci iddhiṃ vikubbatīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci iddhiṃ vikubbati, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

193. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not someone who performs psychic feats? There is. If there is someone who performs psychic feats, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

194. Na [P 0.0056] vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti…pe… paracittaṃ vijānāti… pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati… āsavānaṃ khayaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci āsavānaṃ khayaṃ sacchikaroti, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

194. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not someone who hears sounds with the divine ear element... who knows the minds of others... who recollects past lives... who sees forms with the divine eye... who realizes the destruction of the taints? There is. If there is someone who realizes the destruction of the taints, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

195. Atthi koci iddhiṃ vikubbatīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo iddhiṃ vikubbati, sveva puggalo? Yo iddhiṃ na vikubbati, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

195. Having considered that ‘there is someone who performs psychic feats,’ is a person thereby apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is the one who performs psychic feats that very person? Is the one who does not perform psychic feats not a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

196. Yo dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti…pe… yo paracittaṃ vijānāti… yo [V 0.0057] pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati… yo dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati… yo āsavānaṃ [T 0.0070] khayaṃ sacchikaroti, sveva puggalo? Yo āsavānaṃ khayaṃ na sacchikaroti, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

196. Is the one who hears sounds with the divine ear element... who knows the minds of others... who recollects past lives... who sees forms with the divine eye... who realizes the destruction of the taints, that very person? Is the one who does not realize the destruction of the taints not a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Abhiññānuyogo.

The Section on Supernormal Knowledge.

15-18. Ñātakānuyogādi

15-18. The Inquiry Concerning Relatives, and so forth.

197. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu mātā atthīti? Āmantā. Hañci mātā atthi, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

197. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not a mother? There is. If there is a mother, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

198. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0057] pitā atthi…pe… bhātā atthi… bhaginī atthi… khattiyo atthi [M 0.0051]… brāhmaṇo atthi… vesso atthi… suddo atthi… gahaṭṭho atthi… pabbajito atthi… devo atthi… manusso atthīti? Āmantā. Hañci manusso atthi, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

198. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not a father... a brother... a sister... a noble... a brahmin... a merchant... a commoner... a householder... a renunciant... a deva... a human being? There is. If a human being exists, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

199. Mātā atthīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Atthi koci na mātā hutvā mātā hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci na puggalo hutvā puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi koci na pitā hutvā…pe… na bhātā hutvā… na bhaginī hutvā… na khattiyo hutvā… na brāhmaṇo hutvā… na vesso hutvā… na suddo hutvā… na gahaṭṭho hutvā… na pabbajito hutvā… na devo hutvā… na manusso hutvā manusso hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi [T 0.0071] koci na puggalo hutvā puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

199. Having considered that ‘a mother exists,’ is a person thereby apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been not a mother, becomes a mother? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been not a person, becomes a person? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is there anyone who, having been not a father... and so on... having been not a human being, becomes a human being? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been not a person, becomes a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

200. Mātā atthīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti[V 0.0058]? Āmantā. Atthi koci mātā hutvā na mātā hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci puggalo hutvā na puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

200. Having considered that ‘a mother exists,’ is a person thereby apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a mother, becomes not a mother? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Atthi koci pitā hutvā… bhātā hutvā… bhaginī hutvā… khattiyo hutvā… brāhmaṇo hutvā… vesso hutvā… suddo hutvā… gahaṭṭho hutvā… pabbajito hutvā… devo hutvā… manusso hutvā na manusso hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci puggalo hutvā na puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there anyone who, having been a father... a brother... a sister... a noble... a brahmin... a merchant... a commoner... a householder... a renunciant... a deva... having been a human being, becomes not a human being? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

19. Paṭivedhānuyogo

19. The Inquiry into Penetration.

201. Na [P 0.0058] vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sotāpanno atthīti? Āmantā. Hañci sotāpanno atthi, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

201. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not a stream-enterer? There is. If a stream-enterer exists, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

202. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sakadāgāmī atthi…pe… anāgāmī atthi… arahā atthi… ubhatobhāgavimutto atthi… paññāvimutto atthi… kāyasakkhi kāyasakkhī (syā.) atthi… diṭṭhippatto [M 0.0052] atthi… saddhāvimutto atthi… dhammānusārī atthi… saddhānusārī atthīti? Āmantā.

202. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’? Indeed, it should not. But is there not a once-returner... a non-returner... an Arahant... one liberated in both ways... one liberated by wisdom... a body-witness... one who has attained to the view... one liberated by faith... a Dhamma-follower... a faith-follower? There is.

Hañci saddhānusārī atthi, tena vata re vattabbe [T 0.0072] – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

If a faith-follower exists, then surely it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense’.

203. Sotāpanno atthīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Atthi koci na sotāpanno hutvā sotāpanno hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci na puggalo hutvā puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

203. Having considered that 'a stream-enterer exists,' is a person thereby apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is there anyone who, not being a stream-enterer, becomes a stream-enterer? Yes. Is there anyone who, not being a person, becomes a person? It should not be said thus… and so on.

204. Atthi koci na sakadāgāmī hutvā… na anāgāmī hutvā… na arahā hutvā… na ubhatobhāgavimutto hutvā… na paññāvimutto hutvā… na kāyasakkhi hutvā… na [V 0.0059] diṭṭhippatto hutvā… na saddhāvimutto hutvā… na dhammānusārī hutvā… na saddhānusārī hutvā saddhānusārī hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci na puggalo hutvā puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

204. Is there anyone who, not being a once-returner, not being a non-returner, not being an Arahant, not being one liberated in both ways, not being one liberated by wisdom, not being a body-witness, not being one who has attained to the view, not being one liberated by faith, not being a Dhamma-follower, and not being a faith-follower, becomes a faith-follower? Yes. Is there anyone who, not being a person, becomes a person? This should not be said thus... etc.

205. Sotāpanno atthīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Atthi koci sotāpanno hutvā na sotāpanno hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci puggalo hutvā na puggalo hotīti? Na [P 0.0059] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

205. Considering that a stream-enterer exists, is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a stream-enterer, is no longer a stream-enterer? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, is no longer a person? This should not be said thus... etc.

Atthi koci sakadāgāmī hutvā… anāgāmī hutvā na anāgāmī hotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci puggalo hutvā na puggalo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there anyone who, having been a once-returner... having been a non-returner, is no longer a non-returner? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, is no longer a person? This should not be said thus... etc.

Paṭivedhānuyogo.

Inquiry into Realization.

20. Saṅghānuyogo

20. Inquiry concerning the Saṅgha.

206. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā atthīti? Āmantā[T 0.0073]. Hañci cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā atthi, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

206. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense’? Yes. Are there not the four pairs of noble men, the eight noble individuals? Yes. If the four pairs of noble men, the eight noble individuals, exist, then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense’.

207. Cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā atthīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Cattāro [M 0.0053] purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā buddhapātubhāvā pātubhavantīti? Āmantā. Puggalo buddhapātubhāvā pātubhavatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

207. Considering that the four pairs of noble men, the eight noble individuals, exist, is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Do the four pairs of noble men, the eight noble individuals, appear due to the appearance of a Buddha? Yes. Does a person appear due to the appearance of a Buddha? This should not be said thus... etc.

Puggalo buddhapātubhāvā pātubhavatīti? Āmantā. Buddhassa bhagavato parinibbute ucchinno puggalo, natthi puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a person appear due to the appearance of a Buddha? Yes. When the Blessed One, the Buddha, has attained Parinibbāna, is the person cut off, does the person not exist? This should not be said thus... etc.

Saṅghānuyogo.

Inquiry concerning the Saṅgha.

21. Saccikaṭṭhasabhāgānuyogo

21. Inquiry into what is Analogous to the Real Sense.

208. Puggalo [V 0.0060] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Puggalo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puggalo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

208. Is a person apprehended in the real and ultimate sense? Yes. Is a person conditioned? It should not be said thus... etc. Is a person unconditioned? It should not be said thus... etc. Is a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? It should not be said thus.

209. Puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Āmantā[P 0.0060]. Saṅkhatañca asaṅkhatañca ṭhapetvā atthaññā tatiyā koṭīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

209. Is a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Setting aside the conditioned and the unconditioned, is there another, a third category? It should not be said thus... etc.

210. Saṅkhatañca asaṅkhatañca ṭhapetvā atthaññā tatiyā koṭīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “dvemā, bhikkhave, dhātuyo. Katamā dve? Saṅkhatā ca dhātu asaṅkhatā ca dhātu. Imā kho, bhikkhave, dve dhātuyo”ti ma. ni. 1.125, ālapanamattameva nānaṃ! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “saṅkhatañca asaṅkhatañca ṭhapetvā atthaññā tatiyā koṭī”ti.

210. Setting aside the conditioned and the unconditioned, is there another, a third category? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, there are these two elements. Which two? The conditioned element and the unconditioned element. These, monks, are the two elements!’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘Setting aside the conditioned and the unconditioned, there is another, a third category’.

211. Puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ [T 0.0074] saṅkhataṃ, aññaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

211. Is a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is the conditioned one thing, the unconditioned another, and the person yet another? It should not be said thus... etc.

212. Khandhā saṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Aññe khandhā, aññaṃ nibbānaṃ, añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

212. Are the aggregates conditioned, Nibbāna unconditioned, and a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Are the aggregates other things, Nibbāna another, and the person yet another? It should not be said thus... etc.

213. Rūpaṃ saṅkhataṃ, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ rūpaṃ, aññaṃ nibbānaṃ, añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ saṅkhataṃ, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, puggalo neva saṅkhato nāsaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ viññāṇaṃ, aññaṃ nibbānaṃ, añño puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

213. Is form conditioned, Nibbāna unconditioned, and a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is form another thing, Nibbāna another, and the person yet another? It should not be said thus. Is feeling... perception... formations... consciousness conditioned, Nibbāna unconditioned, and a person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is consciousness another thing, Nibbāna another, and the person yet another? It should not be said thus... etc.

214. Puggalassa [M 0.0054] uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatīti? Āmantā. Puggalo saṅkhatoti? Na [P 0.0061] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, saṅkhatassa saṅkhatalakkhaṇāni. Saṅkhatānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ katamāni tīṇi (a. ni. 3.47) uppādo paññāyati[V 0.0061], vayo paññāyati, ṭhitānaṃ aññathattaṃ paññāyatī”ti a. ni. 3.47. Puggalassa uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati; tena hi puggalo saṅkhatoti.

214. Is the arising of a person apparent, their passing away apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence apparent? Yes. Is a person conditioned? It should not be said thus... etc. It has been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, these are the three characteristics of the conditioned. Of conditioned phenomena, monks, arising is apparent, passing away is apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence is apparent.’ The arising of a person is apparent, their passing away is apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence is apparent; therefore, a person is conditioned.

215. Puggalassa na uppādo paññāyati, na vayo paññāyati, na ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyatīti? Āmantā. Puggalo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vuttaṃ [T 0.0075] bhagavatā – “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, asaṅkhatassa asaṅkhatalakkhaṇāni. Asaṅkhatānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ na uppādo paññāyati, na vayo paññāyati, na ṭhitānaṃ aññathattaṃ paññāyatī”ti a. ni. 3.48. Puggalassa na uppādo paññāyati, na vayo paññāyati, na ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati; tena hi puggalo asaṅkhatoti.

215. Is the arising of a person not apparent, their passing away not apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence not apparent? Yes. Is a person unconditioned? It should not be said thus... etc. It has been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, these are the three characteristics of the unconditioned. Of unconditioned phenomena, monks, arising is not apparent, passing away is not apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence is not apparent.’ The arising of a person is not apparent, their passing away is not apparent, and the alteration of their state of persistence is not apparent; therefore, a person is unconditioned.

216. Parinibbuto puggalo atthatthamhi, natthatthamhīti? Atthatthamhīti. Parinibbuto puggalo sassatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthatthamhīti. Parinibbuto puggalo ucchinnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

216. The person who has attained Parinibbāna—is he in a state of existence or in a state of non-existence? He is in a state of existence. Is the person who has attained Parinibbāna eternal? It should not be said thus... etc. He is in a state of non-existence. Is the person who has attained Parinibbāna annihilated? It should not be said thus... etc.

217. Puggalo kiṃ nissāya tiṭṭhatīti? Bhavaṃ nissāya tiṭṭhatīti. Bhavo anicco saṅkhato paṭiccasamuppanno khayadhammo vayadhammo virāgadhammo nirodhadhammo vipariṇāmadhammoti? Āmantā. Puggalopi anicco saṅkhato paṭiccasamuppanno khayadhammo vayadhammo virāgadhammo nirodhadhammo vipariṇāmadhammoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

217. Depending on what does a person subsist? He subsists depending on becoming. Is becoming impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is a person also impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, subject to change? It should not be said thus... etc.

218. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti? Āmantā[P 0.0062]. Hañci atthi koci sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

218. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’? Yes. But is there not someone who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands: ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling’? Yes. If there is someone who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands: ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’.

219. Na [M 0.0055] vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci dukkhaṃ [T 0.0076] vedanaṃ vediyamāno…pe… adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci adukkhamasukhaṃ [V 0.0062] vedanaṃ vediyamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

219. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’? Yes. But is there not someone who, while experiencing a painful feeling... while experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands: ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling’? Yes. If there is someone who, while experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands: ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,’ then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’.

220. Atthi koci sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānāti, sveva puggalo; yo sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti na pajānāti, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

220. Given that there is someone who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Is the one who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ the person, and the one who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, does not understand, ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ not a person? It should not be said thus...

Yo dukkhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno…pe… yo adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānāti, sveva puggalo; yo adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti na pajānāti, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the one who, while experiencing a painful feeling... while experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,’ that very person; and is the one who, while experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, does not understand, ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,’ not a person? It should not be said thus...

221. Atthi koci sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Aññā sukhā vedanā, añño sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “sukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aññā [P 0.0063] dukkhā vedanā…pe… aññā adukkhamasukhā vedanā, añño adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyamāno “adukkhamasukhaṃ vedanaṃ vediyāmī”ti pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0077] …pe….

221. Given that there is someone who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Is the pleasant feeling one thing, and the one who, while experiencing a pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a pleasant feeling,’ another? It should not be said thus... Is the painful feeling one thing... Is the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling one thing, and the one who, while experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands, ‘I am experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,’ another? It should not be said thus...

222. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci kāye kāyānupassī viharatīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci kāye kāyānupassī viharati, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

222. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’? Yes. But is there not someone who dwells contemplating the body in the body? Yes. If there is someone who dwells contemplating the body in the body, then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’.

223. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci vedanāsu…pe… citte… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharatīti[M 0.0056]? Āmantā. Hañci atthi [V 0.0063] koci dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, tena vata re vattabbe – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

223. Should it not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’? Yes. But is there not someone who dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena? Yes. If there is someone who dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’.

224. Atthi koci kāye kāyānupassī viharatīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Yo kāye kāyānupassī viharati, sveva puggalo; yo na kāye kāyānupassī viharati, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

224. Given that there is someone who dwells contemplating the body in the body, is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Is the one who dwells contemplating the body in the body the person, and the one who does not dwell contemplating the body in the body not a person? It should not be said thus...

Yo vedanāsu…pe… citte… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, sveva puggalo; yo na dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati, na so puggaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the one who dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena the person, and the one who does not dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena not a person? It should not be said thus...

225. Atthi koci kāye kāyānupassī viharatīti katvā tena ca kāraṇena puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Añño kāyo, añño kāye kāyānupassī viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aññā [P 0.0064] vedanā… aññaṃ cittaṃ… aññe dhammā, añño dhammesu dhammānupassī viharatīti? Na [T 0.0078] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

225. Given that there is someone who dwells contemplating the body in the body, is it for that reason that a person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. Is the body one thing, and the one who dwells contemplating the body in the body another? It should not be said thus... Are feelings one thing... Is the mind one thing... Are phenomena one thing, and the one who dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena another? It should not be said thus...

226. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

226. Is a person apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Suññato lokaṃ avekkhassu, mogharāja sadā sato;

Attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca ohacca (syā.), uhacca (ka.), evaṃ maccutaro siyā;

Evaṃ lokaṃ avekkhantaṃ, maccurājā na passatī”ti su. ni. 1125; cūḷani. 88 mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa.

“Look upon the world as empty, Mogharāja, ever mindful; having abandoned the view of self, thus you may cross beyond death. The King of Death does not see one who looks upon the world thus.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in the sense of a real and ultimate meaning’.

227. Puggalo avekkhatīti? Āmantā. Saha rūpena avekkhati, vinā rūpena avekkhatīti? Saha rūpena avekkhatīti. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vinā rūpena avekkhatīti, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

227. Does a person observe? Yes. Does one observe together with form, or without form? [If one says,] ‘One observes together with form,’ [is it then asked,] ‘Is that life-principle that body?’ It should not be said thus... [If one says,] ‘One observes without form,’ [is it then asked,] ‘Is the life-principle one thing and the body another?’ It should not be said thus...

228. Puggalo [M 0.0057][V 0.0064] avekkhatīti? Āmantā. Abbhantaragato avekkhati, bahiddhā nikkhamitvā avekkhatīti? Abbhantaragato avekkhatīti. Taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… bahiddhā nikkhamitvā avekkhatīti, aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

228. Does a person observe? Yes. Does one observe having gone within, or having gone outside? [If one says,] ‘One observes having gone within,’ [is it then asked,] ‘Is that life-principle that body?’ It should not be said thus... [If one says,] ‘One observes having gone outside,’ [is it then asked,] ‘Is the life-principle one thing and the body another?’ It should not be said thus...

229. Na [P 0.0065] vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthi puggalo [T 0.0079] attahitāya paṭipanno”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti.

229. Should it not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense'? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not false? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One: 'There is a person practicing for his own welfare'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.

230. Na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti a. ni. 1.162-169. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti.

230. Should it not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense'? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not false, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One: 'Bhikkhus, one person, arising in the world, arises for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, a person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.

231. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sabbe dhammā anattā”ti ma. ni. 1.356; dha. pa. 279 dhammapade. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

231. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not false, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One: 'All phenomena are not-self'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.'

232. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0066] bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “dukkhameva uppajjamānaṃ uppajjati, dukkhameva dukkhaṃ (saṃ. ni. 2.15) nirujjhamānaṃ nirujjhatīti na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati, aparappaccayaññāṇamevassa ettha hoti. Ettāvatā kho, kaccāna, sammādiṭṭhi hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 2.15. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ [T 0.0080] – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

232. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not false, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One: 'Only suffering, while arising, arises; only suffering, while ceasing, ceases. One does not doubt, one is not perplexed; herein, one's knowledge is independent of another. To this extent, Kaccāna, there is right view'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.'

233. Puggalo [M 0.0058][V 0.0065] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu vajirā bhikkhunī māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca –

233. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Did not the bhikkhunī Vajirā say this to Māra the Evil One:

“Kinnu sattoti paccesi, māra diṭṭhigataṃ nu te;

Suddhasaṅkhārapuñjoyaṃ, nayidha sattupalabbhati.

“Why do you believe in a ‘being’? Māra, is this your speculative view? This is a mere heap of formations; no being is apprehended here.”

“Yathā hi yathāpi (bahūsu) aṅgasambhārā, hoti saddo ratho iti;

Evaṃ khandhesu santesu, hoti sattoti sammuti sammati (syā. kaṃ.).

“Just as from an assemblage of parts, the word ‘chariot’ arises; so, when the aggregates exist, there is the convention ‘a being’.

“Dukkhameva hi sambhoti, dukkhaṃ tiṭṭhati veti ca;

Nāññatra dukkhā sambhoti, nāññaṃ dukkhā nirujjhatī”ti saṃ. ni. 1.171.

“Indeed, only suffering comes to be; suffering persists and passes away. Nothing other than suffering comes to be; nothing other than suffering ceases.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.'

234. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘suñño [P 0.0067] loko suñño loko’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘suñño loko’ti vuccatī”ti? “Yasmā kho, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, tasmā ‘suñño loko’ti vuccati. Kiñcānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā? Cakkhuṃ kho, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, rūpā suññā…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññaṃ… cakkhusamphasso suñño… yampidaṃ cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ [T 0.0081] sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, tampi suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, sotaṃ suññaṃ…pe… saddā suññā… ghānaṃ suññaṃ… gandhā suññā… jivhā suññā… rasā suññā… kāyo suñño… phoṭṭhabbā suññā… mano suñño… dhammā suññā… manoviññāṇaṃ suññaṃ… manosamphasso suñño… yampidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, tampi suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā. Yasmā kho, ānanda, suññaṃ attena vā attaniyena vā, tasmā [V 0.0066] ‘suñño loko’ti vuccatī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.85. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

234. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Did not the Venerable Ānanda say this to the Blessed One: '“The world is empty, the world is empty,” it is said, venerable sir. To what extent, venerable sir, is it said, “The world is empty”?' 'Because, Ānanda, it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, therefore it is said, “The world is empty.” And what, Ānanda, is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; forms are empty... eye-consciousness is empty... eye-contact is empty... and whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self. The ear is empty... sounds are empty... the nose is empty... odors are empty... the tongue is empty... tastes are empty... the body is empty... tangible objects are empty... the mind is empty... mental phenomena are empty... mind-consciousness is empty... mind-contact is empty... and whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self. Because, Ānanda, it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, therefore it is said, “The world is empty.”' Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.'

235. Puggalo [M 0.0059] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “attani vā, bhikkhave, sati ‘attaniyaṃ me’ti assā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Attaniye vā, bhikkhave, sati ‘attā me’ti assā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Attani ca, bhikkhave, attaniye ca saccato thetato anupalabbhiyamāne anupalabbhamāne (ma. ni. 1.244) yampidaṃ yamidaṃ (syā.) yampitaṃ (ma. ni. 1.244) diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ so loko so attā so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo, sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassāmīti – ‘nanvāyaṃ, bhikkhave, kevalo paripūro bāladhammo’”ti? “Kiñhi no siyā, bhante, kevalo hi, bhante, paripūro bāladhammo”ti [T 0.0082] ma. ni. 1.244. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

235. Is a person apprehended in the true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not false, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it said by the Blessed One: “Bhikkhus, if there were a self, would there be ‘what is mine’?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, if there were what is mine, would there be ‘my self’?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Bhikkhus, when a self and what belongs to a self are not apprehended as true and established, is not this viewpoint—‘This world is that self, and I, after death, will become permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change; I will remain just so for all eternity’—a completely and utterly foolish doctrine?” “What else could it be, venerable sir? It is indeed a completely and utterly foolish doctrine.” Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “A person is apprehended in the true and ultimate sense.”

236. Puggalo [P 0.0068] upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tayo me, seniya, satthāro santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame tayo? Idha, seniya, ekacco satthā diṭṭheva dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti, abhisamparāyañca attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti.

236. Is a person apprehended in the ultimate sense of reality? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not deceptive, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: “Seniya, there are these three teachers existing and present in the world. Which three? Here, Seniya, a certain teacher proclaims the self in the present life as true and established, and proclaims the self in the future life as true and established.

“Idha pana, seniya, ekacco satthā diṭṭheva hi kho dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti, no ca kho abhisamparāyaṃ attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti.

Furthermore, Seniya, here a certain teacher proclaims the self in this very life as true and established, but does not proclaim the self in the future life as true and established.

“Idha pana, seniya, ekacco satthā diṭṭhe ceva dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato na paññāpeti, abhisamparāyañca attānaṃ saccato thetato na paññāpeti.

Furthermore, Seniya, here a certain teacher does not proclaim the self as true and established in this very life, and does not proclaim the self as true and established in the life to come.

“Tatra, seniya, yvāyaṃ satthā diṭṭhe ceva dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti, abhisamparāyañca attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti – ayaṃ vuccati, seniya, satthā sassatavādo.

Among these, Seniya, the teacher who proclaims the self as true and established in this very life, and also proclaims the self as true and established in the life to come—this, Seniya, is called a teacher who is an eternalist.

“Tatra[M 0.0060][V 0.0067], seniya, yvāyaṃ satthā diṭṭheva hi kho dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti, no ca kho abhisamparāyaṃ attānaṃ saccato thetato paññāpeti – ayaṃ vuccati, seniya, satthā ucchedavādo.

Among these, Seniya, the teacher who proclaims the self as true and established in this very life, but does not proclaim the self as true and established in the life to come—this, Seniya, is called a teacher who is an annihilationist.

“Tatra, seniya, yvāyaṃ satthā diṭṭhe ceva dhamme attānaṃ saccato thetato [T 0.0083] na paññāpeti, abhisamparāyañca attānaṃ saccato thetato na paññāpeti – ayaṃ vuccati, seniya, satthā sammāsambuddho. Ime kho, seniya, tayo satthāro santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmi”nti pu. pa. 131 puggalapaññattiyaṃ, atthato ekaṃ. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

Among these, Seniya, the teacher who does not proclaim the self as true and established in this very life, and also does not proclaim the self as true and established in the life to come—this, Seniya, is called a teacher who is a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. These, Seniya, are the three teachers existing, being present in the world. Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense.’

237. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sappikumbho”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0069]. Atthi koci sappissa kumbhaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti.

237. Is a person apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not deceptive, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it spoken by the Blessed One: ‘A pot of ghee’? Yes. Is there anyone who makes a pot from ghee itself? It should not be said so… Therefore, it should not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense.’

238. Puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā saccavādī kālavādī bhūtavādī tathavādī avitathavādī anaññathavādīti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “telakumbho… madhukumbho… phāṇitakumbho… khīrakumbho… udakakumbho… pānīyathālakaṃ… pānīyakosakaṃ… pānīyasarāvakaṃ… niccabhattaṃ… dhuvayāgū”ti? Āmantā. Atthi kāci yāgu niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.…Pe…. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “puggalo upalabbhati saccikaṭṭhaparamatthenā”ti. (Saṃkhittaṃ)

238. Is a person apprehended in a true and ultimate sense? Yes. Is not the Blessed One a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is timely, a speaker of what is factual, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not deceptive, a speaker of what is not otherwise? Yes. Was it spoken by the Blessed One: ‘A pot of oil… a pot of honey… a pot of molasses… a pot of milk… a pot of water… a drinking bowl… a drinking cup… a drinking saucer… a perpetual alms-meal… a permanent rice-gruel’? Yes. Is there any rice-gruel that is permanent, constant, eternal, and of a nature not subject to change? It should not be said so… Therefore, it should not be said: ‘A person is apprehended in a true and ultimate sense.’ (Abbreviated)

Aṭṭhakaniggahapeyyālā, sandhāvaniyā upādāya;

Cittena pañcamaṃ kalyāṇaṃ, iddhisuttāharaṇena aṭṭhamaṃ.

The Eightfold Refutation, the Repetition Series, On Transmigration, and On Clinging; the fifth is on the Mind, then the Auspicious, Psychic Power, and the eighth is by Citing Suttas.

Saccikaṭṭhasabhāgānuyogo.

The Section on the Correspondence of the True Essence.

Puggalakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Person is concluded.

2. Parihānikathā

2. Discourse on Decline

1. Vādayuttiparihāni

1. Decline in the Course of the Argument

239. Parihāyati [T 0.0084][M 0.0061][V 0.0068] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sabbattha arahā arahattā parihāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbattha arahā arahattā parihāyatīti? Āmantā. Sabbattha arahato parihānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

239. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship in every existence? It should not be stated thus… Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship in every existence? Yes. Is there decline for an Arahant in every existence? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā[P 0.0070]. Sabbadā arahā arahattā parihāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbadā arahā arahattā parihāyatīti? Āmantā. Sabbadā arahato parihānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does an Arahant always decline from Arahantship? It should not be stated thus… Does an Arahant always decline from Arahantship? Yes. Is there always decline for an Arahant? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sabbeva arahanto arahattā parihāyantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbeva arahanto arahattā parihāyantīti? Āmantā. Sabbesaṃyeva arahantānaṃ parihānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Do all Arahants decline from Arahantship? It should not be stated thus… Do all Arahants decline from Arahantship? Yes. Is there decline for all Arahants? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Arahā arahattā parihāyamāno catūhi phalehi parihāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Declining from Arahantship, does an Arahant decline from the four fruits? It should not be stated thus…

Catūhi satasahassehi seṭṭhī seṭṭhittaṃ kārento satasahasse parihīne seṭṭhittā parihīno hotīti? Āmantā. Sabbasāpateyyā parihīno hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

A great merchant, having established his status as a great merchant with four hundred thousand, when one hundred thousand is lost, has he declined from his status as a great merchant? Yes. Has he declined from all his wealth? It should not be stated thus…

Catūhi [V 0.0069] satasahassehi seṭṭhī seṭṭhittaṃ kārento satasahasse parihīne bhabbo sabbasāpateyyā parihāyitunti? Āmantā. Arahā arahattā parihāyamāno [T 0.0085] bhabbo catūhi phalehi parihāyitunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

A great merchant, having established his status as a great merchant with four hundred thousand, when one hundred thousand is lost, is he liable to decline from all his wealth? Yes. An Arahant, declining from Arahantship, is he liable to decline from the four fruits? It should not be stated thus…

2. Ariyapuggalasaṃsandanaparihāni

2. Decline by Comparison with Noble Persons

240. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na [P 0.0071] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

240. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does a stream-enterer decline from the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati [M 0.0062] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does a once-returner decline from the fruit of once-returning? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does a non-returner decline from the fruit of non-returning? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a non-returner decline from the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a stream-enterer decline from the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a non-returner decline from the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a once-returner decline from the fruit of once-returning? It should not be stated thus…

Parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a once-returner decline from the fruit of once-returning? Yes. Does a stream-enterer decline from the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus…

Na [T 0.0086] parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Āmantā. Na parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a stream-enterer not decline from the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Does an Arahant not decline from Arahantship? It should not be stated thus…

Na [V 0.0070] parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Na parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a once-returner not decline from the fruit of once-returning? Yes. Does an Arahant not decline from Arahantship? It should not be stated thus…

Na parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Na parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a non-returner not decline from the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does an Arahant not decline from Arahantship? It should not be stated thus…

Na parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Āmantā. Na parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a stream-enterer not decline from the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Does a non-returner not decline from the fruit of non-returning? It should not be stated thus…

Na parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā[P 0.0072]. Na parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a once-returner not decline from the fruit of once-returning? Yes. Does a non-returner not decline from the fruit of non-returning? It should not be stated thus…

Na parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Āmantā. Na parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a stream-enterer not decline from the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Does a once-returner not decline from the fruit of once-returning? It should not be stated thus…

241. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Arahā arahattā parihāyamāno kattha saṇṭhātīti? Anāgāmiphaleti. Anāgāmī anāgāmiphalā parihāyamāno kattha saṇṭhātīti? Sakadāgāmiphaleti. Sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalā parihāyamāno kattha saṇṭhātīti? Sotāpattiphaleti. Sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā parihāyamāno puthujjanabhūmiyaṃ saṇṭhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

241. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Where does an Arahant, declining from Arahantship, become established? In the fruit of non-returning. Where does a non-returner, declining from the fruit of non-returning, become established? In the fruit of once-returning. Where does a once-returner, declining from the fruit of once-returning, become established? In the fruit of stream-entry. Does a stream-enterer, declining from the fruit of stream-entry, become established in the plane of a worldling? It should not be stated thus.

Ājānāhi [M 0.0063] niggahaṃ. Hañci arahā arahattā parihāyamāno anāgāmiphale saṇṭhāti, anāgāmī anāgāmiphalā parihāyamāno sakadāgāmiphale saṇṭhāti, sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalā parihāyamāno sotāpattiphale saṇṭhāti; tena vata re vattabbe – “sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā parihāyamāno puthujjanabhūmiyaṃ saṇṭhātī”ti.

Acknowledge the refutation. If an Arahant, declining from Arahantship, were to be established in the fruit of non-returning; a non-returner, declining from the fruit of non-returning, were to be established in the fruit of once-returning; a once-returner, declining from the fruit of once-returning, were to be established in the fruit of stream-entry—then indeed it should be said: 'A stream-enterer, declining from the fruit of stream-entry, is established in the plane of a worldling.'

Arahā arahattā parihāyamāno sotāpattiphale saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalassa anantarā arahattaṃyeva sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant, declining from Arahantship, become established in the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Does one realize Arahantship immediately after the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus…

242. Parihāyati [V 0.0071] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati [T 0.0087] sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa [P 0.0073] bahutarā kilesā pahīnā arahato vā sotāpannassa vāti? Arahato. Hañci arahato bahutarā kilesā pahīnā, parihāyati arahā arahattā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā”ti.

242. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does a stream-enterer decline from the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus… For whom are more defilements abandoned, for an Arahant or for a stream-enterer? For an Arahant. If more defilements are abandoned for an Arahant, and an Arahant declines from Arahantship, then indeed it should be said: “A stream-enterer declines from the fruit of stream-entry.”

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa bahutarā kilesā pahīnā arahato vā sakadāgāmissa vāti? Arahato. Hañci arahato bahutarā kilesā pahīnā, parihāyati arahā arahattā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalā”ti.

It should not be stated thus… For whom are more defilements abandoned, for an Arahant or for a once-returner? For an Arahant. Parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa bahutarā kilesā pahīnā anāgāmissa vā sotāpannassa vāti? Anāgāmissa. Hañci anāgāmissa bahutarā kilesā pahīnā, parihāyati anāgāmī anāgāmiphalā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā”ti.

Hañci sakadāgāmissa bahutarā kilesā pahīnā, parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā”ti.

It should not be stated thus… For whom are more defilements abandoned, for a once-returner or for a stream-enterer? For a once-returner. If more defilements are abandoned for a once-returner, and a once-returner declines from the fruit of once-returning, then indeed it should be said: ‘A stream-enterer declines from the fruit of stream-entry.’

244. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa adhimattā maggabhāvanā arahato vā sotāpannassa vāti? Arahato. Hañci arahato adhimattā maggabhāvanā, parihāyati arahā arahattā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā”ti.

244. Does an Arahant decline from Arahantship? Yes. Does a stream-enterer decline from the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be stated thus… For whom is the cultivation of the path more excellent, for an Arahant or for a stream-enterer? For an Arahant. If the cultivation of the path is more excellent for an Arahant, and an Arahant declines from Arahantship, then indeed it should be said: ‘A stream-enterer declines from the fruit of stream-entry.’

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa adhimattā satipaṭṭhānabhāvanā…pe… sammappadhānabhāvanā… iddhipādabhāvanā… indriyabhāvanā [T 0.0089]… balabhāvanā… bojjhaṅgabhāvanā arahato vā sotāpannassa vāti? Arahato. Hañci arahato adhimattā bojjhaṅgabhāvanā, parihāyati arahā arahattā; tena vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalā”ti.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Does a Stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of Stream-entry? It should not be so said… For whom is the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness more excellent… the cultivation of the right exertions… the cultivation of the bases of spiritual power… the cultivation of the spiritual faculties… the cultivation of the spiritual powers… the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment—for an Arahant or for a Stream-enterer? For an Arahant. If the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment is more excellent for an Arahant, and an Arahant falls away from Arahantship, then, indeed, it should be said: ‘A Stream-enterer falls away from the fruit of Stream-entry.’

Parihāyati [P 0.0075] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kassa adhimattā maggabhāvanā…pe… bojjhaṅgabhāvanā arahato vā sakadāgāmissa vāti? 245. Parihāyati [V 0.0073] anāgāmī anāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? 247. Arahatā dukkhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannena dukkhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

247. By the Arahant suffering has been seen; does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. By the Stream-enterer suffering has been seen; does the Stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of Stream-entry? It should not be so said…

Arahatā samudayo diṭṭho, parihāyati arahā arahattāti[T 0.0091]? Āmantā. Sotāpannena samudayo diṭṭho, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By the Arahant the origin has been seen; does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. By the Stream-enterer the origin has been seen; does the Stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of Stream-entry? It should not be so said…

Arahatā cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannena cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na [P 0.0077] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By the Arahant the four truths have been seen; does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. By the Stream-enterer the four truths have been seen; does the Stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of Stream-entry? It should not be so said…

Arahatā dukkhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāminā dukkhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Arahatā samudayo diṭṭho…pe… nirodho diṭṭho…pe… maggo diṭṭho…pe… cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāminā cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By the Once-returner the four truths have been seen; does the Once-returner fall away from the fruit of Once-returning? It should not be so said…

The origin has been seen by the non-returner... and so on... cessation has been seen... and so on... the path has been seen... and so on... the four truths have been seen. Does the non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes. The four truths have been seen by the stream-enterer. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

249. Suffering has been seen by the once-returner. Does the once-returner fall away from the fruit of once-returning? Yes. Suffering has been seen by the stream-enterer. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

Sakadāgāminā samudayo diṭṭho…pe… nirodho diṭṭho…pe… maggo diṭṭho…pe… cattāri [T 0.0093] saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannena cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Suffering has been seen by the non-returner... and so on... the four truths have been seen. Does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning? Yes. The four truths have been seen by the Arahant. Does the Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? This should not be said… and so on….

251. Arahato rāgo pahīno, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa sakkāyadiṭṭhi pahīnā, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

251. For the Arahant, lust has been abandoned. Does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the stream-enterer, identity view has been abandoned. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

Arahato [P 0.0080] rāgo pahīno, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa vicikicchā pahīnā…pe… sīlabbataparāmāso pahīno…pe… apāyagamanīyo rāgo pahīno [V 0.0077] …pe… apāyagamanīyo doso pahīno…pe… apāyagamanīyo moho pahīno, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant, lust has been abandoned. Does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the stream-enterer, doubt has been abandoned… and so on… clinging to rites and observances has been abandoned… and so on… lust leading to the lower realms has been abandoned… and so on… aversion leading to the lower realms has been abandoned… and so on… delusion leading to the lower realms has been abandoned. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

Arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno… māno pahīno… diṭṭhi pahīnā… vicikicchā pahīnā… thinaṃ thīnaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pahīnaṃ… uddhaccaṃ pahīnaṃ… ahirikaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, parihāyati arahā arahattāti[T 0.0095]? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa sakkāyadiṭṭhi pahīnā, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant, aversion has been abandoned… and so on… delusion has been abandoned… conceit has been abandoned… wrong view has been abandoned… doubt has been abandoned… sloth has been abandoned… restlessness has been abandoned… lack of shame has been abandoned… and so on… lack of moral dread has been abandoned. Does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the stream-enterer, identity view has been abandoned. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

Arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa vicikicchā pahīnā…pe… sīlabbataparāmāso pahīno…pe… apāyagamanīyo rāgo pahīno…pe… apāyagamanīyo doso [M 0.0069] pahīno…pe… apāyagamanīyo moho pahīno, parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant, lack of moral dread has been abandoned. Does the Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the stream-enterer, doubt has been abandoned… and so on… clinging to rites and observances has been abandoned… and so on… lust leading to the lower realms has been abandoned… and so on… aversion leading to the lower realms has been abandoned… and so on… delusion leading to the lower realms has been abandoned. Does the stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry? This should not be said… and so on….

Since for the non-returner identity view has been abandoned… and subtle ill-will has been abandoned, does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-return? It should not be said thus.

Since for the non-returner identity view has been abandoned… and subtle ill-will has been abandoned, does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-return? It should not be said thus.

258. Since for the once-returner identity view has been abandoned, does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-return? Yes. Since for the once-returner doubt has been abandoned… and gross ill-will has been abandoned, does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-return? Yes. Since for the non-returner identity view has been abandoned… and subtle ill-will has been abandoned, does the non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-return? It should not be said thus.

259. Sotāpannassa [T 0.0100] sakkāyadiṭṭhi pahīnā, na parihāyati sotāpanno sotāpattiphalāti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmissa sakkāyadiṭṭhi pahīnā…pe… oḷāriko byāpādo pahīno, na parihāyati sakadāgāmī sakadāgāmiphalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Since for the once-returner identity view has been abandoned… and gross ill-will has been abandoned, does the once-returner not fall away from the fruit of once-return? It should not be said thus.

260. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato anabhāvakato (sī.) āyatiṃ anuppādadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo [M 0.0073] tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, no ca vata re no vata re (syā. pī.) evamuparipi vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

260. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. But for the Arahant, has not lust been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and subject to non-arising in the future? Yes. If for the Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and subject to non-arising in the future, then it should indeed not be said, ‘An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.’

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno… māno pahīno… diṭṭhi pahīnā… vicikicchā pahīnā… thinaṃ pahīnaṃ… uddhaccaṃ pahīnaṃ… ahirikaṃ pahīnaṃ… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. But for the Arahant, has not aversion been abandoned… delusion abandoned… conceit abandoned… wrong view abandoned… doubt abandoned… sloth abandoned… restlessness abandoned… lack of shame abandoned… lack of moral dread abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and subject to non-arising in the future? Yes. If for the Arahant, lack of moral dread is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and subject to non-arising in the future, then it should indeed not be said that ‘an Arahant falls away from Arahantship.’

Parihāyati [T 0.0101] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvitoti[V 0.0082]? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. But for the Arahant, has not the path for the abandoning of lust been developed? Yes. If for the Arahant, the path for the abandoning of lust has been developed, then it should indeed not be said that ‘an Arahant falls away from Arahantship.’

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgappahānāya satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā…pe… sammappadhānā bhāvitā… iddhipādā bhāvitā… indriyā bhāvitā… balā bhāvitā… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0086] arahato rāgappahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Is it not so that for the abandoning of lust, the establishments of mindfulness... the right exertions... the bases of psychic power... the faculties... the powers... the factors of enlightenment have been developed by the Arahant? Yes. If indeed the factors of enlightenment have been developed by the Arahant for the abandoning of lust, then it should indeed not be said, 'An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.'

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Is it not so that for the abandoning of hate... for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, the path... the factors of enlightenment have been developed by the Arahant? Yes. If indeed the factors of enlightenment have been developed by the Arahant for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, then it should indeed not be said, 'An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.'

261. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo; dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ [T 0.0102] abhiññātaṃ[M 0.0074], pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

261. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Is it not so that the Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion, has done what was to be done, has laid down the burden, has attained his own goal, has destroyed the fetters of existence, is liberated by perfect knowledge, has lifted the cross-bar, has filled in the trench, has pulled up the pillar, is unbarred, is noble, has lowered the banner, has laid down the burden, is detached, is supremely victorious; for whom suffering is fully understood, the origin is abandoned, cessation is realized, the path is developed; what should be directly known has been directly known, what should be fully understood has been fully understood, what should be abandoned has been abandoned, what should be developed has been developed, what should be realized has been realized? Yes. If indeed the Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion... and what should be realized has been realized, then it should indeed not be said, 'An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.'

262. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? ( ) (āmantā) (ka.) Samayavimutto arahā arahattā parihāyati, asamayavimutto arahā arahattā na parihāyatīti. Samayavimutto arahā arahattā parihāyatīti? Āmantā. Asamayavimutto arahā arahattā parihāyatīti na parihāyatīti (ka.)? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

262. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? A timely-liberated Arahant falls away from Arahantship, but an untimely-liberated Arahant does not fall away from Arahantship. Does a timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Does an untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Asamayavimutto arahā arahattā na parihāyatīti? Āmantā. Samayavimutto arahā arahattā na parihāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Does a timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimuttassa [P 0.0087][V 0.0083] arahato rāgo pahīno, parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimuttassa arahato rāgo pahīno, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Since for the timely-liberated Arahant lust has been abandoned, does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Since for the untimely-liberated Arahant lust has been abandoned, does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimuttassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimuttassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the timely-liberated Arahant, hate is abandoned... lack of moral dread is abandoned; does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the untimely-liberated Arahant, lack of moral dread is abandoned; does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito, parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā [T 0.0103] arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the timely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust; does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the untimely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust; does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā…pe… sammappadhānā bhāvitā… iddhipādā bhāvitā… indriyā bhāvitā… balā bhāvitā… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya satipaṭṭhānā [M 0.0075] bhāvitā…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the timely-liberated Arahant, the establishments of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust... the right exertions have been developed... the bases of psychic power have been developed... the faculties have been developed... the powers have been developed... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the untimely-liberated Arahant, the establishments of mindfulness have been developed for the abandoning of lust... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimuttassa arahato dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimuttassa arahato anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
