For the timely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of hate... for the abandoning of lack of moral dread... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the untimely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lack of moral dread... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Samayavimutto arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano [P 0.0088] sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ[V 0.0084], parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Asamayavimutto arahā vītarāgo vītadoso [T 0.0104] vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

The timely-liberated Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion, has done what was to be done, has laid down the burden, has attained his own goal, has destroyed the fetters of existence, is liberated by perfect knowledge, has lifted the cross-bar, has filled in the trench, has pulled up the pillar, is unbarred, is noble, has lowered the banner, has laid down the burden, is detached, is supremely victorious; for whom suffering is fully understood, the origin is abandoned, cessation is realized, the path is developed; what should be directly known has been directly known, what should be fully understood has been fully understood, what should be abandoned has been abandoned, what should be developed has been developed, what should be realized has been realized; does the timely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. The untimely-liberated Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion... what should be realized has been realized; does the untimely-liberated Arahant fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

263. Asamayavimuttassa arahato rāgo pahīno, na parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Samayavimuttassa arahato rāgo pahīno, na parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

263. For the untimely-liberated Arahant, lust is abandoned; does the untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the timely-liberated Arahant, lust is abandoned; does the timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Asamayavimuttassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, na parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Samayavimuttassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, na parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the untimely-liberated Arahant, hate is abandoned... lack of moral dread is abandoned; does the untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the timely-liberated Arahant, lack of moral dread is abandoned; does the timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Asamayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, na parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Samayavimuttassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo [M 0.0076] bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, na parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the untimely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the timely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lust... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Asamayavimuttassa arahato dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, na parihāyati asamayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Samayavimuttassa [P 0.0089] arahato anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, na parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the untimely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of hate... for the abandoning of lack of moral dread... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For the timely-liberated Arahant, the path has been developed for the abandoning of lack of moral dread... the factors of enlightenment have been developed; does the timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Asamayavimutto arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, na parihāyati asamayavimutto [T 0.0105] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Samayavimutto arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, na parihāyati samayavimutto arahā arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The untimely-liberated Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion... has realized what is to be realized; does the untimely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. The timely-liberated Arahant is free from lust, free from hate, free from delusion... has realized what is to be realized; does the timely-liberated Arahant not fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus...

264. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Sāriputto thero parihāyittha arahattāti[V 0.0085]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Mahāmoggallāno mahāmoggalāno (ka.) thero… mahākassapo thero… mahākaccāyano mahākaccāno (ma. ni. 1.202 ādayo) thero… mahākoṭṭhiko mahākoṭṭhito (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) thero… mahāpanthako thero parihāyittha arahattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

264. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Did the elder Sāriputta fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus. Did the elder Mahāmoggallāna… the elder Mahākassapa… the elder Mahākaccāyana… the elder Mahākoṭṭhika… the elder Mahāpanthaka fall away from Arahantship? It should not be said thus.

Sāriputto thero na parihāyittha arahattāti? Āmantā. Hañci sāriputto thero na parihāyittha arahattā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Did the elder Sāriputta not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. If the elder Sāriputta did not fall away from Arahantship, then indeed it should not be said that, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Mahāmoggallāno thero… mahākassapo thero… mahākaccāyano thero… mahākoṭṭhiko thero… mahāpanthako thero na parihāyittha arahattāti? Āmantā. Hañci mahāpanthako thero na parihāyittha arahattā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Did the elder Mahāmoggallāna… the elder Mahākassapa… the elder Mahākaccāyana… the elder Mahākoṭṭhika… the elder Mahāpanthaka not fall away from Arahantship? Yes. If the elder Mahāpanthaka did not fall away from Arahantship, then indeed it should not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Ariyapuggalasaṃsandanaṃ.

Concordance with Noble Individuals.

3. Suttasādhanaparihāni

3. Falling Away, Proven by Sutta

265. Parihāyati [M 0.0077] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

265. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Uccāvacā hi paṭipadā paṭipādā (aṭṭha.), samaṇena pakāsitā;

Na pāraṃ diguṇaṃ yanti, nayidaṃ ekaguṇaṃ muta”nti su. ni. 719 suttanipāte.

“Indeed, high and low are the practices proclaimed by the Ascetic; they do not lead to the far shore twice, nor is this reached once.”

Attheva [P 0.0090] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “parihāyati arahā [T 0.0106] arahattā”ti.

Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Atthi chinnassa chediyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Is there something to be cut for one who has already cut? It should not be said thus.

Atthi chinnassa chediyanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is there something to be cut for one who has already cut? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Vītataṇho [V 0.0086] anādāno, kiccaṃ yassa na vijjati;

Chinnassa chediyaṃ natthi, oghapāso samūhato”ti.

“For one free from craving, without grasping, for whom no task remains; for one who has cut, there is nothing further to be cut; the snare of the flood is uprooted.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi chinnassa chediya”nti.

Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is something to be cut for one who has already cut.”

266. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Atthi katassa paticayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

266. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Is there an accumulation for what has been done? It should not be said thus.

Atthi katassa paticayoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is there an accumulation for what has been done? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Tassa sammā vimuttassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno;

Katassa paticayo natthi, karaṇīyaṃ na vijjati.

“For that bhikkhu, rightly liberated, with a peaceful mind, there is no accumulation for what has been done, nor is there anything that needs to be done.

“Selo yathā ekagghano, vātena na samīrati;

Evaṃ rūpā rasā saddā, gandhā phassā ca kevalā.

“As a solid rock mountain is not shaken by the wind, so too mere forms, tastes, sounds, smells, and touches,

“Iṭṭhā dhammā aniṭṭhā ca, nappavedhenti tādino;

Ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ vippamuttaṃ, vayaṃ cassānupassatī”ti mahāva. 244; a. ni. 6.55.

“And desirable and undesirable mental objects, do not agitate one who is steadfast; their mind is firm, liberated, and they constantly see its passing away.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [P 0.0091] hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi katassa paticayo”ti.

Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is an accumulation for what has been done.”

267. Na [T 0.0107][M 0.0078] vattabbaṃ – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṃvattanti. Katame pañca? Kammārāmatā, bhassārāmatā, niddārāmatā, saṅgaṇikārāmatā, yathāvimuttaṃ cittaṃ na paccavekkhati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā samayavimuttassa bhikkhuno parihānāya saṃvattantī”ti a. ni. 5.149. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi parihāyati arahā arahattāti.

267. Should it not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship”? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, these five things lead to the decline of a monk who is temporarily liberated. What five? Delight in work, delight in talk, delight in sleep, delight in company, and not reviewing the mind as it is liberated. These, monks, are the five things that lead to the decline of a monk who is temporarily liberated.” Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, an Arahant falls away from Arahantship.

Atthi arahato kammārāmatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have delight in work? It should not be said thus.

Atthi [V 0.0087] arahato kammārāmatāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have delight in work? Yes. Does an Arahant have lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire? It should not be said thus.

Atthi arahato bhassārāmatā, atthi arahato niddārāmatā, atthi arahato saṅgaṇikārāmatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have delight in talk? Does an Arahant have delight in sleep? Does an Arahant have delight in company? It should not be said thus.

Atthi arahato saṅgaṇikārāmatāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have delight in company? Yes. Does an Arahant have lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire? It should not be said thus.

268. Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Arahā arahattā parihāyamāno kiṃ pariyuṭṭhito parihāyatīti? Rāgapariyuṭṭhito parihāyatīti. Pariyuṭṭhānaṃ kiṃ paṭicca uppajjatīti? Anusayaṃ paṭicca uppajjatīti. Atthi arahato anusayāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

268. Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. When an Arahant is falling away from Arahantship, being assailed by what does he fall away? He falls away assailed by lust. Depending on what does that assault arise? It arises depending on a latent tendency. Does an Arahant have latent tendencies? It should not be said thus.

Atthi [T 0.0108][P 0.0092] arahato anusayāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato kāmarāgānusayo paṭighānusayo mānānusayo diṭṭhānusayo vicikicchānusayo bhavarāgānusayo avijjānusayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have latent tendencies? Yes. Does an Arahant have the latent tendency of sensual lust, the latent tendency of aversion, the latent tendency of conceit, the latent tendency of views, the latent tendency of doubt, the latent tendency of craving for existence, and the latent tendency of ignorance? It should not be said thus.

Dosapariyuṭṭhito parihāyatīti…pe… mohapariyuṭṭhito parihāyatīti…. Pariyuṭṭhānaṃ kiṃ paṭicca uppajjatīti? Anusayaṃ paṭicca uppajjatīti. Atthi arahato anusayāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

He falls away assailed by aversion... he falls away assailed by delusion... Depending on what does that assault arise? It arises depending on a latent tendency. Does an Arahant have latent tendencies? It should not be said thus...

Atthi arahato anusayāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato kāmarāgānusayo…pe… avijjānusayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have latent tendencies? Yes. Does an Arahant have the latent tendency of sensual lust... the latent tendency of ignorance? It should not be said thus.

Parihāyati [M 0.0079] arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Arahato arahattā parihāyamānassa kiṃ upacayaṃ [V 0.0088] gacchatīti? Rāgo upacayaṃ gacchatīti. Sakkāyadiṭṭhi upacayaṃ gacchatīti, vicikicchā upacayaṃ gacchatīti, sīlabbataparāmāso upacayaṃ gacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Doso upacayaṃ gacchatīti…pe… moho upacayaṃ gacchatīti, sakkāyadiṭṭhi upacayaṃ gacchatīti, vicikicchā upacayaṃ gacchatīti, sīlabbataparāmāso upacayaṃ gacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. For an Arahant falling away from Arahantship, what goes to accumulation? Does lust go to accumulation? Does personality view go to accumulation? Does doubt go to accumulation? Does grasping at precepts and practices go to accumulation? It should not be said thus. Does aversion go to accumulation... does delusion go to accumulation? Does personality view go to accumulation? Does doubt go to accumulation? Does grasping at precepts and practices go to accumulation? It should not be said thus.

Parihāyati arahā arahattāti? Āmantā. Arahā ācinatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā apacinatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā pajahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā upādiyatīti? Na [P 0.0093] hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā visinetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā ussinetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā [T 0.0109] vidhūpetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Arahā sandhūpetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant fall away from Arahantship? Yes. Does an Arahant accumulate? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant diminish? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant abandon? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant grasp? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant untangle? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant bind? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant shake off? It should not be said thus. Does an Arahant compose? It should not be said thus.

Nanu arahā nevācinati na apacinati apacinitvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā nevācinati na apacinati apacinitvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Is it not so that an Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but is established, having diminished? Yes. If an Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but is established, having diminished, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Nanu arahā neva pajahati na upādiyati pajahitvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā neva pajahati na upādiyati pajahitvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Is it not so that an Arahant neither abandons nor grasps, but is established, having abandoned? Yes. If an Arahant neither abandons nor grasps, but is established, having abandoned, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Nanu arahā neva visineti na ussineti visinitvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā neva visineti na ussineti visinitvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Is it not so that an Arahant neither untangles nor binds, but is established, having untangled? Yes. If an Arahant neither untangles nor binds, but is established, having untangled, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Nanu arahā neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “parihāyati arahā arahattā”ti.

Is it not so that an Arahant neither shakes off nor composes, but is established, having shaken off? Yes. If an Arahant neither shakes off nor composes, but is established, having shaken off, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, “An Arahant falls away from Arahantship.”

Parihānikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Decline is concluded.

3. Brahmacariyakathā

3. The Discourse on the Holy Life

1. Suddhabrahmacariyakathā

1. The Discourse on the Pure Holy Life

269. Natthi [M 0.0080][V 0.0089] devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Sabbe [P 0.0094] devā jaḷā elamūgā eḷamūgā (syā.) aviññū hatthasaṃvācikā nappaṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitānaṃ atthamaññātuṃ, sabbe devā na buddhe pasannā na dhamme [T 0.0110] pasannā na saṅghe pasannā, na buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsanti, na buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, na buddhena bhagavatā pañhe vissajjite attamanā, sabbe devā kammāvaraṇena samannāgatā kilesāvaraṇena samannāgatā vipākāvaraṇena samannāgatā assaddhā acchandikā duppaññā abhabbā niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṃ, sabbe devā mātughātakā pitughātakā arahantaghātakā ruhiruppādakā saṅghabhedakā, sabbe devā pāṇātipātino adinnādāyino kāmesumicchācārino musāvādino pisuṇavācā pharusāvācā samphappalāpino abhijjhāluno byāpannacittā micchādiṭṭhikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

269. Is there no living of the holy life among the devas? That is so. Are all devas dull, mute, ignorant, communicating by hand gestures, and unable to understand the meaning of what is well-spoken and ill-spoken? Are all devas without faith in the Buddha, without faith in the Dhamma, without faith in the Saṅgha? Do they not attend upon the Blessed One, the Buddha? Do they not ask the Blessed One, the Buddha, a question? When a question is answered by the Blessed One, the Buddha, are they not pleased? Are all devas possessed of the obstruction of kamma, possessed of the obstruction of defilements, possessed of the obstruction of result? Are they faithless, without wholesome desire, of little wisdom, and incapable of entering the fixed course, that which is rightness, in wholesome states? Are all devas matricides, patricides, killers of Arahants, shedders of the Buddha's blood, and creators of schism in the Saṅgha? Are all devas destroyers of life, takers of what is not given, those who engage in sexual misconduct, liars, slanderers, speakers of harsh speech, given to idle chatter, covetous, malevolent in mind, and holders of wrong view? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Nanu atthi devā ajaḷā anelamūgā viññū na hatthasaṃvācikā paṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitānaṃ atthamaññātuṃ, atthi devā buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā, buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ payirupāsanti, buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ pucchanti, buddhena bhagavatā pañhe vissajjite attamanā honti, atthi devā na kammāvaraṇena samannāgatā na kilesāvaraṇena samannāgatā na vipākāvaraṇena samannāgatā saddhā chandikā paññavanto bhabbā niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṃ, atthi devā na mātughātakā na pitughātakā na arahantaghātakā na ruhiruppādakā na saṅghabhedakā, atthi devā na pāṇātipātino na adinnādāyino na kāmesumicchācārino [V 0.0090] na musāvādino na pisuṇāvācā na pharusāvācā na samphappalāpino na abhijjhāluno [T 0.0111] abyāpannacittā sammādiṭṭhikāti? Āmantā.

Are there not devas who are not dull, not mute, intelligent, not communicating by hand gestures, and are capable of understanding the meaning of what is well-spoken and ill-spoken? Are there devas with faith in the Buddha, with faith in the Dhamma, with faith in the Saṅgha, who attend upon the Blessed One, the Buddha, ask the Blessed One, the Buddha, a question, and are pleased when the question is answered by the Blessed One, the Buddha? Are there devas not possessed of the obstruction of kamma, not possessed of the obstruction of defilements, not possessed of the obstruction of result, who have faith, have wholesome desire, are wise, and are capable of entering the fixed course, that which is rightness, in wholesome states? Are there devas who are not matricides, not patricides, not killers of Arahants, not shedders of the Buddha's blood, not creators of schism in the Saṅgha? Are there devas who are not destroyers of life, not takers of what is not given, not those who engage in sexual misconduct, not liars, not slanderers, not speakers of harsh speech, not given to idle chatter, not covetous, not malevolent in mind, and who are holders of right view? Yes, there are.

Hañci atthi devā ajaḷā anelamūgā viññū na hatthasaṃvācikā [P 0.0095] paṭibalā subhāsitadubbhāsitānaṃ atthamaññātuṃ…pe… atthi devā buddhe pasannā…pe… sammādiṭṭhikā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi devesu brahmacariyavāso”ti.

If there are devas who are not dull, not mute, intelligent, not communicating by hand gestures, and are capable of understanding the meaning of what is well-spoken and ill-spoken… and so on… if there are devas with faith in the Buddha… and so on… who are holders of right view, then it should not be said, O good sir, that ‘there is no living of the holy life among the devas’.

270. Atthi [M 0.0081] devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Atthi tattha pabbajjā muṇḍiyaṃ kāsāvadhāraṇā pattadhāraṇā, devesu sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti, paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti, sāvakayugaṃ uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

270. Is there living of the holy life among the devas? Yes, there is. Is there in that case going forth, shaving of the head, wearing of the ochre robe, and carrying of the bowl? Do Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas arise among the devas? Do Paccekabuddhas arise? Does a pair of disciples arise? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu pabbajjā natthīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha atthi pabbajjā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi pabbajjā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha atthi pabbajjā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi pabbajjā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yo pabbajati tasseva brahmacariyavāso, yo na pabbajati natthi tassa brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that there is no going forth among the devas, is there no living of the holy life among the devas? That is so. Is it that wherever there is going forth, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no going forth, there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that wherever there is going forth, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no going forth, there is no living of the holy life? That is so. Is it that only for one who goes forth there is the living of the holy life, and for one who does not go forth there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu muṇḍiyaṃ natthīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha atthi muṇḍiyaṃ tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi muṇḍiyaṃ natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha atthi muṇḍiyaṃ tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha [T 0.0112] natthi muṇḍiyaṃ natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yo muṇḍo hoti tasseva brahmacariyavāso, yo muṇḍo na hoti natthi tassa brahmacariyavāsoti? Na [P 0.0096] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that there is no shaving of the head among the devas, is there no living of the holy life among the devas? That is so. Is it that wherever there is shaving of the head, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no shaving of the head, there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that wherever there is shaving of the head, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no shaving of the head, there is no living of the holy life? That is so. Is it that only for one who is shaven there is the living of the holy life, and for one who is not shaven there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu kāsāvadhāraṇā natthīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha atthi kāsāvadhāraṇā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi kāsāvadhāraṇā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha atthi kāsāvadhāraṇā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi kāsāvadhāraṇā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yo kāsāvaṃ [V 0.0091] dhāreti tasseva brahmacariyavāso, yo kāsāvaṃ na dhāreti natthi tassa brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that there is no wearing of the ochre robe among the devas, is there no living of the holy life among the devas? That is so. Is it that wherever there is the wearing of the ochre robe, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no wearing of the ochre robe, there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that wherever there is the wearing of the ochre robe, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no wearing of the ochre robe, there is no living of the holy life? That is so. Is it that only for one who wears the ochre robe there is the living of the holy life, and for one who does not wear the ochre robe there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu pattadhāraṇā natthīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha atthi pattadhāraṇā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi pattadhāraṇā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha atthi pattadhāraṇā tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha natthi pattadhāraṇā natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā? Yo pattaṃ dhāreti tasseva brahmacariyavāso, yo pattaṃ na dhāreti natthi tassa brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that there is no carrying of an alms bowl among the devas, is there no living of the holy life among the devas? That is so. Is it that wherever there is the carrying of an alms bowl, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no carrying of an alms bowl, there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that wherever there is the carrying of an alms bowl, only there is the living of the holy life, and wherever there is no carrying of an alms bowl, there is no living of the holy life? That is so. Is it that only for one who carries an alms bowl there is the living of the holy life, and for one who does not carry an alms bowl there is no living of the holy life? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu [M 0.0082] sammāsambuddhā nuppajjantīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti[T 0.0113]? Āmantā. Yattha sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha sammāsambuddhā nuppajjanti natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha sammāsambuddhā nuppajjanti natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā[P 0.0097]. Lumbiniyā bhagavā jāto, bodhiyā mūle abhisambuddho, bārāṇasiyaṃ bhagavatā dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ; tattheva brahmacariyavāso, natthaññatra brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

‘Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas do not arise among the devas’; is there, for this reason, no living of the holy life among the devas? Yes. Is it that the holy life is lived only where Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas arise, and where Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas do not arise, the holy life is not lived? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that the holy life is lived only where Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas arise, and where Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas do not arise, the holy life is not lived? Yes. The Blessed One was born in Lumbinī, became perfectly enlightened at the foot of the Bodhi tree, and the Wheel of the Dhamma was set in motion by the Blessed One in Bārāṇasī; is it that the holy life is lived only there, and not elsewhere? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu paccekasambuddhā nuppajjantīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha paccekasambuddhā nuppajjanti natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha paccekasambuddhā nuppajjanti natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Majjhimesu janapadesu paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti, tattheva brahmacariyavāso, natthaññatra brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

‘Paccekabuddhas do not arise among the devas’; is there, for this reason, no living of the holy life among the devas? Yes. Is it that the holy life is lived only where Paccekabuddhas arise, and where Paccekabuddhas do not arise, the holy life is not lived? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that the holy life is lived only where Paccekabuddhas arise, and where Paccekabuddhas do not arise, the holy life is not lived? Yes. Paccekabuddhas arise in the central regions; is it that the holy life is lived only there, and not elsewhere? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Devesu sāvakayugaṃ nuppajjatīti, natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Yattha sāvakayugaṃ uppajjati tattheva brahmacariyavāso, yattha sāvakayugaṃ nuppajjati natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yattha sāvakayugaṃ uppajjati tattheva [T 0.0114] brahmacariyavāso, yattha sāvakayugaṃ nuppajjati natthi tattha brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Magadhesu [V 0.0092] sāvakayugaṃ uppannaṃ, tattheva brahmacariyavāso, natthaññatra brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

‘A pair of disciples does not arise among the devas’; is there, for this reason, no living of the holy life among the devas? Yes. Is it that the holy life is lived only where a pair of disciples arises, and where a pair of disciples does not arise, the holy life is not lived? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it that the holy life is lived only where a pair of disciples arises, and where a pair of disciples does not arise, the holy life is not lived? Yes. A pair of disciples arose in Magadha; is it that the holy life is lived only there, and not elsewhere? It should not be said thus… and so on….

271. Atthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā[P 0.0098]. Sabbadevesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

271. Is there the living of the holy life among the devas? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life among all the devas? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Atthi manussesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Sabbamanussesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there the living of the holy life among human beings? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life among all human beings? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Atthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Asaññasattesu devesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there the living of the holy life among the devas? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life among the non-percipient devas? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Atthi [M 0.0083] manussesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Paccantimesu janapadesu atthi brahmacariyavāso milakkhesu milakkhūsu (syā. ka.) aviññātāresu yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there the living of the holy life among human beings? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life in the border regions, among ignorant barbarians, where monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers have no access? It should not be said thus.

Atthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthīti. Asaññasattesu devesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāso, saññasattesu asaññasattesu (ka.) devesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there the living of the holy life among the devas? There are some among whom it exists, and some among whom it does not. Is it that among the non-percipient devas there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not, and that among the percipient devas there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not? It should not be said thus.

Devesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Kattha atthi, kattha natthīti? Asaññasattesu [T 0.0115] devesu natthi brahmacariyavāso, saññasattesu asaññasattesu (ka.) devesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti. Asaññasattesu devesu natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Saññasattesu asaññasattesu (ka.) devesu natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is it that among the devas there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not? Yes. Among whom is it lived, and among whom is it not? Among the non-percipient devas, the holy life is not lived; among the percipient devas, the holy life is lived. Is it that among the non-percipient devas the holy life is not lived? Yes. Is it that among the percipient devas the holy life is not lived? It should not be said thus.

Saññasattesu devesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Asaññasattesu [P 0.0099] devesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there the living of the holy life among the percipient devas? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life among the non-percipient devas? It should not be said thus.

Atthi [V 0.0093] manussesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthīti. Paccantimesu janapadesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāso milakkhesu aviññātāresu yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, majjhimesu janapadesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there the living of the holy life among human beings? There are some among whom it exists, and some among whom it does not. Is it that in the border regions—among ignorant barbarians where monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers have no access—there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not, and that in the central regions there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not? It should not be said thus.

Manussesu atthi yattha atthi, atthi yattha natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Kattha atthi, kattha natthīti? Paccantimesu janapadesu natthi brahmacariyavāso milakkhesu aviññātāresu yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, majjhimesu janapadesu atthi brahmacariyavāsoti. Paccantimesu janapadesu natthi brahmacariyavāso milakkhesu aviññātāresu yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānanti? Āmantā. Majjhimesu janapadesu natthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is it that among human beings there are some among whom the holy life is lived and some among whom it is not? Yes. Among whom is it lived, and among whom is it not? In the border regions—among ignorant barbarians where monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers have no access—the holy life is not lived; in the central regions, the holy life is lived. Is it that in the border regions—among ignorant barbarians where monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers have no access—the holy life is not lived? Yes. Is it that in the central regions the holy life is not lived? It should not be said thus.

Majjhimesu [M 0.0084] janapadesu [T 0.0116] atthi brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Paccantimesu janapadesu atthi brahmacariyavāso milakkhesu aviññātāresu yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there the living of the holy life in the central regions? Yes. Is there the living of the holy life in the border regions, among ignorant barbarians where monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers have no access? It should not be said thus.

Atthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tīhi, bhikkhave, ṭhānehi jambudīpakā manussā uttarakuruke ca manusse adhiggaṇhanti deve ca tāvatiṃse! Katamehi tīhi? Sūrā, satimanto, idha brahmacariyavāso”ti a. ni. 9.21. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [P 0.0100] hi natthi devesu brahmacariyavāsoti.

Is there the living of the holy life among the devas?" "Yes." "But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, in three respects the humans of Jambudīpa surpass the humans of Uttarakuru and the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. In which three? They are courageous, they are mindful, and here there is the living of the holy life'? Is there not such a discourse?" "Yes." "In that case, there is no living of the holy life among the devas."

Sāvatthiyaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha brahmacariyavāso”ti? Āmantā. Sāvatthiyaṃyeva brahmacariyavāso, natthi aññatra brahmacariyavāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Was it said by the Blessed One at Sāvatthī: 'Here is the living of the holy life'?'" "Yes." "Is the living of the holy life only at Sāvatthī, and not elsewhere?" "It should not be said thus."

272. Anāgāmissa puggalassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni appahīnāni, ito cutassa tattha upapannassa kuhiṃ phaluppattīti? Tattheva. Hañci anāgāmissa puggalassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni[V 0.0094], pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni appahīnāni, ito cutassa tattha upapannassa tahiṃ phaluppatti; no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi devesu brahmacariyavāso”ti.

272. For a non-returner, the five lower fetters are abandoned, and the five higher fetters are unabandoned. For one who has passed away from here and been reborn there, where does the attainment of fruition occur?" "Right there." "If, for a non-returner, the five lower fetters are abandoned and the five higher fetters are unabandoned, and for one who has passed away from here and been reborn there, the attainment of fruition occurs there; then it should not be said, 'There is no living of the holy life among the devas.'"

Anāgāmissa puggalassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni appahīnāni[T 0.0117], ito cutassa tattha upapannassa kuhiṃ bhāroharaṇaṃ, kuhiṃ dukkhapariññātaṃ, kuhiṃ kilesappahānaṃ, kuhiṃ nirodhasacchikiriyā, kuhiṃ akuppapaṭivedhoti? Tattheva. Hañci anāgāmissa puggalassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni appahīnāni, ito cutassa tattha upapannassa tahiṃ akuppapaṭivedho; no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi devesu brahmacariyavāso”ti.

For a non-returner, the five lower fetters are abandoned, and the five higher fetters are unabandoned. For one who has passed away from here and been reborn there, where is the laying down of the burden, where is the full understanding of suffering, where is the abandoning of defilements, where is the realization of cessation, where is the penetration of the unshakable?" "Right there." "If, for a non-returner, the five lower fetters are abandoned and the five higher fetters are unabandoned, and for one who has passed away from here and been reborn there, the penetration of the unshakable occurs there; then it should not be said, 'There is no living of the holy life among the devas.'"

Anāgāmissa puggalassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni appahīnāni, ito cutassa tattha upapannassa tahiṃ [M 0.0085] phaluppatti, tahiṃ bhāroharaṇaṃ, tahiṃ dukkhapariññātaṃ, tahiṃ kilesappahānaṃ, tahiṃ nirodhasacchikiriyā, tahiṃ akuppapaṭivedho; kenaṭṭhena vadesi – “natthi devesu brahmacariyavāso”ti? Handa hi anāgāmī puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti sacchikaroti (bahūsu).

For a non-returner, the five lower fetters are abandoned, and the five higher fetters are unabandoned. For one who has passed away from here and been reborn there, the attainment of fruition occurs there, the laying down of the burden occurs there, the full understanding of suffering occurs there, the abandoning of defilements occurs there, the realization of cessation occurs there, and the penetration of the unshakable occurs there. For what reason do you say, 'There is no living of the holy life among the devas'?" "It is because the non-returner, by means of the path developed here, realizes the fruit there."

2. Saṃsandanabrahmacariyakathā

2. Discourse on Correlating the Holy Life

273. Anāgāmī [P 0.0101] puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Sotāpanno puggalo tattha bhāvitena maggena idha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

273. Does the non-returner realize the fruit of Arahantship there by means of the path developed here?" "Yes." "Does the stream-enterer realize the fruit here by means of the path developed there?" "It should not be said thus."

Anāgāmī puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmī puggalo idha parinibbāyipuggalo idhaparinibbāyī (?) tattha bhāvitena maggena idha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does the non-returner realize the fruit there by means of the path developed here?" "Yes." "Does the once-returner, a person who attains Parinibbāna here, realize the fruit here by means of the path developed there?" "It should not be said thus."

Sotāpanno puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena idha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Anāgāmī puggalo tattha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na [T 0.0118] hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does the stream-enterer realize the fruit here by means of the path developed here?" "Yes." "Does the non-returner realize the fruit there by means of the path developed there?" "It should not be said thus."

Sakadāgāmī [V 0.0095] puggalo idha parinibbāyipuggalo idha bhāvitena maggena idha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Anāgāmī puggalo tattha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the once-returner, a person who attains Parinibbāna here, realize the fruit here by means of the path developed here?" "Yes." "Does the non-returner realize the fruit there by means of the path developed there?" "It should not be said thus… and so on."

Idha vihāya niṭṭhassa puggalassa maggo ca bhāvīyati, na ca kilesā pahīyantīti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa maggo ca bhāvīyati, na ca kilesā pahīyantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For a person who, having passed away from here, is completed, is the path developed but the defilements are not abandoned?" "Yes." "For a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, is the path developed but the defilements are not abandoned?" "It should not be said thus… and so on."

Idha vihāya niṭṭhassa puggalassa maggo ca bhāvīyati, na ca kilesā pahīyantīti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa…pe… arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa maggo ca bhāvīyati, na ca kilesā pahīyantīti? Na [P 0.0102] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For a person who, having passed away from here, is completed, is the path developed but the defilements are not abandoned?" "Yes." "For a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning… and so on… for a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship, is the path developed but the defilements are not abandoned?" "It should not be said thus… and so on."

Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa apubbaṃ acarimaṃ maggo ca bhāvīyati, kilesā ca pahīyantīti? Āmantā. Idha vihāya niṭṭhassa [M 0.0086] puggalassa apubbaṃ acarimaṃ maggo ca bhāvīyati, kilesā ca pahīyantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, are the path developed and the defilements abandoned simultaneously?" "Yes." "For a person who, having passed away from here, is completed, are the path developed and the defilements abandoned simultaneously?" "It should not be said thus."

Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa…pe… arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa apubbaṃ acarimaṃ maggo ca bhāvīyati, kilesā ca pahīyantīti? Āmantā. Idha vihāya niṭṭhassa puggalassa apubbaṃ acarimaṃ maggo ca bhāvīyati, kilesā ca pahīyantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe[T 0.0119].

For a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning… and so on… for a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship, are the path developed and the defilements abandoned simultaneously?" "Yes." "For a person who, having passed away from here, is completed, are the path developed and the defilements abandoned simultaneously?" "It should not be said thus."

Anāgāmī puggalo katakaraṇīyo bhāvitabhāvano tattha upapajjatīti? Āmantā. Arahā upapajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the non-returner, who has done what was to be done and has developed what was to be developed, reborn there?" "Yes." "Is an Arahant reborn?" "It should not be said thus."

Arahā upapajjatīti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato punabbhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is an Arahant reborn?" "Yes." "Is there further existence for an Arahant?" "It should not be said thus."

Atthi [V 0.0096] arahato punabbhavoti? Āmantā. Arahā bhavena bhavaṃ gacchati, gatiyā gatiṃ gacchati, saṃsārena saṃsāraṃ gacchati, upapattiyā upapattiṃ gacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there further existence for an Arahant?" "Yes." "Does an Arahant pass from existence to existence, from destination to destination, from the round of rebirth to the round of rebirth, from arising to arising?" "It should not be said thus."

Anāgāmī puggalo katakaraṇīyo bhāvitabhāvano anohaṭabhāro tattha upapajjatīti? Āmantā. Bhāroharaṇāya puna maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the non-returner—who has done what was to be done and has developed what was to be developed, but has not laid down the burden—reborn there?" "Yes." "Does he develop the path again for the sake of laying down the burden?" "It should not be said thus."

Anāgāmī [P 0.0103] puggalo katakaraṇīyo bhāvitabhāvano apariññātadukkho appahīnakileso asacchikatanirodho appaṭividdhākuppo tattha upapajjatīti? Āmantā. Akuppapaṭivedhāya puna maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the non-returner—who has done what was to be done and has developed what was to be developed, but for whom suffering is not fully understood, defilements are not abandoned, cessation is not realized, and the unshakable is not penetrated—reborn there? Yes. Does he develop the path again for the sake of penetrating the unshakable? It should not be said thus.

Anāgāmī puggalo katakaraṇīyo bhāvitabhāvano anohaṭabhāro tattha upapajjati, na ca bhāroharaṇāya puna maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Anohaṭabhāro ca tattha parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the non-returner—who has done what was to be done, has developed what was to be developed, and has not laid down the burden—reborn there, and does he not develop the path again for the sake of laying down the burden? Yes. And does one who has not laid down the burden attain Parinibbāna there? It should not be said thus.

Anāgāmī puggalo katakaraṇīyo bhāvitabhāvano apariññātadukkho appahīnakileso asacchikatanirodho appaṭividdhākuppo tattha upapajjati, na ca akuppapaṭivedhāya puna maggaṃ bhāvetīti[T 0.0120]? Āmantā. Appaṭividdhākuppo ca tattha parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Yathā migo sallena viddho dūrampi gantvā kālaṃ karoti, evamevaṃ anāgāmī puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena tattha phalaṃ sacchikarotīti.

Is the non-returner—who has done what was to be done, has developed what was to be developed, but for whom suffering is not fully understood, defilements are not abandoned, cessation is not realized, and the unshakable is not penetrated—reborn there, and does he not develop the path again for the sake of penetrating the unshakable? Yes. And does one for whom the unshakable is not penetrated attain Parinibbāna there? It should not be said thus. Just as a deer, shot by an arrow, having gone even a long distance, dies; even so, the non-returner realizes the fruit there by means of the path developed here.

Yathā [M 0.0087] migo sallena viddho dūrampi gantvā sasallova kālaṃ karoti, evamevaṃ anāgāmī puggalo idha bhāvitena maggena tattha sasallova parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Just as a deer, shot by an arrow, having gone even a long distance, dies still with the arrow in it; even so, does the non-returner, by means of the path developed here, attain Parinibbāna there still with the arrow of defilement in him? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Brahmacariyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Holy Life is concluded.

3. Odhisokathā

3. Discourse on Partial Abandonment

274. Odhisodhiso [V 0.0097] kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ [P 0.0104] vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ na sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ sotāpattiphalappatto sotāpattiphalaṃ patto (?) paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ sattakkhattuparamo, kolaṅkolo, ekabījī, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi na samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ [T 0.0121] vattabbe…pe….

274. Does one abandon defilements part by part? Yes. What does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals, and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a stream-enterer, and partly not a stream-enterer? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? Is one partly a seven-times-at-most returner, a family-to-family returner, or a one-seeder? Is one partly endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… and so on… in the Saṅgha… and so on… and with virtues cherished by the noble ones, and partly not endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ jahati, vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ na sotāpanno…pe… ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato, ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi na samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of origin, what does one abandon? One abandons identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals, and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a stream-enterer, and partly not a stream-enterer?… and so on… Is one partly endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, and partly not endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nirodhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ na sotāpanno…pe… ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato, ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi na samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of cessation, what does one abandon? One abandons doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a stream-enterer, and partly not a stream-enterer?… and so on… Is one partly endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, and partly not endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ na sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ [M 0.0088] sotāpattiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ sattakkhattuparamo, kolaṅkolo, ekabījī, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato, ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi na samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the path, what does one abandon? One abandons adherence to rites and rituals and the defilements associated with it. Is one partly a stream-enterer, and partly not a stream-enterer? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? Is one partly a seven-times-at-most returner, a family-to-family returner, or a one-seeder? Is one partly endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… and so on… in the Saṅgha… and so on… and with virtues cherished by the noble ones, and partly not endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones? It should not be said thus… and so on.

275. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya [V 0.0098] paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ jahati, oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ [T 0.0122] sakadāgāmiphalappatto sakadāgāmiphalaṃ patto (?) paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na [P 0.0105] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

275. What does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons coarse sensual desire, coarse ill will, and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a once-returner, and partly not a once-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of once-returning, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ jahati, oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of origin, what does one abandon? One abandons coarse sensual desire, coarse ill will, and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a once-returner, and partly not a once-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of once-returning, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nirodhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahati, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of cessation, what does one abandon? One abandons coarse ill will and, in part, the defilements associated with it. Is one partly a once-returner, and partly not a once-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of once-returning, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahati, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the path, what does one abandon? One abandons coarse ill will and the defilements associated with it. Is one partly a once-returner, and partly not a once-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of once-returning, obtained it, penetrated it, realized it, and dwells having accomplished it? Is one partly one who dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not? It should not be said thus… and so on.

276. Anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya [M 0.0089] paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ jahati, aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na anāgāmī[T 0.0123], ekadesaṃ anāgāmiphalappatto anāgāmiphalaṃ patto (?) paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ antarāparinibbāyī, upahaccaparinibbāyī, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, ekadesaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

276. What does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons subtle sensual desire; one abandons subtle ill will and, in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a non-returner, and partly not a non-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of non-returning, obtained it, attained it, realized it, dwells having attained it, dwells having touched it with the body, and partly dwells not having touched it with the body? Is one partly an antarāparinibbāyī, an upahaccaparinibbāyī, an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena [V 0.0099] kiṃ jahatīti? Aṇusahagataṃ [P 0.0106] kāmarāgaṃ jahati, aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na anāgāmī…pe… ekadesaṃ uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, ekadesaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the origin, what does one abandon? One abandons subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will, and in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly a non-returner, and partly not a non-returner?… and so on… Is one partly one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nirodhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ jahati, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na anāgāmī…pe… ekadesaṃ uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, ekadesaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of cessation, what does one abandon? One abandons subtle ill will and, in part, the defilements associated with it. Is one partly a non-returner, and partly not a non-returner?… and so on… Is one partly one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ anāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ antarāparinibbāyī, upahaccaparinibbāyī, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, ekadesaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the path, what does one abandon? One abandons the defilements associated with that. Is one partly a non-returner, and partly not a non-returner? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of non-returning, obtained it, attained it, realized it, dwells having attained it, dwells having touched it with the body, and partly dwells not having touched it with the body? Is one partly an antarāparinibbāyī, an upahaccaparinibbāyī, an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

277. Arahattasacchikiriyāya [T 0.0124] paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Rūparāgaṃ arūparāgaṃ mānaṃ uddhaccaṃ avijjaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ arahā, ekadesaṃ na arahā, ekadesaṃ arahattappatto [M 0.0090] arahattaṃ patto (?) paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā [P 0.0107] viharati, ekadesaṃ vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, (ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ,) ( ) (?) ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

277. What does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly an Arahant, and partly not an Arahant? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of Arahantship, obtained it, attained it, realized it, dwells having attained it, and dwells having touched it with the body; and partly one who dwells not having touched it with the body? Is one partly free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion, one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained one's own true goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, rightly liberated through final knowledge, one who has lifted the cross-bar, destroyed the moat, pulled up the pillar, is unbolted, a noble one, one who has lowered the banner, laid down the burden, is detached, a victor who has won a good victory? For that person, has suffering been fully understood, the origin abandoned, cessation realized, and the path developed? Has what was to be directly known been directly known, what was to be fully understood been fully understood, what was to be abandoned been abandoned, what was to be developed been developed, and what was to be realized been realized? Is it partly that what was to be realized has been realized, and partly that what was to be realized has not been realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena [V 0.0100] kiṃ jahatīti? Rūparāgaṃ arūparāgaṃ jahati, mānaṃ uddhaccaṃ avijjaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ arahā, ekadesaṃ na arahā…pe… ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the origin, what does one abandon? One abandons lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly an Arahant, and partly not an Arahant?… and so on… Is it partly that what was to be realized has been realized, and partly that what was to be realized has not been realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nirodhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Mānaṃ jahati, uddhaccaṃ avijjaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese ekadese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ arahā, ekadesaṃ na arahā [P 0.0108] …pe… ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na [T 0.0125] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of cessation, what does one abandon? One abandons conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and in part, the defilements associated with them. Is one partly an Arahant, and partly not an Arahant?… and so on… Is it partly that what was to be realized has been realized, and partly that what was to be realized has not been realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Uddhaccaṃ avijjaṃ tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese jahatīti. Ekadesaṃ arahā, ekadesaṃ na arahā, ekadesaṃ arahattappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ[M 0.0091], sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the path, what does one abandon? One abandons restlessness, ignorance, and the defilements associated with them. Is one partly an Arahant, and partly not an Arahant? Is one partly one who has attained the fruit of Arahantship, obtained it, attained it, realized it, dwells having attained it, and dwells having touched it with the body; and partly one who dwells not having touched it with the body? Is one partly free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion, one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained one's own true goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, rightly liberated through final knowledge, one who has lifted the cross-bar, destroyed the moat, pulled up the pillar, is unbolted, a noble one, one who has lowered the banner, laid down the burden, is detached, a victor who has won a good victory? For that person, has suffering been fully understood, the origin abandoned, cessation realized, and the path developed? Has what was to be directly known been directly known, what was to be fully understood been fully understood, what was to be abandoned been abandoned, what was to be developed been developed, and what was to be realized been realized? Is it partly that what was to be realized has been realized, and partly that what was to be realized has not been realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

278. Na vattabbaṃ – “odhisodhiso kilese jahatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

278. Should it not be said: ‘One abandons defilements selectively’? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Anupubbena medhāvī, thokaṃ thokaṃ khaṇe khaṇe;

Kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malamattano”ti dha. pa. 239 dhammapade.

‘Gradually, little by little, moment by moment, a wise person should remove their own defilements, as a smith removes the dross from silver.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “odhisodhiso kilese jahatī”ti.

Is there not such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, one does abandon defilements selectively.

Odhisodhiso [T 0.0126][P 0.0109][V 0.0101] kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Does one abandon defilements selectively? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Sahāvassa dassanasampadāya,

Tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti;

Sakkāyadiṭṭhī vicikicchitañca,

Sīlabbataṃ vāpi yadatthi kiñci;

Catūhapāyehi ca vippamutto,

Chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba abhabbo (sī. syā.) kātu”nti khu. pā. 6.10; su. ni. 233.

Simultaneously with his attainment of the perfection of vision, three things are abandoned: identity-view, doubt, and whatever clinging to rites and rituals there may be. He is freed from the four lower realms and is incapable of committing the six heinous acts.

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “odhisodhiso kilese jahatī”ti.

Is there not such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, it should not be said: ‘One abandons defilements selectively.’

Odhisodhiso kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti, saha dassanuppādā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi vicikicchā sīlabbataparāmāso”ti aṅguttaranikāye. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “odhisodhiso kilese jahatī”ti.

Does one abandon defilements selectively? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, at the time when the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arises in a noble disciple—that “Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation”—simultaneously with the arising of that vision, monks, three fetters are abandoned by the noble disciple: identity-view, doubt, and clinging to rites and rituals.’ Is there not such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, it should not be said: ‘One abandons defilements selectively.’

Odhisokathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Selective Abandonment is concluded.

4. Jahatikathā

4. The Discussion on Abandoning

1. Nasuttāharaṇakathā

1. The Discussion on the Non-citation of Discourses

279. Jahati [T 0.0127][M 0.0092] puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādanti? Āmantā. Accantaṃ jahati, anavasesaṃ jahati, appaṭisandhiyaṃ jahati, samūlaṃ jahati, sataṇhaṃ jahati, sānusayaṃ jahati, ariyena [V 0.0102] ñāṇena jahati, ariyena maggena jahati, akuppaṃ [P 0.0110] paṭivijjhanto jahati, anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

279. Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will? Yes. Does one abandon them completely, without remainder, irreversibly, with their root, with craving, with their underlying tendencies, by noble knowledge, by the noble path, while penetrating the unshakable, while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Vikkhambheti puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādanti? Āmantā. Accantaṃ vikkhambheti, anavasesaṃ vikkhambheti, appaṭisandhiyaṃ vikkhambheti, samūlaṃ vikkhambheti, sataṇhaṃ vikkhambheti, sānusayaṃ vikkhambheti, ariyena ñāṇena vikkhambheti, ariyena maggena vikkhambheti, akuppaṃ paṭivijjhanto vikkhambheti, anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto vikkhambhetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a worldling suppress sensual lust and ill will? Yes. Does one suppress them completely, without remainder, irreversibly, with their root, with craving, with their underlying tendencies, by noble knowledge, by the noble path, while penetrating the unshakable, while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Jahati anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca accantaṃ jahati, anavasesaṃ jahati…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto jahatīti? Āmantā. Jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca accantaṃ jahati, anavasesaṃ jahati…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon sensual lust and ill will, and does that person abandon them completely, without remainder… and so on… while realizing the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will, and does that person abandon them completely, without remainder… and so on… while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Vikkhambheti anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca accantaṃ vikkhambheti, anavasesaṃ vikkhambheti…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto vikkhambhetīti? Āmantā. Vikkhambheti [T 0.0128] puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca accantaṃ [V 0.0103] vikkhambheti, anavasesaṃ vikkhambheti [P 0.0111]…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto vikkhambhetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning suppress sensual lust and ill will, and does that person suppress them completely, without remainder… and so on… while realizing the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a worldling suppress sensual lust and ill will, and does that person suppress them completely, without remainder… and so on… while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca na accantaṃ jahati, na anavasesaṃ jahati…pe… na anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto jahatīti? Āmantā. Jahati anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca na accantaṃ jahati…pe… na anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will, but not completely, not without remainder… and so on… not while realizing the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon sensual lust and ill will, but not completely… and so on… not while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Vikkhambheti [M 0.0093] puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca na accantaṃ vikkhambheti, na anavasesaṃ vikkhambheti…pe… na anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto vikkhambhetīti? Āmantā. Vikkhambheti anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca na accantaṃ vikkhambheti, na anavasesaṃ vikkhambheti…pe… na anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikaronto vikkhambhetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a worldling suppress sensual lust and ill will, but not completely, not without remainder… and so on… not while realizing the fruit of non-returning? Yes. Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning suppress sensual lust and ill will, but not completely, not without remainder… and so on… not while realizing the fruit of non-returning? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādanti? Āmantā. Katamena maggenāti? Rūpāvacarena maggenāti. Rūpāvacaro maggo niyyāniko khayagāmī bodhagāmī apacayagāmī anāsavo asaṃyojaniyo aganthaniyo [T 0.0129] anoghaniyo ayoganiyo anīvaraṇiyo aparāmaṭṭho anupādāniyo asaṃkilesiyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Nanu rūpāvacaro maggo aniyyāniko na khayagāmī na bodhagāmī na apacayagāmī sāsavo saṃyojaniyo…pe… saṃkilesiyoti? Āmantā. Hañci rūpāvacaro maggo aniyyāniko na khayagāmī…pe… saṃkilesiyo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “jahati puthujjano rūpāvacarena maggena kāmarāgabyāpāda”nti.

Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will? Yes. By which path? By the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere. Is the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere one that leads out, leads to destruction, leads to awakening, leads to non-accumulation, is taintless, free from fetters, free from bodily ties, free from floods, free from yokes, free from hindrances, not wrongly grasped, free from clinging, and free from defilements? It should not be said thus. Is not the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere one that does not lead out, does not lead to destruction, does not lead to awakening, does not lead to non-accumulation, is subject to taints, connected to fetters… and so on… connected to defilements? Yes. If the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere is one that does not lead out, does not lead to destruction… and so on… connected to defilements, then, good sir, it should not be said that ‘a worldling abandons sensual lust and ill will by the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere.’

Jahati [P 0.0112] anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo anāgāmimaggena kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca maggo niyyāniko khayagāmī bodhagāmī apacayagāmī anāsavo…pe… asaṃkilesiyoti? Āmantā. Jahati puthujjano rūpāvacarena maggena kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca maggo niyyāniko khayagāmī bodhagāmī apacayagāmī anāsavo…pe… asaṃkilesiyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon sensual lust and ill will by the path of the non-returner, and is that path one that leads out, leads to destruction, leads to awakening, leads to non-accumulation, is taintless… and so on… and free from defilements? Yes. Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will by the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere, and is that path one that leads out, leads to destruction, leads to awakening, leads to non-accumulation, is taintless… and so on… and free from defilements? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Jahati puthujjano rūpāvacarena maggena kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca maggo aniyyāniko na khayagāmī na bodhagāmī na apacayagāmī sāsavo…pe… saṃkilesiyoti? Āmantā. Jahati anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo anāgāmimaggena kāmarāgabyāpādaṃ, so ca maggo aniyyāniko na khayagāmī na bodhagāmī na apacayagāmī sāsavo…pe… saṃkilesiyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a worldling abandon sensual lust and ill will by the path pertaining to the fine-material sphere, and is that path one that does not lead out, does not lead to destruction, does not lead to awakening, does not lead to non-accumulation, is subject to taints… and so on… and is connected to defilements? Yes. Does a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon sensual lust and ill will by the path of the non-returner, and is that path one that does not lead out, does not lead to destruction, does not lead to awakening, does not lead to non-accumulation, is subject to taints… and so on… and is connected to defilements? It should not be said thus… and so on….

280. Puthujjano [T 0.0130] kāmesu vītarāgo saha dhammābhisamayā anāgāmiphale saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Arahatte saṇṭhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

280. Does an ordinary person, free from lust for sensual pleasures, become established in the fruit of non-returning simultaneously with the breakthrough to the Dhamma? Yes. Does one become established in Arahantship? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Puthujjano [M 0.0094] kāmesu vītarāgo saha dhammābhisamayā anāgāmiphale saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ tayo magge bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an ordinary person, free from lust for sensual pleasures, become established in the fruit of non-returning simultaneously with the breakthrough to the Dhamma? Yes. Does one simultaneously develop the three paths? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Apubbaṃ [V 0.0104] acarimaṃ tayo magge bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one simultaneously develop the three paths? Yes. Does one simultaneously realize the three fruits of recluseship? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇaṃ phassānaṃ tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ tissannaṃ saññānaṃ tissannaṃ cetanānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ cittānaṃ tissannaṃ saddhānaṃ [P 0.0113] tiṇṇaṃ vīriyānaṃ tissannaṃ satīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ samādhīnaṃ tissannaṃ paññānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one simultaneously realize the three fruits of recluseship? Yes. Is there a confluence of three contacts, three feelings, three perceptions, three volitions, three consciousnesses, three faiths, three energies, three mindfulnesses, three concentrations, and three wisdoms? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Puthujjano kāmesu vītarāgo saha dhammābhisamayā anāgāmiphale saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a worldling, free from lust for sensual pleasures, established in the fruit of non-return together with the realization of the Dhamma? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sakadāgāmimaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Katamena maggenāti? Anāgāmimaggenāti. Anāgāmimaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
