By the path of the once-returner? It should not be said thus. By which path? By the path of the non-returner. By the path of the non-returner, does one abandon identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals? It should not be said thus… and so on.

2. Suttāharaṇakathā

2. The Discourse on Citing Suttas

281. Anāgāmimaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānā sotāpattiphalaṃ [T 0.0131] vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānā sotāpattiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgāmimaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ jahatī”ti. Anāgāmimaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

281. Does one abandon identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals by the path of the non-returner? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said that the fruit of stream-entry is attained by abandoning the three fetters? Yes. If the fruit of stream-entry is attained by abandoning the three fetters, then it should not be said that one abandons identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals by the path of the non-returner. Does one abandon coarse sensual desire and coarse ill will by the path of the non-returner? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Anāgāmimaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ tanubhāvā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ tanubhāvā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgāmimaggena [P 0.0114] oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatī”ti.

Does one abandon coarse sensual desire and coarse ill will by the path of the non-returner? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said that the fruit of the once-returner is attained by the attenuation of sensual desire and ill will? Yes. If the fruit of the once-returner is attained by the attenuation of sensual desire and ill will, then it should not be said that one abandons coarse sensual desire and coarse ill will by the path of the non-returner.

Puthujjano [V 0.0105] kāmesu vītarāgo saha dhammābhisamayā anāgāmiphale saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Ye keci dhammaṃ abhisamenti, sabbe te saha dhammābhisamayā anāgāmiphale saṇṭhahantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a worldling, free from lust for sensual pleasures, established in the fruit of non-return together with the realization of the Dhamma? Yes. Do all those who realize the Dhamma become established in the fruit of non-return together with the realization of the Dhamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Na [M 0.0095] vattabbaṃ – “jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpāda”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Should it not be said: ‘A worldling abandons sensual desire and ill will’? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said:

“Ahesuṃ te ahiṃsakā (a. ni. 6.54) atītaṃse, cha satthāro yasassino;

Nirāmagandhā karuṇedhimuttā karuṇādhimuttā (sī. ka.), kāmasaṃyojanātigā.

“In the past there were those six glorious teachers, free from the stench of lust, intent on compassion, who had gone beyond the fetter of sensuality.

“Kāmarāgaṃ virājetvā, brahmalokūpagā ahu;

Ahesuṃ sāvakā tesaṃ, anekāni satānipi.

Having become dispassionate towards sensual passion, they went to the Brahma-world; and their disciples numbered many hundreds.

“Nirāmagandhā karuṇedhimuttā, kāmasaṃyojanātigā;

Kāmarāgaṃ virājetvā, brahmalokūpagā ahū”ti a. ni. 6.54.

Free from the stench of lust, intent on compassion, who had gone beyond the fetter of sensuality; having become dispassionate towards sensual passion, they went to the Brahma-world.”

Attheva [T 0.0132] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādanti.

Is there not indeed a sutta? Yes. Therefore, a worldling abandons sensual desire and ill will.

Jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpādanti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0115] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so hi nāma, bhikkhave, sunetto satthā evaṃ dīghāyuko samāno evaṃ ciraṭṭhitiko aparimutto ahosi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi aparimutto dukkhasmāti vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Ariyassa sīlassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā, ariyassa samādhissa, ariyāya paññāya, ariyāya vimuttiyā ananubodhā appaṭivedhā. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ sīlaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, ariyo samādhi anubuddho paṭividdho, ariyā paññā anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ariyā vimutti anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthi dāni punabbhavoti.

Does a worldling abandon sensual desire and ill will? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Indeed, monks, that teacher Sunetta, though being so long-lived and so long-enduring, was not freed from birth, aging, death, sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs—I say he was not freed from suffering. For what reason? Because of not awakening to and not penetrating four things. Which four? Because of not awakening to and not penetrating noble virtue, noble concentration, noble wisdom, and noble liberation. This noble virtue, monks, has been awakened to and penetrated; noble concentration has been awakened to and penetrated; noble wisdom has been awakened to and penetrated; noble liberation has been awakened to and penetrated. Craving for existence is cut off, the cord leading to existence is destroyed, now there is no new existence.”

“Sīlaṃ [V 0.0106] samādhi paññā ca, vimutti ca anuttarā;

Anubuddhā ime dhammā, gotamena yasassinā.

“Virtue, concentration, wisdom, and unsurpassed liberation: these dhammas were awakened to by the glorious Gotama.

“Iti buddho abhiññāya, dhammamakkhāsi bhikkhunaṃ;

Dukkhassantakaro satthā, cakkhumā parinibbuto”ti a. ni. 7.66.

“Thus the Buddha, having known by special knowledge, taught the Dhamma to the monks; the Teacher, the ender of suffering, the one with the eye, has attained final Nibbāna.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “jahati puthujjano kāmarāgabyāpāda”nti.

Is there not indeed a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “A worldling abandons sensual desire and ill will.”

Jahatikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Abandoning is concluded.

5. Sabbamatthītikathā

5. The Discussion on ‘Everything Exists’

1. Vādayutti

1. The Mode of Reasoning

282. Sabbamatthīti[T 0.0133][M 0.0096]? Āmantā. Sabbattha sabbamatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Sabbadā sabbamatthīti? Na [P 0.0116] hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Sabbena sabbaṃ sabbamatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Sabbesu sabbamatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Ayoganti katvā sabbamatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Yampi natthi, tampatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sabbamatthīti? Āmantā. Sabbamatthīti yā diṭṭhi sā diṭṭhi micchādiṭṭhīti, yā diṭṭhi sā diṭṭhi sammādiṭṭhīti, hevamatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. (Saṃkhittaṃ). Vādayutti.

282. Does everything exist? Yes. Does everything exist in every place? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Does everything exist at all times? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Does everything exist in every way? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Does everything exist in all things? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Is everything existent by way of non-association? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Does that which is non-existent also exist? It should not be said thus. Does everything exist? Yes. Is the view ‘everything exists’ wrong view, or is it right view? It should not be said thus. (Abbreviated). The Mode of Reasoning.

2. Kālasaṃsandanā

2. Conjunction of Times

283. Atītaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ atthī”ti.

283. Does the past exist? Yes. But is not the past ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? Yes. If the past is ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished, then truly it should not be said, “The past exists.”

Anāgataṃ [V 0.0107] atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ [P 0.0117] anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgataṃ atthī”ti.

Does the future exist? Yes. But is not the future unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? Yes. If the future is unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested, then truly it should not be said, “The future exists.”

Paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ aniruddhaṃ avigataṃ avipariṇataṃ na atthaṅgataṃ na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ aniruddhaṃ [T 0.0134] avigataṃ avipariṇataṃ na atthaṅgataṃ na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ atthi anāgataṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the present exist—the present that is unceased, undeparted, unchanged, not disappeared, not utterly vanished? Yes. Does the past exist—the past that is unceased, undeparted, unchanged, not disappeared, not utterly vanished? It should not be said thus… Does the present exist—the present that is born, come to be, produced, arisen, newly produced, manifested? Yes. Does the future exist—the future that is born, come to be, produced, arisen, newly produced, manifested? It should not be said thus…

Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ atthi anāgataṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ [M 0.0097] asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does the past exist—the past that is ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? Yes. Does the present exist—the present that is ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? It should not be said thus… Does the future exist—the future that is unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? Yes. Does the present exist—the present that is unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? It should not be said thus.

284. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ rūpaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ rūpaṃ niruddhaṃ…pe… abbhatthaṅgataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthī”ti.

284. Does past form exist? Yes. But is not past form ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? Yes. If past form is ceased… and utterly vanished, then truly it should not be said, “Past form exists.”

Anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0118] anāgataṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ…pe… apātubhūtaṃ, no ca vata [T 0.0135] re vattabbe – “anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthī”ti.

Does future form exist? Yes. But is not future form unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? Yes. If future form is unborn… and unmanifested, then truly it should not be said, “Future form exists.”

Paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ aniruddhaṃ avigataṃ avipariṇataṃ na atthaṅgataṃ na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ aniruddhaṃ avigataṃ avipariṇataṃ na atthaṅgataṃ na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does present form exist—present form that is unceased, undeparted, unchanged, not disappeared, not utterly vanished? Yes. Does past form exist—past form that is unceased, undeparted, unchanged, not disappeared, not utterly vanished? It should not be said thus.

Paccuppannaṃ [V 0.0108] rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthi anāgataṃ rūpaṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ sañjātaṃ nibbattaṃ abhinibbattaṃ pātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does present form exist—present form that is born, come to be, produced, arisen, newly produced, manifested? Yes. Does future form exist—future form that is born, come to be, produced, arisen, newly produced, manifested? It should not be said thus.

Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does past form exist—past form that is ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? Yes. Does present form exist—present form that is ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? It should not be said thus.

Anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthi anāgataṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does future form exist—future form that is unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? Yes. Does present form exist—present form that is unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? It should not be said thus.

Atītā vedanā atthi…pe… saññā atthi, saṅkhārā atthi, viññāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā[P 0.0119]. Hañci [T 0.0136] atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ niruddhaṃ…pe… abbhatthaṅgataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthī”ti.

Does past feeling exist? … Does past perception exist? Do past formations exist? Does past consciousness exist? Yes. But is not past consciousness ceased, gone, changed, disappeared, and utterly vanished? Yes. If past consciousness is ceased… and utterly vanished, then truly it should not be said, “Past consciousness exists.”

Anāgataṃ [M 0.0098] viññāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ…pe… apātubhūtaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ atthī”ti.

Does future consciousness exist? Yes. But is not future consciousness unborn, unbecome, unproduced, unarisen, not newly produced, unmanifested? Yes. If future consciousness is unborn… and unmanifested, then truly it should not be said, “Future consciousness exists.”

Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniruddhaṃ…pe… na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniruddhaṃ…pe… na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does present consciousness exist—present consciousness that is unceased… not utterly vanished? Yes. Does past consciousness exist—past consciousness that is unceased… not utterly vanished? It should not be said thus.

Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ…pe… pātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ…pe… pātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does present consciousness exist—present consciousness that is born… manifested? Yes. Does future consciousness exist—future consciousness that is born… manifested? It should not be said thus.

Atītaṃ [V 0.0109] viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ niruddhaṃ…pe… abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ niruddhaṃ…pe… abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ…pe… apātubhūtanti? Āmantā.

Does past consciousness exist—past consciousness that is ceased… utterly vanished? Yes. Does present consciousness exist—present consciousness that is ceased… utterly vanished? It should not be said thus. Does future consciousness exist—future consciousness that is unborn… unmanifested? Yes.

Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ [T 0.0137] viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ…pe… apātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does present consciousness exist—present consciousness that is unborn… unmanifested? It should not be said thus.

285. “Paccuppannanti vā rūpa”nti vā, “rūpanti vā paccuppanna”nti vā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ appiyaṃ karitvā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ [P 0.0120] rūpaṃ nirujjhamānaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Rūpabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

285. Is it 'the present' or 'form,' or 'form' or 'the present'? Having treated present form as inseparable, are these of one meaning, the same, of equal share, of like kind? Yes. Does present form, while ceasing, abandon its state of being present? Yes. Does it abandon its state of being form? It should not be said thus...

“Paccuppannanti vā rūpa”nti vā, “rūpanti vā paccuppanna”nti vā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ appiyaṃ karitvā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ nirujjhamānaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is it 'the present' or 'form,' or 'form' or 'the present'? Having treated present form as inseparable, are these of one meaning, the same, of equal share, of like kind? Yes. Does present form, while ceasing, not abandon its state of being form? Yes. Does it not abandon its state of being present? It should not be said thus...

“Odātanti vā vattha”nti vā, “vatthanti vā odāta”nti vā odātaṃ vatthaṃ appiyaṃ karitvā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Āmantā. Odātaṃ vatthaṃ rajjamānaṃ odātabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Vatthabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is it 'white' or 'cloth,' or 'cloth' or 'white'? Having treated the white cloth as inseparable, are these of one meaning, the same, of equal share, of like kind? Yes. Does the white cloth, while being dyed, abandon its state of being white? Yes. Does it abandon its state of being cloth? It should not be said thus.

“Odātanti [M 0.0099] vā vattha”nti vā, “vatthanti vā odāta”nti vā odātaṃ vatthaṃ appiyaṃ karitvā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Āmantā. Odātaṃ vatthaṃ rajjamānaṃ vatthabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Odātabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.…Pe….

Is it 'white' or 'cloth,' or 'cloth' or 'white'? Having treated the white cloth as inseparable, are these of one meaning, the same, of equal share, of like kind? Yes. Does the white cloth, while being dyed, not abandon its state of being cloth? Yes. Does it not abandon its state of being white? It should not be said thus...

286. Rūpaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ [T 0.0138] avipariṇāmadhammanti[V 0.0110]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Nanu rūpaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahatīti rūpaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0121] rūpaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahatī”ti.

286. Does form not abandon its state of being form? Yes. Is form permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus. Is it not so that, since form does not abandon its state of being form, form is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? Yes. If form is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature, then it cannot rightly be said, 'Form does not abandon its state of being form.'

Nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahatīti nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahatīti na jahati (sī. ka.) rūpaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ rūpabhāvaṃ na jahati rūpaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati nibbānaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that Nibbāna does not abandon its state of being Nibbāna, is it permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? Yes. Given that form does not abandon its state of being form, is it permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus... Given that form does not abandon its state of being form, is it impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? Yes. Given that Nibbāna does not abandon its state of being Nibbāna, is it impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ atthi anāgataṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that the past exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Given that the future exists, does it not abandon its state of being future? It should not be said thus. Given that the past exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Given that the present exists, does it not abandon its state of being present? It should not be said thus...

Anāgataṃ atthi anāgataṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā? Āmantā. Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that the future exists, does it abandon its state of being future? Yes. Given that the past exists, does it abandon its state of being past? It should not be said thus...

Paccuppannaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā? Āmantā. Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā? Na hevaṃ [T 0.0139] vattabbe.

Given that the present exists, does it abandon its state of being present? Yes. Given that the past exists, does it abandon its state of being past? It should not be said thus.

Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu [P 0.0122] atītaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatī”ti.

Given that the past exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Is the past permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus... Is it not so that the past is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? Yes. If the past is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature, then it cannot rightly be said: 'The past exists and does not abandon its state of being past.'

Nibbānaṃ [M 0.0100] atthi nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahatīti nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti[V 0.0111]? Āmantā. Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti atītaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that Nibbāna exists and does not abandon its state of being Nibbāna, is it permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? Yes. Given that the past exists and does not abandon its state of being past, is it permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ atthi atītaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahati atītaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ atthi nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati nibbānaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that the past exists and does not abandon its state of being past, is it impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? Yes. Given that Nibbāna exists and does not abandon its state of being Nibbāna, is it impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? It should not be said thus...

287. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthi anāgataṃ rūpaṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

287. Given that past form exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Given that future form exists, does it not abandon its state of being future? It should not be said thus... Given that past form exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Given that present form exists, does it not abandon its state of being present? It should not be said thus...

Anāgataṃ rūpaṃ atthi anāgataṃ rūpaṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva[T 0.0140]? Āmantā. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that future form exists, does it abandon its state of being future? Yes. Given that past form exists, does it abandon its state of being past? It should not be said thus...

Paccuppannaṃ [P 0.0123] rūpaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva? Āmantā. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Given that present form exists, does it abandon its state of being present? Yes. Given that past form exists, does it abandon its state of being past? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atītaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatī”ti.

Given that past form exists, does it not abandon its state of being past? Yes. Is past form permanent, stable, eternal, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus… Is it not so that past form is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature? Yes. If past form is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and of a changing nature, then it cannot rightly be said: 'Past form exists; past form does not abandon its state of being past.'

Nibbānaṃ atthi nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati na jahatīti (?) purimapañhehi saṃsandetabbaṃ nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahati na jahatīti (?) purimañhehi saṃsandetabbaṃ atītaṃ rūpaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does Nibbāna exist, does Nibbāna not abandon its state as Nibbāna, and is Nibbāna permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change? Yes. Does past material form exist, does past material form not abandon its state as past, and is past material form permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change? This should not be so said…

Atītaṃ [M 0.0101][V 0.0112] rūpaṃ atthi atītaṃ rūpaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahati atītaṃ rūpaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ atthi nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati nibbānaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does past material form exist, does past material form not abandon its state as past, and is past material form impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change? Yes. Does Nibbāna exist, does Nibbāna not abandon its state as Nibbāna, and is Nibbāna impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change? This should not be so said…

Atītā vedanā atthi… atītā saññā atthi… atītā [T 0.0141] saṅkhārā atthi… atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ [P 0.0124] viññāṇaṃ atthi anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does past feeling exist?… Does past perception exist?… Do past volitional formations exist?… Does past consciousness exist, and does it not abandon its state as past? Yes. Does future consciousness exist, and does it not abandon its state as future? This should not be so said… Does past consciousness exist, and does it not abandon its state as past? Yes. Does present consciousness exist, and does it not abandon its state as present? This should not be so said…

Anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi anāgataṃ viññāṇaṃ anāgatabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does future consciousness exist, and does it abandon its state as future? Yes. Does past consciousness exist, and does it abandon its state as past? This should not be so said…

Paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi paccuppannaṃ viññāṇaṃ paccuppannabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva? Āmantā. Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ jahatīti na jahatīti (bahūsu) anulomapañhoyeva? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does present consciousness exist, and does it abandon its state as present? Yes. Does past consciousness exist, and does it abandon its state as past? This should not be so said…

Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahatī”ti.

Does past consciousness exist, and does it not abandon its state as past? Yes. Is past consciousness permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change? This should not be so said… Is it not that past consciousness is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change? Yes. If past consciousness is impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change, then it should not be said, ‘Past consciousness exists, and it does not abandon its state as past.’

Nibbānaṃ [T 0.0142] atthi nibbānaṃ nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati na jahatīti (?) purimapañhehi saṃsandetabbaṃ nibbānaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ [P 0.0125] na jahati na jahatīti (?) purimapañhehi saṃsandetabbaṃ atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ dhuvaṃ sassataṃ avipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does Nibbāna exist, does Nibbāna not abandon its state as Nibbāna, and is Nibbāna permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change? Yes. Does past consciousness exist, does past consciousness not abandon its state as past, and is past consciousness permanent, stable, eternal, and not subject to change? This should not be so said…

Atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atthi atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ atītabhāvaṃ na jahati atītaṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccaṃ [V 0.0113] adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ atthi nibbānaṃ [M 0.0102] nibbānabhāvaṃ na jahati nibbānaṃ aniccaṃ adhuvaṃ asassataṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does past consciousness exist, does past consciousness not abandon its state as past, and is past consciousness impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change? Yes. Does Nibbāna exist, does Nibbāna not abandon its state as Nibbāna, and is Nibbāna impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, and subject to change? This should not be so said…

Vacanasodhanā

Purification of Wording

288. Atītaṃ nvatthīti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ nvatthi, atītaṃ atthīti micchā. Hañci vā pana atthi nvātītaṃ, atthi atītanti micchā. Anāgataṃ nvatthīti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ nvatthi, anāgataṃ atthīti micchā. Hañci vā pana atthi nvānāgataṃ, atthi anāgatanti micchā.

288. Does the past not exist? Yes. If the past does not exist, then the statement ‘the past exists’ is wrong. And if what exists is not the past, then the statement ‘the past exists’ is wrong. Does the future not exist? Yes. If the future does not exist, then the statement ‘the future exists’ is wrong. And if what exists is not the future, then the statement ‘the future exists’ is wrong.

Anāgataṃ hutvā paccuppannaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Taññeva anāgataṃ taṃ paccuppannanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… taññeva anāgataṃ taṃ paccuppannanti? Āmantā. Hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Āmantā. Na hutvā na hoti na hutvā na hotīti? Na hevaṃ [T 0.0143] vattabbe…pe….

Having been the future, does it become the present? Yes. Is that very future that present? This should not be so said… Is that very future that present? Yes. Having been the future, does it become the present? Having been the present, does it become the future? This should not be so said… Having been the future, does it become the present? Having been the present, does it become the future? Yes. Without having been the future, does it not become the present? Without having been the present, does it not become the future? This should not be so said…

Paccuppannaṃ hutvā atītaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Taññeva paccuppannaṃ taṃ atītanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… taññeva paccuppannaṃ taṃ atītanti? Āmantā[P 0.0126]. Hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Āmantā. Na hutvā na hoti na hutvā na hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been the present, does it become the past? Yes. Is that very present that past? This should not be so said… Is that very present that past? Yes. Having been the present, does it become the past? Having been the past, does it become the present? This should not be so said… Having been the present, does it become the past? Having been the past, does it become the present? Yes. Without having been the present, does it not become the past? Without having been the past, does it not become the present? This should not be so said…

Anāgataṃ hutvā paccuppannaṃ hoti, paccuppannaṃ hutvā atītaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Taññeva anāgataṃ taṃ paccuppannaṃ taṃ atītanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… taññeva anāgataṃ taṃ paccuppannaṃ taṃ atītanti? Āmantā. Hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… hutvā hoti hutvā hotīti? Āmantā. Na hutvā na hoti na hutvā na hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Having been the future, does it become the present; and having been the present, does it become the past? Yes. Is that very future that present and that past? This should not be so said… Is that very future that present and that past? Yes. Having been the future, does it become the present-and-past? Having been the present-and-past, does it become the future? This should not be so said… Having been the future, does it become the present-and-past? Having been the present-and-past, does it become the future? Yes. Without having been the future, does it not become the present-and-past? Without having been the present-and-past, does it not become the future? This should not be so said.

Atītacakkhurūpādikathā

The Discussion on the Past Eye, Form, and So Forth

289. Atītaṃ [V 0.0114] cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Atītena cakkhunā atītaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ sotaṃ atthi saddā atthi sotaviññāṇaṃ atthi ākāso atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Atītena [M 0.0103] sotena atītaṃ saddaṃ suṇātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ ghānaṃ atthi gandhā atthi ghānaviññāṇaṃ [T 0.0144] atthi vāyo atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Atītena ghānena atītaṃ gandhaṃ ghāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā jivhā atthi rasā atthi jivhāviññāṇaṃ atthi āpo atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0127]. Atītāya jivhāya atītaṃ rasaṃ sāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto kāyo atthi phoṭṭhabbā atthi kāyaviññāṇaṃ atthi pathavī atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Atītena kāyena atītaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Atītena manena atītaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

289. Is there a past eye, are there past forms, is there past eye-consciousness, is there past light, is there past attention? Yes. Does one see a past form with the past eye? It should not be said thus… Is there a past ear, are there past sounds, is there past ear-consciousness, is there past space, is there past attention? Yes. Does one hear a past sound with the past ear? It should not be said thus… Is there a past nose, are there past smells, is there past nose-consciousness, is there past air, is there past attention? Yes. Does one smell a past smell with the past nose? It should not be said thus… Is there a past tongue, are there past tastes, is there past tongue-consciousness, is there past water, is there past attention? Yes. Does one taste a past taste with the past tongue? It should not be said thus… Is there a past body, are there past tangibles, is there past body-consciousness, is there past earth, is there past attention? Yes. Does one touch a past tangible with the past body? It should not be said thus… Is there a past mind, are there past mental objects, is there past mind-consciousness, is there a past base, is there past attention? Yes. Does one cognize a past mental object with the past mind? It should not be said thus…

Anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatena cakkhunā anāgataṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ sotaṃ atthi… ghānaṃ atthi… jivhā atthi… kāyo atthi [P 0.0128] … mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatena manena anāgataṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a future eye, are there future forms, is there future eye-consciousness, is there future light, is there future attention? Yes. Does one see a future form with the future eye? It should not be said thus… Is there a future ear… a future nose… a future tongue… a future body… a future mind, are there future mental objects, is there future mind-consciousness, is there a future base, is there future attention? Yes. Does one cognize a future mental object with the future mind? It should not be said thus…

Paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, paccuppannena cakkhunā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā [T 0.0145] atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, atītena cakkhunā atītaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Paccuppannaṃ sotaṃ atthi… ghānaṃ atthi… jivhā atthi… kāyo atthi… mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, paccuppannena manena paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Āmantā. Atīto mano [V 0.0115] atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, atītena manena atītaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a present eye, are there present forms, is there present eye-consciousness, is there present light, is there present attention, and does one see a present form with the present eye? Yes. Is there a past eye, are there past forms, is there past eye-consciousness, is there past light, is there past attention, and does one see a past form with the past eye? It should not be said thus… Is there a present ear… a present nose… a present tongue… a present body… a present mind, are there present mental objects, is there present mind-consciousness, is there a present base, is there present attention, and does one cognize a present mental object with the present mind? Yes. Is there a past mind, are there past mental objects, is there past mind-consciousness, is there a past base, is there past attention, and does one cognize a past mental object with the past mind? It should not be said thus…

Paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, paccuppannena cakkhunā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro [M 0.0104] atthi, anāgatena cakkhunā anāgataṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ sotaṃ atthi… ghānaṃ atthi… jivhā atthi… kāyo atthi… mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, paccuppannena manena paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Āmantā. Anāgato mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, anāgatena manena anāgataṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na [P 0.0129] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a present eye, are there present forms, is there present eye-consciousness, is there present light, is there present attention, and does one see a present form with the present eye? Yes. Is there a future eye, are there future forms, is there future eye-consciousness, is there future light, is there future attention, and does one see a future form with a future eye? It should not be said thus… Is there a present ear… a present nose… a present tongue… a present body… a present mind, are there present mental objects, is there present mind-consciousness, is there a present base, is there present attention, and does one cognize a present mental object with the present mind? Yes. Is there a future mind, are there future mental objects, is there future mind-consciousness, is there a future base, is there future attention, and does one cognize a future mental object with the future mind? It should not be said thus…

Atītaṃ [T 0.0146] cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca atītena cakkhunā atītaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca paccuppannena cakkhunā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ sotaṃ atthi… ghānaṃ atthi… jivhā atthi… kāyo atthi… mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca atītena manena atītaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Āmantā. Paccuppanno mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca paccuppannena manena paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The past eye exists, past forms exist, past eye-consciousness exists, past light exists, past attention exists; and does one not see a past form with the past eye? Yes. The present eye exists, present forms exist, present eye-consciousness exists, present light exists, present attention exists; and does one not see a present form with the present eye? It should not be said thus… The past ear exists… the past nose exists… the past tongue exists… the past body exists… the past mind exists, past mental objects exist, past mind-consciousness exists, the past base exists, past attention exists; and does one not cognize a past mental object with the past mind? Yes. The present mind exists, present mental objects exist, present mind-consciousness exists, the present base exists, present attention exists; and does one not cognize a present mental object with the present mind? It should not be said thus…

Anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca anāgatena cakkhunā anāgataṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ atthi rūpā atthi cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atthi āloko atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca paccuppannena cakkhunā paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ sotaṃ atthi… ghānaṃ atthi… jivhā atthi… kāyo atthi… mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, na [T 0.0147] ca anāgatena manena anāgataṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti[V 0.0116]? Āmantā. Paccuppanno mano atthi dhammā atthi manoviññāṇaṃ atthi vatthuṃ atthi manasikāro atthi, na ca paccuppannena manena paccuppannaṃ dhammaṃ vijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The future eye exists, future forms exist, future eye-consciousness exists, future light exists, future attention exists; and does one not see a future form with the future eye? Yes. The present eye exists, present forms exist, present eye-consciousness exists, present light exists, present attention exists; and does one not see a present form with the present eye? It should not be said thus… The future ear exists… the future nose exists… the future tongue exists… the future body exists… the future mind exists, future mental objects exist, future mind-consciousness exists, the future base exists, future attention exists; and does one not cognize a future mental object with the future mind? Yes. The present mind exists, present mental objects exist, present mind-consciousness exists, the present base exists, present attention exists; and does one not cognize a present mental object with the present mind? It should not be said thus…

Atītañāṇādikathā

Discussion on Past Knowledge, etc.

290. Atītaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na [P 0.0130] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti[M 0.0105]? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

290. Does past knowledge exist? Yes. With that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… With that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? Yes. With that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? It should not be said thus…

Anāgataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti[T 0.0148], maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does future knowledge exist? Yes. With that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… With that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? Yes. With that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? It should not be said thus…

Paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā[P 0.0131]. Anāgataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Present knowledge exists; with that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? Yes. Past knowledge exists; with that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… Present knowledge exists; with that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? Yes. Past knowledge exists; with that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? It should not be said thus… Present knowledge exists; with that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? Yes. Future knowledge exists; with that knowledge, does one perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… Present knowledge exists; with that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? Yes. Future knowledge exists; with that knowledge, is one fully comprehending suffering, abandoning its origin, realizing its cessation, and developing the path? It should not be said thus…

Atītaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Past knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, does one not perform the function of knowledge? Yes. Present knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, does one not perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… Past knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, is one not fully comprehending suffering, not abandoning its origin, not realizing its cessation, and not developing the path? Yes. Present knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, is one not fully comprehending suffering, not abandoning its origin, not realizing its cessation, and not developing the path? It should not be said thus…

Anāgataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ [V 0.0117] ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena ñāṇakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Anāgataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati[T 0.0149], nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā[M 0.0106]. Paccuppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ atthi, na ca tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Future knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, does one not perform the function of knowledge? Yes. Present knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, does one not perform the function of knowledge? It should not be said thus… Future knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, is one not fully comprehending suffering, not abandoning its origin, not realizing its cessation, and not developing the path? Yes. Present knowledge exists, and with that knowledge, is one not fully comprehending suffering, not abandoning its origin, not realizing its cessation, and not developing the path? It should not be said thus…

Arahantādikathā

Discussion on Arahants, etc.

291. Arahato atīto rāgo atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena rāgena sarāgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atīto doso atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0132]. Arahā tena dosena sadosoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atīto moho atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena mohena samohoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atīto māno atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena mānena samānoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītā diṭṭhi atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītā vicikicchā atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tāya vicikicchāya savicikicchoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītaṃ thinaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena thinena sathinoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītaṃ uddhaccaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena uddhaccena sauddhaccoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītaṃ ahirikaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena ahirikena saahirikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atītaṃ anottappaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Arahā tena anottappena [T 0.0150] saanottappīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

291. Does an Arahant have past lust? Yes. Is the Arahant lustful on account of that lust? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past hatred? Yes. Is the Arahant hateful on account of that hatred? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past delusion? Yes. Is the Arahant deluded on account of that delusion? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past conceit? Yes. Is the Arahant conceited on account of that conceit? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have a past view? Yes. Is the Arahant one with a view on account of that view? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past doubt? Yes. Is the Arahant doubtful on account of that doubt? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past sloth? Yes. Is the Arahant slothful on account of that sloth? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past restlessness? Yes. Is the Arahant restless on account of that restlessness? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past shamelessness? Yes. Is the Arahant shameless on account of that shamelessness? It should not be said thus… Does an Arahant have past lack of moral dread? Yes. Is the Arahant one who lacks moral dread on account of that lack of moral dread? It should not be said thus…

Anāgāmissa [V 0.0118] atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0133]. Anāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgāmissa atītā vicikicchā atthi… atīto sīlabbataparāmāso atthi… atīto aṇusahagato kāmarāgo atthi… atīto aṇusahagato byāpādo atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a Non-Returner have a past personality-view? Yes. Is the Non-Returner, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus… Does a Non-Returner have past doubt… past grasping of rites and rituals… past subtle sensual lust… past subtle ill will? Yes. Is the Non-Returner, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus…

Sakadāgāmissa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthīti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmissa atītā vicikicchā atthi… atīto sīlabbataparāmāso atthi… atīto [M 0.0107] oḷāriko kāmarāgo atthi… atīto oḷāriko byāpādo atthīti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a Once-Returner have a past personality-view? Yes. Is the Once-Returner, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus… Does a Once-Returner have past doubt… past grasping of rites and rituals… past gross sensual lust… past gross ill will? Yes. Is the Once-Returner, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus…

Sotāpannassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthīti? Āmantā. Sotāpanno tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpannassa atītā vicikicchā atthi… atīto sīlabbataparāmāso atthi… atīto apāyagamanīyo rāgo atthi… atīto apāyagamanīyo doso atthi… atīto apāyagamanīyo moho atthīti? Āmantā. Sotāpanno tena mohena samohoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a Stream-Enterer have a past personality-view? Yes. Is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a Stream-Enterer have past doubt… past grasping of rites and rituals… past lust leading to the lower realms… past hatred leading to the lower realms… past delusion leading to the lower realms? Yes. Is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that delusion, deluded? It should not be said thus.

292. Puthujjanassa [T 0.0151] atīto rāgo atthi, puthujjano tena rāgena sarāgoti? Āmantā. Arahato atīto rāgo atthi, arahā tena rāgena sarāgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puthujjanassa atīto doso atthi…pe… atītaṃ anottappaṃ atthi puthujjano tena anottappena anottappīti? Āmantā. Arahato atītaṃ anottappaṃ atthi, arahā tena anottappena anottappīti? Na [P 0.0134] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

292. Did a worldling have past lust, and is the worldling, on account of that lust, lustful? Yes. Did an Arahant have past lust, and is the Arahant, on account of that lust, lustful? It should not be said thus. … Did a worldling have past hatred… past lack of moral dread, and is the worldling, on account of that lack of moral dread, one who lacks moral dread? Yes. Did an Arahant have past lack of moral dread, and is the Arahant, on account of that lack of moral dread, one who lacks moral dread? It should not be said thus.

Puthujjanassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Anāgāmissa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, anāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puthujjanassa atītā vicikicchā atthi…pe… atīto aṇusahagato byāpādo atthi, puthujjano tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Āmantā. Anāgāmissa [V 0.0119] atīto aṇusahagato byāpādo atthi, anāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, one with a view? Yes. Did a Non-Returner have a past personality-view, and is the Non-Returner, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a worldling have past doubt… past subtle ill will, and is the worldling, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? Yes. Did a Non-Returner have past subtle ill will, and is the Non-Returner, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus.

Puthujjanassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmissa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, sakadāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puthujjanassa atītā vicikicchā atthi… atīto oḷāriko byāpādo atthi, puthujjano tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti[T 0.0152]? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmissa atīto oḷāriko byāpādo atthi, sakadāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, one with a view? Yes. Did a Once-Returner have a past personality-view, and is the Once-Returner, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a worldling have past doubt… past gross ill will, and is the worldling, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? Yes. Did a Once-Returner have past gross ill will, and is the Once-Returner, on account of that ill will, one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus.

Puthujjanassa [M 0.0108] atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, sotāpanno tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puthujjanassa atītā vicikicchā atthi…pe… atīto apāyagamanīyo moho atthi, puthujjano tena mohena samohoti? Āmantā. Sotāpannassa atīto apāyagamanīyo moho atthi, sotāpanno tena mohena samohoti? Na [P 0.0135] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, one with a view? Yes. Did a Stream-Enterer have a past personality-view, and is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that view, one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a worldling have past doubt… past delusion leading to the lower realms, and is the worldling, on account of that delusion, deluded? Yes. Did a Stream-Enterer have past delusion leading to the lower realms, and is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that delusion, deluded? It should not be said thus.

Arahato atīto rāgo atthi, na ca arahā tena rāgena sarāgoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atīto rāgo atthi, na ca puthujjano tena rāgena sarāgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato atīto doso atthi…pe… atītaṃ anottappaṃ atthi, na ca arahā tena anottappena anottappīti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atītaṃ anottappaṃ atthi, na ca puthujjano tena anottappena anottappīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did an Arahant have past lust, and is the Arahant not lustful on account of that lust? Yes. Did a worldling have past lust, and is the worldling not lustful on account of that lust? It should not be said thus. … Did an Arahant have past hatred… past lack of moral dread, and is the Arahant not one who lacks moral dread on account of that lack of moral dread? Yes. Did a worldling have past lack of moral dread, and is the worldling not one who lacks moral dread on account of that lack of moral dread? It should not be said thus.

Anāgāmissa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, na ca anāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi [T 0.0153] atthi, na ca puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgāmissa atītā vicikicchā atthi…pe… atīto aṇusahagato byāpādo atthi, na ca anāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti[V 0.0120]? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atīto aṇusahagato byāpādo atthi, na ca puthujjano tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a Non-Returner have a past personality-view, and is the Non-Returner, on account of that view, not one with a view? Yes. Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, not one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a Non-Returner have past doubt… past subtle ill will, and is the Non-Returner, on account of that ill will, not one with a mind of ill will? Yes. Did a worldling have past subtle ill will, and is the worldling, on account of that ill will, not one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus.

Sakadāgāmissa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, na ca sakadāgāmī tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, na ca puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmissa atītā vicikicchā atthi…pe… atīto oḷāriko byāpādo atthi, na ca sakadāgāmī tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atīto oḷāriko byāpādo atthi, na ca puthujjano tena byāpādena byāpannacittoti? Na [P 0.0136] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a Once-Returner have a past personality-view, and is the Once-Returner, on account of that view, not one with a view? Yes. Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, not one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a Once-Returner have past doubt… past gross ill will, and is the Once-Returner, on account of that ill will, not one with a mind of ill will? Yes. Did a worldling have past gross ill will, and is the worldling, on account of that ill will, not one with a mind of ill will? It should not be said thus.

Sotāpannassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi atthi, na ca sotāpanno tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atītā sakkāyadiṭṭhi [M 0.0109] atthi, na ca puthujjano tāya diṭṭhiyā sadiṭṭhikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpannassa atītā vicikicchā atthi…pe… atīto apāyagamanīyo moho atthi, na ca sotāpanno tena mohena samohoti? Āmantā. Puthujjanassa atīto apāyagamanīyo [T 0.0154] moho atthi, na ca puthujjano tena mohena samohoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Did a Stream-Enterer have a past personality-view, and is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that view, not one with a view? Yes. Did a worldling have a past personality-view, and is the worldling, on account of that view, not one with a view? It should not be said thus. … Did a Stream-Enterer have past doubt… past delusion leading to the lower realms, and is the Stream-Enterer, on account of that delusion, not deluded? Yes. Did a worldling have past delusion leading to the lower realms, and is the worldling, on account of that delusion, not deluded? It should not be said thus.

Atītahatthādikathā

Discourse on Past Hands, etc.

293. Atītā hatthā atthīti? Āmantā. Atītesu hatthesu sati ādānanikkhepanaṃ paññāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā pādā atthīti? Āmantā. Atītesu pādesu sati abhikkamapaṭikkamo paññāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā pabbā atthīti? Āmantā. Atītesu pabbesu sati samiñjanapasāraṇaṃ paññāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto kucchi atthīti? Āmantā. Atītasmiṃ kucchismiṃ sati jighacchā pipāsā paññāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

293. Are there past hands? Yes. When there are past hands, is taking and putting down discernible? This should not be said... Are there past feet? Yes. When there are past feet, is going forward and backward discernible? This should not be said... Are there past joints? Yes. When there are past joints, is bending and stretching discernible? This should not be said... Is there a past belly? Yes. When there is a past belly, are hunger and thirst discernible? This should not be said...

Atīto kāyo atthīti? Āmantā. Atīto kāyo paggahaniggahupago chedanabhedanupago kākehi gijjhehi kulalehi sādhāraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīte [P 0.0137] kāye visaṃ kameyya[V 0.0121], satthaṃ kameyya, aggi kameyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… labbhā atīto kāyo addubandhanena bandhituṃ, rajjubandhanena bandhituṃ, saṅkhalikabandhanena bandhituṃ, gāmabandhanena bandhituṃ, nigamabandhanena bandhituṃ, nagarabandhanena bandhituṃ, janapadabandhanena bandhituṃ, kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a past body? Yes. Is the past body subject to being lifted up and put down, subject to cutting and breaking, and common to crows, vultures, and hawks? This should not be said... In a past body, could one apply poison, apply a weapon, or apply fire? This should not be said... Is it possible to bind the past body with prison bonds, with rope bonds, with chain bonds, with village bonds, with town bonds, with city bonds, with country bonds, or with the fivefold bonds? This should not be said...

Atīto āpo atthīti? Āmantā. Tena āpena āpakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto tejo atthīti? Āmantā. Tena tejena tejakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na [T 0.0155] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto vāyo atthīti? Āmantā. Tena vāyena vāyakaraṇīyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a past water element? Yes. With that past water element, does one perform the function of water? This should not be said... Is there a past fire element? Yes. With that past fire element, does one perform the function of fire? This should not be said... Is there a past wind element? Yes. With that past wind element, does one perform the function of wind? This should not be said...

Atītakkhandhādisamodhānakathā

Discourse on the Combination of Past Aggregates, etc.

294. Atīto rūpakkhandho atthi, anāgato rūpakkhandho atthi, paccuppanno rūpakkhandho atthīti? Āmantā. Tayo rūpakkhandhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [M 0.0110]…pe… atītā pañcakkhandhā atthi, anāgatā pañcakkhandhā atthi, paccuppannā pañcakkhandhā atthīti? Āmantā. Pannarasakkhandhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

294. Does the past aggregate of form exist, the future aggregate of form exist, and the present aggregate of form exist? Yes. Are there three aggregates of form? This should not be said... Do the five past aggregates exist, the five future aggregates exist, and the five present aggregates exist? Yes. Are there fifteen aggregates? This should not be said...

Atītaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ atthi, paccuppannaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Tīṇi cakkhāyatanānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītāni [P 0.0138] dvādasāyatanāni atthi, anāgatāni dvādasāyatanāni atthi, paccuppannāni dvādasāyatanāni atthīti? Āmantā. Chattiṃsāyatanānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the past eye sense-base exist, the future eye sense-base exist, and the present eye sense-base exist? Yes. Are there three eye sense-bases? This should not be said... Do the twelve past sense-bases exist, the twelve future sense-bases exist, and the twelve present sense-bases exist? Yes. Are there thirty-six sense-bases? This should not be said...

Atītā cakkhudhātu atthi, anāgatā cakkhudhātu atthi, paccuppannā cakkhudhātu atthīti? Āmantā. Tisso cakkhudhātuyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo atthi, anāgatā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo atthi, paccuppannā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo atthīti? Āmantā. Catupaññāsa dhātuyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the past eye-element exist, the future eye-element exist, and the present eye-element exist? Yes. Are there three eye-elements? This should not be said... Do the eighteen past elements exist, the eighteen future elements exist, and the eighteen present elements exist? Yes. Are there fifty-four elements? This should not be said...

Atītaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ cakkhundriyaṃ atthi, paccuppannaṃ cakkhundriyaṃ atthīti[V 0.0122]? Āmantā. Tīṇi cakkhundriyānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītāni bāvīsatindriyāni atthi, anāgatāni bāvīsatindriyāni [T 0.0156] atthi, paccuppannāni bāvīsatindriyāni atthīti? Āmantā. Chasaṭṭhindriyānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the past eye-faculty exist, the future eye-faculty exist, and the present eye-faculty exist? Yes. Are there three eye-faculties? This should not be said... Do the twenty-two past faculties exist, the twenty-two future faculties exist, and the twenty-two present faculties exist? Yes. Are there sixty-six faculties? This should not be said...

Atīto rājā cakkavattī atthi, anāgato rājā cakkavattī atthi, paccuppanno rājā cakkavattī atthīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇannaṃ rājūnaṃ cakkavattīnaṃ sammukhībhāvo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a past wheel-turning king exist, a future wheel-turning king exist, and a present wheel-turning king exist? Yes. Are the three wheel-turning kings present at the same time? This should not be said...

Atīto sammāsammuddho atthi, anāgato sammāsambuddho atthi, paccuppanno sammāsambuddho atthīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇannaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ sammukhībhāvo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a past Perfectly Enlightened One exist, a future Perfectly Enlightened One exist, and a present Perfectly Enlightened One exist? Yes. Are the three Perfectly Enlightened Ones present at the same time? This should not be said...

Padasodhanakathā

Discourse on the Analysis of Words

295. Atītaṃ atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0139]. Atthi atītanti? Atthi siyā atītaṃ, siyā nvātītanti.

295. Does the past exist? Yes. Is that which exists, past? That which exists is sometimes past, and sometimes not past.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci atītaṃ atthi, atthi siyā atītaṃ, siyā nvātītaṃ, tenātītaṃ nvātītaṃ, nvātītaṃ atītanti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi [M 0.0111] – “vattabbe kho – ‘atītaṃ atthi atthi siyā atītaṃ, siyā nvātītaṃ, tenātītaṃ nvātītaṃ, nvātītaṃ atīta’”nti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If the past exists, then that which exists is sometimes past and sometimes not past; therefore, the past is not past, and the not-past is past. That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The past exists; that which exists is sometimes past and sometimes not past; therefore, the past is not past, and the not-past is past”’—is wrong.

No ce pana atītaṃ nvātītaṃ nvātītaṃ atītanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītaṃ atthi atthi siyā atītaṃ, siyā nvātīta”nti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘atītaṃ atthi atthi siyā atītaṃ, siyā nvātītaṃ, tenātītaṃ nvātītaṃ, nvātītaṃ atīta’”nti micchā.

But if it is not said that the past is not past and the not-past is past, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The past exists; that which exists is sometimes past and sometimes not past.’ That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The past exists; that which exists is sometimes past and sometimes not past; therefore, the past is not past, and the not-past is past”’—is wrong.

Anāgataṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Atthi anāgatanti? Atthi siyā anāgataṃ, siyā nvānāgatanti.

Does the future exist? Yes. Is that which exists, future? That which exists is sometimes future, and sometimes not future.

Ājānāhi [V 0.0123] niggahaṃ. Hañci anāgataṃ atthi atthi siyā anāgataṃ siyā nvānāgataṃ, tenānāgataṃ [T 0.0157] nvānāgataṃ, nvānāgataṃ anāgatanti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘anāgataṃ atthi atthi siyā anāgataṃ, siyā nvānāgataṃ, tenānāgataṃ nvānāgataṃ, nvānāgataṃ anāgata’”nti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If the future exists, then that which exists is sometimes future and sometimes not future; therefore, the future is not future, and the not-future is future. That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The future exists; that which exists is sometimes future and sometimes not future; therefore, the future is not future, and the not-future is future”’—is wrong.

No ce panānāgataṃ nvānāgataṃ nvānāgataṃ anāgatanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgataṃ atthi atthi siyā anāgataṃ, siyā nvānāgata”nti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘anāgataṃ atthi atthi siyā anāgataṃ, siyā nvānāgataṃ, tenānāgataṃ nvānāgataṃ, nvānāgataṃ anāgata’”nti micchā.

But if it is not said that the future is not future and the not-future is future, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The future exists; that which exists is sometimes future and sometimes not future.’ That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The future exists; that which exists is sometimes future and sometimes not future; therefore, the future is not future, and the not-future is future”’—is wrong.

Paccuppannaṃ atthīti, āmantā. Atthi paccuppannanti? Atthi siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā no paccuppannanti.

Does the present exist? Yes. Is that which exists, present? That which exists is sometimes present, and sometimes not present.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci paccuppannaṃ atthi atthi siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā no paccuppannaṃ, tena paccuppannaṃ, no paccuppannaṃ, no paccuppannaṃ paccuppannanti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘paccuppannaṃ atthi atthi siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā no paccuppannaṃ, tena paccuppannaṃ no paccuppannaṃ, no paccuppannaṃ paccuppanna’”nti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If the present exists, then that which exists is sometimes present and sometimes not present; therefore, the present is not present, and the not-present is present. That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The present exists; that which exists is sometimes present and sometimes not present; therefore, the present is not present, and the not-present is present”’—is wrong.

No ce pana paccuppannaṃ [P 0.0140] no paccuppannaṃ, no paccuppannaṃ paccuppannanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “paccuppannaṃ atthi atthi siyā paccuppannaṃ, siyā no paccuppanna”nti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘paccuppannaṃ atthi atthi siyā [M 0.0112] paccuppannaṃ, siyā no paccuppannaṃ, tena paccuppannaṃ no paccuppannaṃ, no paccuppannaṃ paccuppanna’”nti micchā.

But if it is not said that the present is not present and the not-present is present, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The present exists; that which exists is sometimes present and sometimes not present.’ That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “The present exists; that which exists is sometimes present and sometimes not present; therefore, the present is not present, and the not-present is present”’—is wrong.

Nibbānaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Atthi nibbānanti? Atthi [T 0.0158] siyā nibbānaṃ siyā no nibbānanti.

Does Nibbāna exist? Yes. Is that which exists, Nibbāna? That which exists is sometimes Nibbāna, and sometimes not Nibbāna.

Ājānāhi niggahaṃ. Hañci nibbānaṃ atthi atthi siyā nibbānaṃ, siyā no nibbānaṃ, tena nibbānaṃ no nibbānaṃ, no nibbānaṃ nibbānanti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho [V 0.0124] – ‘nibbānaṃ atthi atthi siyā nibbānaṃ, siyā no nibbānaṃ, tena nibbānaṃ no nibbānaṃ, no nibbānaṃ nibbāna’”nti micchā.

Acknowledge the refutation. If Nibbāna exists, then that which exists is sometimes Nibbāna and sometimes not Nibbāna; therefore, Nibbāna is not Nibbāna, and not-Nibbāna is Nibbāna. That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “Nibbāna exists; that which exists is sometimes Nibbāna and sometimes not Nibbāna; therefore, Nibbāna is not Nibbāna, and not-Nibbāna is Nibbāna”’—is wrong.

No ce pana nibbānaṃ no nibbānaṃ, no nibbānaṃ nibbānanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “nibbānaṃ atthi atthi siyā nibbānaṃ, siyā no nibbāna”nti. Yaṃ tattha vadesi – “vattabbe kho – ‘nibbānaṃ atthi atthi siyā nibbānaṃ, siyā no nibbānaṃ, tena nibbānaṃ no nibbānaṃ, no nibbānaṃ nibbāna’”nti micchā.

But if it is not said that Nibbāna is not Nibbāna and not-Nibbāna is Nibbāna, then it should certainly not be said: ‘Nibbāna exists; that which exists is sometimes Nibbāna and sometimes not Nibbāna.’ That which you state in this context—‘It should indeed be said: “Nibbāna exists; that which exists is sometimes Nibbāna and sometimes not Nibbāna; therefore, Nibbāna is not Nibbāna, and not-Nibbāna is Nibbāna”’—is wrong.

Suttasādhanaṃ

Proof from the Suttas

296. Na vattabbaṃ – “atītaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā – ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā – ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho”ti saṃ. ni. 3.48. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atītaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ atthīti.

296. Should it not be said: 'The past exists, the future exists'? Yes. Has not the Blessed One said: 'Whatever form, monks—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the aggregate of form. Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness—past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near—this is called the aggregate of consciousness'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, the past exists, the future exists.

Atītaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā [T 0.0159] – “tayome, bhikkhave, niruttipathā [P 0.0141] adhivacanapathā paññattipathā asaṅkiṇṇā asaṅkiṇṇapubbā na saṅkiyanti na saṅkiyissanti appaṭikuṭṭhā samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi. Katame tayo? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ ‘ahosī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’ti. Yā vedanā…pe… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ [M 0.0113] atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ ‘ahosī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘ahosī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’ti.

Does the past exist? Does the future exist? Yes. For has not the Blessed One said: 'Monks, there are these three paths of expression, paths of designation, and paths of concepts, which are unconfused, were unconfused in the past, are not being confused, and will not be confused, and are not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. Which three? Whatever form, monks, that is past, ceased, vanished, and altered: it has the reckoning 'it was,' it has the designation 'it was,' it has the concept 'it was.' It does not have the reckoning 'it is,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it will be.' Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness that is past, ceased, vanished, and altered: it has the reckoning 'it was,' it has the designation 'it was,' it has the concept 'it was.' It does not have the reckoning 'it is,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it will be.'

“Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa [V 0.0125] samaññā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti. Yā vedanā…pe… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ ajātaṃ apātubhūtaṃ ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘bhavissatī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘atthī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti.

Whatever form, monks, is unborn and unmanifested: it has the reckoning 'it will be,' it has the designation 'it will be,' it has the concept 'it will be.' It does not have the reckoning 'it is,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it was.' Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness that is unborn and unmanifested: it has the reckoning 'it will be,' it has the designation 'it will be,' it has the concept 'it will be.' It does not have the reckoning 'it is,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it was.'

“Yaṃ, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ ‘atthī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti, na tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’ti. Yā vedanā…pe… yā saññā… ye saṅkhārā… yaṃ viññāṇaṃ jātaṃ pātubhūtaṃ ‘atthī’ti tassa saṅkhā, ‘atthī’ti tassa samaññā, ‘atthī’ti tassa paññatti; na tassa saṅkhā ‘ahosī’ti, na [T 0.0160] tassa saṅkhā ‘bhavissatī’ti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo niruttipathā adhivacanapathā paññattipathā asaṅkiṇṇā asaṅkiṇṇapubbā na saṅkiyanti na saṅkiyissanti appaṭikuṭṭhā samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi.

Whatever form, monks, has arisen and is manifest: it has the reckoning 'it is,' it has the designation 'it is,' it has the concept 'it is.' It does not have the reckoning 'it was,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it will be.' Whatever feeling… whatever perception… whatever volitional formations… whatever consciousness that has arisen and is manifest: it has the reckoning 'it is,' it has the designation 'it is,' it has the concept 'it is.' It does not have the reckoning 'it was,' nor does it have the reckoning 'it will be.' These, monks, are the three paths of expression, paths of designation, and paths of concepts, which are unconfused, were unconfused in the past, are not being confused, and will not be confused, and are not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins.

“Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ ukkalā vassabhaññā ahetukavādā akiriyavādā natthikavādā, tepime tayo niruttipathe adhivacanapathe paññattipathe na garahitabbaṃ na paṭikkositabbaṃ amaññiṃsu.
