Taṃ kissa hetu? Nindābyārosaupārambhabhayā”ti saṃyuttanikāye. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atītaṃ atthi, anāgataṃ atthī”ti.

Even those, monks, who were the Ukkalas and Vassabhaññas, proponents of causelessness, proponents of inaction, and proponents of nihilism, did not think that these three paths of expression, paths of designation, and paths of concepts should be blamed or rejected. For what reason? For fear of blame, censure, and reproach.” Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'The past exists, the future exists.'

Atītaṃ [P 0.0142] atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā phagguno bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi nu kho taṃ, bhante, cakkhuṃ yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyāti. Atthi nu kho sā, bhante, jivhā…pe… atthi nu kho so, bhante, mano yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti.

Does the past exist? Yes. Did not the Venerable Phagguna say this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is there an eye by which one, designating them, might designate the past Buddhas who have attained final Nibbāna—for whom proliferation is cut off, the round is cut off, the cycle is exhausted, and all suffering is transcended? Venerable sir, is there a tongue… Venerable sir, is there a mind by which one, designating them, might designate the past Buddhas who have attained final Nibbāna—for whom proliferation is cut off, the round is cut off, the cycle is exhausted, and all suffering is transcended?”

“Natthi [M 0.0114] kho taṃ, phagguna, cakkhuṃ yena cakkhunā atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte paññāpayamāno paññāpeyya. Natthi kho sā, phagguna, jivhā…pe… natthi nu kho so, phagguna, mano yena manena atīte buddhe parinibbute chinnapapañce chinnavaṭume [T 0.0161] pariyādinnavaṭṭe sabbadukkhavītivatte paññāpayamāno paññāpeyyā”ti [V 0.0126] saṃ. ni. 4.83. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atītaṃ atthī”ti.

“There is no such eye, Phagguna, by which one, designating them, might designate the past Buddhas who have attained final Nibbāna—for whom proliferation is cut off, the round is cut off, the cycle is exhausted, and all suffering is transcended. There is no such tongue, Phagguna… There is no such mind, Phagguna, by which one, designating them, might designate the past Buddhas who have attained final Nibbāna—for whom proliferation is cut off, the round is cut off, the cycle is exhausted, and all suffering is transcended.” Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The past exists.’”

Atītaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā nandako etadavoca – “ahu pubbe lobho tadahu akusalaṃ, so etarahi natthi, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. Ahu pubbe doso… ahu pubbe moho, tadahu akusalaṃ, so etarahi natthi, iccetaṃ kusala”nti aṅguttaranikāye. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atītaṃ atthī”ti.

Does the past exist? Yes. Did not the Venerable Nandaka say this: ‘Formerly there was greed, and that was unwholesome; now it is not, and this is wholesome. Formerly there was hatred… Formerly there was delusion, and that was unwholesome; now it is not, and this is wholesome.’? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The past exists.’”

Na vattabbaṃ – “anāgataṃ atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “kabaḷīkāre ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo, atthi nandī, atthi taṇhā; patiṭṭhitaṃ tattha viññāṇaṃ virūḷhaṃ. Yattha patiṭṭhitaṃ viññāṇaṃ virūḷhaṃ, atthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti. Yattha atthi nāmarūpassa [P 0.0143] avakkanti, atthi tattha saṅkhārānaṃ vuddhi. Yattha atthi saṅkhārānaṃ vuddhi, atthi tattha āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti. Yattha atthi āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti, atthi tattha āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ. Yattha atthi āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ, sasokaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, sarajaṃ sadaraṃ (saṃ. ni. 2.64) tadeva yuttataraṃ saupāyāsanti vadāmi.

Should it not be said: ‘The future exists’? Yes. Has the Blessed One not said: ‘If, monks, there is lust, if there is delight, if there is craving for physical food, consciousness is established there and has grown. Where consciousness is established and has grown, there is the descent of name-and-form. Where there is the descent of name-and-form, there is the growth of formations. Where there is the growth of formations, there is the future production of renewed existence. Where there is the future production of renewed existence, there is future birth, aging, and death. Where there is future birth, aging, and death, that, monks, I declare to be with sorrow, with affliction, and with despair.’

“Phasse ce, bhikkhave, āhāre… manosañcetanāya ce, bhikkhave, āhāre… viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre atthi rāgo, atthi nandī…pe… sarajaṃ saupāyāsanti vadāmī”ti saṃ. ni. 2.64. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[T 0.0162]. Tena hi anāgataṃ atthīti.

‘If, monks, in the nutriment of contact… if, monks, in the nutriment of mental volition… if, monks, in the nutriment of consciousness there is lust, there is delight… with affliction and with despair, I say.’ Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, the future exists.

Anāgataṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “kabaḷīkāre ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo, natthi nandī, natthi taṇhā; appatiṭṭhitaṃ tattha viññāṇaṃ avirūḷhaṃ. Yattha viññāṇaṃ appatiṭṭhitaṃ avirūḷhaṃ, natthi tattha nāmarūpassa avakkanti. Yattha natthi nāmarūpassa avakkanti, natthi tattha saṅkhārānaṃ vuddhi. Yattha natthi saṅkhārānaṃ vuddhi, natthi tattha āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti. Yattha [M 0.0115] natthi āyatiṃ punabbhavābhinibbatti, natthi tattha āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ. Yattha natthi āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇaṃ, asokaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, arajaṃ anupāyāsanti vadāmi.

Does the future exist? Yes. Has the Blessed One not said: ‘If, monks, in physical food there is no lust, no delight, no craving, consciousness is not established there and has not grown. Where consciousness is not established and has not grown, there is no descent of name-and-form. Where there is no descent of name-and-form, there is no growth of formations. Where there is no growth of formations, there is no future production of renewed existence. Where there is no future production of renewed existence, there is no future birth, aging, and death. Where there is no future birth, aging, and death, that, monks, I declare to be without sorrow, without affliction, and without despair.’

“Phasse [V 0.0127] ce, bhikkhave, āhāre… manosañcetanāya ce, bhikkhave, āhāre… viññāṇe ce, bhikkhave, āhāre natthi rāgo, natthi nandī…pe… arajaṃ anupāyāsanti vadāmī”ti saṃ. ni. 2.64. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “anāgataṃ atthī”ti.

‘If, monks, in the nutriment of contact… if, monks, in the nutriment of mental volition… if, monks, in the nutriment of consciousness there is no lust, no delight… without affliction and without despair, I say.’ Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The future exists.’”

Sabbamatthītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on ‘Everything Exists’ is concluded.

2. Suttasādhanaṃ

2. Proof from the Suttas

298. Na vattabbaṃ – “atītānāgatā khandhā dhātu āyatanaṃ natthi cete”ti? Āmantā[V 0.0131]. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tayome, bhikkhave, niruttipathā adhivacanapathā paññatti…pe… viññūhīti…pe…”. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atītānāgatā khandhā dhātu āyatanaṃ natthi cete”ti.

298. Should it not be said: 'Past and future phenomena are aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and these do not exist'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there are these three paths of expression, paths of designation, concepts... and so on... by the wise... and so on...'? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'Past and future phenomena are aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and these do not exist'.

Atītānāgatā khandhā dhātu āyatanaṃ natthi ceteti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ ajjhattaṃ vā bahiddhā [P 0.0151] vā oḷārikaṃ vā sukhumaṃ vā hīnaṃ vā paṇītaṃ vā yaṃ dūre santike vā, ayaṃ vuccati rūpakkhandho. Yā kāci vedanā… yā kāci saññā… ye keci saṅkhārā… yaṃ kiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ…pe… ayaṃ vuccati viññāṇakkhandho”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atītānāgatā khandhā dhātu āyatanaṃ natthi cete”ti.

Are past and future phenomena aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and do these not exist? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Whatever form there is, monks—past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near—this is called the aggregate of form. Whatever feeling... whatever perception... whatever formations... whatever consciousness there is—past, future, or present... and so on... this is called the aggregate of consciousness'? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'Past and future phenomena are aggregates, elements, and sense bases, and these do not exist'.

Atītakkhandhādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the past aggregates and so on is concluded.

7. Ekaccaṃ atthītikathā

7. The Discussion on 'Some Exists'

1. Atītādiekaccakathā

1. The Discussion on 'Some' Regarding the Past and so on

299. Atītaṃ [T 0.0169][M 0.0119] atthīti? Ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti. Ekaccaṃ niruddhaṃ, ekaccaṃ na niruddhaṃ; ekaccaṃ vigataṃ, ekaccaṃ avigataṃ; ekaccaṃ atthaṅgataṃ, ekaccaṃ na atthaṅgataṃ; ekaccaṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ, ekaccaṃ na abbhatthaṅgatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

299. Does the past exist? Some exists, and some does not exist. Is it that some has ceased, and some has not ceased; some has departed, and some has not departed; some has disappeared, and some has not disappeared; some has utterly disappeared, and some has not utterly disappeared? This should not be said... and so on.

Atītaṃ ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā ekacce atthi, ekacce natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā ekacce atthi, ekacce natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipākā dhammā ekacce atthi ekacce natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does some of the past exist, and some not exist? Yes. Do some past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened exist, and some not exist? This should not be said... and so on... Does some of the past exist, and some not exist? Yes. Do some past phenomena whose results have ripened exist, and some not exist? This should not be said... and so on... Does some of the past exist, and some not exist? Yes. Do some past phenomena that are not results exist, and some not exist? This should not be said... and so on.

Atītaṃ [V 0.0132] ekaccaṃ atthi ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Kiṃ atthi kiṃ natthīti? Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthi; atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā – te natthīti. Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0152]. Atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipākā dhammā – te atthīti atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā te natthīti (ka.)? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does some of the past exist, and some not exist? Yes. What exists, and what does not exist? Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—they exist; past phenomena whose results have ripened—they do not exist. Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—do they exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have ripened—do they exist? This should not be said... and so on... Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—do they exist? Yes. Do past phenomena that are not results—do they exist? This should not be said... and so on.

Atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0170] …pe….

Do past phenomena whose results have ripened—do they not exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—do they not exist? This should not be said... and so on.

Atītā avipākā vipakkavipākā (syā.), avipakkavipākā (ka.) dhammā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipakkavipākā avipākā (syā.) dhammā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do past phenomena that are not results—do they not exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—do they not exist? This should not be said... and so on.

Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhāti? Āmantā. Hañci atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te dhammā niruddhā te (syā. ka.) atthī”ti.

Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—do they exist? Yes. But have not past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened ceased? Yes. If past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened have ceased, then, sir, it should not be said: 'Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—they exist'.

Atītā [M 0.0120] avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipākā avipakkavipākā (sī. ka.) dhammā niruddhā – te atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, which have ceased—do they exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have ripened, which have ceased—do they exist? This should not be said... Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, which have ceased—do they exist? Yes. Do past phenomena that are without result, which have ceased—do they exist? This should not be said...

Atītā vipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do past phenomena whose results have ripened, which have ceased—do they not exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, which have ceased—do they not exist? This should not be said...

Atītā avipākā vipakkavipākā (syā.), avipakkavipākā (ka.) dhammā niruddhā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā avipakkavipākā [T 0.0171] avipākā (syā.) dhammā niruddhā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do past phenomena that are without result, which have ceased—do they not exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, which have ceased—do they not exist? This should not be said...

Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te atthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0153]. Atītā vipakkavipākā [V 0.0133] dhammā niruddhā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Atītā ekadesaṃ vipakkavipākā dhammā ekadesaṃ avipakkavipākā dhammā niruddhā – te ekacce atthi ekacce natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, which have ceased—do they exist? Yes. Do past phenomena whose results have ripened, which have ceased—do they not exist? Yes. Do past phenomena that have ceased, which are partly those whose results have ripened and partly those whose results have not yet ripened—do some of them exist and some not exist? This should not be said...

Na vattabbaṃ – “atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā vipaccissantīti? Āmantā. Hañci atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā vipaccissanti, tena vata re vattabbe – “atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā – te atthī”ti.

Should it not be said: 'Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—they exist'? Yes, it should not be said. But will not past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened come to fruition? Yes. If past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened will come to fruition, then, sir, it should indeed be said: 'Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—they exist'.

Atītā avipakkavipākā dhammā vipaccissantīti katvā te atthīti? Āmantā. Vipaccissantīti katvā paccuppannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vipaccissantīti katvā paccuppannāti? Āmantā. Paccuppannā dhammā nirujjhissantīti katvā te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

On the grounds that they 'will come to fruition,' do past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened exist? Yes. On the grounds that they 'will come to fruition,' are they present? This should not be said... On the grounds that they 'will come to fruition,' are they present? Yes. On the grounds that present phenomena 'will cease,' do they not exist? This should not be said...

2. Anāgatādiekaccakathā

2. The Discussion on 'Some' Regarding the Future, etc.

300. Anāgataṃ atthīti? Ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti. Ekaccaṃ jātaṃ, ekaccaṃ ajātaṃ; ekaccaṃ sañjātaṃ, ekaccaṃ asañjātaṃ; ekaccaṃ nibbattaṃ, ekaccaṃ anibbattaṃ; ekaccaṃ pātubhūtaṃ, ekaccaṃ apātubhūtanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

300. Does the future exist? Some exists, some does not exist. Is some born, some unborn; some well-arisen, some not well-arisen; some produced, some not produced; some manifest, some not manifest? This should not be said...

Anāgataṃ ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā [T 0.0172] uppādino dhammā ekacce atthi, ekacce natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ [M 0.0121] ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā anuppādino dhammā ekacce atthi, ekacce natthīti? Na [P 0.0154] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the future partly exist and partly not exist? Yes. Do future phenomena that are due to arise partly exist and partly not exist? This should not be said... Does the future partly exist and partly not exist? Yes. Do future phenomena that are not due to arise partly exist and partly not exist? This should not be said...

Anāgataṃ ekaccaṃ atthi, ekaccaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Kiṃ atthi, kiṃ natthīti? Anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthi; anāgatā anuppādino dhammā – te natthīti. Anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā anuppādino dhammā – te atthīti[V 0.0134]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgatā anuppādino dhammā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the future partly exist, and partly not exist? Yes. What exists, and what does not exist? Future phenomena that are due to arise—those exist; future phenomena that are not due to arise—those do not exist. Do future phenomena that are due to arise—do those exist? Yes. Do future phenomena that are not due to arise—do those exist? This should not be said... Do future phenomena that are not due to arise—do those not exist? Yes. Do future phenomena that are due to arise—do those not exist? This should not be said...

Anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgatā uppādino dhammā ajātāti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgatā uppādino dhammā ajātā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthī”ti.

Do future phenomena that are due to arise—do those exist? Yes. But are not future phenomena that are due to arise unborn? Yes. If future phenomena that are due to arise are unborn, then it should not be said: 'Future phenomena that are due to arise—those exist.'

Anāgatā uppādino dhammā ajātā – te atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā anuppādino dhammā ajātā – te atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgatā anuppādino dhammā ajātā – te natthīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā uppādino dhammā ajātā – te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are future phenomena that are due to arise unborn—do they exist? Yes. Are future phenomena that are not due to arise unborn—do they exist? This should not be said... Are future phenomena that are not due to arise unborn—do they not exist? Yes. Are future phenomena that are due to arise unborn—do they not exist? This should not be said...

Na vattabbaṃ – “anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgatā uppādino dhammā uppajjissantīti? Āmantā[T 0.0173]. Hañci anāgatā uppādino dhammā uppajjissanti, tena vata re vattabbe – “anāgatā uppādino dhammā – te atthī”ti.

Should it not be said: 'Future phenomena that are due to arise—those exist'? Yes, it should not be said. But will not future phenomena that are due to arise, arise? Yes. If future phenomena that are due to arise will arise, then it should indeed be said: 'Future phenomena that are due to arise—those exist.'

Anāgatā uppādino dhammā uppajjissantīti katvā te atthīti? Āmantā. Uppajjissantīti [P 0.0155] katvā paccuppannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… uppajjissantīti katvā paccuppannāti? Āmantā. Paccuppannā dhammā nirujjhissantīti katvā te natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

On the grounds that future phenomena that are due to arise 'will arise,' do they exist? Yes. On the grounds that they 'will arise,' are they present? This should not be said... On the grounds that they 'will arise,' are they present? Yes. On the grounds that present phenomena 'will cease,' do they not exist? This should not be said...

Ekaccaṃ atthītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion 'Some Exists' is concluded.

8. Satipaṭṭhānakathā

8. Discussion on the Establishments of Mindfulness

301. Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Sabbe dhammā sati satindriyaṃ satibalaṃ sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo ekāyanamaggo khayagāmī bodhagāmī [M 0.0122] apacayagāmī anāsavā asaṃyojaniyā [V 0.0135] aganthaniyā anoghaniyā ayoganiyā anīvaraṇiyā aparāmaṭṭhā anupādāniyā asaṃkilesikā, sabbe dhammā buddhānussati dhammānussati saṅghānussati sīlānussati cāgānussati devatānussati ānāpānassati maraṇānussati kāyagatāsati upasamānussatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

301. Are all phenomena establishments of mindfulness? Yes. Are all phenomena mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the one-way path, leading to destruction, leading to awakening, leading to the dismantling of the round of existence, not objects of the taints, not objects of the fetters, not objects of the ties, not objects of the floods, not objects of the yokes, not objects of the hindrances, not grasped, not objects of clinging, not connected with defilements; and are all phenomena recollection of the Buddha, recollection of the Dhamma, recollection of the Saṅgha, recollection of virtue, recollection of generosity, recollection of deities, mindfulness of breathing, mindfulness of death, mindfulness of the body, and recollection of peace? This should not be said...

Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ satipaṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ satipaṭṭhānanti[T 0.0174]? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ sati satindriyaṃ satibalaṃ sammāsati satisambojjhaṅgo ekāyanamaggo khayagāmī bodhagāmī apacayagāmī anāsavaṃ asaṃyojaniyaṃ…pe… asaṃkilesikaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ buddhānussati dhammānussati saṅghānussati sīlānussati cāgānussati devatānussati ānāpānassati maraṇānussati kāyagatāsati upasamānussatīti? Na [P 0.0156] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāyatanaṃ… ghānāyatanaṃ… jivhāyatanaṃ… kāyāyatanaṃ… rūpāyatanaṃ… saddāyatanaṃ… gandhāyatanaṃ… rasāyatanaṃ… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ… rāgo… doso… moho… māno… diṭṭhi… vicikicchā… thinaṃ… uddhaccaṃ… ahirikaṃ… anottappaṃ satipaṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anottappaṃ satipaṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Anottappaṃ sati satindriyaṃ satibalaṃ sammāsati…pe… kāyagatāsati upasamānussatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. Is the eye-base a foundation of mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on… Is the eye-base a foundation of mindfulness? Yes. Is the eye-base mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the direct path, leading to destruction, leading to awakening, leading to the dismantling of the round of existence, not an object of the taints, not an object of the fetters… and so on… not an object of the defilements; is the eye-base recollection of the Buddha, recollection of the Dhamma, recollection of the Saṅgha, recollection of virtue, recollection of generosity, recollection of deities, mindfulness of breathing, mindfulness of death, mindfulness of the body, and recollection of peace? This should not be said… and so on… The ear-base… the nose-base… the tongue-base… the body-base… the form-base… the sound-base… the smell-base… the taste-base… the tangible-base… greed… hatred… delusion… conceit… wrong view… doubt… sloth… restlessness… lack of shame… Is lack of moral dread a foundation of mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on… Is lack of moral dread a foundation of mindfulness? Yes. Is lack of moral dread mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness… and so on… mindfulness of the body, and recollection of peace? This should not be said… and so on…

Sati satipaṭṭhānā, sā ca satīti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca satīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sati satipaṭṭhānā, sā ca satīti? Āmantā. Sotāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ… rāgo… doso… moho…pe… anottappaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca satīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Mindfulness is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that foundation of mindfulness also mindfulness? Yes. The eye-base is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that eye-base also mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on… Mindfulness is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that foundation of mindfulness also mindfulness? Yes. The ear-base… and so on… the body-base… the form-base… and so on… the tangible-base… greed… hatred… delusion… and so on… Lack of moral dread is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that lack of moral dread also mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on…

Cakkhāyatanaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca na satīti? Āmantā. Sati satipaṭṭhānā, sā ca na satīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ… rāgo [T 0.0175]… doso… moho…pe… anottappaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, tañca na satīti? Āmantā[P 0.0157]. Sati satipaṭṭhānā, sā ca na satīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The eye-base is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that eye-base not mindfulness? Yes. Mindfulness is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that foundation of mindfulness not mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on… The ear-base… and so on… the body-base… the form-base… and so on… the tangible-base… greed… hatred… delusion… and so on… Lack of moral dread is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that lack of moral dread not mindfulness? Yes. Mindfulness is a foundation of mindfulness, and is that foundation of mindfulness not mindfulness? This should not be said… and so on…

302. Na [M 0.0123] vattabbaṃ – “sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sabbe dhamme ārabbha [V 0.0136] sati santiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Hañci sabbe dhamme ārabbha sati santiṭṭhatīti, tena vata re vattabbe – “sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānā”ti.

302. Should it not be said that 'all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness'? Yes. Does not mindfulness become established by taking all phenomena as its object? Yes. If mindfulness becomes established by taking all phenomena as its object, then indeed, sir, it should be said that 'all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness.'

Sabbaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha sati santiṭṭhatīti sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Sabbaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha phasso santiṭṭhatīti sabbe dhammā phassapaṭṭhānāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Because mindfulness becomes established by taking all phenomena as its object, are all phenomena therefore foundations of mindfulness? Yes. Because contact becomes established by taking all phenomena as its object, are all phenomena therefore foundations of contact? This should not be said… and so on…

Sabbaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha sati santiṭṭhatīti sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Sabbaṃ dhammaṃ ārabbha vedanā santiṭṭhati… saññā santiṭṭhati… cetanā santiṭṭhati… cittaṃ santiṭṭhatīti sabbe dhammā cittapaṭṭhānāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Because mindfulness becomes established by taking all phenomena as its object, are all phenomena therefore foundations of mindfulness? Yes. Because feeling becomes established by taking all phenomena as its object… perception becomes established… volition becomes established… consciousness becomes established, are all phenomena therefore foundations of consciousness? This should not be said… and so on…

Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Sabbe sattā upaṭṭhitasatino satiyā samannāgatā satiyā samohitā; sabbesaṃ sattānaṃ sati paccupaṭṭhitāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. Are all beings possessed of established mindfulness, endowed with mindfulness, concentrated in mindfulness? Is mindfulness present to all beings? This should not be said… and so on…

303. Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “amataṃ te, bhikkhave, na paribhuñjanti ye kāyagatāsatiṃ na paribhuñjanti. Amataṃ te, bhikkhave, paribhuñjanti ye kāyagatāsatiṃ paribhuñjantī”ti [T 0.0176] a. ni. 1.600. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Sabbe sattā kāyagatāsatiṃ paribhuñjanti paṭilabhanti āsevanti bhāventi bahulīkarontīti? Na [P 0.0158] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

303. Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, those who do not make use of mindfulness directed to the body do not make use of the Deathless. Monks, those who make use of mindfulness directed to the body make use of the Deathless’? Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Do all beings make use of, obtain, practice, develop, and frequently practice mindfulness directed to the body? This should not be said… and so on…

Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “ekāyano ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti dī. ni. 2.373; ma. ni. 1.106; saṃ. ni. 5.367! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā? Sabbe dhammā ekāyanamaggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, this is the direct path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the cessation of suffering and grief, for the attainment of the method, for the realization of Nibbāna—namely, the four foundations of mindfulness’? Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Are all phenomena the direct path? This should not be said… and so on…

Sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “rañño, bhikkhave, cakkavattissa pātubhāvā sattannaṃ ratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Cakkaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, hatthiratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, assaratanassa… maṇiratanassa… itthiratanassa [V 0.0137]… gahapatiratanassa… pariṇāyakaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti[M 0.0124]. Rañño, bhikkhave, cakkavattissa pātubhāvā imesaṃ sattannaṃ ratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti.

Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, with the appearance of a wheel-turning king, there is the appearance of seven treasures. Which seven? There is the appearance of the wheel treasure, the appearance of the elephant treasure, the appearance of the horse treasure… the jewel treasure… the woman treasure… the householder treasure… and the appearance of the counselor treasure. Monks, with the appearance of a wheel-turning king, there is the appearance of these seven treasures.’

“Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaratanassa [T 0.0177] pātubhāvo hoti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, pītisambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, samādhisambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti. Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa imesaṃ sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 5.223. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa sabbe dhammā satisambojjhaṅgaratanāva hontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbe [P 0.0159] dhammā satipaṭṭhānāti? Āmantā. Sabbe dhammā sammappadhānā… iddhipādā… indriyā… balā… bojjhaṅgāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Monks, due to the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, there is the appearance of the seven treasures of the enlightenment factors. Of which seven? There is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of energy, there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of joy, there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of tranquility, there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of concentration, and there is the appearance of the treasure of the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Monks, due to the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, there is the appearance of these seven treasures of the enlightenment factors.” Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Due to the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, do all phenomena become the treasure of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness? This should not be said… Are all phenomena foundations of mindfulness? Yes. Are all phenomena right strivings… bases of psychic power… faculties… powers… enlightenment factors? This should not be said…

Satipaṭṭhānakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Foundations of Mindfulness is concluded.

9. Hevatthikathā

9. The Discourse on 'Thus It Exists'

304. Atītaṃ atthīti? Hevatthi, heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho, natthaṭṭho atthaṭṭho, atthibhāvo natthibhāvo, natthibhāvo atthibhāvo, atthīti vā natthīti vā, natthīti vā [T 0.0178] atthīti vā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

304. Does the past exist? Thus it exists, and thus it does not exist. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence? Is the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence? Is the state of existence the state of non-existence? Is the state of non-existence the state of existence? Regarding 'it exists' or 'it does not exist', and 'it does not exist' or 'it exists'—is this that? Is that this? Are they one in meaning, the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Anāgataṃ atthīti? Hevatthi, heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho, natthaṭṭho atthaṭṭho, atthibhāvo [V 0.0138] natthibhāvo, natthibhāvo atthibhāvo, atthīti vā natthīti vā, natthīti vā atthīti vā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the future exist? Thus it exists, and thus it does not exist. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence? Is the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence? Is the state of existence the state of non-existence? Is the state of non-existence the state of existence? Regarding 'it exists' or 'it does not exist', and 'it does not exist' or 'it exists'—is this that? Is that this? Are they one in meaning, the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Paccuppannaṃ [M 0.0125] atthīti? Hevatthi, heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā[P 0.0160]. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the present exist? Thus it exists, and thus it does not exist. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence?… are they the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

305. Atītaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Kintatthi, kinti natthīti? Atītaṃ atītanti hevatthi, atītaṃ anāgatanti heva natthi, atītaṃ paccuppannanti heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho, natthaṭṭho atthaṭṭho, atthibhāvo natthibhāvo, natthibhāvo atthibhāvo, atthīti vā natthīti vā, natthīti vā atthīti vā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

305. Does the past thus exist, and thus not exist? Yes. In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist? The past exists thus: as the past. The past does not exist thus: as the future. The past does not exist thus: as the present. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence? Is the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence? Is the state of existence the state of non-existence? Is the state of non-existence the state of existence? Regarding 'it exists' or 'it does not exist', and 'it does not exist' or 'it exists'—is this that? Is that this? Are they one in meaning, the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Anāgataṃ [T 0.0179] hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Kintatthi, kinti natthīti? Anāgataṃ anāgatanti hevatthi, anāgataṃ atītanti heva natthi, anāgataṃ paccuppannanti heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho, natthaṭṭho atthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the future thus exist, and thus not exist? Yes. In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist? The future exists thus: as the future. The future does not exist thus: as the past. The future does not exist thus: as the present. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence? Is the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence?… are they the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Paccuppannaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Kintatthi, kinti natthīti? Paccuppannaṃ paccuppannanti hevatthi, paccuppannaṃ [P 0.0161] atītanti heva natthi, paccuppannaṃ anāgatanti heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the present thus exist, and thus not exist? Yes. In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist? The present exists thus: as the present. The present does not exist thus: as the past. The present does not exist thus: as the future. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence?… are they the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Na vattabbaṃ – “atītaṃ hevatthi, heva natthi; anāgataṃ hevatthi, heva natthi; paccuppannaṃ hevatthi, heva natthī”ti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ anāgatanti hevatthi, atītaṃ paccuppannanti hevatthi, anāgataṃ atītanti hevatthi, anāgataṃ paccuppannanti hevatthi, paccuppannaṃ atītanti hevatthi[V 0.0139], paccuppannaṃ anāgatanti hevatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.…Pe…. Tena hi atītaṃ hevatthi heva natthi, anāgataṃ hevatthi heva natthi, paccuppannaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti.

Should it not be said: ‘The past thus exists, thus does not exist; the future thus exists, thus does not exist; the present thus exists, thus does not exist’? Yes. Does the past thus exist as the future? Does the past thus exist as the present? Does the future thus exist as the past? Does the future thus exist as the present? Does the present thus exist as the past? Does the present thus exist as the future? This should not be said.… Therefore, the past thus exists, thus does not exist; the future thus exists, thus does not exist; the present thus exists, thus does not exist.

306. Rūpaṃ atthīti? Hevatthi, heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti[T 0.0180]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho, natthaṭṭho [M 0.0126] atthaṭṭho, atthibhāvo natthibhāvo, natthibhāvo atthibhāvo, atthīti vā natthīti vā, natthīti vā atthīti vā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

306. Does form exist? Thus it exists, and thus it does not exist. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence? Is the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence? Is the state of existence the state of non-existence? Is the state of non-existence the state of existence? Regarding 'it exists' or 'it does not exist', and 'it does not exist' or 'it exists'—is this that? Is that this? Are they one in meaning, the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ atthīti? Hevatthi, heva natthīti. Sevatthi[P 0.0162], seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do feeling… perception… formations… consciousness exist? Thus it exists, and thus it does not exist. Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? This should not be said… Does that very thing exist, and does that very thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence?… are they the same, of equal share, born of that? This should not be said…

Rūpaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Kintatthi, kinti natthīti? Rūpaṃ rūpanti hevatthi, rūpaṃ vedanāti hevaṃ natthi…pe… rūpaṃ saññāti heva natthi…pe… rūpaṃ saṅkhārāti heva natthi…pe… rūpaṃ viññāṇanti heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi, seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does form exist thus, and not exist thus? Yes. In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist? Form as form exists thus; form as feeling does not exist thus... [etc.]... form as perception does not exist thus... [etc.]... form as formations do not exist thus... [etc.]... form as consciousness does not exist thus. Does that same thing exist, and does that same thing not exist? It should not be said thus... [etc.]... Does that same thing exist, and does that same thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence... [etc.]... are they the same, of equal share, born from that? It should not be said thus... [etc.]...

Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Kintatthi, kinti natthīti? Viññāṇaṃ viññāṇanti hevatthi. Viññāṇaṃ rūpanti heva natthi…pe… viññāṇaṃ vedanāti heva natthi…pe… viññāṇaṃ saññāti heva natthi…pe… viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārāti heva natthīti. Sevatthi, seva natthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sevatthi[T 0.0181], seva natthīti? Āmantā. Atthaṭṭho natthaṭṭho…pe… same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na [P 0.0163] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do feeling... perception... formations... does consciousness exist thus, and not exist thus? Yes. In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist? Consciousness as consciousness exists thus. Consciousness as form does not exist thus... [etc.]... consciousness as feeling does not exist thus... [etc.]... consciousness as perception does not exist thus... [etc.]... consciousness as formations do not exist thus. Does that same thing exist, and does that same thing not exist? It should not be said thus... [etc.]... Does that same thing exist, and does that same thing not exist? Yes. Is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence... [etc.]... are they the same, of equal share, born from that? It should not be said thus... [etc.]...

Na vattabbaṃ – “rūpaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti; vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ vedanāti hevatthi…pe… rūpaṃ saññāti hevatthi…pe… rūpaṃ saṅkhārāti hevatthi…pe… rūpaṃ viññāṇanti hevatthi… vedanā… saññā [V 0.0140]… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ rūpanti hevatthi… viññāṇaṃ vedanāti hevatthi… viññāṇaṃ saññāti hevatthi… viññāṇaṃ saṅkhārāti hevatthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi rūpaṃ hevatthi, heva natthi; vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ hevatthi, heva natthīti.

Should it not be said: 'Form exists thus, and does not exist thus; do feeling... perception... formations... does consciousness exist thus, and not exist thus'? Yes. Does form exist thus as feeling... [etc.]... does form exist thus as perception... [etc.]... do form exist thus as formations... [etc.]... does form exist thus as consciousness... do feeling... perception... formations... does consciousness exist thus as form... does consciousness exist thus as feeling... does consciousness exist thus as perception... do consciousness exist thus as formations? It should not be said thus... [etc.]... In that case, form exists thus, and does not exist thus; feeling... perception... formations... consciousness exists thus, and does not exist thus.

Hevatthikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'Thus It Exists' is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary is:

Upalabbho [M 0.0127] parihāni, brahmacariyavāso odhiso;

Pariññā kāmarāgappahānaṃ, sabbatthivādo āyatanaṃ;

Atītānāgato subhaṅgo atītānāgatesu bhāgo (syā.), sabbe dhammā satipaṭṭhānā.

Apprehension, Decline, the Holy Life, Limitation; Full Understanding, the Abandoning of Sensual Desire, the Doctrine that 'Everything Exists', the Sense Bases; The Past and Future Analyzed, All Phenomena, and the Foundations of Mindfulness.

Hevatthi heva natthīti.

Thus It Exists, and Thus It Does Not Exist.

Paṭhamavaggo

The First Chapter.

Mahāvaggo.

The Great Chapter.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(10) 1. Parūpahārakathā

(10) 1. Discussion on What is Brought by Another

307. Atthi [T 0.0182] arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Atthi [P 0.0164] arahato rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

307. Is there for an Arahant an impure emission of semen? Yes. Is there for an Arahant lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire? It should not be said thus…pe….

Natthi [V 0.0141] arahato rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Is there not for an Arahant lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire? Yes. If there is not for an Arahant lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire, then it certainly should not be said: ‘There is for an Arahant an impure emission of semen.’

Atthi puthujjanassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, atthi tassa rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, atthi tassa rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an ordinary person an impure emission of semen, and is there for him lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, the hindrance of sensual desire? Yes. Is there for an Arahant an impure emission of semen, and is there for him lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust…pe… the hindrance of sensual desire? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, natthi tassa rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, natthi tassa rāgo kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant an impure emission of semen, but there is not for him lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust…pe… the hindrance of sensual desire? Yes. Is there for an ordinary person an impure emission of semen, but there is not for him lust, sensual lust, the obsession of sensual lust…pe… the hindrance of sensual desire? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi [T 0.0183][M 0.0128] arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Kenaṭṭhenāti? Handa hi mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti.

Is there for an Arahant an impure emission of semen? Yes. For what reason? Because the deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant.

Mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti? Āmantā. Atthi mārakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na [P 0.0165] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant? Yes. Is there an impure emission of semen for the deities of Māra’s retinue? It should not be said thus…pe….

Natthi mārakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi mārakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantī”ti.

Is there not an impure emission of semen for the deities of Māra’s retinue? Yes. If there is not an impure emission of semen for the deities of Māra’s retinue, then it certainly should not be said: ‘The deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant.’

Mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti? Āmantā. Mārakāyikā devatā attano asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharanti, aññesaṃ asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ [V 0.0142] upasaṃharanti, tassa asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant? Yes. Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause the emission of their own impure semen, do they cause the emission of the impure semen of others, or do they cause the emission of his impure semen? It should not be said thus…pe….

Mārakāyikā devatā neva attano na aññesaṃ na tassa asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti? Āmantā. Hañci mārakāyikā devatā neva attano na aññesaṃ na tassa asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantī”ti.

Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause the emission of neither their own, nor others’, nor his impure semen? Yes. If the deities of Māra’s retinue cause the emission of neither their own, nor others’, nor his impure semen, then it certainly should not be said: ‘The deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant.’

Mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti[T 0.0184]? Āmantā. Lomakūpehi upasaṃharantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant? Yes. Do they cause it through the pores of the skin? It should not be said thus…pe….

308. Mārakāyikā devatā arahato asuciṃ sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ upasaṃharantīti? Āmantā. Kiṃ kāraṇāti? Handa hi vimatiṃ gāhayissāmāti. Atthi arahato vimatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

308. Do the deities of Māra’s retinue cause an impure emission of semen for the Arahant? Yes. For what reason? So that they might cause him to take up doubt. Is there doubt for an Arahant? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato vimatīti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato satthari vimati, dhamme vimati, saṅghe vimati, sikkhāya vimati, pubbante vimati, aparante vimati, pubbantāparante vimati, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there doubt for an Arahant? Yes. Is there for an Arahant doubt concerning the Teacher, doubt concerning the Dhamma, doubt concerning the Saṅgha, doubt concerning the training, doubt concerning the past, doubt concerning the future, doubt concerning the past and future, doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? It should not be said thus…pe….

Natthi [M 0.0129] arahato satthari vimati, dhamme vimati, saṅghe vimati, sikkhāya vimati, pubbante vimati, aparante vimati[P 0.0166], pubbantāparante vimati, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimatīti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato satthari vimati…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato vimatī”ti.

Is there not for an Arahant doubt concerning the Teacher, doubt concerning the Dhamma, doubt concerning the Saṅgha, doubt concerning the training, doubt concerning the past, doubt concerning the future, doubt concerning the past and future, doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? Yes. If there is not for an Arahant doubt concerning the Teacher…pe… doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality, then it certainly should not be said: ‘There is doubt for an Arahant.’

Atthi puthujjanassa vimati, atthi tassa satthari vimati…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimatīti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato vimati, atthi tassa [V 0.0143] satthari vimati…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there doubt for an ordinary person, and is there for him doubt concerning the Teacher…pe… doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? Yes. Is there doubt for an Arahant, and is there for him doubt concerning the Teacher…pe… doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato vimati, natthi tassa satthari vimati…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu [T 0.0185] dhammesu vimatīti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa vimati, natthi tassa satthari vimati…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu vimatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there doubt for an Arahant, but is there not for him doubt concerning the Teacher…pe… doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? Yes. Is there doubt for an ordinary person, but is there not for him doubt concerning the Teacher…pe… doubt concerning phenomena that are dependently arisen through specific conditionality? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi kissa nissandoti? Asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissandoti. Arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissandoti? Āmantā. Ye keci asanti pivanti khādanti sāyanti, sabbesaṃyeva atthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na [P 0.0167] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant an impure emission of semen? Yes. Of what is the impure emission of semen for an Arahant a consequence? It is a consequence of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted. Is the impure emission of semen for an Arahant a consequence of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted? Yes. Do all those whatsoever who eat, drink, chew, and taste have an impure emission of semen? It should not be said thus…pe….

Ye keci asanti pivanti khādanti sāyanti, sabbesaṃyeva atthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Dārakā asanti pivanti khādanti sāyanti, atthi dārakānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Do all those whatsoever who eat, drink, chew, and taste have an impure emission of semen? Yes. Do children who eat, drink, chew, and taste have an impure emission of semen? It should not be said thus.

Paṇḍakā asanti pivanti khādanti sāyanti, atthi paṇḍakānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Eunuchs eat, drink, chew, and taste; do eunuchs have an impure emission of semen? It should not be said thus…pe….

Devā asanti pivanti khādanti sāyanti, atthi devatānaṃ asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Devas eat, drink, chew, and taste; do devas have an impure emission of semen? It should not be said thus…pe….

309. Arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissandoti? Āmantā. Atthi tassa āsayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

309. Is an Arahant's impure emission of semen a consequence of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted? Yes. Does it have a receptacle? It should not be said thus…pe….

Arahato [M 0.0130] uccārapassāvo asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissando, atthi tassa āsayoti[V 0.0144]? Āmantā. Arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa [T 0.0186] nissando, atthi tassa āsayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is an Arahant's excrement and urine a consequence of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, and does it have a receptacle? Yes. Is an Arahant's impure emission of semen a consequence of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, and does it have a receptacle? It should not be said thus…pe….

Arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissando, natthi tassa āsayoti? Āmantā. Arahato uccārapassāvo asitapītakhāyitasāyitassa nissando, natthi tassa āsayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is an Arahant's impure emission of semen a result of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, and is there no receptacle for it? Yes. Is an Arahant's excrement and urine a result of what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, and is there no receptacle for it? It should not be said thus…pe….

310. Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Arahā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, methunaṃ uppādeyya methunaṃ dhammaṃ uppādeyya (sī. syā.), puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyya, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyya, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyya, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāti? Na [P 0.0168] hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. Would an Arahant engage in sexual intercourse, bring about a sexual union, dwell in a dwelling crowded with children, enjoy Kāśī cloth and sandalwood, wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, or take pleasure in gold and silver? It should not be said thus.

Atthi puthujjanassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, puthujjano methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, methunaṃ uppādeyya, puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyya, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyya, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyya, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, arahā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, methunaṃ uppādeyya, puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyya, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyya, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyya, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

310. Does an ordinary person have an impure emission of semen, and would that ordinary person engage in sexual intercourse, bring about a sexual union, dwell in a dwelling crowded with children, enjoy Kāśī cloth and sandalwood, wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, and take pleasure in gold and silver? Yes. Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen, and would that Arahant engage in sexual intercourse, bring about a sexual union, dwell in a dwelling crowded with children, enjoy Kāśī cloth and sandalwood, wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, and take pleasure in gold and silver? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, na ca arahā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, methunaṃ uppādeyya, puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyya, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyya, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyya, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, na ca puthujjano methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, methunaṃ uppādeyya[T 0.0187], puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyya, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyya, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyya, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen, and would that Arahant not engage in sexual intercourse, not bring about a sexual union, not dwell in a dwelling crowded with children, not enjoy Kāśī cloth and sandalwood, not wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, and not take pleasure in gold and silver? Yes. Does an ordinary person have an impure emission of semen, and would that ordinary person not engage in sexual intercourse, not bring about a sexual union, not dwell in a dwelling crowded with children, not enjoy Kāśī cloth and sandalwood, not wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, and not take pleasure in gold and silver? It should not be said thus.

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ [M 0.0131] anuppādadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato [V 0.0145] rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. But is it not so that for an Arahant, lust has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lust has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno… māno pahīno… diṭṭhi pahīnā… vicikicchā pahīnā… thinaṃ pahīnaṃ… uddhaccaṃ pahīnaṃ… ahirikaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. But is it not so that for an Arahant, hatred has been abandoned… delusion has been abandoned… conceit has been abandoned… wrong view has been abandoned… doubt has been abandoned… sloth has been abandoned… restlessness has been abandoned… shamelessness has been abandoned… lack of moral dread has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lack of moral dread has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

311. Atthi [P 0.0169] arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

311. Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. But has not the path for the abandonment of lust been cultivated by the Arahant? Yes. If the path for the abandonment of lust has been cultivated by the Arahant, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

Atthi [T 0.0188] arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgappahānāya satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā…pe… sammappadhānā bhāvitā… iddhipādā bhāvitā… indriyā bhāvitā… balā bhāvitā…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgappahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. But have not the foundations of mindfulness been cultivated by the Arahant for the abandonment of lust… the right strivings… the bases of spiritual power… the spiritual faculties… the spiritual powers… the factors of enlightenment? Yes. If the factors of enlightenment have been cultivated by the Arahant for the abandonment of lust, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. But for the Arahant, for the abandonment of hatred… for the abandonment of delusion… for the abandonment of lack of moral dread, have not the path been cultivated… and the factors of enlightenment been cultivated? Yes. If for the Arahant, for the abandonment of lack of moral dread, the factors of enlightenment have been cultivated, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo [M 0.0132][V 0.0146] pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ [P 0.0170] pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ, sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho katakaraṇīyo…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ[T 0.0189], no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? Yes. Is not an Arahant free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion, one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained one's own goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, liberated through right understanding, with the cross-bar lifted, the moat filled in, the threshold-post uprooted, without a bolt, a noble one, with banner lowered, burden laid down, detached, with victory well-won; for whom suffering is fully understood, its origin abandoned, its cessation realized, the path developed; for whom what should be directly known is directly known, what should be fully understood is fully understood, what should be abandoned is abandoned, what should be developed is developed, what should be realized is realized? Yes. If an Arahant is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion... and what should be realized has been realized, then it surely should not be said, 'An Arahant has an impure emission of semen.'

312. Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhi, paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti. Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato atthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

312. Does an Arahant have an impure emission of semen? For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, there is an impure emission of semen; for an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, there is no impure emission of semen. Does an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma have an impure emission of semen? Yes. Does an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato natthi asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others not have an impure emission of semen? Yes. Does an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma not have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; does he have an impure emission of semen? Yes. For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, lust is abandoned; does he have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Sadhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, hatred is abandoned... delusion is abandoned... lack of moral dread is abandoned; does he have an impure emission of semen? Yes. For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, lack of moral dread is abandoned; does he have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0171]. Paradhammakusalassa [T 0.0190] arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, the path for abandoning lust has been developed... the enlightenment factors have been developed... for abandoning hatred... for abandoning delusion... the path for abandoning lack of moral dread has been developed... the enlightenment factors have been developed; does he have an impure emission of semen? Yes. For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, the enlightenment factors for abandoning lack of moral dread have been developed; does he have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Sadhammakusalo [V 0.0147] arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalo [M 0.0133] arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

An Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion... what is to be realized has been realized; does he have an impure emission of semen? Yes. An Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion... what is to be realized has been realized; does he have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, lust is abandoned; does he not have an impure emission of semen? Yes. For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; does he not have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Paradhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, hatred is abandoned... delusion is abandoned... lack of moral dread is abandoned; does he not have an impure emission of semen? Yes. For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, lack of moral dread is abandoned; does he not have an impure emission of semen? This should not be said...

Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others, has the path for abandoning lust been developed… has the enlightenment factors been developed… for abandoning hatred… for abandoning delusion… has the path for abandoning lack of moral dread been developed… have the enlightenment factors been developed; does he not have an impure seminal emission? Yes, that is so. For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, have the enlightenment factors for abandoning lack of moral dread been developed; does he not have an impure seminal emission? This should not be said…

Paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ [T 0.0191] sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalo [P 0.0172] arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

An Arahant who is skilled in the Dhamma of others is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… what is to be realized has been realized; does he not have an impure seminal emission? Yes, that is so. An Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… what is to be realized has been realized; does he not have an impure seminal emission? This should not be said…

313. Atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “ye te ye keci (sī.), bhikkhave, bhikkhū puthujjanā sīlasampannā satā sampajānā niddaṃ okkamanti, tesaṃ asuci na muccati. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bāhirakā isayo kāmesu vītarāgā, tesampi asuci na muccati. Aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṃ arahato asuci mucceyyā”ti mahāva. 353 atthato samānaṃ; a. ni. 5.210 passitabbaṃ. Attheva [V 0.0148] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato asuci sukkavissaṭṭhī”ti.

313. Does an Arahant have an impure seminal emission? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, for those monks who are worldlings, accomplished in virtue, mindful, and clearly comprehending when they fall asleep, for them an impure emission is discharged. Monks, even for those ascetics outside the teaching who are free from lust for sensual pleasures, for them too an impure emission is discharged. It is impossible, monks, it is no occasion that an Arahant would have an impure emission discharged.’ Does such a sutta exist? Yes. In that case, it should not be said: ‘An Arahant has an impure seminal emission.’

Na [M 0.0134] vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato parūpahāro”ti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ pare upasaṃhareyyunti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ pare upasaṃhareyyuṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato parūpahāro”ti.

Should it not be said: ‘An Arahant has things brought by others’? Yes, it should not be said. But do not others bring robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick to an Arahant? Yes, they do. If others bring robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick to an Arahant, then surely it should be said: ‘An Arahant has things brought by others.’

Arahato cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ pare upasaṃhareyyunti, atthi arahato parūpahāroti? Āmantā. Arahato sotāpattiphalaṃ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā arahattaṃ vā pare upasaṃhareyyunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since others bring robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick to an Arahant, does an Arahant have things brought by others? Yes. Can others bring the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or Arahantship to an Arahant? This should not be said…

Parūpahārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on What is Brought by Others is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(11) 2. Aññāṇakathā

2. (11) 2. The Discussion on Not-Knowing

314. Atthi [T 0.0192][P 0.0173] arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Natthi arahato avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there not-knowing for an Arahant? Yes. Is there for an Arahant ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? This should not be said. Is there not for an Arahant ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? Yes, there is not. If there is not for an Arahant ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance, then it should not be said, ‘There is not-knowing for an Arahant.’

Atthi [V 0.0149] puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ, atthi tassa avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, atthi tassa avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

314. There is not-knowing for a worldling; is there also for them ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? Yes. There is not-knowing for an Arahant; is there also for them ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? This should not be said.

Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, natthi tassa avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti[M 0.0135]? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ[T 0.0193], natthi tassa avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānusayo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

There is not-knowing for an Arahant; is there not for them ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? Yes. There is not-knowing for a worldling; is there not for them ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the latent tendency of ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance? This should not be said.

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Arahā aññāṇapakato pāṇaṃ haneyya, adinnaṃ ādiyeyya, musā bhaṇeyya, pisuṇaṃ bhaṇeyya, pharusaṃ bhaṇeyya, samphaṃ palapeyya, sandhiṃ chindeyya, nillopaṃ hareyya, ekāgāriyaṃ kareyya, paripanthe tiṭṭheyya, paradāraṃ gaccheyya, gāmaghātaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātaṃ kareyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there not-knowing for an Arahant? Yes. Would an Arahant, on account of not-knowing, kill a living being, take what is not given, speak falsely, speak slanderously, speak harshly, engage in frivolous talk, break into a house, commit robbery, commit burglary, lie in ambush, go to another's wife, plunder a village, or plunder a market-town? This should not be said.

Atthi puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ, puthujjano aññāṇapakato pāṇaṃ [P 0.0174] haneyya, adinnaṃ ādiyeyya, musā bhaṇeyya…pe… gāmaghātaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, arahā aññāṇapakato pāṇaṃ haneyya, adinnaṃ ādiyeyya…pe… gāmaghātaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātaṃ kareyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

There is not-knowing for a worldling; would a worldling, on account of not-knowing, kill a living being, take what is not given, speak falsely… plunder a village, or plunder a market-town? Yes. There is not-knowing for an Arahant; would an Arahant, on account of not-knowing, kill a living being, take what is not given… plunder a village, or plunder a market-town? This should not be said.

Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, na ca arahā aññāṇapakato pāṇaṃ haneyya, adinnaṃ ādiyeyya…pe… gāmaghātaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ, na ca puthujjano aññāṇapakato pāṇaṃ haneyya, adinnaṃ ādiyeyya…pe… gāmaghātaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātaṃ kareyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

There is not-knowing for an Arahant; and would an Arahant, on account of not-knowing, not kill a living being, not take what is not given… not plunder a village, or not plunder a market-town? Yes.
