There is not-knowing for a worldling; and would a worldling, on account of not-knowing, not kill a living being, not take what is not given… not plunder a village, or not plunder a market-town? This should not be said.

Atthi [T 0.0194] arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ, sikkhāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there not-knowing for an Arahant? Yes. Is there for an Arahant not-knowing regarding the Teacher, not-knowing regarding the Dhamma, not-knowing regarding the Saṅgha, not-knowing regarding the training, not-knowing regarding the past, not-knowing regarding the future, not-knowing regarding the past and future, and not-knowing regarding phenomena that are dependently arisen through this conditionality? This should not be said.

Natthi [V 0.0150] arahato satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ, sikkhāya aññāṇaṃ, pubbante aññāṇaṃ, aparante aññāṇaṃ, pubbantāparante aññāṇaṃ, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there not for an Arahant ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha, ignorance regarding the training, ignorance regarding the past, ignorance regarding the future, ignorance regarding the past and future, and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality? Yes. If there is not for an Arahant ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha… and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

Atthi puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ, atthi tassa satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇanti[M 0.0136]? Āmantā. Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, atthi tassa satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇanti? Na [P 0.0175] hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there ignorance for a worldling, and is there for them ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha… and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality? Yes. Is there ignorance for an Arahant, and is there for them ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha… and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality? It should not be said thus.

Atthi arahato aññāṇaṃ, natthi tassa satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu [T 0.0195] dhammesu aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa aññāṇaṃ, natthi tassa satthari aññāṇaṃ, dhamme aññāṇaṃ, saṅghe aññāṇaṃ…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

There is ignorance for an Arahant; is there not for them ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha… and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality? Yes. There is ignorance for a worldling; is there not for them ignorance regarding the Teacher, ignorance regarding the Dhamma, ignorance regarding the Saṅgha… and ignorance regarding phenomena arisen from specific conditionality? It should not be said thus.

315. Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

315. Is there ignorance for an Arahant? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and of a nature not to arise in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and of a nature not to arise in the future, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance for an Arahant? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant, hatred is abandoned… delusion is abandoned… lack of moral dread is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and of a nature not to arise in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lack of moral dread is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to non-existence, and of a nature not to arise in the future, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgappahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance for an Arahant? Yes. Has not the Arahant developed the path for the abandoning of lust… and have not the factors of enlightenment been developed? Yes. If the Arahant has developed the factors of enlightenment for the abandoning of lust, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito [V 0.0151] …pe… bojjhaṅgā [T 0.0196] bhāvitāti? Āmantā[P 0.0176]. Hañci arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance for an Arahant? Yes. Has not the Arahant developed the path for the abandoning of hatred… for the abandoning of delusion… for the abandoning of lack of moral dread… and have not the factors of enlightenment been developed? Yes. If the Arahant has developed the factors of enlightenment for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

Atthi [M 0.0137] arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vītarāgo…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance for an Arahant? Yes. Is not the Arahant free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… and has he not realized what is to be realized? Yes. If the Arahant is free from lust… and has realized what is to be realized, then indeed, O you, it should not be said that 'there is ignorance for an Arahant'.

316. Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi aññāṇaṃ, paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi aññāṇanti. Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato atthi aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

316. Is there ignorance for an Arahant? For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, there is ignorance; for an Arahant who is skilled in other dhammas, there is no ignorance. Is there ignorance for an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma? Yes. Is there ignorance for an Arahant who is skilled in other dhammas? It should not be said thus…

Paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato natthi aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no ignorance for an Arahant who is skilled in other dhammas? Yes. Is there no ignorance for an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma? It should not be said thus…

Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; is there ignorance for him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, lust is abandoned; is there ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Sadhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, hatred is abandoned… delusion is abandoned… lack of moral dread is abandoned; is there ignorance for him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, lack of moral dread is abandoned; is there ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Sadhammakusalassa [T 0.0197] arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi [V 0.0152] tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgappahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na [P 0.0177] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, the path for the abandoning of lust has been developed… the factors of enlightenment have been developed; is there ignorance for him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, the factors of enlightenment for the abandoning of lust have been developed; is there ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Sadhammakusalassa arahato dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, the path for the abandoning of hatred has been developed… for the abandoning of delusion… for the abandoning of lack of moral dread… the factors of enlightenment have been developed; is there ignorance for him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, the factors of enlightenment for the abandoning of lack of moral dread have been developed; is there ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

An Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there ignorance for him? Yes. An Arahant skilled in other dhammas is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Paradhammakusalassa [M 0.0138] arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, lust is abandoned; is there no ignorance for him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; is there no ignorance for him? It should not be said thus…

Paradhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in others' dhammas, is hatred abandoned... is delusion abandoned... is lack of moral dread abandoned, and is there no ignorance in him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, is lack of moral dread abandoned, and is there no ignorance in him? This should not be said.

Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā [T 0.0198] bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato anottappapahānāya bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an Arahant skilled in others' dhammas, has the path for the abandoning of lust been developed... have the factors of enlightenment been developed... for the abandoning of hatred... for the abandoning of delusion... has the path for the abandoning of lack of moral dread been developed... have the factors of enlightenment been developed, and is there no ignorance in him? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, have the factors of enlightenment for the abandoning of lack of moral dread been developed, and is there no ignorance in him? This should not be said.

Paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Āmantā[P 0.0178]. Sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho [V 0.0153] …pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa aññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is an Arahant skilled in others' dhammas free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion... and has that which is to be realized been realized by him, and is there no ignorance in him? Yes. Is an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion... and has that which is to be realized been realized by him, and is there no ignorance in him? This should not be said.

317. Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ jānatāhaṃ (sī.), jānatvāhaṃ (syā. pī. ka.), bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato. Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti? ‘Iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo, iti vedanā…pe… iti saññā… iti saṅkhārā… iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 3.101; itivu. 102; saṃ. ni. 5.1095. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

317. Is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know and does not see. And for one who knows what, for one who sees what, does the destruction of the taints occur? "This is form, this is the origin of form, this is the cessation of form; this is feeling... this is perception... these are formations... this is consciousness, this is the origin of consciousness, this is the cessation of consciousness." Monks, it is for one who knows thus and sees thus that the destruction of the taints occurs.' Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'There is ignorance in an Arahant'.

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato [T 0.0199] no apassato. Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo [M 0.0139] hoti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti – bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti – jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti – jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti – jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 5.1095. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or does not see. And what, Monks, for one who knows what, for one who sees what, does the destruction of the taints occur? ‘This is suffering’—Monks, for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs. ‘This is the origin of suffering’—for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs. ‘This is the cessation of suffering’—for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs. ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs. Thus, Monks, for one who knows thus and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs.” Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant.”

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya, sabbañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ [P 0.0179] virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti saṃ. ni. 4.26; itivu. 7 itivuttakepi! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, one who does not directly know, fully understand, become dispassionate towards, and abandon all, is incapable of the destruction of suffering. But, Monks, one who directly knows, fully understands, becomes dispassionate towards, and abandons all, is capable of the destruction of suffering.” Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant.”

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said:

“Sahāvassa [V 0.0154] dassanasampadāya,

Tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti;

Sakkāyadiṭṭhī vicikicchitañca,

Sīlabbataṃ vāpi yadatthi kiñci;

Catūhapāyehi ca vippamutto,

Chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba kātu”nti.

“Together with his accomplishment of vision, three things are abandoned by him: identity view, doubt, and whatever adherence to rules and observances there may be. He is freed from the four woeful states and is incapable of committing the six heinous acts.”

Attheva [T 0.0200] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant.”

Atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti, saha dassanuppādā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, at the time when the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arises in a noble disciple—‘Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation’—then, Monks, with the arising of vision, three fetters are abandoned by the noble disciple: identity view, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances.” Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant.”

Na [M 0.0140] vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ na jāneyya, maggāmaggaṃ na jāneyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāmaṃ na jāneyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ na jāneyya, maggāmaggaṃ [P 0.0180] na jāneyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāmaṃ na jāneyya, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato aññāṇa”nti.

Should it not be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant”? Yes. But would an Arahant not know the names and clans of men and women, not know the path and the non-path, not know the names of grasses, wood, and trees? Yes. If an Arahant does not know the names and clans of men and women, does not know the path and the non-path, does not know the names of grasses, wood, and trees, then it should indeed be said, “There is ignorance in an Arahant.”

Arahā itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ na jāneyya, maggāmaggaṃ na jāneyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāmaṃ na jāneyyāti, atthi arahato aññāṇanti? Āmantā. Arahā sotāpattiphalaṃ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā arahattaṃ vā na jāneyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since an Arahant would not know the names and clans of men and women, would not know the path and the non-path, and would not know the names of grasses, wood, and trees, is there ignorance in an Arahant? Yes. Would an Arahant not know the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or Arahantship? This should not be said.

Aññāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Ignorance is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(12) 3. Kaṅkhākathā

(12) 3. Discussion on Doubt

318. Atthi [T 0.0201][V 0.0155] arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

2. Is there doubt in an Arahant? Yes. Is there for an Arahant sceptical doubt, the obsession of sceptical doubt, the fetter of sceptical doubt, or the hindrance of sceptical doubt? This should not be said.

Natthi arahato vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Is there not for an Arahant sceptical doubt, the obsession of sceptical doubt, the fetter of sceptical doubt, or the hindrance of sceptical doubt? Yes. If there is not for an Arahant sceptical doubt, the obsession of sceptical doubt, the fetter of sceptical doubt, and the hindrance of sceptical doubt, then it should certainly not be said, 'There is doubt in an Arahant.'

Atthi puthujjanassa kaṅkhā, atthi tassa vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato kaṅkhā, atthi tassa vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a worldling have doubt, and does he have uncertainty, the obsession of uncertainty, the fetter of uncertainty, and the hindrance of uncertainty? Yes. Does an Arahant have doubt, and does he have uncertainty, the obsession of uncertainty, the fetter of uncertainty, and the hindrance of uncertainty? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato kaṅkhā, natthi tassa vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Āmantā[P 0.0181]. Atthi puthujjanassa kaṅkhā, natthi [M 0.0141] tassa vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant have doubt, but does he not have uncertainty, the obsession of uncertainty, the fetter of uncertainty, and the hindrance of uncertainty? Yes. Does a worldling have doubt, but does he not have uncertainty, the obsession of uncertainty, the fetter of uncertainty, and the hindrance of uncertainty? It should not be said thus…pe….

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā, saṅghe kaṅkhā, sikkhāya kaṅkhā, pubbante kaṅkhā, aparante kaṅkhā, pubbantāparante kaṅkhā, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. Does an Arahant have doubt in the Teacher, doubt in the Dhamma, doubt in the Saṅgha, doubt in the training, doubt about the past, doubt about the future, doubt about the past and future, doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? It should not be said thus.

Natthi [T 0.0202] arahato satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti[V 0.0156]? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have no doubt in the Teacher, no doubt in the Dhamma…pe… no doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? Yes. If an Arahant has no doubt in the Teacher, no doubt in the Dhamma…pe… no doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena, then surely it should not be said, 'An Arahant has doubt.'

Atthi puthujjanassa kaṅkhā, atthi tassa satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato kaṅkhā, atthi tassa satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does a worldling have doubt, and does he have doubt in the Teacher, doubt in the Dhamma…pe… doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? Yes. Does an Arahant have doubt, and does he have doubt in the Teacher, doubt in the Dhamma…pe… doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? It should not be said thus.

Atthi arahato kaṅkhā, natthi tassa satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa kaṅkhā, natthi tassa satthari kaṅkhā, dhamme kaṅkhā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does an Arahant have doubt, but does he have no doubt in the Teacher, no doubt in the Dhamma…pe… no doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? Yes. Does a worldling have doubt, but does he have no doubt in the Teacher, no doubt in the Dhamma…pe… no doubt about specifically conditioned, dependently arisen phenomena? It should not be said thus.

319. Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā[P 0.0182]. Nanu arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

319. Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root extirpated, made like a palm-stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root extirpated, made like a palm-stump, brought to non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise again in the future, then surely it should not be said, 'An Arahant has doubt.'

Atthi [T 0.0203] arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā; nanu arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant hatred is abandoned…pe… delusion is abandoned…pe… shamelessness is abandoned…pe… the path for the abandoning of lust is developed…pe… the factors of enlightenment are developed…pe… for the abandoning of hatred…pe… for the abandoning of shamelessness the path is developed…pe… the factors of enlightenment are developed; is it not so that an Arahant is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion…pe… has realized that which is to be realized? Yes. If an Arahant is free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion…pe… has realized that which is to be realized, then surely it should not be said, 'An Arahant has doubt.'

320. Atthi [M 0.0142] arahato kaṅkhāti? Sadhammakusalassa arahato [P 0.0183] atthi kaṅkhā, paradhammakusalassa [V 0.0157] arahato natthi kaṅkhāti. Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato atthi kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

320. Does an Arahant have doubt? For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, there is doubt; for an Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma, there is no doubt. Does an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma have doubt? Yes. Does an Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma have doubt? It should not be said thus…pe….

Paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato natthi kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma have no doubt? Yes. Does the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma have no doubt? It should not be said thus…pe….

Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; does he have doubt? Yes. For the Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma, lust is abandoned; does he have doubt? It should not be said thus…pe….

Sadhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya [T 0.0204] maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho [P 0.0184]…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, hatred is abandoned…pe… delusion is abandoned…pe… shamelessness is abandoned…pe… the path for the abandoning of lust is developed…pe… the factors of enlightenment are developed…pe… for the abandoning of hatred…pe… for the abandoning of delusion…pe… for the abandoning of shamelessness the path is developed…pe… the factors of enlightenment are developed…pe… the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma is without lust, without hatred, without delusion…pe… that which is to be realized is realized. Does he have doubt? Yes. The Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma is without lust, without hatred, without delusion…pe… that which is to be realized is realized. Does he have doubt? It should not be said thus…pe… For the Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma, lust is abandoned. Does he have no doubt? Yes. For the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned. Does he have no doubt? It should not be said thus…pe….

Paradhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… mohappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa kaṅkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma, hatred is abandoned…pe… delusion is abandoned…pe… shamelessness is abandoned…pe… the path for abandoning lust is developed…pe… the enlightenment factors are developed…pe… for abandoning hatred…pe… for abandoning delusion…pe… for abandoning shamelessness, the path is developed…pe… the enlightenment factors are developed…pe… the Arahant skilled in another's Dhamma is without lust, without hatred, without delusion…pe… what is to be realized has been realized. Does he have no doubt? Yes. The Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma is without lust, without hatred, without delusion…pe… what is to be realized has been realized. Does he have no doubt? It should not be said thus…pe….

321. Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no [M 0.0143] apassato! Kiñca, bhikkhave[V 0.0158], jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti[P 0.0185]? ‘Iti rūpaṃ’…pe… ‘iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

321. Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see. And what, monks, does one know and see for the destruction of the taints to occur? ‘Such is form… such is the passing away of consciousness’—thus, monks, for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs.” Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato! Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti, bhikkhave…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti. Evaṃ kho[T 0.0205], bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know or see. And what, monks, does one know and see for the destruction of the taints to occur? ‘This is suffering,’ monks… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs. Thus, monks, for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints occurs.” Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; sabbañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, one who does not directly know all, does not fully understand it, is not dispassionate towards it, and does not abandon it, is incapable of the destruction of suffering; and, monks, one who directly knows all, fully understands it, is dispassionate towards it, and abandons it, is capable of the destruction of suffering.” Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sahāvassa dassanasampadāya [P 0.0186]…pe… chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba kātu”nti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: 'Simultaneously with his attainment of vision… he is incapable of committing the six heinous acts.' Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'An Arahant has doubt.'

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi [T 0.0206] – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti, saha dassanuppādā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, at the time when the stainless, immaculate Dhamma-eye arose in a noble disciple—‘Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation’—then, monks, with the arising of vision, three fetters are abandoned by the noble disciple: self-identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and observances.” Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said:

“Yadā [V 0.0159] have pātubhavanti dhammā,

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Athassa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā,

Yato pajānāti sahetudhammanti.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, then all his doubts vanish, for he understands the phenomenon along with its cause.”

“Yadā [M 0.0144] have pātubhavanti dhammā,

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Athassa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā,

Yato khayaṃ paccayānaṃ avedīti.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, then all his doubts vanish, for he has understood the destruction of conditions.”

“Yadā have pātubhavanti dhammā,

Ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa;

Vidhūpayaṃ tiṭṭhati mārasenaṃ,

Sūriyova suriyova (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) obhāsayamantalikkhanti mahāva. 3; udā. 3.

“When, indeed, phenomena become manifest to the ardent, meditating brahmin, he stands dispelling Māra’s army, like the sun illuminating the sky.”

“Yā kāci kaṅkhā idha vā huraṃ vā,

Sakavediyā vā paravediyā vā;

Jhāyino [T 0.0207] ye jhāyino (udāne) tā pajahanti sabbā,

Ātāpino [P 0.0187] brahmacariyaṃ carantāti udā. 47 udānepi.

“Whatever doubts there are, whether in this world or the next, whether concerning one's own experience or another's, those who are meditating, ardent, and living the holy life abandon them all.”

“Ye kaṅkhāsamatikkantā, kaṅkhābhūtesu pāṇisu;

Asaṃsayā visaṃyuttā, tesu dinnaṃ mahapphalanti.

“Those who have overcome doubt among beings who are subject to doubt, who are free from uncertainty and detached—a gift given to them bears great fruit.”

“Etādisī dhammapakāsanettha,

Na tattha kiṃ kaṅkhati koci sāvako;

Nitthiṇṇaoghaṃ nitiṇṇaoghaṃ (sī. ka.), nittiṇṇaoghaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) vicikicchachinnaṃ,

Buddhaṃ namassāma jinaṃ janindā”ti dī. ni. 2.354.

“Such is the exposition of the Dhamma here; no disciple has any doubt therein. We pay homage to the Buddha—who has crossed the flood, who has cut off doubt, the Victor—O lord of men.”

Attheva [V 0.0160] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā itthipurisānaṃ nāmagotte kaṅkheyya, maggāmagge kaṅkheyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāme kaṅkheyyā”ti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā itthipurisānaṃ nāmagotte kaṅkheyya, maggāmagge kaṅkheyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāme kaṅkheyya; tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato kaṅkhā”ti.

Should it not be said: “An Arahant has doubt”? Yes. But might not an Arahant have doubt about the names and clans of women and men, have doubt about the path and the non-path, have doubt about the names of grasses, wood, and trees? Yes. If an Arahant might have doubt about the names and clans of women and men, have doubt about the path and the non-path, and have doubt about the names of grasses, wood, and trees, then indeed it should be said: “An Arahant has doubt.”

Arahā [M 0.0145] itthipurisānaṃ nāmagotte kaṅkheyya, maggāmagge kaṅkheyya, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāme kaṅkheyyāti, atthi arahato kaṅkhāti? Āmantā. Arahā sotāpattiphale vā sakadāgāmiphale vā anāgāmiphale vā arahatte vā kaṅkheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since an Arahant might have doubt about the names and clans of men and women, might have doubt about the path and the non-path, might have doubt about the names of grass, wood, and trees, does an Arahant have doubt? Yes. Would an Arahant have doubt about the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or Arahantship? This should not be said….

Kaṅkhākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Doubt is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(13) 4. Paravitāraṇakathā

(13) 4. Discourse on Causing Another to Transgress

322. Atthi [T 0.0208] arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā[P 0.0188]. Arahā paraneyyo parapattiyo parapaccayo parapaṭibaddhabhū, na jānāti na passati sammūḷho asampajānoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

2. Is an Arahant guided by another? Yes. Is an Arahant one who can be led by another, convinced by another, conditioned by another, dependent on another; does he not know, not see, being confused and without clear comprehension? This should not be said….

Nanu arahā na paraneyyo na parapattiyo na parapaccayo na parapaṭibaddhabhū jānāti passati asammūḷho sampajānoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā na paraneyyo na parapattiyo na parapaccayo na parapaṭibaddhabhū, jānāti passati asammūḷho sampajāno, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is it not so that an Arahant cannot be led by another, cannot be convinced by another, is not conditioned by another, is not dependent on another, and that he knows and sees, being unconfused and with clear comprehension? Yes. If an Arahant cannot be led by another, cannot be convinced by another, is not conditioned by another, is not dependent on another, and knows and sees, being unconfused and with clear comprehension, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'an Arahant is guided by another.'

Atthi [V 0.0161] puthujjanassa paravitāraṇā, so ca paraneyyo parapattiyo parapaccayo parapaṭibaddhabhū, na jānāti na passati sammūḷho asampajānoti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato paravitāraṇā, so ca paraneyyo parapattiyo parapaccayo parapaṭibaddhabhū, na jānāti na passati sammūḷho asampajānoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

322. Is a worldling guided by another, and is he one who can be led by another, convinced by another, conditioned by another, dependent on another; does he not know, not see, being confused and without clear comprehension? Yes. Is an Arahant guided by another, and is he one who can be led by another, convinced by another, conditioned by another, dependent on another; does he not know, not see, being confused and without clear comprehension? This should not be said….

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇā, so ca na paraneyyo na parapattiyo na parapaccayo na parapaṭibaddhabhū, jānāti passati asammūḷho sampajānoti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa paravitāraṇā, so ca na paraneyyo na parapattiyo na parapaccayo na parapaṭibaddhabhū, jānāti passati asammūḷho sampajānoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant instruction by another, and is he one who cannot be led by another, cannot be made to doubt by another, is not conditioned by another, is not bound to another, and who knows and sees, being unconfused and with clear comprehension? Yes. Is there for a worldling instruction by another, and is he one who cannot be led by another, cannot be made to doubt by another, is not conditioned by another, is not bound to another, and who knows and sees, being unconfused and with clear comprehension? This should not be said…

Atthi [T 0.0209] arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā, saṅghe paravitāraṇā, sikkhāya [M 0.0146] paravitāraṇā, pubbante paravitāraṇā, aparante paravitāraṇā, pubbantāparante paravitāraṇā, idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Na [P 0.0189] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant instruction by another? Yes. Is there for an Arahant instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma, concerning the Saṅgha, concerning the training, concerning the past, concerning the future, concerning the past and future, or concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? This should not be said…

Natthi arahato satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idapaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi arahato satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there for an Arahant no instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? Yes. If there is for an Arahant no instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is for an Arahant instruction by another.'

Atthi puthujjanassa paravitāraṇā, atthi tassa satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato paravitāraṇā, atthi tassa satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For a worldling there is instruction by another; is there for him instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? Yes. For an Arahant there is instruction by another; is there for him instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? This should not be said…

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇā, natthi tassa satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Atthi puthujjanassa [V 0.0162] paravitāraṇā, natthi tassa satthari paravitāraṇā, dhamme paravitāraṇā…pe… idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu [T 0.0210] dhammesu paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant instruction by another, but for him is there no instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? Yes. Is there for a worldling instruction by another, but for him is there no instruction by another concerning the Teacher, concerning the Dhamma… concerning phenomena that have arisen dependently through specific conditionality? This should not be said…

323. Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

323. Is there for an Arahant instruction by another? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root is cut off, it is made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-becoming, and is of a nature not to arise in the future? Yes. If for an Arahant, lust is abandoned, its root is cut off, it is made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-becoming, and is of a nature not to arise in the future, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is for an Arahant instruction by another.'

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0190] arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṅkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ…pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… nanu [M 0.0147] arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatanti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there for an Arahant instruction by another? Yes. Is it not so that for an Arahant, aversion is abandoned… delusion is abandoned… lack of moral dread is abandoned, its root is cut off, it is made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-becoming, and is of a nature not to arise in the future… the path for the abandoning of lust has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… for the abandoning of aversion… for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, the path has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… Is it not so that an Arahant is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized? Yes. If an Arahant is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion, and has realized what is to be realized, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is for an Arahant instruction by another.'

324. Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi paravitāraṇā, paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi paravitāraṇāti. Sadhammakusalassa arahato atthi paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato atthi paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

324. Is there for an Arahant instruction by another? For an Arahant who is skilled in his own Dhamma, there is instruction by another; for an Arahant who is skilled in other dhammas, there is no instruction by another. Is there for an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma instruction by another? Yes. Is there for an Arahant skilled in other dhammas instruction by another? This should not be said…

Paradhammakusalassa arahato natthi paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā[P 0.0191]. Sadhammakusalassa arahato natthi paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ [T 0.0211] vattabbe…pe….

Is there for an Arahant skilled in other dhammas no instruction by another? Yes. Is there for an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma no instruction by another? This should not be said…

Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, atthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; is there for him instruction by another? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, lust is abandoned; is there for him instruction by another? This should not be said.

Sadhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno…pe… moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ [V 0.0163] …pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, atthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, aversion is abandoned… delusion is abandoned… lack of moral dread is abandoned… for the abandoning of lust, the path has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… for the abandoning of aversion… for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, the path has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there for him instruction by another? Yes. For the Arahant skilled in other dhammas, who is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there for him instruction by another? This should not be said…

Paradhammakusalassa [P 0.0192] arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalassa arahato rāgo pahīno, natthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For an Arahant skilled in other dhammas, lust is abandoned; is there for him no instruction by another? Yes. For an Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, lust is abandoned; is there for him no instruction by another? This should not be said.

Paradhammakusalassa arahato doso pahīno, moho pahīno…pe… anottappaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… rāgappahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… dosappahānāya…pe… anottappapahānāya [T 0.0212] maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā…pe… paradhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo [M 0.0148] vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Sadhammakusalo arahā vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, natthi tassa paravitāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the Arahant skilled in other dhammas, aversion is abandoned, delusion is abandoned… lack of moral dread is abandoned… for the abandoning of lust, the path has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… for the abandoning of aversion… for the abandoning of lack of moral dread, the path has been developed… the factors of awakening have been developed… the Arahant skilled in other dhammas is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there for him no instruction by another? Yes. For the Arahant skilled in his own Dhamma, who is free from lust, free from aversion, free from delusion… and has realized what is to be realized; is there for him no instruction by another? This should not be said…

325. Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato! Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti? ‘Iti rūpaṃ’…pe… ‘iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0193]. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

325. Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know, not for one who does not see. And for one who knows what, monks, for one who sees what, does the destruction of the taints come to be? “Such is form”…pe… “such is the cessation of consciousness.” Thus, monks, for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, the destruction of the taints comes to be.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jānatohaṃ, bhikkhave, passato āsavānaṃ khayaṃ vadāmi, no ajānato no apassato! Kiñca, bhikkhave, jānato kiṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti – bhikkhave, jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo [V 0.0164] hoti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti – jānato passato āsavānaṃ khayo hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato evaṃ passato āsavānaṃ khayo hotī”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ [T 0.0213] – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I declare the destruction of the taints for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know, not for one who does not see. And for one who knows what, monks, for one who sees what, does the destruction of the taints come to be? “This is suffering”—for one who knows and sees thus, monks, the destruction of the taints comes to be. “This is the origin of suffering”…pe… “This is the cessation of suffering”…pe… “This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering”—for one who knows and sees thus, the destruction of the taints comes to be. Thus, monks, for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, the destruction of the taints comes to be.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, anabhijānaṃ aparijānaṃ avirājayaṃ appajahaṃ abhabbo dukkhakkhayāya; sabbañca kho, bhikkhave, abhijānaṃ parijānaṃ virājayaṃ pajahaṃ bhabbo dukkhakkhayāyā”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, without directly knowing and fully understanding all, without dispassion towards and abandoning it, one is incapable of the destruction of suffering; and, monks, by directly knowing and fully understanding all, with dispassion towards and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sahāvassa dassanasampadāya…pe… chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba kātu”nti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [P 0.0194] hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘With the very accomplishment of vision…pe… he is incapable of committing the six heinous acts.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Atthi [M 0.0149] arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti, saha dassanuppādā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, at the time when the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arises in the noble disciple—“Whatever is of the nature to arise is all of the nature to cease”—then, monks, with the very arising of that vision, three fetters are abandoned by the noble disciple: personality-view, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Nāhaṃ sahissāmi gamissāmi (sī. syā. ka.), samīhāmi (pī.) pamocanāya,

Kathaṅkathiṃ dhotaka kañci kiñci (ka.) loke;

Dhammañca [T 0.0214] seṭṭhaṃ abhijānamāno,

Evaṃ tuvaṃ oghamimaṃ taresī”ti su. ni. 1070 suttanipāte; cūḷani. 33 dhotakamāṇavapucchāniddesa.

‘I am not able, O Dhotaka, to release from doubt anyone in the world. But having directly known the supreme Dhamma, you will thus cross this flood.’

Attheva [V 0.0165] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Na vattabbaṃ – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu arahato itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, maggāmaggaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāmaṃ pare vitāreyyunti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, maggāmaggaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ [P 0.0195] nāmaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato paravitāraṇā”ti.

Should it not be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant’? Yes. But do not others make known to an Arahant the names and clans of men and women? Do not others make known the path and the not-path? Do not others make known the names of grass, wood, and forest trees? Yes. If others make known to an Arahant the names and clans of men and women, make known the path and the not-path, and make known the names of grass, wood, and forest trees, then, sir, it should indeed be said: ‘There is guidance from another for an Arahant.’

Arahato itthipurisānaṃ nāmagottaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, maggāmaggaṃ pare vitāreyyuṃ, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatīnaṃ nāmaṃ pare vitāreyyunti, atthi arahato paravitāraṇāti? Āmantā. Arahato sotāpattiphalaṃ vā sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vā anāgāmiphalaṃ vā arahattaṃ vā pare vitāreyyunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since others make known to an Arahant the names and clans of men and women, the path and the not-path, and the names of grass, wood, and forest trees, is there guidance from another for an Arahant? Yes. But do others make known to an Arahant the fruit of stream-entry, or the fruit of once-returning, or the fruit of non-returning, or Arahantship? This should not be said thus… …pe…

Paravitāraṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Guidance from Another is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(14) 5. Vacībhedakathā

5. Discussion on the Utterance of Speech

326. Samāpannassa [T 0.0215][M 0.0150] atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Sabbattha samāpannānaṃ atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

326. For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. In every case, for those who have entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Sabbadā samāpannānaṃ atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For those who have entered an attainment, is there always an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa [V 0.0166] atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Sabbesaṃ samāpannānaṃ atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For all who have entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Sabbasamāpattīsu atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. In all attainments, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Samāpannassa atthi kāyabhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered an attainment, is there bodily action? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa [P 0.0196] natthi kāyabhedoti? Āmantā. Samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there no bodily action? Yes. For one who has entered an attainment, is there no utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa atthi vācā, atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Samāpannassa atthi kāyo, atthi kāyabhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there speech, and is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered an attainment, is there a body, and is there bodily action? It should not be said thus... pe...

Samāpannassa atthi kāyo, natthi kāyabhedoti? Āmantā. Samāpannassa atthi vācā, natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there a body, but no bodily action? Yes. For one who has entered an attainment, is there speech, but no utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... pe...

327. Dukkhanti [T 0.0216] jānanto dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Samudayoti jānanto samudayoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

327. Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' speak the words, 'This is suffering'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is the origin,' speak the words, 'This is the origin'? It should not be said thus... pe...

Dukkhanti jānanto dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Nirodhoti jānanto nirodhoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' speak the words, 'This is suffering'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is cessation,' speak the words, 'This is cessation'? It should not be said thus... pe...

Dukkhanti jānanto dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Maggoti jānanto maggoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' speak the words, 'This is suffering'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is the path,' speak the words, 'This is the path'? It should not be said thus... etc....

Samudayoti [M 0.0151][V 0.0167] jānanto na ca samudayoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Dukkhanti jānanto na ca dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who knows, 'This is the origin,' not speak the words, 'This is the origin'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' not speak the words, 'This is suffering'? It should not be said thus... etc....

Nirodhoti jānanto na ca nirodhoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Dukkhanti jānanto na ca dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who knows, 'This is cessation,' not speak the words, 'This is cessation'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' not speak the words, 'This is suffering'? It should not be said thus... etc....

Maggoti jānanto na ca maggoti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Āmantā. Dukkhanti jānanto na ca dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who knows, 'This is the path,' not speak the words, 'This is the path'? Yes. Does one who knows, 'This is suffering,' not speak the words, 'This is suffering'? It should not be said thus... etc....

328. Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā[P 0.0197]. Ñāṇaṃ kiṃgocaranti? Ñāṇaṃ saccagocaranti. Sotaṃ saccagocaranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

328. For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. What is the object of knowledge? The object of knowledge is the truth. Is the object of the ear the truth? It should not be said thus... etc....

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Sotaṃ kiṃ gocaranti? Sotaṃ saddagocaranti. Ñāṇaṃ saddagocaranti? Na hevaṃ [T 0.0217] vattabbe.

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. What is the object of the ear? The object of the ear is sound. Is the object of knowledge sound? It should not be said thus.

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo ñāṇaṃ saccagocaraṃ, sotaṃ saddagocaranti? Āmantā. Hañci ñāṇaṃ saccagocaraṃ, sotaṃ saddagocaraṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech, does knowledge have the truth as its object, and does the ear have sound as its object? Yes. If indeed knowledge has the truth as its object and the ear has sound as its object, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo ñāṇaṃ saccagocaraṃ, sotaṃ saddagocaranti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ, dvinnaṃ vedanānaṃ, dvinnaṃ saññānaṃ, dvinnaṃ cetanānaṃ, dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech, does knowledge have the truth as its object, and does the ear have sound as its object? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts, two feelings, two perceptions, two volitions, and two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus.

329. Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Pathavīkasiṇaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

329. For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the earth-kasiṇa attainment, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus.

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Āpokasiṇaṃ…pe… tejokasiṇaṃ… vāyokasiṇaṃ… nīlakasiṇaṃ… pītakasiṇaṃ… lohitakasiṇaṃ… odātakasiṇaṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [V 0.0168] … viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the attainment of the water-kasiṇa... etc... the fire-kasiṇa... the air-kasiṇa... the blue-kasiṇa... the yellow-kasiṇa... the red-kasiṇa... the white-kasiṇa... the base of infinite space... the base of infinite consciousness... the base of nothingness... etc... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Pathavīkasiṇaṃ [P 0.0198] samāpattiṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Hañci pathavīkasiṇaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered the earth-kasiṇa attainment, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. If indeed for one who has entered the earth-kasiṇa attainment there is no utterance of speech, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

Āpokasiṇaṃ [M 0.0152]… tejokasiṇaṃ… vāyokasiṇaṃ… nīlakasiṇaṃ… pītakasiṇaṃ… lohitakasiṇaṃ… odātakasiṇaṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [T 0.0218]… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Hañci nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered the attainment of the water-kasiṇa... the fire-kasiṇa... the air-kasiṇa... the blue-kasiṇa... the yellow-kasiṇa... the red-kasiṇa... the white-kasiṇa... the base of infinite space... the base of infinite consciousness... the base of nothingness... the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. If indeed for one who has entered the attainment of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception there is no utterance of speech, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokiyasamāpattiṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered a mundane attainment, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokiyaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the mundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc.... For one who has entered an attainment, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the mundane second jhāna... the third jhāna... the fourth jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokiyaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Hañci lokiyaṃ samāpattiṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered a mundane attainment, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. If indeed for one who has entered a mundane attainment there is no utterance of speech, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

Lokiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā[P 0.0199]. Hañci lokiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered the mundane first jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. If indeed for one who has entered the mundane first jhāna there is no utterance of speech, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

Lokiyaṃ [V 0.0169] dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Hañci lokiyaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa [T 0.0219] atthi vacībhedo”ti.

For one who has entered the mundane second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. If indeed for one who has entered the mundane fourth jhāna there is no utterance of speech, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.'

330. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokiyaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

330. For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the mundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokiyaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the mundane second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokiyaṃ [M 0.0153] paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered the mundane first jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokiyaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered the mundane second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there no utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

331. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na [P 0.0200] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

331. For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the supramundane second jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has entered the supramundane first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. For one who has entered the supramundane third jhāna… the fourth jhāna, is there an utterance of speech? It should not be said thus... etc....

Lokuttaraṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā[T 0.0220]. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no utterance of speech for one who has attained the supramundane second jhāna? Yes. Is there no utterance of speech for one who has attained the supramundane first jhāna? It should not be said thus…

Lokuttaraṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti[V 0.0170]? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa natthi vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no utterance of speech for one who has attained the supramundane second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna? Yes. Is there no utterance of speech for one who has attained the supramundane first jhāna? It should not be said thus…

332. Na vattabbaṃ – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhārā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti? Āmantā. Hañci vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhārā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā,” tena vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

332. Should it not be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech'? Yes. Is it not so that initial and sustained application have been declared by the Blessed One to be verbal formations, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application? Yes. If initial and sustained application have indeed been declared by the Blessed One to be verbal formations, and for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application, then for that reason, it should indeed be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech.'

Vitakkavicārā vacīsaṅkhārā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti atthi vitakkavicārā (syā.) evamuparipi, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Pathavīkasiṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that initial and sustained application have been declared by the Blessed One to be verbal formations, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. For one who has attained the first jhāna based on the earth kasiṇa, are there initial and sustained application, and is there an utterance of speech for that person? It should not be said thus…

Vitakkavicārā [M 0.0154] vacīsaṅkhārā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Āmantā[P 0.0201]. Āpokasiṇaṃ… tejokasiṇaṃ… vāyokasiṇaṃ… nīlakasiṇaṃ… pītakasiṇaṃ… lohitakasiṇaṃ… odātakasiṇaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that initial and sustained application have been declared by the Blessed One to be verbal formations, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. For one who has attained the first jhāna based on the water kasiṇa… fire kasiṇa… air kasiṇa… blue kasiṇa… yellow kasiṇa… red kasiṇa… white kasiṇa, are there initial and sustained application, and is there an utterance of speech for that person? It should not be said thus…

Na [T 0.0221] vattabbaṃ – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vitakkasamuṭṭhānā vācā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti? Āmantā. Hañci vitakkasamuṭṭhānā vācā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā,” tena vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

Should it not be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech'? Yes. Is it not so that speech originating from initial application has been declared by the Blessed One, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application? Yes. If speech originating from initial application has indeed been declared by the Blessed One, and for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application, then for that reason, it should indeed be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech.'

Vitakkasamuṭṭhānā vācā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Saññāsamuṭṭhānā vācā vuttā bhagavatā – “dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi saññā, atthi tassa vitakkavicārā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that speech originating from initial application has been declared by the Blessed One, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. Considering that speech originating from perception has been declared by the Blessed One, and that for one who has attained the second jhāna, there is perception—are there initial and sustained application for that person? It should not be said thus…

Vitakkasamuṭṭhānā [V 0.0171] vācā vuttā bhagavatā – “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa atthi vitakkavicārā”ti, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Saññāsamuṭṭhānā vācā vuttā bhagavatā – tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa atthi saññā, atthi tassa vitakkavicārāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that speech originating from initial application has been declared by the Blessed One, and that for one who has attained the first jhāna, there are initial and sustained application—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. Considering that speech originating from perception has been declared by the Blessed One, and that for one who has attained the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna… the sphere of infinite space… the sphere of infinite consciousness… the sphere of nothingness, there is perception—are there initial and sustained application for that person? It should not be said thus…

333. Samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Nanu “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vācā niruddhā hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.259, 263! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0202]. Hañci “paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vācā niruddhā hotī”ti, attheva [T 0.0222] suttantoti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

333. For one who has attained absorption, is there an utterance of speech? Yes. Is it not so that there is a Sutta passage that states: 'For one who has attained the first jhāna, speech has ceased'? Yes, there is. If there is indeed a Sutta passage that states: 'For one who has attained the first jhāna, speech has ceased,' then it should not be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech.'

“Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vācā niruddhā hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.259, 263, attheva suttantoti, atthi tassa vacībhedoti? Āmantā. “Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā hontī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.259, 263, attheva suttantoti, atthi tassa vitakkavicārāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that there is indeed a Sutta passage stating: 'For one who has attained the first jhāna, speech has ceased'—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. Considering that there is indeed a Sutta passage stating: 'For one who has attained the second jhāna, initial and sustained application have ceased'—are there initial and sustained application for that person? It should not be said thus…

“Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vācā niruddhā hotī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.259, 263, attheva suttantoti, atthi tassa vacībhedoti?
