Āmantā. “Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa [M 0.0155] pīti niruddhā hoti, catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa assāsapassāsā niruddhā honti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa rūpasaññā niruddhā hoti, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti, ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā hontī”ti saṃ. ni. 4.259, 263; a. ni. 9.31; dī. ni. 3.344, attheva suttantoti, atthi tassa saññā ca vedanā cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Considering that there is indeed a Sutta passage stating: 'For one who has attained the first jhāna, speech has ceased'—is there an utterance of speech for that person? Yes. Considering that there is indeed a Sutta passage stating: 'For one who has attained the third jhāna, rapture has ceased; for one who has attained the fourth jhāna, in-breaths and out-breaths have ceased; for one who has attained the sphere of infinite space, perception of form has ceased; for one who has attained the sphere of infinite consciousness, the perception of the sphere of infinite space has ceased; for one who has attained the sphere of nothingness, the perception of the sphere of infinite consciousness has ceased; for one who has attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the perception of the sphere of nothingness has ceased; for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, both perception and feeling have ceased'—are there for that person both perception and feeling? It should not be said thus…

Na vattabbaṃ – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇḍako kaṇṭako (syā.) a. ni. 10.72 vutto bhagavatāti a. ni. 10.72 kaṇṭakasuttaṃ nissāya pucchati? Āmantā. Hañci [T 0.0223] paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti.

Should it not be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna? Yes. If it has been said by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna, then for that reason, it should indeed be said: 'For one who has attained absorption, there is an utterance of speech.'

Paṭhamassa [V 0.0172] jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatāti, samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti? Āmantā. Dutiyassa [P 0.0203] jhānassa vitakkavicārā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… tatiyassa jhānassa pīti kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… catutthassa jhānassa assāsapassāsā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā a. ni. 10.72 … ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa rūpasaññā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā… saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā a. ni. 10.72, atthi tassa saññā ca vedanā cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since it has been said by the Blessed One that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna, is there an utterance of speech for one who has entered an attainment? Yes. Since it has been said by the Blessed One that applied thought and sustained thought are a thorn to the second jhāna... that rapture is a thorn to the third jhāna... that in-breaths and out-breaths are a thorn to the fourth jhāna... that perception of form is a thorn for one who has entered the base of infinite space... that the perception of the base of infinite space is a thorn for one who has entered the base of infinite consciousness... that the perception of the base of infinite consciousness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of nothingness... that the perception of the base of nothingness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... that both perception and feeling are a thorn for one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling, are there for that person both perception and feeling? It should not be said thus...

Na vattabbaṃ – “samāpannassa atthi vacībhedo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sikhissa, ānanda, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa abhibhū nāma sāvako brahmaloke ṭhito dasasahassilokadhātuṃ sarena viññāpesi –

Should it not be said: 'For one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Ānanda, a disciple named Abhibhū of the Blessed One Sikhī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, while standing in the Brahmā world, made the ten-thousandfold world-system know by his voice:'

‘Ārabbhatha [M 0.0156] nikkamatha, yuñjatha buddhasāsane;

Dhunātha maccuno senaṃ, naḷāgāraṃva kuñjaro.

'Strive, go forth, exert yourselves in the Buddha's Dispensation; destroy the army of death, as an elephant destroys a house of reeds.

‘Yo [T 0.0224] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati vihessati (sī. syā. kaṃ.) viharissati (ka.);

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’”ti a. ni. 1 tikanipāte; saṃ. ni. 1.285.

'Whoever will dwell heedfully in this Dhamma and Vinaya, having abandoned the saṃsāra of birth, will make an end of suffering.'

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi samāpannassa atthi vacībhedoti.

Is there indeed such a Sutta passage? Yes. If that is so, then for one who has entered an attainment, there is an utterance of speech.

Vacībhedakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Utterance of Speech is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(15) 6. Dukkhāhārakathā

2. (15) 6. Discourse on the Application to Suffering

334. Dukkhāhāro [V 0.0173] maggaṅgaṃ maggapariyāpannanti? Āmantā[P 0.0204]. Ye keci dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsanti, sabbe te maggaṃ bhāventīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the application to suffering a path factor, included in the path? Yes. Do all who utter the word 'suffering' develop the path? It should not be said thus.

Ye keci dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsanti, sabbe te maggaṃ bhāventīti? Āmantā. Bālaputhujjanā dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsanti, bālaputhujjanā maggaṃ bhāventīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Mātughātako… pitughātako… arahantaghātako… ruhiruppādako lohituppādako (sī. ka.) aññaṭṭhānesu pana ruhiruppādakotveva dissati … saṅghabhedako dukkhanti vācaṃ bhāsati, saṅghabhedako maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

334. Do all who utter the word 'suffering' develop the path? Yes. Do foolish ordinary people utter the word 'suffering'? Do foolish ordinary people develop the path? It should not be said thus. Does a matricide... a patricide... a killer of an Arahant... one who sheds the Buddha’s blood... one who creates a schism in the Saṅgha utter the word 'suffering'? Does one who creates a schism in the Saṅgha develop the path? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Dukkhāhārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Application to Suffering is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(16) 7. Cittaṭṭhitikathā

(16) 7. Discourse on the Duration of Mind

335. Ekaṃ [T 0.0225] cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Upaḍḍhadivaso uppādakkhaṇo, upaḍḍhadivaso vayakkhaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

2. Does a single mind last for a day? Yes. Is the arising moment half a day, and the ceasing moment half a day? It should not be said thus.

Ekaṃ [M 0.0157] cittaṃ dve divase tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Divaso uppādakkhaṇo, divaso vayakkhaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does a single mind last for two days? Yes. Is the arising moment a day, and the ceasing moment a day? It should not be said thus.

Ekaṃ cittaṃ cattāro divase tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha divase tiṭṭhati… dasa divase tiṭṭhati… vīsati divase tiṭṭhati… māsaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve māse tiṭṭhati… cattāro māse tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha māse [V 0.0174] tiṭṭhati… dasa māse tiṭṭhati… saṃvaccharaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve vassāni tiṭṭhati… cattāri vassāni tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha vassāni tiṭṭhati… dasa vassāni tiṭṭhati… vīsati vassāni tiṭṭhati… tiṃsa vassāni tiṭṭhati… cattārīsa vassāni tiṭṭhati… paññāsa vassāni tiṭṭhati… vassasataṃ tiṭṭhati… dve vassasatāni [P 0.0205] tiṭṭhati… cattāri vassasatāni tiṭṭhati… pañca vassasatāni tiṭṭhati… vassasahassaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… cattāri vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… soḷasa vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… kappaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve kappe tiṭṭhati… cattāro kappe tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha kappe tiṭṭhati… soḷasa kappe tiṭṭhati… bāttiṃsa kappe tiṭṭhati… catusaṭṭhi kappe tiṭṭhati… pañca kappasatāni tiṭṭhati… kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… dve kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… cattāri kappasahassāni [T 0.0226] tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… soḷasa kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… vīsati kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… cattārīsa kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… saṭṭhi kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… caturāsīti kappasahassāni tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Dvecattārīsa kappasahassāni uppādakkhaṇo, dvecattārīsa kappasahassāni vayakkhaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

335. Does a single mind last for four days… eight days… ten days… twenty days… a month… two months… four months… eight months… ten months… a year… two years… four years… eight years… ten years… twenty years… thirty years… forty years… fifty years… a hundred years… two hundred years… four hundred years… five hundred years… a thousand years… two thousand years… four thousand years… eight thousand years… sixteen thousand years… an aeon… two aeons… four aeons… eight aeons… sixteen aeons… thirty-two aeons… sixty-four aeons… five hundred aeons… a thousand aeons… two thousand aeons… four thousand aeons… eight thousand aeons… sixteen thousand aeons… twenty thousand aeons… forty thousand aeons… sixty thousand aeons… eighty-four thousand aeons? Yes. Are forty-two thousand aeons the arising moment, and forty-two thousand aeons the ceasing moment? It should not be said thus.

Ekaṃ cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Atthaññe dhammā ekāhaṃ bahumpi uppajjitvā nirujjhantīti? Āmantā. Te dhammā cittena lahuparivattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does a single mind last for a day? Yes. Are there other phenomena that arise and cease many times in one day? Yes. Are those phenomena of quick change along with the mind? It should not be said thus.

Te dhammā cittena lahuparivattāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi evaṃ lahuparivattaṃ yathayidaṃ cittaṃ. Yāvañcidaṃ, bhikkhave, upamāpi na sukarā yāva lahuparivattaṃ citta”nti a. ni. 1.48. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “te dhammā cittena lahuparivattā”ti.

Are those phenomena of quick change along with the mind? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, I do not see any other single thing that changes so quickly as this mind. So much so, monks, that it is not easy to give a simile for how quickly the mind changes.” Is there indeed such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Those phenomena are of quick change along with the mind.”

Te [M 0.0158] dhammā cittena lahuparivattāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, makkaṭo [P 0.0206] araññe pavane caramāno sākhaṃ gaṇhati, taṃ muñcitvā aññaṃ gaṇhati, taṃ muñcitvā aññaṃ gaṇhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yamidaṃ yadidaṃ (bahūsu) vuccati cittaṃ itipi mano itipi viññāṇaṃ itipi taṃ rattiyā ca divasassa ca aññadeva uppajjati [T 0.0227] aññaṃ nirujjhatī”ti saṃ. ni. 2.61. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “te dhammā cittena lahuparivattā”ti.

Are those phenomena of quick change along with the mind? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, just as a monkey roaming in a great forest grabs a branch, lets it go and grabs another, lets that go and grabs another; even so, monks, that which is called citta, or mano, or viññāṇa, arises as one thing and ceases as another, by night and by day”? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Those phenomena are of quick change along with the mind.”

336. Ekaṃ [V 0.0175] cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Sotaviññāṇaṃ…pe… ghānaviññāṇaṃ… jivhāviññāṇaṃ… kāyaviññāṇaṃ… akusalaṃ cittaṃ… rāgasahagataṃ… dosasahagataṃ… mohasahagataṃ… mānasahagataṃ… diṭṭhisahagataṃ… vicikicchāsahagataṃ… thinasahagataṃ… uddhaccasahagataṃ… ahirikasahagataṃ… anottappasahagataṃ cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

336. Does a single mind last for a day? Yes. Does eye-consciousness last for a day? It should not be said thus. Does ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… an unwholesome mind… a mind accompanied by greed… by hatred… by delusion… by conceit… by wrong view… by doubt… by sloth… by restlessness… by shamelessness… a mind accompanied by lack of moral dread last for a day? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Ekaṃ cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Yeneva cittena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, teneva cittena sotena saddaṃ suṇāti…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyati… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyati… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusati… manasā dhammaṃ vijānāti…pe… yeneva cittena manasā dhammaṃ vijānāti, teneva cittena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… sotena saddaṃ suṇāti… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyati… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyati…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a single mind last for a day? Yes. With the very same mind by which one sees a form with the eye, does one with that same mind hear a sound with the ear… smell an odor with the nose… taste a flavor with the tongue… feel a tangible object with the body… cognize a mental object with the mind…? … With the very same mind by which one cognizes a mental object with the mind, does one with that same mind see a form with the eye… hear a sound with the ear… smell an odor with the nose… taste a flavor with the tongue… feel a tangible object with the body? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Ekaṃ cittaṃ divasaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Yeneva cittena abhikkamati, teneva cittena paṭikkamati; yeneva cittena paṭikkamati, teneva cittena abhikkamati; yeneva cittena āloketi, teneva cittena viloketi; yeneva [P 0.0207] cittena viloketi, teneva cittena āloketi; yeneva cittena samiñjeti, teneva cittena pasāreti[T 0.0228]; yeneva cittena pasāreti, teneva cittena samiñjetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a single mind last for a day? Yes. By whatever mind one advances, by that very mind does one retreat? By whatever mind one retreats, by that very mind does one advance? By whatever mind one looks forward, by that very mind does one look around? By whatever mind one looks around, by that very mind does one look forward? By whatever mind one contracts, by that very mind does one expand? By whatever mind one expands, by that very mind does one contract? It should not be said thus… and so on.

337. Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ [M 0.0159] devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Manussānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

337. For the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space, does a single mind last for their entire lifespan? Yes. For humans, does a single mind last for their entire lifespan? It should not be said thus.

Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ…pe… tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ… yāmānaṃ devānaṃ… tusitānaṃ devānaṃ… nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ… paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ… brahmapārisajjānaṃ devānaṃ… brahmapurohitānaṃ devānaṃ… mahābrahmānaṃ devānaṃ… parittābhānaṃ devānaṃ… appamāṇābhānaṃ devānaṃ… ābhassarānaṃ devānaṃ… parittasubhānaṃ devānaṃ… appamāṇasubhānaṃ devānaṃ… subhakiṇhānaṃ devānaṃ [V 0.0176]… vehapphalānaṃ devānaṃ… avihānaṃ devānaṃ… atappānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassānaṃ devānaṃ… sudassīnaṃ devānaṃ… akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

For the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space, does a single mind last for their entire lifespan? Yes. For the gods of the Four Great Kings… the gods of the Thirty-Three… the Yāma gods… the Tusita gods… the gods who delight in creation… the gods who wield power over the creations of others… the gods of Brahmā’s retinue… the gods of Brahmā’s ministers… the gods of the Great Brahmā… the gods of limited radiance… the gods of boundless radiance… the gods of streaming radiance… the gods of limited glory… the gods of boundless glory… the gods of radiant glory… the gods of abundant fruit… the Aviha gods… the Atappa gods… the Sudassa gods… the Sudassī gods… the Akaniṭṭha gods—does a single mind last for their entire lifespan? It should not be said thus.

Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ vīsati kappasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ, ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ vīsati kappasahassāni tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Manussānaṃ vassasataṃ āyuppamāṇaṃ, manussānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ vassasataṃ tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

The lifespan of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space is twenty thousand eons. Does a single mind of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space last for twenty thousand eons? Yes. The lifespan of humans is one hundred years. Does a single mind of humans last for one hundred years? It should not be said thus.

Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ [T 0.0229] devānaṃ vīsati kappasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ, ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ vīsati kappasahassāni tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Cātumahārājikānaṃ [P 0.0208] devānaṃ pañca vassasatāni āyuppamāṇaṃ, cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ pañca vassasatāni tiṭṭhati… vassasahassaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… cattāri vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… soḷasa vassasahassāni tiṭṭhati… kappassa tatiyabhāgaṃ tiṭṭhati… upaḍḍhakappaṃ tiṭṭhati… ekaṃ kappaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve kappe tiṭṭhati… cattāro kappe tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha kappe tiṭṭhati… soḷasa kappe tiṭṭhati… bāttiṃsa kappe tiṭṭhati… catusaṭṭhi kappe tiṭṭhati… pañca kappasatāni tiṭṭhati… kappasahassaṃ tiṭṭhati… dve kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… cattāri kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… aṭṭha kappasahassāni tiṭṭhati… akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ soḷasa kappasahassāni āyuppamāṇaṃ, akaniṭṭhānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ soḷasa kappasahassāni tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

The lifespan of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space is twenty thousand eons. Does a single mind of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space last for twenty thousand eons? Yes. The lifespan of the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings is five hundred years. Does a single mind of the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings last for five hundred years… a thousand years… two thousand years… four thousand years… eight thousand years… sixteen thousand years… a third of an eon… half an eon… one eon… two eons… four eons… eight eons… sixteen eons… thirty-two eons… sixty-four eons… five hundred eons… a thousand eons… two thousand eons… four thousand eons… eight thousand eons… The lifespan of the Akaniṭṭha gods is sixteen thousand eons. Does a single mind of the Akaniṭṭha gods last for sixteen thousand eons? It should not be said thus.

Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ [M 0.0160] devānaṃ cittaṃ muhuttaṃ muhuttaṃ uppajjati muhuttaṃ muhuttaṃ nirujjhatīti? Āmantā. Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā devā muhuttaṃ muhuttaṃ cavanti muhuttaṃ muhuttaṃ uppajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Does the mind of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space arise moment by moment and cease moment by moment? Yes. Do the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space pass away moment by moment and arise moment by moment? It should not be said thus.

Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagānaṃ devānaṃ ekaṃ cittaṃ yāvatāyukaṃ tiṭṭhatīti[T 0.0230]? Āmantā. Ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā devā yeneva cittena uppajjanti, teneva cittena cavantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a single mind of the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space last for their entire lifespan? Yes. Do the gods reborn in the sphere of infinite space pass away with the same mind with which they arise? It should not be said thus... and so on...

Cittaṭṭhitikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Duration of Mind is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Section

(17) 8. Kukkuḷakathā

(17) 8. Discourse on Hot Embers

338. Sabbe [V 0.0177] saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi sukhā vedanā, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ, cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ[P 0.0209], dibbaṃ sukhaṃ, mānusakaṃ sukhaṃ, lābhasukhaṃ, sakkārasukhaṃ, yānasukhaṃ, sayanasukhaṃ, issariyasukhaṃ, ādhipaccasukhaṃ, gihisukhaṃ, sāmaññasukhaṃ, sāsavaṃ sukhaṃ, anāsavaṃ sukhaṃ, upadhisukhaṃ, nirūpadhisukhaṃ, sāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, nirāmisaṃ sukhaṃ, sappītikaṃ sukhaṃ, nippītikaṃ sukhaṃ, jhānasukhaṃ, vimuttisukhaṃ, kāmasukhaṃ, nekkhammasukhaṃ, vivekasukhaṃ, upasamasukhaṃ, sambodhasukhanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi sukhā vedanā…pe… sambodhasukhaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

338. Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. But is there not pleasant feeling—bodily pleasure, mental pleasure, divine pleasure, human pleasure, the pleasure of gain, the pleasure of honor, the pleasure of vehicles, the pleasure of beds, the pleasure of lordship, the pleasure of sovereignty, household pleasure, ascetic pleasure, pleasure with taints, pleasure without taints, pleasure with attachments, pleasure without attachments, worldly pleasure, unworldly pleasure, pleasure with rapture, pleasure without rapture, the pleasure of jhāna, the pleasure of liberation, sensual pleasure, the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of serenity, the pleasure of enlightenment? Yes. If there is pleasant feeling… up to the pleasure of enlightenment, then surely, it should not be said that 'all formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā vedanā kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassaupāyāsāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. Are all formations painful feeling, bodily pain, mental pain, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair? It should not be said thus.

Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sabbaṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ! Kiñca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ ādittaṃ? Cakkhuṃ, bhikkhave, ādittaṃ, rūpā ādittā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [T 0.0231] ādittaṃ, cakkhusamphasso āditto; yamidaṃ yampidaṃ (saṃ. ni. 4.28) cakkhusamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? ‘Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi [M 0.0161] domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’nti vadāmi. Sotaṃ ādittaṃ, saddā ādittā…pe… ghānaṃ ādittaṃ, gandhā ādittā…pe… jivhā ādittā, rasā ādittā…pe… kāyo āditto, phoṭṭhabbā ādittā…pe… mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, manoviññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ, manosamphasso āditto; yamidaṃ manosamphassapaccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, tampi ādittaṃ. Kena ādittaṃ? ‘Rāgagginā dosagginā mohagginā ādittaṃ, jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi āditta’nti vadāmī”ti mahāva. 54; saṃ. ni. 4.28. Attheva [V 0.0178] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [P 0.0210] hi vattabbaṃ tena hi (sī. syā.), tena hi na vattabbaṃ (ka.) – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Should it not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'? Yes, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, all is ablaze! And what, monks, is the all that is ablaze? The eye, monks, is ablaze, forms are ablaze, eye-consciousness is ablaze, eye-contact is ablaze; and whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is ablaze. Ablaze with what? Ablaze with the fire of passion, the fire of aversion, the fire of delusion; it is ablaze with birth, aging, and death, with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say. The ear is ablaze, sounds are ablaze… The nose is ablaze, odors are ablaze… The tongue is ablaze, tastes are ablaze… The body is ablaze, tangible objects are ablaze… The mind is ablaze, mental objects are ablaze, mind-consciousness is ablaze, mind-contact is ablaze; and whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is ablaze. Ablaze with what? Ablaze with the fire of passion, the fire of aversion, the fire of delusion; it is ablaze with birth, aging, and death, with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs, and despairs, I say.' Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā! Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā [T 0.0232] manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā”ti ma. ni. 1.166; saṃ. ni. 4.268. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, wished for, agreeable, of a pleasing nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear… Odors cognizable by the nose… Tastes cognizable by the tongue… Tangible objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, wished for, agreeable, of a pleasing nature, connected with sensual desire, and enticing. These, monks, are the five cords of sensual pleasure.' Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “lābhā vo, bhikkhave, suladdhaṃ vo, bhikkhave, khaṇo vo paṭiladdho paṭividdho (bahūsu) brahmacariyavāsāya! Diṭṭhā mayā, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanikā nāma nirayā. Tattha yaṃ kiñci cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, aniṭṭharūpaññeva passati no iṭṭharūpaṃ, akantarūpaññeva passati no kantarūpaṃ, amanāparūpaññeva passati no manāparūpaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci sotena saddaṃ suṇāti…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyati… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyati… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusati… manasā dhammaṃ vijānāti, aniṭṭharūpaññeva vijānāti no iṭṭharūpaṃ, akantarūpaññeva vijānāti no kantarūpaṃ, amanāparūpaññeva vijānāti no manāparūpa”nti saṃ. ni. 4.135. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi vattabbaṃ tena hi na vattabbaṃ (syā. ka.) – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Should it not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'? Yes, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'It is a gain for you, monks! It is well-gained by you, monks! You have obtained the opportune moment for living the holy life! I have seen, monks, the hells named the six sense bases. There, whatever form one sees with the eye, one sees only an undesirable form, not a desirable form; one sees only an unwished-for form, not a wished-for form; one sees only a displeasing form, not a pleasing form. Whatever sound one hears with the ear… whatever odor one smells with the nose… whatever taste one savors with the tongue… whatever tangible object one touches with the body… whatever mental object one cognizes with the mind, one cognizes only an undesirable mental object, not a desirable mental object; one cognizes only an unwished-for mental object, not a wished-for mental object; one cognizes only a displeasing mental object, not a pleasing mental object.' Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Sabbe [M 0.0162] saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “lābhā vo, bhikkhave, suladdhaṃ vo, bhikkhave, khaṇo vo paṭiladdho brahmacariyavāsāya! Diṭṭhā mayā, bhikkhave, cha phassāyatanikā [P 0.0211] nāma saggā. Tattha yaṃ kiñci cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, iṭṭharūpaññeva [T 0.0233] passati no aniṭṭharūpaṃ, kantarūpaññeva passati no akantarūpaṃ, manāparūpaññeva passati no amanāparūpaṃ. Yaṃ kiñci sotena saddaṃ suṇāti…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyati… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyati… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusati… manasā dhammaṃ vijānāti, iṭṭharūpaññeva vijānāti no aniṭṭharūpaṃ, kantarūpaññeva vijānāti [V 0.0179] no akantarūpaṃ, manāparūpaññeva vijānāti no amanāparūpa”nti saṃ. ni. 4.135. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'It is a gain for you, monks! It is well-gained by you, monks! You have obtained the opportune moment for living the holy life! I have seen, monks, the heavens named the six sense bases. There, whatever form one sees with the eye, one sees only a desirable form, not an undesirable form; one sees only a wished-for form, not an unwished-for form; one sees only a pleasing form, not a displeasing form. Whatever sound one hears with the ear… whatever odor one smells with the nose… whatever taste one savors with the tongue… whatever tangible object one touches with the body… whatever mental object one cognizes with the mind, one cognizes only a desirable mental object, not an undesirable mental object; one cognizes only a wished-for mental object, not an unwished-for mental object; one cognizes only a pleasing mental object, not a displeasing mental object.' Is there not such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu “yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ saṃ. ni. 3.15,” vuttaṃ bhagavatā, “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”ti dha. pa. 277; ma. ni. 1.356? Āmantā. Hañci “yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ,” vuttaṃ bhagavatā, “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā,” tena vata re vattabbe – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Should it not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering,' and 'All formations are impermanent'? Yes. If it has been said by the Blessed One: 'Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering,' and 'All formations are impermanent,' then indeed, it should be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Dānaṃ aniṭṭhaphalaṃ akantaphalaṃ amanuññaphalaṃ secanakaphalaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. Is giving of undesirable result, unloved result, disagreeable result, of a result that is irrigated by defilements, having suffering as its outcome, having suffering as its result? It should not be said thus.

Sīlaṃ…pe… uposatho…pe… bhāvanā…pe… brahmacariyaṃ aniṭṭhaphalaṃ akantaphalaṃ amanuññaphalaṃ secanakaphalaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is virtue... Uposatha observance... meditation... the holy life of undesirable result, unloved result, disagreeable result, of a result that is irrigated by defilements, having suffering as its outcome, having suffering as its result? It should not be said thus.

Nanu dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti[T 0.0234]? Āmantā. Hañci dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākaṃ, no [P 0.0212] ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Is not giving of desired result, loved result, agreeable result, of a result not irrigated by defilements, having happiness as its outcome, having happiness as its result? Yes. If giving is of desired result, loved result, agreeable result, of a result not irrigated by defilements, having happiness as its outcome, having happiness as its result, then it should certainly not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Nanu sīlaṃ… uposatho… bhāvanā… brahmacariyaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti? Āmantā. Hañci brahmacariyaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Is not virtue... Uposatha observance... meditation... the holy life of desired result, loved result, agreeable result, of a result not irrigated by defilements, having happiness as its outcome, having happiness as its result? Yes. If the holy life is of desired result, loved result, agreeable result, of a result not irrigated by defilements, having happiness as its outcome, having happiness as its result, then it should certainly not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Sabbe [M 0.0163] saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Are all formations, without exception, like hot embers? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Sukho viveko tuṭṭhassa, sutadhammassa passato;

Abyāpajjaṃ sukhaṃ loke, pāṇabhūtesu saṃyamo.

“Seclusion is happiness for one who is content, who has heard the Dhamma and sees. Non-affliction is happiness in the world; restraint towards living beings.

“Sukhā [V 0.0180] virāgatā loke, kāmānaṃ samatikkamo;

Asmimānassa yo vinayo, etaṃ ve paramaṃ sukhaṃ mahāva. 5; udā. 11 udāne ca.

“Happiness is dispassion in the world, the overcoming of sensual pleasures. The disciplining of the conceit ‘I am’—this, indeed, is the supreme happiness.

“Taṃ sukhena sukhaṃ pattaṃ, accantasukhameva taṃ;

Tisso vijjā anuppattā, etaṃ ve paramaṃ sukha”nti.

“That happiness is attained through happiness; that itself is ultimate happiness. The three true knowledges are attained; this, indeed, is the supreme happiness.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “sabbe saṅkhārā anodhiṃ katvā kukkuḷā”ti.

Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'All formations, without exception, are like hot embers'.

Kukkuḷakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Hot Embers is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(18) 9. Anupubbābhisamayakathā

2. (18) 9. Discussion on Gradual Realization

339. Anupubbābhisamayoti[T 0.0235]? Āmantā. Anupubbena [P 0.0213] sotāpattimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Anupubbena sotāpattimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Anupubbena sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there gradual realization? Yes. Does one develop the path of stream-entry gradually? It should not be said thus. Does one develop the path of stream-entry gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry gradually? It should not be said thus.

Anupubbābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Anupubbena sakadāgāmimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Anupubbena sakadāgāmimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Anupubbena sakadāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

339. Is there gradual realization? Yes. Does one develop the path of the once-returner gradually? It should not be said thus. Does one develop the path of the once-returner gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of the once-returner gradually? It should not be said thus.

Anupubbābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Anupubbena anāgāmimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Anupubbena anāgāmimaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Anupubbena anāgāmiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there gradual realization? Yes. Does one develop the path of the non-returner gradually? It should not be said thus. Does one develop the path of the non-returner gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of the non-returner gradually? It should not be said thus.

Anupubbābhisamayoti[V 0.0181]? Āmantā. Anupubbena arahattamaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Anupubbena arahattamaggaṃ bhāvetīti? Āmantā. Anupubbena arahattaphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is there gradual realization? Yes. Does one develop the path to arahantship gradually? It should not be said thus. Does one develop the path to arahantship gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of arahantship gradually? It should not be said thus.

340. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya [M 0.0164] paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ, vicikicchaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese [T 0.0236] catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ sotāpanno, catubhāgaṃ na sotāpanno, catubhāgaṃ sotāpattiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato [P 0.0214] upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ sattakkhattuparamo kolaṅkolo ekabījī buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato catubhāgaṃ na ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry—what does one abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons a fourth part of identity-view, doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a stream-enterer? By a fourth part, is one not a stream-enterer? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, realized, and dwelled having accomplished the fruit of stream-entry, and does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one not dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one at most a seven-times returner, a family-to-family returner, or a one-seeder? Is one endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… and so on… in the Saṅgha… and so on… with virtues beloved of the noble ones? By a fourth part, is one not endowed with virtues beloved of the noble ones? It should not be said thus.

Samudayadassanena…pe… nirodhadassanena…pe… maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ, vicikicchaṃ, sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ sotāpanno, catubhāgaṃ na sotāpanno, catubhāgaṃ sotāpattiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ sattakkhattuparamo kolaṅkolo ekabījī buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato, catubhāgaṃ na ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

340. By seeing the truth of the origin… and so on… by seeing the truth of cessation… and so on… by seeing the truth of the path—what does one abandon? One abandons a fourth part of identity-view, doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a stream-enterer? By a fourth part, is one not a stream-enterer? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, realized, and dwelled having accomplished the fruit of stream-entry, and does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one not dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one at most a seven-times returner, a family-to-family returner, or a one-seeder? Is one endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… and so on… in the Saṅgha… and so on… with virtues beloved of the noble ones? By a fourth part, is one not endowed with virtues beloved of the noble ones? It should not be said thus… and so on.

341. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ, oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ sakadāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ na sakadāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena [T 0.0237] phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayadassanena…pe… nirodhadassanena…pe… maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ, oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ sakadāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ na sakadāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato [P 0.0215] upasampajja viharati[V 0.0182], kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

341. A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of the once-returner—what does one abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons a fourth part of gross sensual desire, gross ill will, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a once-returner? By a fourth part, is one not a once-returner? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized the fruit of the once-returner, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? It should not be said thus… and so on… By seeing the truth of the origin… and so on… by seeing the truth of cessation… and so on… by seeing the truth of the path—what does one abandon? One abandons a fourth part of gross sensual desire, gross ill will, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a once-returner? By a fourth part, is one not a once-returner? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized the fruit of the once-returner, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? It should not be said thus… and so on.

342. Anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya [M 0.0165] paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ, aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ anāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ na anāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ anāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ antarāparinibbāyī…pe… upahaccaparinibbāyī… asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī… sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī… uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, catubhāgaṃ na uddhaṃsoto na akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

342. A person practicing for the realization of the fruit of the non-returner—what does one abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons a fourth part of subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a non-returner? By a fourth part, is one not a non-returner? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized the fruit of the non-returner, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one who attains parinibbāna in the interval… and so on… one who attains parinibbāna upon landing, one who attains parinibbāna without exertion, one who attains parinibbāna with exertion, or one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? By a fourth part, is one not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena…pe… nirodhadassanena…pe… maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ, aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ anāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ na anāgāmī, catubhāgaṃ anāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena [T 0.0238] phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ antarāparinibbāyī…pe… upahaccaparinibbāyī… asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī… sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī… uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmī, catubhāgaṃ na uddhaṃsoto akaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the origin… and so on… by seeing the truth of cessation… and so on… by seeing the truth of the path—what does one abandon? One abandons a fourth part of subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will, and the defilements co-nascent with them. By a fourth part, is one a non-returner? By a fourth part, is one not a non-returner? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized the fruit of the non-returner, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one who attains parinibbāna in the interval… and so on… one who attains parinibbāna upon landing, one who attains parinibbāna without exertion, one who attains parinibbāna with exertion, or one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? By a fourth part, is one not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? It should not be said thus… and so on.

343. Arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Rūparāgaṃ, arūparāgaṃ, mānaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, avijjaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ arahā, catubhāgaṃ na arahā, catubhāgaṃ arahattappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena [P 0.0216] phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ vītarāgo…pe… vītadoso… vītamoho…pe… katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ [V 0.0183] sacchikataṃ, catubhāgaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

343. What does a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship abandon by seeing the truth of suffering? One abandons, by a fourth part, lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and the defilements co-existent with them. By a fourth part, is one an Arahant? By a fourth part, is one not an Arahant? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized Arahantship, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one free from lust… and so on… free from hatred… free from delusion… and so on… Has one done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained one's own welfare, destroyed the fetters of existence, and become liberated by right knowledge? Is the cross-bar lifted, the moat filled in, the threshold-post uprooted? Is one unbolted, a noble one, with banner lowered, with burden laid down, detached, a triumphant victor? Is suffering fully understood by that person? Is the origin abandoned? Is cessation realized? Is the path developed? Is what is to be directly known, directly known? Is what is to be fully understood, fully understood? Is what is to be abandoned, abandoned? Is what is to be developed, developed… and so on… Is what is to be realized, realized? By a fourth part, is what is to be realized not realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Samudayadassanena [M 0.0166] … nirodhadassanena… maggadassanena kiṃ jahatīti? Rūparāgaṃ, arūparāgaṃ, mānaṃ, uddhaccaṃ, avijjaṃ, tadekaṭṭhe ca kilese catubhāgaṃ jahatīti. Catubhāgaṃ arahā, catubhāgaṃ na arahā, catubhāgaṃ arahattappatto [T 0.0239] paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, catubhāgaṃ vītarāgo… vītadoso… vītamoho… katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto ukkhittapaligho saṅkiṇṇaparikho abbūḷhesiko niraggaḷo ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaññutto suvijitavijayo, dukkhaṃ tassa pariññātaṃ, samudayo pahīno, nirodho sacchikato, maggo bhāvito, abhiññeyyaṃ abhiññātaṃ, pariññeyyaṃ pariññātaṃ, pahātabbaṃ pahīnaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ bhāvitaṃ…pe… sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, catubhāgaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By seeing the truth of the origin… and so on… by seeing the truth of cessation… and so on… by seeing the truth of the path—what does one abandon? One abandons, by a fourth part, lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and the defilements co-existent with them. By a fourth part, is one an Arahant? By a fourth part, is one not an Arahant? By a fourth part, has one attained, obtained, reached, and realized Arahantship, and does one dwell having entered upon it? Does one dwell having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, does one dwell not having touched it with the body? By a fourth part, is one free from lust… and so on… free from hatred… free from delusion… and so on… Has one done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained one's own welfare, destroyed the fetters of existence, and become liberated by right knowledge? Is the cross-bar lifted, the moat filled in, the threshold-post uprooted? Is one unbolted, a noble one, with banner lowered, with burden laid down, detached, a triumphant victor? Is suffering fully understood by that person? Is the origin abandoned? Is cessation realized? Is the path developed? Is what is to be directly known, directly known? Is what is to be fully understood, fully understood? Is what is to be abandoned, abandoned? Is what is to be developed, developed… and so on… Is what is to be realized, realized? By a fourth part, is what is to be realized not realized? It should not be said thus… and so on.

344. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabboti? Āmantā. Dukkhe diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Samudayaṃ dakkhanto…pe… nirodhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabboti? Āmantā[P 0.0217]. Nirodhe diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

344. Should a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, be called 'one who is practicing'? Yes. When suffering is seen, should they be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? This should not be said. While seeing the origin… and so on… while seeing cessation, should they be called 'one who is practicing'? Yes. When cessation is seen, should they be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? This should not be said.

Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo maggaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, magge diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Āmantā. Dukkhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, dukkhe diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggaṃ [T 0.0240] dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, magge diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Āmantā. Samudayaṃ dakkhanto…pe… nirodhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, nirodhe diṭṭhe phale ṭhitoti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing the path, be called 'one who is practicing', and when the path is seen, be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? Yes. Should a person, while seeing suffering, be called 'one who is practicing', and when suffering is seen, be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? This should not be said... Should a person, while seeing the path, be called 'one who is practicing', and when the path is seen, be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? Yes. Should a person, while seeing the origin... while seeing cessation, be called 'one who is practicing', and when cessation is seen, be called 'one who is established in the fruit'? This should not be said...

Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, dukkhe diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Āmantā. Maggaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, magge diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayaṃ dakkhanto… nirodhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti [V 0.0184] vattabbo, nirodhe diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Āmantā. Maggaṃ dakkhanto “paṭipannako”ti [M 0.0167] vattabbo, magge diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, be called 'one who is practicing', and when suffering is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? Yes. Should a person, while seeing the path, be called 'one who is practicing', and when the path is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? This should not be said... Should a person, while seeing the origin... while seeing cessation, be called 'one who is practicing', and when cessation is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? Yes. Should a person, while seeing the path, be called 'one who is practicing', and when the path is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno puggalo dukkhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, dukkhe diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Āmantā. Niratthiyaṃ dukkhadassananti? Na [P 0.0218] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayaṃ dakkhanto…pe… nirodhaṃ dakkhanto paṭipannakoti vattabbo, nirodhe diṭṭhe na vattabbaṃ – “phale ṭhitoti vattabbo”ti? Āmantā. Niratthiyaṃ nirodhadassananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, be called 'one who is practicing', and when suffering is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? Yes. Is seeing suffering fruitless? This should not be said... Should a person, while seeing the origin... while seeing cessation, be called 'one who is practicing', and when cessation is seen, should it not be said, 'one is established in the fruit'? Yes. Is seeing cessation fruitless? This should not be said...

345. paravādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Dukkhe [T 0.0241] diṭṭhe cattāri saccāni diṭṭhāni hontīti? Āmantā. Dukkhasaccaṃ cattāri saccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

345. When suffering is seen, are the four truths seen? Yes. Is the truth of suffering the four truths? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Rūpakkhandhe aniccato diṭṭhe pañcakkhandhā aniccato diṭṭhā hontīti? Āmantā. Rūpakkhandho pañcakkhandhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the form aggregate is seen as impermanent, are the five aggregates seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the form aggregate the five aggregates? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Cakkhāyatane aniccato diṭṭhe dvādasāyatanāni aniccato diṭṭhāni hontīti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ dvādasāyatanānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the eye-base is seen as impermanent, are the twelve bases seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye-base the twelve bases? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Cakkhudhātuyā aniccato diṭṭhāya aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo aniccato diṭṭhā hontīti? Āmantā. Cakkhudhātu aṭṭhārasa dhātuyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the eye-element is seen as impermanent, are the eighteen elements seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye-element the eighteen elements? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Cakkhundriye aniccato diṭṭhe bāvīsatindriyāni aniccato diṭṭhāni hontīti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyaṃ bāvīsatindriyānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the eye faculty is seen as impermanent, are the twenty-two faculties seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye faculty the twenty-two faculties? This should not be said...

sakavādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ Catūhi ñāṇehi sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Cattāri sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhahi ñāṇehi sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā[V 0.0185][P 0.0219]. Aṭṭha sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasahi ñāṇehi sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Dvādasa sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… catucattārīsāya ñāṇehi sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti[T 0.0242]? Āmantā. Catucattārīsaṃ sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sattasattatiyā ñāṇehi sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Sattasattati sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of stream-entry realized by four knowledges? Yes. Are the four knowledges the fruits of stream-entry? This should not be said... Is the fruit of stream-entry realized by eight knowledges? Yes. Are the eight knowledges the fruits of stream-entry? This should not be said... Is the fruit of stream-entry realized by twelve knowledges? Yes. Are the twelve knowledges the fruits of stream-entry? This should not be said... Is the fruit of stream-entry realized by forty-four knowledges? Yes. Are the forty-four knowledges the fruits of stream-entry? This should not be said... Is the fruit of stream-entry realized by seventy-seven knowledges? Yes. Are the seventy-seven knowledges the fruits of stream-entry? This should not be said...

346. Na [M 0.0168] vattabbaṃ – “anupubbābhisamayo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo anupubbaninno anupubbapoṇo anupubbapabbhāro, na āyatakeneva papāto; evameva kho, bhikkhave, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā, na āyatakeneva aññāpaṭivedho”ti cūḷava. 385; a. ni. 8.20; udā. 45 udāne ca. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi anupubbābhisamayoti.

346. Is it incorrect to say that realization is gradual? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: 'Just as, bhikkhus, the great ocean slopes gradually, inclines gradually, deepens gradually, not plunging abruptly; so too, bhikkhus, in this Dhamma and Discipline, the training is gradual, the doing is gradual, the practice is gradual, there is no abrupt penetration of final knowledge'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, realization is gradual.

Na vattabbaṃ – “anupubbābhisamayo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is it incorrect to say that realization is gradual? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said:

“Anupubbena medhāvī, thokaṃ thokaṃ khaṇe khaṇe;

Kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malamattano”ti dha. pa. 239 dhammapade.

A wise person should gradually, little by little, moment by moment, remove their own impurity, just as a smith removes the dross of silver.

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi anupubbābhisamayoti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, realization is gradual.

Anupubbābhisamayoti[P 0.0220]? Āmantā. Nanvāyasmā gavampati thero bhikkhū etadavoca – “sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yo, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ passati dukkhasamudayampi so passati, dukkhanirodhampi passati, dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ [T 0.0243] paṭipadampi passati; yo dukkhasamudayaṃ passati dukkhampi so passati, dukkhanirodhampi passati, dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadampi passati; yo dukkhanirodhaṃ passati dukkhampi so passati, dukkhasamudayampi passati, dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadampi passati; yo dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ passati dukkhampi so passati, dukkhasamudayampi passati, dukkhanirodhampi passatī’”ti saṃ. ni. 5.1100! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “anupubbābhisamayo”ti.

Is realization gradual? Yes. But has not the Venerable Gavampati Thera said this to the bhikkhus: 'Friends, I have heard and learned this directly from the Blessed One: "Bhikkhus, one who sees suffering also sees the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering; one who sees the origin of suffering also sees suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering; one who sees the cessation of suffering also sees suffering, the origin of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering; one who sees the path leading to the cessation of suffering also sees suffering, the origin of suffering, and the cessation of suffering"'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said that realization is gradual.

Anupubbābhisamayoti[V 0.0186]? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is realization gradual? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said:

“Sahāvassa dassanasampadāya,

Tayassu dhammā jahitā bhavanti;

Sakkāyadiṭṭhī vicikicchitañca,

Sīlabbataṃ vāpi yadatthi kiñci;

Catūhapāyehi ca vippamutto,

Chaccābhiṭhānāni abhabba kātu”nti.

“With the attainment of vision, three things are abandoned for him: personality-view, doubt, and whatever adherence to rites and rituals there may be. He is freed from the four woeful states and is incapable of committing the six heinous acts.”

Attheva [M 0.0169] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “anupubbābhisamayo”ti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “Realization is gradual.”

Anupubbābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvakassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti, saha dassanuppādā, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tīṇi saṃyojanāni pahīyanti – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “anupubbābhisamayo”ti.

Is realization gradual? Yes. Has not the Blessed One said: “Bhikkhus, at the time when the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arises in the noble disciple—‘Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation’—then, bhikkhus, with the arising of that vision, three fetters are abandoned by the noble disciple: personality-view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals”? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “Realization is gradual.”

Anupubbābhisamayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Gradual Realization is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Section

(19) 10. Vohārakathā

(19) 10. Discourse on Conventional Usage

347. Buddhassa [T 0.0244][P 0.0221] bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Lokuttare sote paṭihaññati no lokiye, lokuttarena viññāṇena paṭivijānanti no lokiyena, sāvakā paṭivijānanti no puthujjanāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

347. Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Does it impinge on the supramundane ear, not on the mundane? Is it comprehended by supramundane consciousness, not by mundane? Do disciples comprehend it, not ordinary people? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nanu [V 0.0187] buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokiye sote paṭihaññatīti? Āmantā. Hañci buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokiye sote paṭihaññati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Does not the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression impinge on the mundane ear? Yes. If the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression impinges on the mundane ear, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

Nanu buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ lokiyena viññāṇena paṭivijānantīti? Āmantā. Hañci buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ lokiyena viññāṇena paṭivijānanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Do they not comprehend the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression with mundane consciousness? Yes. If they comprehend the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression with mundane consciousness, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

Nanu buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ puthujjanā paṭivijānantīti? Āmantā. Hañci buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ puthujjanā paṭivijānanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Do not ordinary people comprehend the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression? Yes. If ordinary people comprehend the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

348. Buddhassa [M 0.0170] bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmimaggo sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmimaggo anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattamaggo arahattaphalaṃ, satipaṭṭhānaṃ [T 0.0245] sammappadhānaṃ iddhipādo indriyaṃ balaṃ bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

348. Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, Nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the path of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the path of arahantship, the fruit of arahantship, the establishments of mindfulness, the right exertions, the bases of success, the faculties, the powers, or the enlightenment factors? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Atthi keci buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ suṇantīti? Āmantā. Lokuttaro [P 0.0222] dhammo sotaviññeyyo, sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati, sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Are there some who hear the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression? Yes. Is the supramundane Dhamma to be cognized by ear-consciousness, does it impinge on the ear, does it come into the range of the ear? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nanu lokuttaro dhammo na sotaviññeyyo, na sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati, na sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Āmantā. Hañci lokuttaro dhammo na sotaviññeyyo, na sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati, na sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Is it not so that the supramundane Dhamma is not to be cognized by ear-consciousness, does not impinge on the ear, and does not come into the range of the ear? Yes. If the supramundane Dhamma is not to be cognized by ear-consciousness, does not impinge on the ear, and does not come into the range of the ear, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

349. Buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Atthi keci buddhassa bhagavato [V 0.0188] vohāre rajjeyyunti? Āmantā. Lokuttaro dhammo rāgaṭṭhāniyo rajanīyo kamanīyo madanīyo bandhanīyo mucchanīyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

349. Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Are there some who might become attached to the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression? Yes. Is the supramundane Dhamma a basis for lust, arousing, desirable, intoxicating, binding, and infatuating? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nanu lokuttaro dhammo na rāgaṭṭhāniyo na rajanīyo na kamanīyo na madanīyo na bandhanīyo na mucchanīyoti? Āmantā. Hañci lokuttaro dhammo na rāgaṭṭhāniyo na rajanīyo na kamanīyo na madanīyo na bandhanīyo na mucchanīyo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Is it not so that the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for lust, not arousing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, and not infatuating? Yes. If the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for lust, not arousing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, and not infatuating, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

Buddhassa [T 0.0246] bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Atthi keci buddhassa bhagavato vohāre dusseyyunti? Āmantā. Lokuttaro dhammo dosaṭṭhāniyo kopaṭṭhāniyo paṭighaṭṭhāniyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Are there some who might become angry at the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression? Yes. Is the supramundane Dhamma a basis for aversion, a basis for anger, a basis for resentment? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nanu lokuttaro dhammo na dosaṭṭhāniyo na kopaṭṭhāniyo na paṭighaṭṭhāniyoti? Āmantā. Hañci lokuttaro dhammo na dosaṭṭhāniyo na [P 0.0223] kopaṭṭhāniyo [M 0.0171] na paṭighaṭṭhāniyo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Is it not so that the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for aversion, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for resentment? Yes. If the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for aversion, not a basis for anger, and not a basis for resentment, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

Buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Atthi keci buddhassa bhagavato vohāre muyheyyunti? Āmantā. Lokuttaro dhammo mohaṭṭhāniyo aññāṇakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattanikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Are there some who might be deluded by the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression? Yes. Is the supramundane Dhamma a basis for delusion, causing ignorance, causing lack of vision, obstructing wisdom, on the side of vexation, and not conducive to Nibbāna? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Nanu lokuttaro dhammo na mohaṭṭhāniyo na aññāṇakaraṇo na acakkhukaraṇo paññāvuddhiko avighātapakkhiko nibbānasaṃvattanikoti? Āmantā. Hañci lokuttaro dhammo na mohaṭṭhāniyo na aññāṇakaraṇo na acakkhukaraṇo paññāvuddhiko avighātapakkhiko nibbānasaṃvattaniko, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaro”ti.

Is it not so that the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for delusion, not causing ignorance, not causing lack of vision, but increases wisdom, is on the side of non-vexation, and is conducive to Nibbāna? Yes. If the supramundane Dhamma is not a basis for delusion, not causing ignorance, not causing lack of vision, but increases wisdom, is on the side of non-vexation, and is conducive to Nibbāna, then truly it should not be said, “The Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression is supramundane.”

350. Buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokuttaroti? Āmantā. Ye [T 0.0247] keci buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ suṇanti, sabbe te maggaṃ bhāventīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

350. Is the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression supramundane? Yes. Do all those who hear the Blessed Buddha’s conventional expression develop the path? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Ye [V 0.0189] keci buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ suṇanti, sabbe te maggaṃ bhāventīti? Āmantā. Bālaputhujjanā buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ suṇanti, bālaputhujjanā maggaṃ bhāventīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… mātughātako maggaṃ bhāveti…pe… pitughātako… arahantaghātako… ruhiruppādako… saṅghabhedako buddhassa bhagavato vohāraṃ suṇāti, saṅghabhedako maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do all those who hear the expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One, develop the path? Yes. Foolish ordinary people hear the expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One; do foolish ordinary people develop the path? It should not be said thus... and so on. Does a matricide develop the path... and so on... a patricide... a murderer of an arahant... one who sheds the blood of a Buddha... A schismatic in the Sangha hears the expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One; does a schismatic in the Sangha develop the path? It should not be said thus... and so on.

351. Labbhā [P 0.0224] sovaṇṇamayāya laṭṭhiyā dhaññapuñjopi suvaṇṇapuñjopi ācikkhitunti? Āmantā. Evamevaṃ bhagavā lokuttarena vohārena lokiyampi lokuttarampi dhammaṃ voharatīti.

351. Is it possible to indicate both a heap of grain and a heap of gold with a golden staff? Yes. In the same way, the Blessed One, with a supramundane expression, speaks of both mundane Dhamma and supramundane Dhamma.

Labbhā elaṇḍiyāya laṭṭhiyā dhaññapuñjopi suvaṇṇapuñjopi ācikkhitunti? Āmantā. Evamevaṃ bhagavā lokiyena vohārena lokiyampi lokuttarampi dhammaṃ voharatīti.

Is it possible to indicate both a heap of grain and a heap of gold with a castor-oil plant stalk? Yes. In the same way, the Blessed One, with a mundane expression, speaks of both mundane Dhamma and supramundane Dhamma.

352. Buddhassa [M 0.0172] bhagavato vohāro lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiyo hoti, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttaro hotīti? Āmantā. Lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiye sote paṭihaññati, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttare sote paṭihaññati; lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiyena viññāṇena paṭivijānanti, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttarena viññāṇena paṭivijānanti; lokiyaṃ voharantassa puthujjanā paṭivijānanti[T 0.0248], lokuttaraṃ voharantassa sāvakā paṭivijānantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

352. Is the expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One, mundane when He expresses the mundane, and supramundane when He expresses the supramundane? Yes. When He expresses the mundane, does it impinge on the mundane ear? When He expresses the supramundane, does it impinge on the supramundane ear? When He expresses the mundane, do they comprehend with mundane consciousness? When He expresses the supramundane, do they comprehend with supramundane consciousness? When He expresses the mundane, do ordinary people comprehend? When He expresses the supramundane, do disciples comprehend? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiyo hoti, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttaro hotīti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā lokiyampi lokuttarampi dhammaṃ voharatīti? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā lokiyampi lokuttarampi dhammaṃ voharati, tena vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiyo hoti, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttaro hotī”ti.

Should it not be said: ‘The expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is mundane when He expresses the mundane, and supramundane when He expresses the supramundane’? Yes, it should not be said. Does not the Blessed One express both mundane and supramundane phenomena? Yes. If the Blessed One expresses both mundane and supramundane phenomena, then, good sir, it should indeed be said: ‘The expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is mundane when He expresses the mundane, and supramundane when He expresses the supramundane.’

Buddhassa bhagavato vohāro lokiyaṃ voharantassa lokiyo hoti, lokuttaraṃ voharantassa lokuttaro hotīti? Āmantā. Maggaṃ voharantassa maggo hoti, amaggaṃ voharantassa [P 0.0225] amaggo [V 0.0190] hoti, phalaṃ voharantassa phalaṃ hoti, aphalaṃ voharantassa aphalaṃ hoti, nibbānaṃ voharantassa nibbānaṃ hoti, anibbānaṃ voharantassa anibbānaṃ hoti, saṅkhataṃ voharantassa saṅkhataṃ hoti, asaṅkhataṃ voharantassa asaṅkhataṃ hoti, rūpaṃ voharantassa rūpaṃ hoti, arūpaṃ voharantassa arūpaṃ hoti, vedanaṃ voharantassa vedanā hoti, avedanaṃ voharantassa avedanā hoti, saññaṃ voharantassa saññā hoti, asaññaṃ voharantassa asaññā hoti, saṅkhāre voharantassa saṅkhārā honti, asaṅkhāre voharantassa asaṅkhārā honti, viññāṇaṃ voharantassa viññāṇaṃ hoti, aviññāṇaṃ voharantassa aviññāṇaṃ hotīti[T 0.0249]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the expression of the Buddha, the Blessed One, mundane when He expresses the mundane, and supramundane when He expresses the supramundane? Yes. When expressing the path, is it the path? When expressing what is not the path, is it not the path? When expressing the fruit, is it the fruit? When expressing what is not the fruit, is it not the fruit? When expressing Nibbāna, is it Nibbāna? When expressing what is not Nibbāna, is it not Nibbāna? When expressing the conditioned, is it the conditioned? When expressing the unconditioned, is it the unconditioned? When expressing form, is it form? When expressing the formless, is it the formless? When expressing feeling, is it feeling? When expressing what is not feeling, is it not feeling? When expressing perception, is it perception? When expressing what is not perception, is it not perception? When expressing formations, are they formations? When expressing what are not formations, are they not formations? When expressing consciousness, is it consciousness? When expressing what is not consciousness, is it not consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Vohārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Expression is concluded.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

(20) 11. Nirodhakathā

(20) 11. Discourse on Cessation

353. Dve [M 0.0173] nirodhāti? Āmantā. Dve dukkhanirodhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve dukkhanirodhāti? Āmantā. Dve nirodhasaccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve nirodhasaccānīti? Āmantā. Dve dukkhasaccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve nirodhasaccānīti? Āmantā. Dve samudayasaccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve nirodhasaccānīti? Āmantā. Dve [P 0.0226] maggasaccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

353. Are there two cessations? Yes. Are there two cessations of suffering? This should not be said thus... and so on. Are there two cessations of suffering? Yes. Are there two truths of cessation? This should not be said thus... and so on. Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of suffering? This should not be said thus... and so on. Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of origin? This should not be said thus... and so on. Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of the path? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Dve nirodhasaccānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… dve leṇāni… dve saraṇāni… dve parāyaṇāni… dve accutāni… dve amatāni… dve nibbānānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two protections... and so on... two shelters... two refuges... two ultimate goals... two imperishables... two deathless states... two Nibbānas? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Dve nibbānānīti? Āmantā. Atthi dvinnaṃ nibbānānaṃ uccanīcatā hīnapaṇītatā ukkaṃsāvakaṃso sīmā vā bhedo vā rāji vā antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are there two Nibbānas? Yes. Is there any highness or lowness, inferiority or superiority, preeminence or subordination, limit, or division, or boundary, or interval for the two Nibbānas? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Dve nirodhāti? Āmantā. Nanu appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhe saṅkhāre paṭisaṅkhā nirodhentīti? Āmantā. Hañci appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhe saṅkhāre [T 0.0250] paṭisaṅkhā nirodhenti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dve nirodhā”ti.

Are there two cessations? Yes. Are not formations that have ceased without reflection made to cease through reflection? Yes. If formations that have ceased without reflection are made to cease through reflection, then indeed it should not be said, 'There are two cessations.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “dve nirodhā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhāpi saṅkhārā accantabhaggā, paṭisaṅkhāniruddhāpi saṅkhārā accantabhaggāti? Āmantā. Hañci appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhāpi saṅkhārā accantabhaggā, paṭisaṅkhāniruddhāpi saṅkhārā accantabhaggā, tena vata re vattabbe – “dve nirodhā”ti.

Should it not be said: 'There are two cessations'? Yes. Are not formations that have ceased without reflection also utterly broken, and formations that have ceased with reflection also utterly broken? Yes. If formations that have ceased without reflection are utterly broken, and formations that have ceased with reflection are utterly broken, then indeed it should be said: 'There are two cessations.'

Dve [V 0.0191] nirodhāti? Āmantā. Paṭisaṅkhāniruddhāpi paṭisaṅkhāniruddhā (?) saṅkhārā ariyamaggaṃ āgamma niruddhāti? Āmantā. Appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhā [P 0.0227] saṅkhārā ariyamaggaṃ āgamma niruddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are there two cessations? Yes. Do formations that have ceased through reflection also cease by depending on the noble path? Yes. Do formations that have ceased without reflection cease by depending on the noble path? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Dve [M 0.0174] nirodhāti? Āmantā. Paṭisaṅkhāniruddhā saṅkhārā na puna uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Appaṭisaṅkhāniruddhā saṅkhārā na puna uppajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dve nirodhā”ti.

Are there two cessations? Yes. Do formations that have ceased through reflection not arise again? Yes. Do formations that have ceased without reflection not arise again? This should not be said thus... and so on. Therefore, it should not be said, 'There are two cessations.'

Nirodhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Cessation is concluded.

Dutiyavaggo.

The Second Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Parūpahāro aññāṇaṃ, kaṅkhā paravitāraṇā;

Vacībhedo dukkhāhāro, cittaṭṭhiti ca kukkuḷā;

Anupubbābhisamayo, vohāro ca nirodhakoti.

Harming Others, Ignorance, Doubt, Refuting Others, Divisive Speech, Nutriment of Suffering, Mental Steadfastness, Hot Ashes, Gradual Penetration, Convention, and Cessation.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(21) 1. Balakathā

(21) 1. Discourse on Power

354. Tathāgatabalaṃ [T 0.0251][P 0.0228][V 0.0192] sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakabalaṃ, sāvakabalaṃ tathāgatabalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

354. Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Is the Tathāgata's power the disciple's power, and the disciple's power the Tathāgata's power? This should not be said… and so on.

Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Taññeva tathāgatabalaṃ taṃ sāvakabalaṃ, taññeva sāvakabalaṃ taṃ tathāgatabalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Is that very power of the Tathāgata the disciple’s power, and that very disciple’s power the Tathāgata’s power? This should not be said… and so on.

Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Yādisaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ tādisaṃ sāvakabalaṃ, yādisaṃ sāvakabalaṃ tādisaṃ tathāgatabalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
