Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Is the Tathāgata's power of the same kind as the disciple's power, and the disciple's power of the same kind as the Tathāgata's power? This should not be said… and so on.

Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Yādiso tathāgatassa pubbayogo pubbacariyā dhammakkhānaṃ dhammadesanā tādiso sāvakassa pubbayogo pubbacariyā dhammakkhānaṃ dhammadesanāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Are the Tathāgata's previous application, previous conduct, proclamation of the Dhamma, and teaching of the Dhamma of the same kind as a disciple's previous application, previous conduct, proclamation of the Dhamma, and teaching of the Dhamma? This should not be said… and so on.

Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Tathāgato jino satthā sammāsambuddho sabbaññū sabbadassāvī dhammassāmī dhammappaṭisaraṇoti? Āmantā[M 0.0175]. Sāvako jino satthā sammāsambuddho sabbaññū sabbadassāvī dhammassāmī dhammappaṭisaraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Is the Tathāgata a conqueror, a teacher, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, all-knowing, all-seeing, the lord of the Dhamma, one for whom the Dhamma is the refuge? Yes. Is a disciple a conqueror, a teacher, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, all-knowing, all-seeing, the lord of the Dhamma, one for whom the Dhamma is the refuge? This should not be said… and so on.

Tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Tathāgato anuppannassa [T 0.0252] maggassa uppādetā asañjātassa maggassa [P 0.0229] sañjanetā anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā maggaññū maggavidū maggakovidoti? Āmantā. Sāvako anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā maggaññū maggavidū maggakovidoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Tathāgata's power shared with disciples? Yes. Is the Tathāgata the originator of the unarisen path, the producer of the ungenerated path, the proclaimer of the unproclaimed path, the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the one skilled in the path? Yes. Is a disciple the originator of the unarisen path, the producer of the ungenerated path, the proclaimer of the unproclaimed path, the knower of the path, the discoverer of the path, the one skilled in the path? This should not be said… and so on.

Indriyaparopariyattaṃ [V 0.0193] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Sāvako sabbaññū sabbadassāvīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of the faculties of beings as it really is, a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples? Yes. Is a disciple all-knowing and all-seeing? This should not be said… and so on.

355. Sāvako ṭhānāṭhānaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako ṭhānāṭhānaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “ṭhānāṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

355. Does a disciple know the possible and the impossible? Yes. If a disciple knows the possible and the impossible, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the possible and the impossible as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the result of actions undertaken in the past, future, and present, with their conditions and causes? Yes. If a disciple knows the result of actions undertaken in the past, future, and present, with their conditions and causes, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the result of actions undertaken in the past, future, and present, with their conditions and causes, as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the path that leads to all destinations? Yes. If a disciple knows the path that leads to all destinations, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the path that leads to all destinations as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako [T 0.0253] anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the world with its many and various elements? Yes. If a disciple knows the world with its many and various elements, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the world with its many and various elements as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako [P 0.0230] sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “sattānaṃ [M 0.0176] nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the various dispositions of beings? Yes. If a disciple knows the various dispositions of beings, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the various dispositions of beings as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the defilement, purification, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments? Yes. If a disciple knows the defilement, purification, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the defilement, purification, and emergence regarding the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako [V 0.0194] pubbenivāsānussatiṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako pubbenivāsānussatiṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “pubbenivāsānussati yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the recollection of past abodes? Yes. If a disciple knows the recollection of past abodes, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the recollection of past abodes as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Sāvako sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci sāvako sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ jānāti, tena vata re vattabbe – “sattānaṃ cutūpapātaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Does a disciple know the passing away and reappearance of beings? Yes. If a disciple knows the passing away and reappearance of beings, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

Nanu tathāgatassāpi āsavā khīṇā sāvakassāpi āsavā khīṇāti[T 0.0254]? Āmantā. Atthi kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ tathāgatassa vā sāvakassa vā āsavakkhayena vā āsavakkhayaṃ vimuttiyā vā vimuttīti? Natthi. Hañci natthi kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ tathāgatassa vā sāvakassa vā āsavakkhayena vā āsavakkhayaṃ vimuttiyā vā vimutti, tena vata re vattabbe – “āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇa”nti.

Are not the taints of the Tathāgata destroyed, and the taints of a disciple also destroyed? Yes. Is there any difference whatsoever between the Tathāgata and a disciple with regard to the destruction of the taints and the destruction of the taints, or with regard to liberation and liberation? There is not. If there is no difference whatsoever between the Tathāgata and a disciple with regard to the destruction of the taints and the destruction of the taints, or with regard to liberation and liberation, then indeed it should be said: 'The knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is, is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples.'

356. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā[P 0.0231]. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

356. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the possible and the impossible as it really is a power of the Tathāgata shared with disciples? This should not be said… and so on.

Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it really is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared with disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings as it really is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared with disciples? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? This should not be said thus...

Sattānaṃ [M 0.0177] cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they actually are, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as they actually are, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? This should not be said thus...

Indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti[T 0.0255]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe ayamettha sādhāraṇapakkhaṃ sandhāya paṭikkhepo (ṭīkā oloketabbā) …pe….

Is the knowledge of the dispositions of the faculties of other beings as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? This should not be said thus...

Indriyaparopariyattaṃ [V 0.0195] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā…pe…. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakaasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the dispositions of the faculties of other beings as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? Yes... and so on. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, not shared by disciples? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Na [P 0.0232] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared by disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the dispositions of the faculties of other beings as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared by disciples? This should not be said thus...

Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Āmantā. Indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ sāvakasādhāraṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared by disciples? Yes. Is the knowledge of the dispositions of the faculties of other beings as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, shared by disciples? This should not be said thus...

Balakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Powers is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(22) 2. Ariyantikathā

3. (22) 2. Discourse on What is Noble

357. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmimaggo sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmimaggo anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattamaggo arahattaphalaṃ, satipaṭṭhānaṃ sammappadhānaṃ iddhipādo indriyaṃ balaṃ bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, Nibbāna; the path to stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry; the path to once-returning, the fruit of once-returning; the path to non-returning, the fruit of non-returning; the path to arahantship, the fruit of arahantship; the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā[T 0.0256]. Suññatārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Suññatārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhānañca [M 0.0178] manasi karoti, suññatañca manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

357. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble? Yes. Is it with emptiness as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on. Is it with emptiness as its object? Yes. Does one attend to what is possible and impossible, and also attend to emptiness? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhānañca [V 0.0196] manasi karoti, suññatañca manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na [P 0.0233] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhānañca manasi karoti, appaṇihitañca manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one attend to what is possible and impossible, and also attend to emptiness? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two minds? This should not be said thus... and so on. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble? Yes. Is it with the signless as its object... and so on... with the desireless as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on. Is it with the desireless as its object? Yes. Does one attend to what is possible and impossible, and also attend to the desireless? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhānañca manasi karoti, appaṇihitañca manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one attend to what is possible and impossible, and also attend to the desireless? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two minds? This should not be said thus... and so on.

358. Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā suññatārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ suññatārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the foundations of mindfulness noble and with emptiness as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble and with emptiness as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā animittārammaṇā…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

358. Are the foundations of mindfulness noble, with the signless as their object... and so on... with the desireless as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble and with the desireless as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Sammappadhānā, iddhipādā, indriyā, balā, bojjhaṅgā ariyā suññatārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ [T 0.0257] tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ suññatārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment noble and with emptiness as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble and with emptiness as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Bojjhaṅgā ariyā animittārammaṇā… appaṇihitārammaṇāti? Āmantā[P 0.0234]. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the factors of enlightenment noble, with the signless as their object... with the desireless as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble and with the desireless as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on.

359. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “suññatārammaṇa”nti? Āmantā. Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā na vattabbā – “suññatārammaṇā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object’? Yes. Are the foundations of mindfulness, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as their object’? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti[V 0.0197]? Āmantā. Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā na vattabbā – “appaṇihitārammaṇā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

359. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble, not to be called ‘with the signless as its object’... and so on... ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Are the foundations of mindfulness, noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as their object’? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne [M 0.0179] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – suññatārammaṇaṃ…pe… animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Sammappadhānaṃ…pe… bojjhaṅgā ariyā na vattabbā – “appaṇihitārammaṇā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it actually is, a power of the Tathāgata, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object’... and so on... ‘with the signless as its object’... and so on... ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Are the right efforts... and so on... the factors of enlightenment, noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as their object’? This should not be said thus... and so on.

360. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they actually are, a power of the Tathāgata, noble? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, Nibbāna; the path to stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry... and so on... the factors of enlightenment? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Suññatārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… suññātārammaṇanti[P 0.0235]? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapātañca manasi karoti[T 0.0258], suññatañca manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

360. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as they actually are, a power of the Tathāgata, noble? Yes. Is it with emptiness as its object? This should not be said thus... and so on. Is it with emptiness as its object? Yes. Does one attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings, and also attend to emptiness? This should not be said thus... and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapātañca manasi karoti, suññatañca manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings, and also attend to emptiness? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two minds? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Animittārammaṇaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapātañca manasi karoti, appaṇihitañca manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble? Yes. Is it with the signless as its object, with the desireless as its object? That should not be said so, and so on. Is it with the desireless as its object? Yes. Does one attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings, and also attend to the desireless? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapātañca manasi karoti, appaṇihitañca manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings, and also attend to the desireless? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two minds? That should not be said so, and so on.

361. Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā suññatārammaṇā…pe… animittārammaṇā…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

361. Are the foundations of mindfulness noble, with emptiness as their object, and so on, with the signless as their object, and so on, with the desireless as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with the desireless as its object? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sammappadhānaṃ [P 0.0236][V 0.0198] …pe… bojjhaṅgā ariyā suññatārammaṇā…pe… animittārammaṇā…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the right efforts, and so on, the factors of enlightenment noble, with emptiness as their object, and so on, with the signless as their object, and so on, with the desireless as their object? Yes. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with the desireless as its object? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sattānaṃ [M 0.0180] cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – suññatārammaṇaṃ…pe… animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Satipaṭṭhānā ariyā na vattabbā – “appapaṇihitārammaṇā”ti[T 0.0259]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the signless as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Are the foundations of mindfulness noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as their object’? That should not be said so, and so on.

362. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – suññatārammaṇaṃ…pe… animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Sammappadhānā…pe… bojjhaṅgā ariyā na vattabbā – “appaṇihitārammaṇā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

362. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the signless as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Are the right efforts, and so on, the factors of enlightenment noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as their object’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble? That should not be said so, and so on.

Āsavānaṃ [P 0.0237] khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Āmantā. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble? Yes. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble? That should not be said so, and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “ariya”nti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “ariya”nti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, not to be called ‘noble’? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, not to be called ‘noble’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “ariya”nti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “ariya”nti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, not to be called ‘noble’? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, not to be called ‘noble’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Āsavānaṃ [V 0.0199] khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ suññatārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ suññatārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with emptiness as its object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with emptiness as its object? That should not be said so, and so on.

Āsavānaṃ khaye [T 0.0260] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ animittārammaṇaṃ… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with the signless as its object, and so on, with the desireless as its object? Yes. Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with the desireless as its object? That should not be said so, and so on.

Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ suññatārammaṇaṃ…pe… animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā…pe…. Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte [M 0.0181] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with emptiness as its object, and so on, with the signless as its object, and so on, with the desireless as its object? Yes, and so on. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, with the desireless as its object? That should not be said so, and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne [P 0.0238] yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “suññatārammaṇa”nti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “suññatārammaṇa”nti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object’? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Ṭhānāṭhāne yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – animittārammaṇaṃ… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “appaṇihitārammaṇa”nti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of what is possible and impossible as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with the signless as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as its object’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Sattānaṃ cutūpapāte yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – suññatārammaṇaṃ…pe… animittārammaṇaṃ…pe… appaṇihitārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Āsavānaṃ khaye yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ tathāgatabalaṃ ariyaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “appaṇihitārammaṇa”nti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with emptiness as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the signless as its object,’ and so on, ‘with the desireless as its object’? Yes. Is the knowledge of the destruction of the taints as it truly is a Tathāgata’s power, noble, not to be called ‘with the desireless as its object’? That should not be said so, and so on.

Ariyantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Noble is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(23) 3. Vimuttikathā

3. (23) 3. The Discourse on Liberation

363. Sarāgaṃ [T 0.0261][V 0.0200] cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Āmantā. Rāgasahagataṃ rāgasahajātaṃ rāgasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ rāgasampayuttaṃ rāgasahabhu rāgānuparivatti akusalaṃ lokiyaṃ sāsavaṃ saṃyojaniyaṃ ganthaniyaṃ oghaniyaṃ yoganiyaṃ nīvaraṇiyaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ upādāniyaṃ saṃkilesiyaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with lust liberated? Yes. Is an unwholesome, worldly mind, with taints, liable to fetters, liable to bonds, liable to floods, liable to yokes, liable to hindrances, clung to, a basis for clinging, defiled—a mind accompanied by lust, co-arisen with lust, mixed with lust, associated with lust, co-existent with lust, revolving around lust—liberated? That should not be said so, and so on.

Saphassaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Sarāgaṃ [P 0.0239] cittaṃ vimuccati, rāgo ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

363. Is a mind with contact liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with lust liberated, and are both lust and the mind liberated? That should not be said so, and so on.

Savedanaṃ…pe… sasaññaṃ…pe… sacetanaṃ…pe… sapaññaṃ sasaññaṃ (sī. ka.) cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Sarāgaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, rāgo ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling… with perception… with volition… with wisdom liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with lust liberated, and are both lust and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Saphassaṃ [M 0.0182] sarāgaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Rāgo ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with contact and lust liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Are both lust and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Savedanaṃ sarāgaṃ…pe… sasaññaṃ sarāgaṃ…pe… sacetanaṃ sarāgaṃ…pe… sapaññaṃ sarāgaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Rāgo ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling and lust… with perception and lust… with volition and lust… with wisdom and lust liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Are both lust and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

364. Sadosaṃ [T 0.0262] cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Āmantā. Dosasahagataṃ dosasahajātaṃ dosasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ dosasampayuttaṃ dosasahabhu dosānuparivatti akusalaṃ lokiyaṃ sāsavaṃ…pe… saṃkilesiyaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

364. Is a mind with aversion liberated? Yes. Is an unwholesome, worldly mind, with taints… and so on… defiled—a mind accompanied by aversion, co-arisen with aversion, mixed with aversion, associated with aversion, co-existent with aversion, revolving around aversion—liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Saphassaṃ [V 0.0201] cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Sadosaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, doso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with contact liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with aversion liberated, and are both aversion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Savedanaṃ…pe… sasaññaṃ…pe… sacetanaṃ…pe… sapaññaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā[P 0.0240]. Sadosaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, doso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling… with perception… with volition… with wisdom liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with aversion liberated, and are both aversion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Saphassaṃ sadosaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Sadosaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, doso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with contact and aversion liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with aversion liberated, and are both aversion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Savedanaṃ sadosaṃ… sasaññaṃ sadosaṃ… sacetanaṃ sadosaṃ… sapaññaṃ sadosaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Doso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling and aversion… with perception and aversion… with volition and aversion… with wisdom and aversion liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Are both aversion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

365. Samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Āmantā. Mohasahagataṃ mohasahajātaṃ mohasaṃsaṭṭhaṃ mohasampayuttaṃ mohasahabhu mohānuparivatti akusalaṃ [T 0.0263] lokiyaṃ sāsavaṃ…pe… saṃkilesiyaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

365. Is a mind with delusion liberated? Yes. Is an unwholesome, worldly mind, with taints… and so on… defiled—a mind accompanied by delusion, co-arisen with delusion, mixed with delusion, associated with delusion, co-existent with delusion, revolving around delusion—liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Saphassaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, moho ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with contact liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with delusion liberated, and are both delusion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Savedanaṃ [M 0.0183]… sasaññaṃ… sacetanaṃ… sapaññaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, moho ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling… with perception… with volition… with wisdom liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Is a mind with delusion liberated, and are both delusion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Saphassaṃ [V 0.0202] samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, phasso ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā[P 0.0241]. Moho ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with contact and delusion liberated, and are both contact and the mind liberated? Yes. Are both delusion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Savedanaṃ samohaṃ… sasaññaṃ samohaṃ… sacetanaṃ samohaṃ…pe… sapaññaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccati, paññā ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Āmantā. Moho ca cittañca ubho vimuccantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a mind with feeling and delusion… with perception and delusion… with volition and delusion… with wisdom and delusion liberated, and are both wisdom and the mind liberated? Yes. Are both delusion and the mind liberated? This should not be said… and so on….

Sarāgaṃ sadosaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Āmantā. Vītarāgaṃ vītadosaṃ vītamohaṃ nikkilesaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “sarāgaṃ sadosaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ vimuccatī”ti.

Is a mind with lust, with aversion, with delusion liberated? Yes. Is a mind without lust, without aversion, without delusion, without defilements, liberated? This should not be said… and so on… Therefore, it should not be said that 'a mind with lust, with aversion, with delusion is liberated.'

Vimuttikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Liberation is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(24) 4. Vimuccamānakathā

(24) 4. Discussion on Being Liberated

366. Vimuttaṃ [T 0.0264] vimuccamānanti? Āmantā. Ekadesaṃ vimuttaṃ, ekadesaṃ avimuttanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

366. “Is a liberated one being liberated?” “Yes.” “Is one partly liberated and partly unliberated?” “This should not be said…”

Ekadesaṃ vimuttaṃ, ekadesaṃ avimuttanti? Āmantā. Ekadesaṃ sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ na sotāpanno, ekadesaṃ sotāpattiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ sattakkhattuparamo kolaṅkolo ekabījī buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato, ekadesaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi na samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is one partly liberated and partly unliberated?” “Yes.” “Is one partly a stream-enterer and partly not a stream-enterer? Is one partly one who has attained, gained, realized, and dwells having directly experienced the fruit of stream-entry, having touched it with the body, and partly not having touched it with the body? Is one partly a seven-times-at-most, a family-to-family, a one-seed, endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, and partly not endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones?” “This should not be said…”

Ekadesaṃ [V 0.0203] vimuttaṃ, ekadesaṃ avimuttanti? Āmantā[P 0.0242]. Ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na sakadāgāmī, ekadesaṃ sakadāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is one partly liberated and partly unliberated?” “Yes.” “Is one partly a once-returner and partly not a once-returner? Is one partly one who has attained, gained, realized, and dwells having directly experienced the fruit of once-returning, having touched it with the body, and partly not having touched it with the body?” “This should not be said…”

Ekadesaṃ [M 0.0184] vimuttaṃ, ekadesaṃ avimuttanti? Āmantā. Ekadesaṃ anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ na anāgāmī, ekadesaṃ anāgāmiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ antarāparinibbāyī[T 0.0265], upahaccaparinibbāyī, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, uddhaṃsotoakaniṭṭhagāmī, ekadesaṃ na uddhaṃsotoakaniṭṭhagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is one partly liberated and partly unliberated?” “Yes.” “Is one partly a non-returner and partly not a non-returner? Is one partly one who has attained, gained, realized, and dwells having directly experienced the fruit of non-returning, having touched it with the body, and partly not having touched it with the body? Is one partly one who attains final Nibbāna in the interim, one who attains final Nibbāna upon impact, one who attains final Nibbāna without exertion, one who attains final Nibbāna with exertion, one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm?” “This should not be said…”

Ekadesaṃ vimuttaṃ, ekadesaṃ avimuttanti? Āmantā. Ekadesaṃ arahā ekadesaṃ na arahā, ekadesaṃ arahattappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ na kāyena phusitvā viharati, ekadesaṃ vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho…pe… ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikataṃ, ekadesaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ na sacchikatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is one partly liberated and partly unliberated?” “Yes.” “Is one partly an arahant and partly not an arahant? Is one partly one who has attained, gained, realized, and dwells having directly experienced arahantship, having touched it with the body, and partly not having touched it with the body? Is one partly free from lust, free from hatred, free from delusion… and partly what is to be realized has been realized, and partly what is to be realized has not been realized?” “That should not be said…”

Vimuttaṃ vimuccamānanti? Āmantā. Uppādakkhaṇe vimuttaṃ, bhaṅgakkhaṇe vimuccamānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is a liberated mind being liberated?” “Yes.” “Is it liberated at the moment of arising, and being liberated at the moment of dissolution?” “That should not be said…”

367. Na vattabbaṃ – “vimuttaṃ vimuccamāna”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccatī”ti dī. ni. 1.248 ādayo! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0243]. Tena hi vattabbaṃ tena hi (sī. syā. kaṃ.), tena hi na vattabbaṃ (ka.) – “vimuttaṃ vimuccamāna”nti.

367. “Should it not be said, ‘what is liberated is being liberated’?” “Yes.” “But has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘For one who knows thus, who sees thus, their mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, their mind is liberated from the taint of existence, their mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance’?” “Is there such a Sutta?” “Yes.” “Then it should be said, ‘what is liberated is being liberated.’”

Vimuttaṃ vimuccamānanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ [V 0.0204] khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmetī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [T 0.0266] hi na vattabbaṃ – “vimuttaṃ vimuccamāna”nti.

“Is a liberated mind being liberated?” “Yes.” “But has the Blessed One not said: ‘When their mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, spotless, rid of defilements, pliable, workable, firm, and immovable, they direct their mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints’?” “Is there such a Sutta?” “Yes.” “Then it should not be said, ‘what is liberated is being liberated.’”

Atthi cittaṃ vimuccamānanti? Āmantā. Atthi cittaṃ rajjamānaṃ dussamānaṃ muyhamānaṃ kilissamānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu rattañceva arattañca, duṭṭhañceva aduṭṭhañca, mūḷhañceva amūḷhañca, chinnañceva achinnañca, bhinnañceva abhinnañca, katañceva akatañcāti[M 0.0185]? Āmantā. Hañci rattañceva arattañca, duṭṭhañceva aduṭṭhañca, mūḷhañceva amūḷhañca, chinnañceva achinnañca, bhinnañceva abhinnañca, katañceva akatañca, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi cittaṃ vimuccamāna”nti.

“Is there a mind being liberated?” “Yes.” “Is there a mind being impassioned, being corrupted, being deluded, or being defiled?” “That should not be said…” “Is there not both the impassioned and the unimpassioned, the corrupted and the uncorrupted, the deluded and the undeluded, the cut and the uncut, the broken and the unbroken, the done and the undone?” “Yes.” “If there is both the impassioned and the unimpassioned, the corrupted and the uncorrupted, the deluded and the undeluded, the cut and the uncut, the broken and the unbroken, the done and the undone, then it should not be said, ‘There is a mind being liberated.’”

Vimuccamānakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Being Liberated is Concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter.

(25) 5. Aṭṭhamakakathā

3. (25) 5. Discussion on the Eighth Person

368. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo sotāpanno sotāpattiphalappatto paṭiladdho adhigato sacchikato upasampajja viharati, kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with views?” “Yes.” “Is the eighth person a stream-enterer, one who has attained, gained, realized, and dwells having directly experienced the fruit of stream-entry, having touched it with the body?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako [P 0.0244] puggalo sotāpanno sotāpattiphalappatto…pe… kāyena phusitvā viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

368. “Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “Yes.” “Is the eighth person a stream-enterer, one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry… having touched it with the body?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa [T 0.0267] puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhānusayo pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti[V 0.0205]? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchānusayo… sīlabbataparāmāso pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with views?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person abandoned the underlying tendency to views?” “That should not be said…” “Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with views?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person abandoned the underlying tendency to doubt… the clinging to precepts and practices?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchānusayo pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhānusayo… sīlabbataparāmāso pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person abandoned the underlying tendency to doubt?” “That should not be said…” “Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person abandoned the underlying tendency to views… the clinging to precepts and practices?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ appahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhānusayo appahīnoti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ appahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the eighth person not abandoned the underlying tendency to views?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the obsession with views?” “That should not be said…” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the underlying tendency to views?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa [M 0.0186] puggalassa vicikicchānusayo… sīlabbataparāmāso appahīnoti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa [P 0.0245] puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ appahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa sīlabbataparāmāso appahīnoti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ appahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the eighth person not abandoned the underlying tendency to doubt… the clinging to precepts and practices?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the obsession with views?” “That should not be said…” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the clinging to precepts and practices?” “Yes.” “Has the eighth person not abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “That should not be said…”

369. Aṭṭhamakassa [T 0.0268] puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānapahānāya maggo bhāvitoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānapahānāya satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā…pe… sammappadhānā…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

“Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with views?” “Yes.” “Has the path for abandoning the obsession with views been developed by the eighth person?” “That should not be said…” “Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with views?” “Yes.” “Have the foundations of mindfulness… the right efforts… the factors of enlightenment been developed by the eighth person for abandoning the obsession with views?” “That should not be said.”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānapahānāya maggo bhāvito…pe… bojjhaṅgā bhāvitāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

369. “Has the eighth person abandoned the obsession with doubt?” “Yes.” “Has the path for abandoning the obsession with doubt been developed… have the factors of enlightenment been developed?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa [V 0.0206] puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānapahānāya maggo abhāvitoti? Āmantā. Amaggena pahīnaṃ lokiyena sāsavena…pe… saṃkilesiyenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānapahānāya satipaṭṭhānā…pe… bojjhaṅgā abhāvitāti? Āmantā. Amaggena pahīnaṃ lokiyena sāsavena…pe… saṃkilesiyenāti? Na [P 0.0246] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the path for abandoning the obsession with views not been developed by the eighth person?” “Yes.” “Was it abandoned by a non-path, by what is worldly, tainted… defiling?” “That should not be said…” “Have the foundations of mindfulness… the factors of enlightenment for abandoning the obsession with views not been developed by the eighth person?” “Yes.” “Was it abandoned by a non-path, by what is worldly, tainted… defiling?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānapahānāya maggo abhāvito…pe… satipaṭṭhānā…pe… bojjhaṅgā abhāvitāti? Āmantā. Amaggena pahīnaṃ lokiyena sāsavena…pe… saṃkilesiyenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Has the path for abandoning the obsession with doubt not been developed by the eighth person… the foundations of mindfulness… the factors of enlightenment not been developed?” “Yes.” “Was it abandoned by a non-path, by what is worldly, tainted… defiling?” “That should not be said…”

370. Na [T 0.0269] vattabbaṃ – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīna”nti? Āmantā. Uppajjissatīti? Nuppajjissati. Hañci nuppajjissati, tena vata re vattabbe – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīna”nti.

370. “Should it not be said, ‘The obsession with views has been abandoned by the eighth person’?” “Yes.” “Will it arise?” “It will not arise.” “If it will not arise, then indeed it should be said, ‘The obsession with views has been abandoned by the eighth person.’”

Na vattabbaṃ – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīna”nti? Āmantā. Uppajjissatīti? Nuppajjissati. Hañci nuppajjissati, tena vata re vattabbe – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ pahīna”nti.

“Should it not be said, ‘The obsession with doubt has been abandoned by the eighth person’?” “Yes.” “Will it arise?” “It will not arise.” “If it will not arise, then indeed it should be said, ‘The obsession with doubt has been abandoned by the eighth person.’”

Aṭṭhamakassa [M 0.0187] puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhānusayo nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is the obsession with views abandoned for the eighth person on the grounds that it will not arise?” “Yes.” “Is the underlying tendency to views abandoned on the grounds that it will not arise?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchānusayo… sīlabbataparāmāso nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is the obsession with views abandoned for the eighth person on the grounds that it will not arise?” “Yes.” “Is the underlying tendency to doubt… the clinging to precepts and practices abandoned on the grounds that it will not arise?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Āmantā[V 0.0207]. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchānusayo… sīlabbataparāmāso nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnoti? Na [P 0.0247] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is the obsession with doubt abandoned for the eighth person on the grounds that it will not arise?” “Yes.” “Is the underlying tendency to doubt… the clinging to precepts and practices abandoned on the grounds that it will not arise?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā [T 0.0270] pahīnanti? Āmantā. Gotrabhuno puggalassa diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Āmantā. Gotrabhuno puggalassa vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ nuppajjissatīti katvā pahīnanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Is the obsession with views abandoned for the eighth person on the grounds that it will not arise?” “Yes.” “Is the obsession with views abandoned for the person at the change-of-lineage on the grounds that it will not arise?” “That should not be said…” “Is the obsession with doubt abandoned for the eighth person on the grounds that it will not arise?” “Yes.” “Is the obsession with doubt abandoned for the person at the change-of-lineage on the grounds that it will not arise?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Eighth Person is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(26) 6. Aṭṭhamakassaindriyakathā

(26) 6. The Discussion on the Faculties of the Eighth Person

371. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi saddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… natthi satindriyaṃ…pe… natthi samādhindriyaṃ…pe… natthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi paññāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

371. “Does the eighth person lack the faculty of faith?” “Yes.” “Does the eighth person lack faith?” “That should not be said.” “Does the eighth person lack the faculty of energy… lack the faculty of mindfulness… lack the faculty of concentration… lack the faculty of wisdom?” “Yes.” “Does the eighth person lack wisdom?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhāti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi vīriyaṃ…pe… atthi sati… atthi samādhi… atthi paññāti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa [T 0.0271] atthi paññindriyanti? Na [P 0.0248] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Does the eighth person have faith?” “Yes.” “Does the eighth person have the faculty of faith?” “That should not be said…” “Does the eighth person have energy… have mindfulness… have concentration… have wisdom?” “Yes.” “Does the eighth person have the faculty of wisdom?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi mano, atthi manindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa [V 0.0208] atthi saddhā, atthi saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa [M 0.0188] puggalassa atthi mano, atthi manindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“For the eighth person, is there mind, and is there the faculty of mind?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there faith, and is there the faculty of faith?” “That should not be said…” “For the eighth person, is there mind, and is there the faculty of mind?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there wisdom, and is there the faculty of wisdom?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi somanassaṃ, atthi somanassindriyaṃ, atthi jīvitaṃ, atthi jīvitindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, atthi saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi jīvitaṃ, atthi jīvitindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa…pe… atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“For the eighth person, is there gladness and the faculty of gladness, is there life and the faculty of life?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there faith and the faculty of faith?” “That should not be said…” “For the eighth person, is there life and the faculty of life?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person… is there wisdom and the faculty of wisdom?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, natthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi mano, natthi manindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“For the eighth person, is there faith but not the faculty of faith?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there mind but not the faculty of mind?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, natthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi somanassaṃ, natthi somanassindriyanti…pe… atthi jīvitaṃ, natthi jīvitindriyanti? Na [P 0.0249] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa [T 0.0272] puggalassa atthi paññā, natthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi mano, natthi manindriyanti? Atthi somanassaṃ, natthi somanassindriyanti? Atthi jīvitaṃ, natthi jīvitindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“For the eighth person, is there faith but not the faculty of faith?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there gladness but not the faculty of gladness… is there life but not the faculty of life?” “That should not be said…” “For the eighth person, is there wisdom but not the faculty of wisdom?” “Yes.” “For the eighth person, is there mind but not the faculty of mind? Is there gladness but not the faculty of gladness? Is there life but not the faculty of life?” “That should not be said…”

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo assaddhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi vīriyindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo kusīto hīnavīriyoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi satindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo muṭṭhassati asampajānoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi samādhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo asamāhito vibbhantacittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako puggalo duppañño elamūgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the eighth individual lack the faculty of faith? Yes. Is the eighth individual faithless? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does the eighth individual lack the faculty of energy? Yes. Is the eighth individual lazy and of diminished energy? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does the eighth individual lack the faculty of mindfulness? Yes. Is the eighth individual unmindful and without clear comprehension? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does the eighth individual lack the faculty of concentration? Yes. Is the eighth individual unconcentrated and with a deranged mind? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does the eighth individual lack the faculty of wisdom? Yes. Is the eighth individual of poor wisdom and dull-witted? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Aṭṭhamakassa [V 0.0209] puggalassa atthi saddhā, sā ca saddhā niyyānikāti? Āmantā. Hañci aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, sā ca saddhā niyyānikā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi saddhindriya”nti. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi vīriyaṃ, tañca vīriyaṃ niyyānikaṃ; atthi sati, sā ca sati niyyānikā; atthi [T 0.0273] samādhi, so ca samādhi niyyāniko; atthi paññā, sā ca paññā niyyānikāti? Āmantā[P 0.0250]. Hañci aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa [M 0.0189] atthi paññā, sā ca paññā niyyānikā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi paññindriya”nti.

Does the eighth individual possess faith, and is that faith conducive to release? Yes. If the eighth individual possesses faith, and that faith is conducive to release, then surely it should not be said that 'the eighth individual lacks the faculty of faith.' Does the eighth individual possess energy, and is that energy conducive to release; possess mindfulness, and is that mindfulness conducive to release; possess concentration, and is that concentration conducive to release; possess wisdom, and is that wisdom conducive to release? Yes. If the eighth individual possesses wisdom, and that wisdom is conducive to release, then surely it should not be said that 'the eighth individual lacks the faculty of wisdom.'

372. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, atthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, atthi saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

372. For the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning, is there faith and the faculty of faith? Yes. For the eighth individual, is there faith and the faculty of faith? It should not be said thus… and so on… For the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning, is there wisdom and the faculty of wisdom? Yes. For the eighth individual, is there wisdom and the faculty of wisdom? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa… arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, atthi saddhindriyaṃ…pe… atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi paññā, atthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning... for the individual practicing for the realization of arahantship, is there faith, is there the faculty of faith... and so on... is there wisdom, is there the faculty of wisdom? Yes. For the eighth individual, is there wisdom, is there the faculty of wisdom? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, natthi saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, natthi saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi paññā, natthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa [T 0.0274] atthi paññā, natthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the eighth individual have faith but not the faculty of faith? Yes. Does the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning have faith but not the faculty of faith? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does the eighth individual have wisdom but not the faculty of wisdom? Yes. Does the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning have wisdom but not the faculty of wisdom? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi saddhā, natthi saddhindriyanti…pe… atthi paññā, natthi paññindriyanti? Āmantā[P 0.0251]. Anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa… arahattasacchikiriyāya [V 0.0210] paṭipannassa puggalassa atthi paññā, natthi paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the eighth individual have faith but not the faculty of faith… and so on… have wisdom but not the faculty of wisdom? Yes. Does the individual practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning… the individual practicing for the realization of arahantship have wisdom but not the faculty of wisdom? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa natthi pañcindriyānīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni! Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahā hoti. Tato mudutarehi arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti. Yassa kho, bhikkhave, imāni [M 0.0190] pañcindriyāni sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ natthi, tamahaṃ ‘bāhiro puthujjanapakkhe ṭhito’ti vadāmī”ti saṃ. ni. 5.488. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Aṭṭhamako [T 0.0275] puggalo bāhiro puthujjanapakkhe ṭhitoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi aṭṭhamakassa puggalassa atthi pañcindriyānīti.

Does the eighth individual lack the five faculties? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: "Monks, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. These, monks, are the five faculties. Monks, through the completion and perfection of these five faculties, one becomes an arahant. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of arahantship. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is a non-returner. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is a once-returner. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is a stream-enterer. With faculties somewhat weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. Monks, one in whom these five faculties are entirely, completely, and utterly absent—him I declare to be an outsider, standing in the category of ordinary people." Is there such a discourse? Yes. Is the eighth individual an outsider, standing in the category of ordinary people? It should not be said thus… and so on… Therefore, the eighth individual possesses the five faculties.

Aṭṭhamakassa indriyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on the faculties of the eighth individual is concluded.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(27) 7. Dibbacakkhukathā

(27) 7. Discourse on the Divine Eye

373. Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Maṃsacakkhuṃ dibbacakkhuṃ, dibbacakkhuṃ maṃsacakkhunti? Na [P 0.0252] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

373. Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the physical eye the divine eye, and the divine eye the physical eye? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Yādisaṃ maṃsacakkhuṃ tādisaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ, yādisaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ tādisaṃ maṃsacakkhunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the physical eye like the divine eye, and the divine eye like the physical eye? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Maṃsacakkhuṃ [V 0.0211] dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Taññeva maṃsacakkhuṃ taṃ dibbacakkhuṃ, taṃ dibbacakkhuṃ taṃ maṃsacakkhunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is that very physical eye that divine eye, and that very divine eye that physical eye? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Yādiso maṃsacakkhussa visayo ānubhāvo gocaro tādiso dibbassa cakkhussa visayo ānubhāvo gocaroti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the scope, power, and range of the physical eye the same as the scope, power, and range of the divine eye? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Upādiṇṇaṃ upādinnaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) hutvā anupādiṇṇaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Having been subject to clinging, does it become not subject to clinging? It should not be said thus…pe….

Upādiṇṇaṃ hutvā anupādiṇṇaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacaraṃ [T 0.0276] hutvā rūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been subject to clinging, does it become not subject to clinging? Yes. Having been of the sense-sphere, does it become of the form-sphere? It should not be said thus…pe….

Kāmāvacaraṃ hutvā rūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacaraṃ hutvā arūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been of the sense-sphere, does it become of the form-sphere? Yes. Having been of the form-sphere, does it become of the formless-sphere? It should not be said thus…pe….

Rūpāvacaraṃ hutvā arūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Pariyāpannaṃ hutvā apariyāpannaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been of the form-sphere, does it become of the formless-sphere? Yes. Having been mundane, does it become supramundane? It should not be said thus…pe….

374. Maṃsacakkhuṃ [M 0.0191][P 0.0253] dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Dibbacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ maṃsacakkhuṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

374. Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the divine eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the physical eye? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Dibbacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ paññācakkhuṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the divine eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the wisdom eye? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Dibbacakkhuṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ maṃsacakkhuṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Is the divine eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the physical eye? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsacakkhuṃ [V 0.0212] dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbacakkhuṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Dveva cakkhūnīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dveva cakkhūnīti? Āmantā. Nanu tīṇi cakkhūni vuttāni bhagavatā – maṃsacakkhuṃ, dibbacakkhuṃ, paññācakkhunti? Āmantā. Hañci tīṇi cakkhūni vuttāni bhagavatā – maṃsacakkhuṃ, dibbacakkhuṃ, paññācakkhuṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dveva cakkhūnī”ti.

Is the physical eye, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine eye? Yes. Are there only two eyes? It should not be said thus…pe… Are there only two eyes? Yes. But did not the Blessed One speak of three eyes—the physical eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom? Yes. If the Blessed One spoke of three eyes—the physical eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom—then it should not be said, “There are only two eyes.”

Dveva cakkhūnīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, cakkhūni! Katamāni tīṇi? Maṃsacakkhuṃ, dibbacakkhuṃ, paññācakkhunti – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi cakkhūnī”ti.

Are there only two eyes? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: "Monks, there are these three eyes. Which three? The physical eye, the divine eye, and the eye of wisdom. These, monks, are the three eyes"?

“Maṃsacakkhuṃ [T 0.0277][P 0.0254] dibbacakkhuṃ, paññācakkhuṃ anuttaraṃ;

Etāni tīṇi cakkhūni, akkhāsi purisuttamo.

"The physical eye, the divine eye, and the unsurpassed eye of wisdom—these three eyes the Supreme Person has declared.

“Maṃsacakkhussa uppādo, maggo dibbassa cakkhuno;

Yadā ca ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññācakkhuṃ anuttaraṃ;

Tassa cakkhussa paṭilābhā, sabbadukkhā pamuccatī”ti itivu. 61 itivuttake.

"The arising of the physical eye is the way to the divine eye. When knowledge—the unsurpassed eye of wisdom—arose, through the attainment of that eye, one is freed from all suffering."

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dveva cakkhūnī”ti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, "There are only two eyes."

Dibbacakkhukathā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the discussion on the Divine Eye.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(28) 8. Dibbasotakathā

3. (28) 8. Discussion on the Divine Ear

375. Maṃsasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Maṃsasotaṃ dibbasotaṃ, dibbasotaṃ maṃsasotanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is the physical ear the divine ear, and is the divine ear the physical ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsasotaṃ [M 0.0192][V 0.0213] dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Yādisaṃ maṃsasotaṃ tādisaṃ dibbasotaṃ, yādisaṃ dibbasotaṃ tādisaṃ maṃsasotanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

375. Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is the physical ear of the same kind as the divine ear, and is the divine ear of the same kind as the physical ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Taññeva maṃsasotaṃ taṃ dibbasotaṃ, taṃ dibbasotaṃ taṃ maṃsasotanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is that very physical ear the divine ear, and is that divine ear that physical ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsasotaṃ [T 0.0278] dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Yādiso maṃsasotassa visayo ānubhāvo gocaro tādiso dibbassa sotassa visayo ānubhāvo gocaroti? Na [P 0.0255] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is the scope, power, and range of the physical ear the same as the scope, power, and range of the divine ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Upādiṇṇaṃ hutvā anupādiṇṇaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Having been subject to clinging, does it become not subject to clinging? It should not be said thus…pe….

Upādiṇṇaṃ hutvā anupādiṇṇaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacaraṃ hutvā rūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been subject to clinging, does it become not subject to clinging? Yes. Having been of the sense-sphere, does it become of the form-sphere? It should not be said thus…pe….

Kāmāvacaraṃ hutvā rūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacaraṃ hutvā arūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been of the sense-sphere, does it become of the form-sphere? Yes. Having been of the form-sphere, does it become of the formless-sphere? It should not be said thus…pe….

Rūpāvacaraṃ hutvā arūpāvacaraṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Pariyāpannaṃ hutvā apariyāpannaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Having been of the form-sphere, does it become of the formless-sphere? Yes. Having been mundane, does it become supramundane? It should not be said thus…pe….

376. Maṃsasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Dibbasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ maṃsasotaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is the divine ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the physical ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Maṃsasotaṃ dhammupatthaddhaṃ dibbasotaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Ekaṃyeva sotanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

376. Is the physical ear, when supported by the Dhamma, the divine ear? Yes. Is there only one ear? It should not be said thus…pe….

Ekaṃyeva [V 0.0214] sotanti? Āmantā. Nanu dve sotāni vuttāni bhagavatā – “maṃsasotaṃ, dibbasota”nti? Āmantā. Hañci dve sotāni vuttāni bhagavatā – maṃsasotaṃ, dibbasotaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “ekaññeva sota”nti.

Is there only one ear? Yes. But were not two ears spoken of by the Blessed One: ‘the physical ear and the divine ear’? Yes. If two ears were spoken of by the Blessed One—the physical ear and the divine ear—then it should certainly not be said, ‘There is only one ear.’

Dibbasotakathā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the discussion on the Divine Ear.

3. Tatiyavaggo

3. The Third Chapter

(29) 9. Yathākammūpagatañāṇakathā

(29) 9. Discussion on the Knowledge of the Passing Away and Rebirth of Beings According to Their Deeds

377. Yathākammūpagataṃ [T 0.0279][M 0.0193][P 0.0256] ñāṇaṃ yathākammūpagatañāṇaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) dibbacakkhunti? Āmantā. Yathākammūpagatañca manasi karoti, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

3. Is the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds the divine eye? Yes. Does one both attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds and see a form with the divine eye? It should not be said thus…pe….

Yathākammūpagatañca manasi karoti, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one both attend to the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds and see a form with the divine eye? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus…pe….

Yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhunti? Āmantā. “Ime vata bhonto sattā”ti ca manasi karoti, “kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “vacīduccaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “manoduccaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “ariyānaṃ upavādakā”ti ca manasi karoti, “micchādiṭṭhikā”ti ca manasi karoti, “micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā”ti ca manasi karoti, “te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā”ti ca manasi karoti, “ime vā pana bhonto sattā”ti ca manasi karoti, “kāyasucaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “vacīsucaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “manosucaritena samannāgatā”ti ca manasi karoti, “ariyānaṃ anupavādakā”ti ca manasi karoti, “sammādiṭṭhikā”ti ca manasi karoti, “sammādiṭṭhikammasammādānā”ti ca manasi karoti, “te kāyassa [P 0.0257] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ [T 0.0280] saggaṃ [V 0.0215] lokaṃ upapannā”ti ca manasi karoti, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds the divine eye? Yes. Does one both attend [thus]: 'Sirs, these beings are endowed with bodily misconduct,' and attend [thus]: 'endowed with verbal misconduct,' and attend [thus]: 'endowed with mental misconduct,' and attend [thus]: 'are revilers of the noble ones,' and attend [thus]: 'are of wrong view,' and attend [thus]: 'undertake actions based on wrong view,' and attend [thus]: 'they, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, the lower world, in hell'; and also attend [thus]: 'Sirs, these beings are endowed with good bodily conduct,' and attend [thus]: 'endowed with good verbal conduct,' and attend [thus]: 'endowed with good mental conduct,' and attend [thus]: 'are not revilers of the noble ones,' and attend [thus]: 'are of right view,' and attend [thus]: 'undertake actions based on right view,' and attend [thus]: 'they, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world,' and also see a form with the divine eye? It should not be said so... and so on.

“Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā”ti ca manasi karoti, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

And does one attend [thus]: 'They, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world,' and see a form with the divine eye? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts and two consciousnesses? It should not be said so... and so on.

378. Yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhunti? Āmantā. Atthi koci adibbacakkhuko dibbacakkhuṃ appaṭiladdho anadhigato asacchikato yathākammūpagataṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci adibbacakkhuko dibbacakkhuṃ [M 0.0194] appaṭiladdho anadhigato asacchikato yathākammūpagataṃ jānāti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhu”nti.

378. Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds the divine eye? Yes. Is there anyone without the divine eye, who has not obtained, not attained, not realized the divine eye, who knows how beings fare according to their deeds? Yes. If there is anyone without the divine eye, who has not obtained, not attained, not realized the divine eye, who knows how beings fare according to their deeds, then indeed it should not be said, 'The knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds is the divine eye.'

Yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhunti? Āmantā. Āyasmā sāriputto yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Hañci āyasmā sāriputto yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ jānāti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhu”nti.

Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds the divine eye? Yes. Does the Venerable Sāriputta know how beings fare according to their deeds? Yes. If the Venerable Sāriputta knows how beings fare according to their deeds, then indeed it should not be said, 'The knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds is the divine eye.'

Yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhunti? Āmantā. Āyasmā sāriputto yathākammūpagataṃ ñāṇaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Atthāyasmato sāriputtassa dibbacakkhunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their deeds the divine eye? Yes. Does the Venerable Sāriputta know how beings fare according to their deeds? Yes. Does the Venerable Sāriputta have the divine eye? It should not be said so... and so on.
