Should knowledge that has feeling as its object... perception as its object... lack of moral dread as its object not be called 'knowledge of others' minds'? Yes. Should it be called 'knowledge of the course of lack of moral dread'? That should not be said...

438. Na vattabbaṃ – “cetopariyāye ñāṇaṃ cittārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇa”nti? Āmantā. Nanu cetopariyāye ñāṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci cetopariyāye ñāṇaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “cetopariyāye [T 0.0341] ñāṇaṃ cittārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇa”nti.

438. Should it not be said: 'The knowledge of others' minds has only mind as its object, and not another object'? Yes. Is it not 'knowledge of others' minds'? Yes. If it is 'knowledge of others' minds,' then for that reason, good sir, it should be said: 'The knowledge of others' minds has only mind as its object, and not another object.'

Cittārammaṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Object of Mind is concluded.

5. Pañcamavaggo

5. The Fifth Chapter

(50) 8. Anāgatañāṇakathā

5. 50. Discourse on Knowledge of the Future

439. Anāgate ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ mūlato jānāti, hetuto jānāti, nidānato jānāti, sambhavato jānāti, pabhavato jānāti, samuṭṭhānato jānāti, āhārato jānāti[M 0.0236], ārammaṇato jānāti, paccayato jānāti, samudayato jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. Does one know the future from its root, from its cause, from its basis, from its coming-to-be, from its source, from its arising, from its nutriment, from its object, from its condition, or from its origination? It should not be said thus...

Anāgate ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ hetupaccayataṃ jānāti, ārammaṇapaccayataṃ jānāti, adhipatipaccayataṃ [V 0.0263] jānāti, anantarapaccayataṃ jānāti, samanantarapaccayataṃ jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

439. Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. Does one know, regarding the future, the state of being a cause-condition, the state of being an object-condition, the state of being a dominance-condition, the state of being a proximity-condition, or the state of being a contiguity-condition? It should not be said thus...

Anāgate ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Gotrabhuno puggalassa sotāpattimagge ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa sotāpattiphale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. For a person of the change-of-lineage, is there knowledge in the path of stream-entry? It should not be said thus... For a person practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, is there knowledge in the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be said thus...

Sakadāgāmi…pe… anāgāmi [P 0.0314]…pe… arahattasacchikiriyāya paṭipannassa puggalassa arahatte ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Regarding the once-returner... regarding the non-returner... for a person practicing for the realization of Arahantship, is there knowledge in Arahantship? It should not be said thus...

440. Na [T 0.0342] vattabbaṃ – “anāgate ñāṇaṃ atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pāṭaliputtassa kho, ānanda, tayo antarāyā bhavissanti – aggito vā udakato vā mithubhedā vā”ti mahāva. 286; dī. ni. 2.152; udā. 76! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi anāgate ñāṇaṃ atthīti.

Should it not be said, 'There is knowledge of the future'? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Ānanda, for Pāṭaliputta there will be three dangers: from fire, from water, or from internal dissension'? Is there not indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, there is knowledge of the future.

Anāgatañāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

440. The Discourse on Knowledge of the Future is concluded.

5. Pañcamavaggo

5. The Fifth Chapter

(51) 9. Paṭuppannakathā

51. Discourse on the Present

441. Paṭuppanne paccuppanne (sī. syā.) ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena taṃ ñāṇaṃ jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena ñāṇena taṃ ñāṇaṃ jānātīti? Āmantā. Tena ñāṇena taṃ ñāṇaṃ “ñāṇa”nti jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena ñāṇena taṃ ñāṇaṃ “ñāṇa”nti jānātīti? Āmantā. Taṃ ñāṇaṃ tassa ñāṇassa ārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

5. Is there knowledge in the present? Yes. With that knowledge, does one know that knowledge? It should not be said thus... With that knowledge, does one know that knowledge? Yes. With that knowledge, does one know that knowledge as 'knowledge'? It should not be said thus... With that knowledge, does one know that knowledge as 'knowledge'? Yes. Is that knowledge the object of that knowledge? It should not be said thus...

Taṃ [M 0.0237] ñāṇaṃ tassa ñāṇassa ārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Tena phassena taṃ phassaṃ phusati, tāya [V 0.0264] vedanāya taṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, tāya saññāya taṃ saññaṃ sañjānāti, tāya cetanāya taṃ cetanaṃ ceteti, tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ cinteti, tena vitakkena taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakketi, tena vicārena taṃ vicāraṃ vicāreti, tāya pītiyā taṃ pītiṃ piyāyati, tāya satiyā taṃ satiṃ sarati, tāya paññāya [T 0.0343] taṃ paññaṃ pajānāti, tena khaggena taṃ khaggaṃ chindati, tena pharasunā [P 0.0315] taṃ pharasuṃ tacchati, tāya kudhāriyā taṃ kudhāriṃ tacchati, tāya vāsiyā taṃ vāsiṃ tacchati, tāya sūciyā taṃ sūciṃ sibbeti, tena aṅgulaggena taṃ aṅgulaggaṃ parāmasati, tena nāsikaggena taṃ nāsikaggaṃ parāmasati, tena matthakena taṃ matthakaṃ parāmasati, tena gūthena taṃ gūthaṃ dhovati, tena muttena taṃ muttaṃ dhovati, tena kheḷena taṃ kheḷaṃ dhovati, tena pubbena taṃ pubbaṃ dhovati, tena lohitena taṃ lohitaṃ dhovatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe….

Is that knowledge the object of that knowledge? Yes. With that contact, does one touch that contact? With that feeling, does one feel that feeling? With that perception, does one perceive that perception? With that volition, does one intend that volition? With that mind, does one think that mind? With that thought, does one think that thought? With that examination, does one examine that examination? With that joy, does one delight in that joy? With that mindfulness, does one recollect that mindfulness? With that wisdom, does one understand that wisdom? With that sword, does one cut that sword? With that axe, does one chop that axe? With that hatchet, does one chop that hatchet? With that adze, does one carve that adze? With that needle, does one sew that needle? With that fingertip, does one touch that fingertip? With that nose-tip, does one touch that nose-tip? With that head, does one touch that head? With that excrement, does one wash that excrement? With that urine, does one wash that urine? With that saliva, does one wash that saliva? With that pus, does one wash that pus? With that blood, does one wash that blood? It should not be said thus… etc.

442. Na vattabbaṃ – “paṭuppanne ñāṇaṃ atthī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sabbasaṅkhāre aniccato diṭṭhe tampi ñāṇaṃ aniccato diṭṭhaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Hañci sabbasaṅkhāre aniccato diṭṭhe tampi ñāṇaṃ aniccato diṭṭhaṃ hoti, tena vata re vattabbe – “paṭuppanne ñāṇaṃ atthī”ti.

442. Should it not be said: ‘There is knowledge in the present’? Yes. When all conditioned things are seen as impermanent, is not that knowledge also seen as impermanent? Yes. If, when all conditioned things are seen as impermanent, that knowledge is also seen as impermanent, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘There is knowledge in the present’.

Paṭuppannañāṇakathā paccuppannakathā (sī.) niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Knowledge of the Present is concluded.

5. Pañcamavaggo

5. The Fifth Chapter

(52) 10. Phalañāṇakathā

(52) 10. Discourse on Knowledge of Fruition

443. Sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Sāvako phalassa kataṃ paññāpetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabba…pe….

443. Does a disciple have knowledge in the fruition? Yes. Does a disciple designate the function of the fruition? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Atthi sāvakassa phalaparopariyatti indriyaparopariyatti [T 0.0344] puggalaparopariyattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a disciple have knowledge in the fruition? Yes. Does a disciple have knowledge of the higher and lower grades of fruition, the higher and lower grades of faculties, and the higher and lower grades of individuals? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sāvakassa [M 0.0238][V 0.0265] phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Atthi sāvakassa khandhapaññatti āyatanapaññatti dhātupaññatti [P 0.0316] saccapaññatti indriyapaññatti puggalapaññattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a disciple have knowledge in the fruition? Yes. Does a disciple have the designation of aggregates, the designation of sense-bases, the designation of elements, the designation of truths, the designation of faculties, and the designation of individuals? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Sāvako jino satthā sammāsambuddho sabbaññū sabbadassāvī dhammassāmī dhammappaṭisaraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a disciple have knowledge in the fruition? Yes. Is the disciple a conqueror, a teacher, a Perfectly Enlightened One, all-knowing, all-seeing, a master of the Dhamma, a refuge in the Dhamma? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Sāvako anuppannassa maggassa uppādetā asañjātassa maggassa sañjanetā anakkhātassa maggassa akkhātā maggaññū maggavidū maggakovidoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a disciple have knowledge in the fruition? Yes. Is the disciple a producer of the unarisen path, a generator of the ungenerated path, a declarer of the undeclared path, a knower of the path, one who understands the path, one skilled in the path? It should not be said thus… etc.

444. Na vattabbaṃ – “sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthī”ti? Āmantā. Sāvako aññāṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi sāvakassa phale ñāṇaṃ atthīti…pe….

444. Should it not be said, ‘A disciple has knowledge in the fruition’? Yes, it should not be said. Is the disciple ignorant? It should not be said thus… etc. In that case, a disciple has knowledge in the fruition… etc.

Phalañāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Knowledge of Fruition is concluded.

Pañcamavaggo.

The Fifth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Vimuttiñāṇaṃ vimuttaṃ, sekhassa asekhaṃ ñāṇaṃ, viparīte ñāṇaṃ, aniyatassa niyāmagamanāya atthi ñāṇaṃ, sabbaṃ ñāṇaṃ paṭisambhidāti, sammutiñāṇaṃ, cetopariyāye ñāṇaṃ, anāgate ñāṇaṃ, paṭuppanne [T 0.0345] ñāṇaṃ, sāvakassa phale ñāṇanti.

Knowledge of liberation and the liberated; knowledge of the trainee and the non-trainee; contrary knowledge; knowledge for the unfixed to attain fixity; that all knowledge is analytical knowledge; conventional knowledge; knowledge of others’ minds; knowledge of the future; knowledge of the present; and a disciple’s knowledge in the fruition.

Mahāpaṇṇāsako.

The Great Fifty.

Tassāpi uddānaṃ –

The summary of that also:

Sattupaladdhiṃ, upaharato, balaṃ, gihissa arahā ca, vimuttipañcamanti.

Inquiry into a Being, Harming, Power, the Householder Arahant, and Liberation as the fifth.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(53) 1. Niyāmakathā

(53) 1. Discourse on Certainty

445. Niyāmo [M 0.0239][P 0.0317][V 0.0266] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyanaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

445. Is the noble path unconditioned? Yes. Is that noble path a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, the changeless, the deathless? It should not be said thus… etc.

Niyāmo asaṅkhato, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the noble path unconditioned, and Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… etc.

Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni dve leṇāni dve saraṇāni dve parāyanāni dve accutāni dve amatāni dve nibbānānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections, two shelters, two refuges, two final resorts, two changeless states, two deathless states, two Nibbānas? It should not be said thus… etc.

Dve nibbānānīti? Āmantā. Atthi dvinnaṃ nibbānānaṃ uccanīcatā hīnapaṇītatā ukkaṃsāvakaṃso sīmā vā bhedo vā rāji vā antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are there two Nibbānas? Yes. Is there between the two Nibbānas any highness or lowness, inferiority or excellence, superiority or inferiority, a limit, a division, a line of demarcation, or an interval? It should not be said thus… etc.

Niyāmo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Atthi keci niyāmaṃ okkamanti paṭilabhanti uppādenti samuppādenti uṭṭhāpenti samuṭṭhāpenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti janenti sañjanentīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci asaṅkhataṃ okkamanti paṭilabhanti uppādenti samuppādenti uṭṭhāpenti samuṭṭhāpenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti janenti [T 0.0346] sañjanentīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the noble path unconditioned? Yes. Are there any who enter the noble path, attain it, produce it, generate it, bring it forth, establish it, create it, manifest it, give rise to it, or originate it? Yes. Are there any who enter the unconditioned, attain it, produce it, generate it, bring it forth, establish it, create it, manifest it, give rise to it, or originate it? It should not be said thus… etc.

446. Niyāmo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Maggo asaṅkhatoti? Na [P 0.0318] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

446. Is the noble path unconditioned? Yes. Is the path unconditioned? It should not be said thus… etc.

Maggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Niyāmo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the path conditioned? Yes. Is the noble path conditioned? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sotāpattiniyāmo [V 0.0267] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the certainty of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sotāpattimaggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiniyāmo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the path of stream-entry conditioned? Yes. Is the certainty of stream-entry conditioned? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sakadāgāminiyāmo…pe… anāgāminiyāmo…pe… arahattaniyāmo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Arahattamaggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [M 0.0240] …pe… arahattamaggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Arahattaniyāmo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the certainty of the once-returner… etc… the certainty of the non-returner… etc… the certainty of Arahantship unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of Arahantship unconditioned? It should not be said thus… etc. Is the path of Arahantship conditioned? Yes. Is the certainty of Arahantship conditioned? It should not be said thus… etc.

Sotāpattiniyāmo asaṅkhato…pe… arahattaniyāmo asaṅkhato, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Pañca tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the certainty of stream-entry unconditioned... etc... is the certainty of Arahantship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there five unconditioned things? It should not be said thus... etc. Are there five unconditioned things? Yes. Are there five protections... etc... or an interval? It should not be said thus... etc.

Niyāmo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyāmo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… micchattaniyāmo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Sammattaniyāmo saṅkhatoti? Na [P 0.0319] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is certainty unconditioned? Yes. Is the certainty of wrongness unconditioned? It should not be said thus... etc. Is the certainty of wrongness conditioned? Yes. Is the certainty of rightness conditioned? It should not be said thus... etc.

447. Na vattabbaṃ – “niyāmo asaṅkhato”ti? Āmantā. Niyāme uppajja niruddhe aniyato hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Tena [T 0.0347] hi niyāmo asaṅkhatoti. Micchattaniyāme uppajja niruddhe aniyato hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi micchattaniyāmo asaṅkhatoti.

447. Should it not be said, 'Certainty is unconditioned'? Yes, it should not be said. When certainty arises and ceases, does it become uncertain? It should not be said thus... etc. Therefore, certainty is unconditioned. When the certainty of wrongness arises and ceases, does it become uncertain? It should not be said thus... etc. Therefore, the certainty of wrongness is unconditioned.

Niyāmakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Certainty is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(54) 2. Paṭiccasamuppādakathā

6. 2. Discourse on Dependent Origination

448. Paṭiccasamuppādo [V 0.0268] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyanaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhato, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni dve leṇāni dve saraṇāni dve parāyanāni dve accutāni dve amatāni dve nibbānānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve nibbānānīti? Āmantā. Atthi dvinnaṃ nibbānānaṃ uccanīcatā hīnapaṇītatā ukkaṃsāvakaṃso sīmā vā bhedo vā rāji vā antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Is it a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, the immutable, the deathless? It should not be said thus… Is dependent origination unconditioned, and Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections, two shelters, two refuges, two final resorts, two immutable states, two deathless states, two Nibbānas? It should not be said thus… Are there two Nibbānas? Yes. For the two Nibbānas, is there highness and lowness, inferiority and excellence, superiority and inferiority, a limit, a division, a boundary, or an interval? It should not be said thus…

449. Paṭiccasamuppādo [P 0.0320] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Avijjā asaṅkhatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… avijjā saṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Paṭiccasamuppādo saṅkhatoti[M 0.0241]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭiccasamuppādo [T 0.0348] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā asaṅkhatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā saṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Paṭiccasamuppādo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Paṭiccasamuppādo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Paṭiccasamuppādo saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Paṭiccasamuppādo [P 0.0321] saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

448. Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Is ignorance unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is ignorance conditioned? Yes. Is dependent origination conditioned? It should not be said thus… Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Are formations conditioned by ignorance unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Are formations conditioned by ignorance conditioned? Yes. Is dependent origination conditioned? It should not be said thus… Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Is consciousness conditioned by formations unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is consciousness conditioned by formations conditioned? Yes. Is dependent origination conditioned? It should not be said thus… Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Is name-and-form conditioned by consciousness unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is name-and-form conditioned by consciousness conditioned? Yes. Is dependent origination conditioned? It should not be said thus… Is dependent origination unconditioned? Yes. Is aging-and-death conditioned by birth unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is aging-and-death conditioned by birth conditioned? Yes. Is dependent origination conditioned? It should not be said thus…

450. Na vattabbaṃ – “paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhato”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “jātipaccayā, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ. Uppādā vā tathāgatānaṃ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṃ ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā idappaccayatā. Taṃ tathāgato abhisambujjhati [V 0.0269] abhisameti. Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttāniṃ karoti. ‘Passathā’ti cāha – jātipaccayā, bhikkhave, jarāmaraṇaṃ[T 0.0349]. Bhavapaccayā, bhikkhave, jāti…pe… avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā. Uppādā vā tathāgatānaṃ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṃ ṭhitāva sā dhātu…pe… ‘passathā’ti cāha – avijjāpaccayā, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā. Iti kho, bhikkhave, yā tatra tathatā avitathatā anaññathatā idappaccayatā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, paṭiccasamuppādo”ti saṃ. ni. 2.20. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhatoti.

449. Should it not be said: 'Dependent origination is unconditioned'? Yes, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'With birth as condition, bhikkhus, there is aging-and-death. Whether Tathāgatas arise or not, this element stands, this stability of the Dhamma, this fixed order of the Dhamma, this specific conditionality. The Tathāgata fully awakens to this and comprehends it. Having fully awakened to it and comprehended it, he announces, teaches, proclaims, establishes, reveals, explains, and clarifies it. And he says: "See, bhikkhus, with birth as condition, there is aging-and-death." With existence as condition, bhikkhus, there is birth… With ignorance as condition, bhikkhus, there are formations. Whether Tathāgatas arise or not, this element stands… And he says: "See, bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, there are formations." Thus, bhikkhus, that which is the actuality therein, the verity, the invariability, specific conditionality—this, bhikkhus, is called dependent origination.' Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, dependent origination is unconditioned.

451. Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti yā tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

450. In 'With ignorance as condition, there are formations,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or an interval? It should not be said thus…

Avijjāpaccayā [M 0.0242] saṅkhārāti yā tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti yā tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Tīṇi asaṅkhatānīti? Na [P 0.0322] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Tīṇi asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Tīṇi tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

451. In 'With ignorance as condition, there are formations,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned; in 'With formations as condition, there is consciousness,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned; and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there three unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there three unconditioned things? Yes. Are there three protections… or an interval? It should not be said thus…

Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārāti yā tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇanti yā tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā…pe… jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇanti yā [T 0.0350] tattha dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dvādasa asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasa asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dvādasa tāṇāni dvādasa leṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

In 'With ignorance as condition, there are formations,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned; in 'With formations as condition, there is consciousness,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned… in 'With birth as condition, there is aging-and-death,' is that stability of the Dhamma, that fixed order of the Dhamma therein unconditioned; and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there twelve unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there twelve unconditioned things? Yes. Are there twelve protections, twelve shelters… or an interval? It should not be said thus…

Paṭiccasamuppādakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Dependent Origination is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(55) 3. Saccakathā

3. Discourse on the Truths

452. Cattāri [V 0.0270] saccāni asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Cattāri tāṇāni cattāri leṇāni cattāri saraṇāni cattāri parāyanāni cattāri accutāni cattāri amatāni cattāri nibbānānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cattāri nibbānānīti? Āmantā. Atthi catunnaṃ nibbānānaṃ uccanīcatā hīnapaṇītatā ukkaṃsāvakaṃso sīmā vā bhedo vā rāji vā antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

452. Are the four truths unconditioned? Yes. Are there four shelters, four hiding places, four refuges, four final resorts, four immutable things, four deathless things, four Nibbānas? It should not be so said… Are there four Nibbānas? Yes. Is there any superiority or inferiority, baseness or excellence, pre-eminence or subordination, limit, difference, distinction, or interval among the four Nibbānas? It should not be so said…

Dukkhasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā[P 0.0323]. Dukkhaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dukkhasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassaupāyāsā asaṅkhatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Samudayo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā [T 0.0351] asaṅkhatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Maggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasaccaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the truth of suffering unconditioned? Yes. Is suffering unconditioned? It should not be so said… Is the truth of suffering unconditioned? Yes. Are bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair unconditioned? It should not be so said… Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Yes. Is the origin unconditioned? It should not be so said… Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Yes. Are craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence unconditioned? It should not be so said… Is the truth of the path unconditioned? Yes. Is the path unconditioned? It should not be so said… Is the truth of the path unconditioned? Yes. Are right view… right concentration unconditioned? It should not be so said…

Dukkhaṃ [M 0.0243] saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dukkhasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassaupāyāsā saṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Dukkhasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Samudayasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā saṅkhatāti? Āmantā[P 0.0324]. Samudayasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Maggasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Maggasaccaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is suffering conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of suffering conditioned? It should not be so said… Are bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of suffering conditioned? It should not be so said… Is the origin conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the origin conditioned? It should not be so said… Are craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the origin conditioned? It should not be so said… Is the path conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the path conditioned? It should not be so said… Is right view… right concentration conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the path conditioned? It should not be so said…

453. Nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Dukkhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, dukkhaṃ [V 0.0271] asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Samudayasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, samudayo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Maggasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, maggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

453. The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation unconditioned? Yes. The truth of suffering is unconditioned; is suffering unconditioned? It should not be so said… The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation unconditioned? Yes. The truth of the origin is unconditioned; is the origin unconditioned? It should not be so said… The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation unconditioned? Yes. The truth of the path is unconditioned; is the path unconditioned? It should not be so said…

Dukkhasaccaṃ [T 0.0352] asaṅkhataṃ, dukkhaṃ saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… samudayasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, samudayo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, maggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Nirodhasaccaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nirodho saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The truth of suffering is unconditioned; is suffering conditioned? Yes. The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation conditioned? It should not be so said… The truth of the origin is unconditioned; is the origin conditioned? Yes. The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation conditioned? It should not be so said… The truth of the path is unconditioned; is the path conditioned? Yes. The truth of cessation is unconditioned; is cessation conditioned? It should not be so said…

454. Na vattabbaṃ – “cattāri saccāni asaṅkhatānī”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0325]. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni! Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri tathāni avitathāni anaññathānī”ti saṃ. ni. 5.1090. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi cattāri saccāni asaṅkhatānīti.

454. Should it not be said, 'The four truths are unconditioned'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, these four are true, not untrue, not otherwise. What four? ‘This is suffering,’ monks, this is true, not untrue, not otherwise… ‘This is the origin of suffering’… ‘This is the cessation of suffering’… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,’ this is true, not untrue, not otherwise. Monks, these four are indeed true, not untrue, not otherwise.' Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, the four truths are unconditioned.

Saccakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Truths is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(56) 4. Āruppakathā

6. 56. Discussion on the Formless

455. Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [M 0.0244] asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ [T 0.0353] leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyanaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nibbānaṃ [V 0.0272] asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the sphere of infinite space unconditioned? Yes. Is it Nibbāna, a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, the immutable, the deathless? It should not be so said… Is the sphere of infinite space unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be so said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or is there an interval? It should not be so said…

Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhataṃ [P 0.0326] bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

455. Is the sphere of infinite space unconditioned? Yes. Is the sphere of infinite space existence, a destination, an abode of beings, transmigration, a source, a station of consciousness, the acquisition of an individual existence? Yes. Is the unconditioned existence, a destination, an abode of beings, transmigration, a source, a station of consciousness, the acquisition of an individual existence? It should not be so said…

Atthi ākāsānañcāyatanūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi asaṅkhatūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi asaṅkhatūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there kamma that leads to the sphere of infinite space? Yes. Is there kamma that leads to the unconditioned? It should not be so said… Are there beings who go to the sphere of infinite space? Yes. Are there beings who go to the unconditioned? It should not be so said…

Ākāsānañcāyatane sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhate sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ākāsānañcāyatane atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhate atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ catuvokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhataṃ catuvokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

In the sphere of infinite space, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and get reborn? Yes. In the unconditioned, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and get reborn? It should not be so said… In the sphere of infinite space, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In the unconditioned, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be so said… Is the sphere of infinite space a four-constituent existence? Yes. Is the unconditioned a four-constituent existence? It should not be so said…

456. Na [T 0.0354] vattabbaṃ – “cattāro āruppā asaṅkhatā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāro āruppā anejā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāro āruppā anejā vuttā bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe “cattāro āruppā asaṅkhatā”ti.

456. Should it not be said, 'The four formless attainments are unconditioned'? Yes. Were the four formless attainments not declared 'imperturbable' by the Blessed One? Yes. If the four formless attainments were declared 'imperturbable' by the Blessed One, then, sir, it should indeed be said, 'The four formless attainments are unconditioned'.

Āruppakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Formless is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(57) 5. Nirodhasamāpattikathā

57. 5. Discussion on the Attainment of Cessation

457. Nirodhasamāpatti [M 0.0245][P 0.0327][V 0.0273] asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyanaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirodhasamāpatti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

457. Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Yes. Is it a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, the immutable, the deathless? It should not be said so… Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said so… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or is there an intermediate space? It should not be said so…

Nirodhasamāpatti asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Atthi keci nirodhaṃ samāpajjanti paṭilabhanti uppādenti samuppādenti uṭṭhapenti samuṭṭhapenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti janenti sañjanentīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci asaṅkhataṃ samāpajjanti paṭilabhanti uppādenti samuppādenti uṭṭhapenti samuṭṭhapenti nibbattenti abhinibbattenti janenti sañjanentīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Yes. Are there any who enter upon cessation, obtain it, produce it, bring it about, raise it up, establish it, generate it, fully generate it, give it birth, or bring it forth? Yes. Are there any who enter upon the unconditioned, obtain it, produce it, bring it about, raise it up, establish it, generate it, fully generate it, give it birth, or bring it forth? It should not be said so…

458. Nirodhā vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyatīti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhatā vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ paññāyatīti[T 0.0355]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirodhaṃ samāpajjantassa paṭhamaṃ nirujjhati vacīsaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato cittasaṅkhāroti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhataṃ samāpajjantassa paṭhamaṃ nirujjhati vacīsaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato cittasaṅkhāroti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa paṭhamaṃ uppajjati cittasaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato vacīsaṅkhāroti? Āmantā[P 0.0328]. Asaṅkhatā vuṭṭhahantassa paṭhamaṃ uppajjati cittasaṅkhāro, tato kāyasaṅkhāro, tato vacīsaṅkhāroti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

458. Is emergence from cessation perceived as a cleansing? Yes. Is emergence from the unconditioned perceived as a cleansing? It should not be said so… For one entering the attainment of cessation, does the verbal formation cease first, then the bodily formation, and then the mental formation? Yes. For one entering the unconditioned, does the verbal formation cease first, then the bodily formation, and then the mental formation? It should not be said so… For one emerging from cessation, does the mental formation arise first, then the bodily formation, and then the verbal formation? Yes. For one emerging from the unconditioned, does the mental formation arise first, then the bodily formation, and then the verbal formation? It should not be said so…

Nirodhā vuṭṭhitaṃ tayo phassā phusanti – suññato phasso, animitto phasso, appaṇihito phassoti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhatā vuṭṭhitaṃ tayo phassā phusanti – suññato phasso, animitto phasso, appaṇihito phassoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who has emerged from cessation experience three kinds of contact: the contact of emptiness, the contact of the signless, and the contact of the undirected? Yes. Does one who has emerged from the unconditioned experience three kinds of contact: the contact of emptiness, the contact of the signless, and the contact of the undirected? It should not be said so…

Nirodhā vuṭṭhitassa vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāranti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhatā [V 0.0274] vuṭṭhitassa vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who has emerged from cessation, is the mind inclined towards seclusion, does it slope towards seclusion, does it converge on seclusion? Yes. For one who has emerged from the unconditioned, is the mind inclined towards seclusion, does it slope towards seclusion, does it converge on seclusion? It should not be said so…

459. Na [M 0.0246] vattabbaṃ – “nirodhasamāpatti asaṅkhatā”ti? Āmantā. Saṅkhatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi nirodhasamāpatti asaṅkhatāti.

459. Should it not be said, 'The attainment of cessation is unconditioned'? Yes. Is it conditioned? It should not be said so… In that case, the attainment of cessation is unconditioned.

Nirodhasamāpattikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Attainment of Cessation is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(58) 6. Ākāsakathā

58. 6. Discourse on Space

460. Ākāso [T 0.0356] asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyanaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ākāso asaṅkhato, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā[P 0.0329]. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

460. Is space unconditioned? Yes. Is it a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a final resort, the immutable, the deathless? It should not be said so… Is space unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said so… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or are there intervals? It should not be said so…

Ākāso asaṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Atthi keci anākāsaṃ ākāsaṃ karontīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci saṅkhataṃ asaṅkhataṃ karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi keci ākāsaṃ anākāsaṃ karontīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci asaṅkhataṃ saṅkhataṃ karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is space unconditioned? Yes. Are there some who make non-space into space? Yes. Are there some who make the conditioned unconditioned? It should not be said so… Are there some who make space into non-space? Yes. Are there some who make the unconditioned conditioned? It should not be said so…

Ākāse pakkhino gacchanti, candimasūriyā gacchanti, tārakarūpāni gacchanti, iddhiṃ vikubbanti, bāhuṃ cālenti, pāṇiṃ cālenti, leḍḍuṃ khipanti, laguḷaṃ khipanti, iddhiṃ sattiṃ (?) khipanti, usuṃ khipantīti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhate pakkhino gacchanti, candimasūriyā gacchanti, tārakarūpāni [V 0.0275] gacchanti, iddhiṃ vikubbanti, bāhuṃ cālenti, pāṇiṃ cālenti, leḍḍuṃ khipanti, laguḷaṃ khipanti, iddhiṃ khipanti, usuṃ khipantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do birds move in space, do the moon and sun move, do the hosts of stars move, do they perform psychic feats, do they move their arms, do they move their hands, do they throw clods, do they throw sticks, do they send forth psychic power, do they shoot arrows? Yes. Do birds move in the unconditioned, do the moon and sun move, do the hosts of stars move, do they perform psychic feats, do they move their arms, do they move their hands, do they throw clods, do they throw sticks, do they send forth psychic power, do they shoot arrows? It should not be said so…

461. Ākāsaṃ [T 0.0357] parivāretvā gharāni karonti koṭṭhāni karontīti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhataṃ parivāretvā gharāni karonti koṭṭhāni karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

461. Do they build houses and storerooms by enclosing space? Yes. Do they build houses and storerooms by enclosing the unconditioned? It should not be said so…

Udapāne [M 0.0247] khaññamāne anākāso ākāso hotīti? Āmantā. Saṅkhataṃ asaṅkhataṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When a well is being dug, does non-space become space? Yes. Does the conditioned become the unconditioned? It should not be said so…

Tucchaudapāne pūriyamāne, tucchakoṭṭhe pūriyamāne, tucchakumbhiyā pūriyamānāya ākāso antaradhāyatīti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhataṃ [P 0.0330] antaradhāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When an empty well is being filled, when an empty storeroom is being filled, when an empty pot is being filled, does space disappear? Yes. Does the unconditioned disappear? It should not be said so…

462. Na vattabbaṃ – “ākāso asaṅkhato”ti? Āmantā. Ākāso saṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi ākāso asaṅkhatoti.

462. Should it not be said, 'Space is unconditioned'? Yes. Is space conditioned? It should not be said so… Therefore, space is unconditioned.

Ākāsakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Space is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Section

(59) 7. Ākāso sanidassanotikathā

59. 7. Discourse on 'Is Space Visible?'

463. Ākāso sanidassanoti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ rūpadhātu nīlaṃ pītakaṃ lohitakaṃ odātaṃ cakkhuviññeyyaṃ cakkhusmiṃ paṭihaññati cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

463. Is space visible? Yes. Is it form, the form base, the form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by eye-consciousness, does it impinge on the eye, does it come into the range of the eye? It should not be said so…

Ākāso [V 0.0276] sanidassanoti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca ākāsañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0358] …pe….

Is space visible? Yes. Dependent on the eye and space, does eye-consciousness arise? It should not be said so…

Cakkhuñca paṭicca ākāsañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca ākāsañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva atthi (?) suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti ma. ni. 1.400; 3.421; saṃ. ni. 4.60 – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca [P 0.0331] paṭicca ākāsañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

Dependent on the eye and space, does eye-consciousness arise? Yes. Is there indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and space, eye-consciousness arises'? There is not. Is there indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises'? Yes, there is. If there is indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises,' then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'Dependent on the eye and space, eye-consciousness arises.'

464. Na vattabbaṃ – “ākāso sanidassano”ti? Āmantā. Nanu passati dvinnaṃ rukkhānaṃ antaraṃ, dvinnaṃ thambhānaṃ antaraṃ, tāḷacchiddaṃ vātapānacchiddanti? Āmantā[M 0.0248]. Hañci passati dvinnaṃ rukkhānaṃ antaraṃ, dvinnaṃ thambhānaṃ antaraṃ, tāḷacchiddaṃ vātapānacchiddaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “ākāso sanidassano”ti.

464. Should it not be said, 'Space is visible'? Yes. Does one not see the interval between two trees, the interval between two pillars, a keyhole, and a window opening? Yes. If one sees the interval between two trees, the interval between two pillars, a keyhole, and a window opening, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'Space is visible.'

Ākāso sanidassanotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on 'Space is Visible' is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(60) 8. Pathavīdhātu sanidassanātiādikathā

8. Discourse Beginning with 'Is the Earth Element Visible?'

465. Pathavīdhātu sanidassanāti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ rūpadhātu nīlaṃ pītakaṃ lohitakaṃ odātaṃ cakkhuviññeyyaṃ cakkhusmiṃ paṭihaññati cakkhussa [T 0.0359] āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

465. Is the earth element visible? Yes. Is it form, the form base, the form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by eye-consciousness, does it impinge on the eye, does it come into the range of the eye? It should not be said thus... and so on...

Pathavīdhātu sanidassanāti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca pathavīdhātuñca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the earth element visible? Yes. Dependent on the eye and the earth element, does eye-consciousness arise? It should not be said thus... and so on...

Cakkhuñca [V 0.0277] paṭicca pathavīdhātuñca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca pathavīdhātuñca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0332] “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca pathavīdhātuñca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

Dependent on the eye and the earth element, does eye-consciousness arise? Yes. Is there indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and the earth element, eye-consciousness arises'? There is not. Is there indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises'? Yes, there is. If there is indeed a Sutta passage that states, 'Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises,' then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'Dependent on the eye and the earth element, eye-consciousness arises.'

466. Na vattabbaṃ – “pathavīdhātu sanidassanā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu passati bhūmiṃ pāsāṇaṃ pabbatanti? Āmantā. Hañci passati passasi (sī. syā. ka.) evamuparipi bhūmiṃ pāsāṇaṃ pabbataṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “pathavīdhātu sanidassanā”ti…pe….

466. Should it not be said, 'The earth element is visible'? Yes. Does one not see the ground, stone, and a mountain? Yes. If one sees the ground, stone, and a mountain, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The earth element is visible.'... and so on...

Na vattabbaṃ – “āpodhātu sanidassanā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu passati udakanti? Āmantā. Hañci passati udakaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “āpodhātu sanidassanāti…pe….

Should it not be said, 'The water element is visible'? Yes. Does one not see water? Yes. If one sees water, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The water element is visible.'... and so on...

Na vattabbaṃ – tejodhātu sanidassanāti? Āmantā. Nanu passati aggiṃ jalantanti? Āmantā. Hañci passati aggiṃ jalantaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “tejodhātu sanidassanā”ti…pe….

Should it not be said, 'The fire element is visible'? Yes. Does one not see a burning fire? Yes. If one sees a burning fire, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The fire element is visible.'... and so on...

Na [M 0.0249] vattabbaṃ – “vāyodhātu [T 0.0360] sanidassanā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu passati vātena rukkhe sañcāliyamāneti? Āmantā. Hañci passati vātena rukkhe sañcāliyamāne, tena vata re vattabbe – “vāyodhātu sanidassanā”ti…pe….

Should it not be said, 'The air element is visible'? Yes. Does one not see trees being swayed by the wind? Yes. If one sees trees being swayed by the wind, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The air element is visible.'... and so on...

Pathavīdhātu sanidassanātiādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse Beginning with 'Is the Earth Element Visible?' is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(61) 9. Cakkhundriyaṃ sanidassanantiādikathā

(61) 9. The Discourse Beginning with 'Is the Eye Faculty Visible?'

467. Cakkhundriyaṃ [V 0.0278] sanidassananti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ rūpadhātu…pe… cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

467. Is the eye faculty visible? Yes. Is it form, the form base, the form element… and so on… does it come into the range of the eye? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Cakkhundriyaṃ sanidassananti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca cakkhundriyañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na [P 0.0333] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the eye faculty visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and the eye faculty? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Cakkhuñca paṭicca cakkhundriyañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca cakkhundriyañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca cakkhundriyañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and the eye faculty? Yes. Is there indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and the eye faculty'? There is not. Is there indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and forms'? Yes, there is. If there is indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and forms,' then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and the eye faculty.'

468. Na [T 0.0361] vattabbaṃ – “pañcindriyāni sanidassanānī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu passati cakkhuṃ sotaṃ ghānaṃ jivhaṃ kāyanti? Āmantā. Hañci passati cakkhuṃ sotaṃ ghānaṃ jivhaṃ kāyaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “pañcindriyāni sanidassanānī”ti…pe….

468. Should it not be said, 'The five faculties are visible'? Yes. Do you not see the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body? Yes. If you see the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'The five faculties are visible'… and so on.

Cakkhundriyaṃ sanidassanantiādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse Beginning with 'Is the Eye Faculty Visible?' is concluded.

6. Chaṭṭhavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter

(62) 10. Kāyakammaṃ sanidassanantikathā

(62) 10. The Discourse on 'Is Bodily Action Visible?'

469. Kāyakammaṃ sanidassananti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ rūpadhātu nīlaṃ pītakaṃ lohitakaṃ [V 0.0279] odātaṃ cakkhuviññeyyaṃ cakkhusmiṃ paṭihaññati cakkhussa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

469. Is bodily action visible? Yes. Is it form, the form base, the form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by eye-consciousness, does it impinge on the eye, does it come into the range of the eye? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Kāyakammaṃ [M 0.0250] sanidassananti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca kāyakammañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is bodily action visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and bodily action? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Cakkhuñca paṭicca kāyakammañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca kāyakammañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca [P 0.0334] paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca kāyakammañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on bodily action? Yes. Is there indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on bodily action'? No. Is there indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms'? Yes. If there is indeed a sutta passage that states, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms,' then it should certainly not be said, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on bodily action.'

470. Na [T 0.0362] vattabbaṃ – “kāyakammaṃ sanidassana”nti? Āmantā. Nanu passati abhikkamantaṃ paṭikkamantaṃ ālokentaṃ vilokentaṃ samiñjentaṃ pasārentanti? Āmantā. Hañci passati abhikkamantaṃ paṭikkamantaṃ ālokentaṃ vilokentaṃ samiñjentaṃ pasārentaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “kāyakammaṃ sanidassana”nti.

470. Should it not be said, 'Bodily action is visible'? Yes. Does one not see someone going forward, going backward, looking ahead, looking around, bending, and stretching? Yes. If one sees someone going forward, going backward, looking ahead, looking around, bending, and stretching, then it should indeed be said, 'Bodily action is visible.'

Kāyakammaṃ sanidassanantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on 'Bodily action is visible' is concluded.

Chaṭṭhavaggo.

The Sixth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Niyamo asaṅkhato, paṭiccasamuppādo asaṅkhato, cattāri saccāni asaṅkhatāni, cattāro āruppā asaṅkhatā, nirodhasamāpatti asaṅkhatā, ākāso asaṅkhato, ākāso sanidassano, cattāro mahābhūtā, pañcindriyāni, tatheva kāyakammanti.

Determination is unconditioned, dependent origination is unconditioned, the four truths are unconditioned, the four formless attainments are unconditioned, the attainment of cessation is unconditioned, space is unconditioned, space is visible, the four great elements, the five faculties, and likewise bodily action.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(63) 1. Saṅgahitakathā

(63) 1. The Discourse on what is Reckoned

471. Natthi [T 0.0363][P 0.0335][V 0.0280] keci dhammā kehici dhammehi saṅgahitāti saṅgahītāti (pī.)? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi gaṇanaṃ gacchanti uddesaṃ gacchanti pariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi gaṇanaṃ gacchanti [M 0.0251] uddesaṃ gacchanti pariyāpannā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi saṅgahitā”ti.

471. Are there no phenomena reckoned by any phenomena? Yes. But are there not some phenomena that are reckoned, enumerated, and included by other phenomena? Yes. If there are some phenomena that are reckoned, enumerated, and included by other phenomena, then indeed it should not be said that “there are no phenomena reckoned by any phenomena.”

Cakkhāyatanaṃ katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ katamaṃ khandhagaṇanaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) gacchatīti? Rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “cakkhāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhena saṅgahita”nti. Sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci kāyāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “kāyāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhena saṅgahita”nti.

Under which aggregate reckoning does the eye base fall? It falls under the form aggregate reckoning. If the eye base falls under the form aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said, “The eye base is reckoned by the form aggregate.” The ear base… the nose base… the tongue base… the body base—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the form aggregate reckoning. If the body base falls under the form aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said, “The body base is reckoned by the form aggregate.”

Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… saddāyatanaṃ…pe… gandhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ rūpakkhandhena saṅgahita”nti.

The form base… the sound base… the odor base… the taste base… the tangible base—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the form aggregate reckoning. If the tangible base falls under the form aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said that “the tangible base is reckoned by the form aggregate.”

Sukhā [T 0.0364] vedanā katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Vedanākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci sukhā vedanā vedanākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “sukhā vedanā vedanākkhandhena saṅgahitā”ti. Dukkhā vedanā…pe… adukkhamasukhā vedanā katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Vedanākkhandhagaṇanaṃ [P 0.0336] gacchatīti. Hañci adukkhamasukhā vedanā vedanākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “adukkhamasukhā vedanā vedanākkhandhena saṅgahitā”ti.

Pleasant feeling—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the feeling aggregate reckoning. If pleasant feeling falls under the feeling aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said that “pleasant feeling is reckoned by the feeling aggregate.” Painful feeling… neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the feeling aggregate reckoning. If neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling falls under the feeling aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said that “neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is reckoned by the feeling aggregate.”

Cakkhusamphassajā saññā katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Saññākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci cakkhusamphassajā saññā saññākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “cakkhusamphassajā saññā saññākkhandhena saṅgahitā”ti. Sotasamphassajā saññā…pe… manosamphassajā saññā katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Saññākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci manosamphassajā [V 0.0281] saññā saññākkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “manosamphassajā saññā saññākkhandhena saṅgahitā”ti.

Perception born of eye-contact—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the perception aggregate reckoning. If perception born of eye-contact falls under the perception aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said: “Perception born of eye-contact is reckoned by the perception aggregate.” Perception born of ear-contact… perception born of mind-contact—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the perception aggregate reckoning. If perception born of mind-contact falls under the perception aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said: “Perception born of mind-contact is reckoned by the perception aggregate.”

Cakkhusamphassajā cetanā…pe… manosamphassajā cetanā katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti? Saṅkhārakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci manosamphassajā cetanā saṅkhārakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “manosamphassajā cetanā saṅkhārakkhandhena saṅgahitā”ti.

Volition born of eye-contact… volition born of mind-contact—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the formations aggregate reckoning. If volition born of mind-contact falls under the formations aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said: “Volition born of mind-contact is reckoned by the formations aggregate.”

Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [M 0.0252]…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ katamakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti[T 0.0365]? Viññāṇakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchatīti. Hañci manoviññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandhagaṇanaṃ gacchati, tena vata re vattabbe – “manoviññāṇaṃ viññāṇakkhandhena saṅgahita”nti.

Eye-consciousness… mind-consciousness—under which aggregate reckoning does it fall? It falls under the consciousness aggregate reckoning. If mind-consciousness falls under the consciousness aggregate reckoning, then indeed it should be said, “Mind-consciousness is reckoned by the consciousness aggregate.”

472. Yathā dāmena vā yottena vā dve balibaddā saṅgahitā, sikkāya piṇḍapāto saṅgahito, sā gaddulena saṅgahito; evameva te dhammā tehi dhammehi saṅgahitāti sakavādivacanaṃ (aṭṭhakathā passitabbā)? Hañci dāmena vā yottena vā dve balībaddā saṅgahitā, sikkāya [P 0.0337] piṇḍapāto saṅgahito, sā gaddulena saṅgahito, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi saṅgahitā”ti sakavādivacanaṃ (aṭṭhakathā passitabbā).

472. Just as two oxen are held together by a rope or a yoke, alms-food is held by a carrying net, and a dog is held by a leash; in the same way, are those phenomena reckoned by those phenomena? If two oxen are held together by a rope or a yoke, alms-food is held by a carrying net, and a dog is held by a leash, then indeed it should be said—“there are some phenomena reckoned by some phenomena.”

Saṅgahitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on what is Reckoned is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(64) 2. Sampayuttakathā

(64) 2. Discourse on Association

473. Natthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi sampayuttāti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi sahagatā sahajātā saṃsaṭṭhā ekuppādā ekanirodhā ekavatthukā ekārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi sahagatā sahajātā saṃsaṭṭhā [V 0.0282] ekuppādā ekanirodhā ekavatthukā ekārammaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi keci dhammā kehici dhammehi sampayuttā”ti.

473. Are there no phenomena associated with any phenomena? Yes. But are there not phenomena that are conjoined, co-arisen, intermingled, having a single arising, a single cessation, a single basis, and a single object? Yes. If there are phenomena that are conjoined, co-arisen, intermingled, having a single arising, a single cessation, a single basis, and a single object, then surely it should not be said, “There are no phenomena associated with any phenomena.”

Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandhena sahajātoti? Āmantā. Hañci vedanākkhandho saññākkhandhena sahajāto, tena vata re vattabbe – “vedanākkhandho saññākkhandhena sampayutto”ti.

Is the aggregate of feeling co-arisen with the aggregate of perception? Yes. If the aggregate of feeling is co-arisen with the aggregate of perception, then indeed it should be said, “The aggregate of feeling is associated with the aggregate of perception.”

Vedanākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandhena… viññāṇakkhandhena sahajātoti? Āmantā. Hañci [T 0.0366] vedanākkhandho viññāṇakkhandhena sahajāto, tena vata re vattabbe – “vedanākkhandho viññāṇakkhandhena sampayutto”ti.

Is the aggregate of feeling co-arisen with the aggregate of formations… with the aggregate of consciousness? Yes. If the aggregate of feeling is co-arisen with the aggregate of consciousness, then indeed it should be said, “The aggregate of feeling is associated with the aggregate of consciousness.”

Saññākkhandho [M 0.0253]… saṅkhārakkhandho… viññāṇakkhandho vedanākhandhena… saññākkhandhena… saṅkhārakkhandhena sahajātoti? Āmantā. Hañci viññāṇakkhandho saṅkhārakkhandhena sahajāto[P 0.0338], tena vata re vattabbe – “viññāṇakkhandho saṅkhārakkhandhena sampayutto”ti.

Is the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of formations… the aggregate of consciousness co-arisen with the aggregate of feeling… the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of formations? Yes. If the aggregate of consciousness is co-arisen with the aggregate of formations, then indeed it should be said, “The aggregate of consciousness is associated with the aggregate of formations.”

474. Yathā tilamhi telaṃ anugataṃ anupaviṭṭhaṃ, ucchumhi raso anugato anupaviṭṭho; evameva te dhammā tehi dhammehi anugatā anupaviṭṭhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

474. Just as oil is inherent in and pervades sesame, and juice is inherent in and pervades sugarcane; in the same way, are those phenomena inherent in and pervading those phenomena? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sampayuttakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Association is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(65) 3. Cetasikakathā

(65) 3. Discourse on Mental Phenomena

475. Natthi cetasiko dhammoti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci dhammā cittena sahagatā sahajātā saṃsaṭṭhā sampayuttā ekuppādā ekanirodhā ekavatthukā ekārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci dhammā cittena sahagatā sahajātā saṃsaṭṭhā sampayuttā [T 0.0367] ekuppādā ekanirodhā ekavatthukā ekārammaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi cetasiko dhammo”ti.

475. Is there no mental phenomenon? Yes. But are there not certain phenomena that are conjoined with the mind, co-arisen, intermingled, associated, having a single arising, a single cessation, a single basis, and a single object? Yes. If there are certain phenomena that are conjoined with the mind, co-arisen, intermingled, associated, having a single arising, a single cessation, a single basis, and a single object, then surely it should not be said, “There is no mental phenomenon.”

Phasso [V 0.0283] cittena sahajātoti? Āmantā. Hañci phasso cittena sahajāto, tena vata re vattabbe – “phasso cetasiko”ti. Vedanā…pe… saññā… cetanā… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi… paññā… rāgo… doso… moho…pe… anottappaṃ cittena sahajātanti? Āmantā. Hañci anottappaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “anottappaṃ cetasika”nti.

Is contact co-arisen with the mind? Yes. If contact is co-arisen with the mind, then indeed it should be said, “Contact is a mental phenomenon.” Is feeling… perception… volition… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom… lust… hatred… delusion… lack of moral dread co-arisen with the mind? Yes. If lack of moral dread is co-arisen with the mind, then indeed it should be said, “Lack of moral dread is a mental phenomenon.”

476. Cittena sahajātāti katvā cetasikāti? Āmantā. Phassena sahajātāti [M 0.0254] katvā phassasikāti phassikāti (pī. aṭṭha.)? Āmantā. Cittena sahajātāti katvā cetasikāti? Āmantā[P 0.0339]. Vedanāya… saññāya… cetanāya… saddhāya… vīriyena… satiyā… samādhinā… paññāya… rāgena… dosena… mohena…pe… anottappena sahajātāti katvā anottappāsikāti anottappikāti (?)? Āmantā.

476. Are they called “mental phenomena” (cetasika) because they are co-arisen with the mind? Yes. Are they called “contact phenomena” (phassasika) because they are co-arisen with contact? Yes. Are they called “mental phenomena” (cetasika) because they are co-arisen with the mind? Yes. With feeling… perception… volition… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom… lust… hatred… delusion… lack of moral dread—are they called “lack-of-moral-dread phenomena” (anottappasika) because they are co-arisen with lack of moral dread? Yes.

477. Natthi cetasiko dhammoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

477. Is there no mental phenomenon? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Cittañhidaṃ cetasikā ca dhammā,

Anattato saṃviditassa honti;

Hīnappaṇītaṃ tadubhaye viditvā,

Sammaddaso vedi palokadhamma”nti.

“This mind and these mental phenomena are present for one who has understood them as not-self; having known both the inferior and the superior, the one who sees rightly understands the nature of decay.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi cetasiko dhammoti.

Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. Therefore, there is a mental phenomenon.

Natthi cetasiko dhammoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā [T 0.0368] – “idha, kevaṭṭa, bhikkhu parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ cittampi ādisati cetasikampi ādisati vitakkitampi ādisati vicāritampi ādisati – ‘evampi te mano, itthampi te mano, itipi te citta’”nti dī. ni. 1.485. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi cetasiko dhammoti.

Is there no mental phenomenon? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Here, Kevaṭṭa, a bhikkhu discerns the minds of other beings, of other persons; he discerns their mental phenomena, he discerns their initial thoughts, he discerns their sustained thoughts, [saying,] ‘Thus is your mind, so is your mind, in this way is your mind’”? Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. Therefore, there is a mental phenomenon.

Cetasikakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Mental Phenomena is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(66) 4. Dānakathā

(66) 4. Discourse on Giving

478. Cetasiko [V 0.0284] dhammo dānanti? Āmantā. Labbhā [P 0.0340] cetasiko dhammo paresaṃ dātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… labbhā cetasiko dhammo paresaṃ dātunti? Āmantā. Labbhā phasso paresaṃ dātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… labbhā vedanā…pe… saññā… cetanā… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi… paññā paresaṃ dātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

478. Is a mental phenomenon giving? Yes. Is it possible for a mental phenomenon to be given to others? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is it possible for a mental phenomenon to be given to others? Yes. Is it possible for contact to be given to others? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is it possible for feeling… perception… volition… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom to be given to others? It should not be said thus… and so on.

479. Na [M 0.0255] vattabbaṃ – cetasiko dhammo dānanti? Āmantā. Dānaṃ aniṭṭhaphalaṃ akantaphalaṃ amanuññaphalaṃ secanakaphalaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti? Āmantā. Hañci dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākaṃ[T 0.0369], tena vata re vattabbe – “cetasiko dhammo dāna”nti.

479. Should it not be said that 'a mental phenomenon is giving'? Yes, it should not be said. Does giving have an undesirable result, an unwished-for result, a disagreeable result, a result irrigated by defilements, an outcome of suffering, a painful ripening? It should not be said thus… and so on. But does giving not have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? Yes. If giving indeed has a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, and a pleasant ripening, then it should indeed be said: 'A mental phenomenon is giving.'

Dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, cīvaraṃ dānanti upari vuccamānāya paravādīpucchāya sadisā, aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā? Āmantā. Cīvaraṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, piṇḍapāto senāsanaṃ gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro dānanti? Āmantā. Gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro iṭṭhaphalo kantaphalo manuññaphalo asecanakaphalo sukhudrayo sukhavipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Giving was declared by the Blessed One to have a desirable result. Is a robe giving? Yes. Does a robe have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? It should not be said thus… and so on. Giving was declared by the Blessed One to have a desirable result. Are almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick giving? Yes. Do medicinal requisites for the sick have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? It should not be said thus… and so on.

480. Na vattabbaṃ – “cetasiko dhammo dāna”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

480. Should it not be said that 'a mental phenomenon is giving'? Yes, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Saddhā [P 0.0341] hiriyaṃ kusalañca dānaṃ,

Dhammā ete sappurisānuyātā;

Etañhi maggaṃ diviyaṃ vadanti,

Etena hi gacchati devaloka”nti a. ni. 8.32.

Faith, moral shame, and wholesome giving, these are phenomena followed by good persons; indeed, this they call the divine path, by this one goes to the world of the gods.

Attheva [V 0.0285] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi cetasiko dhammo dānanti.

Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, a mental phenomenon is giving.

Na vattabbaṃ – “cetasiko dhammo dāna”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcimāni, bhikkhave, dānāni mahādānāni aggaññāni rattaññāni vaṃsaññāni porāṇāni asaṅkiṇṇāni asaṅkiṇṇapubbāni, na saṅkiyanti na saṅkiyissanti, appaṭikuṭṭhāni samaṇehi [T 0.0370] brāhmaṇehi viññūhi! Katamāni pañca? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti. Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ abhayaṃ deti averaṃ deti abyābajjhaṃ abyāpajjhaṃ (syā. ka.) deti. Aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ abhayaṃ datvā averaṃ datvā abyābajjhaṃ datvā aparimāṇassa abhayassa averassa abyābajjhassa bhāgī hoti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave[M 0.0256], paṭhamaṃ dānaṃ mahādānaṃ aggaññaṃ rattaññaṃ vaṃsaññaṃ porāṇaṃ asaṅkiṇṇaṃ asaṅkiṇṇapubbaṃ, na saṅkiyati na saṅkiyissati, appaṭikuṭṭhaṃ samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi. Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako adinnādānaṃ pahāya…pe… kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya…pe… musāvādaṃ pahāya…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṃ pahāya surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti. Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ abhayaṃ deti averaṃ deti abyābajjhaṃ deti. Aparimāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ abhayaṃ datvā averaṃ datvā abyābajjhaṃ datvā aparimāṇassa abhayassa averassa abyābajjhassa bhāgī hoti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave[P 0.0342], pañcamaṃ dānaṃ mahādānaṃ aggaññaṃ rattaññaṃ vaṃsaññaṃ porāṇaṃ asaṅkiṇṇaṃ asaṅkiṇṇapubbaṃ, na saṅkiyati na saṅkiyissati, appaṭikuṭṭhaṃ samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhi. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca dānāni mahādānāni aggaññāni rattaññāni vaṃsaññāni porāṇāni asaṅkiṇṇāni asaṅkiṇṇapubbāni, na [T 0.0371] saṅkiyanti na saṅkiyissanti, appaṭikuṭṭhāni samaṇehi brāhmaṇehi viññūhī”ti a. ni. 8.39. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi cetasiko dhammo dānanti.

Should it not be said that 'a mental phenomenon is giving'? It should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Monks, there are these five gifts, great gifts—known as foremost, known as long-standing, known as traditional, ancient, unadulterated, unadulterated in the past, they are not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. What five? Here, monks, a noble disciple, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life. By abstaining from the destruction of life, monks, the noble disciple gives fearlessness, gives freedom from enmity, and gives freedom from affliction to limitless beings. Having given fearlessness, freedom from enmity, and freedom from affliction to limitless beings, he becomes a partaker in limitless fearlessness, freedom from enmity, and freedom from affliction. This, monks, is the first gift, a great gift, known as foremost, long-standing, traditional, ancient, unadulterated, unadulterated in the past, it is not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple, having abandoned taking what is not given… having abandoned sexual misconduct… having abandoned false speech… having abandoned intoxicants that are a basis for negligence, abstains from intoxicants that are a basis for negligence. By abstaining from intoxicants that are a basis for negligence, monks, the noble disciple gives fearlessness, gives freedom from enmity, and gives freedom from affliction to limitless beings. Having given fearlessness, freedom from enmity, and freedom from affliction to limitless beings, he becomes a partaker in limitless fearlessness, freedom from enmity, and freedom from affliction. This, monks, is the fifth gift, a great gift, known as foremost, long-standing, traditional, ancient, unadulterated, unadulterated in the past, it is not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. These, monks, are the five gifts, great gifts, known as foremost, long-standing, traditional, ancient, unadulterated, unadulterated in the past, they are not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins.” Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, a mental phenomenon is giving.

481. Na vattabbaṃ – “deyyadhammo dāna”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idhekacco annaṃ deti, pānaṃ deti, vatthaṃ deti, yānaṃ deti, mālaṃ deti, gandhaṃ deti, vilepanaṃ deti, seyyaṃ deti, āvasathaṃ deti, padīpeyyaṃ detī”ti saṃ. ni. 3.362-391 thokaṃ visadisaṃ! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi deyyadhammo dānanti.

481. Should it not be said that 'an object to be given is giving'? It should not be said. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Here a certain person gives food, gives drink, gives clothing, gives a vehicle, gives garlands, gives perfumes, gives ointments, gives a bed, gives a dwelling, gives a lamp”? Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, an object to be given is giving.

482. Deyyadhammo [V 0.0286] dānanti? Āmantā. Deyyadhammo iṭṭhaphalo kantaphalo manuññaphalo asecanakaphalo sukhudrayo sukhavipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, cīvaraṃ dānanti? Āmantā. Cīvaraṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ kantaphalaṃ manuññaphalaṃ asecanakaphalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhavipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dānaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, piṇḍapāto dānaṃ… senāsanaṃ dānaṃ… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro dānanti? Āmantā. Gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro iṭṭhaphalo kantaphalo manuññaphalo asecanakaphalo [M 0.0257] sukhudrayo sukhavipākoti? Na [P 0.0343] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “deyyadhammo dāna”nti.

482. Is an object to be given giving? Yes. Does an object to be given have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? It should not be said thus… Giving was declared by the Blessed One to have a desirable result. Is a robe giving? Yes. Does a robe have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? It should not be said thus… Giving was declared by the Blessed One to have a desirable result. Is almsfood giving?… Is lodging giving?… Are medicinal requisites for the sick giving? Yes. Do medicinal requisites for the sick have a desirable result, a wished-for result, an agreeable result, a result not irrigated by defilements, an outcome of happiness, a pleasant ripening? It should not be said thus… In that case, it should not be said that 'an object to be given is giving'.

Dānakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Giving is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(67) 5. Paribhogamayapuññakathā

5. Discussion on Merit Accomplished by Use

483. Paribhogamayaṃ [T 0.0372] puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Paribhogamayo phasso vaḍḍhati, vedanā vaḍḍhati, saññā vaḍḍhati, cetanā vaḍḍhati, cittaṃ vaḍḍhati, saddhā vaḍḍhati, vīriyaṃ vaḍḍhati, sati vaḍḍhati, samādhi vaḍḍhati, paññā vaḍḍhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

483. Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. Does contact accomplished by use increase, does feeling increase, does perception increase, does volition increase, does faith increase, does energy increase, does concentration increase, does wisdom increase? It should not be said thus... etc.

Paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Latā viya vaḍḍhati, māluvā viya vaḍḍhati, rukkho viya vaḍḍhati, tiṇaṃ viya vaḍḍhati, muñjapuñjo viya vaḍḍhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. Does it increase like a creeper, like a māluvā vine, like a tree, like grass, like a bundle of muñja grass? It should not be said thus... etc.

484. Paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Dāyako dānaṃ datvā na samannāharati, hoti puññanti? Āmantā. Anāvaṭṭentassa anāvaṭṭantassa (sī. pī. ka.), anāvajjhantassa (syā.) hoti… anābhogassa hoti… asamannāharantassa hoti… amanasikarontassa hoti… acetayantassa hoti… apatthayantassa hoti… appaṇidahantassa hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu āvaṭṭentassa hoti… ābhogassa [V 0.0287] hoti… samannāharantassa hoti… manasikarontassa hoti… cetayantassa hoti… patthayantassa hoti… paṇidahantassa hotīti? Āmantā.
