Hañci [P 0.0344] āvaṭṭentassa hoti… ābhogassa hoti… samannāharantassa hoti… manasikarontassa hoti… cetayantassa hoti… patthayantassa hoti… paṇidahantassa hoti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti.

484. Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. When a donor has given a gift and does not reflect on it, does merit arise? Yes. Does it arise for one who does not turn the mind to it... for one who does not attend to it... for one who does not reflect on it... for one who does not pay attention... for one who does not intend... for one who does not aspire... for one who does not resolve upon it? It should not be said thus... etc. But surely, does it not arise for one who turns the mind to it... for one who attends to it... for one who reflects on it... for one who pays attention... for one who intends... for one who aspires... for one who resolves upon it? Yes. If it arises for one who turns the mind to it... for one who attends to it... for one who reflects on it... for one who pays attention... for one who intends... for one who aspires... for one who resolves upon it, then indeed, friend, it should not be said: 'Merit accomplished by use increases.'

485. Paribhogamayaṃ [T 0.0373] puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Dāyako dānaṃ datvā kāmavitakkaṃ vitakketi, byāpādavitakkaṃ vitakketi, vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vitakketi[M 0.0258], hoti puññanti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ. Orimañca, bhikkhave, tīraṃ samuddassa pārimañca tīraṃ – idaṃ dutiyaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ. Yato ca, bhikkhave, verocano abbhudeti yattha ca atthameti – idaṃ tatiyaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ. Satañca, bhikkhave, dhammo asatañca dhammo – idaṃ catutthaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri suvidūravidūrānīti.

485. Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. When a donor has given a gift and thinks thoughts of sensual desire, thinks thoughts of ill will, thinks thoughts of harming—does merit arise? Yes. Is there a conjunction of two contacts…pe… a conjunction of two minds? It should not be said thus…pe… Is there a conjunction of two contacts…pe… a conjunction of two minds? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? It should not be said thus…pe… Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, these four are very, very far apart. What four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first that is very, very far apart. The near shore and the far shore of the ocean, monks—this is the second that is very, very far apart. Where the sun rises and where it sets, monks—this is the third that is very, very far apart. The Dhamma of the good and the Dhamma of the bad, monks—this is the fourth that is very, very far apart. These, monks, are the four that are very, very far apart.’

“Nabhañca dūre pathavī ca dūre,

Pāraṃ samuddassa tadāhu dūre;

Yato [P 0.0345] ca verocano abbhudeti,

Pabhaṅkaro yattha ca atthameti.

‘The sky is far, the earth is far; the far shore of the sea, they say, is far; and where the radiant one rises, and where the light-maker goes to its setting.

“Tato [T 0.0374] have dūrataraṃ vadanti,

Satañca dhammaṃ asatañca dhammaṃ;

Abyāyiko hoti sataṃ samāgamo,

Yāvampi tiṭṭheyya tatheva hoti.

‘Further than that, indeed, they say, is the Dhamma of the good and the Dhamma of the bad. The association with the good is steadfast; for however long it may last, it remains just so.

“Khippañhi [V 0.0288] veti khippaṃhaveti (bahūsu) asataṃ samāgamo;

Tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti a. ni. 4.47.

‘For the association with the bad quickly perishes; therefore, the Dhamma of the good is far from the unvirtuous.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘Wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face.’

486. Na vattabbaṃ – “paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

486. Should it not be said: ‘Merit accomplished by use increases’? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Ārāmaropā vanaropā, ye janā setukārakā;

Papañca udapānañca, ye dadanti upassayaṃ.

‘Those who plant parks and groves, people who build bridges; who provide watering places and wells, and who give lodging—

“Tesaṃ [M 0.0259] divā ca ratto ca, sadā puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati;

Dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā, te janā saggagāmino”ti saṃ. ni. 1.47.

‘For them, by day and by night, merit always increases; established in the Dhamma, endowed with virtue, those people are bound for heaven.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, merit accomplished by use increases.

Na vattabbaṃ – “paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārome, bhikkhave, puññābhisandā [P 0.0346] kusalābhisandā [T 0.0375] sukhassāhārā sovaggikā sukhavipākā saggasaṃvattanikā iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṃvattanti! Katame cattāro? Yassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cīvaraṃ paribhuñjamāno appamāṇaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati, appamāṇo tassa puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṃvattaniko iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṃvattati. Yassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhu piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjamāno…pe… senāsanaṃ paribhuñjamāno…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ paribhuñjamāno appamāṇaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati, appamāṇo tassa puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro sovaggiko sukhavipāko saggasaṃvattaniko iṭṭhāya kantāya manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā sovaggikā sukhavipākā saggasaṃvattanikā iṭṭhāya kantāya [V 0.0289] manāpāya hitāya sukhāya saṃvattantī”ti a. ni. 4.51. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti.

Should it not be said: ‘Merit accomplished by use increases’? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, which are sources of happiness, heavenly, resulting in happiness, leading to heaven, and which conduce to what is wished for, desired, agreeable, to welfare, and to happiness. What four? Monks, in a case where a monk, while using a robe, abides having attained immeasurable concentration of mind, for that donor the stream of merit is immeasurable, the stream of the wholesome is immeasurable, a source of happiness, heavenly, resulting in happiness, leading to heaven, and conducing to what is wished for, desired, agreeable, to welfare, and to happiness. Monks, in a case where a monk, while using almsfood…pe… while using a lodging…pe… while using medicinal requisites for the sick, abides having attained immeasurable concentration of mind, for that donor the stream of merit is immeasurable, the stream of the wholesome is immeasurable, a source of happiness, heavenly, resulting in happiness, leading to heaven, and conducing to what is wished for, desired, agreeable, to welfare, and to happiness. These, monks, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, which are sources of happiness, heavenly, resulting in happiness, leading to heaven, and which conduce to what is wished for, desired, agreeable, to welfare, and to happiness.’ Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, merit accomplished by use increases.

487. Paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Dāyako dānaṃ deti, paṭiggāhako paṭiggahetvā na paribhuñjati chaḍḍeti vissajjeti, hoti puññanti? Āmantā. Hañci dāyako dānaṃ deti, paṭiggāhako paṭiggahetvā na paribhuñjati chaḍḍeti vissajjeti, hoti [T 0.0376] puññaṃ; no ca vata re vattabbe – “paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti.

487. Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. A donor gives a gift; the recipient, having accepted it, does not use it, but discards it and releases it. Does merit arise? Yes. If a donor gives a gift, and the recipient, having accepted it, does not use it, but discards it and releases it, and merit arises, then indeed it should not be said: ‘Merit accomplished by use increases.’

Paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Dāyako dānaṃ deti, paṭiggāhake paṭiggahite rājāno vā haranti, corā vā haranti, aggi vā dahati, udakaṃ vā vahati, appiyā vā dāyādā haranti, hoti puññanti? Āmantā[M 0.0260]. Hañci dāyako dānaṃ deti, paṭiggāhake paṭiggahite rājāno vā haranti, corā vā haranti, aggi vā dahati, udakaṃ vā vahati, appiyā vā dāyādā haranti, hoti puññaṃ; no ca vata [P 0.0347] re vattabbe – “paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti.

Does merit accomplished by use increase? Yes. A donor gives a gift; then either kings take away the recipients and the donated items, or thieves take them away, or fire burns them, or water carries them away, or unloved heirs take them away. Does merit arise? Yes. If a donor gives a gift, and then either kings take away the recipients and the donated items, or thieves take them away, or fire burns them, or water carries them away, or unloved heirs take them away, and merit arises, then indeed it should not be said: ‘Merit accomplished by use increases.’

Paribhogamayapuññakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Merit Accomplished by Use is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(68) 6. Itodinnakathā

7. 6. The Discussion on What Is Given from Here

488. Ito dinnena tattha yāpentīti? Āmantā. Ito cīvaraṃ denti taṃ cīvaraṃ tattha paribhuñjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ito piṇḍapātaṃ denti, ito senāsanaṃ denti, ito gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ denti, ito khādanīyaṃ denti, ito bhojanīyaṃ denti, ito pānīyaṃ denti; taṃ pānīyaṃ tattha paribhuñjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do they subsist there by means of what is given from here? Yes. People give a robe from here; do they use that robe there? It should not be said thus…pe… People give almsfood from here, they give a dwelling from here, they give medicinal requisites which are a support for the sick from here, they give hard food from here, they give soft food from here, they give drink from here; do they use that drink there? It should not be said thus…pe…

Ito [V 0.0290] dinnena tattha yāpentīti? Āmantā. Añño aññassa [T 0.0377] kārako parakataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ añño karoti, añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do they subsist there by means of what is given from here? Yes. Is one the doer for another? Is happiness and suffering made by another? Does one person act, and another person experience the result? This should not be said... (etc.).

489. Na vattabbaṃ – “ito dinnena tattha yāpentī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu petā attano atthāya dānaṃ dentaṃ anumodenti, cittaṃ pasādenti, pītiṃ uppādenti, somanassaṃ paṭilabhantīti? Āmantā. Hañci petā attano atthāya dānaṃ dentaṃ anumodenti, cittaṃ pasādenti, pītiṃ uppādenti, somanassaṃ paṭilabhanti; tena vata re vattabbe – “ito dinnena tattha yāpentī”ti.

489. Should it not be said: 'They subsist there by means of what is given from here'? Yes. Do not the departed spirits, when a gift is being given for their own benefit, rejoice, clarify their minds, generate rapture, and obtain mental happiness? Yes. If the departed spirits, when a gift is being given for their own benefit, rejoice, clarify their minds, generate rapture, and obtain mental happiness, then for that reason, it should indeed be said: 'They subsist there by means of what is given from here.'

490. Na vattabbaṃ – “ito dinnena tattha yāpentī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

490. Should it not be said: 'They subsist there by means of what is given from here'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Unname udakaṃ vuṭṭhaṃ, yathāninnaṃ pavattati;

Evameva [P 0.0348] ito dinnaṃ, petānaṃ upakappati.

‘Just as water rained on high ground flows down to the low ground, even so does what is given from here accrue to the departed spirits.

“Yathā [M 0.0261] vārivahā pūrā, paripūrenti sāgaraṃ;

Evameva ito dinnaṃ, petānaṃ upakappati.

‘Just as the rivers, full of water, fill the ocean, even so does what is given from here accrue to the departed spirits.

“Na hi tattha kasī atthi, gorakkhettha na vijjati;

Vaṇijjā tādisī natthi, hiraññena kayākayaṃ kayakkayaṃ (sī. pī.);

Ito dinnena yāpenti, petā kālaṅkatā tahi”nti khu. pā. 7.6; pe. va. 19.

‘Indeed, there is no agriculture there, nor is cattle-herding found there. There is no such trade, nor any buying and selling with money. The departed who have passed away subsist there by means of what is given from here.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi ito dinnena tattha yāpentīti.

Is there not indeed such a discourse? Yes. If that is so, then they subsist there by means of what is given from here.

491. Na [T 0.0378] vattabbaṃ – “ito dinnena tattha yāpentī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcimāni, bhikkhave, ṭhānāni sampassantā mātāpitaro puttaṃ icchanti kule jāyamānaṃ! Katamāni pañca? Bhaṭo vā no bharissati, kiccaṃ vā no karissati, kulavaṃso ciraṃ ṭhassati, dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjissati, atha vā pana petānaṃ kālaṅkatānaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassati [V 0.0291] – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca ṭhānāni sampassantā mātāpitaro puttaṃ icchanti kule jāyamāna”nti.

491. Should it not be said: 'They subsist there by means of what is given from here'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, seeing these five reasons, parents desire a son to be born in the family. What five? “Having been nourished by us, he will nourish us in return; or he will do our duties for us; the family lineage will long endure; he will succeed to the inheritance; or else, when we have passed away, he will give a dedicatory offering on our behalf.” Monks, it is seeing these five reasons that parents desire a son to be born in the family.'

“Pañca ṭhānāni sampassaṃ, puttaṃ icchanti paṇḍitā;

Bhaṭo vā no bharissati, kiccaṃ vā no karissati.

‘Seeing five reasons, the wise desire a son: “Having been nourished by us, he will nourish us in return; or he will do our duties for us.

“Kulavaṃso ciraṃ tiṭṭhe, dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjati;

Atha [P 0.0349] vā pana petānaṃ, dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassati.

“The family lineage will long endure; he will succeed to the inheritance; or else, he will give a dedicatory offering on behalf of the departed.

“Ṭhānānetāni sampassaṃ, puttaṃ icchanti paṇḍitā;

Tasmā santo sappurisā, kataññū katavedino.

“Seeing these reasons, the wise desire a son. Therefore, good and true persons, being peaceful, are grateful and know what has been done for them.

“Bharanti mātāpitaro, pubbe katamanussaraṃ;

Karonti tesaṃ kiccāni, yathā taṃ pubbakārinaṃ.

“Remembering what was done for them before, they support their mother and father. They perform duties for them, as is fitting for those who were their first benefactors.

“Ovādakārī bhaṭaposī, kulavaṃsaṃ ahāpayaṃ;

Saddho sīlena sampanno, putto hoti pasaṃsiyo”ti a. ni. 5.31.

“A son who follows advice, who nourishes in return, who does not let the family lineage decline, who is faithful and endowed with virtue, is praiseworthy.”’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi ito dinnena tattha yāpentīti.

Is there not indeed such a discourse? Yes. If that is so, then they subsist there by means of what is given from here.

Ito dinnakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on What Is Given from Here is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(69) 7. Pathavī kammavipākotikathā

(69) 7. Discourse on the Earth as the Result of Kamma

492. Pathavī [T 0.0379][M 0.0262] kammavipākoti? Āmantā. Sukhavedaniyā dukkhavedaniyā adukkhamasukhavedaniyā, sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, adukkhamasukhāya [V 0.0292] vedanāya sampayuttā, phassena sampayuttā, vedanāya sampayuttā, saññāya sampayuttā, cetanāya sampayuttā, cittena sampayuttā, sārammaṇā; atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā āvajjanā (syā. kaṃ.) ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Na [P 0.0350] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyā na dukkhavedaniyā na adukkhamasukhavedaniyā, na sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, na dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, na adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā, na phassena sampayuttā, na vedanāya sampayuttā, na saññāya sampayuttā, na cetanāya sampayuttā, na cittena sampayuttā, anārammaṇā; natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci na sukhavedaniyā na dukkhavedaniyā…pe… anārammaṇā; natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pathavī kammavipāko”ti.

492. Is the earth the result of kamma? Yes. Is it to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, or associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? Is it associated with contact, with feeling, with perception, with volition, or with consciousness? Does it have an object? Does it possess turning towards, engagement, application, attention, volition, aspiration, or resolve? This should not be said… (etc.). Is it not the case that it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful, not to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it not the case that it is not associated with pleasant feeling, not associated with painful feeling, not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? Is it not the case that it is not associated with contact, not with feeling, not with perception, not with volition, not with consciousness? Is it not the case that it is without an object? Is it not the case that it has no turning towards, no engagement, no application, no attention, no volition, no aspiration, no resolve? Yes. If it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… (etc.)… is without an object; and has no turning towards… (etc.)… no resolve, then indeed it should not be said: ‘The earth is the result of kamma.’

Phasso kammavipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo dukkhavedaniyo adukkhamasukhavedaniyo sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto dukkhāya…pe… adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto phassena sampayutto vedanāya sampayutto [T 0.0380] saññāya sampayutto cetanāya sampayutto cittena sampayutto sārammaṇo; atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Pathavī kammavipāko, pathavī sukhavedaniyā dukkhavedaniyā adukkhamasukhavedaniyā sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā dukkhāya…pe… adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttā phassena sampayuttā vedanāya sampayuttā saññāya sampayuttā cetanāya sampayuttā cittena sampayuttā sārammaṇā; atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… pathavī kammavipāko, pathavī na sukhavedaniyā na dukkhavedaniyā…pe… anārammaṇā; natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Phasso kammavipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo na dukkhavedaniyo [M 0.0263] …pe… anārammaṇo; natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact the result of kamma? Is contact to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, with painful… (etc.)… with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? Is it associated with contact, with feeling, with perception, with volition, or with consciousness? Does it have an object? Does it possess turning towards… (etc.)… resolve? Yes. Is the earth the result of kamma? Is the earth to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, with painful… (etc.)… with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? Is it associated with contact, with feeling, with perception, with volition, or with consciousness? Does it have an object? Does it possess turning towards, engagement, application, attention, volition, aspiration, or resolve? This should not be said… (etc.). Is the earth the result of kamma? Is it not the case that the earth is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… (etc.)… is without an object; and has no turning towards… (etc.)… resolve? Yes. Is contact the result of kamma? Is it not the case that contact is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… (etc.)… is without an object; and has no turning towards… (etc.)… resolve? This should not be said… (etc.).

Pathavī kammavipākoti? Āmantā. Pathavī paggahaniggahupagā chedanabhedanupagāti? Āmantā[P 0.0351]. Kammavipāko paggahaniggahupago chedanabhedanupagoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the earth element the result of kamma? Yes. Is the earth element subject to being taken up and put down, and to being cut and broken? Yes. Is the result of kamma subject to being taken up and put down, and to being cut and broken? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Labbhā [V 0.0293] pathavī ketuṃ vikketuṃ āṭhapetuṃ ocinituṃ vicinitunti? Āmantā. Labbhā kammavipāko ketuṃ vikketuṃ āṭhapetuṃ ocinituṃ vicinitunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Can the earth element be bought, sold, arranged, gathered, or collected? Yes. Can the result of kamma be bought, sold, arranged, gathered, or collected? It should not be said thus… and so on…

493. Pathavī [T 0.0381] paresaṃ sādhāraṇāti? Āmantā. Kammavipāko paresaṃ sādhāraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

493. Is the earth element common to others? Yes. Is the result of kamma common to others? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Kammavipāko paresaṃ sādhāraṇoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is the result of kamma common to others? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Asādhāraṇamaññesaṃ, acoraharaṇo nidhi;

Kayirātha macco puññāni, sace sucaritaṃ care”ti khu. pā. 8.9 khuddakapāṭhe, thokaṃ visadisaṃ.

‘Not shared with others, a treasure that cannot be taken by thieves; a mortal should perform meritorious deeds, if he would practice good conduct.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kammavipāko paresaṃ sādhāraṇo”ti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The result of kamma is common to others.’

Pathavī kammavipākoti? Āmantā. Paṭhamaṃ pathavī saṇṭhāti, pacchā sattā uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Paṭhamaṃ vipāko uppajjati, pacchā vipākapaṭilābhāya kammaṃ karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the earth element the result of kamma? Yes. Does the earth element come to be first, and do beings arise afterwards? Yes. Does the result arise first, and do they perform kamma afterwards in order to obtain that result? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Pathavī sabbasattānaṃ kammavipākoti? Āmantā[P 0.0352]. Sabbe sattā pathaviṃ paribhuñjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbe sattā pathaviṃ paribhuñjantīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci pathaviṃ aparibhuñjitvā parinibbāyantīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci kammavipākaṃ akhepetvā parinibbāyantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the earth element the result of kamma for all beings? Yes. Do all beings make use of the earth element? It should not be said thus… and so on… Do all beings make use of the earth element? Yes. Are there some who attain final Nibbāna without having made use of the earth element? Yes. Are there some who attain final Nibbāna without having exhausted the result of kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Pathavī cakkavattisattassa kammavipākoti? Āmantā. Aññe sattā pathaviṃ paribhuñjantīti? Āmantā. Cakkavattisattassa kammavipākaṃ aññe sattā paribhuñjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkavattisattassa kammavipākaṃ aññe sattā paribhuñjantīti? Āmantā[T 0.0382]. Cakkavattisattassa phassaṃ vedanaṃ saññaṃ cetanaṃ [M 0.0264] cittaṃ saddhaṃ vīriyaṃ satiṃ samādhiṃ paññaṃ aññe sattā paribhuñjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the earth element the result of kamma for a wheel-turning being? Yes. Do other beings make use of the earth element? Yes. Do other beings make use of the result of kamma of a wheel-turning being? It should not be said thus… and so on… Do other beings make use of the result of kamma of a wheel-turning being? Yes. Do other beings make use of the contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom of a wheel-turning being? It should not be said thus… and so on…

494. Na [V 0.0294] vattabbaṃ – “pathavī kammavipāko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi issariyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ adhipaccasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi issariyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ adhipaccasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “pathavī kammavipāko”ti.

494. Should it not be said: ‘The earth element is the result of kamma’? Yes. Is it not the case that there is kamma that conduces to sovereignty and kamma that conduces to dominion? Yes. If there is kamma that conduces to sovereignty and kamma that conduces to dominion, then indeed, good sir, it should be said: ‘The earth element is the result of kamma.’

Pathavī kammavipākotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Earth Element as the Result of Kamma is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(70) 8. Jarāmaraṇaṃ vipākotikathā

7. 8. The Discourse on Whether Aging and Death is a Resultant

495. Jarāmaraṇaṃ [P 0.0353] vipākoti? Āmantā. Sukhavedaniyaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ, sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, phassena sampayuttaṃ, vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, saññāya sampayuttaṃ, cetanāya sampayuttaṃ, cittena sampayuttaṃ, sārammaṇaṃ; atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ; natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ; natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā [T 0.0383] …pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko”ti.

Is aging and death a resultant? Yes. Is it to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? Is it associated with contact, with feeling, with perception, with volition, or with consciousness? Does it have an object? For it, is there turning towards, engagement, application, attention, volition, aspiration, or resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not true that it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… and so on… without an object? For it, is there no turning towards… and so on… or resolve? Yes. If it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… and so on… without an object; and for it, there is no turning towards… and so on… or resolve, then, good sir, it should indeed not be said, ‘Aging and death is a resultant.’

Phasso vipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo dukkhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo; atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko, jarāmaraṇaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ; atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

495. Is contact a resultant? Is contact to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… and so on… with an object? For it, is there turning towards… and so on… or resolve? Yes. Is aging and death a resultant? Is aging and death to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… and so on… with an object? For it, is there turning towards… and so on… or resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko, jarāmaraṇaṃ na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ; natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Phasso vipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo [V 0.0295] na dukkhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo; natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is aging and death a resultant? Is aging and death not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… and so on… without an object? For it, is there no turning towards… and so on… or resolve? Yes. Is contact a resultant? Is contact not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… and so on… without an object? For it, is there no turning towards… and so on… or resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on…

496. Akusalānaṃ [M 0.0265] dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Na [P 0.0354] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the aging and death of unwholesome states the resultant of unwholesome states? Yes. Is the aging and death of wholesome states the resultant of wholesome states? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

496. Regarding the aging and death of wholesome states, should it not be said, ‘It is the resultant of wholesome states’? Yes. Regarding the aging and death of unwholesome states, should it not be said, ‘It is the resultant of unwholesome states’? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalānaṃ [T 0.0384] dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the aging and death of wholesome states the resultant of unwholesome states? Yes. Is the aging and death of unwholesome states the resultant of wholesome states? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Regarding the aging and death of unwholesome states, should it not be said, ‘It is the resultant of wholesome states’? Yes. Regarding the aging and death of wholesome states, should it not be said, ‘It is the resultant of unwholesome states’? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalānañca akusalānañca dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Kusalānañca akusalānañca dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the aging and death of both wholesome and unwholesome states the resultant of unwholesome states? Yes. Is the aging and death of both wholesome and unwholesome states the resultant of wholesome states? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalānañca akusalānañca dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Kusalānañca akusalānañca dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ vipāko”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Concerning the aging and death of both wholesome and unwholesome states, should it not be said, 'It is the resultant of wholesome states'? Yes. Concerning the aging and death of both wholesome and unwholesome states, should it not be said, 'It is the resultant of unwholesome states'? It should not be said thus... (etc.).

497. Na vattabbaṃ – “jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi dubbaṇṇasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ appāyukasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi dubbaṇṇasaṃvattaniyaṃ [V 0.0296] kammaṃ appāyukasaṃvattaniyaṃ [P 0.0355] kammaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko”ti.

497. Should it not be said, 'Aging and death is a resultant'? Yes. But is there not kamma that leads to an ugly appearance and kamma that leads to a short life? Yes. If there is kamma that leads to an ugly appearance and kamma that leads to a short life, then, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'Aging and death is a resultant.'

Jarāmaraṇaṃ vipākotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'Aging and Death is a Resultant' is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(71) 9. Ariyadhammavipākakathā

(71) 9. Discussion on the Resultant of the Noble Dhamma

498. Natthi [M 0.0266] ariyadhammavipākoti? Āmantā. Nanu mahapphalaṃ sāmaññaṃ mahapphalaṃ brahmaññanti? Āmantā. Hañci mahapphalaṃ sāmaññaṃ [T 0.0385] mahapphalaṃ brahmaññaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi ariyadhammavipāko”ti.

498. Is there no resultant of the Noble Dhamma? Yes. Is not recluseship of great fruit, is not the holy life of great fruit? Yes. If recluseship is of great fruit and the holy life is of great fruit, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is no resultant of the Noble Dhamma'.

Natthi ariyadhammavipākoti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi sotāpattiphalanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi sotāpattiphalaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi ariyadhammavipāko”ti. Nanu atthi sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… arahattaphalanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi arahattaphalaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi ariyadhammavipāko”ti.

Is there no resultant of the Noble Dhamma? Yes. But is there not the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If there is the fruit of stream-entry, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is no resultant of the Noble Dhamma'. Is there not the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... the fruit of arahantship? Yes. If there is the fruit of arahantship, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is no resultant of the Noble Dhamma'.

Sotāpattiphalaṃ na vipākoti? Āmantā. Dānaphalaṃ na vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpattiphalaṃ na vipākoti? Āmantā. Sīlaphalaṃ…pe… bhāvanāphalaṃ na vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of stream-entry not a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of giving not a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is the fruit of stream-entry not a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of virtue... is the fruit of development not a resultant? It should not be said thus...

Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… arahattaphalaṃ na vipākoti? Āmantā. Dānaphalaṃ [P 0.0356] na vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattaphalaṃ na vipākoti? Āmantā. Sīlaphalaṃ…pe… bhāvanāphalaṃ na vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dānaphalaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... the fruit of arahantship not a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of giving not a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is the fruit of arahantship not a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of virtue... is the fruit of development not a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is the fruit of giving a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry a resultant? It should not be said thus...

Dānaphalaṃ [V 0.0297] vipākoti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… arahattaphalaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaphalaṃ…pe… bhāvanāphalaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… bhāvanāphalaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ [T 0.0386] …pe… arahattaphalaṃ vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of giving a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... the fruit of arahantship a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is the fruit of virtue... is the fruit of development a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is the fruit of development a resultant? Yes. Is the fruit of once-returning... the fruit of non-returning... the fruit of arahantship a resultant? It should not be said thus...

499. Kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

499. Is wholesome kamma of the sense-sphere accompanied by a resultant? Yes. Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is wholesome kamma of the form-sphere... of the formless-sphere accompanied by a resultant? Yes. Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant? It should not be said thus...

Lokuttaraṃ [M 0.0267] kusalaṃ avipākanti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ avipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ avipākanti? Āmantā[P 0.0357]. Rūpāvacaraṃ…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ avipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is supramundane wholesome kamma without a resultant? Yes. Is wholesome kamma of the sense-sphere without a resultant? It should not be said thus... Is supramundane wholesome kamma without a resultant? Yes. Is wholesome kamma of the form-sphere... of the formless-sphere without a resultant? It should not be said thus...

500. Kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ ācayagāmīti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ ācayagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpāvacaraṃ…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ ācayagāmīti? Āmantā. Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ ācayagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

500. Is wholesome kamma of the sense-sphere accompanied by a resultant and leading to accumulation? Yes. Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant and leading to accumulation? It should not be said thus... Is wholesome kamma of the form-sphere... of the formless-sphere accompanied by a resultant and leading to accumulation? Yes. Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant and leading to accumulation? It should not be said thus...

Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ apacayagāmīti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ apacayagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ apacayagāmīti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacaraṃ…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ savipākaṃ apacayagāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant and leading to non-accumulation? Yes. Is wholesome kamma of the sense-sphere accompanied by a resultant and leading to non-accumulation? It should not be said thus... Is supramundane wholesome kamma accompanied by a resultant and leading to non-accumulation? Yes. Is wholesome kamma of the form-sphere... of the formless-sphere accompanied by a resultant and leading to non-accumulation? It should not be said thus...

Ariyadhammavipākakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Resultant of the Noble Dhamma is concluded.

7. Sattamavaggo

7. The Seventh Chapter

(72) 10. Vipāko vipākadhammadhammotikathā

(72) 10. Discussion on 'A Resultant is a Dhamma that is a Condition for a Resultant'

501. Vipāko [T 0.0387][V 0.0298] vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Tassa vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tassa vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Tassa tasseva natthi dukkhassa antakiriyā natthi vaṭṭupacchedo natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na [P 0.0358] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

501. Is a resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. Is its resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? It should not be said thus… Is its resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. For that very same resultant, is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus…

Vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Vipākoti vā vipākadhammadhammoti vā vipākadhammadhammoti vā vipākoti vā esese ekaṭṭhe same samabhāge tajjāteti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. Are 'a resultant' and 'a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant'—or 'a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant' and 'a resultant'—one in meaning, the same, of equal portion, and of the same origin? It should not be said thus…

Vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Vipāko ca vipākadhammadhammo ca vipākadhammadhammo ca vipāko ca sahagatā sahajātā saṃsaṭṭhā sampayuttā ekuppādā ekanirodhā ekavatthukā ekārammaṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. Are a resultant and a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant—or a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant and a resultant—associated, co-arisen, intermingled, conjoined, of single arising, of single cessation, of single basis, and of single object? It should not be said thus…

Vipāko [M 0.0268] vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Taññeva akusalaṃ so akusalassa vipāko, taññeva kusalaṃ so kusalassa vipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. Is that very unwholesome state the resultant of the unwholesome, and that very wholesome state the resultant of the wholesome? It should not be said thus…

Vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti? Āmantā. Yeneva cittena pāṇaṃ hanati teneva cittena niraye paccati, yeneva cittena dānaṃ deti teneva cittena sagge modatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a resultant a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant? Yes. Is it that with the very same mind one kills a living being, one is tormented in hell; and with the very same mind one gives a gift, one rejoices in heaven? It should not be said thus…

502. Na [T 0.0388] vattabbaṃ – “vipāko vipākadhammadhammo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vipākā cattāro [V 0.0299] khandhā arūpino aññamaññapaccayāti? Āmantā. Hañci vipākā cattāro khandhā arūpino aññamaññapaccayā, tena vata re vattabbe – “vipāko vipākadhammadhammo”ti.

502. Should it not be said: ‘A resultant is a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant dhamma’? Indeed, it should not be said. Are not the four formless aggregates, being resultants, conditions for one another? Yes. If the four formless aggregates, being resultants, are conditions for one another, then indeed it should be said: ‘A resultant is a dhamma that is a condition for a resultant dhamma’.

Vipāko vipākadhammadhammotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on ‘A Resultant is a Dhamma that is a Condition for a Resultant Dhamma’ is concluded.

Sattamavaggo.

The Seventh Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary is:

Saṅgaho[P 0.0359], sampayutto, cetasiko dhammo, cetasikaṃ dānaṃ, paribhogamayaṃ puññaṃ vaḍḍhati, ito dinnena tattha yāpenti, pathavī kammavipāko, jarāmaraṇaṃ vipāko, natthi ariyadhammavipāko, vipāko vipākadhammadhammoti.

Inclusion, Association, Mental Phenomena, Mental Giving, Merit Increases Through Enjoyment, Subsistence There on What is Given from Here, Earth as Kamma-Resultant, Aging and Death as Resultant, No Resultant of Noble Dhamma, and Resultant as a Dhamma that is a Resultant-Conditioned Phenomenon.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter.

(73) 1. Chagatikathā

1. Discussion on the Six Destinies

503. Cha [P 0.0360] gatiyoti? Āmantā. Nanu pañca gatiyo vuttā bhagavatā – nirayo, tiracchānayoni, pettivisayo, manussā, devāti ma. ni. 1.153? Āmantā. Hañci pañca gatiyo vuttā bhagavatā – nirayo, tiracchānayoni, pettivisayo, manussā, devā; no ca vata re vattabbe – “cha gatiyo”ti.

503. Are there six destinies? Yes. But have not five destinies been declared by the Blessed One—hell, the animal realm, the sphere of spirits, humans, and gods? Yes. If five destinies have been declared by the Blessed One—hell, the animal realm, the sphere of spirits, humans, and gods—then it should not indeed be said, “There are six destinies.”

Cha [M 0.0269] gatiyoti? Āmantā. Nanu kālakañcikā kālakañjikā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), kāḷakañjakā (pī.) surā petānaṃ samānavaṇṇā samānabhogā samānāhārā samānāyukā petehi saha [T 0.0389] āvāhavivāhaṃ gacchantīti? Āmantā. Hañci kālakañcikā asurā petānaṃ samānavaṇṇā samānabhogā samānāhārā samānāyukā petehi saha āvāhavivāhaṃ gacchanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cha gatiyo”ti.

Are there six destinies? Yes. But are not the Kālakañjikā asuras similar in appearance, enjoyment, food, and lifespan to the spirits, and do they not intermarry with the spirits? Yes. If the Kālakañjikā asuras are similar in appearance, enjoyment, food, and lifespan to the spirits and intermarry with the spirits, then it should not indeed be said, “There are six destinies.”

Cha gatiyoti? Āmantā. Nanu vepacittiparisā devānaṃ samānavaṇṇā samānabhogā samānāhārā samānāyukā devehi saha āvāhavivāhaṃ gacchantīti? Āmantā. Hañci vepacittiparisā [V 0.0300] devānaṃ samānavaṇṇā samānabhogā samānāhārā samānāyukā devehi saha āvāhavivāhaṃ gacchanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cha gatiyo”ti.

Are there six destinies? Yes. But are not Vepacitti’s retinue similar in appearance, enjoyment, food, and lifespan to the gods, and do they not intermarry with the gods? Yes. If Vepacitti’s retinue are similar in appearance, enjoyment, food, and lifespan to the gods and intermarry with the gods, then it should not indeed be said, “There are six destinies.”

Cha gatiyoti? Āmantā. Nanu vepacittiparisā pubbadevāti? Āmantā. Hañci vepacittiparisā pubbadevā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cha gatiyo”ti.

Are there six destinies? Yes. But are not Vepacitti’s retinue former gods? Yes. If Vepacitti’s retinue are former gods, then it should not indeed be said, “There are six destinies.”

504. Na vattabbaṃ – “cha gatiyo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0361] atthi asurakāyoti, āmantā. Hañci atthi asurakāyo, tena vata re vattabbe – “cha gatiyo”ti.

504. Should it not be said, “There are six destinies”? Indeed, it should not be said. But is there not the host of asuras? Yes. Since there is the host of asuras, therefore it should indeed be said, “There are six destinies.”

Chagatikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Six Destinies is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter.

(74) 2. Antarābhavakathā

2. Discussion on Intermediate Existence

505. Atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Kāmabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Rūpabhavoti[T 0.0390]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Arūpabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Kāmabhavassa ca rūpabhavassa ca antare atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Rūpabhavassa ca arūpabhavassa ca antare atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

505. Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is it the sensual existence? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is it the form existence? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is it the formless existence? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence between the sensual existence and the form existence? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence between the form existence and the formless existence? It should not be said thus…

Kāmabhavassa [M 0.0270] ca rūpabhavassa ca antare natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmabhavassa ca rūpabhavassa ca antare natthi antarābhavo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti. Rūpabhavassa ca arūpabhavassa ca antare natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā[P 0.0362]. Hañci [V 0.0301] rūpabhavassa ca arūpabhavassa ca antare natthi antarābhavo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti.

Is there no intermediate existence between the sensual existence and the form existence? Yes. If there is no intermediate existence between the sensual existence and the form existence, then it should not indeed be said, “There is an intermediate existence.” Is there no intermediate existence between the form existence and the formless existence? Yes. If there is no intermediate existence between the form existence and the formless existence, then it should not indeed be said, “There is an intermediate existence.”

506. Atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Pañcamī sā yoni, chaṭṭhamī sā gati, aṭṭhamī sā viññāṇaṭṭhiti, dasamo so sattāvāsoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Antarābhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi antarābhavūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… antarābhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… antarābhave [T 0.0391] atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… antarābhavo pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

506. Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is that the fifth place of generation, the sixth destiny, the eighth station of consciousness, the tenth abode of beings? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is intermediate existence an existence, a destiny, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a place of generation, a station of consciousness, or an acquisition of individual existence? It should not be said thus… Is there kamma leading to intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… Are there beings who go to intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… In intermediate existence, are beings born, do they grow old, die, pass away, and reappear? It should not be said thus… In intermediate existence, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… Is intermediate existence a five-constituent existence? It should not be said thus…

507. Atthi kāmabhavo, kāmabhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavo, antarābhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmabhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmabhavūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi [P 0.0363] antarābhavūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmabhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Antarābhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmabhave atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Antarābhave atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmabhavo pañcavokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Antarābhavo pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

507. There is a sensual existence; is the sensual existence an existence, a destiny, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a place of generation, a station of consciousness, and an acquisition of individual existence? Yes. There is an intermediate existence; is intermediate existence an existence, a destiny, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a place of generation, a station of consciousness, and an acquisition of individual existence? It should not be said thus… Is there kamma leading to the sensual existence? Yes. Is there kamma leading to intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… Are there beings who go to the sensual existence? Yes. Are there beings who go to intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… In the sensual existence, are beings born, do they grow old, die, pass away, and reappear? Yes. In intermediate existence, are beings born, do they grow old, die, pass away, and reappear? It should not be said thus… In the sensual existence, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In intermediate existence, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… Is the sensual existence a five-constituent existence? Yes. Is intermediate existence a five-constituent existence? It should not be said thus…

Atthi rūpabhavo, rūpabhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavo, antarābhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni [T 0.0392] viññāṇaṭṭhiti [M 0.0271] attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi rūpabhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi [V 0.0302] rūpabhavūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpabhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Antarābhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpabhave [P 0.0364] atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Antarābhave atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpabhavo pañcavokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Antarābhavo pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a fine-material existence? Yes. Is the fine-material existence an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence? Is the intermediate existence an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? It should not be said thus… Is there kamma that leads to the fine-material existence? Yes. Is there kamma that leads to the intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… Are there beings heading for the fine-material existence? Yes. Are there beings heading for the intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… In the fine-material existence, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and are they reborn? Yes. In the intermediate existence, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and are they reborn? It should not be said thus… In the fine-material existence, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In the intermediate existence, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… Is the fine-material existence a five-constituent existence? Yes. Is the intermediate existence a five-constituent existence? It should not be said thus…

Atthi arūpabhavo, arūpabhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavo, antarābhavo bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi arūpabhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi arūpabhavūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi antarābhavūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpabhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Antarābhave sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti [T 0.0393] upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpabhave atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Antarābhave atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpabhavo catuvokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Antarābhavo [P 0.0365] catuvokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there an immaterial existence? Yes. Is the immaterial existence an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence? Is the intermediate existence an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? It should not be said thus… Is there kamma that leads to the immaterial existence? Yes. Is there kamma that leads to the intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… Are there beings heading for the immaterial existence? Yes. Are there beings heading for the intermediate existence? It should not be said thus… In the immaterial existence, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and are they reborn? Yes. In the intermediate existence, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and are they reborn? It should not be said thus… In the immaterial existence, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In the intermediate existence, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… Is the immaterial existence a four-constituent existence? Yes. Is the intermediate existence a four-constituent existence? It should not be said thus…

508. Atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Sabbesaññeva sattānaṃ atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… sabbesaññeva sattānaṃ natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Hañci sabbesaññeva sattānaṃ natthi antarābhavo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti.

508. Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence for all beings whatsoever? It should not be said thus… Is there no intermediate existence for all beings whatsoever? Yes. If, indeed, there is no intermediate existence for all beings whatsoever, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'There is an intermediate existence.'

Atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Ānantariyassa puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ānantariyassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Hañci ānantariyassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti.

Is there an intermediate existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence for a person destined for an immediate result in the next life? It should not be said thus… Is there no intermediate existence for a person destined for an immediate result in the next life? Yes. If, indeed, a person destined for an immediate result in the next life has no intermediate existence, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'There is an intermediate existence.'

Na [M 0.0272][V 0.0303] ānantariyassa puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Ānantariyassa puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ānantariyassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Na ānantariyassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nirayūpagassa puggalassa…pe… asaññasattūpagassa puggalassa [T 0.0394] …pe… arūpūpagassa puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpūpagassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Hañci arūpūpagassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti.

Is there an intermediate existence for a person not destined for an immediate result in the next life? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence for a person destined for an immediate result in the next life? It should not be said thus… Is there no intermediate existence for a person destined for an immediate result in the next life? Yes. Is it not that there is no intermediate existence for a person not destined for an immediate result in the next life? It should not be said thus… Is there an intermediate existence for a person heading for hell… for a person heading for the existence of non-percipient beings… for a person heading for the immaterial existence? It should not be said thus… Is there no intermediate existence for a person heading for the immaterial existence? Yes. If, indeed, there is no intermediate existence for a person heading for the immaterial existence, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said, 'There is an intermediate existence.'

Na arūpūpagassa puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Arūpūpagassa [P 0.0366] puggalassa atthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpūpagassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Na arūpūpagassa puggalassa natthi antarābhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there an intermediate existence for a person not heading for the immaterial existence? Yes. Is there an intermediate existence for a person heading for the immaterial existence? It should not be said thus… Is there no intermediate existence for a person heading for the immaterial existence? Yes. Is it not that there is no intermediate existence for a person not heading for the immaterial existence? It should not be said thus…

509. Na vattabbaṃ atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Nanu antarāparinibbāyī puggalo atthīti? Āmantā. Hañci antarāparinibbāyī puggalo atthi, tena vata re no ca vata re (sī. ka.), no vata re (syā.) vattabbe – “atthi antarābhavo”ti.

509. Should it not be said, 'There is an intermediate existence'? Yes. Is there not a person who attains parinibbāna in the interval? Yes. If, indeed, there is a person who attains parinibbāna in the interval, then, good sir, it should certainly be said, 'There is an intermediate existence.'

Antarāparinibbāyī puggalo atthīti katvā atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Upahaccaparinibbāyī puggalo atthīti katvā atthi upahaccabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… antarāparinibbāyī puggalo atthīti katvā atthi antarābhavoti? Āmantā. Asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī puggalo…pe… sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī puggalo atthīti katvā atthi sasaṅkhārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is it that because there is a person who attains parinibbāna in the interval, there is an intermediate existence? Yes. Is it that because there is a person who attains parinibbāna upon landing, there is a 'landing' existence? It should not be said thus… Is it that because there is a person who attains parinibbāna in the interval, there is an intermediate existence? Yes. Is it that because there is a person who attains parinibbāna without exertion… because there is a person who attains parinibbāna with exertion, there is a 'with exertion' existence? It should not be said thus…

Antarābhavakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Intermediate Existence is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter

(75) 3. Kāmaguṇakathā

(75) 3. Discourse on the Strands of Sensual Pleasure

510. Pañceva [T 0.0395][V 0.0304] kāmaguṇā kāmadhātūti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi tappaṭisaññutto chandoti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi tappaṭisaññutto chando, no ca [M 0.0273] vata re vattabbe – “pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātū”ti. Nanu atthi tappaṭisaññutto rāgo tappaṭisaññutto chando tappaṭisaññutto chandarāgo [P 0.0367] tappaṭisaññutto saṅkappo tappaṭisaññutto rāgo tappaṭisaññutto saṅkapparāgo tappaṭisaññuttā pīti tappaṭisaññuttaṃ somanassaṃ tappaṭisaññuttaṃ pītisomanassanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi tappaṭisaññuttaṃ pītisomanassaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātū”ti.

510. Are only the five sensual qualities the sense-sphere element? Yes. But is there not desire connected therewith? Yes. If there is desire connected therewith, then, sir, it should not be said, 'Only the five sensual qualities are the sense-sphere element.' Is there not lust connected therewith, desire connected therewith, lustful desire connected therewith, resolve connected therewith, lust connected therewith, lustful resolve connected therewith, rapture connected therewith, joy connected therewith, and rapturous joy connected therewith? Yes. If there is rapturous joy connected therewith, then, sir, it should not be said, 'Only the five sensual qualities are the sense-sphere element.'

Pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātūti? Āmantā. Manussānaṃ cakkhu na kāmadhātūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manussānaṃ sotaṃ…pe… manussānaṃ ghānaṃ…pe… manussānaṃ jivhā…pe… manussānaṃ kāyo…pe… manussānaṃ mano na kāmadhātūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are only the five sensual qualities the sense-sphere element? Yes. Is the eye of humans not the sense-sphere element? It should not be said so... and so on... Is the ear of humans... and so on... the nose of humans... and so on... the tongue of humans... and so on... the body of humans... and so on... Is the mind of humans not the sense-sphere element? It should not be said so... and so on...

Manussānaṃ mano na kāmadhātūti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is the mind of humans not the sense-sphere element? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One—

“Pañca kāmaguṇā loke, manocchaṭṭhā paveditā;

Ettha chandaṃ virājetvā, evaṃ dukkhā pamuccatī”ti su. ni. 173; saṃ. ni. 1.30.

“Five sensual qualities in the world, with mind as the sixth, have been declared; having become dispassionate towards them, one is thus freed from suffering.”

Attheva [T 0.0396] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “manussānaṃ mano na kāmadhātū”ti.

Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'The mind of humans is not the sense-sphere element.'

511. Pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātūti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇā bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmaguṇūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmaguṇūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ [V 0.0305] vattabbe…pe… kāmaguṇe sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na [P 0.0368] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmaguṇe atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmaguṇā pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmaguṇe sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti, paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti, sāvakayugaṃ uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

511. Are only the five sensual qualities the sense-sphere element? Yes. Are the sensual qualities existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, or the acquisition of individuality? It should not be said so... and so on... Is there kamma leading to the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Are there beings destined for the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Do form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness exist in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Are the sensual qualities a five-aggregate existence? It should not be said so... and so on... Do Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas, Solitary Buddhas, and pairs of disciples arise in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on...

Kāmadhātu bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇā bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmadhātūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi kāmaguṇūpagaṃ kammanti[M 0.0274]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi kāmadhātūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi kāmaguṇūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the sense-sphere element existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, or the acquisition of individuality? Yes. Are the sensual qualities existence, a destination, an abode of beings, the round of rebirth, a womb, a station of consciousness, or the acquisition of individuality? It should not be said so... and so on... Is there kamma leading to the sense-sphere element? Yes. Is there kamma leading to the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Are there beings destined for the sense-sphere element? Yes. Are there beings destined for the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on...

Kāmadhātuyā sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇe sattā [T 0.0397] jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… kāmadhātuyā atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇe atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmadhātu pañcavokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇā pañcavokārabhavoti? Na [P 0.0369] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmadhātuyā sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti, paccekasabuddhā uppajjanti, sāvakayugaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Kāmaguṇe sammāsambuddhā uppajjanti, paccekasambuddhā uppajjanti, sāvakayugaṃ uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear in the sense-sphere element? Yes. Are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Do form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness exist in the sense-sphere element? Yes. Do form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness exist in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on... Is the sense-sphere element a five-aggregate existence? Yes. Are the sensual qualities a five-aggregate existence? It should not be said so... and so on... Do Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas, Solitary Buddhas, and pairs of disciples arise in the sense-sphere element? Yes. Do Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas, Solitary Buddhas, and pairs of disciples arise in the sensual qualities? It should not be said so... and so on...

512. Na vattabbaṃ – “pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātū”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā! Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā…pe… jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi pañceva kāmaguṇā kāmadhātūti.

512. Is it incorrect to say, 'Only the five sensual qualities are the sense-sphere element'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there are these five sensual qualities. Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing passion; sounds cognizable by the ear… and so on… smells cognizable by the nose… and so on… tastes cognizable by the tongue… and so on… tangible objects cognizable by the body—agreeable, pleasing, charming, endearing, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing passion. These, monks, are the five sensual qualities.' Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, only the five sensual qualities are the sense-sphere element.

Kāmaguṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Sensual Qualities is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter

(76) 4. Kāmakathā

(76) 4. Discussion on Sensual Pleasures.

513. Pañcevāyatanā [T 0.0398][V 0.0306] kāmāti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi tappaṭisaṃyutto chandoti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi tappaṭisaṃyutto chando, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcevāyatanā kāmā”ti. Nanu atthi tappaṭisaṃyutto rāgo tappaṭisaṃyutto chando tappaṭisaṃyutto chandarāgo tappaṭisaṃyutto saṅkappo tappaṭisaṃyutto rāgo tappaṭisaṃyutto saṅkapparāgo tappaṭisaṃyuttā pīti tappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ somanassaṃ tappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ pītisomanassanti? Āmantā[M 0.0275]. Hañci atthi tappaṭisaṃyuttaṃ pītisomanassaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcevāyatanā kāmā”ti.

513. Are only the five sense-bases sensual pleasures? Yes. Is there not desire connected with them? Yes. If there is desire connected with them, then, good sir, one should certainly not say—'Only the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures.' Is there not lust connected with them, desire connected with them, lustful desire connected with them, resolve connected with them, lust connected with them, lustful resolve connected with them, rapture connected with them, joy connected with them, and rapturous joy connected with them? Yes. If there is rapturous joy connected with them, then, good sir, one should certainly not say—'Only the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures.'

514. Na [P 0.0370] vattabbaṃ – “pañcevāyatanā kāmā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā! Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā…pe… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi pañcevāyatanā kāmāti.

514. Should it not be said that 'Only the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye... tangible objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a dear nature, connected with sensual desire, and alluring—these, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure'? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, only the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures.

Pañcevāyatanā kāmāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā! Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā…pe… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā[T 0.0399]. Api ca, bhikkhave, nete kāmā kāmaguṇā nāmete ariyassa vinaye vucca”nti –

Are only the five sense-bases sensual pleasures? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye... tangible objects cognizable by the body that are desirable, pleasing, delightful, of a dear nature, connected with sensual desire, and alluring—these, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. Furthermore, monks, these are not kāmā; they are called strands of sensual pleasure in the discipline of the noble one'—

“Saṅkapparāgo purisassa kāmo,

Na te kāmā yāni citrāni loke;

Saṅkapparāgo purisassa kāmo,

Tiṭṭhanti citrāni tatheva loke;

Athettha dhīrā vinayanti chanda”nti a. ni. 6.63 nibbedhikasutte.

'Lustful resolve is a person’s sensual pleasure; the varied things in the world are not sensual pleasures. Lustful resolve is a person’s sensual pleasure; the varied things remain just as they are in the world. Herein, the wise dispel the desire.'

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “pañcevāyatanā kāmā”ti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said that 'Only the five sense-bases are sensual pleasures.'

Kāmakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Sensual Pleasures is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter

(77) 5. Rūpadhātukathā

(77) 5. Discussion on the Form Element

515. Rūpino [V 0.0307] dhammā rūpadhātūti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ [P 0.0371] bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ [M 0.0276] vattabbe…pe… atthi rūpūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi rūpūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpe sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpe atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā [T 0.0400] viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

515. Are material phenomena the form element? Yes. Is form existence, a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, a station of consciousness, or an acquisition of individuality? One should not say so... Is there kamma that leads to form? One should not say so... Are there beings who go to form? One should not say so... In form, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? One should not say so... In form, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? One should not say so... Is form the five-constituent existence? One should not say so...

Rūpadhātu bhavo gati…pe… attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ bhavo gati…pe… attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi rūpadhātūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi rūpūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi rūpadhātūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi rūpūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the form element existence, a destination... an acquisition of individuality? Yes. Is form existence, a destination... an acquisition of individuality? One should not say so... Is there kamma that leads to the form element? Yes. Is there kamma that leads to form? One should not say so... Are there beings who go to the form element? Yes. Are there beings who go to form? One should not say so...

Rūpadhātuyā sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Rūpe sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpadhātuyā atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Rūpe atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpadhātu [P 0.0372] pañcavokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ pañcavokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

In the form element, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? Yes. In form, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? One should not say so... In the form element, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In form, is there form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? One should not say so... Is the form element the five-constituent existence? Yes. Is form the five-constituent existence? One should not say so...

516. Rūpino dhammā rūpadhātu, kāmadhātuyā atthi rūpanti? Āmantā. Sāva kāmadhātu, sā rūpadhātūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva kāmadhātu, sā rūpadhātūti? Āmantā. Kāmabhavena samannāgato puggalo dvīhi bhavehi samannāgato hoti – kāmabhavena ca rūpabhavena cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

516. Are material phenomena the form element, and is there form in the sense-sphere element? Yes. Is that very sense-sphere element the form element? One should not say so... Is that very sense-sphere element the form element? Yes. Then is a person endowed with sense-sphere existence endowed with two existences—with sense-sphere existence and with form existence? One should not say so.

Rūpadhātukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Form Element is concluded.

8. Aṭṭhamavaggo

8. The Eighth Chapter

(78) 6. Arūpadhātukathā

(78) 6. Discussion on the Formless Element

517. Arūpino [T 0.0401][V 0.0308] dhammā arūpadhātūti? Āmantā. Vedanā bhavo gati sattāvāso saṃsāro yoni viññāṇaṭṭhiti attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na [M 0.0277] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi vedanūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi vedanūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanāya sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanāya atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā catuvokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

8. Are immaterial phenomena the formless element? Yes. Is feeling existence, a destination, an abode of beings, saṃsāra, a womb, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individuality? It should not be said thus… Is there kamma that leads to feeling? It should not be said thus… Are there beings who go to feeling? It should not be said thus… In feeling, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? It should not be said thus… In feeling, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… Is feeling the four-constituent existence? It should not be said thus….

Arūpadhātu bhavo gati…pe… attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Āmantā. Vedanā [P 0.0373] bhavo gati…pe… attabhāvapaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi arūpadhātūpagaṃ kammanti? Āmantā. Atthi vedanūpagaṃ kammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi arūpadhātūpagā sattāti? Āmantā. Atthi vedanūpagā sattāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the formless element existence, a destination... an acquisition of individuality? Yes. Is feeling existence, a destination... an acquisition of individuality? One should not say so... Is there kamma that leads to the formless element? Yes. Is there kamma that leads to feeling? One should not say so... Are there beings who go to the formless element? Yes. Are there beings who go to feeling? One should not say so...

Arūpadhātuyā sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Āmantā. Vedanāya sattā jāyanti jīyanti mīyanti cavanti upapajjantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpadhātuyā atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Vedanāya atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Na [T 0.0402] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpadhātu catuvokārabhavoti? Āmantā. Vedanā catuvokārabhavoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

In the formless element, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? Yes. In feeling, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away, and reappear? One should not say so... In the formless element, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? Yes. In feeling, is there feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness? One should not say so... Is the formless element the four-constituent existence? Yes. Is feeling the four-constituent existence? One should not say so...

518. Arūpino dhammā arūpadhātu, kāmadhātuyā atthi vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā. Sāva kāmadhātu, sā arūpadhātūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva kāmadhātu, sā arūpadhātūti? Āmantā. Kāmabhavena samannāgato puggalo dvīhi bhavehi samannāgato hoti – kāmabhavena ca arūpabhavena cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are immaterial phenomena the formless element, and in the sense-sphere element, are there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness? Yes. Is that very sense-sphere element the formless element? It should not be said thus… Is that very sense-sphere element the formless element? Yes. Is a person endowed with sense-sphere existence endowed with two existences—with sense-sphere existence and with formless existence? It should not be said thus….

Rūpino dhammā rūpadhātu, arūpino dhammā arūpadhātu, kāmadhātuyā atthi rūpaṃ vedanā saññā [V 0.0309] saṅkhārā viññāṇanti? Āmantā[P 0.0374]. Sāva kāmadhātu, sā rūpadhātu, sā arūpadhātūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva kāmadhātu, sā rūpadhātu, sā arūpadhātūti? Āmantā. Kāmabhavena samannāgato puggalo tīhi bhavehi samannāgato hoti – kāmabhavena ca rūpabhavena ca arūpabhavena cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are material phenomena the form element and immaterial phenomena the formless element, and in the sense-sphere element, is there form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness? Yes. Is that very sense-sphere element the form element and the formless element? It should not be said thus… Is that very sense-sphere element the form element and the formless element? Yes.
