559. Atītārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu atītārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītārammaṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītārammaṇaṃ [M 0.0302] cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti. Atītārammaṇaṃ [P 0.0411] cittaṃ anārammaṇanti micchā. Hañci vā pana anārammaṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītārammaṇa”nti. Anārammaṇaṃ atītārammaṇanti micchā.

9. Is a mind with a past object without an object? Yes. But is it not with a past object? Yes. If it is with a past object, then it should not be said, 'a mind with a past object is without an object.' To say that a mind with a past object is without an object is wrong. But if it is without an object, then it should not be said that it is 'with a past object.' To say that what is without an object is with a past object is wrong.

Atītārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti.

Is a mind with a past object without an object? Yes. But is there not, with regard to the past, advertence... and aspiration? Yes. If there is, with regard to the past, advertence... and aspiration, then it should not be said that 'a mind with a past object is without an object.'

560. Anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgatārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgatārammaṇaṃ, no [T 0.0441] ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti. Anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti micchā. Hañci vā pana anārammaṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgatārammaṇa”nti. Anārammaṇaṃ anāgatārammaṇanti micchā.

559. Is a mind with a future object without an object? Yes. But is it not with a future object? Yes. If it is with a future object, then it should not be said, 'A mind with a future object is without an object.' To say that a mind with a future object is without an object is wrong. But if it is without an object, then it should not be said that it is 'with a future object.' To say that what is without an object is with a future object is wrong.

Anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti.

Is a mind with a future object without an object? Yes. But is there not, with regard to the future, advertence... and aspiration? Yes. If there is, with regard to the future, advertence... and aspiration, then it should not be said that 'a mind with a future object is without an object.'

Paccuppannaṃ [V 0.0336] ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, paccuppannārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ sārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ [P 0.0412] ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, atītārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ sārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, paccuppannārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ sārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Anāgataṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ sārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

560. Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the present, is a mind with a present object with an object? Yes. Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the past, is a mind with a past object with an object? It should not be said thus... Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the present, is a mind with a present object with an object? Yes. Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the future, is a mind with a future object with an object? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, atītārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, paccuppannārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the past, is a mind with a past object without an object? Yes. Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the present, is a mind with a present object without an object? It should not be said thus...

Anāgataṃ [T 0.0442] ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, anāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Paccuppannaṃ ārabbha atthi āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, paccuppannārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the future, is a mind with a future object without an object? Yes. Since there is advertence... and aspiration with regard to the present, is a mind with a present object without an object? It should not be said thus...

561. Na [M 0.0303] vattabbaṃ – “atītānāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti? Āmantā. Nanu atītānāgataṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Hañci atītānāgataṃ natthi, tena vata re vattabbe – “atītānāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ anārammaṇa”nti…pe….

561. Should it not be said: 'A mind with a past or future object is without an object'? Yes. Is it not so that the past and future do not exist? Yes. If the past and future do not exist, then it should indeed be said: 'A mind with a past or future object is without an object'… and so on.

Atītānāgatārammaṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Past and Future Objects is concluded.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

(90) 7. Vitakkānupatitakathā

(90) 7. Discourse on Being Subject to Applied Thought

562. Sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatitanti? Āmantā. Sabbaṃ cittaṃ vicārānupatitaṃ pītānupatitaṃ sukhānupatitaṃ dukkhānupatitaṃ somanassānupatitaṃ domanassānupatitaṃ [P 0.0413] upekkhānupatitaṃ [V 0.0337] saddhānupatitaṃ vīriyānupatitaṃ satānupatitaṃ samādhānupatitaṃ paññānupatitaṃ rāgānupatitaṃ dosānupatitaṃ…pe… anottappānupatitanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

562. Is all consciousness subject to applied thought? Yes. Is all consciousness subject to sustained thought, subject to rapture, subject to happiness, subject to suffering, subject to gladness, subject to sadness, subject to equanimity, subject to faith, subject to energy, subject to mindfulness, subject to concentration, subject to wisdom, subject to lust, subject to hatred… and so on… subject to lack of moral shame? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatitanti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi avitakko vicāramatto samādhīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi avitakko vicāramatto samādhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatita”nti[T 0.0443].

Is all consciousness subject to applied thought? Yes. But is there not a concentration that is without applied thought and with only sustained thought? Yes. If there is a concentration that is without applied thought and with only sustained thought, then it should not be said that 'all consciousness is subject to applied thought.'

Sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatitanti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi avitakko avicāro samādhīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi avitakko avicāro samādhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatita”nti. Sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatitanti? Āmantā. Nanu tayo samādhī vuttā bhagavatā – savitakko savicāro samādhi, avitakko vicāramatto samādhi, avitakko avicāro samādhīti dī. ni. 3.305, 353? Āmantā. Hañci tayo samādhī vuttā bhagavatā – savitakko savicāro samādhi, avitakko vicāramatto samādhi, avitakko avicāro samādhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatita”nti.

Is all consciousness subject to applied thought? Yes. But is there not a concentration that is without applied thought and without sustained thought? Yes. If there is a concentration that is without applied thought and without sustained thought, then it should not be said that 'all consciousness is subject to applied thought.' Is all consciousness subject to applied thought? Yes. But were not three kinds of concentration spoken of by the Blessed One: concentration with applied thought and with sustained thought; concentration without applied thought and with only sustained thought; and concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought? Yes. If three kinds of concentration were spoken of by the Blessed One—concentration with applied thought and with sustained thought; concentration without applied thought and with only sustained thought; and concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought—then it should not be said that 'all consciousness is subject to applied thought.'

Vitakkānupatitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Being Subject to Applied Thought is concluded.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

(91) 8. Vitakkavipphārasaddakathā

(91) 8. Discourse on Sound as the Diffusion of Applied Thought

563. Sabbaso [M 0.0304] vitakkayato vicārayato vitakkavipphāro saddoti? Āmantā. Sabbaso phusayato phassavipphāro saddo, sabbaso vedayato [P 0.0414] vedanāvipphāro saddo, sabbaso sañjānato saññāvipphāro saddo, sabbaso cetayato cetanāvipphāro saddo, sabbaso cintayato cittavipphāro [V 0.0338] saddo, sabbaso sarato sativipphāro saddo, sabbaso pajānato [T 0.0444] paññāvipphāro saddoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

563. For one who is in every way applying thought and sustaining thought, is the diffusion of applied thought sound? Yes. For one who is in every way in contact, is the diffusion of contact sound? For one who is in every way feeling, is the diffusion of feeling sound? For one who is in every way perceiving, is the diffusion of perception sound? For one who is in every way forming volitions, is the diffusion of volition sound? For one who is in every way thinking, is the diffusion of consciousness sound? For one who is in every way mindful, is the diffusion of mindfulness sound? For one who is in every way discerning, is the diffusion of wisdom sound? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sabbaso vitakkayato vicārayato vitakkavipphāro saddoti? Āmantā. Vitakkavipphāro saddo sotaviññeyyo sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Nanu vitakkavipphāro saddo na sotaviññeyyo na sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati na sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchatīti? Āmantā. Hañci vitakkavipphāro saddo na sotaviññeyyo na sotasmiṃ paṭihaññati na sotassa āpāthaṃ āgacchati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaso vitakkayato vicārayato vitakkavipphāro saddo”ti.

For one who is in every way applying thought and sustaining thought, is the diffusion of applied thought sound? Yes. Is the sound that is the diffusion of applied thought cognizable by ear-consciousness, does it strike against the ear-base, does it come into the range of the ear-base? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is it not so that the sound that is the diffusion of applied thought is not cognizable by ear-consciousness, does not strike against the ear-base, and does not come into the range of the ear-base? Yes. If the sound that is the diffusion of applied thought is not cognizable by ear-consciousness, does not strike against the ear-base, and does not come into the range of the ear-base, then it should not be said that 'for one who is in every way applying thought and sustaining thought, the diffusion of applied thought is sound.'

Vitakkavipphārasaddakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Sound as the Diffusion of Applied Thought is concluded.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

(92) 9. Na yathācittassa vācātikathā

(92) 9. Discourse on 'Speech is Not in Accordance with Consciousness'

564. Na yathācittassa vācāti? Āmantā. Aphassakassa vācā avedanakassa vācā asaññakassa vācā acetanakassa vācā acittakassa vācāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphassakassa vācā savedanakassa vācā sasaññakassa vācā sacetanakassa vācā sacittakassa vācāti? Āmantā. Hañci saphassakassa vācā…pe… sacittakassa vācā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti.

564. Is speech not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is there speech for one without contact, for one without feeling, for one without perception, for one without volition, for one without consciousness? This should not be said… and so on. Is there not speech for one with contact, for one with feeling, for one with perception, for one with volition, for one with consciousness? Yes. If there is speech for one with contact… and so on… for one with consciousness, then it should not be said that 'speech is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na [M 0.0305][T 0.0445][P 0.0415] yathācittassa vācāti? Āmantā. Anāvaṭṭentassa anāvaṭṭantassa (pī.), anāvajjantassa (sī. syā. ka.) kathā. 484 passitabbaṃ vācā…pe… anābhogassa vācā…pe… appaṇidahantassa vācāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu āvaṭṭentassa vācā ābhogassa vācā…pe… paṇidahantassa vācāti? Āmantā. Hañci āvaṭṭentassa vācā ābhogassa vācā paṇidahantassa vācā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti.

Is speech not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is there speech for one who does not advert… and so on… for one who does not attend… and so on… for one who does not direct the mind? This should not be said… and so on. Is there not speech for one who adverts, for one who attends… and so on… for one who directs the mind? Yes. If there is speech for one who adverts, for one who attends, for one who directs the mind, then it should not be said that 'speech is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na [V 0.0339] yathācittassa vācāti? Āmantā. Nanu vācā cittasamuṭṭhānā cittena sahajātā cittena saha ekuppādāti? Āmantā. Hañci vācā cittasamuṭṭhānā cittena sahajātā cittena saha ekuppādā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti.

Is speech not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is not speech originated from consciousness, co-arisen with consciousness, and arising at the same moment as consciousness? Yes. If speech is originated from consciousness, co-arisen with consciousness, and arising at the same moment as consciousness, then it should not be said that 'speech is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na yathācittassa vācāti? Āmantā. Na bhaṇitukāmo bhaṇati, na kathetukāmo katheti, na ālapitukāmo ālapati, na voharitukāmo voharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu bhaṇitukāmo bhaṇati, kathetukāmo katheti, ālapitukāmo ālapati, voharitukāmo voharatīti? Āmantā. Hañci bhaṇitukāmo bhaṇati, kathetukāmo katheti, ālapitukāmo ālapati, voharitukāmo voharati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti.

Is speech not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Does one who does not wish to speak, speak? Does one who does not wish to converse, converse? Does one who does not wish to address, address? Does one who does not wish to express, express? This should not be said… and so on. Does not one who wishes to speak, speak? Does not one who wishes to converse, converse? Does not one who wishes to address, address? Does not one who wishes to express, express? Yes. If one who wishes to speak, speaks; one who wishes to converse, converses; one who wishes to address, addresses; one who wishes to express, expresses; then it should not be said that 'speech is not in accordance with consciousness'.

565. Na vattabbaṃ – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci “aññaṃ bhaṇissāmī”ti aññaṃ bhaṇati, “aññaṃ kathessāmī”ti aññaṃ katheti, “aññaṃ ālapissāmī”ti aññaṃ ālapati, “aññaṃ voharissāmī”ti [T 0.0446] aññaṃ voharatīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci “aññaṃ bhaṇissāmī”ti aññaṃ bhaṇati,…pe… [P 0.0416] “aññaṃ voharissāmī”ti aññaṃ voharati, tena vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa vācā”ti.

565. Should it not be said, 'Speech is not in accordance with consciousness'? Yes. Is there not someone who, intending 'I will say something else,' says something else; intending 'I will speak of something else,' speaks of something else; intending 'I will address something else,' addresses something else; intending 'I will express something else,' expresses something else? Yes. If there is someone who, intending 'I will say something else,' says something else… and so on… intending 'I will express something else,' expresses something else, then for that reason, opponent, it should indeed be said, 'Speech is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na yathācittassa vācātikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on 'Speech is Not in Accordance with Consciousness' is concluded.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

(93) 10. Na yathācittassa kāyakammantikathā

9. (93) 10. The Discourse on 'Bodily Action is Not in Accordance with Consciousness'

566. Na [M 0.0306] yathācittassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Aphassakassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… acittakassa kāyakammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphassakassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… sacittakassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Hañci saphassakassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… sacittakassa kāyakammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti.

Is it that bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is there bodily action for one without contact… for one without consciousness? That should not be said… Is there not bodily action for one with contact… for one with consciousness? Yes. If there is bodily action for one with contact… for one with consciousness, then indeed, opponent, it should not be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na [V 0.0340] yathācittassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Anāvaṭṭentassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… appaṇidahantassa kāyakammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu āvaṭṭentassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… paṇidahantassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Hañci āvaṭṭentassa kāyakammaṃ…pe… paṇidahantassa kāyakammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti.

566. Is it that bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is there bodily action for one who does not advert… for one who does not direct the mind? That should not be said… Is there not bodily action for one who adverts… for one who directs the mind? Yes. If there is bodily action for one who adverts… for one who directs the mind, then indeed, opponent, it should not be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na yathācittassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Nanu kāyakammaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ cittena saha ekuppādanti? Āmantā[T 0.0447]. Hañci [P 0.0417] kāyakammaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ cittena saha ekuppādaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti.

Is it that bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Is not bodily action originated from consciousness, co-nascent with consciousness, and having a single arising together with consciousness? Yes. If bodily action is originated from consciousness, co-nascent with consciousness, and has a single arising together with consciousness, then indeed, opponent, it should not be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na yathācittassa kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Na abhikkamitukāmo abhikkamati, na paṭikkamitukāmo paṭikkamati, na āloketukāmo āloketi, na viloketukāmo viloketi, na samiñjitukāmo samiñjeti, na pasāretukāmo pasāretīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Nanu abhikkamitukāmo abhikkamati, paṭikkamitukāmo paṭikkamati, āloketukāmo āloketi, viloketukāmo viloketi, samiñjitukāmo samiñjeti, pasāretukāmo pasāretīti? Āmantā. Hañci abhikkamitukāmo abhikkamati…pe… pasāretukāmo pasāreti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti.

Is it that bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness? Yes. Does one who wishes to go forward not go forward, one who wishes to retreat not retreat, one who wishes to look ahead not look ahead, one who wishes to look around not look around, one who wishes to bend not bend, one who wishes to stretch not stretch? That should not be said… Does not one who wishes to go forward go forward, one who wishes to retreat retreat, one who wishes to look ahead look ahead, one who wishes to look around look around, one who wishes to bend bend, one who wishes to stretch stretch? Yes. If one who wishes to go forward goes forward… and one who wishes to stretch stretches, then indeed, opponent, it should not be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'.

567. Na vattabbaṃ – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci “aññatra gacchissāmī”ti aññatra gacchati…pe… “aññaṃ pasāressāmī”ti aññaṃ pasāretīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci “aññatra [M 0.0307] gacchissāmī”ti aññatra gacchati…pe… “aññaṃ pasāressāmī”ti aññaṃ pasāreti, tena vata re vattabbe – “na yathācittassa kāyakamma”nti.

Should it not be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'? Yes. Is there not someone who, intending, 'I will go elsewhere,' goes elsewhere… who, intending, 'I will stretch another limb,' stretches another limb? Yes. If there is someone who, intending, 'I will go elsewhere,' goes elsewhere… who, intending, 'I will stretch another limb,' stretches another limb, then for that reason, opponent, it should indeed be said, 'Bodily action is not in accordance with consciousness'.

Na yathācittassa kāyakammantikathā niṭṭhitā.

567. The Discourse on 'Bodily Action is Not in Accordance with Consciousness' is concluded.

9. Navamavaggo

9. The Ninth Chapter

(94) 11. Atītānāgatasamannāgatakathā

(94) 11. The Discourse on Being Endowed with the Past and Future

568. Atītena [T 0.0448][V 0.0341] samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgatanti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0418] atītaṃ niruddhaṃ vigataṃ vipariṇataṃ atthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgataṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atītena samannāgato”ti.

9. Is one endowed with the past? Yes. But is not the past ceased, departed, transformed, disappeared, completely disappeared? Yes. If the past is ceased, departed, transformed, disappeared, and completely disappeared, then, opponent, it should not be said, 'One is endowed with the past'.

Anāgatena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ asañjātaṃ anibbattaṃ anabhinibbattaṃ apātubhūtaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgatena samannāgato”ti.

Is one endowed with the future? Yes. But is not the future unborn, unbecome, unarisen, unproduced, not fully produced, unmanifest? Yes. If the future is unborn, unbecome, unarisen, unproduced, not fully produced, and unmanifest, then, opponent, it should not be said, 'One is endowed with the future'.

569. Atītena rūpakkhandhena samannāgato, anāgatena rūpakkhandhena samannāgato, paccuppannena rūpakkhandhena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Tīhi rūpakkhandhehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītehi pañcahi khandhehi samannāgato, anāgatehi pañcahi khandhehi samannāgato, paccuppannehi pañcahi khandhehi samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Pannarasahi khandhehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

568. Is one endowed with the past aggregate of form, endowed with the future aggregate of form, and endowed with the present aggregate of form? Yes. Is one endowed with three aggregates of form? It should not be said so… Is one endowed with the five past aggregates, endowed with the five future aggregates, and endowed with the five present aggregates? Yes. Is one endowed with fifteen aggregates? It should not be said so…

Atītena cakkhāyatanena samannāgato, anāgatena cakkhāyatanena samannāgato, paccuppannena cakkhāyatanena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Tīhi cakkhāyatanehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītehi [T 0.0449] dvādasahi āyatanehi samannāgato, anāgatehi dvādasahi āyatanehi samannāgato, paccuppannehi dvādasahi āyatanehi samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Chattiṃsāyatanehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one endowed with the past eye-base, endowed with the future eye-base, and endowed with the present eye-base? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye-bases? It should not be said so… Is one endowed with the twelve past bases, endowed with the twelve future bases, and endowed with the twelve present bases? Yes. Is one endowed with thirty-six bases? It should not be said so…

Atītāya cakkhudhātuyā samannāgato, anāgatāya cakkhudhātuyā samannāgato, paccuppannāya cakkhudhātuyā samannāgatoti? Āmantā[M 0.0308][P 0.0419]. Tīhi cakkhudhātūhi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītāhi aṭṭhārasahi dhātūhi samannāgato, anāgatāhi aṭṭhārasahi dhātūhi samannāgato[V 0.0342], paccuppannāhi aṭṭhārasahi dhātūhi samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Catupaññāsadhātūhi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

569. Is one endowed with the past eye-element, endowed with the future eye-element, and endowed with the present eye-element? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye-elements? It should not be said so… Is one endowed with the eighteen past elements, endowed with the eighteen future elements, and endowed with the eighteen present elements? Yes. Is one endowed with fifty-four elements? It should not be said so…

Atītena cakkhundriyena samannāgato, anāgatena cakkhundriyena samannāgato, paccuppannena cakkhundriyena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Tīhi cakkhundriyehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītehi bāvīsatindriyehi samannāgato, anāgatehi bāvīsatindriyehi samannāgato, paccuppannehi bāvīsatindriyehi samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Chasaṭṭhindriyehi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one endowed with the past eye-faculty, endowed with the future eye-faculty, and endowed with the present eye-faculty? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye-faculties? It should not be said so… Is one endowed with the twenty-two past faculties, endowed with the twenty-two future faculties, and endowed with the twenty-two present faculties? Yes. Is one endowed with sixty-six faculties? It should not be said so…

570. Na vattabbaṃ – “atītānāgatehi samannāgato”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi aṭṭhavimokkhajhāyī catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ nikāmalābhī navannaṃ anupubbavihārasamāpattīnaṃ [T 0.0450] lābhīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi aṭṭhavimokkhajhāyī catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ nikāmalābhī navannaṃ anupubbavihārasamāpattīnaṃ lābhī, tena vata re vattabbe – “atītānāgatehi samannāgato”ti.

570. Should it not be said, ‘One is endowed with the past and the future’? Yes. But is there not one who attains the eight liberations, who obtains the four jhānas at will, and who gains the nine successive abidings? Yes. If there is one who attains the eight liberations, who obtains the four jhānas at will, and who gains the nine successive abidings, then, good sir, it should indeed be said, ‘One is endowed with the past and the future.’

Atītānāgatasamannāgatakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on being endowed with the past and future is concluded.

Navamavaggo.

The Ninth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Ānisaṃsadassāvissa saṃyojanānaṃ pahānaṃ, amatārammaṇaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, rūpaṃ [P 0.0420] sārammaṇaṃ, anusayā anārammaṇā, evamevaṃ ñāṇaṃ, atītānāgatārammaṇaṃ cittaṃ, sabbaṃ cittaṃ vitakkānupatitaṃ, sabbaso vitakkayato vicārayato vitakkavipphāro saddo, na yathācittassa vācā, tatheva kāyakammaṃ atītānāgatehi samannāgatoti.

The abandoning of fetters for one who sees the benefits; the fetter having the deathless as its object; form having an object; latent tendencies being without an object; likewise, knowledge being without an object; the mind having the past and future as its object; all mind being followed by initial thought; for one who thinks and reflects in every way, sound being the diffusion of initial thought; speech not being according to the mind; likewise bodily action; being endowed with the past and future.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(95) 1. Nirodhakathā

Discourse on Cessation

571. Upapattesiye [P 0.0421][V 0.0343] pañcakkhandhe aniruddhe kiriyā pañcakkhandhā uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Dasannaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, dasa khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti[T 0.0451][M 0.0309]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dasannaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, dasa khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

10. When the five aggregates that seek rebirth have not ceased, do the five functional aggregates arise? Yes. Is there a convergence of ten aggregates, do ten aggregates come into direct presence? It should not be said so… Is there a convergence of ten aggregates, do ten aggregates come into direct presence? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts… of two consciousnesses? It should not be said so…

Upapattesiye pañcakkhandhe aniruddhe kiriyā cattāro khandhā uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Navannaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, nava khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… navannaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, nava khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the five aggregates that seek rebirth have not ceased, do the four functional aggregates arise? Yes. Is there a convergence of nine aggregates, do nine aggregates come into direct presence? It should not be said so… Is there a convergence of nine aggregates, do nine aggregates come into direct presence? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts… of two consciousnesses? It should not be said so…

Upapattesiye pañcakkhandhe aniruddhe kiriyāñāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Channaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, cha khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… channaṃ khandhānaṃ samodhānaṃ hoti, cha khandhā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

571. When the five aggregates that seek rebirth have not ceased, does functional knowledge arise? Yes. Is there a convergence of six aggregates, do six aggregates come into direct presence? It should not be said so… Is there a convergence of six aggregates, do six aggregates come into direct presence? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts… of two consciousnesses? It should not be said so…

572. Upapattesiye [P 0.0422] pañcakkhandhe niruddhe maggo uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Mato maggaṃ bhāveti, kālaṅkato maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When the five aggregates that seek rebirth have ceased, does the path arise? Yes. Does a dead person develop the path? Does one who has died develop the path? It should not be said so…

Nirodhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Cessation is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(96) 2. Rūpaṃ maggotikathā

572. Discourse on ‘Form is the Path’

573. Maggasamaṅgissa [T 0.0452][V 0.0344] rūpaṃ maggoti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi; no ca vata re vattabbe – “maggasamaṅgissa rūpaṃ maggo”ti.

Of a person endowed with the path, is form the path? Yes. Does it have an object? Is there for it turning towards, adverting, collecting, attention, volition, aspiration, and resolve? It should not be said so… Is it not without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is no turning towards… and resolve for it, then indeed it should not be said, ‘Of a person endowed with the path, form is the path.’

Sammāvācā maggoti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi; no ca vata re vattabbe – “sammāvācā maggo”ti.

10. Is Right Speech the path? Yes. Does it have an object? Is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so… Is it not without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is no turning towards… and resolve for it, then indeed it should not be said, ‘Right Speech is the path.’

Sammākammanto [M 0.0310] …pe… sammāājīvo maggoti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0423]. Hañci anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi; no ca vata re vattabbe – “sammāājīvo maggo”ti.

Is Right Action… Right Livelihood the path? Yes. Does it have an object? Is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so… Is it not without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is no turning towards… and resolve for it, then indeed it should not be said, ‘Right Livelihood is the path.’

574. Sammādiṭṭhi maggo, sā ca sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā maggo, sā ca sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na [T 0.0453] hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… sammādiṭṭhi maggo, sā ca sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo maggo, so ca sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo…pe… sammāsati…pe….

573. Is Right View the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. Is Right Speech the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so… Is Right View the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. Is Right Action… Right Livelihood the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so… Right Thought… Right Effort… Right Mindfulness…

Sammāsamādhi maggo, so ca sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā maggo, sā ca sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na [V 0.0345] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāsamādhi maggo, so ca sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo maggo, so ca sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is Right Concentration the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. Is Right Speech the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so… Is Right Concentration the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? Yes. Is Right Action… Right Livelihood the path, and does it have an object; is there for it turning towards… and resolve? It should not be said so…

Sammāvācā maggo, sā ca anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi maggo, sā ca anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāvācā maggo, sā ca anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati [P 0.0424] … sammāsamādhi maggo, so ca anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is Right Speech the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? Yes. Is Right View the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? It should not be said so... Is Right Speech the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? Yes. Is Right Thought... Right Effort... Right Mindfulness... Right Concentration the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? It should not be said so...

Sammākammanto [T 0.0454] …pe… sammāājīvo maggo, so ca anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi… sammāsaṅkappo… sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi maggo, so ca anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is Right Action... Right Livelihood the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? Yes. Is Right View... Right Thought... Right Effort... Right Mindfulness... Right Concentration the path, and is it without an object; is there no turning towards... and resolve for it? It should not be said so...

575. Na [M 0.0311] vattabbaṃ – “maggasamaṅgissa rūpaṃ maggo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo maggoti? Āmantā. Hañci sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo maggo, tena vata re vattabbe – “maggasamaṅgissa rūpaṃ maggo”ti.

575. Should it not be said: 'The form of a person endowed with the path is the path'? Yes. Are not Right Speech, Right Action, and Right Livelihood the path? Yes. If Right Speech, Right Action, and Right Livelihood are the path, then indeed it should be said, 'The form of a person endowed with the path is the path.'

Rūpaṃ maggotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on 'Form is the Path' is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(97) 3. Pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa maggakathā

(97) 3. Discourse on the Path for One Endowed with the Five Consciousnesses

576. Pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa [V 0.0346] atthi maggabhāvanāti? Āmantā. Nanu pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā”ti.

576. For one endowed with the five consciousnesses, is there development of the path? Yes. Are not the five consciousnesses those that have a presently arisen basis and a presently arisen object? Yes. If the five consciousnesses are those that have a presently arisen basis and a presently arisen object, then it certainly should not be said that 'for one endowed with the five consciousnesses, there is development of the path.'

Nanu pañcaviññāṇā purejātavatthukā purejātārammaṇā ajjhattikavatthukā bāhirārammaṇā asambhinnavatthukā asambhinnārammaṇā nānāvatthukā nānārammaṇā [P 0.0425] na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ [T 0.0455] paccanubhonti, na asamannāhārā uppajjanti, na amanasikārā uppajjanti, na abbokiṇṇā uppajjanti, na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjanti, na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjanti, nanu pañcaviññāṇā anābhogāti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā anābhogā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā”ti.

Are not the five consciousnesses those that have a pre-arisen basis, a pre-arisen object, an internal basis, an external object, an unmixed basis, an unmixed object, diverse bases, and diverse objects? Do they not experience the range of each other's objects? Do they not arise without being brought to bear? Do they not arise without attention? Do they not arise intermingled? Do they not arise neither before nor after one another? Do they not arise immediately one after another? Are not the five consciousnesses without application? Yes. If the five consciousnesses are without application, then it certainly should not be said that 'for one endowed with the five consciousnesses, there is development of the path.'

577. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanāti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

577. For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? This should not be said… Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on emptiness? This should not be said… Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on emptiness? Yes. Is there a Sutta that says, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on emptiness'? There is not. Is there a Sutta that says, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms'? Yes. If there is a Sutta that says, 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms,' then it certainly should not be said that 'eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on emptiness.'

578. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa [M 0.0312] atthi maggabhāvanāti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanāti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [P 0.0426][T 0.0456] phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… vedanaṃ ārabbha… saññaṃ ārabbha [V 0.0347] … cetanaṃ ārabbha… cittaṃ ārabbha… cakkhuṃ ārabbha… kāyaṃ ārabbha…pe… saddaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

578. For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking the past or future as its object? This should not be said… For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… taking feeling as its object… taking perception as its object… taking volition as its object… taking consciousness as its object… taking the eye as its object… taking the body as its object… taking sound as its object… taking a tangible object as its object? This should not be said…

Manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, manoviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, manoviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, manoviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha… vedanaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha… vedanaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one endowed with mind-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does mind-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? This should not be said… For one endowed with mind-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does mind-consciousness arise taking the past or future as its object? Yes. For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does eye-consciousness arise taking the past or future as its object? This should not be said… For one endowed with mind-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does mind-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… feeling as its object… a tangible object as its object? Yes. For one endowed with eye-consciousness, is there development of the path, and does eye-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… feeling as its object… a tangible object as its object? This should not be said…

579. Na vattabbaṃ – “pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī…pe… sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī”ti! ma. ni. 1.349; a. ni. 4.37 Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[T 0.0457]. Tena hi pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanāti.

579. Should it not be said, 'For one endowed with the five consciousnesses, there is development of the path'? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, is not one who grasps at its sign or its details… having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled an odor with the nose… having tasted a flavor with the tongue… having touched a tangible object with the body, is not one who grasps at its sign or its details'? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, for one endowed with the five consciousnesses, there is development of the path.

Pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa maggakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Path for One Endowed with the Five Consciousnesses is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(98) 4. Pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpītikathā

(98) 4. Discourse on the Five Consciousnesses Being Both Wholesome and Unwholesome

580. Pañcaviññāṇā [P 0.0427] kusalāpi akusalāpīti? Āmantā. Nanu pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā [M 0.0313] uppannārammaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpī”ti. Nanu pañcaviññāṇā [V 0.0348] purejātavatthukā purejātārammaṇā ajjhattikavatthukā bāhirārammaṇā asambhinnavatthukā asambhinnārammaṇā nānāvatthukā nānārammaṇā na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti, na asamannāhārā uppajjanti, na amanasikārā uppajjanti, na abbokiṇṇā uppajjanti, na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjanti, na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjanti, nanu pañcaviññāṇā anābhogāti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā anābhogā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpī”ti.

580. Are the five consciousnesses both wholesome and unwholesome? Yes. But are not the five consciousnesses having a presently arisen base and a presently arisen object? Yes. If the five consciousnesses have a presently arisen base and a presently arisen object, then indeed it should not be said, “The five consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome.” Are not the five consciousnesses having a pre-arisen base and a pre-arisen object, having an internal base and an external object, having an unmixed base and an unmixed object, having diverse bases and diverse objects, not experiencing each other’s sphere of activity, not arising without advertence, not arising without attention, not arising intermingled, not arising simultaneously, not arising in immediate succession to one another? Are not the five consciousnesses without application? Yes. If the five consciousnesses are without application, then indeed it should not be said, “The five consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome.”

581. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalanti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca paṭicca [T 0.0458] suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0428]. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

581. Is eye-consciousness wholesome? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? That should not be said thus… Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise in dependence on the eye and emptiness? That should not be said thus. Does eye-consciousness arise in dependence on the eye and emptiness? Yes. “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and emptiness”—is there such a Sutta? No. “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on forms”—is there such a Sutta? Yes. If there is indeed a Sutta that states, “eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on forms,” then it should not be said that “eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and emptiness.”

582. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… cittaṃ ārabbha… cakkhuṃ ārabbha…pe… kāyaṃ ārabbha… saddaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

582. Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking the past and future as its object? That should not be said thus… Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… taking mind as its object… taking the eye as its object… taking the body as its object… taking sound as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? That should not be said thus…

Manoviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, manoviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na [T 0.0459] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, manoviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, manoviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… cittaṃ ārabbha…pe… kāyaṃ ārabbha [V 0.0349]… saddaṃ ārabbha [M 0.0314]…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does mind-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking emptiness as its object? That should not be said thus… Does mind-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking the past and future as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking the past and future as its object? That should not be said thus… Does mind-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking contact as its object… taking mind as its object… taking the body as its object… taking sound as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness, being both wholesome and unwholesome, arise taking contact as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? That should not be said thus…

583. Na vattabbaṃ – “pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā [P 0.0429] rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hotī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpīti.

583. Should it not be said that “the five consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome”? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Here, monks, a monk, having seen a form with the eye, grasps at its sign… does not grasp at its sign… having heard a sound with the ear… having felt a tangible object with the body, grasps at its sign… does not grasp at its sign”? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, the five consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome.

Pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Five Consciousneses Being Both Wholesome and Unwholesome is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(99) 5. Sābhogātikathā

10. (99) 5. Discussion on Being with Application

584. Pañcaviññāṇā sābhogāti? Āmantā. Nanu pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā uppannavatthukā uppannārammaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇā sābhogā”ti. Nanu pañcaviññāṇā [T 0.0460] purejātavatthukā purejātārammaṇā ajjhattikavatthukā bāhirārammaṇā asambhinnavatthukā asambhinnārammaṇā nānāvatthukā nānārammaṇā na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti, na asamannāhārā uppajjanti, na amanasikārā uppajjanti, na abbokiṇṇā uppajjanti, na apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjanti, nanu pañcaviññāṇā na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Hañci pañcaviññāṇā na aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇā sābhogā”ti.

Are the five consciousnesses with application? Yes. But are not the five consciousnesses having a presently arisen base and a presently arisen object? Yes. If the five consciousnesses have a presently arisen base and a presently arisen object, then indeed it should not be said, “The five consciousnesses are with application.” Are not the five consciousnesses having a pre-arisen base and a pre-arisen object, an internal base and an external object, an unmixed base and an unmixed object, diverse bases and diverse objects, not experiencing each other’s sphere of activity, not arising without advertence, not arising without attention, not arising intermingled, and not arising simultaneously? And are not the five consciousnesses those that do not arise in immediate succession to one another? Yes. If the five consciousnesses do not arise in immediate succession to one another, then indeed it should not be said, “The five consciousnesses are with application.”

585. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [V 0.0350] sābhoganti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca [P 0.0430] paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca [M 0.0315] paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi…pe… “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca suññatañca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti.

585. Is eye-consciousness with deliberation? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? That should not be said thus… Does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise in dependence on the eye and on emptiness? That should not be said thus… Does eye-consciousness arise in dependence on the eye and on emptiness? Yes. “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on emptiness”—is there such a Sutta? No… “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on forms”—is there such a Sutta? Yes. If the Sutta, “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on forms,” exists, then indeed it should not be said, “Eye-consciousness arises in dependence on the eye and on emptiness.”

Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sābhoganti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ [T 0.0461] atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sābhoganti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ sābhogaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sābhogaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ suññataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ [P 0.0431] sābhogaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sābhogaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ atītānāgataṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manoviññāṇaṃ sābhogaṃ, manoviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ sābhogaṃ, cakkhuviññāṇaṃ phassaṃ ārabbha…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ ārabbha uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is eye-consciousness with deliberation? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking the past and future as its object? That should not be said thus… Is eye-consciousness with deliberation? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? That should not be said thus… Is mind-consciousness with deliberation, and does mind-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? Yes. Is eye-consciousness with deliberation, and does eye-consciousness arise taking emptiness as its object? That should not be said thus… Is mind-consciousness with deliberation, and does mind-consciousness arise taking the past and future as its object? Yes. Is eye-consciousness with deliberation, and does eye-consciousness arise taking the past and future as its object? That should not be said thus… Is mind-consciousness with deliberation, and does mind-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? Yes. Is eye-consciousness with deliberation, and does eye-consciousness arise taking contact as its object… taking tangible objects as its object? That should not be said thus…

586. Na vattabbaṃ – “pañcaviññāṇā sābhogā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hotī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi pañcaviññāṇā sābhogāti…pe….

586. Should it not be said, “The five sense-consciousnesses are with deliberation”? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Here, monks, a monk, having seen a form with the eye, grasps the sign… does not grasp the sign… having touched a tangible object with the body, grasps the sign… does not grasp the sign”? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, the five sense-consciousnesses are with deliberation…

Sābhogātikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Deliberation is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(100) 6. Dvīhisīlehikathā

(100) 6. The Discussion on Two Virtues

587. Maggasamaṅgī [T 0.0462][V 0.0351] dvīhi sīlehi samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī dvīhi phassehi dvīhi vedanāhi dvīhi saññāhi dvīhi cetanāhi dvīhi cittehi [M 0.0316] dvīhi saddhāhi dvīhi vīriyehi dvīhi satīhi dvīhi samādhīhi dvīhi paññāhi samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

587. Is one who possesses the path endowed with two kinds of virtue? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with two kinds of contact, two kinds of feeling, two kinds of perception, two kinds of volition, two kinds of consciousness, two kinds of faith, two kinds of energy, two kinds of mindfulness, two kinds of concentration, and two kinds of wisdom? That should not be said thus…

Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena sīlena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena phassena lokiyāya vedanāya lokiyāya paññāya lokiyāya cetanāya lokiyena cittena lokiyāya saddhāya lokiyena vīriyena lokiyāya satiyā lokiyena samādhinā lokiyāya paññāya samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane virtue? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane contact, mundane feeling, mundane perception, mundane volition, mundane consciousness, mundane faith, mundane energy, mundane mindfulness, mundane concentration, and mundane wisdom? That should not be said thus…

Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sīlena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī [P 0.0432] lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca phassena samannāgato…pe… lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca paññāya samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasamaṅgī lokiyena sīlena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī puthujjanoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane virtue? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane contact… both mundane and supramundane wisdom? That should not be said thus… Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane virtue? Yes. Is one who possesses the path a worldling? That should not be said thus…

588. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya sammāvācāya samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya sammāvācāya samannāgatoti[T 0.0463]? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena sammāsaṅkappena…pe… lokiyena sammāvāyāmena…pe… lokiyāya sammāsatiyā…pe… lokiyena sammāsamādhinā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasamaṅgī lokiyena sammākammantena…pe… lokiyena sammāājīvena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya sammādiṭṭhiyā…pe… lokiyena sammāsamādhinā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

588. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right speech? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right view? That should not be said thus… Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right speech? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right intention… mundane right effort… mundane right mindfulness… mundane right concentration? That should not be said thus… Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right action… mundane right livelihood? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with mundane right view… mundane right concentration? That should not be said thus…

Maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca sammāvācāya samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī [V 0.0352] lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca sammāvācāya samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāsaṅkappena…pe… lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāvāyāmena [P 0.0433]…pe… lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca sammāsatiyā…pe… lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāsamādhinā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right speech? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right view? That should not be said thus… Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right speech? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right intention… both mundane and supramundane right effort… both mundane and supramundane right mindfulness… both mundane and supramundane right concentration? That should not be said thus…

Maggasamaṅgī [M 0.0317] lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammākammantena…pe… sammāājīvena samannāgatoti? Āmantā. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyāya ca lokuttarāya ca sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… maggasamaṅgī lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāājīvena samannāgatoti? Āmantā[T 0.0464]. Maggasamaṅgī lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāsaṅkappena…pe… lokiyena ca lokuttarena ca sammāsamādhinā samannāgatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right action… etc…. and right livelihood? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right view? That should not be said thus… etc…. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right livelihood? Yes. Is one who possesses the path endowed with both mundane and supramundane right intention… etc…. both mundane and supramundane right concentration? That should not be said thus… etc….

589. Na vattabbaṃ – “maggasamaṅgī dvīhi sīlehi samannāgato”ti? Āmantā. Lokiye sīle niruddhe maggo uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Dussīlo khaṇḍasīlo chinnasīlo maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… tena hi maggasamaṅgī dvīhi sīlehi samannāgatoti.

589. Should it not be said that ‘one who possesses the path is endowed with two kinds of virtue’? Yes. Does the path arise when mundane virtue has ceased? Yes. Does an immoral person, one with broken virtue, one with severed virtue, develop the path? That should not be said thus… etc…. Therefore, one who possesses the path is endowed with two kinds of virtue.

Dvīhisīlehikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Twofold Virtue is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(101) 7. Sīlaṃ acetasikantikathā

10. (101) 7. The Discussion on Virtue Being Non-Mental

590. Sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ…pe… nibbānaṃ…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ [P 0.0434]…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Phasso acetasikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0353] …pe… sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… cetanā…pe… saddhā…pe… vīriyaṃ…pe… sati…pe… samādhi…pe… paññā acetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is virtue non-mental? Yes. Is virtue form? …pe… Nibbāna? …pe… the eye-base? …pe… the body-base? … the form-base? …pe… the tangible-base? That should not be said thus…pe… Is virtue non-mental? Yes. Is contact non-mental? That should not be said thus …pe… Is virtue non-mental? Yes. Are feeling…pe… perception…pe… volition…pe… faith…pe… energy…pe… mindfulness…pe… concentration…pe… wisdom non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe…

Phasso cetasikoti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ cetasikanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… cetanā…pe… saddhā…pe… vīriyaṃ…pe… sati…pe… samādhi…pe… paññā cetasikāti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ cetasikanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

590. Is contact a mental factor? Yes. Is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe… Are feeling…pe… perception…pe… volition…pe… faith…pe… energy…pe… mindfulness…pe… concentration…pe… wisdom mental factors? Yes. Is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe…

591. Sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Aniṭṭhaphalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu iṭṭhaphalanti? Āmantā. Hañci iṭṭhaphalaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sīlaṃ acetasika”nti.

Is virtue non-mental? Yes. Does it have an undesirable result? That should not be said thus…pe… But does it not have a desirable result? Yes. If it has a desirable result, then it should not be said that ‘virtue is non-mental’.

Saddhā [M 0.0318] iṭṭhaphalā, saddhā cetasikāti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ cetasikanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vīriyaṃ…pe… sati…pe… samādhi…pe… paññā iṭṭhaphalā, paññā cetasikāti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ cetasikanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

591. Faith has a desirable result; is faith a mental factor? Yes. Virtue has a desirable result; is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe… Energy…pe… mindfulness…pe… concentration…pe… wisdom has a desirable result; is wisdom a mental factor? Yes. Virtue has a desirable result; is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe…

Sīlaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā[P 0.0435]. Saddhā iṭṭhaphalā, saddhā acetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaṃ iṭṭhaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Vīriyaṃ…pe… sati…pe… samādhi…pe… paññā iṭṭhaphalā, paññā acetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Virtue has a desirable result; is virtue non-mental? Yes. Faith has a desirable result; is faith non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe… Virtue has a desirable result; is virtue non-mental? Yes. Energy…pe… mindfulness…pe… concentration…pe… wisdom has a desirable result; is wisdom non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe…

592. Sīlaṃ acetasikanti? Āmantā. Aphalaṃ avipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphalaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Hañci saphalaṃ savipākaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sīlaṃ acetasika”nti…pe….

Is virtue non-mental? Yes. Is it fruitless and without result? That should not be said thus…pe… But is it not fruitful and with result? Yes. If it is fruitful and with result, then it should not be said that ‘virtue is non-mental’…pe…

Cakkhāyatanaṃ acetasikaṃ avipākanti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ acetasikaṃ avipākanti? Na [V 0.0354] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ [T 0.0466] …pe… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ acetasikaṃ avipākanti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ acetasikaṃ avipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

592. Is the eye-base non-mental and non-resultant? Yes. Is virtue non-mental and non-resultant? That should not be said thus…pe… Is the ear-base…pe… the body-base …pe… the form-base…pe… the tangible-base non-mental and non-resultant? Yes. Is virtue non-mental and non-resultant? That should not be said thus…pe…

Sīlaṃ acetasikaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ acetasikaṃ savipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaṃ acetasikaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Sotāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ… rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ acetasikaṃ savipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is virtue non-mental and with result? Yes. Is the eye-base non-mental and with result? That should not be said thus…pe… Is virtue non-mental and with result? Yes. Is the ear-base…pe… the body-base… the form-base…pe… the tangible-base non-mental and with result? That should not be said thus…pe…

593. Sammāvācā acetasikāti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi acetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāvācā [P 0.0436] acetasikāti? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo…pe… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi acetasikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo acetasikoti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi acetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāājīvo acetasikoti? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo… sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati… sammāsamādhi acetasikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is right speech non-mental? Yes. Is right view non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right speech non-mental? Yes. Is right intention…pe… right effort…pe… right mindfulness…pe… right concentration non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right action…pe… right livelihood non-mental? Yes. Is right view non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right livelihood non-mental? Yes. Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… right concentration non-mental? That should not be said thus…pe…

Sammādiṭṭhi cetasikāti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā cetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammādiṭṭhi cetasikāti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo [M 0.0319] cetasikoti? Na [T 0.0467] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo…pe… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi cetasikoti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā cetasikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāsamādhi cetasikoti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo cetasikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

593. Is right view a mental factor? Yes. Is right speech a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right view a mental factor? Yes. Is right action…pe… right livelihood a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right intention…pe… right effort…pe… right mindfulness…pe… right concentration a mental factor? Yes. Is right speech a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe… Is right concentration a mental factor? Yes. Is right action…pe… right livelihood a mental factor? That should not be said thus…pe…

594. Na vattabbaṃ – “sīlaṃ acetasika”nti? Āmantā. Sīle uppajjitvā niruddhe dussīlo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi sīlaṃ acetasikanti.

Should it not be said that ‘virtue is non-mental’? Yes. When virtue has arisen and ceased, does one become immoral? That should not be said thus. Therefore, virtue is non-mental.

Sīlaṃ acetasikantikathā niṭṭhitā.

594. The Discussion on Virtue Being Non-Mental is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(102) 8. Sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattītikathā

(102) 8. The Discussion on 'Virtue is Not Concomitant with the Mind'

595. Sīlaṃ [P 0.0437][V 0.0355] na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ… nibbānaṃ… cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Phasso na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Vedanā…pe… saññā… cetanā… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

10. Is virtue not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is form… Nibbāna… the eye-base…pe… the tangible-base not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus…pe… Is virtue not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is contact not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus…pe… Is virtue not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is feeling…pe… perception… volition… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration…pe… wisdom not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus…pe…

Phasso cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā… cetanā [T 0.0468]… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is virtue concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is feeling… and so on… perception… volition… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… and so on… wisdom concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is virtue concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on…

596. Sammāvācā na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāvācā na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo… sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

596. Is right speech not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right view not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is right speech not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… and so on… right concentration not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo na cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā[P 0.0438]. Sammādiṭṭhi na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāājīvo na cittānuparivattīti[M 0.0320]? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo… sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi na cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is right action… and so on… right livelihood not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right view not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is right livelihood not concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… and so on… right concentration not concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Sammādiṭṭhi cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammādiṭṭhi cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is right view concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right speech concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is right view concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right action… and so on… right livelihood concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Sammāsaṅkappo [V 0.0356] … sammāvāyāmo… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā cittānuparivattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāsamādhi cittānuparivattīti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo cittānuparivattīti[T 0.0469]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… and so on… right concentration concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right speech concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is right concentration concomitant with the mind? Yes. Is right action… and so on… right livelihood concomitant with the mind? That should not be said thus… and so on…

597. Na vattabbaṃ – “sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattī”ti? Āmantā. Sīle uppajjitvā niruddhe dussīlo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattīti.

597. Should it not be said that “virtue is not concomitant with the mind”? Yes. When virtue has arisen and ceased, does one become immoral? That should not be said thus. Therefore, virtue is not concomitant with the mind.

Sīlaṃ na cittānuparivattītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'Virtue is Not Concomitant with the Mind' is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(103) 9. Samādānahetukathā

(103) 9. Discussion on the Cause of Undertaking

598. Samādānahetukaṃ [P 0.0439] sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Samādānahetuko phasso vaḍḍhati, vedanā vaḍḍhati, saññā vaḍḍhati, cetanā vaḍḍhati, cittaṃ vaḍḍhati, saddhā vaḍḍhati, vīriyaṃ vaḍḍhati, sati vaḍḍhati, samādhi vaḍḍhati, paññā vaḍḍhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

598. Does virtue that has undertaking as its cause increase? Yes. Does contact that has undertaking as its cause increase? Does feeling increase? Does perception increase? Does volition increase? Does mind increase? Does faith increase? Does energy increase? Does mindfulness increase? Does concentration increase? Does wisdom increase? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Samādānahetukaṃ sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Latā viya vaḍḍhati, māluvā viya vaḍḍhati, rukkho viya vaḍḍhati, tiṇaṃ viya vaḍḍhati, muñjapuñjo viya vaḍḍhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does virtue that has undertaking as its cause increase? Yes. Does it increase like a creeper? Does it increase like a māluvā vine? Does it increase like a tree? Does it increase like grass? Does it increase like a clump of muñja grass? That should not be said thus… and so on…

599. Samādānahetukaṃ sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Sīlaṃ samādiyitvā kāmavitakkaṃ vitakkentassa byāpādavitakkaṃ vitakkentassa vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vitakkentassa sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ [M 0.0321] hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti[T 0.0470]? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā [V 0.0357] sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

599. Does virtue that has undertaking as its cause increase? Yes. For a person who, having undertaken virtue, thinks a thought of sensual pleasure, thinks a thought of ill will, or thinks a thought of violence, does virtue increase? Yes. Is there a confluence of two contacts… and so on… of two minds? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is there a confluence of two contacts… and so on… of two minds? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior phenomena with dark and bright counterparts come to be face to face? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0440]. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior phenomena with dark and bright counterparts come to be face to face? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, these four are very, very far apart. What four? Monks, the sky and the earth—this is the first that is very, very far apart… and so on… Therefore, the Dhamma of the good is far from the wicked.' Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior phenomena with dark and bright counterparts come to be face to face.'

600. Na vattabbaṃ – “samādānahetukaṃ sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “ārāmaropā vanaropā…pe… dhammaṭṭhā sīlasampannā te janā saggagāmino”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi samādānahetukaṃ sīlaṃ vaḍḍhatīti.

600. Should it not be said: 'Virtue that has undertaking as its cause increases'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Those who plant parks, who plant groves… and so on… established in Dhamma, accomplished in virtue, those people are bound for heaven.' Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, virtue that has undertaking as its cause increases.

Samādānahetukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Cause of Undertaking is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(104) 10. Viññatti sīlantikathā

(104) 10. Discussion on Intimation as Virtue

601. Viññatti sīlanti? Āmantā. Pāṇātipātā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adinnādānā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0471] …pe… musāvādā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

601. Is intimation virtue? Yes. Is it abstention from the destruction of life? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is it abstention from taking what is not given? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is it abstention from sexual misconduct? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is it abstention from false speech? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is it abstention from intoxicants that are the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said thus… and so on…

Abhivādanaṃ sīlaṃ, paccuṭṭhānaṃ sīlaṃ, añjalikammaṃ sīlaṃ, sāmīcikammaṃ sīlaṃ, āsanābhihāro [V 0.0358] sīlaṃ, seyyābhihāro sīlaṃ, pādodakābhihāro sīlaṃ, pādakathalikābhihāro sīlaṃ, nhāne piṭṭhiparikammaṃ sīlanti? Āmantā[P 0.0441]. Pāṇātipātā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is paying homage virtue? Is rising to greet virtue? Is performing the añjali gesture virtue? Is respectful conduct virtue? Is offering a seat virtue? Is offering a bed virtue? Is offering water for the feet virtue? Is offering a foot-scrubber virtue? Is scrubbing the back while bathing virtue? Yes. Is it abstention from the destruction of life? That should not be said thus… and so on… Is it abstention from intoxicants that are the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said thus… and so on…

602. Na [M 0.0322] vattabbaṃ – “viññatti sīla”nti? Āmantā. Dussilyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi viññatti sīlanti.

602. Should it not be said: 'Intimation is virtue'? Yes. Is it immorality? That should not be said thus… and so on… Therefore, intimation is virtue.

Viññatti sīlantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Intimation as Virtue is concluded.

10. Dasamavaggo

10. The Tenth Chapter

(105) 11. Aviññatti dussilyantikathā

(105) 11. Discussion on Non-Intimation as Immorality

603. Aviññatti dussilyanti? Āmantā. Pāṇātipātoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adinnādānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmesumicchācāroti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… musāvādoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
