603. Is non-intimation immorality? Yes. Is it the destruction of life? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it taking what is not given? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it sexual misconduct? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it false speech? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it intoxicants that are the basis for heedlessness? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Pāpakammaṃ samādiyitvā dānaṃ dadantassa puññañca apuññañca ubho vaḍḍhantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puññañca apuññañca ubho vaḍḍhantīti? Āmantā[T 0.0472]. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā [P 0.0442] sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who gives a gift after having undertaken an evil deed, do both merit and demerit increase? It should not be said thus… and so on… Do both merit and demerit increase? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts… and so on… of two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is there a convergence of two contacts… and so on… of two consciousnesses? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart qualities come into direct presence? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0443] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni[V 0.0359]! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart qualities come into direct presence? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, these four are exceedingly far apart! Which four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first that is exceedingly far apart… and so on… Therefore, the Dhamma of the good is far from the wicked.' Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart qualities come into direct presence.'

604. Na vattabbaṃ – “aviññatti dussilya”nti? Āmantā. Nanu pāpakammaṃ samādinno āsīti? Āmantā. Hañci pāpakammaṃ samādinno āsi, tena vata re vattabbe – “aviññatti dussilya”nti.

604. Should it not be said: 'Non-intimation is immorality'? Yes. But was he not one who had undertaken an evil deed? Yes. If he was one who had undertaken an evil deed, then indeed it should be said: 'Non-intimation is immorality.'

Aviññatti dussilyantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Non-Intimation as Immorality is concluded.

Dasamavaggo.

The Tenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof is:

Upapattesiye [M 0.0323] pañcakkhandhe aniruddhe kiriyā pañcakkhandhā uppajjanti, maggasamaṅgissa rūpaṃ maggo, pañcaviññāṇasamaṅgissa atthi maggabhāvanā, pañcaviññāṇā kusalāpi akusalāpi, pañcaviññāṇā sābhogā, maggasamaṅgī dvīhi sīlehi samannāgato, sīlaṃ acetasikaṃ, sīlaṃ na cittānuparivatti, samādānahetukaṃ sīlaṃ [T 0.0474] vaḍḍhatīti, viññattisīlaṃ aviññatti dussilyanti.

The cessation of the five-constituent existence for one endowed with the path; for one endowed with the path, form is the path; for one endowed with the five consciousnesses, there is development of the path; the five consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome; the five consciousnesses are accompanied by application; one endowed with the path is possessed of two virtues; virtue is non-mental; virtue does not follow the mind; virtue grows because of undertaking; intimation is virtue; non-intimation is immorality.

Dutiyo paṇṇāsako.

The Second Fifty.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof is:

Niyāmasaṅgahagatānisaṃsatā ca nirodhoti niyāma saṅgahagatānisaṃsatā atthi pañcavokārabhavo nirodho maggasamaṅgissa pañcavokārabhavoti (sī. syā. ka.), niyāma saṅgaha gatānisaṃsatā atthi pañcavokārabhavo maggasamaṅgissa no pañcavokārabhavo (pī.).

The benefit of inclusion in the fixed course, and cessation.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(106-108) 1-3. Tissopi anusayakathā

The Three Discussions on Latent Dispositions

605. Anusayā [P 0.0444][V 0.0360] abyākatāti? Āmantā. Vipākābyākatā kiriyābyākatā rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

605. Are the latent dispositions indeterminate? Yes. Are they resultant-indeterminate, functional-indeterminate, material form, Nibbāna, the eye-base… up to… the tangible-base? It should not be said thus….

Kāmarāgānusayo abyākatoti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of sensual lust indeterminate? Yes. Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, and the hindrance of sensual desire indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust... and the hindrance of sensual desire unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of sensual lust unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Paṭighānusayo abyākatoti? Āmantā. Paṭighaṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānaṃ paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭighaṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānaṃ paṭighasaṃyojanaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Paṭighānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of aversion indeterminate? Yes. Are aversion, the obsession with aversion, and the fetter of aversion indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are aversion, the obsession with aversion, and the fetter of aversion unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of aversion unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Mānānusayo [M 0.0324] abyākatoti? Āmantā. Māno mānapariyuṭṭhānaṃ [T 0.0475] mānasaṃyojanaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… māno mānapariyuṭṭhānaṃ mānasaṃyojanaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Mānānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe….

Is the latent disposition of conceit indeterminate? Yes. Are conceit, the obsession with conceit, and the fetter of conceit indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are conceit, the obsession with conceit, and the fetter of conceit unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of conceit unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Diṭṭhānusayo [P 0.0445] abyākatoti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhi diṭṭhogho diṭṭhiyogo diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… diṭṭhi diṭṭhogho diṭṭhiyogo diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānaṃ diṭṭhisaṃyojanaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of views indeterminate? Yes. Are views, the flood of views, the yoke of views, the obsession with views, and the fetter of views indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are views, the flood of views, the yoke of views, the obsession with views, and the fetter of views unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of views unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Vicikicchānusayo abyākatoti? Āmantā. Vicikicchā vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vicikicchā [V 0.0361] vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ vicikicchāsaṃyojanaṃ vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Vicikicchānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of doubt indeterminate? Yes. Are doubt, the obsession with doubt, the fetter of doubt, and the hindrance of doubt indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are doubt, the obsession with doubt, the fetter of doubt, and the hindrance of doubt unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of doubt unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Bhavarāgānusayo abyākatoti? Āmantā. Bhavarāgo bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… bhavarāgo bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ bhavarāgasaṃyojanaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Bhavarāgānusayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of craving for existence indeterminate? Yes. Are craving for existence, the obsession with craving for existence, and the fetter of craving for existence indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are craving for existence, the obsession with craving for existence, and the fetter of craving for existence unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of craving for existence unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Avijjānusayo abyākatoti? Āmantā. Avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo [T 0.0476] avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Avijjānusayo [P 0.0446] akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of ignorance indeterminate? Yes. Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the obsession with ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance indeterminate? It should not be said thus... Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the obsession with ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance unwholesome? Yes. Is the latent disposition of ignorance unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

606. Na vattabbaṃ – “anusayā abyākatā”ti? Āmantā. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sānusayo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi anusayā abyākatāti. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sarāgo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi rāgo abyākatoti.

606. Should it not be said, 'The latent dispositions are indeterminate'? Indeed, it should not be said. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with latent dispositions'? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states come into direct presence? It should not be said thus... Therefore, the latent dispositions are indeterminate. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with lust'? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states come into direct presence? It should not be said thus... Therefore, lust is indeterminate.

607. Anusayā [M 0.0325] ahetukāti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

607. Are the latent dispositions rootless? Yes. Is a latent disposition material form, Nibbāna, the eye-base… up to… the tangible-base? It should not be said thus….

Kāmarāgānusayo ahetukoti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ ahetukanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ sahetukanti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgānusayo sahetukoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭighānusayo…pe… mānānusayo… diṭṭhānusayo… vicikicchānusayo… bhavarāgānusayo… avijjānusayo ahetukoti? Āmantā. Avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ avijjāsaṃyojanaṃ avijjānīvaraṇaṃ ahetukanti[V 0.0362]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0477] …pe… avijjā [P 0.0447] avijjogho…pe… avijjānīvaraṇaṃ sahetukanti? Āmantā. Avijjānusayo sahetukoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of sensual lust rootless? Yes. Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, and the hindrance of sensual desire rootless? It should not be said thus... Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust... and the hindrance of sensual desire with roots? Yes. Is the latent disposition of sensual lust with roots? It should not be said thus... Is the latent disposition of aversion… the latent disposition of conceit… the latent disposition of views… the latent disposition of doubt… the latent disposition of craving for existence… the latent disposition of ignorance rootless? Yes. Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the obsession with ignorance, the fetter of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance rootless? It should not be said thus... Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance... and the hindrance of ignorance with roots? Yes. Is the latent disposition of ignorance with roots? It should not be said thus...

608. Na vattabbaṃ – “anusayā ahetukā”ti? Āmantā. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sānusayo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Anusayā tena hetunā sahetukāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi anusayā ahetukāti. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sarāgo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Rāgo tena hetunā sahetukoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi rāgo ahetukoti.

608. Should it not be said, 'The latent dispositions are rootless'? Indeed, it should not be said. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with latent dispositions'? Yes. Are the latent dispositions rooted by that cause? It should not be said thus... Therefore, the latent dispositions are rootless. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with lust'? Yes. Is lust rooted by that cause? It should not be said thus... Therefore, lust is rootless.

609. Anusayā cittavippayuttāti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

609. Are the latent dispositions dissociated from mind? Yes. Is a latent disposition material form, Nibbāna, the eye-base… up to… the tangible-base? It should not be said thus….

Kāmarāgānusayo cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kāmarāgasaṃyojanaṃ kāmogho kāmayogo kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmarāgo kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānaṃ…pe… kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ cittasampayuttanti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgānusayo cittasampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of sensual lust dissociated from mind? Yes. Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust, the fetter of sensual lust, the flood of sensuality, the yoke of sensuality, and the hindrance of sensual desire dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus... Are sensual lust, the obsession with sensual lust... and the hindrance of sensual desire associated with mind? Yes. Is the latent disposition of sensual lust associated with mind? It should not be said thus...

610. Kāmarāgānusayo cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Katamakkhandhapariyāpannoti? Saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannoti. Saṅkhārakkhandho [P 0.0448] cittavippayuttoti? Na [M 0.0326] hevaṃ vattabbe. Saṅkhārakkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

610. Is the latent disposition of sensual lust dissociated from mind? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of formations. Is the aggregate of formations dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus. Is the aggregate of formations dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

Kāmarāgānusayo [T 0.0478] saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmarāgo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Kāmarāgānusayo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittasampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind? Yes. Is sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? Yes. Is the latent disposition of sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? It should not be said thus…

Kāmarāgānusayo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittavippayutto, kāmarāgo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno [V 0.0363] cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind, and is sensual lust, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? Yes. Is the aggregate of formations partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

Saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the aggregate of formations partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

611. Paṭighānusayo mānānusayo diṭṭhānusayo vicikicchānusayo bhavarāgānusayo avijjānusayo cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Avijjā avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānīvaraṇaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… avijjā [P 0.0449] avijjogho avijjāyogo avijjānīvaraṇaṃ cittasampayuttanti? Āmantā. Avijjānusayo cittasampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

611. Are the latent disposition of aversion, the latent disposition of conceit, the latent disposition of views, the latent disposition of doubt, the latent disposition of craving for existence, and the latent disposition of ignorance dissociated from mind? Yes. Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, and the hindrance of ignorance associated with mind? Yes. Is the latent disposition of ignorance associated with mind? It should not be said thus…

612. Avijjānusayo cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Katamakkhandhapariyāpannoti? Saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannoti. Saṅkhārakkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe[T 0.0479]. Saṅkhārakkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

612. Is the latent disposition of ignorance dissociated from mind? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of formations. Is the aggregate of formations dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus. Is the aggregate of formations dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

Avijjānusayo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Avijjā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā cittavippayuttāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… avijjā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā cittasampayuttāti? Āmantā. Avijjānusayo saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittasampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the latent disposition of ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind? Yes. Is ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? Yes. Is the latent disposition of ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? It should not be said thus…

Avijjānusayo [M 0.0327] saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno cittavippayutto, avijjāsaṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā cittasampayuttāti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

Is the latent disposition of ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, dissociated from mind, and is ignorance, being included in the aggregate of formations, associated with mind? Yes. Is the aggregate of formations partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus.

Saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho [V 0.0364] saññākkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na [P 0.0450] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the aggregate of formations in one part associated with mind and in one part dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling and the aggregate of perception in one part associated with mind and in one part dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

613. Na vattabbaṃ – “anusayā cittavippayuttā”ti? Āmantā. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sānusayo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Anusayā tena cittena sampayuttāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi anusayā cittavippayuttāti. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sarāgo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Rāgo tena cittena sampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi rāgo cittavippayuttoti.

613. Should it not be said that 'the underlying tendencies are dissociated from mind'? Yes, it should not be said. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with underlying tendencies'? Yes. Are the underlying tendencies associated with that mind? It should not be said thus. Therefore, the underlying tendencies are dissociated from mind. When the mind of a worldling is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said that he is 'with passion'? Yes. Is passion associated with that mind? It should not be said thus. Therefore, passion is dissociated from mind.

Tissopi anusayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The three discourses on the underlying tendencies are concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(109) 4. Ñāṇakathā

(109) 4. Discourse on Ignorance

614. Aññāṇe [T 0.0480] vigate ñāṇavippayutte citte vattamāne na vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇī”ti? Āmantā. Rāge vigate na vattabbaṃ – “vītarāgo”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… aññāṇe vigate ñāṇavippayutte citte vattamāne na vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇī”ti? Āmantā. Dose vigate… mohe vigate… kilese vigate na vattabbaṃ – “nikkileso”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

614. When ignorance is absent and a mind dissociated from knowledge is present, should it not be said that one is 'knowing'? Yes, it should not be said. When lust is absent, should it not be said that one is 'free from lust'? It should not be said thus… When ignorance is absent and a mind dissociated from knowledge is present, should it not be said that one is 'knowing'? Yes, it should not be said. When hatred is absent… when delusion is absent… when defilements are absent, should it not be said that one is 'free from defilements'? It should not be said thus…

Rāge vigate vattabbaṃ – “vītarāgo”ti? Āmantā. Aññāṇe vigate ñāṇavippayutte citte vattamāne vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇī”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dose [P 0.0451] vigate… mohe vigate… kilese vigate vattabbaṃ – “nikkileso”ti? Āmantā. Aññāṇe vigate ñāṇavippayutte citte vattamāne vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇī”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

When lust is absent, should it be said that one is 'free from lust'? Yes. When ignorance is absent and a mind dissociated from knowledge is present, should it be said that one is 'knowing'? It should not be said thus… When hatred is absent… when delusion is absent… when defilements are absent, should it be said that one is 'free from defilements'? Yes. When ignorance is absent and a mind dissociated from knowledge is present, should it be said that one is 'knowing'? It should not be said thus…

615. Aññāṇe [M 0.0328] vigate ñāṇavippayutte citte vattamāne vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇī”ti? Āmantā[V 0.0365]. Atītena ñāṇena ñāṇī niruddhena vigatena paṭipassaddhena ñāṇena ñāṇīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

615. When ignorance is absent and a mind dissociated from knowledge is present, should it be said that one is 'knowing'? Yes. Is one 'knowing' through past knowledge that has ceased, vanished, and subsided? It should not be said thus…

Ñāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Ignorance is concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(110) 5. Ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttantikathā

(110) 5. Discourse on Knowledge being Dissociated from Mind

616. Ñāṇaṃ [T 0.0481] cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paññā paññindriyaṃ paññābalaṃ sammādiṭṭhi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Ñāṇaṃ cittasampayuttanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

616. Is knowledge dissociated from mind? Yes. Is it form, Nibbāna, the eye-base… the tangible-base? It should not be said thus… Is knowledge dissociated from mind? Yes. Are wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view, and the investigation-of-states enlightenment-factor dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Are wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view, and the investigation-of-states enlightenment-factor associated with mind? Yes. Is knowledge associated with mind? It should not be said thus…

Ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Katamakkhandhapariyāpannanti[P 0.0452]? Saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannanti. Saṅkhārakkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saṅkhārakkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ñāṇaṃ saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Paññā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā cittavippayuttāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paññā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā cittasampayuttāti? Āmantā. Ñāṇaṃ saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannaṃ cittasampayuttanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ñāṇaṃ saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannaṃ cittavippayuttaṃ, paññā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā [T 0.0482] cittasampayuttāti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saṅkhārakkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Āmantā. Vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho ekadeso cittasampayutto ekadeso cittavippayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is knowledge dissociated from mind? Yes. Under which aggregate is it included? It is included in the formations aggregate. Is the formations aggregate dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is the formations aggregate dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the feeling aggregate and the perception aggregate dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is knowledge included in the formations aggregate and dissociated from mind? Yes. Is wisdom included in the formations aggregate and dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is wisdom included in the formations aggregate and associated with mind? Yes. Is knowledge included in the formations aggregate and associated with mind? It should not be said thus… Is knowledge included in the formations aggregate and dissociated from mind, while wisdom is included in the formations aggregate and associated with mind? Yes. Is the formations aggregate partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus… Is the formations aggregate partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? Yes. Are the feeling aggregate and the perception aggregate partly associated with mind and partly dissociated from mind? It should not be said thus…

617. Na [V 0.0366] vattabbaṃ – “ñāṇaṃ cittavippayutta”nti? Āmantā. Arahā cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī “ñāṇī”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. Ñāṇaṃ tena cittena sampayuttanti? Na [P 0.0453] hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttanti.

617. Should it not be said that 'knowledge is dissociated from mind'? Yes, it should not be said. Should an arahant endowed with eye-consciousness be said to be 'one who possesses knowledge'? Yes. Is that knowledge associated with that mind? It should not be said thus. Therefore, knowledge is dissociated from mind.

Arahā [M 0.0329] cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī “paññavā”ti vattabboti sakavādīpucchā viya dissati? Āmantā. Paññā tena cittena sampayuttāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi paññā cittavippayuttāti.

Should an arahant endowed with eye-consciousness be called 'wise'? Yes. Is wisdom associated with that mind? It should not be said thus. Therefore, wisdom is dissociated from mind.

Ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Knowledge being Dissociated from Mind is concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(111) 6. Idaṃ dukkhantikathā

(111) 6. Discourse on 'This is Suffering'

618. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo”ti vācaṃ bhāsato “ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… “idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Ayaṃ dukkhanirodho”ti vācaṃ bhāsato “ayaṃ dukkhanirodho”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na [T 0.0483] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… “idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Ayaṃ maggo”ti vācaṃ bhāsato “ayaṃ maggo”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

618. When one speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering' arise? Yes. When one speaks the words, 'This is the origin of suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is the origin of suffering' arise? It should not be said thus... When one speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering' arise? Yes. When one speaks the words, 'This is the cessation of suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is the cessation of suffering' arise? It should not be said thus... When one speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering' arise? Yes. When one speaks the words, 'This is the path,' does the knowledge, 'This is the path' arise? It should not be said thus...

“Ayaṃ samudayo”ti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “ayaṃ samudayo”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… “ayaṃ [P 0.0454] nirodho”ti… “ayaṃ maggo”ti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “ayaṃ maggo”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who speaks the words, 'This is the origin,' does the knowledge, 'This is the origin,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said... For one who speaks the words, 'This is the cessation'... 'This is the path,' does the knowledge, 'This is the path,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said...

619. “Idaṃ [V 0.0367] dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Rūpaṃ anicca”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “rūpaṃ anicca”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… “idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. Vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… “viññāṇaṃ anicca”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “viññāṇaṃ anicca”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

619. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'Form is impermanent,' does the knowledge, 'Form is impermanent,' arise? This should not be so said... For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' arise? Yes. Feeling... perception... formations... For one who speaks the words, 'Consciousness is impermanent,' does the knowledge, 'Consciousness is impermanent,' arise? This should not be so said...

“Idaṃ [M 0.0330] dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Rūpaṃ anattā”ti vācaṃ bhāsato “rūpaṃ anattā”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… “idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. Vedanā [T 0.0484]… saññā… saṅkhārā… “viññāṇaṃ anattā”ti vācaṃ bhāsato “viññāṇaṃ anattā”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'Form is not-self,' does the knowledge, 'Form is not-self,' arise? This should not be so said... For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' arise? Yes. Feeling... perception... formations... For one who speaks the words, 'Consciousness is not-self,' does the knowledge, 'Consciousness is not-self,' arise? This should not be so said...

“Rūpaṃ [P 0.0455] anicca”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “rūpaṃ anicca”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… “viññāṇaṃ anicca”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “viññāṇaṃ anicca”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who speaks the words, 'Form is impermanent,' does the knowledge, 'Form is impermanent,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said... Feeling... perception... formations... For one who speaks the words, 'Consciousness is impermanent,' does the knowledge, 'Consciousness is impermanent,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said...

“Rūpaṃ anattā”ti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “rūpaṃ anattā”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… “viññāṇaṃ anattā”ti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “viññāṇaṃ anattā”ti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato na ca “dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For one who speaks the words, 'Form is not-self,' does the knowledge, 'Form is not-self,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said... Feeling... perception... formations... For one who speaks the words, 'Consciousness is not-self,' does the knowledge, 'Consciousness is not-self,' not arise? Yes. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'suffering,' not arise? This should not be so said...

620. “Idaṃ dukkha”nti vācaṃ bhāsato “idaṃ dukkha”nti ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Āmantā. “I”ti īti (syā. pī.) ca “da”nti ca “du”ti dūti (syā. pī.) ca “kha”nti ca ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

620. For one who speaks the words, 'This is suffering,' does the knowledge, 'This is suffering,' arise? Yes. And does the knowledge arise as 'i,' as 'daṃ,' as 'du,' and as 'kkhaṃ'? This should not be so said...

Idaṃ dukkhantikathā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the Discourse on 'This is Suffering'.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(112) 7. Iddhibalakathā

7. The Discourse on Psychic Power

621. Iddhibalena [T 0.0485][P 0.0456][V 0.0368] samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Iddhimayiko so āyu, iddhimayikā sā gati, iddhimayiko so attabhāvappaṭilābhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

621. Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Is that life-span made of psychic power, is that destiny made of psychic power, is that attainment of individual existence made of psychic power? This should not be so said...

Iddhibalena [M 0.0331] samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ kappaṃ tiṭṭheyya, anāgataṃ kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Dve kappe tiṭṭheyya, tayo kappe tiṭṭheyya, cattāro kappe tiṭṭheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Sati jīvite jīvitāvasese tiṭṭheyya, asati jīvite jīvitāvasese tiṭṭheyyāti? Sati jīvite jīvitāvasese tiṭṭheyyāti. Hañci sati jīvite jīvitāvasese tiṭṭheyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti. Asati jīvite jīvitāvasese tiṭṭheyyāti, mato tiṭṭheyya, kālaṅkato tiṭṭheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Could one remain for a past aeon, or for a future aeon? This should not be so said... Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Could one remain for two aeons, three aeons, or four aeons? This should not be so said... Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. While life exists, could one remain for the remainder of the life-span; or, when life does not exist, could one remain for the remainder of the life-span? While life exists, one could remain for the remainder of the life-span. If, while life exists, one could remain for the remainder of the life-span, then, good sir, it should not be said: 'One endowed with psychic power could remain for an aeon.' When life does not exist, could one remain for the remainder of the life-span? Could a dead person remain? Could one who has passed away remain? This should not be so said...

622. Iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Uppanno phasso mā nirujjhīti labbhā iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… uppannā vedanā…pe… uppannā saññā [T 0.0486] …pe… uppannā cetanā…pe… uppannaṃ cittaṃ… uppannā saddhā… uppannaṃ vīriyaṃ… uppannā sati… uppanno samādhi [P 0.0457] …pe… uppannā paññā mā nirujjhīti labbhā iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

622. Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that arisen contact may not cease? This should not be so said... Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that arisen feeling... arisen perception... arisen volition... arisen consciousness... arisen faith... arisen energy... arisen mindfulness... arisen concentration... arisen wisdom may not cease? This should not be so said...

Iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ niccaṃ hotūti labbhā iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ hotūti labbhā iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that form may be permanent? This should not be so said... Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that feeling... perception... formations... consciousness may be permanent? This should not be so said...

Iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Jātidhammā sattā mā jāyiṃsūti labbhā [V 0.0369] iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… jarādhammā sattā mā jīriṃsūti…pe… byādhidhammā sattā mā byādhiyiṃsūti…pe… maraṇadhammā sattā mā mīyiṃsūti labbhā iddhiyā paggahetunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that beings subject to birth may not be born? This should not be so said... Is it possible by psychic power to uphold it so that beings subject to aging may not age... beings subject to sickness may not fall sick... beings subject to death may not die? This should not be so said...

623. Na vattabbaṃ – “iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā”ti dī. ni. 2.166; saṃ. ni. 5.822; udā. 51! Attheva [M 0.0332] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti.

623. Should it not be said: “One endowed with psychic power could remain for an aeon”? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Ānanda, anyone who has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a basis of, established, practiced, and thoroughly undertaken the four bases of psychic power, could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon, should they wish”? Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, one endowed with psychic power could remain for an aeon.

624. Iddhibalena [T 0.0487] samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ natthi koci pāṭibhogo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṃ! Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Jarādhammo “mā jīrī”ti natthi koci pāṭibhogo [P 0.0458] samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṃ. Byādhidhammo “mā byādhiyī”ti…pe… maraṇadhammo “mā mīyī”ti…pe… yāni kho pana tāni pubbe katāni pāpakāni kammāni saṃkilesikāni ponobbhavikāni ponobhavikāni (sī. pī.) sadarāni nissārāni (sī. pī. ka.), dukkhudrayāni (syā.) dukkhavipākāni āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyāni tesaṃ vipāko “mā nibbattī”ti natthi koci pāṭibhogo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ natthi koci pāṭibhogo samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmi”nti a. ni. 4.182. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti.

624. Could one endowed with psychic power remain for an aeon? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Monks, for these four things, there is no guarantor—whether an ascetic, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, a Brahmā, or anyone in the world. What four? That a thing subject to aging should not age—for this, there is no guarantor in the world, whether an ascetic, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, or a Brahmā. That a thing subject to sickness should not sicken…pe… That a thing subject to death should not die…pe… That the result of past evil deeds—which are defiling, lead to renewed existence, are fraught with anxiety, result in suffering, and lead to future birth, aging, and death—should not arise; for this, there is no guarantor in the world, whether an ascetic, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, or a Brahmā. For these four things, monks, there is no guarantor in the world, whether an ascetic, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, or a Brahmā.” Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “One endowed with psychic power could remain for an aeon.”

Iddhibalakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Psychic Power is concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(113) 8. Samādhikathā

(113) 8. Discourse on Concentration

625. Cittasantati [T 0.0488] samādhīti? Āmantā. Atītā cittasantati samādhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0370] …pe… cittasantati samādhīti? Āmantā. Anāgatā cittasantati samādhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cittasantati samādhīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ niruddhaṃ anāgataṃ ajātanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ niruddhaṃ anāgataṃ ajātaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cittasantati samādhī”ti.

625. Is the continuity of mind concentration? Yes. Is the past continuity of mind concentration? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the continuity of mind concentration? Yes. Is the future continuity of mind concentration? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the continuity of mind concentration? Yes. But surely, is not what is past ceased, and what is future unborn? Yes. If what is past has ceased and what is future is unborn, then it should not be said: “The continuity of mind is concentration.”

626. Ekacittakkhaṇiko [M 0.0333] samādhīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī samāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotaviññāṇasamaṅgī…pe… ghānaviññāṇasamaṅgī… jivhāviññāṇasamaṅgī… kāyaviññāṇasamaṅgī…pe… akusalacittasamaṅgī [P 0.0459]…pe… rāgasahagatacittasamaṅgī…pe… dosasahagatacittasamaṅgī…pe… mohasahagatacittasamaṅgī…pe… anottappasahagatacittasamaṅgī samāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

626. Is concentration a single mind-moment? Yes. Is one endowed with eye-consciousness in a state of attainment? It should not be said thus…pe… Is one endowed with ear-consciousness…pe… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness…pe… unwholesome consciousness…pe… consciousness accompanied by greed…pe… consciousness accompanied by aversion…pe… consciousness accompanied by delusion…pe… consciousness accompanied by lack of moral shame in a state of attainment? It should not be said thus…pe…

Cittasantati samādhīti? Āmantā. Akusalacittasantati samādhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgasahagatā…pe… dosasahagatā…pe… mohasahagatā…pe… anottappasahagatā cittasantati samādhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the continuity of mind concentration? Yes. Is the continuity of unwholesome mind concentration? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the continuity of mind accompanied by lust…pe… accompanied by aversion…pe… accompanied by delusion…pe… accompanied by lack of moral shame concentration? It should not be said thus…pe…

Na vattabbaṃ – “cittasantati samādhī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ [T 0.0489] bhagavatā – “ahaṃ kho, āvuso nigaṇṭhā, pahomi aniñjamāno kāyena, abhāsamāno vācaṃ, satta rattindivāni rattidivāni (ka.) ekantasukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedī viharitu”nti ma. ni. 1.180! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi cittasantati samādhīti.

Should it not be said: “The continuity of mind is concentration”? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “I, friends Nigaṇṭhas, am able, without moving my body, without uttering speech, to dwell for seven days and nights experiencing exclusive bliss”? Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the continuity of mind is concentration.

Samādhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Concentration is concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter

(114) 9. Dhammaṭṭhitatākathā

(114) 9. Discourse on the Stability of Phenomena

627. Dhammaṭṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya tāyeva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā[V 0.0371], natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

627. Is the stability of phenomena perfected? Yes. Is the stability of that stability perfected? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the stability of that stability perfected? Yes. Is it by that very stability that there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus…pe…

Rūpassa [P 0.0460] ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya tāyeva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the stability of form perfected? Yes. Is the stability of that stability perfected? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the stability of that stability perfected? Yes. Is it by that very stability that there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus…pe…

Vedanāya [M 0.0334] ṭhitatā…pe… saññāya ṭhitatā…pe… saṅkhārānaṃ ṭhitatā…pe… viññāṇassa ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tāya ṭhitatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya [T 0.0490] tāyeva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the stability of feeling…pe… the stability of perception…pe… the stability of formations…pe… the stability of consciousness perfected? Yes. Is the stability of that stability perfected? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the stability of that stability perfected? Yes. Is it by that very stability that there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus…pe…

Dhammaṭṭhitatākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Stability of Phenomena is concluded.

11. Ekādasamavaggo

11. The Eleventh Chapter.

(115) 10. Aniccatākathā

(115) 10. Discourse on Impermanence

628. Aniccatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya aniccatāya aniccatā parinipphannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tāya aniccatāya aniccatā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya tāyeva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe.

628. Is impermanence perfected? Yes. Is the impermanence of that impermanence perfected? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the impermanence of that impermanence perfected? Yes. Is it by that very impermanence that there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus.

Jarā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya jarāya jarā parinipphannāti? Na [P 0.0461] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tāya jarāya jarā parinipphannāti? Āmantā. Tāya tāyeva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā[V 0.0372], natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is aging perfected? Yes. Is the aging of that aging perfected? It should not be said thus…pe… Is the aging of that aging perfected? Yes. Is it by that very aging that there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no final Nibbāna without clinging? It should not be said thus…pe…

Maraṇaṃ parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Tassa maraṇassa maraṇaṃ parinipphannanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tassa maraṇassa maraṇaṃ parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Tassa tasseva natthi dukkhassantakiriyā, natthi vaṭṭupacchedo, natthi anupādāparinibbānanti? Na [T 0.0491] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is death produced? Yes. Is the death of that death produced? It should not be said thus. Is the death of that death produced? Yes. For that very death, is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, no final Nibbāna without remainder? It should not be said thus...

629. Rūpaṃ parinipphannaṃ, rūpassa aniccatā atthīti? Āmantā. Aniccatā parinipphannā, aniccatāya aniccatā atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ parinipphannaṃ, rūpassa jarā atthīti? Āmantā. Jarā parinipphannā, jarāya jarā atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

629. Form is produced, and is there impermanence of form? Yes. Impermanence is produced, and is there impermanence of impermanence? It should not be said thus... Form is produced, and is there aging of form? Yes. Aging is produced, and is there aging of aging? It should not be said thus...

Rūpaṃ parinipphannaṃ, rūpassa bhedo atthi, antaradhānaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Maraṇaṃ parinipphannaṃ, maraṇassa bhedo atthi, antaradhānaṃ atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Form is produced, and is there a breaking up of form, a disappearance of form? Yes. Death is produced, and is there a breaking up of death, a disappearance of death? It should not be said thus...

Vedanā [M 0.0335]…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ parinipphannaṃ, viññāṇassa aniccatā atthīti? Āmantā. Aniccatā parinipphannā, aniccatāya aniccatā atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… viññāṇaṃ parinipphannaṃ, viññāṇassa jarā atthīti? Āmantā. Jarā parinipphannā, jarāya jarā atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is feeling… and so on… perception… formations… and so on… consciousness accomplished, and is there impermanence of consciousness? Yes. Is impermanence accomplished, and is there impermanence of impermanence? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is consciousness accomplished, and is there aging of consciousness? Yes. Is aging accomplished, and is there aging of aging? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Viññāṇaṃ [P 0.0462] parinipphannaṃ, viññāṇassa bhedo atthi, antaradhānaṃ atthīti? Āmantā. Maraṇaṃ parinipphannaṃ, maraṇassa bhedo atthi, antaradhānaṃ atthīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is consciousness accomplished, and is there breaking up and disappearance of consciousness? Yes. Is death accomplished, and is there breaking up and disappearance of death? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Aniccatākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Impermanence is concluded.

Ekādasamavaggo.

The Eleventh Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Anusayā [V 0.0373] abyākatā, ahetukā, cittavippayuttā, aññāṇe [T 0.0492] vigate ñāṇī, ñāṇaṃ cittavippayuttaṃ, yattha sadde yattha saddo (sī.), yathāsaddaṃ (?) ñāṇaṃ pavattati, iddhibalena samannāgato kappaṃ tiṭṭheyya, cittasantati samādhi, dhammaṭṭhitatā, aniccatāti.

Latent tendencies are indeterminate; they are rootless; they are dissociated from consciousness; one who has knowledge when ignorance has departed; knowledge is dissociated from consciousness; knowledge proceeds with regard to the word; one endowed with psychic power could remain for an eon; the continuity of consciousness is concentration; the stability of phenomena; impermanence.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(116) 1. Saṃvaro kammantikathā

(116) 1. The Discourse on Restraint as Kamma

630. Saṃvaro [P 0.0463] kammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotindriyasaṃvaro…pe… ghānindriyasaṃvaro…pe… jivhindriyasaṃvaro…pe… kāyindriyasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

630. Is restraint kamma? Yes. Is restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is restraint of the nose faculty… and so on… is restraint of the tongue faculty… and so on… is restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Kāyindriyasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāyindriyasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Sotindriyasaṃvaro…pe… ghānindriyasaṃvaro…pe… jivhindriyasaṃvaro jivhākammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manindriyasaṃvaro manokammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? Yes. Is restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? Yes. Is restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is restraint of the nose faculty… and so on… is restraint of the tongue faculty tongue-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Manindriyasaṃvaro manokammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manindriyasaṃvaro manokammanti? Āmantā. Sotindriyasaṃvaro [M 0.0336] …pe… ghānindriyasaṃvaro… jivhindriyasaṃvaro…pe… kāyindriyasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? Yes. Is restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? Yes. Is restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is restraint of the nose faculty… is restraint of the tongue faculty… and so on… is restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

631. Asaṃvaro kammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyaasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti[T 0.0493]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… ghānindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… jivhindriyaasaṃvaro… kāyindriyaasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Na [P 0.0464] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

631. Is non-restraint kamma? Yes. Is non-restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is non-restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the nose faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the tongue faculty… is non-restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Kāyindriyaasaṃvaro [V 0.0374] kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyaasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāyindriyaasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Āmantā. Sotindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… ghānindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… jivhindriyaasaṃvaro jivhākammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manindriyaasaṃvaro manokammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is non-restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? Yes. Is non-restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is non-restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? Yes. Is non-restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the nose faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the tongue faculty tongue-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is non-restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Manindriyaasaṃvaro manokammanti? Āmantā. Cakkhundriyaasaṃvaro cakkhukammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… manindriyaasaṃvaro manokammanti? Āmantā. Sotindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… ghānindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… jivhindriyaasaṃvaro…pe… kāyindriyaasaṃvaro kāyakammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is non-restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? Yes. Is non-restraint of the eye faculty eye-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is non-restraint of the mind faculty mind-kamma? Yes. Is non-restraint of the ear faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the nose faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the tongue faculty… and so on… is non-restraint of the body faculty body-kamma? It should not be said thus… and so on.

632. Na vattabbaṃ – “saṃvaropi asaṃvaropi kamma”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hoti, sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya nimittaggāhī hoti…pe… na nimittaggāhī hotī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi saṃvaropi asaṃvaropi kammanti.

632. Should it not be said, 'Both restraint and non-restraint are kamma'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having seen a form with the eye, grasps its signs… and so on… does not grasp its signs; having heard a sound with the ear… and so on… having cognized a mental object with the mind, grasps its signs… and so on… does not grasp its signs'? Is there indeed such a Suttanta? Yes. Therefore, both restraint and non-restraint are kamma.

Saṃvaro kammantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Restraint as Kamma is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(117) 2. Kammakathā

(117) 2. The Discourse on Kamma

633. Sabbaṃ [T 0.0494] kammaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Sabbā [P 0.0465] cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbā cetanā savipākāti? Āmantā. Vipākābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbā cetanā savipākāti[M 0.0337]? Āmantā. Kiriyābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

633. Is all kamma resultant? Yes. Is all volition resultant? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is all volition resultant? Yes. Is resultant-indeterminate volition resultant? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is all volition resultant? Yes. Is functional-indeterminate volition resultant? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sabbā [V 0.0375] cetanā savipākāti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacarā vipākābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbā cetanā savipākāti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacarā arūpāvacarā apariyāpannā vipākābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is all volition resultant? Yes. Is sense-sphere resultant-indeterminate volition resultant? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is all volition resultant? Yes. Is form-sphere, formless-sphere, and supramundane resultant-indeterminate volition resultant? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Sabbā cetanā savipākāti? Āmantā. Kāmāvacarā kiriyābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbā cetanā savipākāti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacarā arūpāvacarā kiriyābyākatā cetanā savipākāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is all volition with result? Yes. Is sense-sphere functional indeterminate volition with result? It should not be said thus… and so on…. Is all volition with result? Yes. Is form-sphere and formless-sphere functional indeterminate volition with result? It should not be said thus… and so on….

634. Vipākābyākatā cetanā avipākāti? Āmantā. Hañci vipākābyākatā cetanā avipākā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbā cetanā savipākā”ti.

634. Is resultant indeterminate volition without result? Yes. If resultant indeterminate volition is without result, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “all volition is with result.”

Kiriyābyākatā cetanā avipākāti? Āmantā. Hañci kiriyābyākatā cetanā avipākā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbā [T 0.0495] cetanā savipākā”ti.

Is functional indeterminate volition without result? Yes. If functional indeterminate volition is without result, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “all volition is with result.”

Kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā arūpāvacarā apariyāpannā vipākābyākatā cetanā avipākāti? Āmantā[P 0.0466]. Hañci apariyāpannā vipākābyākatā cetanā avipākā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbā cetanā savipākā”ti.

Is sense-sphere, form-sphere, formless-sphere, and unincluded resultant indeterminate volition without result? Yes. If unincluded resultant indeterminate volition is without result, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “all volition is with result.”

Kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā arūpāvacarā kiriyābyākatā cetanā avipākāti? Āmantā. Hañci arūpāvacarā kiriyābyākatā cetanā avipākā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbā cetanā savipākā”ti.

Is sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere functional indeterminate volition without result? Yes. If formless-sphere functional indeterminate volition is without result, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “all volition is with result.”

635. Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbaṃ kammaṃ savipāka”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃviditvā byantibhāvaṃ vadāmi, tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje upapajjaṃ (a. ni. 10.17) vā apare vā pariyāye”ti a. ni. 10.217! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi sabbaṃ kammaṃ savipākanti.

635. Should it not be said that “all kamma is with result”? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, I do not declare the cessation of intentional kammas, done and accumulated, without their being experienced, and that either in this very life, or in the next life, or in a subsequent life”? Is there not indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, all kamma is with result.

Kammakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Kamma is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter

(118) 3. Saddo vipākotikathā

(118) 3. Discussion on Sound as Result

636. Saddo [M 0.0338][V 0.0376] vipākoti? Āmantā. Sukhavedaniyo dukkhavedaniyo adukkhamasukhavedaniyo, sukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayutto[T 0.0496], adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayutto, phassena sampayutto, vedanāya sampayutto, saññāya sampayutto, cetanāya sampayutto, cittena sampayutto, sārammaṇo; atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā ābhogo samannāhāro manasikāro cetanā patthanā paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyo na dukkhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0467] na sukhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saddo vipāko”ti.

636. Is sound a result? Yes. Is it to be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful, to be experienced as neither-pleasant-nor-painful? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-pleasant-nor-painful feeling? Is it associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with volition, associated with consciousness, having an object? Is there for it turning, directing the mind, application, attention, volition, wish, or resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on… But is it not the case that it is not to be experienced as pleasant, not to be experienced as painful… and so on… is without an object, and that there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it? Yes. If it is not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is without an object, and there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “sound is a result.”

Phasso vipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Saddo vipāko, saddo sukhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact a result, and is contact to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… having an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… resolve? Yes. Is sound a result, and is sound to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… having an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Saddo vipāko, saddo na sukhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Phasso vipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo, na dukkhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is sound a result, and is sound not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is it without an object, and is there no turning… and so on… or resolve for it? Yes. Is contact a result, and is contact not to be experienced as pleasant, not to be experienced as painful… and so on… is it without an object, and is there no turning… and so on… or resolve for it? It should not be said thus… and so on….

637. Na vattabbaṃ – “saddo vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so tassa kammassa katattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā brahmassaro hoti karavikabhāṇī”ti dīghanikāye! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[T 0.0497]. Tena hi saddo vipākoti.

637. Should it not be said that “sound is a result”? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Because of that kamma being done, accumulated, abundant, and vast, he has a voice like Brahmā, speaking like the karavīka bird”? Is there not indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, sound is a result.

Saddo vipākotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Sound as Result is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter

(119) 4. Saḷāyatanakathā

(119) 4. Discussion on the Six Sense-Bases

638. Cakkhāyatanaṃ [M 0.0339][V 0.0377] vipākoti? Āmantā. Sukhavedaniyaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0468] na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhāyatanaṃ vipāko”ti…pe….

638. Is the eye-base a result? Yes. Is it to be experienced as pleasant, to be experienced as painful… and so on… with an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… a resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not the case that it is not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is without an object, and that there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it? Yes. If it is not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is without an object, and there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “the eye-base is a result”… and so on….

Phasso vipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ vipāko, cakkhāyatanaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact a result, and is contact to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… with an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… a resolve? Yes. Is the eye-base a result, and is the eye-base to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… with an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… a resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Cakkhāyatanaṃ vipāko, cakkhāyatanaṃ na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Phasso vipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the eye-base a result, and is the eye-base not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is it without an object, and is there no turning… and so on… no resolve for it? Yes. Is contact a result, and is contact not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is it without an object, and is there no turning… and so on… no resolve for it? It should not be said thus… and so on….

639. Sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ [T 0.0498] vipākoti? Āmantā. Sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kāyāyatanaṃ vipāko”ti.

639. Is the ear-base… and so on… the nose-base… and so on… the tongue-base… and so on… the body-base a result? Yes. Is it to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… with an object? Is there for it turning… and so on… a resolve? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not the case that it is not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is without an object, and that there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it? Yes. If it is not to be experienced as pleasant… and so on… is without an object, and there is no turning… and so on… no resolve for it, then indeed, O good sir, it should not be said that “the body-base is a result.”

Phasso vipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Kāyāyatanaṃ vipāko, kāyāyatanaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0378] …pe… kāyāyatanaṃ vipāko, kāyāyatanaṃ na sukhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0469]. Phasso vipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact a resultant? Is contact accompanied by pleasant feeling… with an object? Does it have adverting… aspiration? Yes. Is the body-base a resultant? Is the body-base accompanied by pleasant feeling… with an object? Does it have adverting… aspiration? It should not be said thus… Is the body-base a resultant, and is the body-base not accompanied by pleasant feeling… without an object, and does it not have adverting… aspiration? Yes. Is contact a resultant, and is contact not accompanied by pleasant feeling… without an object, and does it not have adverting… aspiration? It should not be said thus…

640. Na [M 0.0340] vattabbaṃ – “saḷāyatanaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu saḷāyatanaṃ kammassa katattā uppannanti? Āmantā. Hañci saḷāyatanaṃ kammassa katattā uppannaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “saḷāyatanaṃ vipāko”ti.

640. Should it not be said: ‘The six sense-bases are a resultant’? Yes. Is it not the case that the six sense-bases have arisen because kamma was done? Yes. If the six sense-bases have arisen because kamma was done, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘The six sense-bases are a resultant.’

Saḷāyatanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Six Sense-Bases is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(120) 5. Sattakkhattuparamakathā

(120) 5. The Discussion on One with a Maximum of Seven Rebirths

641. Sattakkhattuparamo [T 0.0499] puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Mātā jīvitā voropitā… pitā jīvitā voropito… arahā jīvitā voropito… duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditaṃ… saṅgho bhinnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

641. Is a person with a maximum of seven rebirths fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. Has his mother been deprived of life… his father been deprived of life… an Arahant been deprived of life… with a malevolent mind, has the blood of the Tathāgata been shed… has the Saṅgha been split? It should not be said thus…

Sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Abhabbo antarā dhammaṃ abhisametunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Abhabbo antarā dhammaṃ abhisametunti? Āmantā. Mātā jīvitā voropitā… pitā jīvitā voropito… arahā jīvitā voropito… duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditaṃ… saṅgho bhinnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a person with a maximum of seven rebirths fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. Is he incapable of realizing the Dhamma in the interval? It should not be said thus… Is he incapable of realizing the Dhamma in the interval? Yes. Has his mother been deprived of life… his father been deprived of life… an Arahant been deprived of life… with a malevolent mind, has the blood of the Tathāgata been shed… has the Saṅgha been split? It should not be said thus…

642. Sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Atthi so niyamo [V 0.0379] yena niyamena sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi [P 0.0470] te satipaṭṭhānā…pe… sammappadhānā… iddhipādā… indriyā… balā… bojjhaṅgā yehi bojjhaṅgehi sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

642. Is a person with a maximum of seven rebirths fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. Is there that path by which a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state? It should not be said thus… Are there those foundations of mindfulness… right strivings… bases of spiritual power… faculties… powers… factors of enlightenment, by which factors of enlightenment a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state? It should not be said thus…

643. Natthi so niyamo yena niyamena sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi so [T 0.0500] niyamo yena niyamena sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato”ti.

643. Is there not that path by which a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state? Yes. If there is not that path by which a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state, then indeed, sir, it should not be said: ‘A person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state.’

Natthi [M 0.0341] te satipaṭṭhānā… bojjhaṅgā yehi bojjhaṅgehi sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi te bojjhaṅgā yehi bojjhaṅgehi sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato”ti.

Are there not those foundations of mindfulness… factors of enlightenment, by which factors of enlightenment a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state? Yes. If there are not those factors of enlightenment by which a person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state, then indeed, sir, it should not be said: ‘A person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state.’

644. Sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Sakadāgāminiyamenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgāminiyamenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattaniyamenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

644. Is a person with a maximum of seven rebirths fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. Is it by the path of a once-returner? It should not be said thus… Is it by the path of a non-returner? It should not be said thus… Is it by the path of Arahantship? It should not be said thus…

Katamena niyamenāti? Sotāpattiniyamenāti. Sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyatoti? Āmantā. Ye keci sotāpattiniyāmaṃ okkamanti, sabbe te sattakkhattuparamatāniyatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

By which path? By the path of stream-entry. Is a person with a maximum of seven rebirths fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. All those who enter upon the path of stream-entry, are they all fixed in the state of having a maximum of seven rebirths? It should not be said thus…

645. Na vattabbaṃ – “sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0471]. Nanu so sattakkhattuparamoti? Āmantā. Hañci so sattakkhattuparamo, tena vata re vattabbe – “sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato”ti.

645. Should it not be said: ‘A person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths’? Yes. Is that person not one with a maximum of seven rebirths? Yes. If that person is one with a maximum of seven rebirths, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘A person with a maximum of seven rebirths is fixed in that state of having a maximum of seven rebirths.’

Sattakkhattuparamakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on One with a Maximum of Seven Rebirths is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(121) 6. Kolaṅkolakathā

(121) 6. The Discussion on the Kolaṅkola

646. Na [T 0.0501][V 0.0380] vattabbaṃ – “kolaṅkolo puggalo kolaṅkolatāniyato”ti? Āmantā. Nanu so kolaṅkoloti? Āmantā. Hañci so kolaṅkolo, tena vata re vattabbe – “kolaṅkolo puggalo kolaṅkolatāniyato”ti.

646. Should it not be said: ‘A kolaṅkola person is fixed in the state of a kolaṅkola’? Yes. Is he not a kolaṅkola? Yes. If he is a kolaṅkola, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘A kolaṅkola person is fixed in the state of a kolaṅkola’.

Kolaṅkolakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Kolaṅkola is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(122) 7. Ekabījīkathā

(122) 7. The Discussion on the Ekabījī

647. Na [M 0.0342] vattabbaṃ – “ekabījī puggalo ekabījitāniyato”ti? Āmantā. Nanu so ekabījīti? Āmantā. Hañci so ekabījī, tena vata re vattabbe – “ekabījī puggalo ekabījitāniyato”ti.

647. Should it not be said: ‘An ekabījī person is fixed in the state of an ekabījī’? Yes. Is he not an ekabījī? Yes. If he is an ekabījī, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘An ekabījī person is fixed in the state of an ekabījī’.

Ekabījīkathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Ekabījī is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Chapter.

(123) 8. Jīvitā voropanakathā

(123) 8. The Discussion on Depriving of Life

648. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyāti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya…pe… pitaraṃ jīvitā voropeyya [V 0.0381] …pe… arahantaṃ jīvitā voropeyya…pe… duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppādeyya…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindeyyāti? Na [P 0.0472] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

648. Would a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. Would a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive his mother of life… his father of life… an Arahant of life… with a malevolent mind, shed the Tathāgata’s blood… or split the Saṅgha? It should not be said thus…

Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyāti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo satthari agāravoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… sikkhāya [T 0.0502] agāravoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Would a person endowed with right view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. Is a person endowed with right view disrespectful towards the Teacher? It should not be said thus… towards the Dhamma… towards the Saṅgha… towards the training? It should not be said thus…

Nanu diṭṭhisampanno puggalo satthari sagāravoti? Āmantā. Hañci diṭṭhisampanno puggalo satthari sagāravo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyā”ti. Nanu diṭṭhisampanno puggalo dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… sikkhāya sagāravoti? Āmantā. Hañci diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sikkhāya sagāravo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyā”ti.

Is not a person accomplished in view respectful towards the Teacher? Yes. If a person accomplished in view is respectful towards the Teacher, then indeed, O opponent, it should not be said: 'A person accomplished in view would intentionally deprive a living being of life.' Is not a person accomplished in view respectful towards the Dhamma… towards the Saṅgha… towards the training? Yes. If a person accomplished in view is respectful towards the training, then indeed, O opponent, it should not be said: 'A person accomplished in view would intentionally deprive a living being of life.'

649. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo satthari agāravoti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo buddhathūpe ohadeyya omutteyya niṭṭhubheyya buddhathūpe apabyāmato asabyākato (sī. ka.) kareyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

649. Is a person accomplished in view disrespectful towards the Teacher? Yes. Would a person accomplished in view defecate, urinate, or spit at a Buddha stūpa, or treat a Buddha stūpa with contempt? It should not be said thus…

Diṭṭhisampanno [M 0.0343] puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamuddo ṭhitadhammo velaṃ nātivattati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ mayā sāvakānaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattaṃ taṃ mama sāvakā jīvitahetupi nātikkamantī”ti cūḷava. 385; a. ni. 8.20; udā. 45! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0473]. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyyā”ti.

Would a person accomplished in view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Just as, monks, the great ocean has a fixed nature and does not transgress its shore; so too, monks, whatever training rule has been laid down by me for my disciples, my disciples do not transgress it even for the sake of life'? Is there such a Suttanta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'A person accomplished in view would intentionally deprive a living being of life.'
