Jīvitā voropanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Depriving of Life is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Section

(124) 9. Duggatikathā

(124) 9. Discussion on Unhappy Destinations

650. Diṭṭhisampannassa [T 0.0503][V 0.0382] puggalassa pahīnā duggatīti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike rūpe rajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike rūpe rajjeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatī”ti.

650. For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned? Yes. Would a person accomplished in view be attracted to forms in the states of woe? Yes. If a person accomplished in view were to be attracted to forms in the states of woe, then indeed it should not be said: “For a person accomplished in view, unhappy destinations are abandoned.”

Diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatīti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike sadde…pe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe…pe… amanussitthiyā tiracchānagatitthiyā nāgakaññāya methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, ajeḷakaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, hatthigavassavaḷavaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya… tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ … kapiñjalaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) paṭiggaṇheyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci diṭṭhisampanno puggalo tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatī”ti.

For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned? Yes. Would a person accomplished in view be attracted to sounds in the states of woe… smells… tastes… tactile objects… or engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal, or a nāga maiden; or accept goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares… partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl? Yes. If a person accomplished in view were to accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl, then indeed it should not be said: “For a person accomplished in view, unhappy destinations are abandoned.”

651. Diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggati, diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike rūpe rajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Arahato pahīnā duggati, arahā āpāyike rūpe rajjeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggati, diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe…pe… tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyyāti? Āmantā[T 0.0504][P 0.0474]. Arahato [M 0.0344] pahīnā duggati, arahā tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

651. For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would a person accomplished in view be attracted to forms in the states of woe? Yes. For an arahant, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would an arahant be attracted to forms in the states of woe? That should not be said… For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would a person accomplished in view be attracted to sounds in the states of woe… smells… tastes… tactile objects… or accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl? Yes. For an arahant, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would an arahant accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl? That should not be said…

Arahato pahīnā duggati, na ca arahā āpāyike rūpe rajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggati, na ca diṭṭhisampanno puggalo āpāyike rūpe rajjeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahato pahīnā duggati, na ca arahā āpāyike sadde…pe… gandhe…pe… rase…pe… phoṭṭhabbe…pe… amanussitthiyā tiracchānagatitthiyā nāgakaññāya methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya, ajeḷakaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, kukkuṭasūkaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, hatthigavassavaḷavaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya…pe… tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyyāti? Āmantā[V 0.0383]. Diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggati, na ca diṭṭhisampanno puggalo tittiravaṭṭakamorakapiñjaraṃ paṭiggaṇheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

For an arahant, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would an arahant not be attracted to forms in the states of woe? Yes. For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would a person accomplished in view not be attracted to forms in the states of woe? That should not be said… For an arahant, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would an arahant not be attracted to sounds in the states of woe… smells… tastes… tactile objects… nor engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal, or a nāga maiden; nor accept goats and sheep, chickens and pigs, elephants, cattle, horses, and mares… nor partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl? Yes. For a person accomplished in view, are unhappy destinations abandoned, and would a person accomplished in view not accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and jungle fowl? That should not be said…

652. aṭṭhakathānulomaṃ paravādīpucchālakkhaṇaṃ. tathāpāyaṃ pucchā sakavādissa, purimāyo ca imissaṃ duggatikathāyaṃ paravādissāti gahetabbā viya dissanti Na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatī”ti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhisampanno puggalo nirayaṃ upapajjeyya…pe… tiracchānayoniṃ upapajjeyya… pettivisayaṃ upapajjeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatīti.

652. Should it not be said: “For a person accomplished in view, unhappy destinations are abandoned”? Yes. Could a person accomplished in view be reborn in hell… or be reborn in the animal realm… or be reborn in the realm of petas? That should not be said. Therefore, for a person accomplished in view, unhappy destinations are abandoned.

Duggatikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Unhappy Destinations is concluded.

12. Dvādasamavaggo

12. The Twelfth Section

(125) 10. Sattamabhavikakathā

(125) 10. Discussion on the Person of the Seventh Existence

653. Na [T 0.0505][P 0.0475] vattabbaṃ “sattamabhavikassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatī”ti? Āmantā. Sattamabhaviko puggalo nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, tiracchānayoniṃ upapajjeyya, pettivisayaṃ upapajjeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi sattamabhavikassa puggalassa pahīnā duggatīti.

653. Should it not be said, 'For a person of the seventh existence, the woeful states are abandoned'? Yes. Could a person of the seventh existence be reborn in hell, be reborn in the animal realm, or be reborn in the realm of the petas? It should not be said thus. Therefore, for a person of the seventh existence, the woeful states are abandoned.

Sattamabhavikakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Person of the Seventh Existence is concluded.

Dvādasamavaggo.

The Twelfth Section.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Recapitulation:

Saṃvaro [M 0.0345] kammaṃ tatheva asaṃvaro, sabbakammaṃ savipākaṃ, saddo vipāko, saḷāyatanaṃ vipāko, sattakkhattuparamo puggalo sattakkhattuparamatāniyato, kolaṅkolapuggalo kolaṅkolatāniyato, ekabījī puggalo ekabījitāniyato, diṭṭhisampanno puggalo sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropeyya, diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa pahīnā duggati, tatheva sattamabhavikassāti.

Restraint is kamma, and likewise non-restraint; all kamma has a result; sound is a result; the six sense bases are a result; a person limited to seven rebirths is fixed in being limited to seven rebirths at most; a Kolaṅkola person is fixed in the Kolaṅkola state; a one-seed person is fixed in the one-seed state; a person accomplished in view might intentionally deprive a living being of life; for a person accomplished in view, the woeful states are abandoned; and likewise for the person of the seventh existence.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Section

(126) 1. Kappaṭṭhakathā

(126) 1. Discussion on One Who Stands for an Aeon

654. Kappaṭṭho [P 0.0476][V 0.0384] kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappo ca saṇṭhāti buddho ca loke uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Kappaṭṭho [T 0.0506] kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappo ca saṇṭhāti saṅgho ca bhijjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappo ca saṇṭhāti kappaṭṭho ca kappaṭṭhiyaṃ kammaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappo ca saṇṭhāti kappaṭṭho ca puggalo kālaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

654. Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. And would the aeon endure, and a Buddha arise in the world? This should not be said so… Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. And would the aeon endure, and the Sangha split? This should not be said so… Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. And would the aeon endure, and one who stands for an aeon perform the kamma for standing for an aeon? This should not be said so… Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. And would the aeon endure, and the person who stands for an aeon pass away? This should not be said so…

655. Kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Atītaṃ kappaṃ tiṭṭheyya, anāgataṃ kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Dve kappe tiṭṭheyya… tayo kappe tiṭṭheyya… cattāro kappe tiṭṭheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

655. Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. Would they last for a past aeon, or would they last for a future aeon? This should not be said so… Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. Would they last for two aeons… three aeons… four aeons? This should not be said so…

656. Kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappaṭṭho kappe ḍayhante kattha gacchatīti? Aññaṃ lokadhātuṃ gacchatīti. Mato gacchati, vehāsaṃ gacchatīti? Mato gacchatīti. Kappaṭṭhiyaṃ kammaṃ aparāpariyavepakkanti? Na [P 0.0477] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vehāsaṃ gacchatīti (?) ayaṃ hi paravādissa paṭiññāyeva, kathā. 621-623 navamapantiyaṃ viya vehāsaṃ gacchatīti? Āmantā vehāsaṃ gacchatīti (?) ayaṃ hi paravādissa paṭiññāyeva, kathā. 621-623 navamapantiyaṃ viya. Kappaṭṭho iddhimāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kappaṭṭho iddhimāti? Āmantā. Kappaṭṭhena [M 0.0346] chandiddhipādo bhāvito vīriyiddhipādo bhāvito cittiddhipādo bhāvito vīmaṃsiddhipādo bhāvitoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

656. Would one who stands for an aeon last for an aeon? Yes. When the aeon is burning, where do they go? They go to another world-system. Do they go when dead, or do they go through the sky? They go when dead. Is the kamma for standing for an aeon one whose result is experienced in a subsequent life? This should not be said so… Do they go through the sky? Yes. Is one who stands for an aeon endowed with psychic power? This should not be said so… Is one who stands for an aeon endowed with psychic power? Yes. Has one who stands for an aeon developed the basis of psychic power of zeal… the basis of psychic power of energy… the basis of psychic power of mind… the basis of psychic power of investigation? This should not be said so…

657. Na vattabbaṃ – “kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

657. Should it not be said, 'One who stands for an aeon would last for an aeon'? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Āpāyiko [T 0.0507] nerayiko, kappaṭṭho saṅghabhedako;

Vaggarato adhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā padhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ bhetvāna bhinditvā (sī. ka.), kappaṃ nirayamhi paccatī”ti cūḷava. 354; a. ni. 10.39; itivu. 18.

‘One who belongs to the states of deprivation, a hell-dweller, staying for an eon, a schismatic of the Sangha; delighting in factions, established in what is not Dhamma, he falls away from security from the bonds. Having split the united Sangha, he is boiled in hell for an eon.’

Attheva [V 0.0385] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi kappaṭṭho kappaṃ tiṭṭheyyāti.

Is there indeed such a Suttanta? Yes. Therefore, one who stands for an aeon would last for an aeon.

Kappaṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on One Who Stands for an Aeon is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(127) 2. Kusalapaṭilābhakathā

13. (127) 2. Discourse on the Acquisition of the Wholesome

658. Kappaṭṭho kusalaṃ cittaṃ na paṭilabheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappaṭṭho dānaṃ dadeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci kappaṭṭho dānaṃ dadeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kappaṭṭho kusalaṃ cittaṃ na paṭilabheyyā”ti.

Would one established in the aeon not acquire a wholesome mind? Yes. Would one established in the aeon give a gift? Yes. If one established in the aeon were to give a gift, then it should not indeed be said, 'One established in the aeon would not acquire a wholesome mind.'

Kappaṭṭho kusalaṃ cittaṃ na paṭilabheyyāti? Āmantā. Kappaṭṭho cīvaraṃ dadeyya…pe… piṇḍapātaṃ dadeyya…pe… senāsanaṃ dadeyya…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyya [P 0.0478]… khādanīyaṃ dadeyya… bhojanīyaṃ dadeyya… pānīyaṃ dadeyya… cetiyaṃ vandeyya… cetiye mālaṃ āropeyya… gandhaṃ āropeyya… vilepanaṃ āropeyya…pe… cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ (pī.) kareyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci kappaṭṭho cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ kareyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kappaṭṭho kusalaṃ cittaṃ na paṭilabheyyā”ti…pe….

658. Would one established in the aeon not acquire a wholesome mind? Yes. Would one established in the aeon give a robe... give almsfood... give lodging... give requisites of medicine for the sick... give hard food... give soft food... give drinks... pay homage to a shrine... offer flowers at a shrine... offer incense... offer fragrant paste... respectfully circumambulate a shrine? Yes. If one established in the aeon were to respectfully circumambulate a shrine, then it should not indeed be said, 'One established in the aeon would not acquire a wholesome mind.'

659. Kappaṭṭho [T 0.0508][M 0.0347] kusalaṃ cittaṃ paṭilabheyyāti? Āmantā. Tato vuṭṭhānaṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ paṭilabheyyāti? Āmantā. Rūpāvacaraṃ…pe… arūpāvacaraṃ…pe… lokuttaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ paṭilabheyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Would one established in the aeon obtain a wholesome mind? Yes. Would one obtain a wholesome mind that is an emergence from that? Yes. Would one obtain a wholesome mind that is of the fine-material sphere... of the immaterial sphere... that is supramundane? This should not be said so…

Kusalapaṭilābhakathā niṭṭhitā.

659. The Discourse on the Acquisition of the Wholesome is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(128) 3. Anantarāpayuttakathā

(128) 3. Discourse on One Connected with an Immediately Effective Kamma

660. Anantarāpayutto [V 0.0386] puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyyāti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyāmañca sammattaniyāmañca ubho okkameyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anantarāpayutto puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyyāti? Āmantā. Nanu taṃ kammaṃ payuttaṃ kukkuccaṃ uppāditaṃ vippaṭisāriyaṃ janitanti? Āmantā. Hañci taṃ kammaṃ payuttaṃ kukkuccaṃ uppāditaṃ vippaṭisāriyaṃ janitaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anantarāpayutto puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyyā”ti.

13. Would a person connected with an immediately effective kamma enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Would one enter both the fixed course of wrongness and the fixed course of rightness? This should not be said so… Would a person connected with an immediately effective kamma enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Surely that kamma was engaged in, remorse was produced, and regret was generated? Yes. If that kamma was engaged in, remorse was produced, and regret was generated, then it should not indeed be said, 'A person connected with an immediately effective kamma would enter the fixed course of rightness.'

661. Anantarāpayutto [P 0.0479] puggalo abhabbo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamitunti? Āmantā. Mātā jīvitā voropitā… pitā jīvitā voropito… arahā jīvitā voropito… duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditaṃ… saṅgho bhinnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is a person connected with an immediately effective kamma incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Has a mother been deprived of life... a father been deprived of life... an arahant been deprived of life... has the blood of the Tathāgata been shed with a corrupt mind... has the Saṅgha been split? This should not be said so…

Anantarāpayutto puggalo taṃ kammaṃ paṭisaṃharitvā kukkuccaṃ paṭivinodetvā vippaṭisāriyaṃ [T 0.0509] paṭivinetvā paṭivinodetvā (sī. pī. ka.) abhabbo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamitunti? Āmantā. Mātā jīvitā voropitā… pitā jīvitā voropito…pe… saṅgho bhinnoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

660. Having withdrawn that kamma, dispelled remorse, and removed regret, is a person connected with an immediately effective kamma incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Has a mother been deprived of life... a father been deprived of life... has the Saṅgha been split? This should not be said so…

Anantarāpayutto puggalo taṃ kammaṃ paṭisaṃharitvā kukkuccaṃ paṭivinodetvā vippaṭisāriyaṃ paṭivinetvā abhabbo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamitunti? Āmantā. Nanu taṃ kammaṃ paṭisaṃhaṭaṃ kukkuccaṃ paṭivinoditaṃ vippaṭisāriyaṃ paṭivinītanti? Āmantā. Hañci taṃ kammaṃ paṭisaṃhaṭaṃ kukkuccaṃ paṭivinoditaṃ vippaṭisāriyaṃ [M 0.0348] paṭivinītaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anantarāpayutto puggalo taṃ kammaṃ paṭisaṃharitvā kukkuccaṃ paṭivinodetvā vippaṭisāriyaṃ paṭivinetvā abhabbo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamitu”nti.

661. Having withdrawn that kamma, dispelled remorse, and removed regret, is a person connected with an immediately effective kamma incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Surely that kamma was withdrawn, remorse dispelled, and regret removed? Yes. If that kamma was withdrawn, remorse dispelled, and regret removed, then it should not indeed be said, 'A person connected with an immediately effective kamma, having withdrawn that kamma, dispelled remorse, and removed regret, is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness.'

662. Anantarāpayutto puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyyāti? Āmantā. Nanu taṃ kammaṃ [V 0.0387] payutto āsīti? Āmantā. Hañci taṃ kammaṃ payutto āsi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anantarāpayutto puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyyā”ti.

662. Would a person connected with an immediately effective kamma enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Surely one was connected with that kamma? Yes. If one was connected with that kamma, then it should not indeed be said, 'A person connected with an immediately effective kamma would enter the fixed course of rightness.'

Anantarāpayuttakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on One Connected with an Immediately Effective Kamma is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Section

(129) 4. Niyatassa niyāmakathā

(129) 4. Discourse on the Fixed Course of the Fixed Person

663. Niyato [P 0.0480] niyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyato sammattaniyāmaṃ okkamati, sammattaniyato micchattaniyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Na [T 0.0510] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

663. Does one who is fixed enter the fixed course? Yes. Does one fixed in wrongness enter the fixed course of rightness, and one fixed in rightness enter the fixed course of wrongness? That should not be said...

Niyato niyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Āmantā. Pubbe maggaṃ bhāvetvā pacchā niyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pubbe sotāpattimaggaṃ bhāvetvā pacchā sotāpattiniyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pubbe sakadāgāmi…pe… anāgāmi…pe… arahattamaggaṃ bhāvetvā pacchā arahattaniyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who is fixed enter the fixed course? Yes. Having first developed the path, does one afterward enter the fixed course? That should not be said... Having first developed the path of stream-entry, does one afterward enter the fixed course of stream-entry? That should not be said... Having first developed the path of once-returning... non-returning... arahantship, does one afterward enter the fixed course of arahantship? That should not be said...

Pubbe satipaṭṭhānaṃ…pe… sammappadhānaṃ… iddhipādaṃ… indriyaṃ… balaṃ… bojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetvā pacchā niyāmaṃ okkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one first develop the establishments of mindfulness... the right exertions... the bases of spiritual power... the faculties... the powers... the factors of enlightenment and afterward enter the fixed course? That should not be said...

664. Na vattabbaṃ – “niyato niyāmaṃ okkamatī”ti? Āmantā. Bhabbo bodhisatto tāya jātiyā dhammaṃ nābhisametunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi niyato niyāmaṃ okkamatīti.

664. Should it not be said, 'One who is fixed enters the fixed course'? Yes. Is it possible that the Bodhisatta in that birth would not awaken to the Dhamma? That should not be said. Therefore, one who is fixed enters the fixed course.

Niyatassa niyāmakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Fixed Course of the Fixed Person is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Section

(130) 5. Nivutakathā

(130) 5. Discourse on Being Covered

665. Nivuto [M 0.0349][V 0.0388] nīvaraṇaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Ratto rāgaṃ jahati, duṭṭho dosaṃ jahati, mūḷho mohaṃ jahati, kiliṭṭho kilese jahatīti? Na [P 0.0481] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgena rāgaṃ jahati, dosena dosaṃ jahati, mohena mohaṃ jahati, kilesehi kilese jahatīti[T 0.0511]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

665. Does one who is covered abandon the hindrances? Yes. Does one who is lustful abandon lust, one who is hateful abandon hate, one who is deluded abandon delusion, one who is defiled abandon the defilements? That should not be said... Does one abandon lust with lust, hate with hate, delusion with delusion, the defilements with defilements? That should not be said...

Rāgo cittasampayutto, maggo cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgo akusalo, maggo kusaloti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is lust associated with the mind, and the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a conjunction of two contacts... of two minds? That should not be said... Is lust unwholesome, and the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright counterpart states come face to face? That should not be said...

666. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā…pe… sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

666. Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright counterpart states come face to face? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, these four things are very far apart. What four? The sky and the earth—this is the first very far apart... Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from the unrighteous.' Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'Wholesome and unwholesome states... come face to face.'

Nivuto nīvaraṇaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmetī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “nivuto nīvaraṇaṃ jahatī”ti…pe….

Does one who is covered abandon the hindrances? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, unblemished, free from defilements, pliant, workable, steady, and unshaken, he directs it to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.' Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'One who is covered abandons the hindrances'...

667. Na vattabbaṃ – “nivuto nīvaraṇaṃ jahatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato [P 0.0482] kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati…pe… avijjāsavāpi [V 0.0389] cittaṃ vimuccatī”ti! Attheva suttantoti[T 0.0512]? Āmantā. Tena hi nivuto nīvaraṇaṃ jahatīti.

667. Should it not be said, 'One who is covered abandons the hindrances'? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'When he knows thus and sees thus, his mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire... his mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance.' Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, one who is covered abandons the hindrances.

Nivutakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Being Covered is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Section

(131) 6. Sammukhībhūtakathā

(131) 6. Discourse on One Who is Confronted

668. Sammukhībhūto [M 0.0350] saṃyojanaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Ratto rāgaṃ jahati, duṭṭho dosaṃ jahati, mūḷho mohaṃ jahati, kiliṭṭho kilese jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgena rāgaṃ jahati, dosena dosaṃ jahati, mohena mohaṃ jahati, kilesehi kilese jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

668. Does one who is confronted abandon a fetter? Yes. Does one who is lustful abandon lust, one who is hateful abandon hatred, one who is deluded abandon delusion, one who is defiled abandon defilements? That should not be said… Does one abandon lust with lust, hatred with hatred, delusion with delusion, defilements with defilements? That should not be said…

Rāgo cittasampayutto, maggo cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgo akusalo, maggo kusaloti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is lust associated with the mind, and is the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a conjunction of two contacts… of two minds? That should not be said… Is lust unwholesome, and is the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, states with dark and bright counterparts, come to be present? That should not be said…

669. Kusalākusalā…pe… sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā…pe… sammukhībhāvaṃ [T 0.0513] āgacchantī”ti.

669. Do wholesome and unwholesome states… come to be present? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, these four are very far apart. What four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first that is very far apart… Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from the unrighteous.' Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'Wholesome and unwholesome states… come to be present.'

Sammukhībhūto [P 0.0483] saṃyojanaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so evaṃ samāhite [V 0.0390] citte…pe… āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmetī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “sammukhībhūto saṃyojanaṃ jahatī”ti.

Does one who is confronted abandon a fetter? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'With the mind thus concentrated… he inclines the mind toward the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.' Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'One who is confronted abandons a fetter.'

670. Na vattabbaṃ – “sammukhībhūto saṃyojanaṃ jahatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati…pe… avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccatī”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi sammukhībhūto saṃyojanaṃ jahatīti.

670. Should it not be said: “One who is face to face with a fetter abandons it”? Yes, it should not be said. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Of one who knows thus and sees thus, the mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire… the mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance.” Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, one who is face to face with a fetter abandons it.

Sammukhībhūtakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Being Face to Face is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(132) 7. Samāpanno assādetikathā

7. Discussion on One Who Attains a Meditative State and Relishes It

671. Samāpanno [M 0.0351] assādeti, jhānanikanti jhānārammaṇāti? Āmantā. Taṃ jhānaṃ tassa jhānassa ārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… taṃ jhānaṃ tassa jhānassa ārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Tena phassena taṃ phassaṃ phusati, tāya vedanāya taṃ vedanaṃ vedeti, tāya saññāya taṃ saññaṃ sañjānāti, tāya cetanāya taṃ cetanaṃ ceteti, tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ cinteti, tena vitakkena taṃ vitakkaṃ vitakketi, tena vicārena taṃ vicāraṃ vicāreti[T 0.0514], tāya pītiyā taṃ pīti piyāyati, tāya satiyā taṃ satiṃ sarati, tāya paññāya taṃ paññaṃ pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

671. One who has attained a meditative state relishes it; does the delight in jhāna have jhāna as its object? Yes. Is that jhāna the object of that jhāna? This should not be said… Is that jhāna the object of that jhāna? Yes. Does one contact that contact with that contact, feel that feeling with that feeling, perceive that perception with that perception, intend that volition with that volition, think that thought with that mind, apply that applied thought with that applied thought, sustain that sustained thought with that sustained thought, cherish that rapture with that rapture, recollect that mindfulness with that mindfulness, or understand that wisdom with that wisdom? This should not be said…

Jhānanikanti [P 0.0484] cittasampayuttā, jhānaṃ cittasampayuttanti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is delight in jhāna associated with the mind, and is jhāna associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a confluence of two instances of contact… of two minds? This should not be said…

Jhānanikanti akusalaṃ, jhānaṃ kusalanti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā [V 0.0391] kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is delight in jhāna unwholesome, and jhāna wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart states come face to face? This should not be said…

672. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

672. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart states come face to face? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, these four things are very far apart. What four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first pair that is very far apart… Therefore, the Dhamma of the good is far from the ignoble.” Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterpart states come face to face.”

673. Na vattabbaṃ – “samāpanno assādeti, jhānanikanti jhānārammaṇā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, so taṃ assādeti taṃ nikāmeti tena ca vittiṃ āpajjati; vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati[M 0.0352], so taṃ assādeti taṃ nikāmeti [T 0.0515] tena ca vittiṃ āpajjatī”ti a. ni. 4.123! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi samāpanno assādeti, jhānanikanti jhānārammaṇāti.

673. Should it not be said: “One who has attained a meditative state relishes it, and the delight in jhāna has jhāna as its object”? Yes, it should be said. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Here, monks, a bhikkhu, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna. He relishes it, desires it, and finds satisfaction in it. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought… the second jhāna… the third jhāna… he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna. He relishes it, desires it, and finds satisfaction in it”? Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, one who has attained a meditative state relishes it, and the delight in jhāna has jhāna as its object.

Samāpanno assādetikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on One Who Attains a Meditative State and Relishes It is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(133) 8. Asātarāgakathā

8. Discussion on Lust for the Unpleasant

674. Atthi [P 0.0485] asātarāgoti? Āmantā. Dukkhābhinandino sattā, atthi keci dukkhaṃ patthenti pihenti esanti gavesanti pariyesanti, dukkhaṃ ajjhosāya tiṭṭhantīti? Na hevaṃ [V 0.0392] vattabbe…pe… nanu sukhābhinandino sattā, atthi keci sukhaṃ patthenti pihenti esanti gavesanti pariyesanti, sukhaṃ ajjhosāya tiṭṭhantīti? Āmantā. Hañci sukhābhinandino sattā, atthi keci sukhaṃ patthenti pihenti esanti gavesanti pariyesanti, sukhaṃ ajjhosāya tiṭṭhanti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi asātarāgo”ti.

674. Is there lust for the unpleasant? Yes. Are there beings who delight in suffering, who long for, desire, seek, search for, and thoroughly search for suffering, and who cling to suffering? This should not be said... But are there not beings who delight in happiness, who long for, desire, seek, search for, and thoroughly search for happiness, and who cling to happiness? Yes. If there are beings who delight in happiness, who long for, desire, seek, search for, and thoroughly search for happiness, and who cling to happiness, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is lust for the unpleasant'.

Atthi asātarāgoti? Āmantā. Dukkhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, sukhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anusetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anusetīti? Āmantā. Hañci sukhāya vedanāya rāgānusayo anuseti, dukkhāya vedanāya paṭighānusayo anuseti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi asātarāgo”ti.

Is there lust for the unpleasant? Yes. Does the underlying tendency of lust lie latent in painful feeling, and the underlying tendency of aversion lie latent in pleasant feeling? It should not be said thus... Is it not the case that the underlying tendency of lust lies latent in pleasant feeling, and the underlying tendency of aversion lies latent in painful feeling? Yes. If the underlying tendency of lust lies latent in pleasant feeling, and the underlying tendency of aversion lies latent in painful feeling, then, good sir, you should not say: 'There is lust for the unpleasant.'

675. Na [T 0.0516] vattabbaṃ – “atthi asātarāgo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “so evaṃ anurodhavirodhaṃ samāpanno yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedayati sukhaṃ vā dukkhaṃ vā adukkhamasukhaṃ vā, so taṃ vedanaṃ abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhatī”ti ma. ni. 3.409 mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaye! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi asātarāgoti.

675. Should it not be said: 'There is lust for the unpleasant'? Yes, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Thus involved in attraction and repulsion, whatever feeling one experiences—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—one delights in that feeling, welcomes it, and clings to it'? Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, there is lust for the unpleasant.

Asātarāgakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Lust for the Unpleasant is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(134) 9. Dhammataṇhā abyākatātikathā

9. Discussion on Craving for Mental Phenomena as Indeterminate

676. Dhammataṇhā [M 0.0353][P 0.0486] abyākatāti? Āmantā. Vipākābyākatā kiriyābyākatā rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

676. Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. Is it resultant-indeterminate? Is it functional-indeterminate? Is it form? Is it Nibbāna? Is it the eye-base... is it the tangible-object-base? This should not be said...

Dhammataṇhā abyākatāti? Āmantā. Rūpataṇhā abyākatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0393] …pe… dhammataṇhā abyākatāti? Āmantā. Saddataṇhā…pe… gandhataṇhā…pe… rasataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā abyākatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for forms indeterminate? This should not be said… Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for sounds... smells... tastes... tangible objects indeterminate? This should not be said...

Rūpataṇhā akusalāti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā akusalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saddataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā akusalāti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā akusalāti? Na [T 0.0517] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is craving for forms unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena unwholesome? This should not be said... Is craving for sounds... is craving for tangible objects unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena unwholesome? This should not be said...

677. Dhammataṇhā abyākatāti? Āmantā. Nanu taṇhā akusalā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci taṇhā akusalā vuttā bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā abyākatā”ti.

677. Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. But has not craving been declared unwholesome by the Blessed One? Yes. If craving has been declared unwholesome by the Blessed One, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate'.

Dhammataṇhā abyākatāti? Āmantā. Nanu lobho akusalo vutto bhagavatā, dhammataṇhā lobhoti? Āmantā. Hañci lobho akusalo vutto bhagavatā, dhammataṇhā lobho, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā abyākatā”ti.

Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. But has not greed been declared unwholesome by the Blessed One, and is not craving for mental phenomena greed? Yes. If greed has been declared unwholesome by the Blessed One, and craving for mental phenomena is greed, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate'.

678. Dhammataṇhā lobho abyākatoti? Āmantā[P 0.0487]. Rūpataṇhā lobho abyākatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dhammataṇhā lobho abyākatoti? Āmantā. Saddataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā lobho abyākatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

678. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for forms, which is greed, indeterminate? This should not be said... Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for sounds... is craving for tangible objects, which is greed, indeterminate? This should not be said...

Rūpataṇhā lobho akusaloti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā lobho akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saddataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā lobho akusaloti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā lobho akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is craving for forms, which is greed, unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, unwholesome? This should not be said... Is craving for sounds... is craving for tangible objects, which is greed, unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, unwholesome? This should not be said...

679. Dhammataṇhā [M 0.0354] abyākatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā”ti mahāva. 14; dī. ni. 2.400! Attheva suttantoti[T 0.0518]? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dhammataṇhā abyākatā”ti.

679. Is craving for mental phenomena indeterminate? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “That craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, relishing here and there—that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence”? Does such a Suttanta exist? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “Craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate.”

680. Na [V 0.0394] vattabbaṃ – “dhammataṇhā abyākatā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sā dhammataṇhāti? Āmantā. Hañci sā dhammataṇhā, tena vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā abyākatā”ti.

680. Should it not be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate'? Yes. But is not that craving for mental phenomena? Yes. If that is craving for mental phenomena, then, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate'.

Dhammataṇhā abyākatātikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'Craving for Mental Phenomena is Indeterminate' is concluded.

13. Terasamavaggo

13. The Thirteenth Chapter

(135) 10. Dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayotikathā

13. (135) 10. The Discussion on 'Craving for Mental Phenomena is Not the Origin of Suffering'

681. Dhammataṇhā [P 0.0488] na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Rūpataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Saddataṇhā…pe… gandhataṇhā…pe… rasataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for forms not the origin of suffering? This should not be said... Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for sounds... smells... tastes... tangible objects not the origin of suffering? This should not be said...

Rūpataṇhā dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saddataṇhā…pe… gandhataṇhā…pe… rasataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

681. Is craving for forms the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena the origin of suffering? This should not be said... Is craving for sounds... smells... tastes... tangible objects the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena the origin of suffering? This should not be said...

682. Dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Nanu taṇhā dukkhasamudayo vutto bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci taṇhā dukkhasamudayo [T 0.0519] vutto bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo”ti. Dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Nanu lobho dukkhasamudayo [M 0.0355] vutto bhagavatā, dhammataṇhā lobhoti? Āmantā. Hañci lobho dukkhasamudayo vutto bhagavatā, dhammataṇhā lobho, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo”ti.

Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? Yes. But has it not been declared by the Blessed One that craving is the origin of suffering? Yes. If craving has been declared by the Blessed One to be the origin of suffering, then, good sir, it should not be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.' Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? Yes. But has it not been declared by the Blessed One that greed is the origin of suffering, and is not craving for mental phenomena greed? Yes. If greed has been declared by the Blessed One to be the origin of suffering, and craving for mental phenomena is greed, then, good sir, it should not be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.'

683. Dhammataṇhā lobho, na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Rūpataṇhā lobho, na dukkhasamudayoti[V 0.0395]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dhammataṇhā [P 0.0489] lobho, na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Saddataṇhā…pe… gandhataṇhā…pe… rasataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā lobho, na dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

682. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for forms, which is greed, not the origin of suffering? This should not be said... Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for sounds... smells... tastes... tangible objects, which is greed, not the origin of suffering? This should not be said...

Rūpataṇhā lobho dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā lobho dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saddataṇhā…pe… phoṭṭhabbataṇhā lobho dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Dhammataṇhā lobho dukkhasamudayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

683. Is craving for forms, which is greed, the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, the origin of suffering? This should not be said... Is craving for sounds... tangible objects, which is greed, the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental phenomena, which is greed, the origin of suffering? This should not be said...

684. Dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandīrāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo”ti.

Is craving for mental phenomena not the origin of suffering? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'That craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, relishing here and there—that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence'? Does such a Suttanta exist? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.'

685. Na [T 0.0520] vattabbaṃ – “dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sā dhammataṇhāti? Āmantā. Hañci sā dhammataṇhā, tena vata re vattabbe – “dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayo”ti.

684. Should it not be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering'? Yes. But is not that craving for mental phenomena? Yes. If that is craving for mental phenomena, then, good sir, it should be said, 'Craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.'

Dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayotikathā niṭṭhitā.

685. The Discussion on 'Craving for Mental Phenomena is Not the Origin of Suffering' is concluded.

Terasamavaggo.

The Thirteenth Section.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Kappaṭṭho [P 0.0490] kappaṃ tiṭṭheyya, kappaṭṭho kusalaṃ cittaṃ na paṭilabheyya, anantarāpayutto puggalo sammattaniyāmaṃ okkameyya, niyato niyāmaṃ okkamati, nivuto nīvaraṇaṃ jahati, sammukhībhūto saṃyojanaṃ jahati, jhānanikanti, asātarāgo, dhammataṇhā abyākatā, dhammataṇhā na dukkhasamudayoti.

One who stands for an eon might remain for an eon; one who stands for an eon might not obtain a wholesome mind; a person who has immediate succession might enter the path of rightness; one who is certain enters the path of certainty; one who is hindered abandons the hindrance; one who is face to face abandons the fetters; attachment to jhāna; lust for the unpleasant; craving for mental phenomena is indeterminate; craving for mental phenomena is not the origin of suffering.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(136) 1. Kusalākusalapaṭisandahanakathā

Discussion on the Connection of Wholesome and Unwholesome States.

686. Akusalamūlaṃ [M 0.0356][P 0.0491][V 0.0396] paṭisandahati kusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Yā akusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva kusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an unwholesome root connect with a wholesome root? Yes. Is the turning… aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome the very same as the turning… aspiration for the arising of the wholesome? This should not be said…

Akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūlaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “yā akusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva kusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā. Kusalaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa anāvaṭṭantassa (sī. pī. ka.), anāvajjantassa (syā. kaṃ.) uppajjati [T 0.0521] …pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu kusalaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci kusalaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūla”nti.

An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root; should it not be said: 'The turning... aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome is the very same as the turning... aspiration for the arising of the wholesome'? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who does not turn towards it... for one who does not aspire? It should not be said thus... But does not the wholesome arise for one who turns towards it... for one who aspires? Yes. If the wholesome arises for one who turns towards it... for one who aspires, then, good sir, it should surely not be said: 'An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root'.

687. Akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Akusalamūlaṃ ayoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Kusalaṃ ayoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu kusalaṃ yoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci kusalaṃ yoniso manasikaroto uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūla”nti.

687. Does an unwholesome root connect with a wholesome root? Yes. Does an unwholesome root arise for one who attends unwisely? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who attends unwisely? It should not be said thus... But does not the wholesome arise for one who attends wisely? Yes. If the wholesome arises for one who attends wisely, then, good sir, it should surely not be said: 'An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root'.

Akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Kāmasaññāya anantarā nekkhammasaññā uppajjati, byāpādasaññāya anantarā abyāpādasaññā uppajjati, vihiṃsāsaññāya anantarā avihiṃsāsaññā uppajjati, byāpādassa [P 0.0492] anantarā mettā uppajjati, vihiṃsāya anantarā karuṇā uppajjati, aratiyā anantarā muditā uppajjati, paṭighassa anantarā upekkhā uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an unwholesome root connect with a wholesome root? Yes. Does the perception of renunciation arise immediately after the perception of sensual desire, the perception of non-ill will after the perception of ill will, the perception of non-harming after the perception of harming, loving-kindness after ill will, compassion after harming, sympathetic joy after discontent, and equanimity after aversion? It should not be said thus...

688. Kusalamūlaṃ [V 0.0397] paṭisandahati akusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Yā kusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva akusalassa uppādāya [T 0.0522] āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

688. Does a wholesome root connect with an unwholesome root? Yes. Is the turning... aspiration for the arising of the wholesome the very same as the turning... aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome? It should not be said thus...

Kusalamūlaṃ [M 0.0357] paṭisandahati akusalamūlaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “yā kusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva akusalassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā. Akusalaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu akusalaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci akusalaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūla”nti.

A wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root; should it not be said: 'The turning... aspiration for the arising of the wholesome is the very same as the turning... aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome'? Yes. Does the unwholesome arise for one who does not turn towards it... for one who does not aspire? It should not be said thus... But does not the unwholesome arise for one who turns towards it... for one who aspires? Yes. If the unwholesome arises for one who turns towards it... for one who aspires, then, good sir, it should surely not be said: 'A wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root'.

689. Kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Kusalaṃ yoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Akusalaṃ yoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu akusalaṃ ayoniso manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci akusalaṃ ayoniso manasikaroto uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūla”nti.

689. Does a wholesome root connect with an unwholesome root? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who attends wisely? Yes. Does the unwholesome arise for one who attends wisely? It should not be said thus... But does not the unwholesome arise for one who attends unwisely? Yes. If the unwholesome arises for one who attends unwisely, then, good sir, it should surely not be said: 'A wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root'.

Kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūlanti? Āmantā. Nekkhammasaññāya anantarā kāmasaññā uppajjati, abyāpādasaññāya [P 0.0493] anantarā byāpādasaññā uppajjati, avihiṃsāsaññāya anantarā vihiṃsāsaññā uppajjati, mettāya anantarā byāpādo uppajjati, karuṇāya anantarā vihiṃsā uppajjati, muditāya anantarā arati [T 0.0523] uppajjati, upekkhāya anantarā paṭighaṃ uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a wholesome root connect with an unwholesome root? Yes. Does the perception of sensual desire arise immediately after the perception of renunciation, the perception of ill will after the perception of non-ill will, the perception of harming after the perception of non-harming, ill will after loving-kindness, harming after compassion, discontent after sympathetic joy, and aversion after equanimity? It should not be said thus...

690. Na vattabbaṃ – “akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūlaṃ, kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūla”nti? Āmantā. Nanu yasmiṃyeva vatthusmiṃ rajjati tasmiññeva vatthusmiṃ virajjati, yasmiṃyeva vatthusmiṃ virajjati tasmiññeva vatthusmiṃ rajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci yasmiññeva vatthusmiṃ rajjati tasmiññeva vatthusmiṃ virajjati, yasmiññeva vatthusmiṃ virajjati tasmiññeva [V 0.0398] vatthusmiṃ rajjati, tena vata re vattabbe – “akusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati kusalamūlaṃ, kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūla”nti.

690. Should it not be said: 'An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root, and a wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root'? Yes. But is it not so that in whatever object one has passion, in that very object one becomes dispassionate, and in whatever object one becomes dispassionate, in that very object one has passion? Yes. If in whatever object one has passion, in that very object one becomes dispassionate, and in whatever object one becomes dispassionate, in that very object one has passion, then, good sir, it should surely be said: 'An unwholesome root connects with a wholesome root, and a wholesome root connects with an unwholesome root'.

Kusalākusalapaṭisandahanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Connection of the Wholesome and Unwholesome is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(137) 2. Saḷāyatanuppattikathā

14. Discourse on the Arising of the Six Sense Bases

691. Saḷāyatanaṃ [M 0.0358] apubbaṃ acarimaṃ mātukucchismiṃ saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Sabbaṅgapaccaṅgī ahīnindriyo mātukucchismiṃ okkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do the six sense bases arise without prior or subsequent development in the mother's womb? Yes. Does one with all major and minor limbs complete and with faculties unimpaired descend into the mother's womb? It should not be said thus...

Upapattesiyena cittena cakkhāyatanaṃ saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Upapattesiyena cittena hatthā saṇṭhanti, pādā saṇṭhanti, sīsaṃ saṇṭhāti, kaṇṇo saṇṭhāti, nāsikā saṇṭhāti, mukhaṃ saṇṭhāti, dantā saṇṭhantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

691. Does the eye-base arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness? Yes. Do hands, feet, head, ears, nose, mouth, and teeth arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness? It should not be said thus...

Upapattesiyena [T 0.0524][P 0.0494] cittena sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ saṇṭhātīti? Āmantā. Upapattesiyena cittena hatthā saṇṭhanti, pādā saṇṭhanti, sīsaṃ saṇṭhāti, kaṇṇo saṇṭhāti, nāsikā saṇṭhāti, mukhaṃ saṇṭhāti, dantā saṇṭhantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the ear-base... the nose-base... the tongue-base arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness? Yes. Do hands, feet, head, ears, nose, mouth, and teeth arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness? It should not be said thus...

692. Mātukucchigatassa pacchā cakkhāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Mātukucchismiṃ cakkhupaṭilābhāya kammaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… mātukucchigatassa pacchā sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Mātukucchismiṃ jivhāpaṭilābhāya kammaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the eye-base arise later for one who is in the mother's womb? Yes. Does one perform kamma in the mother's womb for the acquisition of the eye? It should not be said thus... Does the ear-base... the nose-base... the tongue-base arise later for one who is in the mother's womb? Yes. Does one perform kamma in the mother's womb for the acquisition of the tongue? It should not be said thus...

Mātukucchigatassa [V 0.0399] pacchā kesā lomā nakhā dantā aṭṭhī uppajjantīti? Āmantā. Mātukucchismiṃ aṭṭhipaṭilābhāya kammaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Do hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, and bones arise later for one who is in the mother's womb? Yes. Does one perform kamma in the mother's womb for the acquisition of bones? This should not be said... and so on.

Na vattabbaṃ – “mātukucchigatassa pacchā kesā lomā nakhā dantā aṭṭhī uppajjantī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Should it not be said: 'Hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, and bones arise later for one who is in the mother's womb'? Yes, it should not be said. But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Paṭhamaṃ kalalaṃ hoti, kalalā hoti abbudaṃ;

Abbudā jāyate pesi pesī (syā. kaṃ. pī.), pesi nibbattate nibbattatī (sī. syā., saṃ. ni. 1.235), nibbattati (pī. ka.) ghano;

Ghanā pasākhā jāyanti, kesā lomā nakhāpi ca.

First, there is the 'kalala'; from the 'kalala' there is the 'abbuda'; from the 'abbuda' the 'pesi' is born; from the 'pesi' the 'ghana' is produced; from the 'ghana' the five branches, hair of the head, hair of the body, and also nails are born.

“Yañcassa [M 0.0359] bhuñjati mātā, annaṃ pānañca bhojanaṃ;

Tena so tattha yāpeti, mātukucchigato naro”ti saṃ. ni. 1.235.

And whatever rice, drink, and food that being's mother eats, by that he who is in the mother's womb is sustained there.

Attheva [T 0.0525] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi mātukucchigatassa pacchā kesā lomā nakhā dantā aṭṭhī uppajjantīti.

Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. If that is so, then hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, and bones arise later for one who is in the mother's womb.

Saḷāyatanuppattikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Arising of the Six Sense Bases is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(138) 3. Anantarapaccayakathā

3. Discourse on the Contiguity Condition

693. Cakkhuviññāṇassa [P 0.0495] anantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yā cakkhuviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva sotaviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

693. Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Is the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of eye-consciousness the same as the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of ear-consciousness? This should not be said... and so on.

Cakkhuviññāṇassa [V 0.0400] anantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ uppajjati, na vattabbaṃ – “yā cakkhuviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva sotaviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Sotaviññāṇaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Nanu sotaviññāṇaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti, āmantā. Hañci sotaviññāṇaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuviññāṇassa anantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatī”ti.

Ear-consciousness arises immediately after eye-consciousness; should it not be said that 'the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of eye-consciousness is the same as the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of ear-consciousness'? Yes, it should not be said. Does ear-consciousness arise for one who does not turn the mind... and so on... for one who does not direct the mind? This should not be said... and so on. But surely, does not ear-consciousness arise for one who turns the mind... and so on... for one who directs the mind? Yes. If ear-consciousness arises for one who turns the mind... and so on... for one who directs the mind, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'ear-consciousness arises immediately after eye-consciousness'.

694. Cakkhuviññāṇassa anantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ rūpanimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjatīti[T 0.0526]? Āmantā. Sotaviññāṇaṃ rūpanimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

694. Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise for one who attends to the form-sign? Yes. Does ear-consciousness arise for one who attends to the form-sign? This should not be said... and so on.

Cakkhuviññāṇaṃ rūpārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Sotaviññāṇaṃ rūpārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does eye-consciousness have only form as its object and not another object? Yes. Does ear-consciousness have only form as its object and not another object? This should not be said... and so on.

Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇanti? Āmantā. Cakkhuñca [P 0.0496] paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on forms? Yes. Does ear-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on forms? This should not be said... and so on.

Cakkhuñca [M 0.0360] paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati cakkhuviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuñca paṭicca rūpe ca uppajjati sotaviññāṇa”nti.

Does ear-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on forms? Yes. Is there a discourse that states: 'Ear-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms'? There is not. Is there a discourse that states: 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms'? Yes. If there is indeed a discourse that states: 'Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms', then, good sir, it should not be said that 'ear-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on forms'.

Cakkhuviññāṇassa anantarā sotaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva cakkhuviññāṇaṃ taṃ sotaviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Is that very eye-consciousness the same as that ear-consciousness? This should not be said... and so on.

695. Sotaviññāṇassa anantarā ghānaviññāṇaṃ uppajjati…pe… ghānaviññāṇassa anantarā [V 0.0401] jivhāviññāṇaṃ uppajjati…pe… jivhāviññāṇassa anantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Yā jivhāviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva kāyaviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti[T 0.0527]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… jivhāviññāṇassa anantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjati, na vattabbaṃ – “yā jivhāviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva kāyaviññāṇassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā. Kāyaviññāṇaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu kāyaviññāṇaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci kāyaviññāṇaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “jivhāviññāṇassa anantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatī”ti.

695. Does nose-consciousness arise immediately after ear-consciousness... and so on... does tongue-consciousness arise immediately after nose-consciousness... and so on... does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Is the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of tongue-consciousness the same as the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of body-consciousness? This should not be said... and so on. Body-consciousness arises immediately after tongue-consciousness; should it not be said that 'the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of tongue-consciousness is the same as the turning of the mind... and so on... the directing of the mind for the arising of body-consciousness'? Yes, it should not be said. Does body-consciousness arise for one who does not turn the mind... and so on... for one who does not direct the mind? This should not be said... and so on. But surely, does not body-consciousness arise for one who turns the mind... and so on... for one who directs the mind? Yes. If body-consciousness arises for one who turns the mind... and so on... for one who directs the mind, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'body-consciousness arises immediately after tongue-consciousness'.

696. Jivhāviññāṇassa [P 0.0497] anantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Jivhāviññāṇaṃ rasanimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Kāyaviññāṇaṃ rasanimittaṃ manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

696. Does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Does tongue-consciousness arise for one who attends to the taste-sign? Yes. Does body-consciousness arise for one who attends to the taste-sign? This should not be said... and so on.

Jivhāviññāṇaṃ rasārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Kāyaviññāṇaṃ rasārammaṇaññeva na aññārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does tongue-consciousness have only taste as its object and not another object? Yes. Does body-consciousness have only taste as its object and not another object? This should not be said... and so on.

Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇanti? Āmantā. Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does tongue-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? Yes. Does body-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? This should not be said... and so on.

Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇanti? Āmantā. “Jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇa”nti – attheva [T 0.0528] suttantoti? Natthi. “Jivhañca [M 0.0361] paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Hañci “jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati jivhāviññāṇa”nti – attheva suttantoti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “jivhañca paṭicca rase ca uppajjati kāyaviññāṇa”nti.

Does body-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? Yes. Is there a discourse that states: 'Body-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes'? There is not. Is there a discourse that states: 'Tongue-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes'? Yes. If there is indeed a discourse that states: 'Tongue-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes', then, good sir, it should not be said that 'body-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes'.

Jivhāviññāṇassa [V 0.0402] anantarā kāyaviññāṇaṃ uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva jivhāviññāṇaṃ taṃ kāyaviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Is that very tongue-consciousness the same as that body-consciousness? This should not be said... and so on.

697. Na vattabbaṃ – “pañcaviññāṇā aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjantī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi koci naccati gāyati vādeti, rūpañca passati, saddañca [P 0.0498] suṇāti, gandhañca ghāyati, rasañca sāyati, phoṭṭhabbañca phusatīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi koci naccati gāyati vādeti, rūpañca passati, saddañca suṇāti, gandhañca ghāyati, rasañca sāyati, phoṭṭhabbañca phusati, tena vata re vattabbe – “pañcaviññāṇā aññamaññassa samanantarā uppajjantī”ti.

697. Should it not be said: 'The five consciousnesses arise in immediate succession to one another'? Indeed, it should not be said. But is there not someone who dances, sings, or plays music, and sees a form, hears a sound, smells an odor, tastes a flavor, and touches a tangible object? Yes. If there is someone who dances, sings, or plays music, and sees a form, hears a sound, smells an odor, tastes a flavor, and touches a tangible object, then, good sir, it should indeed be said: 'The five consciousnesses arise in immediate succession to one another'.

Anantarapaccayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Proximity Condition is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(139) 4. Ariyarūpakathā

(139) 4. Discourse on Noble Material Form

698. Ariyarūpaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyāti? Āmantā. Ariyarūpaṃ kusalanti? Āmantā. Mahābhūtā kusalāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0529] …pe… mahābhūtā abyākatāti? Āmantā. Ariyarūpaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ariyarūpaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyāti? Āmantā. Ariyarūpaṃ anāsavaṃ asaṃyojaniyaṃ aganthaniyaṃ anoghaniyaṃ ayoganiyaṃ anīvaraṇiyaṃ aparāmaṭṭhaṃ anupādāniyaṃ asaṃkilesiyanti? Āmantā. Mahābhūtā anāsavā…pe… asaṃkilesiyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… mahābhūtā sāsavā saṃyojaniyā…pe… saṃkilesiyāti? Āmantā. Ariyarūpaṃ sāsavaṃ saṃyojaniyaṃ…pe… saṃkilesiyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

14. Is noble material form produced in dependence on the great primary elements? Yes. Is noble material form wholesome? Yes. Are the great primary elements wholesome? This should not be said... and so on. Are the great primary elements indeterminate? Yes. Is noble material form indeterminate? This should not be said... and so on. Is noble material form produced in dependence on the great primary elements? Yes. Is noble material form not an object for the taints, not an object for the fetters, not an object for the ties, not an object for the floods, not an object for the yokes, not an object for the hindrances, not an object for misapprehension, not an object for clinging, not an object for the defilements? Yes. Are the great primary elements not objects for the taints... and so on... not objects for the defilements? This should not be said... and so on. Are the great primary elements objects for the taints, objects for the fetters... and so on... objects for the defilements? Yes. Is noble material form an object for the taints, an object for the fetters... and so on... an object for the defilements? This should not be said... and so on.

699. Na vattabbaṃ – “ariyarūpaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0499] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yaṃ kiñci, bhikkhave, rūpaṃ cattāri mahābhūtāni catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ [M 0.0362] upādāyarūpa”nti [V 0.0403] ma. ni. 1.347; a. ni. 11.15! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi ariyarūpaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāyāti.

Should it not be said: “Noble material form is produced in dependence on the great primary elements”? Indeed, it should not be said. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, whatever material form there is, it is the four great primary elements and material form produced in dependence on the four great primary elements”? Is there not indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, noble material form is produced in dependence on the great primary elements.

Ariyarūpakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Noble Material Form is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(140) 5. Añño anusayotikathā

(140) 5. Discourse on 'Is the Underlying Tendency Another Thing?'

700. Añño kāmarāgānusayo aññaṃ kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Añño kāmarāgo aññaṃ kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti[T 0.0530]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sveva kāmarāgo taṃ kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva kāmarāgānusayo taṃ kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

698. Is the underlying tendency to sensual lust one thing, and the obsession of sensual lust another? Yes. Is sensual lust one thing, and the obsession of sensual lust another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very sensual lust the obsession of sensual lust? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to sensual lust the obsession of sensual lust? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño paṭighānusayo aññaṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Aññaṃ paṭighaṃ aññaṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… taññeva paṭighaṃ taṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva paṭighānusayo taṃ paṭighapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

699. Is the underlying tendency to aversion one thing, and the obsession of aversion another? Yes. Is aversion one thing, and the obsession of aversion another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very aversion the obsession of aversion? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to aversion the obsession of aversion? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño mānānusayo aññaṃ mānapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Añño māno aññaṃ mānapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sveva māno taṃ mānapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva mānānusayo taṃ mānapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the underlying tendency to conceit one thing, and the obsession of conceit another? Yes. Is conceit one thing, and the obsession of conceit another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very conceit the obsession of conceit? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to conceit the obsession of conceit? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño [P 0.0500] diṭṭhānusayo aññaṃ diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Aññā diṭṭhi aññaṃ diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva diṭṭhi taṃ diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva diṭṭhānusayo taṃ diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

14. Is the underlying tendency to views one thing, and the obsession of views another? Yes. Is a view one thing, and the obsession of views another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very view the obsession of views? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to views the obsession of views? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño vicikicchānusayo aññaṃ vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Aññā vicikicchā [V 0.0404] aññaṃ vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva vicikicchā taṃ vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva vicikicchānusayo taṃ vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the underlying tendency to doubt one thing, and the obsession of doubt another? Yes. Is doubt one thing, and the obsession of doubt another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very doubt the obsession of doubt? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to doubt the obsession of doubt? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño [M 0.0363][T 0.0531] bhavarāgānusayo aññaṃ bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Añño bhavarāgo aññaṃ bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sveva bhavarāgo taṃ bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva bhavarāgānusayo taṃ bhavarāgapariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

700. Is the underlying tendency to craving for existence one thing, and the obsession of craving for existence another? Yes. Is craving for existence one thing, and the obsession of craving for existence another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very craving for existence the obsession of craving for existence? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to craving for existence the obsession of craving for existence? This should not be said... and so on.

Añño avijjānusayo aññaṃ avijjāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Aññā avijjā aññaṃ avijjāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāva avijjā taṃ avijjāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Āmantā. Sveva avijjānusayo taṃ avijjāpariyuṭṭhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the underlying tendency to ignorance one thing, and the obsession of ignorance another? Yes. Is ignorance one thing, and the obsession of ignorance another? This should not be said... and so on. Is that very ignorance the obsession of ignorance? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to ignorance the obsession of ignorance? This should not be said... and so on.

701. Na vattabbaṃ – “añño anusayo aññaṃ pariyuṭṭhāna”nti? Āmantā[P 0.0501]. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sānusayo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. “Pariyuṭṭhito”ti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi añño anusayo aññaṃ pariyuṭṭhānanti. Puthujjano kusalābyākate citte vattamāne “sarāgo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. “Pariyuṭṭhito”ti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi añño rāgo aññaṃ pariyuṭṭhānanti.

Should it not be said: “The underlying tendency is one thing, and the obsession is another”? Indeed, it should not be said. When a worldling’s mind is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said, “He is with underlying tendency”? Yes. Should it be said, “He is in a state of obsession”? This should not be said. Therefore, the underlying tendency is one thing, and the obsession is another. When a worldling’s mind is occurring in a wholesome or indeterminate state, should it be said, “He is with passion”? Yes. Should it be said, “He is in a state of obsession”? This should not be said. Therefore, passion is one thing, and the obsession is another.

Añño anusayotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on 'Is the Underlying Tendency Another Thing?' is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(141) 6. Pariyuṭṭhānaṃ cittavippayuttantikathā

(141) 6. Discourse on Obsession Being Dissociated from Consciousness

702. Pariyuṭṭhānaṃ [T 0.0532] cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pariyuṭṭhānaṃ cittavippayuttanti? Āmantā. Natthi sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittaṃ samohaṃ [V 0.0405] cittaṃ…pe… akusalaṃ cittaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ cittanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atthi sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ…pe… akusalaṃ cittaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ cittanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sadosaṃ cittaṃ samohaṃ cittaṃ…pe… akusalaṃ cittaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pariyuṭṭhānaṃ cittavippayutta”nti.

702. Is preoccupation dissociated from the mind? Yes. Is it form, Nibbāna, the eye-sphere… up to… the tangible-sphere? That should not be said… (and so on). Is preoccupation dissociated from the mind? Yes. Is there no mind with lust, no mind with hatred, no mind with delusion… up to… no unwholesome mind, no defiled mind? That should not be said… (and so on). But is there not a mind with lust, a mind with hatred, a mind with delusion… up to… an unwholesome mind, a defiled mind? Yes. If there is a mind with lust, a mind with hatred, a mind with delusion… up to… an unwholesome mind, a defiled mind, then indeed it should not be said: “Preoccupation is dissociated from the mind.”

Pariyuṭṭhānaṃ cittavippayuttantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on preoccupation being dissociated from the mind is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(142) 7. Pariyāpannakathā

7. Discussion on What is Included

703. Rūparāgo [M 0.0364][P 0.0502] rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Samāpattesiyo upapattesiyo diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu [T 0.0533] na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena na upapattesiyena cittena na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro…pe… ekārammaṇo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti…pe….

703. Does lust for form underlie the form element and is it included in the form element? Yes. Is it conducive to attainment, conducive to rebirth, a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it co-existent, co-nascent, intermingled, associated, of single arising, of single cessation, of single base, of single object with a mind conducive to attainment, a mind conducive to rebirth, or a mind that is a pleasant abiding in the present life? That should not be said… (and so on). But is it not that it is not conducive to attainment, not conducive to rebirth, not a pleasant abiding in the present life? And is it not that it is co-existent, co-nascent, intermingled, associated, of single arising, of single cessation, of single base, of single object with a mind that is not conducive to attainment, a mind that is not conducive to rebirth, or a mind that is not a pleasant abiding in the present life? Yes. If it is not conducive to attainment, not conducive to rebirth, not a pleasant abiding in the present life… up to… of single object, then indeed it should not be said: “Lust for form underlies the form element and is included in the form element.”… (and so on).

Rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Saddarāgo saddadhātuṃ anuseti, saddadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo phoṭṭhabbadhātuṃ anuseti, phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
