Does lust for form underlie the form element and is it included in the form element? Yes. Does lust for sound underlie the sound element and is it included in the sound element? That should not be said… (and so on). Does lust for form underlie the form element and is it included in the form element? Yes. Does lust for odors… (and so on)… lust for tastes… (and so on)… lust for tangible objects underlie the tangible-object element and is it included in the tangible-object element? That should not be said… (and so on).

Saddarāgo [V 0.0406] saddadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “saddadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo [P 0.0503] phoṭṭhabbadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Lust for sound underlies the sound element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the sound element’? Yes. Lust for form underlies the form element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the form element’? That should not be said… (and so on). Lust for odors… (and so on)… lust for tastes… (and so on)… lust for tangible objects underlies the tangible-object element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the tangible-object element’? Yes. Lust for form underlies the form element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the form element’? That should not be said… (and so on).

704. Arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā[T 0.0534]. Samāpattesiyo upapattesiyo diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko [M 0.0365] ekārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Nanu na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena…pe… ekārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo…pe… ekārammaṇo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti.

704. Does lust for the formless underlie the formless element and is it included in the formless element? Yes. Is it conducive to attainment, conducive to rebirth, a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it co-existent, co-nascent, intermingled, associated, of single arising, of single cessation, of single base, of single object with a mind conducive to attainment, a mind conducive to rebirth, or a mind that is a pleasant abiding in the present life? That should not be said… (and so on). But is it not that it is not conducive to attainment, not conducive to rebirth, not a pleasant abiding in the present life? And is it not that it is co-existent… with a mind that is not conducive to attainment… up to… of single object? Yes. If it is not conducive to attainment, not conducive to rebirth… up to… of single object, then indeed it should not be said: “Lust for the formless underlies the formless element and is included in the formless element.”

Arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Saddarāgo saddadhātuṃ anuseti, saddadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo phoṭṭhabbadhātuṃ anuseti, phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does lust for the formless underlie the formless element and is it included in the formless element? Yes. Does lust for sound underlie the sound element and is it included in the sound element? That should not be said… (and so on). Does lust for the formless underlie the formless element and is it included in the formless element? Yes. Does lust for odors… (and so on)… lust for tastes… (and so on)… lust for tangible objects underlie the tangible-object element and is it included in the tangible-object element? That should not be said… (and so on).

Saddarāgo saddadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “saddadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0504]. Arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti, na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo phoṭṭhabbadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Arūparāgo [T 0.0535] arūpadhātuṃ anuseti, na vattabbaṃ – “arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Lust for sound underlies the sound element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the sound element’? Yes. Lust for the formless underlies the formless element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the formless element’? That should not be said… (and so on). Lust for odors… (and so on)… lust for tastes… (and so on)… lust for tangible objects underlies the tangible-object element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the tangible-object element’? Yes. Lust for the formless underlies the formless element; should it not be said that ‘it is included in the formless element’? That should not be said… (and so on).

705. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti rūpadhātupariyāpanno, arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Nanu kāmarāgo kāmadhātuṃ anuseti, kāmadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmarāgo kāmadhātuṃ anuseti kāmadhātupariyāpanno[V 0.0407], tena vata re vattabbe – “rūparāgo rūpadhātuṃ anuseti rūpadhātupariyāpanno, arūparāgo arūpadhātuṃ anuseti arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti.

705. Should it not be said: “Lust for form underlies the form element and is included in the form element; lust for the formless underlies the formless element and is included in the formless element”? Yes. But does not lust for sensual pleasures underlie the sensual-sphere element and is it included in the sensual-sphere element? Yes. If lust for sensual pleasures underlies the sensual-sphere element and is included in the sensual-sphere element, then indeed it should be said: “Lust for form underlies the form element and is included in the form element; lust for the formless underlies the formless element and is included in the formless element.”

Pariyāpannakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on what is included is concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(143) 8. Abyākatakathā

8. Discussion on the Undeclared

706. Diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Vipākābyākataṃ kiriyābyākataṃ rūpaṃ nibbānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatananti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… diṭṭhigataṃ [M 0.0366] abyākatanti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhigatasampayutto phasso abyākatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhigatasampayuttā [P 0.0505] vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… cetanā…pe… cittaṃ abyākatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

706. Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. Is it resultant-undeclared, functional-undeclared, material form, Nibbāna, the eye-base… up to… the tangible-base? It should not be said so… Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. Is contact associated with wrong view undeclared? It should not be said so… Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. Are feeling… perception… volition… consciousness associated with wrong view undeclared? It should not be said so…

Diṭṭhigatasampayutto [T 0.0536] phasso akusaloti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhigataṃ akusalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… diṭṭhigatasampayuttā vedanā saññā cetanā cittaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhigataṃ akusalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is contact associated with wrong view unwholesome? Yes. Is wrong view unwholesome? It should not be said so… Are feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness associated with wrong view unwholesome? Yes. Is wrong view unwholesome? It should not be said so…

707. Diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Aphalaṃ avipākanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphalaṃ savipākanti? Āmantā. Hañci saphalaṃ savipākaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti.

707. Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. Is it without fruit and without result? It should not be said so… Is it not with fruit and with result? Yes. If it is with fruit and with result, then indeed it should not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared.”

Diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Nanu micchādiṭṭhiparamāni vajjāni aṅguttaranikāye vuttāni bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci micchādiṭṭhiparamāni vajjāni vuttāni bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti.

Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said that wrong views are the worst of faults? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that wrong views are the worst of faults, then indeed it should not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared.”

Diṭṭhigataṃ [V 0.0408] abyākatanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “micchādiṭṭhi kho, vaccha, akusalā akusalaṃ (ma. ni. 2.194), sammādiṭṭhi kusalā” kusalaṃ (ma. ni. 2.104) ti ma. ni. 2.194! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti.

Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Wrong view, Vaccha, is unwholesome; right view is wholesome”? Does such a discourse exist? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared.”

Diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0506] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “micchādiṭṭhissa kho ahaṃ, puṇṇa, dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā”ti ma. ni. 2.79! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti.

Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “For one with wrong view, Puṇṇa, I declare one of two destinations—either hell or the animal realm”? Does such a discourse exist? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared.”

708. Na [T 0.0537] vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “‘sassato loko’ti kho, vaccha, abyākatametaṃ, ‘asassato loko’ti kho, vaccha, abyākatametaṃ, ‘antavā loko’ti kho, vaccha, abyākatametaṃ, ‘anantavā loko’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti kho[M 0.0367], vaccha…pe… ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha…pe… ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti kho, vaccha, abyākatameta”nti saṃ. ni. 4.416, thokaṃ pana visadisaṃ! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti.

708. Should it not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared”? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “‘The world is eternal’—this, Vaccha, is undeclared. ‘The world is not eternal’—this, Vaccha, is undeclared. ‘The world is finite’—this, Vaccha, is undeclared. ‘The world is infinite’—this, Vaccha… ‘The soul is the same as the body’—this, Vaccha… ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’—this, Vaccha… ‘The Tathāgata exists after death’—this, Vaccha… ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death’—this, Vaccha… ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’—this, Vaccha… ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’—this, Vaccha, is undeclared”? Does such a discourse exist? Yes. Therefore, wrong view is undeclared.

Diṭṭhigataṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “micchādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, purisapuggalassa yañceva kāyakammaṃ yathādiṭṭhisamattaṃ samādinnaṃ, yañca vacīkammaṃ…pe… yañca manokammaṃ, yā ca cetanā, yā ca patthanā, yo ca paṇidhi, ye ca saṅkhārā, sabbe te dhammā aniṭṭhāya akantāya amanāpāya ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattantī”ti a. ni. 1.306! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhigataṃ abyākata”nti.

Is wrong view undeclared? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said: “Monks, for a person with wrong view, whatever bodily action is undertaken and accomplished in accordance with that view, whatever verbal action… whatever mental action, whatever the volition, whatever the aspiration, whatever the resolve, and whatever the formations—all those phenomena conduce to what is undesired, disagreeable, unpleasant, to what is unbeneficial, and to suffering”? Does such a discourse exist? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: “Wrong view is undeclared.”

Abyākatakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Undeclared is Concluded.

14. Cuddasamavaggo

14. The Fourteenth Chapter

(144) 9. Apariyāpannakathā

(144) 9. Discussion on the Unincluded

709. Diṭṭhigataṃ [P 0.0507][V 0.0409][T 0.0538] apariyāpannanti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmimaggo sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmimaggo anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattamaggo arahattaphalaṃ, satipaṭṭhānaṃ sammappadhānaṃ iddhipādo indriyaṃ balaṃ bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

709. Is wrong view unincluded? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, Nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-return, the fruit of once-return, the path of non-return, the fruit of non-return, the path of Arahantship, the fruit of Arahantship, the establishments of mindfulness, the right strivings, the bases of spiritual power, the faculties, the powers, or the factors of enlightenment? It should not be said so…

710. Na vattabbaṃ – “diṭṭhigataṃ apariyāpanna”nti? Āmantā. Puthujjano “kāmesu vītarāgo”ti vattabboti? Āmantā. “Vigatadiṭṭhiyo”ti vattabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi diṭṭhigataṃ apariyāpannanti.

710. Should it not be said, 'Wrong view is unincluded'? Yes. Should an ordinary person be called 'one who is free from passion for sensual pleasures'? Yes. Should they be called 'one who is free from views'? It should not be said so. Therefore, wrong view is unincluded.

Apariyāpannakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Unincluded is Concluded.

Cuddasamavaggo.

The Fourteenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary of It Is:

Akusalamūlaṃ [M 0.0368] paṭisandahati kusalamūlaṃ, kusalamūlaṃ paṭisandahati akusalamūlaṃ, saḷāyatanaṃ chaviññāṇakāyā, ariyarūpaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya, sveva anusayo taṃ pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, pariyuṭṭhānaṃ cittavippayuttaṃ, yathādhātu taññeva anuseti, diṭṭhigataṃ abyākataṃ, diṭṭhigataṃ apariyāpannanti.

An unwholesome root joins with a wholesome root, a wholesome root joins with an unwholesome root; the six sense bases; the six bodies of consciousness; noble form is derived from the great elements; that very latent tendency is the obsession; the obsession is dissociated from consciousness; it lies latent according to its nature; a view is indeterminate; a view is unincluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(145) 1. Paccayatākathā

(145) 1. Discussion on Conditionality

711. Paccayatā [T 0.0539][P 0.0508] vavatthitāti? Āmantā. Nanu vīmaṃsā hetu, so ca adhipatīti? Āmantā[V 0.0410]. Hañci vīmaṃsā hetu, so ca adhipati, tena vata re vattabbe – “hetupaccayena paccayo, adhipatipaccayena paccayo”ti.

711. Is conditionality demarcated? Yes. Is not investigation a root, and is it also a dominant factor? Yes. If investigation is a root and also a dominant factor, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by way of root condition, and it is a condition by way of dominance condition.'

Nanu chandādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipatīti? Āmantā. Hañci chandādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of desire a dominant factor for co-nascent states? Yes. If the dominance of desire is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by way of dominance condition, and it is a condition by way of co-nascence condition.'

712. Nanu vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipatīti? Āmantā. Hañci vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti.

712. Is not the dominance of energy a dominant factor for co-nascent states? Yes. If the dominance of energy is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by way of dominance condition, and it is a condition by way of co-nascence condition.'

Nanu vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyanti? Āmantā. Hañci vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, indriyapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of energy a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also a faculty? Yes. If the dominance of energy is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also a faculty, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by faculty condition.'

Nanu vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca maggaṅganti? Āmantā. Hañci vīriyādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca maggaṅgaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, maggapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of energy a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also a path factor? Yes. If the dominance of energy is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also a path factor, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by path condition.'

713. Nanu [M 0.0369][T 0.0540] cittādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipatīti? Āmantā[P 0.0509]. Hañci cittādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti.

713. Is not the dominance of consciousness a dominant factor for co-nascent states? Yes. If the dominance of consciousness is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by co-nascence condition.'

Nanu cittādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, so ca āhāroti? Āmantā. Hañci cittādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, so ca āhāro, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, āhārapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of consciousness a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also nutriment? Yes. If the dominance of consciousness is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also nutriment, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by nutriment condition.'

Nanu cittādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyanti? Āmantā. Hañci cittādhipati [V 0.0411] sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, indriyapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of consciousness a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also a faculty? Yes. If the dominance of consciousness is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also a faculty, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by faculty condition.'

714. Nanu vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipatīti? Āmantā. Hañci vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, sahajātapaccayena paccayo”ti.

714. Is not the dominance of investigation a dominant factor for co-nascent states? Yes. If the dominance of investigation is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by co-nascence condition.'

Nanu vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyanti? Āmantā. Hañci vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca indriyaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, indriyapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of investigation a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also a faculty? Yes. If the dominance of investigation is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also a faculty, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by faculty condition.'

Nanu vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati, tañca maggaṅganti? Āmantā. Hañci vīmaṃsādhipati sahajātānaṃ dhammānaṃ adhipati[T 0.0541], tañca maggaṅgaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, maggapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Is not the dominance of investigation a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and is it not also a path factor? Yes. If the dominance of investigation is a dominant factor for co-nascent states, and it is also a path factor, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by path condition.'

715. Nanu ariyaṃ dhammaṃ garuṃ katvā uppajjati paccavekkhaṇā, tañcārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci ariyaṃ dhammaṃ garuṃ katvā uppajjati paccavekkhaṇā, tañcārammaṇaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “adhipatipaccayena paccayo, ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo”ti.

715. Does not reviewing arise by treating the noble Dhamma as weighty, and is not that noble Dhamma an object? Yes. If reviewing arises by treating the noble Dhamma as weighty, and that noble Dhamma is an object, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by dominance condition; it is a condition by object condition.'

716. Nanu purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca āsevanāti? Āmantā. Hañci [M 0.0370][P 0.0510] purimā purimā kusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca āsevanā, tena vata re vattabbe – “anantarapaccayena paccayo, āsevanapaccayena paccayo”ti.

716. Are not preceding, preceding wholesome states a condition for succeeding, succeeding wholesome states by proximity condition, and is that not repetition? Yes. If preceding, preceding wholesome states are a condition for succeeding, succeeding wholesome states by proximity condition, and that is repetition, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by proximity condition; it is a condition by repetition condition.'

Nanu purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca āsevanāti? Āmantā. Hañci purimā purimā akusalā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca āsevanā, tena vata re vattabbe – “anantarapaccayena paccayo, āsevanapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Are not preceding, preceding unwholesome states a condition for succeeding, succeeding unwholesome states by proximity condition, and is that not repetition? Yes. If preceding, preceding unwholesome states are a condition for succeeding, succeeding unwholesome states by proximity condition, and that is repetition, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by proximity condition; it is a condition by repetition condition.'

Nanu [V 0.0412] purimā purimā kiriyābyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca [T 0.0542] āsevanāti? Āmantā. Hañci purimā purimā kiriyābyākatā dhammā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ kiriyābyākatānaṃ dhammānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo, sā ca āsevanā, tena vata re vattabbe – “anantarapaccayena paccayo, āsevanapaccayena paccayo”ti.

Are not preceding, preceding functional indeterminate states a condition for succeeding, succeeding functional indeterminate states by proximity condition, and is that not repetition? Yes. If preceding, preceding functional indeterminate states are a condition for succeeding, succeeding functional indeterminate states by proximity condition, and that is repetition, then surely it should be said: 'It is a condition by proximity condition; it is a condition by repetition condition.'

717. Na vattabbaṃ – “paccayatā vavatthitā”ti? Āmantā. Hetupaccayena paccayo hoti, ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo hoti, anantarapaccayena paccayo hoti, samanantarapaccayena paccayo hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi paccayatā vavatthitāti.

717. Should it not be said: 'Conditionality is established'? It should not be said. Is it a condition by root condition, a condition by object condition, a condition by proximity condition, or a condition by contiguity condition? It should not be said thus. Then in that case, conditionality is established.

Paccayatākathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on conditionality is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter.

(146) 2. Aññamaññapaccayakathā

2. The Discourse on the Mutuality Condition

718. Avijjāpaccayāva saṅkhārā, na vattabbaṃ – “saṅkhārapaccayāpi avijjā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu avijjā saṅkhārena sahajātāti? Āmantā[P 0.0511]. Hañci avijjā saṅkhārena sahajātā, tena vata re vattabbe – “avijjāpaccayāpi saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayāpi avijjā”ti.

718. Are formations conditioned only by ignorance, and should it not be said, 'Ignorance is also conditioned by formations'? It should not be said. Is not ignorance co-nascent with formations? Yes. If ignorance is co-nascent with formations, then surely it should be said: 'Formations are also conditioned by ignorance, and ignorance is also conditioned by formations.'

Taṇhāpaccayāva upādānaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “upādānapaccayāpi taṇhā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu taṇhā upādānena sahajātāti? Āmantā. Hañci taṇhā upādānena [M 0.0371] sahajātā, tena vata re vattabbe – “taṇhāpaccayāpi upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayāpi taṇhā”ti.

Is clinging conditioned only by craving, and should it not be said, 'Craving is also conditioned by clinging'? It should not be said. Is not craving co-nascent with clinging? Yes. If craving is co-nascent with clinging, then surely it should be said: 'Clinging is also conditioned by craving, and craving is also conditioned by clinging.'

719. “Jarāmaraṇapaccayā[T 0.0543], bhikkhave, jāti, jātipaccayā bhavo”ti – attheva suttantoti[V 0.0413]? Natthi. Tena hi avijjāpaccayāva saṅkhārā, na vattabbaṃ – “saṅkhārapaccayāpi avijjā”ti. Taṇhāpaccayāva upādānaṃ, na vattabbaṃ – “upādānapaccayāpi taṇhā”ti.

719. “Bhikkhus, conditioned by aging and death is birth; conditioned by birth is existence”—is there indeed such a Sutta passage? There is not. Therefore, formations are conditioned only by ignorance; it should not be said, “Ignorance is also conditioned by formations.” Clinging is conditioned only by craving; it should not be said, “Craving is also conditioned by clinging.”

“Viññāṇapaccayā, bhikkhave, nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayāpi viññāṇa”nti dī. ni. 2.58, thokaṃ pana visadisaṃ – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi avijjāpaccayāpi saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayāpi avijjā; taṇhāpaccayāpi upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayāpi taṇhāti.

“Bhikkhus, conditioned by consciousness is name-and-form; and conditioned by name-and-form is consciousness”—is there indeed such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, formations are also conditioned by ignorance, and ignorance is also conditioned by formations; clinging is also conditioned by craving, and craving is also conditioned by clinging.

Aññamaññapaccayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Mutual Conditionality is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(147) 3. Addhākathā

(147) 3. Discourse on Time

720. Addhā parinipphannoti? Āmantā. Rūpanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīto addhā parinipphannoti? Āmantā. Rūpanti[P 0.0512]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgato addhā parinipphannoti? Āmantā. Rūpanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppanno [T 0.0544] addhā parinipphannoti? Āmantā. Rūpanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

720. Is time a produced phenomenon? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling?… and so on… Is it perception?… and so on… Are they formations?… and so on… Is it consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is past time a produced phenomenon? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling?… and so on… Is it perception?… and so on… Are they formations?… and so on… Is it consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is future time a produced phenomenon? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling?… and so on… Is it perception?… and so on… Are they formations?… and so on… Is it consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is present time a produced phenomenon? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling?… and so on… Is it perception?… and so on… Are they formations?… and so on… Is it consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atītaṃ rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ atīto addhāti? Āmantā. Atītā pañcaddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ rūpaṃ vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ anāgato addhāti? Āmantā. Anāgatā pañcaddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ rūpaṃ [V 0.0414] vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ paccuppanno addhāti? Āmantā. Paccuppannā pañcaddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is past form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness the past time? Yes. Are the past aggregates five times? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is future form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness the future time? Yes. Are the future aggregates five times? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is present form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness the present time? Yes. Are the present aggregates five times? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atītā pañcakkhandhā [M 0.0372] atīto addhā, anāgatā pañcakkhandhā anāgato addhā, paccuppannā pañcakkhandhā paccuppanno addhāti? Āmantā. Pannarasaddhāti[P 0.0513]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the past five aggregates the past time, the future five aggregates the future time, and the present five aggregates the present time? Yes. Are there fifteen times? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atītāni dvādasāyatanāni atīto addhā, anāgatāni dvādasāyatanāni anāgato addhā, paccuppannāni dvādasāyatanāni paccuppanno addhāti? Āmantā. Chattiṃsa addhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the past twelve bases the past time, the future twelve bases the future time, and the present twelve bases the present time? Yes. Are there thirty-six times? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atītā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo atīto addhā, anāgatā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo anāgato addhā, paccuppannā aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo paccuppanno addhāti? Āmantā. Catupaññāsa addhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the past eighteen elements the past time, the future eighteen elements the future time, and the present eighteen elements the present time? Yes. Are there fifty-four times? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atītāni bāvīsatindriyāni atīto addhā, anāgatāni bāvīsatindriyāni anāgato addhā, paccuppannāni bāvīsatindriyāni paccuppanno [T 0.0545] addhāti? Āmantā. Chasaṭṭhi addhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Are the past twenty-two faculties the past time, the future twenty-two faculties the future time, and the present twenty-two faculties the present time? Yes. Are there sixty-six times? It should not be said thus… and so on…

721. Na vattabbaṃ – “addhā parinipphannoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, kathāvatthūni! Katamāni tīṇi? Atītaṃ vā, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ ahosi atītamaddhāna’nti; anāgataṃ vā, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ bhavissati anāgatamaddhāna’nti; etarahi vā, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ hoti etarahi paccuppanna’nti. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi kathāvatthūnī”ti a. ni. 3.68; dī. ni. 3.305. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi addhā parinipphannoti.

721. Should it not be said that 'time is a produced phenomenon'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Bhikkhus, there are these three grounds for discourse. What three? One might speak with reference to the past, saying, ‘Thus it was in the past’; or, bhikkhus, one might speak with reference to the future, saying, ‘Thus it will be in the future’; or, bhikkhus, one might speak with reference to the present, saying, ‘Thus it is now in the present.’ These, bhikkhus, are the three grounds for discourse.” Is there indeed such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, time is a produced phenomenon.

Addhākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Time is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(148) 4. Khaṇalayamuhuttakathā

(148) 4. Discourse on Moments, Instants, and Short Periods

722. Khaṇo [P 0.0514][V 0.0415] parinipphanno, layo parinipphanno, muhuttaṃ parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Rūpanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

722. Is a moment a produced phenomenon? Is an instant a produced phenomenon? Is a short period a produced phenomenon? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling… perception… formations… consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on…

723. Na [M 0.0373] vattabbaṃ – “muhuttaṃ parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, kathāvatthūni! Katamāni tīṇi? Atītaṃ vā, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ ahosi atītamaddhāna’nti; anāgataṃ [T 0.0546] vā, bhikkhave, addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ bhavissati anāgatamaddhāna’nti; etarahi vā, bhikkhave, paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ hoti etarahi paccuppanna’nti. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi kathāvatthūnī”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi muhuttaṃ parinipphannanti.

723. Should it not be said that 'a short period is a produced phenomenon'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: 'Bhikkhus, there are these three grounds for discourse. What three? One might speak with reference to the past, saying, “Thus it was in the past”; or, bhikkhus, one might speak with reference to the future, saying, “Thus it will be in the future”; or, bhikkhus, one might speak with reference to the present, saying, “Thus it is now in the present.” These, bhikkhus, are the three grounds for discourse.' Is there indeed such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, a short period is a produced phenomenon.

Khaṇalayamuhuttakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Moments, Instants, and Short Periods is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(149) 5. Āsavakathā

(149) 5. Discourse on the Taints

724. Cattāro āsavā anāsavāti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

724. Are the four taints taintless? Yes. Are they the path, the fruit, Nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… and so on… the factors of enlightenment? It should not be said thus… and so on…

725. Na vattabbaṃ – “cattāro āsavā anāsavāti? Āmantā. Atthaññeva āsavā yehi [V 0.0416] āsavehi te āsavā sāsavā hontīti? Na [P 0.0515] hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi cattāro āsavā anāsavāti.

725. Should it not be said: 'The four taints are taintless'? Yes. But are there other taints by which those taints become tainted? It should not be said thus. Therefore, the four taints are taintless.

Āsavakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Taints is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(150) 6. Jarāmaraṇakathā

(150) 6. Discourse on Aging and Death

726. Lokuttarānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ lokuttaranti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… bojjhaṅgoti[T 0.0547]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpattimaggassa jarāmaraṇaṃ sotāpattimaggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpattimaggassa jarāmaraṇaṃ sotāpattimaggoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalassa jarāmaraṇaṃ sotāpattiphalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [M 0.0374]…pe… sakadāgāmimaggassa…pe… sakadāgāmiphalassa…pe… anāgāmimaggassa…pe… anāgāmiphalassa…pe… arahattamaggassa jarāmaraṇaṃ arahattamaggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattamaggassa jarāmaraṇaṃ arahattamaggoti? Āmantā. Arahattaphalassa jarāmaraṇaṃ arahattaphalanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… satipaṭṭhānānaṃ… sammappadhānānaṃ… iddhipādānaṃ… indriyānaṃ… balānaṃ… bojjhaṅgānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

726. Is the aging and death of supramundane phenomena supramundane? Yes. Are they the path, the fruit, Nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… and so on… the factors of enlightenment? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the aging and death of the path of stream-entry the path of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the aging and death of the path of stream-entry the path of stream-entry? Yes. Is the aging and death of the fruit of stream-entry the fruit of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… and so on… of the path of the once-returner… and so on… of the fruit of the once-returner… and so on… of the path of the non-returner… and so on… of the fruit of the non-returner… and so on… Is the aging and death of the path of arahantship the path of arahantship? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the aging and death of the path of arahantship the path of arahantship? Yes. Is the aging and death of the fruit of arahantship the fruit of arahantship? It should not be said thus… and so on… of the foundations of mindfulness… the right strivings… the bases for spiritual power… the spiritual faculties… the powers… Is the aging and death of the factors of enlightenment the factors of enlightenment? It should not be said thus… and so on…

727. Na vattabbaṃ – “lokuttarānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ lokuttaranti? Āmantā. Lokiyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi lokuttaranti.

727. Should it not be said that the aging and death of supramundane phenomena is supramundane? Yes. Is it mundane? It should not be said thus. In that case, it is supramundane.

Jarāmaraṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Aging and Death is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(151) 7. Saññāvedayitakathā

(151) 7. Discourse on Perception and Feeling

728. Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti [P 0.0516][V 0.0417] lokuttarāti? Āmantā. Maggo phalaṃ nibbānaṃ, sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… bojjhaṅgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

728. Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling supramundane? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, Nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… and so on… a factor of enlightenment? It should not be said thus… and so on…

729. Na vattabbaṃ – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti [T 0.0548] lokuttarāti? Āmantā. Lokiyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi lokuttarāti.

729. Should it not be said that the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is supramundane? Yes. Is it mundane? It should not be said thus. Therefore, it is supramundane.

Saññāvedayitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Perception and Feeling is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(152) 8. Dutiyasaññāvedayitakathā

(152) 8. Second Discourse on Perception and Feeling

730. Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti lokiyāti? Āmantā. Rūpanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāmāvacarāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpāvacarāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūpāvacarāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

730. Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling mundane? Yes. Is it form? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it feeling… perception… formations… consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it of the sense-sphere? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it of the form-sphere? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it of the formless-sphere? It should not be said thus… and so on…

731. Na [M 0.0375] vattabbaṃ – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti lokiyāti? Āmantā. Lokuttarāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi lokiyāti.

731. Should it not be said that the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is mundane? Yes. Is it supramundane? It should not be said thus. Therefore, it is mundane.

Dutiyasaññāvedayitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Second Discourse on Perception and Feeling is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(153) 9. Tatiyasaññāvedayitakathā

(153) 9. Third Discourse on Perception and Feeling

732. Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ [P 0.0517][V 0.0418] samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa māraṇantiyo phasso, māraṇantiyā vedanā, māraṇantiyā saññā, māraṇantiyā cetanā[T 0.0549], māraṇantiyaṃ cittanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa māraṇantiyo phasso, māraṇantiyā vedanā, māraṇantiyā saññā, māraṇantiyā cetanā, māraṇantiyaṃ cittanti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa māraṇantiyo phasso, māraṇantiyā vedanā, māraṇantiyā saññā, māraṇantiyā cetanā, māraṇantiyaṃ cittaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyā”ti.

732. Can one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, is there a death-ending contact, a death-ending feeling, a death-ending perception, a death-ending volition, a death-ending consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, is there no death-ending contact, no death-ending feeling, no death-ending perception, no death-ending volition, no death-ending consciousness? Yes. If for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling there is no death-ending contact, feeling, perception, volition, or consciousness, then surely it should not be said: 'One who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling can die.'

Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittanti? Āmantā. Aphassakassa kālaṃ kiriyā, avedanakassa kālaṃ kiriyā…pe… acittakassa kālaṃ kiriyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphassakassa kālaṃ kiriyā…pe… sacittakassa kālaṃ kiriyāti? Āmantā. Hañci saphassakassa kālaṃ kiriyā…pe… sacittakassa kālaṃ kiriyā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyā”ti.

Can one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Does one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling have contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Does one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling not have contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness? Yes. Does one without contact die? Does one without feeling die… and so on… Does one without consciousness die? It should not be said thus… and so on… But does not one with contact die… and so on… does not one with consciousness die? Yes. If one with contact dies… and so on… if one with consciousness dies, then surely it should not be said: 'One who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling can die.'

Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa kāye visaṃ kameyya, satthaṃ kameyya, aggi kameyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ [P 0.0518] samāpannassa kāye visaṃ na kameyya, satthaṃ na [T 0.0550] kameyya, aggi na kameyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci [M 0.0376] saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa kāye visaṃ na kameyya, satthaṃ na kameyya, aggi na kameyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyā”ti.

Can one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Could poison, a weapon, or fire affect the body of one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling? It should not be said thus… and so on… Could poison, a weapon, or fire not affect the body of one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling? Yes. If poison, a weapon, or fire could not affect the body of one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, then surely it should not be said: 'One who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling can die.'

Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ [V 0.0419] samāpanno kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa kāye visaṃ kameyya, satthaṃ kameyya, aggi kameyyāti? Āmantā. Na nirodhaṃ samāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Can one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Can poison, a weapon, or fire affect the body of one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling? Yes. Is one then not an attainer of cessation? It should not be said thus… and so on…

733. Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno na kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi so niyāmo yena niyāmena niyato saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno na kālaṃ kareyyāti? Natthi. Hañci natthi so niyāmo yena niyāmena niyato saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno na kālaṃ kareyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno na kālaṃ kareyyāti.

733. Does one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling not die? Yes. Is there a principle by which one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling is fixed as not dying? No. If there is no principle by which one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling is fixed as not dying, then surely it should not be said: 'One who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling does not die.'

734. Cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī na kālaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā. Atthi so niyāmo yena niyāmena niyato cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī na kālaṃ kareyyāti? Natthi. Hañci natthi so niyāmo yena niyāmena niyato cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī na kālaṃ kareyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhuviññāṇasamaṅgī na kālaṃ kareyyā”ti.

734. Should one endowed with eye-consciousness not die? Yes. Is there a principle by which it is determined that one endowed with eye-consciousness should not die? No. If there is no principle by which it is determined that one endowed with eye-consciousness should not die, then surely it should not be said: 'One endowed with eye-consciousness should not die.'

Tatiyasaññāvedayitakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Third Discourse on Perception and Feeling is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(154) 10. Asaññasattupikakathā

(154) 10. Discourse on Being Like the Non-percipient Beings

735. Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti [T 0.0551] asaññasattupikāti? Āmantā. Atthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa alobho kusalamūlaṃ[P 0.0519], adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ, saddhā vīriyaṃ sati samādhi paññāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa alobho kusalamūlaṃ[M 0.0377], adoso kusalamūlaṃ…pe… paññāti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso [V 0.0420] kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ, saddhā vīriyaṃ sati samādhi paññā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikā”ti.

735. Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling similar to the non-percipient beings? Yes. For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, are there the wholesome root of non-greed, the wholesome root of non-hatred, the wholesome root of non-delusion, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom? This should not be said thus… and so on… For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, are there not the wholesome root of non-greed, the wholesome root of non-hatred… and so on… and wisdom? Yes. If, for one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, there are not the wholesome root of non-greed, the wholesome root of non-hatred, the wholesome root of non-delusion, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, then it should certainly not be said, 'The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is similar to the non-percipient beings.'

Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikāti? Āmantā. Atthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa phasso vedanā saññā cetanā cittanti? Āmantā. Aphassakassa maggabhāvanā…pe… acittakassa maggabhāvanāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saphassakassa maggabhāvanā…pe… sacittakassa maggabhāvanāti? Āmantā. Hañci saphassakassa maggabhāvanā…pe… sacittakassa maggabhāvanā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikā”ti.

Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling similar to the non-percipient beings? Yes. For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, are there contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness? This should not be said thus… and so on… For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, are there not contact, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness? Yes. Is there development of the path for one without contact… and so on… for one without consciousness? This should not be said thus… and so on… Is there not development of the path for one with contact… and so on… for one with consciousness? Yes. If there is development of the path for one with contact… and so on… for one with consciousness, then it should certainly not be said, 'The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is similar to the non-percipient beings.'

Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti [T 0.0552] asaññasattupikāti? Āmantā. Ye keci saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjanti, sabbe te asaññasattupikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling similar to the non-percipient beings? Yes. Whoever attains the cessation of perception and feeling, are they all similar to the non-percipient beings? This should not be said thus… and so on…

736. Na vattabbaṃ – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu idhāpi asaññī tatrāpi asaññīti? Āmantā. Hañci idhāpi asaññī tatrāpi asaññī, tena vata re vattabbe – “saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikā”ti.

736. Should it not be said, 'The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is similar to the non-percipient beings'? Yes. Is one not non-percipient here and also non-percipient there? Yes. If one is non-percipient here and also non-percipient there, then for that reason, it should certainly be said, 'The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is similar to the non-percipient beings'.

Asaññasattupikakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Being Like the Non-percipient Beings is concluded.

15. Pannarasamavaggo

15. The Fifteenth Chapter

(155) 11. Kammūpacayakathā

(155) 11. Discourse on the Accumulation of Kamma

737. Aññaṃ [P 0.0520] kammaṃ añño kammūpacayoti? Āmantā. Añño phasso, añño phassūpacayo; aññā vedanā, añño vedanūpacayo; aññā saññā, añño saññūpacayo; aññā [V 0.0421] cetanā, añño cetanūpacayo; aññaṃ cittaṃ, añño cittūpacayo; aññā saddhā, añño saddhūpacayo; aññaṃ vīriyaṃ, añño vīriyūpacayo; aññā sati, añño satūpacayo[M 0.0378]; añño samādhi, añño samādhūpacayo; aññā paññā, añño paññūpacayo; añño rāgo, añño rāgūpacayo…pe… aññaṃ anottappaṃ, añño anottappūpacayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

737. Is kamma one thing and the accumulation of kamma another? Yes. Is contact one thing and the accumulation of contact another; is feeling one thing and the accumulation of feeling another; is perception one thing and the accumulation of perception another; is volition one thing and the accumulation of volition another; is consciousness one thing and the accumulation of consciousness another; is faith one thing and the accumulation of faith another; is energy one thing and the accumulation of energy another; is mindfulness one thing and the accumulation of mindfulness another; is concentration one thing and the accumulation of concentration another; is wisdom one thing and the accumulation of wisdom another; is lust one thing and the accumulation of lust another… and so on… is lack of moral dread one thing and the accumulation of lack of moral dread another? This should not be said thus… and so on…

738. Aññaṃ [T 0.0553] kammaṃ, añño kammūpacayoti? Āmantā. Kammūpacayo kammena sahajātoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

738. Is kamma one thing and the accumulation of kamma another? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with kamma? This should not be said thus… and so on…

Kammūpacayo kammena sahajātoti, āmantā. Kusalena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo kusaloti, na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with kamma? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with wholesome kamma wholesome? This should not be said thus… and so on…

Kusalena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo kusaloti? Āmantā. Sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dukkhāya vedanāya…pe… adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with wholesome kamma wholesome? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with kamma associated with pleasant feeling itself associated with pleasant feeling? This should not be said thus… and so on… with painful feeling… and so on… Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with kamma associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling itself associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? This should not be said thus… and so on…

739. Kammūpacayo kammena sahajātoti? Āmantā. Akusalena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo akusaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

739. Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with kamma? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with unwholesome kamma unwholesome? This should not be said thus… and so on…

Akusalena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo akusaloti? Āmantā. Sukhāya [P 0.0521] vedanāya sampayuttena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dukkhāya vedanāya…pe… adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttena kammena sahajāto kammūpacayo adukkhamasukhāya vedanāya sampayuttoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with unwholesome kamma unwholesome? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with kamma associated with pleasant feeling itself associated with pleasant feeling? This should not be said thus… and so on… with painful feeling… and so on… Is the accumulation of kamma that is co-arisen with kamma associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling itself associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? This should not be said thus… and so on…

740. Kammaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ, kammaṃ sārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Kammūpacayo cittena sahajāto, kammūpacayo sārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kammūpacayo cittena sahajāto[V 0.0422], kammūpacayo anārammaṇoti[T 0.0554]? Āmantā. Kammaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ, kammaṃ anārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

740. Is kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and is kamma with an object? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and is the accumulation of kamma with an object? This should not be said thus… and so on… Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and is the accumulation of kamma without an object? Yes. Is kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and is kamma without an object? This should not be said thus… and so on…

Kammaṃ [M 0.0379] cittena sahajātaṃ, cittaṃ bhijjamānaṃ kammaṃ bhijjatīti? Āmantā. Kammūpacayo cittena sahajāto, cittaṃ bhijjamānaṃ kammūpacayo bhijjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and when consciousness ceases, does kamma cease? Yes. Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and when consciousness ceases, does the accumulation of kamma cease? This should not be said thus… and so on…

Kammūpacayo cittena sahajāto, cittaṃ bhijjamānaṃ kammūpacayo na bhijjatīti? Āmantā. Kammaṃ cittena sahajātaṃ, cittaṃ bhijjamānaṃ kammaṃ na bhijjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the accumulation of kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and when consciousness ceases, does the accumulation of kamma not cease? Yes. Is kamma co-arisen with consciousness, and when consciousness ceases, does kamma not cease? This should not be said thus… and so on…

741. Kammamhi kammūpacayoti? Āmantā. Taññeva kammaṃ so kammūpacayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

741. “When there is kamma, is there an accumulation of kamma?” “Yes.” “Is that very kamma the accumulation of kamma?” “This should not be said.” …

Kammamhi kammūpacayo, kammūpacayato vipāko nibbattatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva [P 0.0522] kammaṃ, so kammūpacayo, so kammavipākoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“When there is kamma, is there an accumulation of kamma, and from the accumulation of kamma, is a result produced?” “Yes.” “Is that very kamma the accumulation of kamma, and is that accumulation of kamma the result of kamma?” “This should not be said.” …

Kammamhi kammūpacayo, kammūpacayato vipāko nibbattati, vipāko sārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Kammūpacayo sārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kammūpacayo anārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Vipāko anārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“When there is kamma, is there an accumulation of kamma; from the accumulation of kamma, is a result produced; and is that result accompanied by an object?” “Yes.” “Is the accumulation of kamma accompanied by an object?” “This should not be said.” … “Is the accumulation of kamma not accompanied by an object?” “Yes.” “Is the result not accompanied by an object?” “This should not be said.” …

742. Aññaṃ kammaṃ añño kammūpacayoti, āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, puṇṇa, ekacco sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi sabyāpajjhampi abyāpajjhampi (ka.) ma. ni. 2.81 passitabbaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ…pe… manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, so sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi [T 0.0555] abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṃ…pe… manosaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharitvā sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapajjati. Tamenaṃ sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṃ upapannaṃ samānaṃ sabyābajjhāpi abyābajjhāpi phassā phusanti. So sabyābajjhehipi abyābajjhehipi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vedanaṃ vedeti vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṃ, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce [V 0.0423] ca vinipātikā. Iti kho, puṇṇa, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti, yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati, upapannametaṃ phassā phusanti. Evampāhaṃ, puṇṇa, ‘kammadāyādā [M 0.0380] sattā’ti vadāmī”ti ma. ni. 2.81. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “aññaṃ kammaṃ, añño kammūpacayo”ti.

742. “Is kamma one thing, and the accumulation of kamma another?” “Yes.” “But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, Puṇṇa, someone generates bodily formations that are both vexatious and non-vexatious, verbal formations that are both vexatious and non-vexatious… mental formations that are both vexatious and non-vexatious. Having generated bodily formations that are both vexatious and non-vexatious, verbal formations… mental formations that are both vexatious and non-vexatious, they are reborn into a world that is both vexatious and non-vexatious. Being reborn into a world that is both vexatious and non-vexatious, they are touched by contacts that are both vexatious and non-vexatious. Touched by contacts that are both vexatious and non-vexatious, they experience a feeling that is both vexatious and non-vexatious, a mixture of pleasure and pain, just like some humans, some devas, and some beings in states of deprivation. Thus, Puṇṇa, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be; one is reborn by what one does; having been reborn, contacts touch them. In this way, Puṇṇa, I say that beings are heirs to their kamma.’ Is there such a suttanta?” “Yes.” “Therefore, it should not be said, ‘kamma is one thing, and the accumulation of kamma is another.’”

Kammūpacayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Accumulation of Kamma is concluded.

Pannarasamavaggo.

The Fifteenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Paccayatā [P 0.0523] vavatthitā, paṭiccasamuppādo, addhā, khaṇo layo muhuttaṃ, cattāro āsavā anāsavā, lokuttarānaṃ dhammānaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ lokuttarā, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti lokuttarā, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti lokiyā, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno kālaṃ kareyya, sveva maggo asaññasattupapattiyā[T 0.0556], aññaṃ kammaṃ añño kammūpacayoti.

Conditionality and determination, dependent origination; duration, instant, moment, short time; the four taints and the taintless; aging and death for supramundane states; the attainment of cessation as supramundane; the attainment of cessation as mundane; dying while in the attainment of cessation; the path to rebirth among non-percipient beings; and that kamma is one thing and its accumulation another.

Tatiyo paṇṇāsako.

The Third Set of Fifty.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Anusayā, saṃvaro, kappo, mūlañca vavatthitāti.

Latent tendencies, restraint, an eon, and roots are determined.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

The Sixteenth Chapter

(156) 1. Niggahakathā

(156) 1. The Discourse on Restraint

743. Paro [P 0.0524] parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa cittaṃ “mā rajji”, “mā dussi”, “mā muyhi”, “mā kilissī”ti niggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa uppanno phasso “mā nirujjhī”ti niggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa uppannā vedanā…pe… uppannā saññā… uppannā cetanā… uppannaṃ cittaṃ… uppannā saddhā… uppannaṃ vīriyaṃ [V 0.0424]… uppannā sati… uppanno samādhi…pe… uppannā paññā “mā nirujjhī”ti niggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

16. “Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Does one person restrain the mind of another, thinking, ‘May it not be lustful,’ ‘May it not be hateful,’ ‘May it not be deluded,’ ‘May it not be defiled’?” “This should not be said.” … “Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Does one person restrain the arisen contact of another, thinking, ‘May it not cease’?” “This should not be said.” … “Does one person restrain the arisen feeling of another… arisen perception… arisen volition… arisen consciousness… arisen faith… arisen energy… arisen mindfulness… arisen concentration… arisen wisdom, thinking, ‘May it not cease’?” “This should not be said.” …

Paro [M 0.0381] parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya rāgaṃ pajahati… dosaṃ pajahati…pe… anottappaṃ pajahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Does one person, for the benefit of another, abandon lust… abandon hatred… abandon lack of moral dread?” “This should not be said.” …

Paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya maggaṃ bhāveti… satipaṭṭhānaṃ bhāveti…pe… bojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetīti[T 0.0557]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

743. “Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Does one person, for the benefit of another, develop the path… develop the foundations of mindfulness… develop the factors of enlightenment?” “This should not be said.” …

Paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya dukkhaṃ parijānāti, samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Does one person, for the benefit of another, fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path?” “This should not be said.” …

Paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Añño [P 0.0525] aññassa kārako, paraṅkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

“Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “Is one person the agent of another? Is happiness and suffering created by another? Does one person act while another experiences the result?” “This should not be said.” …

Paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

“Does one person restrain the mind of another?” “Yes.” “But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Attanāva kataṃ pāpaṃ, attanā saṃkilissati;

Attanā akataṃ pāpaṃ, attanāva visujjhati;

Suddhi asuddhi paccattaṃ, nāñño aññaṃ visodhaye”ti dha. pa. 165.

‘By oneself is evil done, by oneself is one defiled. By oneself evil is not done, by oneself is one purified. Purity and impurity are personal; one person cannot purify another.’

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātī”ti.

“Is there not such a suttanta?” “Yes.” “Therefore, it should not be said: ‘One person restrains the mind of another.’”

744. Na vattabbaṃ – “paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi balappattā, atthi vasībhūtāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi balappattā, atthi vasībhūtā, tena vata re vattabbe – “paro parassa cittaṃ niggaṇhātī”ti.

“Should it not be said, ‘One person restrains the mind of another’?” “Indeed, it should not be said.” “But are there not those who have attained the powers, are there not those who have attained mastery?” “Yes.” “If there are those who have attained the powers and those who have attained mastery, then indeed, sir, it should be said: ‘One person restrains the mind of another.’”

Niggahakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Restraint is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

744. The Sixteenth Chapter

(157) 2. Paggahakathā

(157) 2. The Discourse on Uplifting

745. Paro [T 0.0558][V 0.0425] parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa cittaṃ “mā rajji,”“mā dussi,”“mā muyhi,”“mā kilissī”ti paggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro [M 0.0382] parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa alobhaṃ kusalamūlaṃ janeti… adosaṃ kusalamūlaṃ [P 0.0526] janeti… amohaṃ kusalamūlaṃ janeti… saddhaṃ janeti… vīriyaṃ janeti… satiṃ janeti… samādhiṃ janeti… paññaṃ janetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa uppanno phasso “mā nirujjhī”ti paggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa uppannā vedanā…pe… uppannā paññā “mā nirujjhī”ti paggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

745. Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person uplift another's mind, thinking, 'Let it not be lustful,' 'Let it not be hateful,' 'Let it not be deluded,' 'Let it not be defiled'? It should not be said thus... Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person generate in another the wholesome root of non-greed... non-hatred... non-delusion... faith... energy... mindfulness... concentration... wisdom? It should not be said thus... Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person uplift another's arisen contact, thinking, 'Let it not cease'? It should not be said thus... Does one person uplift another's arisen feeling... arisen wisdom, thinking, 'Let it not cease'? It should not be said thus...

Paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya rāgaṃ pajahati… dosaṃ pajahati… mohaṃ pajahati…pe… anottappaṃ pajahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person, for another's benefit, abandon passion... abandon hatred... abandon delusion... abandon lack of moral dread? It should not be said thus...

Paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya maggaṃ bhāveti… satipaṭṭhānaṃ bhāveti…pe… bojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person, for another's benefit, develop the path... develop the foundations of mindfulness... develop the factors of enlightenment? It should not be said thus...

Paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa atthāya dukkhaṃ parijānāti…pe… maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Does one person, for another's benefit, fully comprehend suffering... develop the path? It should not be said thus...

Paro [T 0.0559] parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Añño aññassa kārako, paraṅkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. Is one person the agent for another? Is happiness and suffering made by another? Does one person act and another experience it? It should not be said thus...

Paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “attanāva [P 0.0527] kataṃ pāpaṃ…pe… nāñño aññaṃ visodhaye”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

Does one person uplift another's mind? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'By oneself is evil done... another does not purify another'? Is there indeed such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: 'One person uplifts another's mind.'

746. Na [V 0.0426] vattabbaṃ – “paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi balappattā, atthi vasībhūtāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi balappattā, atthi vasībhūtā, tena vata re vattabbe – “paro parassa cittaṃ paggaṇhātī”ti.

746. Should it not be said: 'One person uplifts another's mind'? Yes. But are there not those who have attained the powers, and those who have attained mastery? Yes. If there are those who have attained the powers and those who have attained mastery, then indeed, sir, it should be said: 'One person uplifts another's mind.'

Paggahakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Uplifting is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(158) 3. Sukhānuppadānakathā

(158) 3. Discourse on the Bestowing of Happiness

747. Paro [M 0.0383] parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa dukkhaṃ anuppadetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa dukkhaṃ na anuppadetīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa sukhaṃ na [T 0.0560] anuppadetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti? Āmantā. Paro parassa attano sukhaṃ anuppadeti, aññesaṃ sukhaṃ anuppadeti, tassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paro parassa nevattano, na aññesaṃ, na tassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti? Āmantā. Hañci paro parassa nevattano, na aññesaṃ, na tassa sukhaṃ [P 0.0528] anuppadeti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “paro parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetī”ti.

747. Does one person bestow happiness on another? Yes. Does one person bestow suffering on another? It should not be said thus... Does one person not bestow suffering on another? Yes. Does one person not bestow happiness on another? It should not be said thus... Does one person bestow happiness on another? Yes. Does one person bestow on another his own happiness, the happiness of others, or that person's happiness? It should not be said thus... Does one person bestow on another happiness that is neither his own, nor others', nor that person's? Yes. If one person bestows on another happiness that is neither his own, nor others', nor that person's, then indeed, sir, it should not be said: 'One person bestows happiness on another.'

Paro parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti? Āmantā. Añño aññassa kārako, paraṅkataṃ sukhaṃ dukkhaṃ añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one person bestow happiness on another? Yes. Is one person the agent for another? Is happiness and suffering made by another? Does one person act and another experience it? It should not be said thus...

748. Na vattabbaṃ – “paro parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā udāyī etadavoca – “bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā dukkhadhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā sukhadhammānaṃ upahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ apahattā, bahūnaṃ vata no bhagavā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upahattā”ti ma. ni. 2.148 laṭukikopame! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi paro parassa sukhaṃ anuppadetīti.

748. Should it not be said: 'One person bestows happiness on another'? Yes. But did not the Venerable Udāyī say this: 'Truly, for us, the Blessed One is the remover of many states of suffering; truly, for us, the Blessed One is the bringer of many states of happiness; truly, for us, the Blessed One is the remover of many unwholesome states; truly, for us, the Blessed One is the bringer of many wholesome states'? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, one person bestows happiness on another.

Sukhānuppadānakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Bestowing of Happiness is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(159) 4. Adhigayhamanasikārakathā

Discourse on Complete Attention

749. Adhigayha [T 0.0561][V 0.0427] manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ pajānātīti? Āmantā[M 0.0384]. Tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ “citta”nti pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena cittena taṃ cittaṃ “citta”nti pajānātīti? Āmantā. Taṃ cittaṃ tassa cittassa ārammaṇanti? Na [P 0.0529] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

749. Does one attend completely? Yes. Does one discern that consciousness with that consciousness? It should not be said thus... Does one discern that consciousness with that consciousness? Yes. Does one discern that consciousness as 'consciousness' with that consciousness? It should not be said thus... Does one discern that consciousness as 'consciousness' with that consciousness? Yes. Is that consciousness an object for that consciousness? It should not be said thus...

Taṃ cittaṃ tassa cittassa ārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Tena phassena taṃ phassaṃ phusati, tāya vedanāya…pe… tāya saññāya… tāya cetanāya… tena cittena… tena vitakkena… tena vicārena… tāya pītiyā… tāya satiyā… tāya paññāya taṃ paññaṃ pajānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is that consciousness an object for that consciousness? Yes. Does one contact that contact by means of that contact, feel that feeling by means of that feeling... perceive that perception by means of that perception... intend that volition by means of that volition... cognize that consciousness by means of that consciousness... apply that initial application by means of that initial application... sustain that sustained application by means of that sustained application... experience that joy by means of that joy... be mindful by means of that mindfulness... discern that wisdom by means of that wisdom? It should not be said thus...

750. Atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

750. Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the future as 'future'? It should not be said thus... Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the future as 'future'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts... two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasikaronto, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasikaronto, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the present as 'present'? It should not be said thus... Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the present as 'present'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts... two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus...

Atītaṃ [T 0.0562] “atīta”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karoti, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti [V 0.0428] manasi karoti, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… tiṇṇaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the future as 'future' and to the present as 'present'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the past as 'past' attend to the future as 'future' and to the present as 'present'? Yes. Is there a convergence of three contacts…pe… three consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

751. Anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karotīti? Na [P 0.0530] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

751. Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the past as 'past'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the past as 'past'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts…pe… two consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

Anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the present as 'present'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the present as 'present'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts…pe… two consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

Anāgataṃ [M 0.0385] “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karoti, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karoti, paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… tiṇṇaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the past as 'past' and to the present as 'present'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the future as 'future' attend to the past as 'past' and to the present as 'present'? Yes. Is there a convergence of three contacts…pe… three consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

752. Paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto[T 0.0563], atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

752. Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the past as 'past'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the past as 'past'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts…pe… two consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

Paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Na [P 0.0531] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the future as 'future'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the future as 'future'? Yes. Is there a convergence of two contacts…pe… two consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

Paccuppannaṃ [V 0.0429] “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karoti, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paccuppannaṃ “paccuppanna”nti manasikaronto, atītaṃ “atīta”nti manasi karoti, anāgataṃ “anāgata”nti manasi karotīti? Āmantā. Tiṇṇaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… tiṇṇaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the past as 'past' and to the future as 'future'? That should not be said…pe… Does one who attends to the present as 'present' attend to the past as 'past' and to the future as 'future'? Yes. Is there a convergence of three contacts…pe… three consciousnesses? That should not be said…pe…

753. Na vattabbaṃ – “adhigayha manasi karotī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

753. Should it not be said: “One attends by grasping completely”? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti, yadā paññāya passati;

Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.

“All conditioned phenomena are impermanent”—when one sees this with wisdom, then one becomes disenchanted with suffering. This is the path to purification.

“Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhāti, yadā paññāya passati;

Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.

“All conditioned phenomena are suffering”—when one sees this with wisdom, then one becomes disenchanted with suffering. This is the path to purification.

“Sabbe [T 0.0564] dhammā anattāti, yadā paññāya passati;

Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā”ti dha. pa. 277-279.

“All phenomena are not-self”—when one sees this with wisdom, then one becomes disenchanted with suffering. This is the path to purification.

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi adhigayha manasi karotīti.

Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, one attends by grasping completely.

Adhigayhamanasikārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Attention by Grasping Completely is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(160) 5. Rūpaṃ hetūtikathā

16. 5. Discussion on ‘Is Form a Condition?’

754. Rūpaṃ [M 0.0386][P 0.0532] hetūti? Āmantā. Alobho hetūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adoso hetu…pe… amoho hetu… lobho hetu… doso hetu… moho hetūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….
