Is form a condition? Yes. Is non-greed a condition? That should not be said…pe… Is non-hatred a condition…pe… is non-delusion a condition… is greed a condition… is hatred a condition… is delusion a condition? That should not be said…pe…

Rūpaṃ [V 0.0430] hetūti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ hetū”ti.

754. Is form a condition? Yes. Is it with an object, is there a turning towards it…pe… a directing of the mind to it? That should not be said…pe… But is it not without an object, is there no turning towards it…pe… no directing of the mind to it? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is no turning towards it…pe… no directing of the mind to it, then indeed it should not be said that ‘form is a condition.’

755. Alobho hetu sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ hetu sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adoso hetu… amoho hetu… lobho hetu… doso hetu… moho hetu sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ [T 0.0565] hetu sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is non-greed a condition with an object, is there a turning towards it…pe… a directing of the mind to it? Yes. Is form a condition with an object, is there a turning towards it…pe… a directing of the mind to it? That should not be said…pe… Is non-hatred a condition… is non-delusion a condition… is greed a condition… is hatred a condition… is delusion a condition with an object, is there a turning towards it…pe… a directing of the mind to it? Yes. Is form a condition with an object, is there a turning towards it…pe… a directing of the mind to it? That should not be said…pe…

Rūpaṃ hetu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Alobho hetu anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ hetu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0533]. Adoso hetu… amoho hetu… lobho hetu… doso hetu… moho hetu anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is form a root, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? Yes. Is non-greed a root, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? It should not be said thus... Is form a root, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? Yes. Is non-hatred a root... non-delusion a root... greed a root... hatred a root... delusion a root, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? It should not be said thus...

756. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūpaṃ hetū”ti? Āmantā. Nanu mahābhūtā upādāyarūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) upādāyahetūti? Āmantā. Hañci mahābhūtā upādāyarūpānaṃ upādāyahetu, tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ hetū”ti.

Should it not be said that ‘form is a condition’? Yes. But are not the great elements a supporting condition for derived form? Yes. If the great elements are a supporting condition for derived form, then indeed it should be said that ‘form is a condition.’

Rūpaṃ hetūtikathā niṭṭhitā.

756. The Discussion on ‘Is Form a Condition?’ is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(161) 6. Rūpaṃ sahetukantikathā

Discussion on Whether Material Form is with a Cause

757. Rūpaṃ [M 0.0387] sahetukanti? Āmantā. Alobhahetunāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adosahetunāti [V 0.0431] …pe… amohahetunāti…pe… lobhahetunā…pe… dosahetunā…pe… mohahetunāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

757. Is material form with a cause? Yes. Is it with the cause of non-greed? It should not be said thus. … Is it with the cause of non-hatred? … Is it with the cause of non-delusion? … Is it with the cause of greed? … Is it with the cause of hatred? … Is it with the cause of delusion? It should not be said thus. …

Rūpaṃ [T 0.0566] sahetukanti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ sahetuka”nti.

Is material form with a cause? Yes. Is it with an object? Is there for it turning towards… directing the mind? It should not be said thus. … Is it not, in fact, without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… directing the mind? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is not for it turning towards… directing the mind, then, good sir, it should not be said that 'material form is with a cause'.

758. Alobho sahetuko sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ sahetukaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… adoso [P 0.0534] sahetuko…pe… amoho… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi… paññā… lobho… doso… moho… māno… diṭṭhi… vicikicchā… thinaṃ… uddhaccaṃ… ahirikaṃ… anottappaṃ sahetukaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ sahetukaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

758. Is non-greed with a cause and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… directing the mind? Yes. Is material form with a cause and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… directing the mind? It should not be said thus. … Is non-hatred with a cause… non-delusion… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom… greed… hatred… delusion… conceit… wrong view… doubt… sloth… restlessness… lack of shame… lack of fear of wrongdoing with a cause and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… directing the mind? Yes. Is material form with a cause and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… directing the mind? It should not be said thus. …

Rūpaṃ sahetukaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Alobho sahetuko anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ sahetukaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Adoso sahetuko…pe… anottappaṃ sahetukaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is material form with a cause and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… directing the mind? Yes. Is non-greed with a cause and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… directing the mind? It should not be said thus. … Is material form with a cause and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… directing the mind? Yes. Is non-hatred with a cause… lack of fear of wrongdoing with a cause and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… directing the mind? It should not be said thus. …

759. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūpaṃ sahetuka”nti? Āmantā. Nanu rūpaṃ sappaccayanti[T 0.0567]? Āmantā. Hañci rūpaṃ sappaccayaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ sahetuka”nti.

759. Is it incorrect to say, 'material form is with a cause'? Yes. Is not material form, in fact, dependent on conditions? Yes. If material form is dependent on conditions, then, good sir, it should indeed be said that 'material form is with a cause'.

Rūpaṃ sahetukantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Whether Material Form is with a Cause is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(162) 7. Rūpaṃ kusalākusalantikathā

Discussion on Whether Material Form is Wholesome or Unwholesome

760. Rūpaṃ [M 0.0388][V 0.0432] kusalanti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci [P 0.0535] anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ kusala”nti.

760. Is material form wholesome? Yes. Is it with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. … Is it not, in fact, without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is not for it turning towards… aspiration, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said, 'Material form is wholesome.'

761. Alobho kusalo sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ kusalaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

761. Is non-greed wholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is material form wholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. …

Adoso kusalo…pe… amoho kusalo…pe… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā kusalā sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ kusalaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is non-hatred wholesome… non-delusion wholesome… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… is wisdom wholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is material form wholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. …

Rūpaṃ kusalaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Alobho kusalo anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā [T 0.0568] …pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is material form wholesome and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is non-greed wholesome and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. …

Rūpaṃ kusalaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Adoso kusalo…pe… paññā kusalā anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is material form wholesome and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is non-hatred wholesome… is wisdom wholesome and without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. …

762. Rūpaṃ akusalanti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti[V 0.0433]? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ akusala”nti…pe….

762. Is material form unwholesome? Yes. Is it with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. … Is it not, in fact, without an object? Is there not for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object and there is not for it turning towards… aspiration, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said, 'Material form is unwholesome.'…

763. Lobho akusalo sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0536]. Rūpaṃ akusalaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… doso… moho… māno…pe… anottappaṃ akusalaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti[M 0.0389]? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ akusalaṃ sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

763. Is greed unwholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is material form unwholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. … Is hatred… delusion… conceit… is lack of fear of wrongdoing unwholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? Yes. Is material form unwholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning towards… aspiration? It should not be said thus. …

Rūpaṃ akusalaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Lobho akusalo anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpaṃ akusalaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Doso… moho…pe… anottappaṃ akusalaṃ anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is form unwholesome, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? Yes. Is greed unwholesome, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? It should not be said thus... Is form unwholesome, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? Yes. Is hatred... delusion... lack of moral dread unwholesome, without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? It should not be said thus...

764. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūpaṃ kusalampi akusalampī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ kusalampi akusalampīti? Āmantā. Hañci kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ kusalampi akusalampī”ti.

764. Is it incorrect to say, 'Material form is both wholesome and unwholesome'? Yes. Are not bodily action and verbal action both wholesome and unwholesome? Yes. If bodily action and verbal action are both wholesome and unwholesome, then indeed, good sir, it should be said, 'Material form is both wholesome and unwholesome.'

Rūpaṃ kusalākusalantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Whether Material Form is Wholesome or Unwholesome is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(163) 8. Rūpaṃ vipākotikathā

Discussion on Material Form as Resultant

765. Rūpaṃ vipākoti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ adukkhamasukhavedaniyaṃ[P 0.0537], sukhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, dukkhāya vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, adukkhamasukhāya [V 0.0434] vedanāya sampayuttaṃ, phassena sampayuttaṃ…pe… cittena sampayuttaṃ, sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ vipāko”ti.

765. Is material form resultant? Yes. Is material form to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, or to be felt as neither-painful-nor-pleasant? Is it associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, associated with contact… (etc.)… associated with consciousness, with an object? Does it have adverting… (etc.)… aspiration? It should not be said thus… (etc.)… Is it not that it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… (etc.)… is without an object? Is it not that it does not have adverting… (etc.)… aspiration? Yes. If it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… (etc.)… is without an object, and does not have adverting… (etc.)… aspiration, then indeed, friend, it should not be said, ‘Material form is resultant.’

766. Phasso vipāko, phasso sukhavedaniyo dukkhavedaniyo…pe… sārammaṇo[T 0.0570], atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ vipāko, rūpaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… sārammaṇaṃ, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

766. Contact is resultant. Is contact to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… (etc.)… with an object? Does it have adverting… (etc.)… aspiration? Yes. Material form is resultant. Is material form to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… (etc.)… with an object? Does it have adverting… (etc.)… aspiration? It should not be said thus… (etc.)…

Rūpaṃ vipāko[M 0.0390], rūpaṃ na sukhavedaniyaṃ na dukkhavedaniyaṃ…pe… anārammaṇaṃ, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Phasso vipāko, phasso na sukhavedaniyo na dukkhavedaniyo…pe… anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is form a resultant, is form not associated with pleasant feeling, not associated with painful feeling... without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? Yes. Is contact a resultant, is contact not associated with pleasant feeling, not associated with painful feeling... without an object, and is there no adverting... no aspiration for it? It should not be said thus...

767. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūpaṃ vipāko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu kammassa katattā uppannā cittacetasikā dhammā vipākoti? Āmantā. Hañci kammassa katattā uppannā cittacetasikā dhammā vipāko, tena vata re vattabbe – “kammassa katattā uppannaṃ rūpaṃ vipāko”ti.

767. Should it not be said, ‘Material form is resultant’? Yes. Are not consciousness and its mental factors, which have arisen due to kamma having been done, resultant? Yes. If consciousness and its mental factors, which have arisen due to kamma having been done, are resultant, then indeed, friend, it should be said, ‘Material form that has arisen due to kamma having been done is resultant.’

Rūpaṃ vipākotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on ‘Material Form is Resultant’ is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(164) 9. Rūpaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacarantikathā

16. (164) 9. Discussion on Material Form as Pertaining to the Fine-Material and Immaterial Spheres

768. Atthi [P 0.0538] rūpaṃ rūpāvacaranti? Āmantā. Samāpattesiyaṃ upapattesiyaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagataṃ [V 0.0435] sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ [T 0.0571] ekuppādaṃ ekanirodhaṃ ekavatthukaṃ ekārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na samāpattesiyaṃ na upapattesiyaṃ na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ, na samāpattesiyena cittena na upapattesiyena cittena na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagataṃ sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ ekuppādaṃ ekanirodhaṃ ekavatthukaṃ ekārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyaṃ na upapattesiyaṃ na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ, na samāpattesiyena cittena…pe… ekārammaṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi rūpaṃ rūpāvacara”nti.

Is there material form that is of the fine-material sphere? Yes. Is it for the sake of attainment, for the sake of rebirth, for a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it accompanied by, co-nascent with, conjoined with, associated with, of single arising, of single cessation, of single basis, and of single object with consciousness that is for the sake of attainment, with consciousness that is for the sake of rebirth, and with consciousness that is for a pleasant abiding in the present life? It should not be said thus… (etc.)… Is it not that it is not for the sake of attainment, not for the sake of rebirth, not for a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it not that it is not accompanied by, co-nascent with, conjoined with, associated with, of single arising, of single cessation, of single basis, and of single object with consciousness that is for the sake of attainment, with consciousness that is for the sake of rebirth, and with consciousness that is for a pleasant abiding in the present life? Yes. If it is not for the sake of attainment, not for the sake of rebirth, not for a pleasant abiding in the present life, and is not… (etc.)… of a single object with consciousness that is for the sake of attainment, then indeed, friend, it should not be said, ‘There is material form that is of the fine-material sphere.’

769. Atthi rūpaṃ arūpāvacaranti? Āmantā. Samāpattesiyaṃ upapattesiyaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagataṃ sahajātaṃ saṃsaṭṭhaṃ sampayuttaṃ ekuppādaṃ ekanirodhaṃ ekavatthukaṃ ekārammaṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na samāpattesiyaṃ na upapattesiyaṃ na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāraṃ, na samāpattesiyena cittena [M 0.0391] …pe… ekārammaṇanti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyaṃ na upapattesiyaṃ…pe… ekavatthukaṃ ekārammaṇaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi rūpaṃ arūpāvacara”nti.

768. Is there material form that is of the immaterial sphere? Yes. Is it for the sake of attainment, for the sake of rebirth, for a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it accompanied by, co-nascent with, conjoined with, associated with, of single arising, of single cessation, of single basis, and of single object with consciousness that is for the sake of attainment, with consciousness that is for the sake of rebirth, and with consciousness that is for a pleasant abiding in the present life? It should not be said thus… (etc.)… Is it not that it is not for the sake of attainment, not for the sake of rebirth, not for a pleasant abiding in the present life, and is not… (etc.)… of a single object with consciousness that is for the sake of attainment? Yes. If it is not for the sake of attainment, not for the sake of rebirth… (etc.)… of a single base, and of a single object, then indeed, friend, it should not be said, ‘There is material form that is of the immaterial sphere.’

770. Na vattabbaṃ – “atthi rūpaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ, atthi rūpaṃ arūpāvacara”nti? Āmantā. Nanu kāmāvacarakammassa katattā rūpaṃ kāmāvacaranti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmāvacarakammassa katattā rūpaṃ kāmāvacaraṃ[T 0.0572][P 0.0539], tena vata re vattabbe – “rūpāvacarakammassa katattā rūpaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ, arūpāvacarakammassa katattā rūpaṃ arūpāvacara”nti.

769. Should it not be said, ‘There is material form that is of the fine-material sphere, and there is material form that is of the immaterial sphere’? Yes. Is it not that material form, having arisen due to sense-sphere kamma having been done, is of the sense-sphere? Yes. If material form, having arisen due to sense-sphere kamma having been done, is of the sense-sphere, then indeed, friend, it should be said, ‘Material form, having arisen due to fine-material-sphere kamma having been done, is of the fine-material sphere; and material form, having arisen due to immaterial-sphere kamma having been done, is of the immaterial sphere.’

Rūpaṃ rūpāvacarārūpāvacarantikathā niṭṭhitā.

770. The Discussion on Material Form as Pertaining to the Fine-Material and Immaterial Spheres is concluded.

16. Soḷasamavaggo

16. The Sixteenth Chapter

(165) 10. Rūpārūpadhātupariyāpannakathā

(165) 10. Discourse on Inclusion in the Form and Formless Realms

771. Rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Samāpattesiyo upapattesiyo diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena [V 0.0436] sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena…pe… ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena…pe… ekavatthuko ekārammaṇo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti.

Is lust for form included in the form element? Yes. Is it for seeking attainment, for seeking rebirth, for a pleasant abiding in the present life? Is it accompanied by, co-nascent with, conjoined with, associated with, of single arising, of single cessation, of single basis, and of single object with consciousness that is for seeking attainment, with consciousness that is for seeking rebirth, and with consciousness that is for a pleasant abiding in the present life? It should not be said thus… (etc.)… Is it not that it is not for seeking attainment, not for seeking rebirth, not for a pleasant abiding in the present life, and is not accompanied by… (etc.)… of single basis, and of single object with consciousness that is for seeking attainment? Yes. If it is not for seeking attainment, not for seeking rebirth, not for a pleasant abiding in the present life, and is not accompanied by… (etc.)… of single basis, and of single object, then indeed, friend, it should not be said, ‘Lust for form is included in the form element.’

772. Rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Saddarāgo saddadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

16. Is lust for form included in the form element? Yes. Is lust for sound included in the sound element? It should not be said thus… (etc.)… Is lust for form included in the form element? Yes. Is lust for smell… (etc.)… Is lust for taste… (etc.)… Is lust for tangible objects included in the tangible element? It should not be said thus… (etc.)…

Saddarāgo [T 0.0573][M 0.0392] na vattabbaṃ – “saddadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Rūparāgo na vattabbaṃ – “rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo na vattabbaṃ – “phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0540]. Rūparāgo na vattabbaṃ – “rūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should it not be said, 'Lust for sound is included in the sound element'? Yes. Should it not be said, 'Lust for form is included in the form element'? It should not be said thus… and so on. Lust for smell… and so on… lust for taste… and so on… Should it not be said, 'Lust for tangible objects is included in the tangible element'? Yes. Should it not be said, 'Lust for form is included in the form element'? It should not be said thus… and so on.

773. Arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Arūparāgo na vattabbaṃ – “arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Samāpattesiyo upapattesiyo diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, samāpattesiyena cittena upapattesiyena cittena diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena…pe… ekavatthuko ekārammaṇoti? Āmantā. Hañci na samāpattesiyo na upapattesiyo na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihāro, na samāpattesiyena cittena na upapattesiyena cittena na diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārena cittena sahagato sahajāto saṃsaṭṭho sampayutto ekuppādo ekanirodho ekavatthuko ekārammaṇo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti.

773. Is lust for the formless included in the formless element? Yes. Should it not be said, 'Lust for the formless is included in the formless element'? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is lust for the formless included in the formless element? Yes. Is it for the sake of meditative attainment, for the sake of rebirth, a dwelling in bliss in the present life; and is it conascent, co-arisen, mixed, and associated with a mind that is for the sake of meditative attainment, with a mind that is for the sake of rebirth, with a mind that is a dwelling in bliss in the present life—of single arising, single cessation, single basis, and single object? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is it not the case that it is not for the sake of meditative attainment, not for the sake of rebirth, not a dwelling in bliss in the present life; and that it is not conascent… and so on… not of single basis, and not of single object with a mind that is for the sake of meditative attainment? Yes. If it is not for the sake of meditative attainment, not for the sake of rebirth, not a dwelling in bliss in the present life; and it is not conascent, not co-arisen, not mixed, not associated, not of single arising, not of single cessation, not of single basis, and not of single object with a mind that is for the sake of meditative attainment, with a mind that is for the sake of rebirth, and with a mind that is a dwelling in bliss in the present life, then indeed it should not be said, 'Lust for the formless is included in the formless element.'

774. Arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Saddarāgo saddadhātupariyāpannoti[V 0.0437]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpannoti? Āmantā. Gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

774. Is lust for the formless included in the formless element? Yes. Is lust for sound included in the sound element? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is lust for the formless included in the formless element? Yes. Is lust for smell… and so on… is lust for taste… and so on… is lust for tangible objects included in the tangible element? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Saddarāgo na vattabbaṃ – “saddadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Arūparāgo na vattabbaṃ – “arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… gandharāgo…pe… rasarāgo…pe… phoṭṭhabbarāgo na vattabbaṃ – “phoṭṭhabbadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Arūparāgo na vattabbaṃ – “arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Na [P 0.0541] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should it not be said, 'Lust for sound is included in the sound element'? Yes. Should it not be said, 'Lust for the formless is included in the formless element'? It should not be said thus… and so on. Lust for smell… and so on… lust for taste… and so on… Should it not be said, 'Lust for tangible objects is included in the tangible element'? Yes. Should it not be said, 'Lust for the formless is included in the formless element'? It should not be said thus… and so on.

775. Na vattabbaṃ – “rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpanno, arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Nanu kāmarāgo kāmadhātupariyāpannoti[M 0.0393]? Āmantā. Hañci kāmarāgo kāmadhātupariyāpanno, tena vata re vattabbe – “rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpanno, arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpanno”ti.

775. Should it not be said, 'Lust for form is included in the form element, and lust for the formless is included in the formless element'? Yes. Surely, lust for sensual pleasures is included in the sensual element? Yes. If lust for sensual pleasures is included in the sensual element, then indeed it should be said, 'Lust for form is included in the form element, and lust for the formless is included in the formless element.'

Rūparāgo rūpadhātupariyāpanno arūparāgo arūpadhātupariyāpannotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on 'Lust for form is included in the form element, and lust for the formless is included in the formless element' is concluded.

Rūpārūpadhātupariyāpannakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Inclusion in the Form and Formless Realms is concluded.

Soḷasamavaggo.

The Sixteenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Cittaniggaho, cittapaggaho, sukhānuppadānaṃ, adhigayha manasikāro, rūpaṃ hetu, rūpaṃ sahetukaṃ, rūpaṃ kusalampi akusalampi, rūpaṃ vipāko, atthi rūpaṃ rūpāvacaraṃ atthi rūpaṃ arūpāvacaraṃ, sabbe kilesā kāmadhātupariyāpannāti.

The discourse on restraint of the mind, the discourse on exertion of the mind, the discourse on the production of happiness, the discourse on attention by way of mastering, the discourse on 'Form is a cause', the discourse on 'Form has a cause', the discourse on 'Form is wholesome or unwholesome', the discourse on 'Form is a result', the discourse on 'There is form belonging to the fine-material sphere and form belonging to the immaterial sphere', and the discourse on 'All defilements are included in the sensual element'.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(166) 1. Arahato puññūpacayakathā

(166) 1. Discourse on the Accumulation of Merit by an Arahant

776. Atthi [P 0.0542][V 0.0438] arahato puññūpacayoti? Āmantā. Atthi arahato apuññūpacayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi arahato apuññūpacayoti? Āmantā. Natthi arahato puññūpacayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there an accumulation of merit for an Arahant? Yes. Is there an accumulation of demerit for an Arahant? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is there no accumulation of demerit for an Arahant? Yes. Is there no accumulation of merit for an Arahant? It should not be said thus… and so on.

777. Atthi arahato puññūpacayoti? Āmantā. Arahā puññābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, āneñjābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharoti, gatisaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, bhavasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, issariyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, adhipaccasaṃvattaniyaṃ ādhipaccasaṃvattanikaṃ (?) kammaṃ karoti, mahābhogasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, mahāparivārasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, devasobhagyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karoti, manussasobhagyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

17. Is there an accumulation of merit for an Arahant? Yes. Does an Arahant form meritorious formations, form imperturbable formations, perform kamma that leads to a destination, perform kamma that leads to becoming, perform kamma that leads to dominion, perform kamma that leads to sovereignty, perform kamma that leads to great wealth, perform kamma that leads to a great retinue, perform kamma that leads to divine good fortune, or perform kamma that leads to human good fortune? It should not be said thus… and so on.

778. Atthi arahato puññūpacayoti? Āmantā. Arahā ācinātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahā apacinātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [M 0.0394] …pe… arahā pajahatīti…pe… arahā upādiyatīti…pe… arahā visinetīti…pe… arahā ussinetīti…pe… arahā vidhūpetīti [T 0.0576]…pe… arahā sandhūpetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu [P 0.0543] arahā nevācināti na apacināti apacinitvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā nevācināti nāpacināti apacinitvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato puññūpacayo”ti.

Is there an accumulation of merit for an Arahant? Yes. Does an Arahant accumulate? It should not be said thus… and so on. Does an Arahant diminish? It should not be said thus… and so on. Does an Arahant abandon? …and so on. Does an Arahant cling? …and so on. Does an Arahant disentangle? …and so on. Does an Arahant entangle? …and so on. Does an Arahant shake off? …and so on. Does an Arahant establish? It should not be said thus… and so on. Is it not the case that an Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but having diminished, remains? Yes. If an Arahant neither accumulates nor diminishes, but having diminished, remains, then indeed it should not be said: ‘There is an accumulation of merit for an Arahant.’

Nanu arahā neva pajahati na upādiyati pajahitvā ṭhito, neva visineti na ussineti visinetvā ṭhito, neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi arahato puññūpacayo”ti.

776. Is it not the case that an Arahant neither abandons nor clings, but having abandoned, remains; that he neither disentangles nor entangles, but having disentangled, remains; that he neither shakes off nor establishes, but having shaken off, remains? Yes. If an Arahant neither shakes off nor establishes, but having shaken off, remains, then indeed it should not be said: ‘There is an accumulation of merit for an Arahant.’

779. Natthi arahato puññūpacayoti? Āmantā. Arahā dānaṃ dadeyyāti? Āmantā[V 0.0439]. Hañci arahā dānaṃ dadeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi arahato puññūpacayo”ti.

777. Is there no accumulation of merit for an Arahant? Yes. Should an Arahant give a gift? Yes. If an Arahant should give a gift, then indeed it should not be said: ‘There is no accumulation of merit for an Arahant.’

Arahā cīvaraṃ dadeyya…pe… piṇḍapātaṃ dadeyya… senāsanaṃ dadeyya… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyya… khādanīyaṃ dadeyya… bhojanīyaṃ dadeyya… pānīyaṃ dadeyya… cetiyaṃ vandeyya… cetiye mālaṃ āropeyya… gandhaṃ āropeyya… vilepanaṃ āropeyya…pe… cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ (?) kareyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ kareyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi arahato puññūpacayo”ti.

Should an Arahant give robes… almsfood… lodging… medicinal requisites for the sick… snacks… meals… drinks… venerate a shrine… offer garlands at a shrine… offer incense… offer fragrant ointment… perform circumambulation to the right of a shrine? Yes. If an Arahant should perform circumambulation to the right of a shrine, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is no accumulation of merit for an Arahant.’

Atthi arahato puññūpacayotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Accumulation of Merit by an Arahant is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(167) 2. Natthi arahato akālamaccūtikathā

17. The Discussion on an Arahant Having No Untimely Death

780. Natthi [T 0.0577] arahato akālamaccūti? Āmantā. Natthi arahantaghātakoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi arahantaghātakoti? Āmantā. Atthi [M 0.0395][P 0.0544] arahato akālamaccūti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi arahato akālamaccūti? Āmantā. Yo arahantaṃ jīvitā voropeti, sati jīvite jīvitāvasese jīvitā voropeti, asati jīvite jīvitāvasese jīvitā voropetīti? Sati jīvite jīvitāvasese jīvitā voropetīti. Hañci sati jīvite jīvitāvasese jīvitā voropeti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi arahato akālamaccū”ti. Asati jīvite jīvitāvasese jīvitā voropetīti, natthi arahantaghātakoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no untimely death for an Arahant? Yes. Is there no killer of an Arahant? It should not be said thus… Is there a killer of an Arahant? Yes. Is there an untimely death for an Arahant? It should not be said thus… Is there no untimely death for an Arahant? Yes. When someone deprives an Arahant of life, do they deprive them of life while life still exists and a remnant of life remains, or when life does not exist and no remnant of life remains? They deprive them of life while life still exists and a remnant of life remains. If they deprive them of life while life still exists and a remnant of life remains, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is no untimely death for an Arahant.’ If it is said that they deprive them of life when life does not exist and no remnant of life remains, then is there no killer of an Arahant? It should not be said thus….

781. Natthi arahato akālamaccūti? Āmantā. Arahato kāye visaṃ na kameyya, satthaṃ na kameyya, aggi na kameyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu arahato kāye visaṃ kameyya[V 0.0440], satthaṃ kameyya, aggi kameyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci arahato kāye visaṃ kameyya, satthaṃ kameyya, aggi kameyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi arahato akālamaccū”ti.

780. Is there no untimely death for an Arahant? Yes. Would poison not pervade an Arahant’s body, a weapon not strike it, fire not burn it? It should not be said thus… Surely, would poison pervade an Arahant’s body, a weapon strike it, and fire burn it? Yes. If poison were to pervade an Arahant’s body, a weapon were to strike it, and fire were to burn it, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is no untimely death for an Arahant.’

Arahato kāye visaṃ na kameyya, satthaṃ na kameyya, aggi na kameyyāti? Āmantā. Natthi arahantaghātakoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

781. Would poison not pervade an Arahant’s body, a weapon not strike it, fire not burn it? Yes. Is there no killer of an Arahant? It should not be said thus….

782. Atthi [T 0.0578] arahato akālamaccūti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi; tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajjaṃ vā apare vā pariyāye”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[P 0.0545]. Tena hi natthi arahato akālamaccūti.

Is there an untimely death for an Arahant? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, I do not declare the coming to an end of intentional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result being experienced, and that result is to be experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life’? Does such a discourse exist? Yes. Therefore, there is no untimely death for an Arahant.

Natthi arahato akālamaccūtikathā niṭṭhitā.

782. The Discussion on an Arahant Having No Untimely Death is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(168) 3. Sabbamidaṃ kammatotikathā

The Discussion on 'All This Is from Kamma'

783. Sabbamidaṃ kammatoti? Āmantā. Kammampi kammatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbamidaṃ kammatoti? Āmantā. Sabbamidaṃ pubbekatahetūti? Na hevaṃ [M 0.0396] vattabbe…pe… sabbamidaṃ kammatoti? Āmantā. Sabbamidaṃ kammavipākatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

17. Is all this from kamma? Yes. Is kamma itself also from kamma? It should not be said thus… Is all this from kamma? Yes. Is all this caused by past actions? It should not be said thus… Is all this from kamma? Yes. Is all this from the result of kamma? It should not be said thus…

784. Sabbamidaṃ kammavipākatoti? Āmantā. Kammavipākena pāṇaṃ haneyyāti? Āmantā. Pāṇātipāto saphaloti? Āmantā. Kammavipāko saphaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kammavipāko aphaloti? Āmantā. Pāṇātipāto aphaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is all this from the result of kamma? Yes. By means of the result of kamma, should one kill a living being? Yes. Is the killing of a living being fruitful? Yes. Is the result of kamma fruitful? It should not be said thus… Is the result of kamma fruitless? Yes. Is the killing of a living being fruitless? It should not be said thus…

Kammavipākena [V 0.0441] adinnaṃ ādiyeyya…pe… musā bhaṇeyya… pisuṇaṃ bhaṇeyya… pharusaṃ bhaṇeyya… samphaṃ palapeyya… sandhiṃ chindeyya… nillopaṃ hareyya… ekāgārikaṃ kareyya… paripanthe tiṭṭheyya… paradāraṃ gaccheyya… gāmaghātakaṃ [T 0.0579] kareyya… nigamaghātakaṃ kareyya… kammavipākena dānaṃ dadeyya… cīvaraṃ dadeyya [P 0.0546] … piṇḍapātaṃ dadeyya… senāsanaṃ dadeyya… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyyāti? Āmantā. Gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro saphaloti? Āmantā. Kammavipāko saphaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kammavipāko aphaloti? Āmantā. Gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāro aphaloti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

783. By means of the result of kamma, should one take what is not given… speak falsely… speak divisively… speak harshly… engage in frivolous talk… break into houses… plunder… commit robbery in a single house… lie in wait on a highway… go to another's wife… plunder a village… plunder a town… By means of the result of kamma, should one give a gift… give a robe… give almsfood… give lodging… give medicine and requisites for the sick? Yes. Is giving medicine and requisites for the sick fruitful? Yes. Is the result of kamma fruitful? It should not be said thus… Is the result of kamma fruitless? Yes. Is giving medicine and requisites for the sick fruitless? It should not be said thus…

785. Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbamidaṃ kammato”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

784. Should it not be said: ‘All this is from kamma’? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Kammunā vattatī vattati (pī. ka., ma. ni. 2.460), vattate (?) loko, kammunā vattatī vattati (pī. ka., ma. ni. 2.460), vattate (?) pajā;

Kammanibandhanā sattā, rathassāṇīva yāyato ma. ni. 2.460; su. ni. 659.

“By kamma the world proceeds, by kamma beings proceed; beings are bound by kamma, like the linchpin of a moving chariot.”

“Kammena kittiṃ labhate pasaṃsaṃ,

Kammena jāniñca vadhañca bandhaṃ;

Taṃ kammaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ viditvā,

Kasmā vade natthi kammanti loke”ti.

“Through kamma one gains fame and praise; through kamma, loss, slaughter, and bondage. Knowing that kamma has various effects, why would one say, ‘In the world, there is no kamma’?”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi “sabbamidaṃ kammato”ti.

“Does such a discourse exist?” “Yes.” “Therefore, you should say: ‘All this is due to kamma’.”

Sabbamidaṃ kammatotikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'All This Is Due to Kamma' is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(169) 4. Indriyabaddhakathā

Discussion on What is Bound to the Faculties

786. Indriyabaddhaññeva [M 0.0397] dukkhanti? Āmantā. Indriyabaddhaññeva [T 0.0580] aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ [P 0.0547][V 0.0442] khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anindriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci anindriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “indriyabaddhaññeva dukkha”nti.

Is only what is bound to the faculties suffering? Yes. Is only what is bound to the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change? It should not be said thus… Indeed, is not what is not bound to the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change? Yes. If what is not bound to the faculties is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘Only what is bound to the faculties is suffering.’

Anindriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, tañca na dukkhanti? Āmantā. Indriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, tañca na dukkhanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is that which is not connected with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen… subject to change, and yet not suffering? Yes. Is that which is connected with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen… subject to change, and yet not suffering? This should not be said…

Indriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, tañca dukkhanti idaṃ-pucchādvayena purimapucchādvayassa purato bhavitabbaṃ? Āmantā. Anindriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, tañca dukkhanti idaṃ-pucchādvayena purimapucchādvayassa purato bhavitabbaṃ? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is that which is connected with the faculties impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, and also suffering? Yes. Is that which is not connected with the faculties impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, and also suffering? This should not be said…

787. Indriyabaddhaññeva dukkhanti? Āmantā. Nanu yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ saṃ. ni. 3.15 vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “anindriyabaddhaṃ anicca”nti? Āmantā. Hañci yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ saṃ. ni. 3.15 vuttaṃ bhagavatā – anindriyabaddhaṃ aniccaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “indriyabaddhaññeva dukkha”nti.

787. Is only that which is connected with the faculties suffering? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One, ‘Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering’? And is that which is not connected with the faculties impermanent? Yes. If it has been said by the Blessed One, ‘Whatever is impermanent, that is suffering,’ and if that which is not connected with the faculties is impermanent, then it certainly should not be said that ‘only that which is connected with the faculties is suffering.’

788. Na vattabbaṃ – “indriyabaddhaññeva dukkha”nti? Āmantā. Yathā indriyabaddhassa dukkhassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussati, evamevaṃ anindriyabaddhassa dukkhassa pariññāya bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatīti[T 0.0581]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yathā indriyabaddhaṃ dukkhaṃ pariññātaṃ na puna uppajjati[P 0.0548], evamevaṃ anindriyabaddhaṃ dukkhaṃ pariññātaṃ na puna uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi indriyabaddhaññeva dukkhanti.

788. Should it not be said that ‘only that which is connected with the faculties is suffering’? Yes. Just as the holy life is lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering connected with the faculties, in the same way, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering not connected with the faculties? This should not be said… Just as suffering connected with the faculties, when fully understood, does not arise again, in the same way, does suffering not connected with the faculties, when fully understood, not arise again? This should not be said. Therefore, only that which is connected with the faculties is suffering.

Indriyabaddhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on What is Connected with the Faculties is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(170) 5. Ṭhapetvā ariyamaggantikathā

(170) 5. Discussion on ‘Excluding the Noble Path’

789. Ṭhapetvā [M 0.0398][V 0.0443] ariyamaggaṃ avasesā saṅkhārā dukkhāti? Āmantā. Dukkhasamudayopi dukkhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dukkhasamudayopi dukkhoti? Āmantā. Tīṇeva ariyasaccānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tīṇeva ariyasaccānīti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāri ariyasaccāni vuttāni bhagavatā – dukkhaṃ, dukkhasamudayo, dukkhanirodho, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāri ariyasaccāni vuttāni bhagavatā – dukkhaṃ, dukkhasamudayo, dukkhanirodho, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā; no ca vata re vattabbe – “tīṇeva ariyasaccānī”ti.

789. Excluding the Noble Path, are the remaining formations suffering? Yes. Is the origin of suffering also suffering? This should not be said… Is the origin of suffering also suffering? Yes. Are there only three Noble Truths? This should not be said… Are there only three Noble Truths? Yes. But have not four Noble Truths been spoken of by the Blessed One—suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering? Yes. If four Noble Truths have been spoken of by the Blessed One—suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the path leading to the cessation of suffering—then it certainly should not be said that “there are only three Noble Truths.”

Dukkhasamudayopi dukkhoti? Āmantā. Kenaṭṭhenāti? Aniccaṭṭhena. Ariyamaggo aniccoti? Āmantā. Ariyamaggo dukkhoti? Na [P 0.0549] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the origin of suffering also suffering? Yes. In what sense? In the sense of impermanence. Is the Noble Path impermanent? Yes. Is the Noble Path suffering? This should not be said…

Ariyamaggo anicco, so ca na dukkhoti? Āmantā. Dukkhasamudayo anicco, so ca na dukkhoti? Na [T 0.0582] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dukkhasamudayo anicco, so ca dukkhoti? Āmantā. Ariyamaggo anicco, so ca dukkhoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Noble Path impermanent, and is it not suffering? Yes. Is the origin of suffering impermanent, and is it not suffering? This should not be said… Is the origin of suffering impermanent, and is it suffering? Yes. Is the Noble Path impermanent, and is it suffering? This should not be said…

790. Na vattabbaṃ – “ṭhapetvā ariyamaggaṃ avasesā saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu sā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti? Āmantā. Hañci sā dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā, tena vata re vattabbe – “ṭhapetvā ariyamaggaṃ avasesā saṅkhārā dukkhā”ti.

790. Should it not be said: “Excluding the Noble Path, the remaining formations are suffering”? Yes. But is that not the practice leading to the cessation of suffering? Yes. If that is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering, then indeed it should be said: “Excluding the Noble Path, the remaining formations are suffering.”

Ṭhapetvā ariyamaggantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on ‘Excluding the Noble Path’ is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(171) 6. Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātikathā

(171) 6. Discussion on ‘It Should Not Be Said that the Saṅgha Accepts an Offering’

791. Na [V 0.0444] vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu saṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti? Āmantā. Hañci saṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo [M 0.0399] dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti.

791. Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha accepts an offering”? Yes. Is not the Saṅgha worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Saṅgha is worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then indeed it should be said: “The Saṅgha accepts an offering.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāro purisayugā aṭṭhapurisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā [T 0.0583][P 0.0550] vuttā bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti.

Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha accepts an offering”? Yes. Have not the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals, been declared by the Blessed One to be worthy of gifts? Yes. If the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals, have been declared by the Blessed One to be worthy of gifts, then indeed it should be said: “The Saṅgha accepts an offering.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci saṅghassa dānaṃ dentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci saṅghassa dānaṃ denti, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti. Nanu atthi keci saṅghassa cīvaraṃ denti…pe… piṇḍapātaṃ denti… senāsanaṃ denti… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ denti… khādanīyaṃ denti… bhojanīyaṃ denti…pe… pānīyaṃ dentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci saṅghassa pānīyaṃ denti, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti.

Should it not be said, “The Saṅgha accepts an offering”? Yes. Are there not some who give a gift to the Saṅgha? Yes. If there are some who give a gift to the Saṅgha, then indeed it should be said, “The Saṅgha accepts an offering.” Are there not some who give robes to the Saṅgha… almsfood… lodging… medicinal requisites for the sick… hard food… soft food… drink? Yes. If there are some who give drink to the Saṅgha, then indeed it should be said, “The Saṅgha accepts an offering.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha accepts an offering”? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Āhutiṃ jātavedova, mahāmeghaṃva medanī;

Saṅgho samādhisampanno, paṭiggaṇhāti dakkhiṇa”nti.

“As the fire accepts the oblation, as the earth accepts the great cloud; the Saṅgha, accomplished in concentration, accepts the offering.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātīti.

Is there indeed such a sutta passage? Yes. In that case, the Saṅgha accepts an offering.

792. Saṅgho [V 0.0445] dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Maggo paṭiggaṇhāti, phalaṃ paṭiggaṇhātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

792. Does the Saṅgha accept an offering? Yes. Does the path accept, does the fruit accept? This should not be said…

Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhātītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on ‘It Should Not Be Said that the Saṅgha Accepts an Offering’ is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(172) 7. Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetītikathā

(172) 7. Discussion on ‘It should not be said that the Saṅgha purifies an offering’

793. Na [P 0.0551][T 0.0584] vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu saṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti? Āmantā. Hañci saṅgho āhuneyyo…pe… anuttaraṃ [M 0.0400] puññakkhettaṃ lokassa, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti.

793. Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering”? Yes. Is not the Saṅgha worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of noble offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Saṅgha is worthy of offerings… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, therefore, indeed, it should be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti.

Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering”? Yes. Has not the Blessed One declared that the four pairs of men, the eight individual persons, are worthy of noble offerings? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the four pairs of men, the eight individual persons, are worthy of noble offerings, then indeed it should be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci saṅghassa dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci saṅghassa dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhenti, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti.

Should it not be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering”? Yes. Are there not some who, having given a gift to the Saṅgha, accomplish the noble offering? Yes. If there are some who, having given a gift to the Saṅgha, accomplish the noble offering, then indeed it should be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering.”

Nanu atthi keci saṅghassa cīvaraṃ datvā…pe… piṇḍapātaṃ datvā…pe… senāsanaṃ datvā… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ datvā… khādanīyaṃ datvā… bhojanīyaṃ datvā…pe… pānīyaṃ [V 0.0446] datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci [T 0.0585] saṅghassa pānīyaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhenti, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetī”ti.

Are there not some who, having given robes to the Saṅgha… almsfood… lodging… medicinal requisites for the sick… hard food… soft food… drink, accomplish the noble offering? Yes. If there are some who, having given drink to the Saṅgha, accomplish the noble offering, then indeed it should be said: “The Saṅgha purifies the noble offering.”

794. Saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetīti? Āmantā. Maggo [P 0.0552] visodheti, phalaṃ visodhetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

794. Does the Saṅgha purify the noble offering? Yes. Does the path purify, does the fruit purify? It should not be said thus…

Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodhetītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on ‘It should not be said that the Saṅgha purifies the noble offering’ is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(173) 8. Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho bhuñjatītikathā

Discussion on ‘It should not be said that the Saṅgha eats’

795. Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci saṅghabhattāni karonti, uddesabhattāni karonti, yāgupānāni karontīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci saṅghabhattāni karonti, uddesabhattāni karonti, yāgupānāni karonti, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti.

795. Should it not be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks’? Yes. Are there not some who prepare meals for the Saṅgha, designated meals, and gruel drinks? Yes. If there are some who prepare meals for the Saṅgha, designated meals, and gruel drinks, then indeed it should be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks.’

Na [M 0.0401] vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “gaṇabhojanaṃ paramparabhojanaṃ atirittabhojanaṃ anatirittabhojana”nti? Āmantā. Hañci vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “gaṇabhojanaṃ paramparabhojanaṃ atirittabhojanaṃ anatirittabhojanaṃ”, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti.

Should it not be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks’? Yes. Has not the Blessed One spoken of group meals, successive meals, leftover meals, and non-leftover meals? Yes. If the Blessed One has spoken of group meals, successive meals, leftover meals, and non-leftover meals, then indeed it should be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks.’

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu aṭṭha pānāni vuttāni bhagavatā – ambapānaṃ, jambupānaṃ[T 0.0586], cocapānaṃ, mocapānaṃ, madhukapānaṃ, madhupānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) mahāva. 300 pana passitabbaṃ muddikapānaṃ, sālukapānaṃ, phārusakapānanti? Āmantā. Hañci aṭṭha pānāni vuttāni bhagavatā – ambapānaṃ, jambupānaṃ, cocapānaṃ, mocapānaṃ, madhukapānaṃ, muddikapānaṃ[P 0.0553], sālukapānaṃ, phārusakapānaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatī”ti.

Should it not be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks’? Yes. Have not eight kinds of drinks been spoken of by the Blessed One—mango drink, rose-apple drink, plantain drink, banana drink, madhuka drink, grape drink, lotus root drink, and phārusaka drink? Yes. If eight kinds of drinks have been spoken of by the Blessed One—mango drink, rose-apple drink, plantain drink, banana drink, madhuka drink, grape drink, lotus root drink, and phārusaka drink—then indeed it should be said: ‘The Saṅgha eats, drinks, chews, and licks.’

796. Saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatīti? Āmantā. Maggo bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyati, phalaṃ bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

796. Does the Saṅgha eat, drink, chew, and lick? Yes. Does the path eat, drink, chew, and lick? Does the fruit eat, drink, chew, and lick? It should not be said thus…

Na vattabbaṃ saṅgho bhuñjatītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on ‘It should not be said that the Saṅgha eats’ is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(174) 9. Na vattabbaṃ saṅghassadinnaṃ mahapphalantikathā

Discussion on 'It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Saṅgha Is of Great Fruit'

797. Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu saṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti? Āmantā. Hañci saṅgho āhuneyyo…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

797. Should it not be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit'? Yes. Is not the Saṅgha worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of noble offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Saṅgha is worthy of offerings... the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then indeed it should be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā [T 0.0587] dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

Should it not be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit'? Yes. Were not the four pairs of persons, the eight individual persons, declared by the Blessed One to be worthy of noble offerings? Yes. If the four pairs of persons, the eight individual persons, were declared by the Blessed One to be worthy of noble offerings, then indeed it should be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.'

798. Na [M 0.0402] vattabbaṃ – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “saṅghe, gotami, dehi, saṅghe te dinne ahañceva pūjito bhavissāmi saṅgho cā”ti ma. ni. 3.376. Attheva [P 0.0554] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphalanti.

798. Should it not be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit'? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Give to the Saṅgha, Gotamī. When it is given by you to the Saṅgha, both I and the Saṅgha will be honored'? Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.

Na [V 0.0448] vattabbaṃ – “saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

Should it not be said: 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit'? Yes. Did not Sakka, the lord of the devas, say this to the Blessed One:

“Yajamānānaṃ manussānaṃ, puññapekkhāna pāṇinaṃ;

Karotaṃ opadhikaṃ puññaṃ, kattha dinnaṃ mahapphalanti.

“For human beings who are donors, for beings who seek merit, for those performing merit that pertains to the substrata of existence, to what person is a gift given that is of great fruit?”

“Cattāro ca paṭipannā, cattāro ca phale ṭhitā;

Esa saṅgho ujubhūto, paññāsīlasamāhito.

'Four who are practicing the path and four who are established in the fruit; this Saṅgha is upright, established in wisdom and virtue.'

“Yajamānānaṃ manussānaṃ, puññapekkhāna pāṇinaṃ;

Karotaṃ opadhikaṃ puññaṃ, saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti saṃ. ni. 1.262; vi. va. 642, 751.

'For humans who are donors, for beings who seek merit, for those performing merit that pertains to the substrata of existence, a gift given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.'

“Eso hi saṅgho vipulo mahaggato,

Esappameyyo udadhīva sāgaro;

Ete hi seṭṭhā naravīrasāvakā narasīhasāvakā (ka.),

Pabhaṅkarā dhammamudīrayanti.

'For this Saṅgha is extensive and great, immeasurable like the ocean, the sea. These are the excellent disciples of the heroic man, the light-makers who proclaim the Dhamma.'

“Tesaṃ sudinnaṃ suhutaṃ suyiṭṭhaṃ,

Ye saṅghamuddissa dadanti dānaṃ;

Sā [T 0.0588] dakkhiṇā saṅghagatā patiṭṭhitā,

Mahapphalā lokavidūna vaṇṇitā.

For those who give a donation with the Saṅgha as their aim, their donation is well-given, well-offered, a good sacrifice. That offering, directed to and established in the Saṅgha, is praised by the Knower of the World as being of great fruit.

“Etādisaṃ yaññamanussarantā,

Ye vedajātā vicaranti viharanti (sī. ka.) loke;

Vineyya maccheramalaṃ samūlaṃ,

Aninditā saggamupenti ṭhāna”nti vi. va. 645, 754.

Those who, with joy arisen, live in the world recollecting such a sacrifice, having removed the stain of stinginess together with its root, they, being unblamed, approach the heavenly state.

Attheva [P 0.0555] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphalanti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. If that is so, what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.

Na vattabbaṃ saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphalantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Saṅgha Is of Great Fruit' is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(175) 10. Na vattabbaṃ buddhassadinnaṃ mahapphalantikathā

(175) 10. Discussion: It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Buddha Is of Great Fruit

799. Na [M 0.0403][V 0.0449] vattabbaṃ – “buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā dvipadānaṃ aggo, dvipadānaṃ seṭṭho, dvipadānaṃ pamokkho, dvipadānaṃ uttamo, dvipadānaṃ pavaro asamo asamasamo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggaloti? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā dvipadānaṃ aggo, dvipadānaṃ seṭṭho, dvipadānaṃ pamokkho, dvipadānaṃ uttamo, dvipadānaṃ pavaro asamo asamasamo appaṭisamo appaṭibhāgo appaṭipuggalo, tena vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

799. Should it not be said, “What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit”? Yes. Is not the Blessed One the foremost of bipeds, the best of bipeds, the chief of bipeds, the highest of bipeds, the most excellent of bipeds, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, incomparable, without a counterpart, without a person like him? Yes. If the Blessed One is the foremost of bipeds, the best of bipeds, the chief of bipeds, the highest of bipeds, the most excellent of bipeds, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, incomparable, without a counterpart, without a person like him, then indeed it should be said, “What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Atthi koci buddhena samasamo – sīlena samādhinā paññāyāti? Natthi[T 0.0589]. Hañci natthi koci buddhena samasamo – sīlena samādhinā paññāya, tena vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti.

Should it not be said, “What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit”? Yes. Is there anyone equal to the Buddha in virtue, concentration, and wisdom? There is not. If there is no one equal to the Buddha in virtue, concentration, and wisdom, then indeed it should be said, “What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.”

Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Should it not be said, “What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit”? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“Nayimasmiṃ vā loke parasmiṃ [P 0.0556] vā pana,

Buddhena seṭṭho ca samo ca vijjati;

Yamāhuneyyānaṃ aggataṃ gato,

Puññatthikānaṃ vipulapphalesina”nti vi. va. 1047.

“Neither in this world nor in another is there one better or equal to the Buddha, who has attained the foremost state among those worthy of offerings, for those seeking merit, desiring abundant fruits.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphalanti.

Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.

Na vattabbaṃ buddhassa dinnaṃ mahapphalantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on 'It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Buddha Is of Great Fruit' is concluded.

17. Sattarasamavaggo

17. The Seventeenth Chapter

(176) 11. Dakkhiṇāvisuddhikathā

(176) 11. Discussion on the Purity of Offerings

800. Dāyakatova [V 0.0450] dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakatoti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi keci paṭiggāhakā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti? Āmantā[M 0.0404]. Hañci atthi keci paṭiggāhakā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato”ti.

800. Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But are there not some recipients who are worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If there are indeed such recipients—worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world—then surely it should not be said that “a gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient.”

Dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakatoti? Āmantā[T 0.0590]. Nanu cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci cattāro purisayugā aṭṭha purisapuggalā dakkhiṇeyyā vuttā bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato”ti.

Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But has the Blessed One not declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight individuals, are worthy of offerings? Yes. If the four pairs of persons, the eight individuals, have indeed been declared by the Blessed One as worthy of offerings, then surely it should not be said that “a gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient.”

Dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakatoti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0557] atthi keci sotāpanne dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci sotāpanne dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhenti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato”ti.

Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But are there not some who, by giving a gift to a stream-enterer, accomplish an offering? Yes. If there are some who, by giving a gift to a stream-enterer, accomplish an offering, then surely it should not be said that “a gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient.”

Nanu atthi keci sakadāgāmissa…pe… anāgāmissa…pe… arahato dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhentīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi keci arahato dānaṃ datvā dakkhiṇaṃ ārādhenti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato”ti.

But are there not some who, by giving a gift to a once-returner… to a non-returner… to an arahant, accomplish an offering? Yes. If there are some who, by giving a gift to an arahant, accomplish an offering, then surely it should not be said that “a gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient.”

801. Paṭiggāhakato dānaṃ visujjhatīti? Āmantā. Añño aññassa kārako, parakataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ, añño karoti añño paṭisaṃvedetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

801. Is a gift purified by the recipient? Yes. Is one the agent for another? Is pleasure and pain caused by another? Does one person perform an action and another experience it? This should not be said… and so on.

Dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakatoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “catasso [V 0.0451] kho imā, ānanda, dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo! Katamā catasso? Atthānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato; atthānanda, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati, no dāyakato[T 0.0591]; atthānanda, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca; atthānanda, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato. Imā kho, ānanda, catasso dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo”ti ma. ni. 3.381. Attheva [M 0.0405] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dāyakatova dānaṃ visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato”ti.

Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “There are, Ānanda, these four purifications of offerings. What are the four? There is, Ānanda, an offering purified by the giver, not by the recipient; there is, Ānanda, an offering purified by the recipient, not by the giver; there is, Ānanda, an offering purified by both the giver and the recipient; there is, Ānanda, an offering purified by neither the giver nor the recipient. These, Ānanda, are the four purifications of offerings.” Is there such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, “A gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient.”

Dakkhiṇāvisuddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Purity of Offerings is concluded.

Sattarasamavaggo.

The Seventeenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Atthi [T 0.0592][P 0.0558] arahato puññūpacayo, natthi arahato akālamaccu, sabbamidaṃ kammato, indriyabaddhaññeva dukkhaṃ, ṭhapetvā ariyamaggaṃ avasesā saṅkhārā dukkhā, saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ paṭiggaṇhāti, saṅgho dakkhiṇaṃ visodheti, saṅgho bhuñjati pivati khādati sāyati, saṅghassa dinnaṃ mahapphalaṃ, atthi dānaṃ visuddhiyāti visujjhatīti (syā.).

The discourse on 'There is accumulation of merit for an Arahant', the discourse on 'There is no untimely death for an Arahant', the discourse on 'All this is due to kamma', the discourse on 'Only that which is bound to the sense faculties is suffering', the discourse on 'Except for the Noble Path, the remaining formations are suffering', the discourse on 'The Saṅgha receives offerings', the discourse on 'The Saṅgha purifies offerings', the discourse on 'The Saṅgha eats, drinks, consumes, and savors', the discourse on 'What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit', and the discourse on 'There is giving for purification'.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(177) 1. Manussalokakathā

(177) 1. Discussion on the Human World

802. Na [P 0.0559] vattabbaṃ – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi buddhavutthāni cetiyāni ārāmavihāragāmanigamanagarāni raṭṭhāni janapadānīti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi buddhavutthāni cetiyāni ārāmavihāragāmanigamanagarāni raṭṭhāni janapadāni, tena vata re vattabbe – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti.

802. Should it not be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world'? Indeed, it should not be said. Are there not shrines where the Buddha dwelt, monasteries, villages, market towns, cities, realms, and districts? Yes. If there are shrines where the Buddha dwelt, monasteries, villages, market towns, cities, realms, and districts, then indeed it should be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā lumbiniyā jāto, bodhiyā mūle abhisambuddho, bārāṇasiyaṃ bhagavatā dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ, cāpāle [V 0.0452] cetiye āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho, kusinārāyaṃ bhagavā parinibbutoti? Āmantā. Hañci [T 0.0593] bhagavā lumbiniyā jāto…pe… kusinārāyaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, tena vata re vattabbe – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti.

Should it not be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world'? Indeed, it should not be said. But was the Blessed One not born in Lumbinī and fully awakened at the foot of the Bodhi tree; was the Wheel of Dhamma not set in motion by the Blessed One in Bārāṇasī; was his life-span not relinquished at the Cāpāla Shrine; and did the Blessed One not attain final Nibbāna in Kusinārā? Yes. If the Blessed One was born in Lumbinī… and attained final Nibbāna in Kusinārā, then indeed it should be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ ukkaṭṭhāyaṃ viharāmi subhagavane sālarājamūle”ti [M 0.0406] dī. ni. 2.91; “ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ uruvelāyaṃ viharāmi ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho”ti a. ni. 4.21; “ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ rājagahe viharāmi veḷuvane kaḷandakanivāpe”ti dī. ni. 2.180; “ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ sāvatthiyaṃ viharāmi jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme”ti[P 0.0560]; “ekamidāhaṃ, bhikkhave, samayaṃ vesāliyaṃ viharāmi mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāya”nti dī. ni. 3.11! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsīti.

Should it not be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world'? Indeed, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Once, monks, I was staying at Ukkaṭṭhā in the Subhaga Grove at the foot of a great Sāla tree'; 'Once, monks, I was staying at Uruvelā at the Goatherd's Banyan tree, newly awakened'; 'Once, monks, I was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary'; 'Once, monks, I was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park'; 'Once, monks, I was staying at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Peaked Roof'? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world.

803. Buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsīti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā loke jāto, loke saṃvaḍḍho, lokaṃ abhibhuyya viharati anupalitto lokenāti a. ni. 4.36? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā loke jāto, loke saṃvaḍḍho, lokaṃ abhibhuyya viharati anupalitto lokena, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsī”ti.

803. Did the Buddha, the Blessed One, dwell in the human world? Yes. But was the Blessed One not born in the world, did he not grow up in the world, and does he not dwell having overcome the world, unstained by the world? Yes. If the Blessed One was born in the world, grew up in the world, and dwells having overcome the world, unstained by the world, then it should not be said: 'The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelt in the human world.'

Manussalokakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Human World is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(178) 2. Dhammadesanākathā

18. (178) 2. Discourse on the Teaching of the Dhamma

804. Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desito”ti? Āmantā. Kena desitoti? Abhinimmitena desitoti. Abhinimmito jino satthā sammāsambuddho sabbaññū sabbadassāvī dhammassāmī dhammappaṭisaraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should it not be said: 'The Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One'? Indeed, it should not be said. By whom was it taught? It was taught by a created being. Is that created being the Conqueror, the Teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Omniscient, the All-Seeing, the Lord of the Dhamma, one for whom the Dhamma is the refuge? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Na [V 0.0453] vattabbaṃ – “buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desito”ti? Āmantā. Kena desitoti? Āyasmatā ānandena desitoti. Āyasmā ānando jino satthā sammāsambuddho sabbaññū sabbadassāvī dhammassāmī dhammappaṭisaraṇoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

804. Should it not be said: 'The Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One'? Indeed, it should not be said. By whom was it taught? It was taught by the Venerable Ānanda. Is the Venerable Ānanda the Conqueror, the Teacher, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Omniscient, the All-Seeing, the Lord of the Dhamma, one for whom the Dhamma is the refuge? It should not be said thus… and so on.

805. Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desito”ti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0561] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “saṃkhittenapi kho ahaṃ, sāriputta, dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ; vitthārenapi [M 0.0407] kho ahaṃ, sāriputta, dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ; saṃkhittavitthārenapi kho ahaṃ, sāriputta, dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ; aññātāro ca dullabhā”ti a. ni. 3.33 sāriputtasutte! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desitoti.

Should it not be said: 'The Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One'? Indeed, it should not be said. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Sāriputta, I could teach the Dhamma in brief; Sāriputta, I could teach the Dhamma in detail; Sāriputta, I could teach the Dhamma both in brief and in detail; but those who understand are rare'? Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.

806. Na vattabbaṃ – “buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desito”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “‘abhiññāyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desemi, no anabhiññāya; sanidānāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desemi, no anidānaṃ[T 0.0595]; sappāṭihāriyāhaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desemi, no appāṭihāriyaṃ; tassa yañcassa (sī. pī. ka.) mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, abhiññāya dhammaṃ desayato no anabhiññāya, sanidānaṃ dhammaṃ desayato no anidānaṃ, sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desayato no appāṭihāriyaṃ karaṇīyo ovādo karaṇīyā anusāsanī; alañca pana vo, bhikkhave, tuṭṭhiyā alaṃ attamanatāya alaṃ somanassāya – sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto dhammo, suppaṭipanno saṅgho’ti. Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne dasasahassilokadhātu akampitthā”ti a. ni. 3.126! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desitoti.

805. Should it not be said: 'The Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One'? Indeed, it should not be said.
