But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, I teach the Dhamma having directly known it, not without having directly known it; I teach the Dhamma with its cause, not without a cause; I teach the Dhamma with its wonders, not without wonders. For me, monks, who teaches the Dhamma having directly known it, not without having directly known it; who teaches the Dhamma with its cause, not without a cause; who teaches the Dhamma with its wonders, not without wonders—my instruction is to be followed, my admonition is to be followed. And it is enough, monks, for your satisfaction, enough for your delight, enough for your joy that: “The Blessed One is a Perfectly Enlightened One, the Dhamma is well-proclaimed, the Saṅgha is of good conduct.” And while this exposition was being spoken, the ten-thousandfold world-system trembled'? Is there not such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.

Dhammadesanākathā niṭṭhitā.

806. The Discourse on the Teaching of the Dhamma is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(179) 3. Karuṇākathā

(179) 3. Discourse on Compassion

807. Natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Āmantā. Natthi buddhassa bhagavato mettāti[V 0.0454]? Na [P 0.0562] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Āmantā. Natthi buddhassa bhagavato muditā…pe… upekkhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

18. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no loving-kindness? It should not be said thus… Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no sympathetic joy… equanimity? It should not be said thus….

Atthi buddhassa bhagavato mettāti? Āmantā. Atthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi buddhassa [T 0.0596] bhagavato muditā…pe… upekkhāti? Āmantā. Atthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have loving-kindness? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have compassion? It should not be said thus… Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have sympathetic joy… equanimity? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have compassion? It should not be said thus….

Natthi [M 0.0408] buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Āmantā. Bhagavā akāruṇikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu bhagavā kāruṇiko lokahito lokānukampako lokatthacaroti? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā kāruṇiko lokahito lokānukampako lokatthacaro, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇā”ti…pe….

807. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Is the Blessed One uncompassionate? It should not be said thus… Is not the Blessed One compassionate, a benefactor of the world, one who has compassion for the world, and one who acts for the welfare of the world? Yes. If the Blessed One is compassionate, a benefactor of the world, one who has compassion for the world, and one who acts for the welfare of the world, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion.’

Natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā mahākaruṇāsamāpattiṃ samāpajjīti? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā mahākaruṇāsamāpattiṃ samāpajji, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇā”ti.

Does the Blessed One, the Buddha, have no compassion? Yes. Did not the Blessed One enter the attainment of great compassion? Yes. If the Blessed One entered the attainment of great compassion, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The Blessed One, the Buddha, has no compassion.’

808. Atthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti? Āmantā. Bhagavā sarāgoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇāti.

808. Does the Blessed One, the Buddha, have compassion? Yes. Is the Blessed One lustful? It should not be said thus. Then the Blessed One, the Buddha, has no compassion.

Karuṇākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Compassion is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(180) 4. Gandhajātikathā

(180) 4. The Discussion on Kinds of Fragrance

809. Buddhassa [P 0.0563] bhagavato uccārapassāvo ativiya aññe gandhajāte adhiggaṇhātīti[V 0.0455]? Āmantā. Bhagavā gandhabhojīti? Na [T 0.0597] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu bhagavā odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “buddhassa bhagavato uccārapassāvo ativiya aññe gandhajāte adhiggaṇhātī”ti.

809. Does the Blessed One’s excrement and urine exceedingly surpass all other kinds of fragrance? Yes. Is the Blessed One one who feeds on fragrances? It should not be said thus… Does not the Blessed One eat boiled rice and gruel? Yes. If the Blessed One eats boiled rice and gruel, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The Blessed One’s excrement and urine exceedingly surpass all other kinds of fragrance.’

Buddhassa bhagavato uccārapassāvo ativiya aññe gandhajāte adhiggaṇhātīti? Āmantā. Atthi keci buddhassa bhagavato uccārapassāvaṃ nhāyanti vilimpanti ucchādenti uccārenti (sī. pī. ka.) peḷāya paṭisāmenti karaṇḍāya nikkhipanti āpaṇe pasārenti, tena ca gandhena gandhakaraṇīyaṃ karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the Blessed One’s excrement and urine exceedingly surpass all other kinds of fragrance? Yes. Are there any who bathe in, anoint themselves with, or smear themselves with the Blessed One’s excrement and urine, put it away in a basket, deposit it in a box, display it in shops, and use that fragrance to make perfumes? It should not be said thus….

Gandhajātikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Kinds of Fragrance is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(181) 5. Ekamaggakathā

(181) 5. The Discussion on the Single Path

810. Ekena [M 0.0409] ariyamaggena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Catunnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… catunnaṃ saññānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ekena ariyamaggena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotīti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggenāti[P 0.0564]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmi…pe… anāgāmimaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

810. Is it through one Noble Path that the four fruits of recluseship are realized? Yes. Is it a convergence of the four contacts… the four perceptions? It should not be said thus… Is it through one Noble Path that the four fruits of recluseship are realized? Yes. Is it by the path of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… by the path of once-returning… by the path of non-returning? It should not be said thus….

Katamena maggenāti? Arahattamaggenāti. Arahattamaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ [T 0.0598] jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattamaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānaṃ sotāpattiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ pahānaṃ sotāpattiphalaṃ vuttaṃ [V 0.0456] bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahattamaggena sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ vicikicchaṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ jahatī”ti.

By which path? By the path of arahantship. Does the path of arahantship abandon identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals? It should not be said thus… Does the path of arahantship abandon identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals? Yes. Has not the Blessed One declared that the abandoning of the three fetters is the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the abandoning of the three fetters is the fruit of stream-entry, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The path of arahantship abandons identity view, doubt, and adherence to rites and rituals.’

Arahattamaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattamaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ tanubhāvaṃ sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ tanubhāvaṃ sakadāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahattamaggena oḷārikaṃ kāmarāgaṃ oḷārikaṃ byāpādaṃ jahatī”ti.

Does the path of arahantship abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will? It should not be said thus… Does the path of arahantship abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will? Yes. Has not the Blessed One declared that the attenuation of sensual desire and ill will is the fruit of once-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the attenuation of sensual desire and ill will is the fruit of once-returning, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The path of arahantship abandons gross sensual desire and gross ill will.’

Arahattamaggena aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattamaggena aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ jahatīti? Āmantā[P 0.0565]. Nanu kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ anavasesappahānaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci kāmarāgabyāpādānaṃ anavasesappahānaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahattamaggena aṇusahagataṃ kāmarāgaṃ aṇusahagataṃ byāpādaṃ jahatī”ti.

Does the path of arahantship abandon subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will? It should not be said thus… Does the path of arahantship abandon subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will? Yes. Has not the Blessed One declared that the complete abandoning of sensual desire and ill will is the fruit of non-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the complete abandoning of sensual desire and ill will is the fruit of non-returning, then it should certainly not be said: ‘The path of arahantship abandons subtle sensual desire and subtle ill will.’

811. Na vattabbaṃ – “ekena ariyamaggena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotī”ti? Āmantā. Bhagavatā sotāpattimaggo bhāvitoti? Āmantā[T 0.0599][M 0.0410]. Bhagavā sotāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… bhagavatā sakadāgāmi…pe… anāgāmimaggo bhāvitoti? Āmantā. Bhagavā anāgāmīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

811. Should it not be said: ‘One realizes the four fruits of recluseship through a single Noble Path’? Yes. Has the path of stream-entry been developed by the Blessed One? Yes. Is the Blessed One a stream-enterer? It should not be said thus… Has the path of once-returning… the path of non-returning been developed by the Blessed One? Yes. Is the Blessed One a non-returner? It should not be said thus….

812. Bhagavā ekena ariyamaggena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikaroti, sāvakā catūhi ariyamaggehi cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarontīti? Āmantā. Sāvakā buddhassa bhagavato adiṭṭhaṃ dakkhanti anadhigataṃ adhigacchanti asacchikataṃ sacchikarontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

812. Does the Blessed One realize the four fruits of recluseship through a single Noble Path, while disciples realize the four fruits of recluseship through four Noble Paths? Yes. Do disciples see what the Buddha, the Blessed One, has not seen, attain what he has not attained, and realize what he has not realized? It should not be said thus….

Ekamaggakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Single Path is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(182) 6. Jhānasaṅkantikathā

(182) 6. The Discussion on Transitioning Between Jhānas

813. Jhānā [V 0.0457] jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Paṭhamā [P 0.0566] jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… jhānā jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Dutiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

813. Does one transition from a jhāna to a jhāna? Yes. Does one transition from the first jhāna to the third jhāna? It should not be said thus… Does one transition from a jhāna to a jhāna? Yes. Does one transition from the second jhāna to the fourth jhāna? It should not be said thus….

Paṭhamā jhānā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Yā paṭhamassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva dutiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one transition from the first jhāna to the second jhāna? Yes. Is the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the first jhāna the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the second jhāna? It should not be said thus….

Paṭhamā jhānā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamati, na vattabbaṃ [T 0.0600] – “yā paṭhamassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva dutiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “paṭhamā jhānā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatī”ti…pe….

Given that one transitions from the first jhāna to the second jhāna, should it not be said that 'the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the first jhāna is the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the second jhāna'? Yes. Does the second jhāna arise for one who does not advert… for one who does not resolve? That should not be said… Does not the second jhāna arise for one who adverts… for one who resolves? Yes. If the second jhāna arises for one who adverts… for one who resolves, then indeed, friend, it should not be said that 'one transitions from the first jhāna to the second jhāna'…

Paṭhamā jhānā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ kāme ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ kāme ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one transition from the first jhāna to the second jhāna? Yes. Does the first jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in sensual pleasures? Yes. Does the second jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in sensual pleasures? That should not be said…

Paṭhamaṃ [P 0.0567] jhānaṃ savitakkaṃ savicāranti? Āmantā[M 0.0411]. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ savitakkaṃ savicāranti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… paṭhamā jhānā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ taṃ dutiyaṃ jhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the first jhāna accompanied by initial application and sustained application? Yes. Is the second jhāna accompanied by initial application and sustained application? That should not be said… Does one transition from the first jhāna to the second jhāna? Yes. Is that very first jhāna the second jhāna? That should not be said…

814. Dutiyā [V 0.0458] jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Yā dutiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva tatiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

814. Does one transition from the second jhāna to the third jhāna? Yes. Is the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the second jhāna the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the third jhāna? That should not be said…

Dutiyā jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamati, na vattabbaṃ – “yā dutiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva tatiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā[T 0.0601]. Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… nanu tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dutiyā jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatī”ti.

Given that one transitions from the second jhāna to the third jhāna, should it not be said that 'the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the second jhāna is the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the third jhāna'? Yes. Does the third jhāna arise for one who does not advert… for one who does not resolve? That should not be said… Does not the third jhāna arise for one who adverts… for one who resolves? Yes. If the third jhāna arises for one who adverts… for one who resolves, then indeed, friend, it should not be said that 'one transitions from the second jhāna to the third jhāna'.

Dutiyā jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ vitakkavicāre ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ vitakkavicāre ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one transition from the second jhāna to the third jhāna? Yes. Does the second jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in initial and sustained application? Yes. Does the third jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in initial and sustained application? That should not be said…

Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ sappītikanti? Āmantā. Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ sappītikanti? Na [P 0.0568] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dutiyā jhānā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ taṃ tatiyaṃ jhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the second jhāna accompanied by rapture? Yes. Is the third jhāna accompanied by rapture? That should not be said… Does one transition from the second jhāna to the third jhāna? Yes. Is that very second jhāna the third jhāna? That should not be said…

815. Tatiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Yā tatiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva catutthassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

815. Does one transition from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna? Yes. Is the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the third jhāna the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the fourth jhāna? That should not be said…

Tatiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamati, na vattabbaṃ – “yā tatiyassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, sāva catutthassa jhānassa uppādāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhī”ti? Āmantā. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ anāvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… appaṇidahantassa [T 0.0602] uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu catutthaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa [V 0.0459] uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Hañci [M 0.0412] catutthaṃ jhānaṃ āvaṭṭentassa uppajjati…pe… paṇidahantassa uppajjati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “tatiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatī”ti.

Given that one transitions from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna, should it not be said that 'the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the third jhāna is the same as the adverting… and resolve for the arising of the fourth jhāna'? Yes. Does the fourth jhāna arise for one who does not advert… for one who does not resolve? That should not be said… Does not the fourth jhāna arise for one who adverts… for one who resolves? Yes. If the fourth jhāna arises for one who adverts… for one who resolves, then indeed, friend, it should not be said that 'one transitions from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna'.

Tatiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ pītiṃ ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Āmantā. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ pītiṃ ādīnavato manasikaroto uppajjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one transition from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna? Yes. Does the third jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in rapture? Yes. Does the fourth jhāna arise for one who gives attention to the danger in rapture? That should not be said…

Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ sukhasahagatanti? Āmantā. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ sukhasahagatanti? Na [P 0.0569] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tatiyā jhānā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti? Āmantā. Taññeva tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ taṃ catutthaṃ jhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the third jhāna accompanied by happiness? Yes. Is the fourth jhāna accompanied by happiness? That should not be said… Does one transition from the third jhāna to the fourth jhāna? Yes. Is that very third jhāna the fourth jhāna? That should not be said…

816. Na vattabbaṃ – “jhānā jhānaṃ saṅkamatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti a. ni. 2.13; 4.163! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi jhānā jhānaṃ saṅkamatīti.

816. Should it not be said that 'one transitions from a jhāna to a jhāna'? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures… having entered upon the fourth jhāna, abides in it'? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, one transitions from a jhāna to a jhāna.

Jhānasaṅkantikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Transitioning Between Jhānas is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(183) 7. Jhānantarikakathā

(183) 7. Discourse on the Jhāna-Interval

817. Atthi [T 0.0603] jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Atthi phassantarikā…pe… atthi saññantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

18. Is there an intermediate jhāna concentration? Yes. Is there an intermediate contact concentration… and so on… is there an intermediate perception concentration? That should not be said thus… and so on.

Atthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Dutiyassa ca jhānassa tatiyassa ca jhānassa antare atthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there an intermediate jhāna concentration? Yes. Is there an intermediate jhāna concentration between the second jhāna and the third jhāna? That should not be said thus… and so on.

Atthi [V 0.0460] jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Tatiyassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa antare atthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

817. Is there an intermediate jhāna concentration? Yes. Is there an intermediate jhāna concentration between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna? That should not be said thus… and so on.

Dutiyassa ca jhānassa tatiyassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Hañci dutiyassa ca jhānassa tatiyassa ca jhānassa antare natthi [P 0.0570] jhānantarikā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi jhānantarikā”ti.

Is there no intermediate jhāna concentration between the second jhāna and the third jhāna? Yes. If there is no intermediate jhāna concentration between the second jhāna and the third jhāna, then indeed, friend, it should not be said that 'there is an intermediate jhāna concentration'.

Tatiyassa [M 0.0413] ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Hañci tatiyassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi jhānantarikā”ti.

Is there no jhāna-interval concentration between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna? Yes. If there is no jhāna-interval concentration between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'there is jhāna-interval concentration'.

818. Paṭhamassa ca jhānassa dutiyassa ca jhānassa antare atthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Dutiyassa ca jhānassa tatiyassa ca jhānassa antare atthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

818. Is there jhāna-interval concentration between the first jhāna and the second jhāna? Yes. Is there jhāna-interval concentration between the second jhāna and the third jhāna? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Paṭhamassa ca jhānassa dutiyassa ca jhānassa antare atthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Tatiyassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa antare [T 0.0604] atthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there jhāna-interval concentration between the first jhāna and the second jhāna? Yes. Is there jhāna-interval concentration between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Dutiyassa ca jhānassa tatiyassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Paṭhamassa ca jhānassa dutiyassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no jhāna-interval concentration between the second jhāna and the third jhāna? Yes. Is there no jhāna-interval concentration between the first jhāna and the second jhāna? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Tatiyassa ca jhānassa catutthassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Paṭhamassa ca jhānassa dutiyassa ca jhānassa antare natthi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there no jhāna-interval concentration between the third jhāna and the fourth jhāna? Yes. Is there no jhāna-interval concentration between the first jhāna and the second jhāna? It should not be said thus... and so on.

819. Avitakko [V 0.0461] vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Savitakko savicāro samādhi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

819. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Is concentration with initial application and with sustained application the jhāna-interval concentration? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Avitakko [P 0.0571] avicāro samādhi jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Is concentration without initial application and without sustained application the jhāna-interval concentration? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Savitakko savicāro samādhi na jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi na jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is concentration with initial application and with sustained application not the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application not the jhāna-interval concentration? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Avitakko avicāro samādhi na jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi na jhānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is concentration without initial application and without sustained application not the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application not the jhāna-interval concentration? It should not be said thus... and so on.

820. Dvinnaṃ jhānānaṃ paṭuppannānamantare avitakko vicāramatto samādhīti? Āmantā. Nanu avitakke vicāramatte samādhimhi vattamāne paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ niruddhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ paṭuppannanti? Āmantā. Hañci avitakke vicāramatte [M 0.0414] samādhimhi vattamāne paṭhamaṃ [T 0.0605] jhānaṃ niruddhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ paṭuppannaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dvinnaṃ jhānānaṃ paṭuppannānamantare avitakko vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikāti.

820. Between two presently arisen jhānas, is there concentration without initial application and with only sustained application? Yes. Is it not so that when concentration without initial application and with only sustained application is present, the first jhāna has ceased and the second jhāna has arisen? Yes. If, when concentration without initial application and with only sustained application is present, the first jhāna has ceased and the second jhāna has arisen, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'between two presently arisen jhānas, concentration without initial application and with only sustained application is the jhāna-interval concentration'.

821. Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi na jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi avitakko vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikāti.

821. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application not the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application the first jhāna... and so on... the second jhāna... and so on... the third jhāna... and so on... the fourth jhāna? It should not be said thus. In that case, concentration without initial application and with only sustained application is the jhāna-interval concentration.

822. Avitakko vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikāti? Āmantā. Nanu tayo samādhī vuttā bhagavatā – savitakko savicāro samādhi, avitakko vicāramatto samādhi, avitakko avicāro samādhīti dī. ni. 3.305, 353? Āmantā. Hañci tayo samādhī vuttā bhagavatā – savitakko…pe… avicāro samādhi, no ca vata re vattabbe [P 0.0572] – “avitakko vicāramatto samādhi jhānantarikā”ti.

822. Is concentration without initial application and with only sustained application the jhāna-interval concentration? Yes. Have not three kinds of concentration been taught by the Blessed One: concentration with initial application and with sustained application, concentration without initial application and with only sustained application, and concentration without initial application and without sustained application? Yes. If three kinds of concentration have been taught by the Blessed One—concentration with initial application... and so on... and without sustained application—then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'concentration without initial application and with only sustained application is the jhāna-interval concentration'.

Jhānantarikakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Jhāna-Interval is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(184) 8. Saddaṃ suṇātītikathā

18. (184) 8. The Discourse on 'One Hears a Sound'

823. Samāpanno [V 0.0462] saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Samāpanno cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… sotena…pe… ghānena…pe… jivhāya…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who has attained an absorption hear a sound? Yes. Does one who has attained an absorption see a form with the eye... and so on... hear with the ear... and so on... smell with the nose... and so on... taste with the tongue... and so on... touch a tangible object with the body? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Samāpanno [T 0.0606] saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Sotaviññāṇasamaṅgī samāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Nanu samādhi manoviññāṇasamaṅgissāti? Āmantā. Hañci samādhi manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātī”ti.

823. Does one who has attained an absorption hear a sound? Yes. Is one endowed with ear-consciousness a person who has attained an absorption? It should not be said thus. Is not concentration a state of one endowed with mind-consciousness? Yes. If concentration is a state of one endowed with mind-consciousness, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'one who has attained an absorption hears a sound'.

Samādhi manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa, sotaviññāṇasamaṅgī saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Hañci samādhi manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa, sotaviññāṇasamaṅgī saddaṃ suṇāti, no ca vata re vattabbe – “samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātī”ti[M 0.0415]. Samādhi manoviññāṇasamaṅgissa, sotaviññāṇasamaṅgī saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ phassānaṃ…pe… dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Concentration is a state of one endowed with mind-consciousness, and one endowed with ear-consciousness hears a sound? Yes. If concentration is a state of one endowed with mind-consciousness, and one endowed with ear-consciousness hears a sound, then indeed, good sir, it should not be said that 'one who has attained an absorption hears a sound'. Concentration is a state of one endowed with mind-consciousness, and one endowed with ear-consciousness hears a sound? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts... and so on... a coming together of two consciousnesses? It should not be said thus... and so on.

824. Na vattabbaṃ – “samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatāti? Āmantā[P 0.0573]. Hañci paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātī”ti.

Should it not be said that 'one who has attained an absorption hears a sound'? Yes. Has not the Blessed One said that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna, then for that reason, good sir, it should be said that 'one who has attained an absorption hears a sound'.

825. Paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatāti, samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Dutiyassa jhānassa vitakko vicāro kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā, atthi tassa vitakkavicārāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

824. Because the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first jhāna, does one who has attained an absorption hear a sound? Yes. The Blessed One has said that initial application and sustained application are thorns to the second jhāna; do initial application and sustained application exist for it? It should not be said thus... and so on.

Paṭhamassa jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatāti, samāpanno saddaṃ suṇātīti? Āmantā. Tatiyassa jhānassa pīti kaṇṭako…pe… catutthassa jhānassa assāsapassāso kaṇṭako [V 0.0463] … ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa [T 0.0607] rūpasaññā kaṇṭako… viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā kaṇṭako… saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca kaṇṭako vutto bhagavatā, atthi tassa saññā ca vedanā cāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn for the first jhāna; does one who has attained it hear a sound? Yes. For the third jhāna, rapture is a thorn… For the fourth jhāna, in-and-out breathing is a thorn… For one who has attained the base of infinite space, perception of form is a thorn… For one who has attained the base of infinite consciousness, perception of the base of infinite space is a thorn… For one who has attained the base of nothingness, perception of the base of infinite consciousness is a thorn… For one who has attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, perception of the base of nothingness is a thorn… For one who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling are thorns, as declared by the Blessed One. Does one who has attained it have perception and feeling? It should not be said thus…

Saddaṃ suṇātītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discussion on 'One Hears a Sound' is concluded.

18. Aṭṭhārasamavaggo

18. The Eighteenth Chapter

(185) 9. Cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatītikathā

(185) 9. Discourse on 'One Sees Form with the Eye'

826. Cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Rūpena rūpaṃ passatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpena rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Rūpena rūpaṃ paṭivijānātīti? Na [P 0.0574] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpena rūpaṃ paṭivijānātīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ manoviññāṇanti[M 0.0416]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatīti? Āmantā. Atthi cakkhussa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu natthi cakkhussa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi cakkhussa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatī”ti.

826. Does one see form with the eye? Yes. Does one see form with form? That should not be said… Does one see form with form? Yes. Does one cognize form with form? That should not be said… Does one cognize form with form? Yes. Is form mind-consciousness? That should not be said… Does one see form with the eye? Yes. Is there adverting… and directing of the eye? That should not be said… Is there not adverting… and directing of the eye? Yes. If there is no adverting… and directing of the eye, then truly it should not be said, "One sees form with the eye."

Sotena saddaṃ suṇātīti…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyatīti…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyatīti…pe… kāyena [T 0.0608] phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti? Āmantā. Rūpena rūpaṃ phusatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one hear a sound with the ear… smell an odor with the nose… taste a flavor with the tongue… touch a tangible object with the body? Yes. Does one touch form with form? That should not be said…

Rūpena rūpaṃ phusatīti? Āmantā. Rūpena rūpaṃ paṭivijānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpena rūpaṃ paṭivijānātīti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ manoviññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0464] …pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti? Āmantā. Atthi kāyassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu natthi kāyassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi kāyassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatī”ti…pe….

Does one touch form with form? Yes. Does one cognize form with form? That should not be said… Does one cognize form with form? Yes. Is form mind-consciousness? That should not be said… Does one touch a tangible object with the body? Yes. Is there adverting… and directing of the body? That should not be said… Is there not adverting… and directing of the body? Yes. If there is no adverting… and directing of the body, then it should not be said, "One touches a tangible object with the body."…

827. Na vattabbaṃ – “cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatī”ti…pe… “kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu [P 0.0575] vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatī”ti ma. ni. 1.349; a. ni. 4.37 (aṭṭhakathā passitabbā)! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusatīti.

827. Should it not be said, "One sees form with the eye"… "One touches a tangible object with the body"? Yes. But has not the Blessed One said, "Here, monks, a monk sees form with the eye… touches a tangible object with the body"? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, one sees form with the eye… one touches a tangible object with the body.

Cakkhunā rūpaṃ passatītikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on 'One Sees Form with the Eye' is concluded.

Aṭṭhārasamavaggo.

The Eighteenth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The recapitulation is:

Buddho bhagavā manussaloke aṭṭhāsi, buddhena bhagavatā dhammo desito, natthi buddhassa bhagavato karuṇā, buddhassa bhagavato uccārapassāvo ativiya [T 0.0609] aññe gandhajāte adhiggaṇhāti, ekena ariyamaggena cattāri sāmaññaphalāni sacchikaroti, jhānā jhānaṃ saṅkamati, atthi jhānantarikā, samāpanno saddaṃ suṇāti, cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusati.

The Buddha, the Blessed One, dwelled in the human world; the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One; the Blessed One has no compassion; the excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, surpasses all other kinds of scents; one realizes the four fruits of asceticism with a single noble path; one passes from jhāna to jhāna; there is an interval between jhānas; one in attainment hears a sound; one sees form with the eye and touches a tangible object with the body.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter

(186) 1. Kilesajahanakathā

(186) 1. Discourse on the Abandoning of Defilements

828. Atīte [M 0.0417][P 0.0576] kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Niruddhaṃ nirodheti, vigataṃ vigameti, khīṇaṃ khepeti, atthaṅgataṃ atthaṅgameti, abbhatthaṅgataṃ abbhatthaṅgametīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atīte kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ niruddhanti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ niruddhaṃ[V 0.0465], no ca vata re vattabbe – “atīte kilese jahatī”ti. Atīte kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu atītaṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Hañci atītaṃ natthi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atīte kilese jahatī”ti.

828. Does one abandon defilements in the past? Yes. Does one cause the ceased to cease again, the departed to depart again, the exhausted to be exhausted again, the set to set again, the completely set to completely set again? It should not be said thus… Does one abandon defilements in the past? Yes. Is not the past ceased? Yes. If the past is ceased, then it should not be said, ‘One abandons defilements in the past.’ Does one abandon defilements in the past? Yes. Is not the past non-existent? Yes. If the past is non-existent, then it should not be said, ‘One abandons defilements in the past.’

829. Anāgate kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Ajātaṃ ajaneti, asañjātaṃ asañjaneti, anibbattaṃ anibbatteti, apātubhūtaṃ apātubhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… anāgate kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ ajātanti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ ajātaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgate kilese jahatī”ti[T 0.0610]. Anāgate kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Nanu anāgataṃ natthīti? Āmantā. Hañci anāgataṃ natthi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “anāgate kilese jahatī”ti.

829. Does one abandon defilements in the future? Yes. Does one cause to be born that which is not yet born, cause to arise that which has not yet arisen, cause to be produced that which is not yet produced, cause to appear that which has not yet appeared? It should not be said thus… Does one abandon defilements in the future? Yes. Is not the future unborn? Yes. If the future is unborn, then it should not be said, ‘One abandons defilements in the future.’ Does one abandon defilements in the future? Yes. Is not the future non-existent? Yes. If the future is non-existent, then it should not be said, ‘One abandons defilements in the future.’

830. Paccuppanne [P 0.0577] kilese jahatīti? Āmantā. Ratto rāgaṃ jahati, duṭṭho dosaṃ jahati, mūḷho mohaṃ jahati, kiliṭṭho kilese jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rāgena rāgaṃ jahati, dosena dosaṃ jahati, mohena mohaṃ jahati, kilesehi kilese jahatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

830. Does one abandon defilements in the present? Yes. Does a lustful person abandon lust, a hateful person abandon hatred, a deluded person abandon delusion, a defiled person abandon defilements? It should not be said thus… Does one abandon lust with lust, hatred with hatred, delusion with delusion, defilements with defilements? It should not be said thus…

Rāgo cittasampayutto, maggo cittasampayuttoti? Āmantā. Dvinnaṃ cittānaṃ samodhānaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is lust associated with the mind, and is the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a meeting of the two minds? It should not be said thus…

Rāgo akusalo, maggo kusaloti? Āmantā. Kusalākusalā sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is lust unwholesome, and is the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and excellent states, the counterparts of dark and bright, come into a state of presence? It should not be said thus…

Kusalākusalā [M 0.0418] sāvajjānavajjā hīnapaṇītā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “cattārimāni, bhikkhave, suvidūravidūrāni! Katamāni cattāri? Nabhañca, bhikkhave, pathavī ca – idaṃ paṭhamaṃ suvidūravidūraṃ…pe… tasmā sataṃ dhammo asabbhi ārakā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kusalākusalā…pe… sammukhībhāvaṃ āgacchantī”ti.

Do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and excellent states, the counterparts of dark and bright, come into a state of presence? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, these four are very, very far apart. What four? The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first that is very, very far apart… Therefore, the Dhamma of the good is far from the unrighteous.’ Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, ‘Wholesome and unwholesome states… come into a state of presence.’

831. Na [V 0.0466] vattabbaṃ – “atīte kilese jahati, anāgate kilese jahati, paccuppanne kilese jahatī”ti? Āmantā. Natthi kilese jahatīti[T 0.0611]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… tena hi atīte kilese jahati, anāgate kilese jahati, paccuppanne kilese jahatīti.

831. Should it not be said, ‘One abandons defilements in the past, one abandons defilements in the future, and one abandons defilements in the present’? Yes. Is there no one who abandons defilements? It should not be said thus… Therefore, one abandons defilements in the past, one abandons defilements in the future, and one abandons defilements in the present.

Kilesajahanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Abandoning of Defilements is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter

(187) 2. Suññatākathā

(187) 2. Discourse on Emptiness

832. Suññatā [P 0.0578] saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Animittaṃ saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Appaṇihito saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… animittaṃ na vattabbaṃ – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanna”nti? Āmantā. Suññatā na vattabbā – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… appaṇihito na vattabbo – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpanno”ti? Āmantā. Suññatā na vattabbā – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

832. Is emptiness included in the aggregate of formations? Yes. Is the signless included in the aggregate of formations? It should not be said thus… Is emptiness included in the aggregate of formations? Yes. Is the desireless included in the aggregate of formations? It should not be said thus… Should it not be said that the signless is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? Yes. Should it not be said that emptiness is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? It should not be said thus… Should it not be said that the desireless is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? Yes. Should it not be said that emptiness is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? It should not be said thus…

Suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandho na anicco na saṅkhato na paṭiccasamuppanno na khayadhammo na vayadhammo na virāgadhammo na nirodhadhammo na vipariṇāmadhammoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu saṅkhārakkhandho anicco saṅkhato paṭiccasamuppanno khayadhammo vayadhammo virāgadhammo nirodhadhammo vipariṇāmadhammoti? Āmantā. Hañci saṅkhārakkhandho anicco…pe… vipariṇāmadhammo[T 0.0612], no ca vata re vattabbe – “suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti.

Is emptiness included in the aggregate of formations? Yes. Is the aggregate of formations not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently arisen, not of a nature to decay, not of a nature to perish, not of a nature to fade away, not of a nature to cease, not of a nature to change? It should not be said thus… Is not the aggregate of formations impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, of a nature to decay, of a nature to perish, of a nature to fade away, of a nature to cease, of a nature to change? Yes. If the aggregate of formations is impermanent… of a nature to change, then it should indeed not be said: 'emptiness is included in the aggregate of formations'.

833. Rūpakkhandhassa [M 0.0419] suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandhassa [P 0.0579] suññatā [V 0.0467] rūpakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanākkhandhassa…pe… saññākkhandhassa… viññāṇakkhandhassa suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Āmantā. Saṅkhārakkhandhassa suññatā viññāṇakkhandhapariyāpannāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

833. Is the emptiness of the aggregate of form included in the aggregate of formations? Yes. Is the emptiness of the aggregate of formations included in the aggregate of form? It should not be said thus… of the aggregate of feeling… of the aggregate of perception… Is the emptiness of the aggregate of consciousness included in the aggregate of formations? Yes. Is the emptiness of the aggregate of formations included in the aggregate of consciousness? It should not be said thus…

Saṅkhārakkhandhassa suññatā na vattabbā – “rūpakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Āmantā. Rūpakkhandhassa suññatā na vattabbā – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… saṅkhārakkhandhassa suññatā na vattabbā – “vedanākkhandhapariyāpannā…pe… saññākkhandhapariyāpannā… viññāṇakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Āmantā. Viññāṇakkhandhassa suññatā na vattabbā – “saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Should it not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of formations is 'included in the aggregate of form'? Yes. Should it not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of form is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? It should not be said thus… Should it not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of formations is 'included in the aggregate of feeling'… 'included in the aggregate of perception'… 'included in the aggregate of consciousness'? Yes. Should it not be said that the emptiness of the aggregate of consciousness is 'included in the aggregate of formations'? It should not be said thus…

834. Na vattabbaṃ – suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “suññamidaṃ, bhikkhave, saṅkhārā attena vā attaniyena vā”ti ma. ni. 3.69 āneñjasappāye! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannāti.

834. Should it not be said: 'emptiness is included in the aggregate of formations'? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Monks, these formations are empty of self or of what belongs to self”? Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, emptiness is included in the aggregate of formations.

Suññatākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Emptiness is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter

(188) 3 Sāmaññaphalakathā

(188) 3. Discourse on the Fruit of Recluseship

835. Sāmaññaphalaṃ [T 0.0613] asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ [P 0.0580] tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāmaññaphalaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

835. Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned? Yes. Is it Nibbāna, a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a supreme resort, the immutable, the deathless? It should not be said thus… Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or two intermediate states? It should not be said thus…

836. Sāmaññaphalaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Sāmaññaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0468] …pe… sāmaññaṃ saṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Sāmaññaphalaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

836. Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned? Yes. Is recluseship unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is recluseship conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of recluseship conditioned? It should not be said thus…

Sotāpattiphalaṃ [M 0.0420] asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sotāpattimaggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Sotāpattiphalaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is the path of stream-entry conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry conditioned? It should not be said thus…

Sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… arahattaphalaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Arahattamaggo asaṅkhatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattamaggo saṅkhatoti? Āmantā. Arahattaphalaṃ saṅkhatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship unconditioned? Yes. Is the path to arahantship unconditioned? It should not be said thus… Is the path to arahantship conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of arahantship conditioned? It should not be said thus…

Sotāpattiphalaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ…pe… anāgāmiphalaṃ [P 0.0581]…pe… arahattaphalaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Pañca tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned, the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there five unconditioned things? It should not be said thus… Are there five unconditioned things? Yes. Are there five protections… or five intermediate states? It should not be said thus…

Sāmaññaphalakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Fruit of Recluseship is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter

(189) 4. Pattikathā

(189) 4. Discourse on Attainment

837. Patti [T 0.0614] asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ saraṇaṃ parāyaṇaṃ accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… patti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

837. Is attainment unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna a protection, a shelter, a refuge, a supreme resort, the immutable, the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… Is attainment unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

838. Cīvarassa [V 0.0469] patti asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cīvarassa patti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na [P 0.0582] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… piṇḍapātassa…pe… senāsanassa…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārassa patti asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārassa patti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

838. Is the attainment of a robe unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… Is the attainment of a robe unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on… The attainment of almsfood… and so on… The attainment of lodging… and so on… Is the attainment of medicines and provisions for the sick unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the immutable, the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… Is the attainment of medicines and provisions for the sick unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

Cīvarassa [M 0.0421] patti asaṅkhatā…pe… piṇḍapātassa…pe… senāsanassa…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārassa [T 0.0615] patti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pañca asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Pañca tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the attainment of a robe unconditioned… and so on… of almsfood… and so on… of lodging… and so on… the attainment of medicines and provisions for the sick unconditioned, and Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there five unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there five unconditioned things? Yes. Are there five protections… and so on… or five intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

839. Paṭhamassa jhānassa patti asaṅkhatā (evaṃ sabbaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ) dutiyassa jhānassa… tatiyassa jhānassa… catutthassa jhānassa… ākāsānañcāyatanassa… viññāṇañcāyatanassa… ākiñcaññāyatanassa… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa… sotāpattimaggassa… sotāpattiphalassa… sakadāgāmimaggassa… sakadāgāmiphalassa… anāgāmimaggassa… anāgāmiphalassa… arahattamaggassa… arahattaphalassa patti asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… accutaṃ amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… arahattaphalassa patti asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā[P 0.0583]. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

839. Is the attainment of the first jhāna unconditioned? (Thus should all be elaborated in detail.) The attainment of the second jhāna… of the third jhāna… of the fourth jhāna… of the base of infinite space… of the base of infinite consciousness… of the base of nothingness… of the base of neither perception nor non-perception… of the path of stream-entry… of the fruit of stream-entry… of the path of a once-returner… of the fruit of a once-returner… of the path of a non-returner… of the fruit of a non-returner… of the path of arahantship… Is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the immutable, the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… Is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

Sotāpattimaggassa patti asaṅkhatā… sotāpattiphalassa patti asaṅkhatā… arahattamaggassa patti asaṅkhatā… arahattaphalassa patti asaṅkhatā… nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Nava asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nava asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Nava tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the attainment of the path of stream-entry unconditioned… the attainment of the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned… the attainment of the path of arahantship unconditioned… the attainment of the fruit of arahantship unconditioned… and Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there nine unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there nine unconditioned things? Yes. Are there nine protections… and so on… or nine intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

840. Na [V 0.0470] vattabbaṃ – patti asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Patti rūpaṃ [T 0.0616]… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi patti asaṅkhatāti.

840. Should it not be said: 'Attainment is unconditioned'? Yes. Is attainment form… feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness? This should not be said. Therefore, attainment is unconditioned.

Pattikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Attainment is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Section

(190) 5. Tathatākathā

5. Discussion on Suchness

841. Sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti[M 0.0422]? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve [P 0.0584] asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

841. Is the suchness of all phenomena unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… Is the suchness of all phenomena unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

842. Rūpassa rūpatā, nanu rūpatā asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… rūpassa rūpatā, nanu rūpatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Dve asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dve asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Dve tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

842. The form-ness of form—is not form-ness unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the deathless? This should not be said… and so on… The form-ness of form—is not form-ness unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… and so on… or two intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

Vedanāya vedanatā, nanu vedanatā…pe… saññāya saññatā, nanu saññatā…pe… saṅkhārānaṃ saṅkhāratā, nanu saṅkhāratā…pe… viññāṇassa viññāṇatā, nanu viññāṇatā asaṅkhatāti? Āmantā. Nibbānaṃ…pe… amatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0617]…pe….

The feeling-ness of feeling—is not feeling-ness… and so on… The perception-ness of perception—is not perception-ness… and so on… The formation-ness of formations—is not formation-ness… and so on… The consciousness-ness of consciousness—is not consciousness-ness unconditioned? Yes. Is Nibbāna… and so on… the deathless? This should not be said… and so on….

Rūpassa rūpatā, nanu rūpatā…pe… viññāṇassa viññāṇatā, nanu viññāṇatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānaṃ asaṅkhatanti? Āmantā. Cha asaṅkhatānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cha [V 0.0471] asaṅkhatānīti? Āmantā. Cha tāṇāni…pe… antarikā vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

The form-ness of form—is not form-ness… and so on… The consciousness-ness of consciousness—is not consciousness-ness unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there six unconditioned things? This should not be said… and so on… Are there six unconditioned things? Yes. Are there six protections… and so on… or six intermediate states? This should not be said… and so on….

843. Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā asaṅkhatā”ti? Āmantā. Sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā rūpaṃ… vedanā… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe[P 0.0585]. Tena hi sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā asaṅkhatāti.

843. Should it not be said: 'The suchness of all phenomena is unconditioned'? Yes. Is the suchness of all phenomena form… feeling… perception… formations… consciousness? This should not be said. Therefore, the suchness of all phenomena is unconditioned.

Tathatākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Suchness is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Section

(191) 6. Kusalakathā

6. Discussion on the Wholesome

844. Nibbānadhātu kusalāti? Āmantā. Sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Hañci anārammaṇā, natthi tāya [M 0.0423] āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “nibbānadhātu kusalā”ti.

844. Is the Nibbāna-element wholesome? Yes. Is it with an object, is there adverting towards it… and so on… aspiration? This should not be said… and so on… Is it not without an object, is there no adverting towards it… and so on… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object, and there is no adverting towards it… and so on… aspiration, then indeed it should not be said: 'The Nibbāna-element is wholesome'.

845. Alobho kusalo sārammaṇo, atthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Nibbānadhātu kusalā sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe …pe… adoso [T 0.0618] kusalo…pe… amoho kusalo…pe… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā kusalā sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā. Nibbānadhātu kusalā sārammaṇā, atthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

845. Is non-greed wholesome and with an object, is there adverting towards it… aspiration? Yes. Is the Nibbāna-element wholesome and with an object, is there adverting towards it… aspiration? It should not be said so… Is non-hatred wholesome… Is non-delusion wholesome… Is faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… Is wisdom wholesome and with an object, is there adverting towards it… aspiration? Yes. Is the Nibbāna-element wholesome and with an object, is there adverting towards it… aspiration? It should not be said so….

Nibbānadhātu kusalā anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[V 0.0472]. Alobho kusalo anārammaṇo, natthi tassa āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nibbānadhātu kusalā anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Āmantā[P 0.0586]. Adoso kusalo…pe… amoho kusalo…pe… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā kusalā anārammaṇā, natthi tāya āvaṭṭanā…pe… paṇidhīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Nibbāna-element wholesome and without an object, is there no adverting towards it… aspiration? Yes. Is non-greed wholesome and without an object, is there no adverting towards it… aspiration? It should not be said so… Is the Nibbāna-element wholesome and without an object, is there no adverting towards it… aspiration? Yes. Is non-hatred wholesome… Is non-delusion wholesome… Is faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… Is wisdom wholesome and without an object, is there no adverting towards it… aspiration? It should not be said so….

846. Na vattabbaṃ – “nibbānadhātu kusalā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu nibbānadhātu anavajjāti? Āmantā. Hañci nibbānadhātu anavajjā, tena vata re vattabbe – “nibbānadhātu kusalā”ti.

846. Should it not be said: “The Nibbāna-element is wholesome”? Yes. Is not the Nibbāna-element blameless? Yes. If the Nibbāna-element is blameless, then indeed it should be said: “The Nibbāna-element is wholesome.”

Kusalakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Wholesome is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Chapter

(192) 7. Accantaniyāmakathā

19. (192) 7. Discussion on Absolute Certainty

847. Atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatāti? Āmantā. Mātughātako accantaniyato, pitughātako…pe… arahantaghātako…pe… ruhiruppādako [T 0.0619]…pe… saṅghabhedako accantaniyatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there absolute certainty for a worldling? Yes. Is a matricide absolutely certain, a patricide... an Arahant-killer... one who sheds the blood of a Buddha... a schismatic absolutely certain? It should not be said so...

848. Atthi [M 0.0424] puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatāti? Āmantā. Accantaniyatassa puggalassa vicikicchā uppajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci accantaniyatassa puggalassa vicikicchā uppajjeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatā”ti.

847. Is there absolute certainty for a worldling? Yes. Could doubt arise for a person who is absolutely certain? Yes. If doubt could arise for a person who is absolutely certain, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is absolute certainty for a worldling.’

Accantaniyatassa puggalassa vicikicchā nuppajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Pahīnāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pahīnāti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggenāti? Na [P 0.0587] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmimaggena [V 0.0473] …pe… anāgāmimaggena…pe… arahattamaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

848. Could doubt not arise for a person who is absolutely certain? Yes. Is it abandoned? It should not be said so... Is it abandoned? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? It should not be said so... by the path of once-returning... by the path of non-returning... by the path of Arahantship? It should not be said so...

Katamena maggenāti? Akusalena maggenāti. Akusalo maggo niyyāniko khayagāmī bodhagāmī anāsavo…pe… asaṃkilesikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu akusalo maggo aniyyāniko…pe… saṃkilesikoti? Āmantā. Hañci akusalo maggo aniyyāniko…pe… saṃkilesiko, no ca vata re vattabbe – “accantaniyatassa puggalassa vicikicchā akusalena maggena pahīnā”ti.

By what path? By an unwholesome path. Is an unwholesome path a means of deliverance, leading to destruction, leading to enlightenment, untainted... undefiling? It should not be said so... Is not an unwholesome path not a means of deliverance... defiling? Yes. If an unwholesome path is not a means of deliverance... defiling, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘For a person who is absolutely certain, doubt is abandoned by an unwholesome path.’

849. Sassatadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa ucchedadiṭṭhi uppajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci sassatadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa ucchedadiṭṭhi uppajjeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatā”ti.

Could the annihilationist view arise for a person fixed in the eternalist view? Yes. If the annihilationist view were to arise for a person fixed in the eternalist view, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is absolute certainty for a worldling.’

Sassatadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa ucchedadiṭṭhi nuppajjeyyāti[T 0.0620]? Āmantā. Pahīnāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pahīnāti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sakadāgāmimaggena…pe… anāgāmimaggena…pe… arahattamaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

849. Could the annihilationist view not arise for a person fixed in the eternalist view? Yes. Is it abandoned? It should not be said so... Is it abandoned? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? It should not be said so... by the path of once-returning... by the path of non-returning... by the path of Arahantship? It should not be said so...

Katamena maggenāti? Akusalena maggena. Akusalo maggo…pe… no ca vata re [P 0.0588] vattabbe – “sassatadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa ucchedadiṭṭhi akusalena maggena pahīnā”ti.

By what path? By an unwholesome path. Is an unwholesome path... then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘For a person fixed in the eternalist view, the annihilationist view is abandoned by an unwholesome path.’

850. Ucchedadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa sassatadiṭṭhi uppajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci ucchedadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa sassatadiṭṭhi uppajjeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatā”ti.

Could the eternalist view arise for a person fixed in the annihilationist view? Yes. If the eternalist view were to arise for a person fixed in the annihilationist view, then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘There is absolute certainty for a worldling.’

Ucchedadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa sassatadiṭṭhi nuppajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Pahīnāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pahīnāti? Āmantā. Sotāpattimaggenāti[M 0.0425]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0474] …pe… sakadāgāmimaggena…pe… anāgāmimaggena…pe… arahattamaggenāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

850. Could the eternalist view not arise for a person fixed in the annihilationist view? Yes. Is it abandoned? It should not be said so... Is it abandoned? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? It should not be said so... by the path of once-returning... by the path of non-returning... by the path of Arahantship? It should not be said so...

Katamena maggenāti? Akusalena maggenāti. Akusalo maggo…pe… no ca vata re vattabbe – “ucchedadiṭṭhiyā niyatassa puggalassa sassatadiṭṭhi akusalena maggena pahīnā”ti.

By what path? By an unwholesome path. Is an unwholesome path... then, good sir, it should not be said: ‘For a person fixed in the annihilationist view, the eternalist view is abandoned by an unwholesome path.’

851. Na vattabbaṃ – “atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatā”ti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo samannāgato hoti ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi, so evaṃ kho bhikkhave puggalo (a. ni. 7.15) sakiṃ nimuggo [T 0.0621] nimuggova hotī”ti a. ni. 7.15! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena [P 0.0589] hi atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatāti.

Should it not be said: ‘There is absolute certainty for a worldling’? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, monks, a certain person is endowed with entirely black, unwholesome states; once submerged, he remains submerged’? Is there indeed such a Suttanta? Yes. In that case, there is absolute certainty for a worldling.

852. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo samannāgato hoti ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi, so sakiṃ nimuggo nimuggova hotī”ti katvā tena ca kāraṇena atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatāti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā nimujjatī”ti a. ni. 7.15! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Sabbakālaṃ ummujjitvā nimujjatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

851. Because it was said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, monks, a certain person is endowed with entirely black, unwholesome states; once submerged, he remains submerged,’ and for that reason, is there absolute certainty for a worldling? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, monks, a certain person, having emerged, submerges’? Is there indeed such a Suttanta? Yes. Does he, having emerged, submerge at all times? It should not be said so...

Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo samannāgato hoti ekantakāḷakehi akusalehi dhammehi, so sakiṃ nimuggo nimuggova hotī”ti – katvā tena ca kāraṇena atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatāti? Āmantā. Vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ummujjitvā ṭhito hoti, ummujjitvā vipassati viloketi, ummujjitvā patarati, ummujjitvā patigādhappatto hotī”ti a. ni. 7.15! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Sabbakālaṃ ummujjitvā patigādhappatto hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Since it was said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, monks, a certain person is endowed with entirely black, unwholesome states; once submerged, he remains submerged,’ is it for that reason that there is absolute certainty for a worldling? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Here, monks, a certain person, having emerged, stands firm; having emerged, he looks around and observes; having emerged, he crosses over; having emerged, he has reached a firm footing’? Is there indeed such a Suttanta? Yes. Does he, having emerged, reach a firm footing at all times? It should not be said so…

Accantaniyāmakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Absolute Certainty is concluded.

19. Ekūnavīsatimavaggo

19. The Nineteenth Section

(193) 8. Indriyakathā

(193) 8. The Discussion on the Faculties

853. Natthi [T 0.0622][M 0.0426][V 0.0475] lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Natthi lokiyā saddhāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi lokiyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ…pe… samādhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyanti? Āmantā[P 0.0590]. Natthi lokiyā paññāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

853. Is there no mundane faculty of faith? Yes. Is there no mundane faith? It should not be said so… Is there no mundane faculty of energy… no faculty of mindfulness… no faculty of concentration… no faculty of wisdom? Yes. Is there no mundane wisdom? It should not be said so…

Atthi lokiyā saddhāti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyaṃ vīriyaṃ…pe… sati…pe… samādhi…pe… paññāti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there mundane faith? Yes. Is there a mundane faculty of faith? It should not be said so… Is there mundane energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom? Yes. Is there a mundane faculty of wisdom? It should not be said so…

Atthi lokiyo mano, atthi lokiyaṃ manindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā saddhā, atthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyo mano, atthi lokiyaṃ manindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā paññā, atthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there a mundane mind, and is there a mundane mind-faculty? Yes. Is there mundane faith, and is there a mundane faculty of faith? It should not be said so… Is there a mundane mind, and is there a mundane mind-faculty? Yes. Is there mundane wisdom, and is there a mundane faculty of wisdom? It should not be said so…

Atthi lokiyaṃ somanassaṃ, atthi lokiyaṃ somanassindriyaṃ…pe… atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitaṃ, atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā saddhā, atthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitaṃ, atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā paññā, atthi lokiyaṃ [T 0.0623] paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there mundane gladness, and is there a mundane faculty of gladness… Is there mundane life, and is there a mundane life-faculty? Yes. Is there mundane faith, and is there a mundane faculty of faith? It should not be said so… Is there mundane life, and is there a mundane life-faculty? Yes. Is there mundane wisdom, and is there a mundane faculty of wisdom? It should not be said so…

854. Atthi lokiyā saddhā, natthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyo mano, natthi lokiyaṃ manindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyā paññā, natthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyo mano, natthi lokiyaṃ manindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

854. There is mundane faith, but is there no mundane faculty of faith? Yes. There is a mundane mind, but is there no mundane mind-faculty? It should not be said so… There is mundane wisdom, but is there no mundane faculty of wisdom? Yes. There is a mundane mind, but is there no mundane mind-faculty? It should not be said so…

Atthi [V 0.0476] lokiyā saddhā, natthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Āmantā[P 0.0591]. Atthi lokiyaṃ somanassaṃ, natthi lokiyaṃ somanassindriyanti… atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitaṃ, natthi lokiyaṃ jīvitindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyā paññā, natthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyo mano, natthi lokiyaṃ manindriyanti…pe… atthi lokiyaṃ jīvitaṃ, natthi lokiyaṃ jīvitindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

There is mundane faith, but is there no mundane faculty of faith? Yes. There is mundane gladness, but is there no mundane faculty of gladness… There is mundane life, but is there no mundane life-faculty? It should not be said so… There is mundane wisdom, but is there no mundane faculty of wisdom? Yes. There is a mundane mind, but is there no mundane mind-faculty… There is mundane life, but is there no mundane life-faculty? It should not be said so…

855. Atthi [M 0.0427] lokuttarā saddhā, atthi lokuttaraṃ saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā saddhā, atthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokuttaraṃ vīriyaṃ…pe… atthi lokuttarā paññā, atthi lokuttaraṃ paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokiyā paññā, atthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

855. Is there supramundane faith, and is there a supramundane faculty of faith? Yes. Is there mundane faith, and is there a mundane faculty of faith? It should not be said so… Is there supramundane energy… Is there supramundane wisdom, and is there a supramundane faculty of wisdom? Yes. Is there mundane wisdom, and is there a mundane faculty of wisdom? It should not be said so…

Atthi lokiyā saddhā, natthi lokiyaṃ saddhindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokuttarā saddhā, natthi lokuttaraṃ saddhindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi lokiyaṃ vīriyaṃ…pe… atthi [T 0.0624] lokiyā paññā, natthi lokiyaṃ paññindriyanti? Āmantā. Atthi lokuttarā paññā, natthi lokuttaraṃ paññindriyanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

There is mundane faith, but is there no mundane faculty of faith? Yes. There is supramundane faith, but is there no supramundane faculty of faith? It should not be said so… There is mundane energy… There is mundane wisdom, but is there no mundane faculty of wisdom? Yes. There is supramundane wisdom, but is there no supramundane faculty of wisdom? It should not be said so…

856. Natthi lokiyāni pañcindriyānīti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe, tikkhindriye mudindriye, svākāre, suviññāpaye[P 0.0592], appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvino viharante”ti ma. ni. 1.283 tattha “dvākāre duviññāpaye” iccādīnipi padāni dissanti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi lokiyāni pañcindriyānīti.

856. Are there no mundane five faculties? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: “Monks, with the Buddha-eye, surveying the world, I saw beings with little dust, with much dust, with keen faculties, with dull faculties, of good disposition, easy to instruct, and some dwelling seeing danger and blame in the other world”? Is there indeed such a sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, there are the mundane five faculties.

Indriyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Faculties is concluded.

Ekūnavīsatimavaggo.

The Nineteenth Section.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Atīte kilese jahati anāgate kilese jahati paccuppanne kilese jahati, suññatā saṅkhārakkhandhapariyāpannā, sāmaññaphalaṃ asaṅkhataṃ, patti asaṅkhatā, sabbadhammānaṃ tathatā asaṅkhatā, nibbānadhātu [V 0.0477] kusalā, atthi puthujjanassa accantaniyāmatā, natthi lokiyāni pañcindriyānīti.

One abandons defilements in the past, one abandons defilements in the future, one abandons defilements in the present; emptiness is included in the aggregate of formations; the fruit of recluseship is unconditioned; attainment is unconditioned; the suchness of all phenomena is unconditioned; the Nibbāna-element is wholesome; there is absolute certainty for the worldling; there are no mundane five faculties.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(194) 1. Asañciccakathā

(194) 1. The Discussion on Unintentionality

857. Asañcicca [T 0.0625][P 0.0593] mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotīti? Āmantā. Asañcicca pāṇaṃ hantvā pāṇātipātī hotīti? Na hevaṃ [M 0.0428] vattabbe…pe… asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotīti? Āmantā. Asañcicca adinnaṃ ādiyitvā…pe… musā bhaṇitvā musāvādī hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

857. Does one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life become liable to an act with immediate retribution? Yes. Does one who unintentionally kills a living being become a taker of life? It should not be said so... Does one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life become liable to an act with immediate retribution? Yes. Does one who unintentionally takes what is not given... speaks falsely become a speaker of falsehood? It should not be said so...

Asañcicca pāṇaṃ hantvā pāṇātipātī na hotīti? Āmantā. Asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko na hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… asañcicca adinnaṃ ādiyitvā…pe… musā bhaṇitvā musāvādī na hotīti? Āmantā. Asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko na hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does one who unintentionally kills a living being not become a taker of life? Yes. Does one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life not become liable to an act with immediate retribution? It should not be said so... Does one who unintentionally takes what is not given... speaks falsely not become a speaker of falsehood? Yes. Does one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life not become liable to an act with immediate retribution? It should not be said so....

858. Asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotīti? Āmantā. “Asañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. “Sañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Āmantā.
