Hañci “sañcicca mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotī”ti – attheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “asañcicca mātaraṃ [T 0.0626] jīvitā voropetvā ānantariko hotī”ti.

858. Does one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life become liable to an act with immediate retribution? Yes. Is there a Sutta passage that says, 'One who unintentionally deprives his mother of life becomes liable to an act with immediate retribution'? There is not. Is there a Sutta passage that says, 'One who intentionally deprives his mother of life becomes liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. If there is a Sutta passage that says, 'One who intentionally deprives his mother of life becomes liable to an act with immediate retribution,' then, good sir, it should certainly not be said that 'one who unintentionally deprives his mother of life becomes liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

859. Na vattabbaṃ – “mātughātako ānantariko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu mātā jīvitā voropitāti? Āmantā. Hañci mātā jīvitā voropitā, tena vata re vattabbe – “mātughātako ānantariko”ti.

859. Should it not be said, 'A matricide is liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. Was the mother not deprived of life? Yes. If the mother was deprived of life, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'A matricide is liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

Na [V 0.0478] vattabbaṃ – “pitughātako ānantariko”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0594]. Nanu pitā jīvitā voropitoti? Āmantā. Hañci pitā jīvitā voropito, tena vata re vattabbe – “pitughātako ānantariko”ti.

Should it not be said, 'A patricide is liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. Was the father not deprived of life? Yes. If the father was deprived of life, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'A patricide is liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “arahantaghātako ānantariko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā jīvitā voropitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā jīvitā voropito, tena vata re vattabbe – “arahantaghātako ānantariko”ti.

Should it not be said, 'One who kills an arahant is liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. Was an arahant not deprived of life? Yes. If an arahant was deprived of life, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'One who kills an arahant is liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

Na vattabbaṃ – “ruhiruppādako ānantariko”ti? Āmantā. Nanu tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditanti? Āmantā. Hañci tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppāditaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “ruhiruppādako ānantariko”ti.

Should it not be said, 'One who sheds the blood of a Tathāgata is liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. Was blood not drawn from the Tathāgata? Yes. If blood was drawn from the Tathāgata, then for that reason, good sir, it should indeed be said, 'One who sheds the blood of a Tathāgata is liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

860. Saṅghabhedako [M 0.0429] ānantarikoti? Āmantā. Sabbe saṅghabhedakā ānantarikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sabbe saṅghabhedakā ānantarikāti? Āmantā. Dhammasaññī saṅghabhedako ānantarikoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

860. Is one who creates a schism in the Saṅgha liable to an act with immediate retribution? Yes. Are all who create schisms in the Saṅgha liable to acts with immediate retribution? It should not be said so... Are all who create schisms in the Saṅgha liable to acts with immediate retribution? Yes. Is one who creates a schism in the Saṅgha, perceiving it as Dhamma, liable to an act with immediate retribution? It should not be said so....

861. Dhammasaññī saṅghabhedako ānantarikoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “atthupāli, saṅghabhedako āpāyiko nerayiko kappaṭṭho atekiccho; atthupāli, saṅghabhedako na āpāyiko na nerayiko na kappaṭṭho na atekiccho”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā[T 0.0627]. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “dhammasaññī saṅghabhedako ānantariko”ti.

861. Is a schism-maker who perceives it as Dhamma liable to an act with immediate retribution? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Upāli, there is a schism-maker who is destined for the plane of misery, destined for hell, remaining for the aeon, incurable; and Upāli, there is a schism-maker who is not destined for the plane of misery, not destined for hell, not remaining for the aeon, curable'? Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said, 'A schism-maker who perceives it as Dhamma is liable to an act with immediate retribution.'

862. Na vattabbaṃ – “dhammasaññī saṅghabhedako ānantariko”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0595]. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

862. Should it not be said, 'A schismatic who perceives it as Dhamma is liable to an act with immediate retribution'? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Āpāyiko nerayiko, kappaṭṭho saṅghabhedako;

Vaggarato adhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā padhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ bhetvāna, kappaṃ nirayamhi paccatī”ti cūḷava. 354; a. ni. 10.39; itivu. 18.

Liable to the woeful state, hell-bound, standing firm for an aeon, a Saṅgha-splitter, delighting in factions, standing for unrighteousness, he ruins security from bondage; having split the harmonious Saṅgha, he is roasted in hell for an aeon.

Attheva [V 0.0479] suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi saṅghabhedako ānantarikoti.

Is there such a Sutta passage? Yes. Therefore, a schism-maker is liable to an act with immediate retribution.

Asañciccakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Unintentionality is concluded.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(195) 2. Ñāṇakathā

(195) 2. Discourse on Knowledge

863. Natthi puthujjanassa ñāṇanti? Āmantā. Natthi puthujjanassa paññā pajānanā vicayo pavicayo dhammavicayo sallakkhaṇā upalakkhaṇā paccupalakkhaṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atthi puthujjanassa paññā pajānanā vicayo…pe… paccupalakkhaṇāti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi puthujjanassa paññā pajānanā vicayo…pe… paccupalakkhaṇā, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi puthujjanassa ñāṇa”nti.

20. Does an ordinary person lack knowledge? Yes. Does an ordinary person lack wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, consideration, reflection, and close reflection? It should not be said thus… But does an ordinary person not possess wisdom, understanding, investigation… and close reflection? Yes. If an ordinary person possesses wisdom, understanding, investigation… and close reflection, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said: 'An ordinary person lacks knowledge.'

864. Natthi [M 0.0430] puthujjanassa ñāṇanti? Āmantā. Puthujjano paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci puthujjano paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “natthi puthujjanassa ñāṇa”nti.

Does an ordinary person lack knowledge? Yes. Might an ordinary person attain the first jhāna? Yes. If an ordinary person might attain the first jhāna, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said: 'An ordinary person lacks knowledge.'

Puthujjano [T 0.0628] dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajjeyya, viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjeyya, puthujjano dānaṃ dadeyya [P 0.0596]…pe… cīvaraṃ dadeyya, piṇḍapātaṃ dadeyya, senāsanaṃ dadeyya, gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci puthujjano gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – natthi puthujjanassa ñāṇa”nti.

863. Might an ordinary person attain the second jhāna… the third jhāna… the fourth jhāna… the base of the infinity of space, the base of the infinity of consciousness, the base of nothingness, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? Might an ordinary person give a gift… give robes, give almsfood, give lodging, give medicinal requisites for the sick? Yes. If an ordinary person might give medicinal requisites for the sick, then, good sir, it should certainly not be said: 'An ordinary person lacks knowledge.'

865. Atthi puthujjanassa ñāṇanti? Āmantā. Puthujjano tena ñāṇena dukkhaṃ parijānāti[V 0.0480], samudayaṃ pajahati, nirodhaṃ sacchikaroti, maggaṃ bhāvetīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

864. Does an ordinary person possess knowledge? Yes. Does an ordinary person, with that knowledge, fully comprehend suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path? It should not be said thus…

Ñāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Knowledge is concluded.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(196) 3. Nirayapālakathā

(196) 3. Discourse on Hell-Wardens

866. Natthi nirayesu nirayapālāti? Āmantā. Natthi nirayesu kammakāraṇāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi nirayesu kammakāraṇāti? Āmantā. Atthi nirayesu nirayapālāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

865. Are there no hell-wardens in the hells? Yes. Are there no causes of torment in the hells? It should not be said thus… Are there causes of torment in the hells? Yes. Are there hell-wardens in the hells? It should not be said thus…

Atthi manussesu kammakāraṇā, atthi ca kāraṇikāti? Āmantā. Atthi nirayesu kammakāraṇā, atthi ca kāraṇikāti? Na [T 0.0629] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi nirayesu kammakāraṇā, natthi ca kāraṇikāti? Āmantā. Atthi manussesu kammakāraṇā, natthi ca kāraṇikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Among humans, are there causes of torment, and also punishers? Yes. In the hells, are there causes of torment, and also punishers? It should not be said thus… In the hells, are there causes of torment, but no punishers? Yes. Among humans, are there causes of torment, but no punishers? It should not be said thus…

867. Atthi nirayesu nirayapālāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

20. Are there hell-wardens in the hells? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:

“Na [M 0.0431][P 0.0597] vessabhū nopi ca pettirājā,

Somo yamo vessavaṇo ca rājā;

Sakāni kammāni hananti tattha, ito paṇunnaṃ paṇuṇṇaṃ (syā. ka.), panunnaṃ (sī.) paralokapatta”nti.

“Neither Vessabhū, nor the king of the petas, nor Soma, nor Yama, nor King Vessavaṇa torments one who, driven from here, has reached the next world; their own deeds torment them there.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi natthi nirayesu nirayapālāti.

Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, there are no hell-wardens in the hells.

868. Natthi nirayesu nirayapālāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tamenaṃ, bhikkhave[V 0.0481], nirayapālā pañcavidhabandhanaṃ nāma kāraṇaṃ kārenti karonti (ma. ni. 3.250; a. ni. 3.36) – tattaṃ ayokhīlaṃ hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhīlaṃ dutiye hatthe gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhīlaṃ pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhīlaṃ dutiye pāde gamenti, tattaṃ ayokhīlaṃ majjheurasmiṃ gamenti; so tattha dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vedeti; na ca tāva kālaṃ karoti yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhotī”ti ma. ni. 3.250; a. ni. 3.36! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi nirayesu nirayapālāti.

868. Are there no hell-wardens in the hells? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, the hell-wardens inflict upon him a punishment called the fivefold bond—they drive a red-hot iron stake into one hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake into the other hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake into one foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake into the other foot, and they drive a red-hot iron stake into the middle of his chest. There he experiences painful, sharp, and bitter feelings; and he does not die so long as that evil deed is not exhausted’? Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, there are hell-wardens in the hells.

Natthi nirayesu nirayapālāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā saṃvesetvā kuṭhārīhi kudhārīhi (sabbattha) tacchanti…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhampādaṃ adhosiraṃ ṭhapetvā vāsīhi tacchanti…pe… tamenaṃ[T 0.0630], bhikkhave, nirayapālā rathe yojetvā ādittāya pathaviyā sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya sañjotibhūtāya (syā.) sārentipi paccāsārentipi…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā mahantaṃ aṅgārapabbataṃ ādittaṃ sampajjalitaṃ sajotibhūtaṃ [P 0.0598] āropentipi oropentipi…pe… tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā uddhampādaṃ adhosiraṃ gahetvā tattāya lohakumbhiyā pakkhipanti ādittāya sampajjalitāya sajotibhūtāya. So tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccati, so tattha pheṇuddehakaṃ paccamāno sakimpi uddhaṃ gacchati, sakimpi adho gacchati, sakimpi tiriyaṃ gacchati. So tattha dukkhā tibbā kaṭukā vedanā vedayati, na ca tāva kālaṃ karoti yāva na [M 0.0432] taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantīhoti. Tamenaṃ, bhikkhave, nirayapālā mahāniraye pakkhipanti! So kho pana, bhikkhave, mahānirayo –

Are there no hell-wardens in the hells? Yes. But has it not been said by the Blessed One: “Then, monks, the hell-wardens, having made him lie down, chop him with axes… Then, monks, the hell-wardens, having placed him feet up and head down, chop him with adzes… Then, monks, the hell-wardens harness him to a chariot and drive him back and forth across the burning ground, which is ablaze, aflame, and radiant… Then, monks, the hell-wardens make him ascend and descend a great mountain of burning coals, which is ablaze, aflame, and radiant… Then, monks, the hell-wardens, taking him feet up and head down, throw him into a hot metal cauldron, which is ablaze, aflame, and radiant. There he is cooked, boiling up with foam, and as he is cooked, boiling up with foam, he goes sometimes up, sometimes down, sometimes across. He experiences painful, sharp, and bitter feelings, yet he does not die so long as that evil deed is not exhausted. Then, monks, the hell-wardens throw him into the Great Hell! And that Great Hell, monks—

“Catukkaṇṇo catudvāro, vibhatto bhāgaso mito;

Ayopākārapariyanto, ayasā paṭikujjito.

“It has four corners and four doors, is divided into portions and measured; it is surrounded by an iron wall and covered with an iron roof.

“Tassa ayomayā bhūmi, jalitā tejasā yutā;

Samantā yojanasataṃ, pharitvā tiṭṭhati sabbadā”ti ma. ni. 3.250; a. ni. 3.36; pe. va. 71.

“Its iron ground is blazing and fiery; extending a hundred yojanas all around, it stands so always.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi nirayesu nirayapālāti.

Is there indeed such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, there are hell-wardens in the hells.

Nirayapālakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Hell-Wardens is concluded.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(197) 4. Tiracchānakathā

(197) 4. Discourse on Animals

869. Atthi [T 0.0631][V 0.0482] devesu tiracchānagatāti? Āmantā. Atthi tiracchānagatesu devāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi devesu tiracchānagatāti? Āmantā[P 0.0599]. Devaloko tiracchānayonīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi devesu tiracchānagatāti? Āmantā. Atthi tattha kīṭā paṭaṅgā makasā makkhikā ahī vicchikā satapadī gaṇḍuppādāti gaṇḍupādāti (syā. kaṃ. pī.)? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

20. Are there animals among the devas? Yes. Are there devas among the animals? It should not be said thus… (etc.) Are there animals among the devas? Yes. Is the realm of devas an animal realm? It should not be said thus… (etc.) Are there animals among the devas? Yes. Are there insects, moths, mosquitoes, flies, snakes, scorpions, centipedes, and earthworms there? It should not be said thus… (etc.)

870. Natthi devesu tiracchānagatāti? Āmantā. Nanu atthi tattha erāvaṇo nāma hatthināgo sahassayuttaṃ dibbaṃ yānanti? Āmantā. Hañci atthi tattha erāvaṇo nāma hatthināgo sahassayuttaṃ dibbaṃ yānaṃ, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi devesu tiracchānagatā”ti.

Are there no animals among the devas? Yes. But is there not a great elephant named Erāvaṇa, a divine vehicle yoked to a thousand, there? Yes. If there is indeed a great elephant named Erāvaṇa, a divine vehicle yoked to a thousand, there, then surely it must be said: ‘There are animals among the devas.’

871. Atthi devesu tiracchānagatāti? Āmantā. Atthi tattha hatthibandhā assabandhā hatthibhaṇḍā assabhaṇḍā (?) yāvasikā kāraṇikā bhattakārakāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi natthi devesu tiracchānagatāti.

869. Are there animals among the devas? Yes. Are there elephant keepers, horse keepers, grooms, elephant trainers, and cooks there? It should not be said thus. Therefore, there are no animals among the devas.

Tiracchānakathā niṭṭhitā.

870. The Discussion on Animals is concluded.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(198) 5. Maggakathā

(198) 5. Discourse on the Path

872. Pañcaṅgiko [T 0.0632][M 0.0433] maggoti? Āmantā. Nanu aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vutto bhagavatā, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhīti? Āmantā. Hañci aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo vutto bhagavatā[V 0.0483], seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi [P 0.0600] …pe… sammāsamādhi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “pañcaṅgiko maggo”ti.

871. Is the path five-factored? Yes. But was the path not declared by the Blessed One as eight-factored, namely: right view... up to right concentration? Yes. If the path was declared by the Blessed One as eight-factored, namely: right view... up to right concentration, then it should not be said: "the path is five-factored."

Pañcaṅgiko maggoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

Is the path five-factored? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One –

“Maggānaṃ aṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṃ caturo padā;

Virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṃ, dvipadānañca cakkhumā”ti dha. pa. 273 dhammapade.

20. “Of paths, the Eightfold is best; of truths, the four statements; dispassion is the best of states; and of the two-footed, the One with Vision.”

Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi aṭṭhaṅgiko maggoti.

Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the path is eight-factored.

873. Sammāvācā maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca na maggoti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca na maggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammāvācā maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca na maggoti? Āmantā. Sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo…pe… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi maggaṅgaṃ, so ca na maggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

872. Is it the case that Right Speech is a path-factor, but it is not the path? Yes. Is it the case that Right View is a path-factor, but it is not the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.) Is it the case that Right Speech is a path-factor, but it is not the path? Yes. Is it the case that Right Intention… (etc.) Right Effort… (etc.) Right Mindfulness… (etc.) Right Concentration is a path-factor, but it is not the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.)

Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ, so ca na maggoti? Āmantā. Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi maggaṅgaṃ, so ca na maggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is it the case that Right Action… (etc.) Right Livelihood is a path-factor, but it is not the path? Yes. Is it the case that Right View… (etc.) Right Concentration is a path-factor, but it is not the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.)

Sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca maggoti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā [T 0.0633] maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca maggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammādiṭṭhi maggaṅgaṃ, sā ca maggoti? Āmantā. Sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ, so ca maggoti? Na [P 0.0601] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Right View is a path-factor, and is it also the path? Yes. Right Speech is a path-factor, and is it also the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.) Right View is a path-factor, and is it also the path? Yes. Right Action… (etc.) Right Livelihood is a path-factor, and is it also the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.)

Sammāsaṅkappo…pe… sammāvāyāmo…pe… sammāsati…pe… sammāsamādhi maggaṅgaṃ, so ca maggoti? Āmantā. Sammāvācā…pe… sammākammanto…pe… sammāājīvo maggaṅgaṃ, so ca maggoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Right Intention… (etc.) Right Effort… (etc.) Right Mindfulness… (etc.) Right Concentration is a path-factor, and is it also the path? Yes. Right Speech… (etc.) Right Action… (etc.) Right Livelihood is a path-factor, and is it also the path? It should not be said thus… (etc.)

874. Ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hoti; evamassāyaṃ [M 0.0434] ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo [V 0.0484] bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti ma. ni. 3.431! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi pañcaṅgiko maggoti.

874. Is the Noble Path eightfold? Yes. Has it not been said by the Blessed One: ‘Indeed, his bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood are already well purified; thus this Noble Eightfold Path of his goes to the perfection of development’? Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the path is fivefold.

875. Pañcaṅgiko maggoti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo na upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati, tatiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati, catutthopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Yasmiñca kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha upalabbhati, dutiyopi…pe… tatiyopi…pe… catutthopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati. Imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati. Idheva, subhadda[T 0.0634], samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehī”ti dī. ni. 2.214! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi aṭṭhaṅgiko maggoti.

875. Is the path fivefold? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Subhadda, in whatever teaching and discipline the Noble Eightfold Path is not found, no ascetic is found there, no second ascetic is found there, no third ascetic is found there, no fourth ascetic is found there. And in whatever teaching and discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found, an ascetic is found there, a second ascetic… and so on… a third ascetic… and so on… a fourth ascetic is found there. In this teaching and discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found. Here, Subhadda, is an ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, here a fourth ascetic. Other doctrines are empty of ascetics.’ Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the path is eightfold.

Maggakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Path is concluded.

20. Vīsatimavaggo

20. The Twentieth Section

(199) 6. Ñāṇakathā

(199) 6. Discourse on Knowledge

876. Dvādasavatthukaṃ [P 0.0602] ñāṇaṃ lokuttaranti? Āmantā. Dvādasa lokuttarañāṇānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasa lokuttarañāṇānīti? Āmantā. Dvādasa sotāpattimaggāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasa sotāpattimaggāti? Āmantā. Dvādasa sotāpattiphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasa sakadāgāmimaggā…pe… anāgāmimaggā…pe… arahattamaggāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… dvādasa arahattamaggāti? Āmantā. Dvādasa arahattaphalānīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

20. Is the knowledge with twelve bases supramundane? Yes. Are there twelve supramundane knowledges? It should not be said thus… and so on… Are there twelve supramundane knowledges? Yes. Are there twelve paths of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… and so on… Are there twelve paths of stream-entry? Yes. Are there twelve fruits of stream-entry? It should not be said thus… and so on… twelve paths of a once-returner… and so on… paths of a non-returner… and so on… paths of an arahant? It should not be said thus… and so on… Are there twelve paths of an arahant? Yes. Are there twelve fruits of an arahant? It should not be said thus… and so on.

877. Na vattabbaṃ – “dvādasavatthukaṃ ñāṇaṃ lokuttara”nti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā [V 0.0485] – “idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasacca”nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu [M 0.0435] cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyya’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… pariññātanti [T 0.0635] me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘idaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā. kaṃ. pī.) ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahātabba’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… pahīnanti me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘idaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodhā (syā. kaṃ. pī.) ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikātabba’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… sacchikatanti me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘idaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave…pe… ‘taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvetabba’nti [P 0.0603] me, bhikkhave…pe… bhāvitanti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi…pe… āloko udapādī”ti mahāva. 15; saṃ. ni. 5.1081; paṭi. ma. 2.30! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi dvādasavatthukaṃ ñāṇaṃ lokuttaranti.

Should it not be said that ‘the knowledge with twelve bases is supramundane’? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘“This is the Noble Truth of Suffering”—concerning this, monks, regarding things unheard before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose. “This Noble Truth of Suffering is to be fully understood”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “it has been fully understood”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering is to be abandoned”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “it has been abandoned”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is to be realized”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “it has been realized”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This is the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “This Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering is to be developed”—concerning this, monks… and so on… “it has been developed”—concerning this, monks, regarding things unheard before, vision arose in me… and so on… light arose.’ Is there such a discourse? Yes. Therefore, the knowledge with twelve bases is supramundane.

Ñāṇakathā niṭṭhitā.

876. The Discourse on Knowledge is concluded.

Vīsatimavaggo.

877. The Twentieth Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Mātughātako ānantariko pitughātako ānantariko arahantaghātako ānantariko ruhiruppādako ānantariko saṅghabhedako ānantariko, natthi puthujjanassa ñāṇaṃ, natthi nirayesu nirayapālā, atthi devesu tiracchānagatā, pañcaṅgiko maggo, dvādasavatthukaṃ ñāṇaṃ lokuttaranti.

The matricide commits an act with immediate result; the patricide commits an act with immediate result; the killer of an arahant commits an act with immediate result; the one who sheds a Buddha's blood commits an act with immediate result; the creator of a schism in the Saṅgha commits an act with immediate result; there is no knowledge for a worldling; there are no wardens in the hells; there are animal births among the devas; the path is fivefold; the knowledge with twelve bases is supramundane.

Catuttho paṇṇāsako.

The Fourth Fifty.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Niggaho, puññasañcayo, aṭṭhāsi, atītena ca mātughātako.

The discourse on restraint, the discourse on accumulation of merit, the discourse on 'He stood', and the discourse on 'A matricide in the past'—these are seven.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

The Twenty-First Chapter.

(200) 1. Sāsanakathā

(200) 1. Discourse on the Dispensation

878. Sāsanaṃ [T 0.0636][M 0.0436][P 0.0604][V 0.0486] navaṃ katanti? Āmantā. Satipaṭṭhānā navaṃ katāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sāsanaṃ navaṃ katanti? Āmantā. Sammappadhānā…pe… iddhipādā…pe… indriyā…pe… balā…pe… bojjhaṅgā navaṃ katāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pubbe akusalaṃ pacchā kusalaṃ katanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… pubbe sāsavaṃ…pe… saṃyojaniyaṃ ganthaniyaṃ oghaniyaṃ yoganiyaṃ nīvaraṇiyaṃ parāmaṭṭhaṃ upādāniyaṃ…pe… saṃkilesikaṃ pacchā asaṃkilesikaṃ katanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is the Dispensation newly made? Yes. Are the establishments of mindfulness newly made? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the Dispensation newly made? Yes. Are the right strivings… the bases of spiritual power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of enlightenment newly made? It should not be said thus… and so on… Was what was formerly unwholesome subsequently made wholesome? It should not be said thus… and so on… Was what was formerly with taints… conducive to fetters, to bonds, to floods, to yokes, to hindrances, subject to grasping, a basis for clinging… conducive to defilement, subsequently made free from defilement? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Atthi koci tathāgatassa sāsanaṃ navaṃ karotīti? Āmantā. Atthi koci satipaṭṭhāne navaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi koci sammappadhāne…pe… iddhipāde…pe… indriye…pe… bale…pe… bojjhaṅge navaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi koci pubbe akusalaṃ pacchā kusalaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… atthi koci pubbe sāsavaṃ…pe… saṃkilesikaṃ pacchā asaṃkilesiyaṃ karotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there anyone who makes the Tathāgata’s Dispensation new? Yes. Is there anyone who makes the establishments of mindfulness new? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is there anyone who makes the right strivings… the bases of spiritual power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of enlightenment new? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is there anyone who makes what was formerly unwholesome subsequently wholesome? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is there anyone who makes what was formerly with taints… conducive to defilement, subsequently free from defilement? It should not be said thus… and so on.

Labbhā tathāgatassa sāsanaṃ puna navaṃ kātunti? Āmantā. Labbhā satipaṭṭhānā puna navaṃ kātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… labbhā sammappadhānā…pe… iddhipādā…pe… indriyā…pe… balā…pe… bojjhaṅgā [T 0.0637] puna navaṃ kātunti? Na [P 0.0605] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… labbhā pubbe akusalaṃ pacchā kusalaṃ kātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… labbhā pubbe sāsavaṃ…pe… saṃkilesiyaṃ pacchā asaṃkilesiyaṃ kātunti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is it possible for the Tathāgata’s Teaching to be made new again? Yes. Is it possible for the establishments of mindfulness to be made new again? It should not be said thus… Is it possible for the right exertions… the bases of spiritual power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of enlightenment to be made new again? It should not be said thus… Is it possible for what was unwholesome before to be made wholesome afterward? It should not be said thus… Is it possible for what was with taints before… conducive to defilement to be made not conducive to defilement afterward? It should not be said thus…

Sāsanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Teaching is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(201) 2. Avivittakathā

(201) 2. Discourse on Non-Dissociation

879. Puthujjano [V 0.0487] tedhātukehi dhammehi avivittoti? Āmantā. Puthujjano tedhātukehi phassehi…pe… tedhātukāhi vedanāhi… saññāhi [M 0.0437]… cetanāhi… cittehi… saddhāhi… vīriyehi… satīhi… samādhīhi…pe… tedhātukāhi paññāhi avivittoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

879. Is an ordinary person not dissociated from the phenomena of the three realms? Yes. Is an ordinary person not dissociated from the contacts of the three realms… the feelings… perceptions… volitions… consciousnesses… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom of the three realms? This should not be said…

Puthujjano tedhātukehi kammehi avivittoti? Āmantā. Yasmiṃ khaṇe puthujjano cīvaraṃ deti, tasmiṃ khaṇe paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… yasmiṃ khaṇe puthujjano piṇḍapātaṃ deti…pe… senāsanaṃ deti…pe… gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ deti, tasmiṃ khaṇe catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is an ordinary person not dissociated from actions pertaining to the three realms? Yes. When an ordinary person gives a robe, does he, at that moment, attain and abide in the first jhāna… attain and abide in the base of infinite space? This should not be said… When an ordinary person gives almsfood… lodging… medicine and other requisites for the sick, does he, at that moment, attain and abide in the fourth jhāna… attain and abide in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? This should not be said…

880. Na vattabbaṃ – “puthujjano tedhātukehi kammehi avivitto”ti? Āmantā[T 0.0638]. Puthujjanassa rūpadhātuarūpadhātūpagaṃ kammaṃ pariññātanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi puthujjano tedhātukehi kammehi avivittoti…pe….

880. Should it not be said: “An ordinary person is not dissociated from actions in the three realms”? Yes. Has the kamma of an ordinary person that leads to the form realm and the formless realm been fully understood? That should not be said. Therefore, an ordinary person is not dissociated from actions in the three realms…

Avivittakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Non-Dissociation is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(202) 3. Saṃyojanakathā

(202) 3. The Discourse on Fetters

881. Atthi [P 0.0606] kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappattīti? Āmantā. Atthi kiñci sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ appahāya…pe… vicikicchaṃ appahāya…pe… sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ appahāya… rāgaṃ appahāya… dosaṃ appahāya… mohaṃ appahāya… anottappaṃ appahāya arahattappattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

881. Is there the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some fetter? Yes. Is there the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some identity-view… without abandoning doubt… without abandoning adherence to rites and rituals… without abandoning lust… without abandoning hatred… without abandoning delusion… without abandoning lack of moral dread? It should not be said thus…

Atthi [V 0.0488] kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappattīti? Āmantā. Arahā sarāgo sadoso samoho samāno samakkho sapaḷāso saupāyāso sakilesoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu arahā nirāgo niddoso nimmoho nimmāno nimmakkho nippaḷāso nirupāyāso nikkilesoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā nirāgo…pe… nikkileso, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappattī”ti.

“Is there the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some fetter?” “Yes.” “Is an Arahant with lust, with hatred, with delusion, with conceit, with hypocrisy, with spite, with despair, with defilements?” “It should not be said thus… Is it not that an Arahant is without lust, without hatred, without delusion, without conceit, without hypocrisy, without spite, without despair, without defilements?” “Yes.” “If an Arahant is without lust… without defilements, then indeed, oh you, it should not be said: ‘There is the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some fetter’.”

882. Na [M 0.0438] vattabbaṃ – “atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappattī”ti[T 0.0639]? Āmantā. Arahā sabbaṃ buddhavisayaṃ jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappattīti.

882. “Should it not be said: ‘There is the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some fetter’?” “Yes.” “Does an Arahant know the entire domain of a Buddha?” “It should not be said thus.” “Therefore, there is the attainment of Arahantship without abandoning some fetter.”

Saṃyojanakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Fetters is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(203) 4. Iddhikathā

(203) 4. The Discourse on Psychic Power

883. Atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Āmantā. “Niccapaṇṇā [P 0.0607] rukkhā hontū”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… niccapupphā rukkhā hontu…pe… niccaphalikā rukkhā hontu… niccaṃ juṇhaṃ hotu… niccaṃ khemaṃ hotu… niccaṃ subhikkhaṃ hotu… “niccaṃ suvatthi suvuṭṭhikaṃ (syā.) hotū”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

883. Is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? Yes. ‘May trees always have leaves’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus… May trees always have flowers… may they always bear fruit… may there always be moonlight… may there always be safety… may there always be abundant food… ‘may there always be good rain’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus…

Atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Āmantā[T 0.0640]. “Uppanno phasso mā nirujjhī”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? Yes. ‘May arisen contact not cease’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus…

Uppannā [V 0.0489] vedanā…pe… saññā… cetanā… cittaṃ… saddhā… vīriyaṃ… sati… samādhi…pe… paññā mā nirujjhīti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

‘May arisen feeling… perception… volition… consciousness… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom not cease’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus…

Atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Āmantā. “Rūpaṃ niccaṃ hotū”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… “viññāṇaṃ niccaṃ hotū”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? Yes. ‘May form be permanent’—is there the psychic power of resolve… feeling… perception… formations… ‘May consciousness be permanent’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus…

Atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Āmantā. “Jātidhammā sattā mā jāyiṃsū”ti atthi…pe… “jarādhammā sattā mā jīriṃsū”ti…pe… “byādhidhammā sattā mā byādhiyiṃsū”ti…pe… “maraṇadhammā sattā mā mīyiṃsū”ti – atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? Yes. ‘May beings subject to birth not be born’… ‘May beings subject to aging not age’… ‘May beings subject to sickness not fall ill’… ‘May beings subject to death not die’—is there the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples? It should not be said thus…

884. Na [M 0.0439] vattabbaṃ – “atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vā”ti? Āmantā[P 0.0608]. Nanu āyasmā pilindavaccho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa pāsādaṃ “suvaṇṇa”ntveva adhimucci, suvaṇṇo ca pana āsīti pārā. 621; mahāva. 271? Āmantā. Hañci āyasmā pilindavaccho rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa pāsādaṃ suvaṇṇantveva adhimucci, suvaṇṇo ca pana āsi, tena vata re vattabbe – “atthi adhippāyaiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vā”ti.

884. Should it not be said: ‘There is the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples’? Yes. Did not the Venerable Pilindavaccha resolve the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha to be ‘gold,’ and it was indeed gold? Yes. If the Venerable Pilindavaccha resolved the palace of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha to be gold, and it was indeed gold, then surely it should be said: ‘There is the psychic power of resolve for Buddhas or their disciples.’

Iddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Psychic Power is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(204) 5. Buddhakathā

21. (204) 5. Discourse on the Buddha

885. Atthi [T 0.0641] buddhānaṃ buddhehi hīnātirekatāti? Āmantā. Satipaṭṭhānatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [V 0.0490] …pe… sammappadhānato…pe… iddhipādato… indriyato… balato… bojjhaṅgato… vasibhāvato…pe… sabbaññutañāṇadassanatoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

885. Is there inferiority or superiority among Buddhas? Yes. In terms of the foundations of mindfulness? That should not be said… and so on… in terms of the right exertions… and so on… in terms of the bases of spiritual power… in terms of the faculties… in terms of the powers… in terms of the factors of enlightenment… in terms of mastery… and so on… in terms of the knowledge and vision of omniscience? That should not be said… and so on.

Buddhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the Buddha is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(205) 6. Sabbadisākathā

(205) 6. The Discourse on All Directions

886. Sabbā disā buddhā tiṭṭhantīti? Āmantā. Puratthimāya disāya buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… puratthimāya disāya buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Kinnāmo so bhagavā, kiṃjacco, kiṃgotto, kinnāmā tassa [P 0.0609] bhagavato mātāpitaro, kinnāmaṃ tassa bhagavato sāvakayugaṃ, konāmo tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhāko, kīdisaṃ cīvaraṃ dhāreti, kīdisaṃ pattaṃ dhāreti, katarasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā nagare vā raṭṭhe vā janapade vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

886. Do Buddhas stand in all directions? Yes. Does a Buddha stand in the eastern direction? That should not be said… and so on. Does a Buddha stand in the eastern direction? Yes. What is the name of that Blessed One? What is his birth? What is his lineage? What are the names of that Blessed One's parents? What is the name of that Blessed One's pair of disciples? What kind of robe does he wear? What kind of bowl does he carry? In what village, market town, city, district, or region does he live? That should not be said… and so on.

Dakkhiṇāya disāya…pe… pacchimāya disāya…pe… uttarāya disāya…pe… heṭṭhimāya disāya buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… heṭṭhimāya disāya [M 0.0440] buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Kinnāmo so [T 0.0642] bhagavā…pe… janapade vāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

In the southern direction… and so on… in the western direction… and so on… in the northern direction… and so on… Does a Buddha stand in the lower direction? That should not be said… and so on. Does a Buddha stand in the lower direction? Yes. What is the name of that Blessed One… and so on… in what region does he live? That should not be said… and so on.

Uparimāya disāya buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Uparimāya disāya buddho tiṭṭhatīti? Āmantā. Cātumahārājike tiṭṭhati…pe… tāvatiṃse tiṭṭhati…pe… yāme tiṭṭhati…pe… tusite tiṭṭhati…pe… nimmānaratiyā tiṭṭhati…pe… paranimmitavasavattiyā tiṭṭhati…pe… brahmaloke tiṭṭhatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does a Buddha stand in the upper direction? That should not be said… and so on. Does a Buddha stand in the upper direction? Yes. Does he stand in the realm of the Four Great Kings… and so on… in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven… and so on… in the Yāma heaven… and so on… in the Tusita heaven… and so on… in the Nimmānarati heaven… and so on… in the Paranimmitavasavatti heaven… and so on… in the Brahma world? That should not be said… and so on.

Sabbadisākathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on all directions is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(206) 7. Dhammakathā

(206) 7. Discourse on Dhamma

887. Sabbe [V 0.0491] dhammā niyatāti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi aniyato rāsīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atthi aniyato rāsīti? Āmantā[P 0.0610]. Hañci atthi aniyato rāsi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe dhammā niyatā”ti.

887. Are all phenomena fixed? Yes. Are they fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Are they fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on. Is there no undetermined category? That should not be said… and so on. But is there an undetermined category? Yes. If there is an undetermined category, then indeed it should not be said, “All phenomena are fixed.”

Sabbe dhammā niyatāti? Āmantā. Nanu tayo rāsī vuttā bhagavatā – micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsīti dha. sa. tikamātikā 15? Āmantā. Hañci tayo rāsī vuttā bhagavatā – micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe dhammā niyatā”ti.

Are all phenomena fixed? Yes. But were not three categories spoken of by the Blessed One—the category fixed in wrongness, the category fixed in rightness, and the undetermined category? Yes. If three categories were spoken of by the Blessed One—the category fixed in wrongness, the category fixed in rightness, and the undetermined category—then indeed it should not be said, “All phenomena are fixed.”

Rūpaṃ [T 0.0643] rūpaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ viññāṇaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is form fixed by way of its characteristic of form? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Is it fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on. Is feeling… and so on… perception… and so on… mental formations… and so on… consciousness fixed by way of its characteristic of consciousness? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Is it fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on.

888. Na vattabbaṃ – rūpaṃ rūpaṭṭhena niyataṃ…pe… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ viññāṇaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ vedanā hoti…pe… [M 0.0441] saññā hoti… saṅkhārā honti… viññāṇaṃ hoti… vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ rūpaṃ hoti…pe… vedanā hoti… saññā hoti… saṅkhārā hontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi rūpaṃ rūpaṭṭhena niyataṃ, vedanā…pe… saññā…pe… saṅkhārā…pe… viññāṇaṃ viññāṇaṭṭhena niyatanti.

888. Should it not be said: “Form is fixed by way of its characteristic of form… and so on… feeling… and so on… perception… and so on… mental formations… and so on… consciousness is fixed by way of its characteristic of consciousness”? Yes. Is form feeling… and so on… perception… mental formations… consciousness? Is feeling… and so on… perception… and so on… mental formations… and so on… consciousness form… and so on… feeling… perception… mental formations? That should not be said. Therefore, form is fixed by way of its characteristic of form, feeling… and so on… perception… and so on… mental formations… and so on… consciousness is fixed by way of its characteristic of consciousness.

Dhammakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on Dhamma is concluded.

21. Ekavīsatimavaggo

21. The Twenty-First Section

(207) 8. Kammakathā

(207) 8. Discourse on Kamma

889. Sabbe [P 0.0611][V 0.0492] kammā niyatāti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi aniyato rāsīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu atthi aniyato rāsīti? Āmantā. Hañci [T 0.0644] atthi aniyato rāsi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe kammā niyatā”ti.

889. Are all kamma fixed? Yes. Are they fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Are they fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on. Is there no undetermined category? That should not be said… and so on. But is there an undetermined category? Yes. If there is an undetermined category, then indeed it should not be said, “All kamma are fixed.”

Sabbe kammā niyatāti? Āmantā. Nanu tayo rāsī vuttā bhagavatā – micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsīti? Āmantā. Hañci tayo rāsī vuttā bhagavatā – micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsi, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbe kammā niyatā”ti.

Are all kamma fixed? Yes. But were not three categories spoken of by the Blessed One—the category fixed in wrongness, the category fixed in rightness, and the undetermined category? Yes. If three categories were spoken of by the Blessed One—the category fixed in wrongness, the category fixed in rightness, and the undetermined category—then indeed it should not be said, “All kamma are fixed.”

890. Diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe…. Upapajjavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ…pe… aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Micchattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… sammattaniyatanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

890. Is kamma to be experienced in this very life fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in this very life? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Is it fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on. Is kamma to be experienced in the next life… and so on… Is kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in subsequent lives? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… and so on. Is it fixed in rightness? That should not be said… and so on.

891. Na vattabbaṃ – diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṭṭhena [P 0.0612] niyataṃ, upapajjavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ…pe… aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyaṭṭhena niyatanti? Āmantā. Diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ upapajjavedanīyaṃ hoti, aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ hoti…pe… upapajjavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hoti, aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ [M 0.0442] hoti…pe… aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ hoti, upapajjavedanīyaṃ hotīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe[V 0.0493]. Tena hi diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ diṭṭhadhammavedanīyaṭṭhena niyataṃ, upapajjavedanīyaṃ kammaṃ…pe… aparāpariyavedanīyaṃ [T 0.0645] kammaṃ aparāpariyavedanīyaṭṭhena niyatanti.

891. Should it not be said: “Kamma to be experienced in this very life is fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in this very life; kamma to be experienced in the next life… and so on… kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives is fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in subsequent lives”? Yes. Does kamma to be experienced in this very life become kamma to be experienced in the next life, or kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives?… and so on… Does kamma to be experienced in the next life become kamma to be experienced in this very life, or kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives?… and so on… Does kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives become kamma to be experienced in this very life, or kamma to be experienced in the next life? It should not be said thus. Therefore, kamma to be experienced in this very life is fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in this very life; kamma to be experienced in the next life… and so on… kamma to be experienced in subsequent lives is fixed by way of its characteristic of being experienced in subsequent lives.

Kammakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Kamma is concluded.

Ekavīsatimavaggo.

The Twenty-First Section.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sāsanaṃ navaṃ kataṃ atthi koci tathāgatassa sāsanaṃ navaṃ karoti labbhā tathāgatassa sāsanaṃ puna navaṃ kātuṃ, puthujjano tedhātukehi dhammehi avivitto, atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya arahattappatti, atthi adhippāyiddhi buddhānaṃ vā sāvakānaṃ vā, atthi buddhānaṃ buddhehi hīnātirekatā, sabbā disā buddhā tiṭṭhanti, sabbe dhammā niyatā, sabbe kammā niyatāti.

The discourse on 'The Dispensation is made new', the discourse on 'Is there anyone who makes the Dispensation of the Tathāgata new', the discourse on 'Is it possible to make the Dispensation of the Tathāgata new again', the discourse on 'An ordinary person is not separated from the dhammas of the three realms', the discourse on 'Is there attainment of Arahantship without abandoning any fetter', the discourse on 'Is there accomplishment through resolve for Buddhas or for disciples', the discourse on 'Is there inferiority or superiority of Buddhas in relation to other Buddhas', the discourse on 'Buddhas stand in all directions', the discourse on 'All dhammas are fixed', and the discourse on 'All kamma are fixed'.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-Second Section

(208) 1. Parinibbānakathā

(208) 1. Discourse on Parinibbāna

892. Atthi [P 0.0613] kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbānanti? Āmantā. Atthi kiñci sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ appahāya…pe… anottappaṃ appahāya parinibbānanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there some fetter without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna? Yes. Is there any personality-view without abandoning which… and so on… any lack of moral dread without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbānanti? Āmantā. Arahā sarāgo…pe… sakilesoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu arahā nirāgo…pe… nikkilesoti? Āmantā. Hañci [T 0.0646] arahā nirāgo…pe… nikkileso, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbāna”nti.

22. Is there some fetter without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna? Yes. Is an Arahant with lust… and so on… with defilements? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not so that an Arahant is without lust… and so on… without defilements? Yes. If an Arahant is without lust… and so on… without defilements, then indeed it should not be said that, 'there is some fetter without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna'.

893. Na vattabbaṃ – “atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbāna”nti? Āmantā[V 0.0494]. Arahā sabbaṃ buddhavisayaṃ jānātīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbānanti.

Should it not be said, 'there is some fetter without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna'? Yes. Does an Arahant know the entire domain of a Buddha? It should not be said thus. Therefore, there is some fetter without abandoning which there is Parinibbāna.

Parinibbānakathā niṭṭhitā.

892. The Discourse on Parinibbāna is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-Second Section

(209) 2. Kusalacittakathā

(209) 2. Discourse on Wholesome Consciousness

894. Arahā [M 0.0443] kusalacitto parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Arahā puññābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharonto… āneñjābhisaṅkhāraṃ abhisaṅkharonto… gatisaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ [P 0.0614] karonto… bhavasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… issariyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… adhipaccasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… mahābhogasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… mahāparivārasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… devasobhagyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto… manussasobhagyasaṃvattaniyaṃ kammaṃ karonto parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does an Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attain Parinibbāna? Yes. Does an Arahant, while forming a meritorious volitional formation… while forming an imperturbable volitional formation… while performing kamma conducive to rebirth… while performing kamma conducive to existence… while performing kamma conducive to mastery… while performing kamma conducive to supremacy… while performing kamma conducive to great possessions… while performing kamma conducive to a great retinue… while performing kamma conducive to divine splendor… while performing kamma conducive to human splendor, attain Parinibbāna? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Arahā ācinanto apacinanto pajahanto upādiyanto visinento ussinento vidhūpento sandhūpento parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe [T 0.0647]…pe… nanu arahā nevācināti na apacināti apacinitvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā nevācināti na apacināti apacinitvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyatī”ti. Nanu arahā neva pajahati na upādiyati pajahitvā ṭhito, neva visineti na ussineti visinetvā ṭhito; nanu arahā neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhitoti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā neva vidhūpeti na sandhūpeti vidhūpetvā ṭhito, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyatī”ti.

893. Does an Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attain Parinibbāna? Yes. Does an Arahant, while accumulating or decreasing, abandoning or taking up, unbinding or binding, dispelling or consolidating, attain Parinibbāna? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not so that an Arahant neither accumulates nor decreases, but is established, having decreased? Yes. If an Arahant neither accumulates nor decreases, but is established, having decreased, then indeed it should not be said, 'An Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains Parinibbāna.' Is it not so that an Arahant neither abandons nor takes up, but is established, having abandoned; neither unbinds nor binds, but is established, having unbound; is it not so that an Arahant neither dispels nor consolidates, but is established, having dispelled? Yes. If an Arahant neither dispels nor consolidates, but is established, having dispelled, then indeed it should not be said, 'An Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains Parinibbāna'.

895. Na vattabbaṃ – “arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyatī”ti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā [V 0.0495] upaṭṭhitassati sato sampajāno parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā upaṭṭhitassati sato sampajāno parinibbāyati, tena vata re vattabbe – “arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyatī”ti.

Should it not be said, 'An Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains Parinibbāna'? Yes. Is it not so that an Arahant, with mindfulness established, being mindful and clearly comprehending, attains Parinibbāna? Yes. If an Arahant, with mindfulness established, being mindful and clearly comprehending, attains Parinibbāna, then indeed it should be said, 'An Arahant, with a wholesome mind, attains Parinibbāna'.

Kusalacittakathā niṭṭhitā.

22. The Discourse on Wholesome Consciousness is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-Second Section

(210) 3. Āneñjakathā

(210) 3. Discourse on the Imperturbable

896. Arahā [M 0.0444][P 0.0615] āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Nanu arahā pakaticitte ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā pakaticitte ṭhito parinibbāyati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatī”ti.

Does an Arahant attain Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Is it not so that an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in a normal state of mind? Yes. If an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in a normal state of mind, then indeed it should not be said, “An Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable.”

Arahā [T 0.0648] āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Arahā kiriyamaye citte ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu arahā vipākacitte ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vipākacitte ṭhito parinibbāyati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatī”ti.

894. Does an Arahant attain Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does an Arahant attain Parinibbāna while established in a functional consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not so that an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in resultant consciousness? Yes. If an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in resultant consciousness, then indeed it should not be said: “An Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable.”

Arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Arahā kiriyābyākate citte ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu arahā vipākābyākate citte ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Hañci arahā vipākābyākate citte ṭhito parinibbāyati, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatī”ti.

Does an Arahant attain Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does an Arahant attain Parinibbāna while established in a functional indeterminate consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not so that an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in a resultant indeterminate consciousness? Yes. If an Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in a resultant indeterminate consciousness, then indeed it should not be said, “An Arahant attains Parinibbāna while established in the imperturbable.”

Arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatīti? Āmantā. Nanu bhagavā catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā [V 0.0496] samanantarā parinibbutoti dī. ni. 2.219? Āmantā. Hañci bhagavā catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā parinibbuto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyatī”ti.

Does an arahant attain final Nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Is it not so that the Blessed One, having arisen from the fourth jhāna, immediately attained final Nibbāna? Yes. If the Blessed One, having arisen from the fourth jhāna, immediately attained final Nibbāna, then indeed it should not be said, “An arahant attains final Nibbāna while established in the imperturbable.”

Āneñjakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Imperturbable is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-second Chapter

(211) 4. Dhammābhisamayakathā

(211) 4. Discussion on the Realization of the Dhamma

897. Atthi [P 0.0616] gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammadesanā, dhammassavanaṃ, dhammasākacchā, paripucchā, sīlasamādānaṃ[T 0.0649], indriyesu guttadvāratā, bhojane mattaññutā, pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogoti[M 0.0445]? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… natthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammadesanā, dhammassavanaṃ…pe… pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogoti? Āmantā. Hañci natthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammadesanā, dhammassavanaṃ…pe… pubbarattāpararattaṃ jāgariyānuyogo, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayo”ti.

897. Is there realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there teaching of the Dhamma, hearing of the Dhamma, discussion of the Dhamma, questioning, undertaking precepts, guarding the sense-faculties, moderation in food, and devotion to wakefulness in the early and late watches of the night, for one lying in the womb? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is it not so that there is no teaching of the Dhamma, hearing of the Dhamma… and so on… devotion to wakefulness in the early and late watches of the night, for one lying in the womb? Yes. If there is no teaching of the Dhamma, hearing of the Dhamma… and so on… devotion to wakefulness in the early and late watches of the night, for one lying in the womb, then indeed it should not be said, “There is realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb.”

Atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Nanu dve paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāya – parato ca ghoso, yoniso ca manasikāroti? Āmantā. Hañci dve paccayā sammādiṭṭhiyā uppādāya – parato ca ghoso, yoniso ca manasikāro, no ca vata re vattabbe – “atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayo”ti.

Is there realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is it not so that there are two conditions for the arising of right view—the voice of another and wise attention? Yes. If there are two conditions for the arising of right view—the voice of another and wise attention—then indeed it should not be said, “There is realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb.”

Atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Suttassa pamattassa muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa dhammābhisamayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Is there realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there realization of the Dhamma for one who is asleep, heedless, of lapsed mindfulness, and without clear comprehension? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Dhammābhisamayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Realization of the Dhamma is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-second Chapter

(212-4) 5-7. Tissopikathā

(212-4) 5-7. The Three Discussions

898. Atthi [V 0.0497] gabbhaseyyāya arahattappattīti? Āmantā. Suttassa [P 0.0617] pamattassa muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa arahattappattīti? Na [T 0.0650] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

898. Is there attainment of Arahantship for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there attainment of Arahantship for one who is sleeping, heedless, of lapsed mindfulness, and without clear comprehension? It should not be said thus… and so on…

899. Atthi supinagatassa dhammābhisamayoti? Āmantā. Suttassa pamattassa muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa dhammābhisamayoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

899. Is there realization of the Dhamma for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there realization of the Dhamma for one who is sleeping, heedless, of lapsed mindfulness, and without clear comprehension? It should not be said thus… and so on…

900. Atthi supinagatassa arahattappattīti? Āmantā. Suttassa pamattassa muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa arahattappattīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

900. Is there attainment of Arahantship for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there attainment of Arahantship for one who is sleeping, heedless, of lapsed mindfulness, and without clear comprehension? It should not be said thus… and so on…

Tissopikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Three Discussions are concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-second Chapter

(215) 8. Abyākatakathā

(215) 8. The Discussion on the Indeterminate

901. Sabbaṃ [M 0.0446] supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākatanti? Āmantā. Supinantena pāṇaṃ haneyyāti? Āmantā. Hañci supinantena pāṇaṃ haneyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākata”nti.

901. Is all the mind of one who is dreaming indeterminate? Yes. Could one kill a living being in a dream? Yes. If one could kill a living being in a dream, then indeed it should not be said, ‘All the mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate’.

Supinantena adinnaṃ ādiyeyya…pe… musā bhaṇeyya, pisuṇaṃ bhaṇeyya, pharusaṃ bhaṇeyya, samphaṃ palapeyya, sandhiṃ chindeyya, nillopaṃ hareyya, ekāgārikaṃ kareyya, paripanthe tiṭṭheyya, paradāraṃ gaccheyya, gāmaghātakaṃ kareyya, nigamaghātakaṃ kareyya, supinantena methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyya[V 0.0498], supinagatassa asuci mucceyya, supinantena dānaṃ dadeyya, cīvaraṃ dadeyya, piṇḍapātaṃ dadeyya, senāsanaṃ dadeyya, gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṃ dadeyya, khādanīyaṃ dadeyya, bhojanīyaṃ dadeyya, pānīyaṃ dadeyya, cetiyaṃ vandeyya, cetiye mālaṃ āropeyya, gandhaṃ āropeyya[T 0.0651], vilepanaṃ āropeyya…pe… cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ kareyyāti? Āmantā[P 0.0618]. Hañci supinantena cetiyaṃ abhidakkhiṇaṃ kareyya, no ca vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākata”nti.

In a dream, could one take what was not given… and so on… speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter, break into a house, plunder, commit burglary, lie in ambush, commit adultery, destroy a village, destroy a town; in a dream, could one engage in sexual intercourse, have a seminal emission; in a dream, could one give a gift, give a robe, give almsfood, give lodging, give medicine and requisites for the sick, give hard food, give soft food, give a drink, pay homage to a shrine, offer garlands at a shrine, offer incense, offer ointment… and so on… circumambulate a shrine to the right? Yes. If, in a dream, one could circumambulate a shrine to the right, then indeed it should not be said, ‘All the mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate’.

902. Na vattabbaṃ – “sabbaṃ supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākata”nti? Āmantā. Nanu supinagatassa cittaṃ abbohāriyaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatāti? Āmantā. Hañci supinagatassa cittaṃ abbohāriyaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā, tena vata re vattabbe – “sabbaṃ supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākata”nti.

902. Should it not be said, ‘All the mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate’? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One that the mind of one who is dreaming is not conventionally valid? Yes. If it was said by the Blessed One that the mind of one who is dreaming is not conventionally valid, then indeed it should be said, ‘All the mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate’.

Abyākatakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Indeterminate is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-second Chapter

(216) 9. Āsevanapaccayakathā

(216) 9. Discussion on the Repetition Condition

903. Natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “pāṇātipāto, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato [M 0.0447] nirayasaṃvattaniko tiracchānayonisaṃvattaniko pettivisayasaṃvattaniko, yo sabbalahuso pāṇātipātassa vipāko manussabhūtassa appāyukasaṃvattaniko hotī”ti a. ni. 8.40. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

903. Is there no repetition conditionality? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: ‘Monks, the destruction of life, when repeated, developed, and made much of, is conducive to hell, is conducive to the animal realm, is conducive to the sphere of the departed spirits. The very lightest result of the destruction of life, for one who has become a human, is conducive to a short lifespan’? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. Therefore, there is some repetition conditionality.

Natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “adinnādānaṃ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ nirayasaṃvattanikaṃ [T 0.0652] tiracchānayonisaṃvattanikaṃ pettivisayasaṃvattanikaṃ, yo sabbalahuso adinnādānassa vipāko manussabhūtassa bhogabyasanasaṃvattaniko [V 0.0499] hoti…pe… yo sabbalahuso kāmesumicchācārassa vipāko manussabhūtassa sapattaverasaṃvattaniko hoti…pe… yo sabbalahuso musāvādassa vipāko [P 0.0619] manussabhūtassa abbhūtabbhakkhānasaṃvattaniko hoti…pe… yo sabbalahuso pisuṇāya vācāya vipāko manussabhūtassa mittehi bhedanasaṃvattaniko hoti…pe… yo sabbalahuso pharusāya vācāya vipāko manussabhūtassa amanāpasaddasaṃvattaniko hoti…pe… yo sabbalahuso samphappalāpassa vipāko manussabhūtassa anādeyyavācāsaṃvattaniko hoti, surāmerayapānaṃ, bhikkhave, āsevitaṃ…pe… yo sabbalahuso surāmerayapānassa vipāko manussabhūtassa ummattakasaṃvattaniko hotī”ti a. ni. 8.40! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

Is there no repetition conditionality? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Monks, taking what is not given, when pursued, developed, and cultivated, is conducive to hell, is conducive to the animal realm, is conducive to the sphere of the departed spirits. The very lightest result of taking what is not given, for one who has become a human, is conducive to the destruction of wealth... The very lightest result of sexual misconduct... is conducive to enmity with rivals... The very lightest result of false speech... is conducive to false accusations... The very lightest result of divisive speech... is conducive to division from friends... The very lightest result of harsh speech... is conducive to unpleasant sounds... The very lightest result of frivolous talk... is conducive to one's words not being accepted. Monks, the drinking of spirits and intoxicants, when pursued... The very lightest result of drinking spirits and intoxicants, for one who has become a human, is conducive to madness'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. If that is so, then there is some repetition conditionality.

904. Natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “micchādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nirayasaṃvattanikā tiracchānayonisaṃvattanikā pettivisayasaṃvattanikā”ti. Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

904. Is there no repetition conditionality? No. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Wrong view, monks, when pursued, developed, and cultivated, is conducive to hell, is conducive to the animal realm, is conducive to the sphere of the departed spirits'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. If that is so, then there is some repetition conditionality.

Natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “micchāsaṅkappo…pe… micchāsamādhi, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito…pe… pettivisayasaṃvattaniko”ti! Attheva suttantoti[T 0.0653]? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

Is there no repetition conditionality? No. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Wrong intention... wrong concentration, monks, when pursued, developed... is conducive to the sphere of the departed spirits'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. If that is so, then there is some repetition conditionality.

905. Natthi [M 0.0448] kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sammādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkatā amatogadhā hoti amataparāyanā amatapariyosānā”ti! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

905. Is there no repetition conditionality? Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Right view, monks, when pursued, developed, and cultivated, plunges into the deathless, has the deathless as its resort, and culminates in the deathless'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. If that is so, then there is some repetition conditionality.

Natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti? Āmantā. Nanu vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “sammāsaṅkappo, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito bahulīkato…pe… sammāsamādhi, bhikkhave, āsevito bhāvito [V 0.0500] bahulīkato amatogadho [P 0.0620] hoti amataparāyano amatapariyosāno”ti attheva suttantoti, āmantā. Tena hi atthi kāci āsevanapaccayatāti.

Is there no repetition conditionality? No. But was it not said by the Blessed One: 'Right intention, monks, when pursued, developed, and cultivated... Right concentration, monks, when pursued, developed, and cultivated, plunges into the deathless, has the deathless as its resort, and culminates in the deathless'? Is there not such a sutta? Yes. If that is so, then there is some repetition conditionality.

Āsevanapaccayakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Repetition Condition is concluded.

22. Bāvīsatimavaggo

22. The Twenty-second Chapter.

(217) 10. Khaṇikakathā

(217) 10. The Discourse on Momentariness

906. Ekacittakkhaṇikā sabbe dhammāti? Āmantā. Citte mahāpathavī saṇṭhāti, mahāsamuddo saṇṭhāti, sinerupabbatarājā saṇṭhāti, āpo saṇṭhāti, tejo saṇṭhāti, vāyo saṇṭhāti, tiṇakaṭṭhavanappatayo saṇṭhahantīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

906. Are all phenomena of a single mind-moment? Yes. Does the great earth exist in the mind, does the great ocean exist in the mind, does Mount Sineru, the king of mountains, exist in the mind, does water exist in the mind, does fire exist in the mind, does wind exist in the mind, do grasses, sticks, and forest trees exist in the mind? It should not be said thus… and so on….

Ekacittakkhaṇikā sabbe dhammāti? Āmantā. Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇena sahajātanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ [T 0.0654] cakkhuviññāṇena sahajātanti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – “ajjhattikañceva, āvuso, cakkhuṃ aparibhinnaṃ hoti, bāhirā ca rūpā na āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, no ca tajjo samannāhāro hoti, neva tāva tajjassa viññāṇabhāgassa viññāṇabhāvassa (bahūsu) pātubhāvo hoti. Ajjhattikañceva, āvuso, cakkhuṃ aparibhinnaṃ hoti, bāhirā ca rūpā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, no ca tajjo samannāhāro hoti, neva tāva tajjassa viññāṇabhāgassa pātubhāvo hoti. Yato ca kho, āvuso, ajjhattikañceva cakkhuṃ aparibhinnaṃ hoti[M 0.0449], bāhirā ca rūpā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, tajjo ca samannāhāro hoti, evaṃ tajjassa viññāṇabhāgassa pātubhāvo hotī”ti ma. ni. 1.306! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇena sahajāta”nti.

Are all phenomena of a single mind-moment? Yes. Is the eye-base conascent with eye-consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the eye-base conascent with eye-consciousness? Yes. Did not the venerable Sāriputta say this: ‘Friends, when the internal eye is intact, but external forms do not come into range, and there is no appropriate attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding part of consciousness does not yet occur. Friends, when the internal eye is intact, and external forms come into range, but there is no appropriate attention, then the manifestation of the corresponding part of consciousness does not yet occur. But when, friends, the internal eye is intact, external forms come into range, and there is appropriate attention, thus the manifestation of the corresponding part of consciousness occurs’? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The eye-base is conascent with eye-consciousness.’

Sotāyatanaṃ…pe… ghānāyatanaṃ…pe… jivhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇena sahajātanti? Na [P 0.0621] hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇena [V 0.0501] sahajātanti? Āmantā. Nanu āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca – “ajjhattiko ceva, āvuso, kāyo aparibhinno hoti, bāhirā ca phoṭṭhabbā na āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, no ca…pe… ajjhattiko ceva, āvuso, kāyo aparibhinno hoti, bāhirā ca phoṭṭhabbā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, no ca…pe… yato ca kho, āvuso, ajjhattiko [T 0.0655] ceva kāyo aparibhinno hoti, bāhirā ca phoṭṭhabbā āpāthaṃ āgacchanti, tajjo ca samannāhāro hoti, evaṃ tajjassa viññāṇabhāgassa pātubhāvo hotī”ti ma. ni. 1.306! Attheva suttantoti? Āmantā. Tena hi na vattabbaṃ – “kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇena sahajāta”nti.

The ear-base… and so on… the nose-base… and so on… the tongue-base… and so on… Is the body-base conascent with body-consciousness? It should not be said thus… and so on… Is the body-base conascent with body-consciousness? Yes. But did not the venerable Sāriputta say this: ‘Friends, when the internal body is intact and external tactile objects do not come into range, and there is no appropriate attention… and so on… when the internal body is intact and external tactile objects come into range, but there is no appropriate attention… and so on… but when, friends, the internal body is intact, external tactile objects come into range, and there is appropriate attention, thus the manifestation of the corresponding part of consciousness occurs’? Is there indeed such a Sutta? Yes. Therefore, it should not be said: ‘The body-base is conascent with body-consciousness.’

907. Na vattabbaṃ – “ekacittakkhaṇikā sabbe dhammā”ti? Āmantā. Sabbe dhammā niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe. Tena hi ekacittakkhaṇikā sabbe dhammāti.

907. Should it not be said: ‘All phenomena are of a single mind-moment’? No, it should not be said. Are all phenomena permanent, stable, everlasting, and of an unchanging nature? It should not be said thus. Therefore, all phenomena are of a single mind-moment.

Khaṇikakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Momentariness is concluded.

Bāvīsatimavaggo.

The Twenty-second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Atthi kiñci saṃyojanaṃ appahāya parinibbānaṃ, arahā kusalacitto parinibbāyati, arahā āneñje ṭhito parinibbāyati, atthi gabbhaseyyāya dhammābhisamayo, atthi gabbhaseyyāya arahattappatti, atthi supinagatassa dhammābhisamayo, atthi supinagatassa arahattappatti, sabbaṃ supinagatassa cittaṃ abyākataṃ, natthi kāci āsevanapaccayatā, ekacittakkhaṇikā sabbe dhammāti.

The discourse on 'The attainment of Parinibbāna without having abandoned a certain fetter', the discourse on 'An Arahant attains Parinibbāna with a wholesome mind', the discourse on 'An Arahant established in the imperturbable attains Parinibbāna', the discourse on 'There is realization of the Dhamma for one lying in the womb', the discourse on 'There is attainment of Arahantship for one lying in the womb', the discourse on 'There is realization of the Dhamma for one who is dreaming', the discourse on 'There is attainment of Arahantship for one who is dreaming', the discourse on 'All consciousness of one who is dreaming is indeterminate', the discourse on 'There is no conditionality by way of repetition', and the discourse on 'All phenomena are momentary'.

23. Tevīsatimavaggo

23. The Twenty-Third Section

(218) 1. Ekādhippāyakathā

(218) 1. Discourse on the Same Intention

908. Ekādhippāyena [M 0.0450][P 0.0622] methuno dhammo paṭisevitabboti? Āmantā. Ekādhippāyena assamaṇena [V 0.0502] hotabbaṃ, abhikkhunā hotabbaṃ, chinnamūlena hotabbaṃ pārājikena hotabbanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… ekādhippāyena methuno dhammo paṭisevitabboti? Āmantā. Ekādhippāyena pāṇo hantabbo, adinnaṃ ādiyitabbaṃ, musā bhaṇitabbā, pisuṇaṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ, pharusaṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ, samphaṃ palapitabbaṃ, sandhi cheditabbo, nillopaṃ hātabbaṃ, ekāgārikaṃ kātabbaṃ, paripanthe ṭhātabbaṃ, paradāro gantabbo, gāmaghātako kātabbo, nigamaghātako kātabboti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

908. Should the sexual act be engaged in with the same intention? Yes. With the same intention, should one become a non-ascetic, a non-bhikkhu, one with a severed root, one who has committed a pārājika offense? It should not be said thus… Should the sexual act be engaged in with the same intention? Yes. With the same intention, should a living being be killed, should what is not given be taken, should a falsehood be spoken, should divisive speech be spoken, should harsh speech be spoken, should frivolous chatter be spoken, should a house be broken into, should robbery be committed, should a single-house robbery be committed, should one stand on the path to waylay, should another's wife be gone to, should village-slaughter be committed, should town-slaughter be committed? It should not be said thus…

Ekādhippāyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Same Intention is concluded.

23. Tevīsatimavaggo

23. The Twenty-Third Section

(219) 2. Arahantavaṇṇakathā

(219) 2. Discourse on the Guise of an Arahant

909. Arahantānaṃ vaṇṇena amanussā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevantīti? Āmantā. Arahantānaṃ vaṇṇena amanussā pāṇaṃ hananti…pe… adinnaṃ ādiyanti, musā bhaṇanti, pisuṇaṃ bhaṇanti, pharusaṃ bhaṇanti, samphaṃ palapanti, sandhiṃ chindanti, nillopaṃ haranti, ekāgārikaṃ [T 0.0657] karonti, paripanthe tiṭṭhanti, paradāraṃ gacchanti, gāmaghātakaṃ karonti…pe… nigamaghātakaṃ karontīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

909. In the guise of Arahants, do non-humans engage in the sexual act? Yes. In the guise of Arahants, do non-humans kill living beings… take what is not given, speak falsehood, speak divisive speech, speak harsh speech, speak frivolous chatter, break into houses, plunder, commit single-house robbery, stand on the path to waylay, go to another's wife, commit village-slaughter… commit town-slaughter? It should not be said thus…

Arahantavaṇṇakathā niṭṭhitā.
