The Discourse on the Guise of an Arahant is concluded.

23. Tevīsatimavaggo

23. The Twenty-Third Section

(220-4) 3-7. Issariyakāmakārikādikathā

(220-4) 3-7. Discourses on Acting from a Desire for Sovereignty, etc.

910. Bodhisatto [P 0.0623] issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchatīti? Āmantā. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu nirayaṃ gacchati[M 0.0451], sañjīvaṃ gacchati, kālasuttaṃ gacchati, tāpanaṃ gacchati, mahātāpanaṃ patāpanaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) gacchati, saṅghātakaṃ gacchati, roruvaṃ gacchati…pe… avīciṃ gacchatīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

910. Does the Bodhisatta go to a state of ruin due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Does the Bodhisatta, due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, go to hell, go to the Sañjīva hell, go to the Kālasutta hell, go to the Tāpana hell, go to the Mahātāpana hell, go to the Saṅghāta hell, go to the Roruva hell… go to the Avīci hell? It should not be said thus…

Bodhisatto [V 0.0503] issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchatīti? Āmantā. “Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchatī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. Hañci “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchatī”ti – nattheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchatī”ti.

Does the Bodhisatta go to a state of ruin due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Is there indeed a Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin due to acting from a desire for sovereignty'? There is not. If there is indeed no Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin due to acting from a desire for sovereignty,' then it should not be said, 'The Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin due to acting from a desire for sovereignty.'

911. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatīti? Āmantā. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu nirayaṃ upapajjeyya, tiracchānayoniṃ upapajjeyyāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

911. Does the Bodhisatta descend into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, would the Bodhisatta be reborn in hell, or be reborn in the animal realm? It should not be said thus…

Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatīti[T 0.0658]? Āmantā. Bodhisatto iddhimāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… bodhisatto iddhimāti? Āmantā. Bodhisattena chandiddhipādo bhāvito…pe… vīriyiddhipādo…pe… cittiddhipādo…pe… vīmaṃsiddhipādo bhāvitoti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

Does the Bodhisatta descend into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Is the Bodhisatta possessed of psychic power? It should not be said thus… Is the Bodhisatta possessed of psychic power? Yes. Has the base of psychic power of desire been developed by the Bodhisatta… the base of psychic power of energy… the base of psychic power of mind… has the base of psychic power of investigation been developed? It should not be said thus…

Bodhisatto [P 0.0624] issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatīti? Āmantā. “Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. Hañci “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatī”ti – nattheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamatī”ti.

Does the Bodhisatta descend into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Is there indeed a Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta descends into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty'? There is not. If there is indeed no Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta descends into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty,' then it should not be said, 'The Bodhisatta descends into the womb due to acting from a desire for sovereignty.'

912. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu dukkarakārikaṃ akāsīti? Āmantā. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu “sassato loko”ti paccāgacchi, “asassato loko”ti…pe… “antavā loko”ti…pe… “anantavā loko”ti… “taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra”nti [M 0.0452]… “aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra”nti… “hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti… “na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti… “hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti…pe… “neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti paccāgacchīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

912. Did the Bodhisatta perform difficult practices due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, did the Bodhisatta revert to the view that 'the world is eternal,' that 'the world is not eternal,'… that 'the world is finite,'… that 'the world is infinite,' that 'the life-principle is the same as the body,' that 'the life-principle is different from the body,' that 'the Tathāgata exists after death,' that 'the Tathāgata does not exist after death,' that 'the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,'… that 'the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death'? It should not be said thus…

Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu dukkarakārikaṃ akāsīti? Āmantā. “Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu dukkarakārikaṃ akāsī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. Hañci “bodhisatto [V 0.0504] issariyakāmakārikāhetu [T 0.0659] dukkarakārikaṃ akāsī”ti – nattheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu dukkarakārikaṃ akāsī”ti.

Did the Bodhisatta perform difficult practices due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Is there indeed a Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta performed difficult practices due to acting from a desire for sovereignty'? There is not. If there is indeed no Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta performed difficult practices due to acting from a desire for sovereignty,' then it should not be said, 'The Bodhisatta performed difficult practices due to acting from a desire for sovereignty.'

913. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu aparantapaṃ amaraṃ tapaṃ (saṃ. ni. 1.137) akāsi, aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisīti? Āmantā. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu “sassato loko”ti paccāgacchi…pe… [P 0.0625] “neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā”ti paccāgacchīti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

913. Due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, did the Bodhisatta torment others and designate another teacher? Yes. Due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, did the Bodhisatta revert to the view that 'the world is eternal'… that 'the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death'? It should not be said thus…

914. Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisīti? Āmantā. “Bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisī”ti – attheva suttantoti? Natthi. Hañci “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisī”ti – nattheva suttanto, no ca vata re vattabbe – “bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisī”ti.

914. Did the Bodhisatta designate another teacher due to acting from a desire for sovereignty? Yes. Is there indeed a Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta designated another teacher due to acting from a desire for sovereignty'? There is not. If there is indeed no Suttanta that says, 'The Bodhisatta designated another teacher due to acting from a desire for sovereignty,' then it should not be said, 'The Bodhisatta designated another teacher due to acting from a desire for sovereignty.'

Issariyakāmakārikākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Acting from a Desire for Sovereignty is concluded.

23. Tevīsatimavaggo

23. The Twenty-Third Section

(225) 8. Patirūpakathā

(225) 8. Discussion on Resemblance

915. Atthi na rāgo rāgapatirūpakoti? Āmantā. Atthi na phasso phassapatirūpako, atthi na vedanā vedanāpatirūpikā, atthi na saññā saññāpatirūpikā[M 0.0453], atthi na cetanā cetanāpatirūpikā, atthi na cittaṃ cittapatirūpakaṃ, atthi na saddhā saddhāpatirūpikā, atthi na vīriyaṃ vīriyapatirūpakaṃ, atthi na sati satipatirūpikā, atthi na samādhi samādhipatirūpako[T 0.0660], atthi na paññā paññāpatirūpikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

915. Is there that which is not passion but resembles passion? Yes. Is there that which is not contact but resembles contact, that which is not feeling but resembles feeling, that which is not perception but resembles perception, that which is not volition but resembles volition, that which is not mind but resembles mind, that which is not faith but resembles faith, that which is not energy but resembles energy, that which is not mindfulness but resembles mindfulness, that which is not concentration but resembles concentration, that which is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? It should not be said so…

916. Atthi na doso dosapatirūpako, atthi na moho mohapatirūpako, atthi na kileso [V 0.0505] kilesapatirūpakoti? Āmantā. Atthi [P 0.0626] na phasso phassapatirūpako…pe… atthi na paññā paññāpatirūpikāti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe….

916. Is there that which is not aversion but resembles aversion, that which is not delusion but resembles delusion, that which is not a defilement but resembles a defilement? Yes. Is there that which is not contact but resembles contact… up to… that which is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? It should not be said so…

Patirūpakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on Resemblance is Concluded.

23. Tevīsatimavaggo

23. The Twenty-Third Section

(226) 9. Aparinipphannakathā

(226) 9. Discussion on the Unperfected

917. Rūpaṃ aparinipphannanti? Āmantā. Rūpaṃ na aniccaṃ na saṅkhataṃ na paṭiccasamuppannaṃ na khayadhammaṃ na vayadhammaṃ na virāgadhammaṃ na nirodhadhammaṃ na vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu rūpaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci rūpaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “rūpaṃ aparinipphanna”nti.

917. Is form unperfected? Yes. Is form not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently arisen, not subject to destruction, not subject to vanishing, not subject to dispassion, not subject to cessation, not subject to change? It should not be said so… Is it not so that form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to dispassion, subject to cessation, and subject to change? Yes. If form is impermanent, conditioned… up to… subject to change, then it should not be said that ‘form is unperfected.’

Dukkhaññeva parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Nanu yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ saṃ. ni. 3.15 vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “rūpaṃ anicca”nti? Āmantā. Hañci yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “rūpaṃ aniccaṃ”, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dukkhaññeva parinipphanna”nti…pe….

Is only suffering perfected? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One that what is impermanent is suffering, and that ‘form is impermanent’? Yes. If the Blessed One said that what is impermanent is suffering, and that ‘form is impermanent’, then it should not be said that ‘only suffering is perfected’…

918. Vedanā [T 0.0661]…pe… saññā… saṅkhārā… viññāṇaṃ… cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ… cakkhudhātu… dhammadhātu… cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… aññātāvindriyaṃ aparinipphannanti? Āmantā. Aññātāvindriyaṃ [P 0.0627] na aniccaṃ…pe… na vipariṇāmadhammanti? Na hevaṃ vattabbe…pe… nanu aññātāvindriyaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ…pe… vipariṇāmadhammanti? Āmantā. Hañci aññātāvindriyaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammaṃ vipariṇāmadhammaṃ, no ca vata re vattabbe – “aññātāvindriyaṃ aparinipphanna”nti.

918. Is feeling… perception… volitional formations… consciousness… the eye-base… up to… the mind-base… the eye-element… the mind-element… the eye-faculty… up to… the faculty of final knowledge unperfected? Yes. Is the faculty of final knowledge not impermanent… up to… not subject to change? It should not be said so… Is it not so that the faculty of final knowledge is impermanent, conditioned… up to… subject to change? Yes. If the faculty of final knowledge is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to dispassion, subject to cessation, and subject to change, then it should not be said that ‘the faculty of final knowledge is unperfected.’

Dukkhaññeva [M 0.0454][V 0.0506] parinipphannanti? Āmantā. Nanu yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “aññātāvindriyaṃ anicca”nti? Āmantā. Hañci yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā – “aññātāvindriyaṃ aniccaṃ”, no ca vata re vattabbe – “dukkhaññeva parinipphanna”nti.

Is only suffering perfected? Yes. Was it not said by the Blessed One that what is impermanent is suffering, and that ‘the faculty of final knowledge is impermanent’? Yes. If the Blessed One said that what is impermanent is suffering, and that ‘the faculty of final knowledge is impermanent’, then it should not be said that ‘only suffering is perfected.’

Aparinipphannakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Unperfected is concluded.

Tevīsatimavaggo.

The Twenty-Third Section.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Ekādhippāyena methuno dhammo paṭisevitabbo, arahantānaṃ vaṇṇena amanussā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanti, bodhisatto issariyakāmakārikāhetu vinipātaṃ gacchati, gabbhaseyyaṃ okkamati, dukkarakārikaṃ akāsi[T 0.0662], aparantapaṃ akāsi, aññaṃ satthāraṃ uddisi, atthi na rāgo rāgapatirūpako atthi na doso dosapatirūpako atthi na moho mohapatirūpako atthi na kileso kilesapatirūpako, rūpaṃ aparinipphannaṃ aññātāvindriyaṃ aparinipphannanti.

Sexual intercourse should be engaged in with a single intention; non-humans engage in sexual intercourse through praise of the arahants; the Bodhisatta, due to acting from a desire for sovereignty, goes to a state of loss, enters the womb, performed difficult austerities, tormented others, and designated another teacher; there is that which is not passion but resembles passion, that which is not aversion but resembles aversion, that which is not delusion but resembles delusion, that which is not a defilement but resembles a defilement; form is unperfected, and the faculty of final knowledge is unperfected.

Khuddako aḍḍhapaṇṇāsako.

The Minor Half-Fifty.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Navaṃ, nibbuti, ekādhippāyoti.

New, extinguished, with a single intention.

Paṇṇāsakuddānaṃ –

Summary of the Fifties:

Mahāniyāmo[P 0.0628], anusayā, niggaho, khuddakapañcamo;

Parappavādamaddanā, suttamūlasamāhitā;

Ujjotanā satthusamaye, kathāvatthupakaraṇeti.

The Great Section, the Underlying Tendencies, the Refutation, with the Minor as the fifth; the crushing of others' doctrines, established in the root of the suttas; the illumination in the Teacher's dispensation, the treatise of the Points of Controversy.

Pañcattiṃsabhāṇavāraṃ

Thirty-five recitation sections.

Kathāvatthupakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The treatise of the Points of Controversy is concluded.
